Heading: Eat route - Indian Express
Content:
Pani Puri
Star OneSaturday, 9 pm
Rating***

Ques: What's it about?

Pani Puri is the story of Divya Pani (Smita Bansal) and Vikas Puri (Sumeet Raghavan) who are completely different as individuals. Divya Pani is sophistication personified and leads a disciplined life. Vikas Puri is a carefree guy, a stage actor by profession, in complete contrast to Ms Pani. Like in every other soap on Indian television, both of them meet and fall in love and marry. The twists come in when two families from diverse cultures come close to each other due to this marriage. Divya Pani's family is sophisticated and Vikas Puri's family the exact opposite. After Divya and Vikas's wedding their families try to influence the couple. The never-ending clash of views creates humorous situations in the serial.

Ques: Who's in it?

Along with Bansal and Raghavan, the show also features other fine actors such as Bhavna

Balsaver, Shagufta Ali and Sudhir Pandey. All these seasoned actors, have been great promoters of comedy even during their younger days. The storyline of the sitcom mainly consists of these six characters and the issues surrounding them.

Ques: What's hot?

In the Indian television arena, that is loaded with saas bahu dramas and hot and spicy reality shows, this one comes as a pleasant surprise. Raghavan, as usual is the captain of the ship, getting his comic timing right on most occasions. Besides, Balsaver puts up a good performance in a role that demands her to be the authoritative mother of the bride. Pandey is good in his loud Punjabi act, dishing out some witty one-liners. Also, the title song is catchy and makes for a good start.

Ques: What's not?

The channel, Star One, has been associated with a number of shows like Sarabhai vs Sarabhai, Instant Khichdi which are remembered till date. So when this serial got on air, there were lots of expectations with this new show Pani Puri. But it doesn't quite make a mark in the comedy genre. The comedy is quite slapstick, but at times most jokes feel like a rip off of the popular series Sarabhai. The concept too isn't novel and can strike similarities with many movies and serials of the past. Also, the house in which the entire series is set up reminds you of may be a Hum Paanch or Sarabhai. Bansal is too plastic and suffers from bad dialogue delivery, while Shagufta Ali doesn't fit into the character of a loud Punjabi housewife.

Ques: Should you be watching it?

For those not out partying on a Saturday night, you could share some funny moments with the Pani-Puri couple. But those of you with a plan, no point hanging out with your idiot box. May be you could catch a re-run during the week.

Heading: Nitin’s death result of road rage, say police - Indian Express
Content:
Add food to travel; get the perfect recipe for adventure

The association of travel with food dates back to the age when most people lived as nomads, travelling from one city to the other.

The one question that logically sprung to mind was, 'What do we eat when we get there?' The question continues to haunt us till date.

Television producers have done a smart job by tapping this to come up with food cum travel shows to suit our urge to see the world and to satisfy our taste-buds with some sumptuous meals. "Food is limiting in a particular region. Hence, it becomes important to travel around the country or the world to get a taste of ingredients there," says Seema Chandra, who will be hosting a new show Fully Fed Up to be aired next month on NDTV Good Times.

Apart from this, NDTV Good Times has several other food cum travel shows that are more relatable to the globe-trotting Indians and have moved beyond anchors cooking behind a counter—Chakh Le India, Highway on my Plate, Around the World in 85 Plates and Fully Fed Up. "The viewer does not just want to see the food being prepared inside a studio, they also want to see the places these dishes belong to. They want to get a taste of not just the cuisine, but also the culture, people and stories surrounding them," says Monica Narula, head-food programming, NDTV Lifestyle.

It is a well-known fact that food in India changes with every milestone. And the popularity of Anthony Bourdain's No Reservations and Floyd's India on

Discovery Travel and Living is testimony to this fact. "Bourdain made it to India and tried the quintessential vada pav," says Rajiv Bakshi, marketing director, Discovery Networks Asia. Highway on my Plate explores the uniquely Indian phenomenon of dhabas, while Chakh Le India is all about regional flavours, where the anchor Aditya Bal soaks in history and trivia, rediscovers old recipes and relives culinary delights. "Talking to the locals and eating with them gives a clear cut view of the food culture of that region which helps put up a better show," feels Bal.

However, it is foreign food that best captures our attention. "When we see people having exotic food on TV, it develops an urge in you to travel to the destination. And most places are within one's reach," says Chandra, adding, "Whenever I'm anchoring I make sure I involve the locals of that particular state or country, because that helps strike a better rapport with the viewer."

When World Café Asia was first telecast on Discovery Travel and Living, it popularised sushi and sashimi even outside Japan and now with their latest venture Hairy Bikers Ride Again they plan to extend their culinary journey to more exotic locales like Morocco, Argentina, Belgium and so on. "Filled with adventure and enthusiasm, Dave Myers and Simon King travel around the world on their bikes to cook regional delicacies. Having an unconventional anchor always helps because the viewer can relate to them," says Bakshi.

Heading: Coming this November: new software to prevent vehicle theft - Indian Express
Content:
A day after a youth was stabbed to death at the Sector 15-16 traffic light, the police gave a clean chit to the two friends of the accused, who were with him at the time of the incident.

Nitin Bansal (21), a resident of Talwandi Sabo, was allegedly stabbed to death by one Vishal Sharma on Saturday. The incident occurred around 11.30 pm when the victim was travelling in his Skoda car (PB10K7177) along with two friends — Siddhak Jot and Rahul Bajaj.

According to the police, the three entered into a scuffle with three occupants of another Indica (HR03J0257) — Vishal Sharma, Vishal Dogra and Amit Soma — at the crossing. According to the police, the cars were racing against each other, with the occupants continuously passing remarks.

ASP Madhur Verma said the Indica, driven by Vishal, did not move after the signal went green at the Sector 15-16 traffic light. The occupants of the Skoda, which was behind it, confronted them after crossing the red light. Vishal, who was in an inebriated condition, took out hockey sticks and a small dagger from his car and hit the occupants of the Skoda.

Nitin was hit on his back, with the dagger piercing his heart. While the other two occupants of the Indica fled, Siddakh and Rahul beat up Vishal.

A severely bleeding Nitin was rushed to the Sector 16 hospital where he was declared dead on arrival. Vishal has been admitted to the PGI with injuries. A case of murder under Section 302 of the IPC has been registered against him in the Sector 11 police station. Vishal Dogra and Amit Somar, who were booked under Section 324 for causing injury, have been given a clean chit.

"We have recorded their statements. According to them, Vishal was the culprit. The other two were trying to stop him," said Ramesh Chander, SHO of the Sector 11 police station. He added that Vishal would be arrested once he was discharged from the PGI.

Vishal is an employee with Dell in Mohali. The incident took place when he was returning home after work. His parents are settled abroad.

Heading: A thousand turn up to elect Senators - Indian Express
Content:
After the metropolitans, Chandigarh is all set to avail itself of the facility of Vahan — the highly sophisticated software used for registration of vehicles. The software will not only expedite registrations, but also prevent vehicle lifters from registering a stolen vehicle with a new number in any part of the country.

Vahan, which is likely to be launched in Chandigarh by the first week of November, is in its testing stage these days. Officials of the Registering and Licensing Authority are being provided training at the National Informatics Centre to execute the software.

The software was launched as a pilot project in Chennai last year, after which, all metros had adopted it. A few states including Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh have already started to use the software.

With the help of Vahan, the registering and licensing authorities and transport departments of all states and union territories will be connected online, with their headquarters at Hyderabad. Any changes pertaining to the registration or the legal status of a vehicle can be accessed online through this software.

Registering and Licensing Officer Jairam said: "Vahan attempts to bring about uniformity in the registration of vehicles by issuing smart cards (registration cards), to be operational all over India. Though we are already using a software to register vehicles, as per a Central policy, this software is to be used as a nationwide mechanism for the registration of vehicles. So, we are going to adopt it soon."

According to government officials, Vahan will help provide better citizen services, monitoring government revenue, management, faster implementation of revision in government policies and instant accesses to information to any department, among others.

While implementing the software, the RLA will be required to maintain several databases including a list of vehicle-dealers, driving schools, banks, regional transport offices, makers and models, insurance companies, reasons for blacklisting a particular vehicle and jurisdiction of the concerned Registering and Licensing Office, etc.

Ques: How will Vahan work?

* Registration of new vehicle/other state vehicle/temporarily registered vehicle / consulate vehicle

* Addition/removal/continuation of hypothecation on registration card (RC)

* Change of address or transfer of owner in RC

* Any kind of alteration in the vehicle

* Renewal of registration for private vehicles and issuing no objection certificates

* Surrender or Cancellation of RC

* Temporary registration

* Issue of fresh or temporary permit, renewal, replacement, surrender, transfer or cancellation of permit

* Replacement of vehicle or change of address in permit

* Recording stolen vehicle

* Entry for black-listed vehicle

Heading: Will faith in stem cell therapy help stem ailments? - Indian Express
Content:
PANJAB UNIVERSITY SENATE ELECTIONS Results to be declared tomorrow

The Senate elections for the graduate constituency went off smoothly on Sunday, with a voter turnout of nearly 25 per cent. The 33 booths in the city polled around 10,000 votes.

The contestants kept shuttling from one booth to another and even on the D-Day, were seen wooing prospective voters. Leaving no stone unturned, they nearly dragged the voters to the booths.

The voting was held for three groups — graduate, lecturer and principal constituency. The lecturer constituency got the maximum response with 95 per cent voting taking place.

This was followed by principal constituency and the poorest was for the graduate constituency. Overall, the elections were held for 31 posts with 15 posts for graduates, 8 for lecturers and principal constituency each.

The voting, which began in the morning, concluded at 5 pm but voters could be seen dropping in till evening. The afternoon saw the maximum rush. The counting will begin on the September 23 and the results will be announced the same day.

Identity crisis

In some cases, the voters had to face problems after their election cards were not considered suitable identity cards. At DAV College, three lecturers, Niti Gupta, Vibha Sinha and Kavita Nanda, were not allowed to vote initially. They were carrying stamped papers signed by principal B S Josan, which identified them as lecturers. The issue was resolved only after the Registrar was asked to intervene.

Dinesh Kumar, contestant and lecturer at the DAV College said: "It was pure humiliation. One had come all the way from Panchkula and had to go and come back again." At SD College too, election cards were not accepted and the voters had to approach the Registrar.

Chin up

Most of the contestants seemed cheerful as they kept shuttling between booths — the idea was keep a check on bogus voting.

And most were confident of victory. S C Gupta, one of the contestants, said: "I am quite hopeful as I know that a number of people have supported me. I am awaiting the results which I expect to be in my favour".

G K Chatrath, whose daughter Anu Chatrath is a contestant, said: "Looking at the response, I am sure my daughter will win."

Happy it's over

The Director of DAV Management Committee, M L Aeri, being a contestant, the DAVs had gone overboard over the election.

The college at Sector 10 wore a festive look and lunch was organised for everyone. The teachers had been put on duty and despite it being a holiday, there was much activity.

Aeri has been trying everything — from power point presentation, SMS and emails to woo voters — and a section of the staff had been roped in to help. A teacher of the DAV school said, "It has been over 15 days since we have been campaigning." The schools as well as the college staff heaved a sigh of relief when the election was finally over.

'100% voting' at SD College, but one lecturer in hospital, another abroad

At the SD College, which claims 100 per cent voting for the lecturer constituency, lecturer Rinki Priya Bali has been admitted in the hospital since September 19. On Sunday, as the voting was on, she delivered a baby girl following a caesarean. Confirming that she is still in the hospital, her husband Pawan Kumar said: "She delivered a baby girl at 4.30 pm. She has not left the hospital since September 19". Principal AC Vaid, who made the claim of 100 per cent voting, was foxed when Newsline informed him about Rinki. Later, he told Newsline: "Rinki did cast her vote in the morning. You can speak to her husband". When contacted again, Pawan Kumar said: "I am not too sure whether she went to cast the vote or not. I was away in the morning so she might have gone on her own."

Dinesh Talwar, a lecturer at the DAV College, said: "This is surprising. Even last time, there was a bogus voting charge involving the same college."

Besides Rinki, another lecturer of the college, HK Khanna, was not in a position to vote. He is currently abroad.

Heading: On bank loan, city cardiologists start ambulance service - Indian Express
Content:
Even as there is no clarity on the use of stem cells to cure ailments, residents are apparently lured by marketing gimmicks, celebrity endorsements and emotional advertising to bank on the cord blood stem cell banking.

Deepak and Savita Thakur, a couple in the tricity, are expecting their second child. Despite a substantial chunk of money involved (on an average the storage of such stem cells requires Rs 70,000), the Thakurs have already made up their mind to go in for cord blood stem cell banking or the umbilical blood banking.

"My elder daughter, now 5 years, is suffering from leukemia. After consulting doctors, we have come to know that the matching of the stem cells between siblings is quite high. I pray to Almighty that my second child remains healthy. The stem cells stored at the time of my second delivery can be used for my daughter," says Deepak.

If the figures of the city's first such collection centre Life Cell are to believed, within two years they have registered more than 300 couples who have opted for cord blood banking. This blood is collected at the time of delivery from placenta and is believed to carry stem cells.

"People from every walk of life are getting registered with us. We have cases where there is some disease existing in the family but at the same time, there are a large number of couples who have gone in for banking by studying the pros and cons," claims Hridesh Jaiswal, Centre head of LifeCell.

While the affluent certainly find their names in the registration lists, the middle class and salaried couple too want to jump the bandwagon. To lure this profile, the centres are even offering payments in instalments for 21 years (the whole time of storage of the stem cells) with the initial payment of Rs 7,000 as the registration fee.

Even as the experts lament the hype and huge investments surrounding umbilical cord blood banking especially in the absence of a long-term research, the young couples treat it as a long-term investment.

"We treat it as an investment for our child. We wish he does not need to use these stored cells ever but just in case, we have stored the stem cells through the best technology that is available. The whole process of going in for the banking is not merely medical but also emotional," says a working mother in Chandigarh.

Ques: Is there any hope?

Prof Vivekanand Jha, PGI

"At the moment, all the claims of stem cell banking are merely a promise. It just gives us hope about a therapy that we are still are not sure about. All the claims by private banks are pre-mature as there is no study or concrete research to back the. No public sector hospital is as yet a part of the cord blood banking."

Prof Vanita Jain, Department of Gynaecology, PGI

"The whole issue of stem cell banking has lots of pros and cons and there are no clear cut answers at the moment. A lot of research still needs to be conducted to see if the banking has the future benefits as has been understood at the moment."

Heading: Panel to present report on MCM - Indian Express
Content:
Dial 09915444550 and a cardiac care ambulance will reach your doorstep-as a group of dedicated cardiologists have launched their own ambulance service in the city.

Former director general of the Army Medical Forces Gen (Retd) B N Shahi launched the cardiac ambulance carrying a coronary care response team on Sunday.

To be available in Chandigarh, Mohali and Panchkula, the ambulances will be operational from September 22. The air-conditioned ambulance has been brought with a bank loan and is currently being equipped with EKG, scanner, laptop with internet, cellphone with a 5 MP camera, portable ventilator and oxygen supply apart from the usual setup. The ambulance will also have an Emergency Medical Technician (EMT), a nurse-cum-EKG technician and an MBBS doctor.

Chandigarh PGIMER's former Additional Professor of Cardiology Dr Anil Grover has teamed up with 5 other cardiologists to launch the Panjab Remote Telecardiology Access Project (PARTAP) and Chandigarh Heart Electronic Tele-Access Kardiogram (CHETAK) for the residents of the tricity.

The new project comes after the failure of the telemedicine project for cardiac patients under "Rural Punjab Heart Attack Tele-Access Project" at Kharar and Dera Bassi Civil Hospitals.

Content:

Director Higher Education Raji P Srivastava had directed the college authorities to form a committee to look into the matter and pulled up principal Dr Puneet Bedi for failing to maintain peace in the college.

Heading: Big Bang: PU profs say no reason to panic over helium leakage - Indian Express
Content:
The District Consumer Disputes Redressal Forum has directed the State Bank of India to pay Rs 2000 for deficiency in services.

The complainant, Sanjhi Ram, deposited a Cheque of Rs 3,39,000 in the State Bank of India, University branch, in 2007.

The amount was credited to his saving account on December 5.

The said the cheque amount was obtained by the complainant as a loan from his Provident Fund Account. It was averred that he applied to the Housing Board Haryana for a flat on a prescribed form alongwith the Cheque for Rs.3,39,000 and deposited the same with the ICICI Bank, Sector 9-D, Chandigarh. Thereafter, the ICICI Bank presented the cheque in the account of the complainant on November 30, 2007, but the concerned SBI Branch dishonoured and returned the same with the memo of 'Insufficient Funds".

His application with the Housing Board Haryana was thus rejected. Alleging that he suffered mental and physical harassment, he moved the consumer forum.

In their reply, the bank stated that the cheque was deposited in the drop-box of their bank only on December 5, 2007 and not on November 29, 2007 as said by the complainant and the amount was promptly credited in the account without any delay. It was stated that the bank has acted in the ordinary course of its business and since there was insufficient credit balance in the account of the complainant, therefore, the cheque issued by the complainant in favour of the Haryana Housing Board was returned with remarks of insufficient funds. They also said the account number has not been correctly mentioned and questioned if the complainant was really interested in getting a plot, he would have first ensured that the cheque for the PF amount was received early and credited in the account before issuing a cheque in favour of the Haryana Housing Board.

The forum found deficiency on part of the bank in not crediting the amount on the same day as the cheque was deposited.

"The complainant lost a chance to participate in the allotment of flats and therefore, the bank is liable to pay compensation. The mere fact that the complainant lost a chance to participate in the allotment of flats cannot be said to be a sufficient ground to ask for compensation. It was a speculative investment to be made by the complainant," ruled the forum.

The forum added, "While issuing the cheque in favour of the Housing Board Haryana, he should have ensured that his own cheque was credited to his account before issuance of any such cheque."

Heading: For faulty TV, Philips Electronics asked to pay Rs 60,000 - Indian Express
Content:
The world's largest experiment to know the birth of the universe has come to a halt after a leakage of helium gas occurred during the beam test. According to the Panjab University professors, those involved in the experiment, the process has been halted for an indefinite time period as the repair work is likely to take time.

The entire experiment is about identifying the missing particle — Hizss Poson. Hizss Poson is responsible for giving mass to everything in the universe and once this link is found, entire details about the formation of the universe will come to light. The professors say that the helium leakage is no threat and people need not feel panic about the same.

Speaking to Newsline, Manmohan Gupta, chairperson, Physics department said: "The experiment has been halted because of helium leakage but there is nothing to panic about. Such things keep happening as it is a complex experiment."

The team from the Physics department that is involved in the experiment includes Prof Suman Bala, Prof J M Kohli, Prof Manjit Kaur and Prof T B Singh. The team has contributed in making a sub-detector named Compact Muon Spectrometer that would be used in collision of protons at a very high energy level.

The experiment to know the birth of the universe was being planned for over fifteen years but with this halt, the experiment is likely to be delayed further. The main experiment is yet to begin and it is only the testing part that is being carried out. The leakage occurred while the beam was being tested.

The project titled Compact Muon Spectrometer (CMS), a unit of the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) experiment is being conducted at European Particle Physics Laboratory (CERN) near Geneva in Switzerland.

Heading: The feeling of being all powerful blinds the ability to reason - Indian Express
Content:
The District Consumer Disputes Redressal Forum has directed Philips Electronics to pay Rs 60,000 for a faulty television set.

They have also been directed to pay Rs 5,500 as costs of litigation The complainant, Atul Grover, a resident of Sector 10, purchased a Philips 52" television for Rs 96,000 in October 2004.

After nearly two years, the television blanked out. As the company failed to repair the television set, Grover moved the forum alleging deficiency on part of the electronics company who kept him in the dark despite making repeated promises to replace the same.

Philips Electronics, in its reply, stated that a standby set was offered to the complainant, which was, however, refused by him. While denying any false promises ever made, it was pleaded that the consumer had to take the set to their authorised service centre for inspection and repair, which was not acceptable to the complainant.

The company alleged he was rather adamant that the service engineer should inspect the set at his residence only owing to which, the service engineer could not rectify the problem despite his best efforts.

The forum found that the company had admitted that the television developed certain problems and they tried to repair it, but failed.

The forum added, "It appears the television has gone beyond repair, because the spares are to be received from Singapore which were not being received as mentioned by the company, due to which it was difficult to repair."

Heading: SYL canal breached in Ambala, ‘paddy bowl’ under threat - Indian Express
Content:
A rich industrialist's son mowed down innocent people under his expensive car a few days ago. While the channels and newspapers were busy devoting airtime and print space to the BMW-II, I wondered whether money is so important a component that it makes one forget the basic lessons of humanity.

This is not the first time that a heady cocktail of youth and money has behaved recklessly with those who are lesser mortals in front of him. The Jessica Lal murder case and the Nitish Katara case are all examples of how money and power breed arrogance in the mind of the youth.

As they are aware that they can be bailed out of any offence, they lose all respect for their fellow beings.

Though the blame game will not serve any purpose, the parents in such cases should be held accountable. These children are told and taught by example that money is omnipotent; that one can buy anything with money. The heady feeling of being 'all powerful' blinds the ability to reason.

It thus becomes the duty of parents to teach their children the basic lessons of morality and humility. Keeping aside their desire to earn more and acquire more, parents should spend time with their children. Only parents can teach children how to value others and also what God has given them.

Children should be taught that money is not everything in life; the ability to treat everyone at par with oneself and respect for everyone irrespective of the social and economic status are the most valuable lessons in life.

Heading: ‘People have realised that only peace can bring prosperity’ - Indian Express
Content:
Thousands of acres of paddy and other crops stand in deep waters after the SYL canal was reportedly breached at five places under P S Naggal in the district on Sunday.

The five places near village Sarala at the Haryana-Punjab border were breached, reportedly due to poor maintenance of the SYL canal. The canal touched the danger mark when it started taking in water from the swollen Ghaggar River. The small breach between Sarala and Khaira villages has developed into an almost 60-feet-wide opening.

Reacting to the situation, Army jawans from the Engineering unit were pressed into action as a company headed by Col S K Vidyarthi was sent with the flood control equipment to plug the breaches. Residents from over a dozen villages were seen lending assistance to the administration and the Army.

The flood water has spread to the villages of Naggal, Khera, Nadiali, Ismailpur, Amipur, Badingan, Tangerian and others where the crops can be seen submerged in water.

Every year residents of villages from the bordering Punjab state allegedly breach the bridge across the Haryana border when rainwater accumulates in their villages. Consequently, the water flowed downstream and increased the level of the SYL canal during rains.

A contractor from Punjab is learnt to have incited the villagers to cut the bridge for safe flow of flood water into the SYL canal.

For the residents, their matured paddy crops have been damaged thereby causing them losses to the tune of crores of rupees. The area, known as the "paddy bowl" of the district faces the risk of its paddy being perished.

Khaira village residents, Jai Singh, Harnek Singh, Hardayal and Nirmail Singh, on the basis of their past experience, approached the SYL Canal department urging them to take flood control measures, lest their villages are inundated by the canal.

The residents feared if the water level continued to increase; it might enter their village and also the low lying areas of Naggal village. They, however, stated that they had not received any warning from the Administration about evacuation in case the flood water started entering the populated areas.

A cross-section of the residents including Joginder Singh, Amarjeet and Kirpal Singh from Naggal complained that mice holes were not plugged and water started leaking, which ultimately started taking the shape of breaches in the embankment.

Ambala SDM M K Ahuja, camping on the site since morning, said the Army had been requisitioned to plug the wide breach. He said sand bags and other construction material had been arranged for plugging the breach at Khaira village.

Heading: Card Apart - Indian Express
Content:
After a long time, the hope for peace in Northeast India has gathered momentum with the public deciding to extend their full support and cooperation to the Indian Army and other security agencies to eradicate militancy.

The security agencies have also acknowledged the increasing participation and cooperation of the public.

The Indian Army along with the police raided several militant hideouts in the region. The recent example was the joint action involving the Indian Army and Manipur Police wherein they successfully destroyed two camps of the banned militant outfit PREPAK, near Loktak Lake in Thoubal district, Manipur. The outfit was allegedly involved in planting a bomb at the Chief Minister's residence.

The locals provided key inputs about the militant hideouts and extended full support in the operation. During the operation, five militants were killed and a large amount of arms were seized.

The people have understood that only peace can bring prosperity in their lives and the region. Many civilian lives have been lost in militant attacks.

The Army believes that it is because people are fed up with the militants that they are helping the security forces to clear the undergrounds. It is a positive development and different from what happened in 2006.

It is evident from the examples of Punjab and Tripura where security agencies successfully eradicated militancy when people lent support to the security agencies. Mizoram is also on the path of peace.

The Army has also intensified their search operations to weed out militants from the region. In the past few months, the Army has managed to kill and capture many insurgents on tip-offs provided by the locals.

The demands of the different militant groups range from autonomy within the provisions of the Indian Constitution to outright secession.

Such militant movements started early after India's independence in 1947. At one point, more than 120 militant groups operated in the Northeast.

In recent years, the government has achieved considerable success in achieving stability for the region by using tactics from negotiations to military operations.

Militants in the Northeast once enjoyed popular support since they, in their formative years, voiced genuine grievances of the people such as poor governance, alienation, lack of development and an apathetic attitude from the Central government.

Even as their influence declined off late, in most of the states in the region, anti-government militants retain significant nuisance value and often indulge in successful strikes against government interests.

China is believed to have provided some assistance to groups such as the NSCN in the 1980s. The militant leaders have on record confessed to have travelled to China and secured help for their movements.

Such a nexus, if any, does not exist today as people are helping the Army to weed them out.

Heading: Admn clueless, non-AC cabs yet to take off - Indian Express
Content:
Biswaroop Roy launches the first animated cosmic energy card

Mind games. That's what Guinness World Record Holder Biswaroop Roy Chowdhury is an expert at and experiments with. Then whether it's about improving students' memories, helping them build concentration or in the latest case heal them. Having fashioned and patented "the world's first animated cosmic energy card" Roy tells us the cards reflect positive thoughts and help one remain energetic, as he takes one out from a pack of 12 and formally launches it at Rajasthan Bhavan. "It is based on neorobic exercises of mind's association and visualization techniques to tap cosmic energy," he shows the green and white card. "This becomes animated when we move the PVC sheet sideways," Roy says viewing this constant movement enables one to tap green coloured cosmic energy.

At present available at The Rajasthan Bhavan, Sector 33, "the cards are priced at Rs 200 for a set of 12 cards," Roy tells us.

Heading: Spectacular Sapphire - Indian Express
Content:
The much-hyped proposal of the UT Administration of introducing non-AC cabs in the tricity is still hanging fire. The decision to ply non-AC cabs was taken after the AC cabs received the 'not so good' response. The authorities are themselves clueless about when the service, expected to be launched in August, would begin.

Justifying the delay in implementing the proposal, Finance Secretary Sanjay Kumar said the litigation process for the same was taking time. Having no clue about the time when the non-AC cabs will start plying in the city, he said, "I have no idea when the proposal will take off."

Retracting upon the fare declared by the State Transport Authority, Rs 6 per kilometre, Kumar said that fare could be altered keeping the demand of the user and consumer in mind at this stage since it was only a proposal.

It was announced around three months ago that among the applications received by the State Transport Authority (STA) from six private companies, one that agreed to the STA's terms and conditions has been granted permission to ply the non-AC cabs. Guneet Finalese Private Ltd. in Sector 22, already into the business of taxis, was the one that was selected as one of the companies to run the non-AC cabs.

The Finance Secretary, however, said: "The in-principle agreement has been done and one company has only given its proposal but not finalised. I have scheduled a meeting to decide on this matter."

These cabs were said to not only ply within Chandigarh but also between Chandigarh and Mohali. The agreement with Punjab government has already been inked on June 4, 2008. As per the agreement made as a counter signature between Punjab and UT government, the number of cabs entering the city would be same as leaving. Nothing of similar sort has still been materialised with Haryana to allow these cabs to enter Panchkula.

"We have already spoken with the Haryana Transport Secretary for the agreement but nothing concrete has come out of it. The taxi operators can take the initiative at their own level and have held talks with the Haryana transport authorities," added Sanjay Kumar.

Heading: Mercedes buses to hit roads of City Beautiful soon - Indian Express
Content:
Threaten your men! Say you have unfaithful thoughts. Then narrate the legend of loving husbands gifting their wives sapphire necklaces to ward off extra-marital temptations. Worth a shot isn't it? Sapphire represents purity of soul and fuels harmonious relations. One is easily hypnotized by the lucid glow breathing from within the spectacular gem. Its ancient appeal traces back to various origins. In Greek 'sappherios ' refers to the ancient island of Sappherine where it was found in abundance. The Latin variation 'sapphirus ' simply means blue stone. Today, Australia leads the sapphire supply though the best are procured from Burma and the sand and grate of Sri Lanka. The supply list also includes USA, Thailand, Vietnam and Madagascar. Kashmir was once famous for its cornflower-blue sapphire.

This mesmerizing mineral (corundum) gem appears in a spectrum of colours except red. FANCY SAPPHIRE category includes colourless, green, pale-pink, yellow, violet, brown, grey and an orange-pink. PADPARADSCHA SAPPHIRE i.e, the orange-pink sapphire is the most sought after in its category, a glance is reminiscent of a tropical sunset. CABACHONS categorize the ones cut into smooth domes some of which produce 'asterism'. It is a star like phenomenon where six rays stretch across the sapphire surface, hence aptly named STAR SAPPHIRE. BLUE SAPPHIRE is the strongest and abundantly available category and is available in a passionate range of grey blue to cobalt blue. Cornflower-blue sapphire is the best in this league. Confused? Recall the stunning cornflower blue eyes of Princess Diana. No wonder, her engagement ring by Garrards was a large oval sapphire surrounded by fourteen diamonds.

Sapphires are mostly heat treated to intensify their colour. Do not be fooled by synthetic look-alikes, Iolite, and Kayanite being sold as sapphires. Insist on reports from agencies like AGTA or AGL for natural sapphires. Being highly tough and durable they also provide industrial use.

Besides its alluring beauty, sapphire was held in great esteem by various civilizations for their associated beliefs. The Greek considered sapphire as gem of Apollo and was worn by all its worshippers. Egyptians believed powdered sapphire used as an eyewash would enhance vision. Cleopatra used it as eye-shadows! The Ten Commandments were originally believed to be inscribed on a sapphire tablet. Till about the Middle ages priests wore sapphire as protection against temptation of flesh. The medieval royalty valued them set in brooches and rings to ward off envy and harm. The 13th century French valued it for protection against poisonous reptiles. Simulated blue sapphire is the Zodiac birthstone of a September born. Sapphires unanimous appeal may be appreciated in the famous Imperial State Crown of Queen Victoria which carries two gorgeous sapphires. The 422.99 carat Logan Sapphire is one of the largest faceted gem quality blue sapphire. The 182 carat Star of Bombay is another consuming example. Both are exhibited in the National Museum , Washington D.C.

Sapphires have graced the attire of royalty for centuries and can reflect most style statements any day. Silks and crepes may be used in both Indian and western wear to complement the vibrancy of sapphire. Get inspired by designers like Emililo Pucci, Marc Jacobs, Raakesh Agarwal and Manish Malhotra. Splurge in Mac for make-up. I personally love the dial hues of Baume & Mercier watches. They best complement sapphire colours.

Sapphires may be set in various accessories since they are available in most cuts. They look great solo or in various diamond settings. Blue sapphire set in kundan with polki canvases design heritage and luxury at its best. I request jewellery designers to indulge men in sapphire cuff-links and kurta buttons. It would be heavenly to see a well-designed sapphire spectrum necklace. It shall be equivalent to the navratana neckpiece in terms of wearability. Go indulge yourself in super rich colours. Rest assured, any amount you pay shall be worth for its price and value.

(The writer is a city-based researcher specialising in jewellery art and can be contacted at sameeraahaan02@gmail.com)

Heading: 57 Candles - Indian Express
Content:
With Mercedes launching its luxury AC buses in India, city residents will soon have more options of transport apart from the existing buses like Volvo. The Haryana Roadways plans to introduce this global leader into their fleet for long routes.

"We are planning to add Mercedes buses in the fleet of luxury AC buses which we had recently bought from Volvo. As we already have plans to expand the number of AC luxury buses we would certainly see the prospects of buying Mercedes buses," said K S Kalson, Haryana Roadways General Manager.

At present, the Haryana Roadways has ten Volvo buses plying on the Chandigarh-Delhi-Gurgaon and Shimla routes. Kalson added that since the Roadways is on the move to provide comfort with luxury to its passengers, Mercedes would certainly be an open option.

The fleet owners of luxury buses are already switching loyalties despite a premium pricing over the Volvo. The cost of Mercedes is said to be Rs 80 lakh whereas that of Volvo is around Rs 60-65 lakh. Mercedes is said to have the fuel efficiency higher than Volvo, stronger bodyline, better speed and a more powerful AC. "This would take care of the extra pricing. The breakeven will take more time as compared to Volvo but still Mercedes is a safer bet," said Kalson.

Mercedes-Benz entered the bus business in the country in the first week of September with the launch of its first-ever bus, a luxury inter-city coach that will initially operate on a few designated routes. Sutlej Motors Ltd (SML) of Jalandhar will build bus bodies on a Mercedes-Benz chassis produced by DaimlerChrysler India Private Limited (DCIL). The alliance will involve development, production, marketing, sales and after sales of the coaches. The DCIL will manufacture the Mercedes-Benz chassis, the body will be built by SML and then DCIL will take care of the sales and after sales.

Heading: MBA institute asked to pay for ‘unfair trade practice’ - Indian Express
Content:
The panel discussion for Screen's The Big Picture (our third edition this year) was attended by eminent personalities from the Hindi film industry who exchanged their views on various issues related to cinema. An elite panel of eight film industry professionals discussed the topic 'New, Improved Bollywood: Are we ready to take on the world?'. The panel included prominent names like writer-lyricist Javed Akhtar, actor-director Anupam Kher, actor Farooque Sheikh, writer-lyricist Prasoon Joshi, director-turned-actor Farhan Akhtar, actor Shiney Ahuja, Saurabh Varma, Chief Marketing Officer, Reliance Big Picture and Pankaj Khandpur, Creative Director, Visual Computing Labs, Tata Elxsi. They discussed film industry trends and achievements which excited an audience that comprised a combination of both film and media personnel.

After a stimulating experience for the grey-cells, it was time to hit nightclub Enigma at the JW Marriott for a grand celebration. Amitabh Bachchan cut the anniversary cake and what followed was a pulsating evening that celebrated the success of one of the film industry's most respected publications.

Several Bollywood celebrities attended Screen's 57th birthday bash and the party went on till the early hours. Film legends, popular TV artistes, dashing newcomers and popular filmmakers were all part of the celebration. The guest-list included Shatrughan Sinha with Poonam Sinha, Manmohan Shetty, Govind Nihalani, David Dhawan, Poonam Dhillon, Anu Malik, Sanjay Gadhvi, Sanjay Gupta and Madhur Bhandarkar, Kailash and Arti Surendranath, Sachin Pilgoankar, Renuka Shahane and Ashutosh Rana, Shankar Mahadevan, Pritam, Aadesh Srivastava, Sajid Khan, Lilette and Ravi Dubey and young guns like Arjun Rampal, Sonu Nigam, Himmesh Reshammiya, Luke Kenny, Purab Kohli, Nishikant Kamat, Sikandar Kher, Meera, Ronit Roy, Manasi and Rohit Roy, Sonal Chauhan, Mughda Godse, Vidya Malavade and many others.

A successful and engaging discussion on the happy developments in the film industry followed by a merry evening of glamour and glitz—it was a perfect way to bring in Screen's 57th year in business.

Heading: In the hot seat - Indian Express
Content:
The District Consumer Disputes Redressal Forum has directed a management institute to return the cheques beyond the amount of Rs 32,750 to the complainant who discontinued his studies. The institute has also been directed to pay Rs 5,000 as compensation for mental and physical harassment and Rs 2,200 as costs of litigation.

The complainant, Ramandeep Singh, stated that for an MBA course, he paid Rs 73,774 as fees for 18 months to ICFAI, Hyderabad, through its branch office in Chandigarh. For this, his mother (also the complainant) issued 13 post-dated cheques in favour of the institute and delivered the same in the office at Chandigarh in Sector 35. Ramandeep averred he attended classes for four months and thereafter left studies for which he sent a letter to the institute. Since he discontinued studies after four months, the institute was not entitled for any fees for the rest of the period because the principle of no education no fee was applicable. He, thus, sent repeated letters demanding Rs 42,516 back. In its reply, the ICFAI stated that they are not liable to return the cheques beyond the amount of Rs 32,750, as they are entitled for fee of 14 months.

The forum found that the institute indulged in unfair trade practice in the matter of not returning the cheques beyond the amount of Rs 32,750 as canvassed in the complaint.

Heading: CN & Heard - Indian Express
Content: If you love all the naach-gaana that television has to offer these days, then you would have surely caught Nach Baliye episodes back to back. The popular dance show that brought in real life couples on to stage has seen as many as three seasons on the tube. And looks like they aren't giving up. All set for Season Four, Nach Baliye producers are currently scouting around for a celebrity judge for the show. According to insider news, hottie Malika Sherawat has been approached to sit on the hot seat. And what's her take? "Apparently she's really thrilled at turning a judge for a dance show. She even suggested doing an item number as an opening act for the show," tells our insider. With 'Maan Gaye Mughal-e-Azam' sinking without trace, the lady sure is looking to be back in action. We'll keep you posted!

Heading: Stage of strength - Indian Express
Content:
Cars, cars and more cars

The fascination of Punjab politicians and bureaucrats with motorcars is well documented. Known to possess fleets of automobiles, these law and policy makers ensure that their sarkari gaddi keeps up with the times. But even by their standards, one particular principal secretary level officer, has a garage strength, which is astounding. He is known to have smartly worked his way in a manner that allows him official cars from more than a couple of departments. Till last count he had, eight official vehicles, including Corolla, Ambassador and Innova. As regards the identity of the officer, some things are best said, unsaid. But in case you are even slightly familiar with the who is who of Punjab bureaucracy, it wouldn't take you much time to zero in on this car aficionado.

Wrong side

Punjab Chief Secretary Ramesh Inder Singh is a modest, soft spoken and unpretentious man. In fact, he is a bit uncomfortable with all the spotlight, which comes to him by virtue of being the state's top most bureaucrat. But then sometimes the paraphernalia is an essential part of the official decorum. For example, recently when he was travelling in the state, his high speeding entourage comprising security and escort vehicles were slowed by a truck. Repeated honking couldn't goad the truck driver from giving way as he continued to drive in the middle of the road at his own merry speed. As the cars tried to overtake, the truck's side collided with the chief secretary's car, thereby, severely damaging it. The Chief Secretary luckily escaped without injuries but the poor truck driver couldn't, at least, the security staff ensured that he didn't.

Laymen brothers

People used to say that when American economy sneezes, India catches cold. Well, the morbid fear, which the collapse of Lehman brothers has caused in India, testifies the veracity of this aphorism. Lots of bright youngsters, from the city are working with this investment bank. While some are employed with the captive KPO centre owned by the company in Powai, others are working as ace investment bankers in various parts of the world. Whereas the Powai centre is certainly on the verge of closure, the fate of the top-notch investment bankers isn't any better either. A local boy, who went to IIM Ahmedabad, and subsequently, joined Lehman brothers' office in Tokyo called up his parents to convey his pitiable state. He had been given an excellent salary package, but the high cost of living in Tokyo ensured that he barely saved a dime, which means that ten days later when he returns to India, he would come with an empty bank account. We sincerely hope that the worst is over. But perhaps it is time to introspect and look at the merits of that age old adage- It is never good to place all your eggs in one basket.

All roads lead to 10 Janpath

Congressmen and women across the country seem to have a one-stop solution for all their problems - Sonia Gandhi. The members of the city unit of the party unhappy at being 'ignored' and 'sidelined' by the bureaucrats could think of only one remedy - going to 10 Janpath to tell their tale of woes. Whether Her Majesty's magic will work on the functioning of the Administration or not remains to be seen.

The good, the bad and the ugly

Gulping down more than 10 tablets in one go, Ravinder Singh, prime accused in the Judge-bribery case, was wearing a fake smile to hide his nervousness. Every time a mediaperson came close to ask him something; he feigned a smile immediately searching for his counsel to reply on his behalf. After he was remanded to CBI custody, Ravinder quietly requested a couple of mediapersons "Please write something good about me". When asked as to what good things shall be written in his favour, he said, "Whatever you feel is good". Is there any, though?

Wah Taj!

When it was opened, around three years back, Taj Hotel did not do much to endear itself to city. Persistent reports of shoddy service, ill mannered clumsy staff and poor quality of food (especially in Coffee shop) ensured that high hopes from what is one of India's best known hospitality brands were dashed. But the hotel made up lost ground very fast. The service and quality improved drastically. Though there still are some lacunae, Taj is one of the better-maintained and efficiently run hotels in the city. A fact testified by the predilection of the high and mighty.If you have been wanting to meet Sukhbir Badal, Amarinder Singh, Bikram Majithia or any other elusive top shot, you can expect to find him at the Taj.

Heading: The Makeover - Indian Express
Content:
City's Kamal Vidrohi continues his act of life, theatre, in Germany

The sun's blazing rays are mellower, the nip's slowly enveloping our mornings and nights, there's a cheer in the air and new colours and fragrances fill the senses. It's time to come home. To be among the circle of friends, relive memories and feel at home. All this and more keeps inviting theatre director Kamal Vidrohi back from Germany year after year. Here for a rub-a-ru organized by his old colleagues and friends of Theatre Age and Theatre for Theatre, Kamal walked down memory lane and talked about the constant in his life, theatre, which he continues to live and breathe in Germany, where he now lives.

Kamal is among the few who gave Punjabi theatre in Chandigarh a concrete ground, provided people with hope and cultural activity in the dark days of terrorism and began in Chandigarh, a far-reaching and unique concept of terrace theatre. It was here that he learnt the art and science of theatre. The ecstasy overshadowed the agony and Kamal decided to pursue theatre head-on, leaving his job at the Secretariat for a degree in theatre and involving his entire family in the process. "I studied Western theatre and Bertolt Brecht extensively and from folk to realistic to experimental , I only focused on the positives and growth on stage,'' Kamal has his own theatre group in Germany, People's Act Theatre which comprises both Indian and German actors. Having worked closely with Brecht's students and his wife, Kamal feels the barriers of language cease to exist on stage, though he is now comfortable with German too. Kamal adapts many Indian plays into German and also stages Punjabi plays there, "our movies, clothes, culture…it's all a big hit back in Germany, and so is theatre,'' Kamal has been associated with people like Ajmer Aulakh, Balwant Gargi, Shiv Kumar Batalvi and created magic on stage with plays like Paagal Khana,Madi Da Diva, Lahu Di Lau…

"Theatre in Germany is big and people spend huge money to come and see theatre. It's very professional and scientific and I stage popular and meaningful Indian plays which have a universal appeal , without changing my style,'' Kamal says Mohan Rakesh's Aaadhe Adhure was a big hit with the audiences back there. What's best, adds the director, is the fact that even sponsored shows there are ticketed and so theatre people have enough room to follow their passion and earn their living, which is still a tough proposition in India. "The idea is to reach out and keep the act alive,'' Vidrohi sums it up aptly.

Heading: 22 years on, beautician on wheels continues to roll - Indian Express
Content:
Fashion design students from the city are working to change the way Ravana dresses up this Ramleela

Till sometime back, this motley bunch of fashion design students had issues like Fall-Winter trends, annual collections and the season's colour palette to discuss and deal with. That was until this came along. Project 'Dashagriva' has seen Rashmi, Pankaj Prabhakar, Sunil Rana, Arka, Ashish, Robin and Amanraj, all students of the Inter National Institute of Fashion Design (INIFD) get down to serious research, one that's seen them pore over history books at length!

"Dashagriva is another name for Ravana," their faculty guide Anuradha Thakur is quick to point out. With Diwali not too far and the Ramleela ready to be staged soon, is that what's got them to delve into Ravana's life, we ask? "Actually we are giving Ravana a makeover," tells second year student Rashmi as she powers up a laptop to take us through a quick presentation. Just then Ravana walks in! Dressed in a rather flamboyant outfit, he trudges in with classmates Ashish and Robin to help him through. "That's the way we see Ravana dressed at the city's oldest Ramleela staged in the Sector 17 Parade grounds each year," INIFD's centre manager Nimisha Gupta pitches in with more details as we eye the dress. The present design is very amateurish - black outfit with golden tassles and sequins all over. This year, however, Ravana will slip into something new.

"I have been enacting the role for many years now. The outfit has remained the same and I was really taken by surprise when told that the students want to change it for the better," admits Sunil Sharma who steps into Ravana's shoes at the Sector 17 Ramleela each year.

"It's not that we want to make him look completely out of place but we are looking to add some aspects of history to the outfit," explains second year student Amanraj as he flips open a file that holds in designs and sketches defining the new look. To streamline the project, the students were given singular responsibilities like research, putting together a story board, a presentation et al. "And it's been such a learning experience. Did you know that Ravana excelled in 64 art forms?" questions Amanraj. The students also got to learn the lesser known albeit nicer aspects of Ravana's personality. "Like he was a huge devotee of Lord Shiva and that's something we are incorporating in the new outfit," adds Ashish.

Going by the research put in, the students have decided to stick to three colours. Rashmi takes us through. "We are using gold to depict royalty, red for energy and black to depict him as a ruler," she lists out. Also since it's royalty they are dealing with, the students have decided to use equally rich fabrics like silk, tissue and velvet. "To make the outfit more meaningful, the students have designed an emblem depicting Kuber to be used on the belt while the 64 art forms will be depicted on his cloak," faculty guide Thakur adds. That apart there will be extensive use of dabka, aari and applique work. "It's a lot of work but we are really looking forward to the final result," chorus the students who don't want to stop just with Ravana. "Given a choice we would like to make new outfits for everyone playing a part at the Ramleela," they answer in unison. That's Generation Y for you!

Heading: Police hold meeting with Ram Lila organisers - Indian Express
Content:
The clock strikes 5 in the morning and Renu, a beautician by profession, begins her day. She munches breakfast and prepares for yet another packed day ahead.

"Let's see, wax, strips, thread, cream, scrub, brush, towel, packs, cotton, tweezers, scissors, grooming sets," Renu ticks her checklist as this beautician "on wheels" cannot afford to miss a thing.

"In 1986, I began my work after training with Salochna Ahuja," says Renu as she is all set to take the first call for the day. "I'm off to Sector 34," she smiles adding "how wonderful it is when passion grows into a profession. But there are no holidays and it's not as easy as it looks."

Life has been tough for Renu who has been looking after her siblings ever since her parents passed away. "Time has just flown by, scooting from one client to another, waxing, threading, massaging. I've seen their children grow up and get married," she recalls as nostaglia runs across her face remembering all the brides she has prepared for their special day.

But why a parlour on wheels? "This is more personalised, it's like I have a monopoly on it, and I am my own boss. I don't like too many people around," she takes charge. Her mobile keeps beeping with clients calling and booking. "Sometimes, the days are stretched and I just stop and have a sandwich for lunch," she says. On her way to Panchkula, Renu asserts, "Two hours, and I'll be back to sector 34 and then 7."

From 5 in the morning till 5in the evening, Renu is in demand. An old-fashioned beautician, we watch her roll up her sleeves, tie her hair back and neatly lay out her tools. Everything in place, she goes about her work with effortless ease and speed. Few match the speed at which she waxes, or does the sarson ka tel and besan wattna, or for that matter, light up your face with a homemade fruit pack.

"Secrets of the trade," she winks, as she tells how her job has made her a better listener, more patient and blessed.

"People have so many stories to tell, and then you realise that all they need is someone to listen."

But where does she vent out her stress? "Once I'm home, I hit the gym." This is something Renu never misses. A quick channel surf, light dinner and it is goodnight for the beautician as she prepares for another heavy day.

Heading: Shraadhs no longer a deterrent for shopaholics - Indian Express
Content:
Keeping in view the coming festive season and the approaching Ram Lila, senior officers of the UT Police department held a meeting with the organisers of various Ram Lilas across the city on Sunday. The Ram Lilas are starting from September 29 in almost all sectors, colonies and villages of the city.

In view of the series of bomb blasts in Ahmedabad, Banglore, Jaipur and recently in Delhi, and keeping in view the prevailing security concerned and to sensitise the Ram Lila organisers, UT SSP SS Srivastava held the meeting. The organisers were advised to strictly adhere to the instructions issued by the Chandigarh DM, like timing of starting of the shows, availability of fire fighting equipment, sand bags, construction of morchas, crowd control arrangements, liaison with local police, appointment of volunteers, sitting arrangements and installation of CCTV cameras.

Heading: Be role models, Somnath urges legislators - Indian Express
Content:
With times, the superstition attached with shraadhs seems to have lost significance. Till a few years ago, people would refrain from making purchases during this time. Now, the trend has changed and is clearly reflected in the new shoppers who do not let religion inhibit buying. Shoppers across city continue to buy clothes, jewellery, consumer goods and even property.

Traditionally, the shraadh period was considered inauspicious to buy anything — from clothes, to cars, gold and property. The trend has clearly shifted now and experts find little difference in the shopping pattern of the residents in this period.

Many believe that the presence of an educated and young population in the city is the force behind this change whereas others claim that with the new generation being the spending decision-makers, shopping during these days now is nothing abnormal.

"The effect of shraadh is coming down every year with little difference in the purchases. With the increase in working members in the family, all days are considered same by the consumers and no superstition is attached to the shraadh," says Anil Talwar, one of the oldest jewellers in the city.

"God has made all the days equal and I do not really believe that some kind of bad omen is attached to a particular period. I recently bought gold jewellery for a wedding next month," says Rakesh K Narad, a city resident.

There has been no dearth of activity in the real estate industry in the tricity either. "There has been a certain shift in the perception of people especially when we compare the residents of Chandigarh with those in Delhi and the NCR. As we have real estate projects in both the regions there is hardly any difference noticed among the city residents as compared to residents of Delhi NCR who follow the shraadh days more stringently," says RS Bullar, vice-president, ATS Infrastructure Ltd.

The property consultants agree that the sale or purchase of properties goes on at its normal pace with a slight fall of around 20 per cent only. "The mindset of people has changed. The sellers want best price for their property and the buyers want properties at the most affordable prices irrespective of the time of the year," says property consultant Mangat Rai Baboota.

Dealers across the city have also felt the impact. Many say the purchase period is no longer restricted to the festive season that starts only with the beginning of the navratras.

The traders are happy. "There has been an impact but not significant. If on a normal day, we would sell 15 consumer goods, these days nine to ten units are being sold," says Akshit Gupta, owner of Gupta Electric Company in Sector 22. Rajneesh Verma of Lakshmi Infotech dealing in computers, says, "It has to do nothing with caste or religion... right now a laptop is ready for delivery to a Hindu customer."

Heading: Members resolve to have code of conduct for legislators - Indian Express
Content:
Expresses concern at growing indiscipline, misconduct of legislators; says self-cleansing needed

Lok Sabha Speaker Somnath Chatterjee has expressed deep concern at the growing indiscipline and misconduct of members of legislative bodies in the country. "All of us have been facing unruly conduct of members inside the House, disrupting proceedings and forcing adjournments. It is a matter of great concern that the malaise still remains acute,'' he said.

Delivering the inaugural address at the four-day "73rd Conference of Presiding Officers of Legislative Bodies in India", organised by the Haryana Vidhan Sabha here today, Chatterjee said it was with great sadness that in April he had to refer the names of 32 members of the Lok Sabha to the House Committee of Privileges for examination, investigation and report on the disorderly conduct in the House.

He said later he withdrew his decision only after being assured by various party leaders of full cooperation in smooth running of the House. "Unfortunately, despite such assurances, disruptions of the House proceedings and forced adjournments due to unruly behaviour of members have continued,'' he regretted.

Somnath Chatterjee advised legislators to be role models, both inside and outside the House. He said an impression has gained ground that people with access to political power, resource and influence can remain out of the reach of the legal process.

The Speaker cautioned the legislators that the July 22 incident during the debate on the motion of confidence moved by Prime Minister Dr Manmohan Singh in the Lok Sabha should never be repeated. "I constituted a seven-member committee on July 26 to inquire into the complaints made by the three members who are alleged to have been approached with the offer of money for their votes. The report of the Committee is awaited and necessary action will be taken,'' said Chatterjee.

Chatterjee said it was a matter of pride that India was the largest democracy in the world and significant progress had been made through the working of the parliamentary system of governance. "However, there is a now a growing disillusionment and despair among a large number of people because of the manner of functioning of the elected representatives and the representative bodies,'' he added.

He regretted that the disturbances in the House had led to delay in transaction of business, waste of time and money.

Commenting on the current political scenario, Chatterjee regretted the fact that "today's political atmosphere, characterised by intolerance, divisiveness, confrontation and disrespect for dissent, is increasingly corroding our socio-political system".

"The use of money and muscle power in the electoral process and the criminalisation of politics has vitiated the political environment in the country,'' he said.

However, not all is lost yet. The Lok Sabha Speaker said the House had demonstrated its resolve to cleanse itself. "This process of self-cleansing must continue, should there be any such occasion in future,'' he suggested.

Heading: Democratic system chronicled - Indian Express
Content:
The 73rd Conference of Presiding Officers of Legislative Bodies in India, which began here today, placed on record its deep sympathies for the innocent people who lost their lives or were grievously injured in the recent serial blasts in Delhi and various other parts of the country.

Expressing distress over the trail of death and devastation caused by the recent floods in Bihar and other parts of the country, members of the conference conveyed their heartfelt condolences to the bereaved families.

A condolence resolution was also passed, expressing deep sense of grief and sorrow at the demise of several speakers and deputy speakers who at one time or other were members of the fraternity of presiding officers.

Lok Sabha Speaker Somnath Chatterjee inaugurated the conference at the Haryana Vidhan Sabha. Speaker of Haryana Vidhan Sabha Dr Raghuvir Singh Kadian was unanimously elected as the co-chairman of the conference.

The session concluded with the adoption of a resolution urging the leaders of all political parties and other stakeholders to take immediate steps, including the formulation of a code of conduct based on a wide consensus, to ensure that legislators adhere to prescribed norms of conduct in the House.

Sukhdeo Rajbhar, Speaker of Uttar Pradesh Vidhan Sabha, initiated the discussion on the subject.

Heading: ‘Capt’s expulsion a dangerous trend’ - Indian Express
Content:
Lok Sabha Speaker Somnath Chatterjee evinced keen interest in the exhibition "Indian Parliamentary Democracy: A Journey Forward" at the Haryana Vidhan Sabha complex, organised as a part of the ongoing conference of presiding officers and secretaries of legislative bodies in India here. Somnath Chatterjee wrote in the visitors' book: "I must complement the Lok Sabha Secretariat for organising the very informative and well-laid exhibition in cooperation with the Haryana Legislative Assembly Secretariat. This provides a saga of important chapters of our history, including our freedom struggle. Let us all resolve to strengthen our parliamentary system for the sake of the country and the people. I hope many of our citizens will also come to see this."

The exhibition has been organised by the Parliamentary Museum and Archives Division of Lok Sabha Secretariat and Haryana Vidhan Sabha Secretariat, in collaboration with the Directorate of Advertising and Visual Publicity.

The exhibition provides details on total number of sittings, questions, etc, held in the Haryana Legislative Assembly since its inception.

The exhibition, spread over 13 sections, traces the growth and development of democratic traditions in our country beginning from the ancient times to the modern parliamentary institutions. It lays special emphasis on the democratic heritage in ancient India, including the Rig Vedic and Buddhist period, Indian freedom movement, Constitution of India and working of the Indian Parliament, with the help of photographs, write-ups, charts and press-clippings.

The exhibition also showcases the Indian federal system and the legislative set-up in different states of the country, with particular emphasis on the legislative activities in Haryana. The voices of Mahatma Gandhi, Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru, Dr B.R. Ambedkar and Subhash Chandra Bose can also be heard.

The scanned copy of the Constitution of India can be accessed by visitors on the computer. Also available are programmes on ancient democratic heritage, legislative reforms, Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha and state legislature buildings.

Heading: BSF, Corps of Signal, RCF and Eastern Railways move into semis - Indian Express
Content:
Speakers of various state assemblies largely view the expulsion of former chief minister Capt Amarinder Singh from the Vidhan Sabha as a "dangerous" trend with far-reaching repercussions. The Indian Express spoke to some of them and this is what they had to say:

* Speaker of Uttar Pradesh Vidhan Sabha Sukhdev Rajbhar (BSP): "The House has to exercise restraint when it comes to unseating an elected representative. To expel is wrong. This way there will be no opposition. The majority will rule. However, the proceedings of a previous House can be taken up by the present House if it was left pending earlier."

* Karnataka Assembly Speaker Jagdish Sattar (BJP): "The expulsion of an elected representative sets a wrong trend. Such cases involve a lot of constitutional complexities. The opposition will find it hard to say or survive if such a trend picks up."

* Chairman of Karnataka Legislative Council Viranna Matikatti (Congress): "The expulsion sets a wrong precedent. It should not happen if the opposition has to act freely."

* Rajasthan Deputy Speaker R.N. Bishnoi: "The merits of the case have to be gone into. It's now for the court to see its constitutionality."

Somnath refuses to comment

Lok Sabha Speaker Somnath Chatterjee said the matters of the previous House can be taken up by the present House if they are left pending and the MLA has been re-elected to the next House. Normally, matters are not left pending. When asked to comment on former CM Amarinder Singh's expulsion, the Lok Sabha Speaker said, "The matter is now before the consideration of the court." One of the points that the Congress is raising to condemn the expulsion of the former CM is that the issue which led to Amarinder's expulsion pertains to a matter of the previous House and, therefore, cannot be taken up by the present House.

Heading: CM surveys flood-hit areas - Indian Express
Content:
Border Security Force (BSF), Jalandhar defeated Roomi Eleven by 3-1 while Corps of Signal managed to overcome a spirited CRPF Delhi side 8-7 by sudden death in a high-voltage game to cruise into the semi-finals of the 17th All India Baba Farid Gold Cup Hockey Tournament being played at Government Berjindera College Hockey Stadium on Sunday.

BSF opened its account in as early as the seventh minute when right full back Swaranjit Singh converted the penalty corner. However, their joy was short-lived as Jaswinder Singh of Roomi Eleven leveled the score through a penalty stroke in the 12th minute. After ten minutes, Sushil Kumar of BSF put the lead in the lead when he converted a short corner into a goal in the 22nd minute. Just before the whitsle of the first half, Parkash Karak hit the final nail into the Roomi Eleven's coffin by scoring the goal off a field goal stop.

Roomi tried their best to reduce the margin but BSF thwarted their challenge and the second half failed to produce any goals. In the end, it was BSF who had all the smiles on their face.

Meanwhile, in the second quarter-finals, both Corps of Signal and CRPF were tied 1-1 at the end of full time. In the tie-breaker also, the team were locked at 2-2 and the game finally moved into sudden death. Corps of Signal held on their nerves and came out as winner by 8-7.

RCF Kapurthala also reached the semis when it snuffed out the challenge of Punjab & Sind Bank Academy by 3-2. Parveen Kumar scored the opening goal for RCF when he converted penalty corner in the seventh minute. RCF scored tow more goals while Punjab & Sind managed to pull two goals to make it 3-2.

In the last quarter-final match, Eastern Railways edged out Pakistanteam by 5-4 to move into the semis. The match was decided by tie-breaker after both the team were tied at 2-2 at the end of the match.

Heading: Tarush claims U-16 badminton title - Indian Express
Content:
Chief Minister Bhupinder Singh Hooda said on Sunday that he has made an aerial survey of the areas falling in Yamuna belt and damage caused by the flood waters would be assessed and victims compensated. The CM launched several health facilities and other public utility projects costing around Rs 11.5 crore at various places in Karnal district.

He inaugurated a 25-bed community health centre at

Nissing which has been constructed at a cost of over Rs 2.24 crore. This CHC would cater to the needs of medical services to around 65,000 people of 51 villages. This CHC would also

provide round-the-clock emergency medical services to

the masses.

Heading: Mane, Vineet anchor BPCL win - Indian Express
Content:
Kenneth Wong failed to carry his impressive form into the final as he was beaten by Tarush Sharma who clinched the boys' Under-16 singles title in the 20th Yonex Chandigarh State Badminton Championship being organised by Chandigarh Badminton Club at the Government Model School, Sector 23 on Sunday.

Tarush defeated Kenneth Wong by 21-18, 21-9 in a one-sided match to walk away with the title. Meanwhile, top seed Kevin Wong took just 27 minutes to dispose off the challenge of second seed Tushar Khurana by 19-21, 21-2, 21-17 to win the Under-10 singles title.

In the Under-13 singles final, Robin Saini put up a brave fight before bowing to second seed Chaitanya in an evenly contested match by 22-20, 21-23, 21-13.

Damandeep snuffed out the challenge of Arshia Sethi 15-21, 21-17, 21-17 to bag the girls' Under-10 singles title. Meanwhile, Daaman Sharma and Mehak Sood paired up to claim the girl's Under-13 doubles title by beating the duo of Kashish Singh and Sanya Sethi by 21-3, 21-5. Mehak Sood overcame her doubles partner Daaman Sharma by 21-3, 21-6 in the girls' Under-13 singles final to claim the title. The day belonged to Mehak Soodf as she won her third title of the day when she defeated Shreya by 15-21, 21-17, 21-19 to lay her hands on the girls's Under-16 title.

Heading: Organic is the way - Indian Express
Content:
A Captain's knock of 44 runs and a hurricane unbeaten knock of 77 runs by Vineet Indulkar helped BPCL edge out HPCA by 25 runs in 15th All India J P Atray Memorial Cricket tournament for PEARLS Trophy being played at Sector 16 Cricket Stadium on Sunday.

Batting first after being put in to bat, BPCL posted 168 runs for the loss of two wickets in 23 overs. Vineet Indulkar hammered the ball all over the ground to raise up his half century. His knock of 77 runs came off just 54 balls with the help of nine hits to the boundary and two towering sixes. His stand of 84 runs for the second wicket with Onkar Khanilkar powered BPCL towards a commanding score. Onkar's 26 runs from just 15 balls consisted of four boundaries and one huge six. Skipper Vinayak Mane also displayed his skills during his innings of 44 off 56 balls.

In reply, HPCA were bundled out for 143 runs for the loss of five wickets in 23 overs. Sangram Singh hit a swashbuckling 51 runs off 56 balls but others failed to put up decent scores and HPCA lost by 25 runs. Kiran Adhab bagged three wickets for 31runs for BPCL. In this way, BPCL gathered four points from the match.

Meanwhile, MRF managed a narrow six run victory over Moody ICL in another exciting match played at DAV School, Sector-8, Chandigarh. Put in to bat, MRF put 164 runs on the score board for the loss of eight wickets in 30 overs. Sambha Siva (38 runs) and Venogopal Rao (30 runs), the chief contributors for MRF, were involved in a third wicket stand of 45 runs off 55 balls. For ICL, Vikash Chauhan claimed three wickets while Rohit bagged two wickets. Chasing the target, ICL were cruising merrily at 137 for 2 when MRF bowlers struck and snapped four quick wickets to leave the side reeling at 158 for 6. The tailenders failed to hold on for long and ICL lost by six runs. Rajinder Bisht scored a pugnacious 42 runs off 36 balls with the help of seven fours and one six. Pankaj Joshi (37) and Vishal (26) were other notable contributors. For MRF, Nyas claimed three wickets and was adjudged the Man-of-the-Match.

Brief Scores:

BPCL: 168 for 2 in 23 overs (Vineet Indulkar 77 no, Vinayak Mane 44, Onkar Khanilkar 26); HPCA: 143 for 5 in 23 overs (Sangram Singh 51, Kiran Adhab 3 for 31)

MRF: 164 for 8 in 30 overs (Sambha Siva 38, Venogopal Rao 30, Vikash Chauhan 3 for 33, Rohit 2 for 35); ICL: 158 for 6 (Rajinder 42, Pankaj Joshi 37, Vishal 26, Nyas 3 for 27).

Heading: The healthy prescription - Indian Express
Content:
The hazards of pesticides have brought managers, doctors and engineers to hoe and plough. While some have chucked in their high-profile jobs, others have two strings attached to the bow.
This bunch of natural farmers have paved the way for many to follow

Thirty-two-year-old Gaurav Sahay from Panchkula, who has done his MBA from New York and chemical engineering from Regional Engineering College, Jalandhar, jumped on the organic farming bandwagon after quitting his Rs 12-lakh per annum job in information technology sector in Gurgaon.

"All I was doing was making money. I was like a machine. One day I gave up everything and decided to grow crops, naturally," he says.

"It has been a drastic change from my desk job in an air-conditioned swanky office, but I love every moment of it," he says.

The health hazards of conventional farming and excessive and unchecked use of chemical pesticides have changed the mindset of many like Gaurav. "Organic farming is the most sustainable form of agriculture. It is eco-friendly and safe," says Gaurav, who started farming on a one-acre farm a few months ago, but plans to expand to three acres. "I want to adopt natural farming as my full-time profession," he says.
