"I was just lost. Middle-class people like me do not have any contact persons in the US," said Mahajik. He then approached Jayant Dhulap, a reporter in the Marathi daily Loksatta.

Dhulap sensed the nervousness and urgency in Mahajik's voice. Mahajik had approached several eminent persons in Alibaug. He didn't get any help from people at his hometown. Dhulap remembered one Cathy Shreedhar, who had associations with Thane-based Shramjivi Sanghatna. Shreedhar (73) is now a member and office bearer of the Unitarian Universalist Association in (UUA) the US. The UUA is a religious association that is engaged in social and human rights work in the US.

After collecting Shreedhar's phone number and e-mail address from Vivek Pandit of the Shramjivi Sanghatna, Dhulap sent the details of the students to Shreedhar and faxed a copy of the correspondence also. In no time, he received a message saying that Shreedhar would personally go in search of the five students. With the help of the police and disaster management service, Shreedhar launched a manhunt for the five Indian students.

A day after Ike hit the island— September 16,2008 — Shreedhar called up Pandit and told that the five students were yet to be traced and search would continue. However, after four hours of intense search with the help of the US Police, Cathy could give a good news that all the five students were safe. The US Police rescued the students after their search using helicopters and shifted them to a safe place before the situtation in the island turned grave. However, on the same day at 10.30 pm, Shreedhar could arrange facilities for the students to call up their family members back in India, thanks to the emergency communication system. Mahajik, finally, got the call from his son Rohan who later said how Ike helped him gain practical knowledge in hotel management during disasters.

When contacted, Cathy Shreedhar said, "I just kept calling many people until I got the right person. After I could trace the children, I insisted that they should speak to their family back in India. I'll do anything for anybody during these kinds of situations. However, a call from (Shramjivi) Sanghatna was so special that I had left everything to search for the missing students."

Heading: Activists empower disabled voters - Indian Express
Content:
Slum dwellers who have encroached upon land belonging to the erstwhile Mafatlal Company as well as government land in Kalwa will have to brace themselves for demolition following a Bombay High Court order on Friday. The court has directed the Thane Municipal Corporation to demolish those structures that have been constructed on the premises of Mafatlal Company as well as the government land which is over 60 hectares. The order comes in the wake of Thane Inspector of Land Records' report which stated that the actual demarcation of boundaries at the ground level is yet to be completed due to the presence of encroachments on Mafatlal land and partly on the government land. Assistant government pleader GW Mattos submitted before the court that the demarcation cannot be done unless the encroachments coming in the path are removed. Justice RY Ganoo accepted the state government's contention and directed the TMC to demolish those structures on Monday. The court, however, did not entertain the slum dwellers plea seeking a stay on demolitions and adjourned further hearing to September 30. The encroachers contended that the TMC would have to follow the procedure laid down under the Bombay Provincial Municipal Corporation Act. However, the court turned down this plea on the ground that TMC was not doing its statutory duty even though the court had directed earlier that the encroachments be removed. According to the slum dwellers there are around 9000 structures. However, Mattos pointed out a 2003 report filed by the TMC stating that it had removed around 21,000 structures from the Mafatlal land. Mattos stated that apparently all these were reconstructed following demolition. However, only those structures which are coming in the way of demarcation would be demolished on Monday.

The court observed that directions for further demolitions would be decided later. The court had ordered a sum of Rs 15 lakh to be paid by the Court Receiver to the Thane Police Commissioner as expenses towards making extensive bandobast for removal of encroachments in November 2003. TMC, too, claimed Rs 18 lakh as charges for demolition. The court, however, sought for documentary proof of the expenses incurred based on which the court would give appropriate orders later. The High Court, last year, had upheld Maharashtra government's claim on more than 25 hectare of land from Mafatlal Company's erstwhile Mafatlal Engineering Industries Ltd thereby restraining the latter from selling it for paying dues.

Justice Roshan Dalvi had further directed the discharge of the court receiver appointed for the government land and also imposed a sum of Rs 10,000 on Kotak Mahindra Bank Ltd towards cost for the government.

"The financial institutions did not take the care and caution required from them as public bodies and Mafatlal breached the provisions of Land Acquisition Act and the Land Revenue Code by mortgaging the land," the order had said. The order came after the state government moved the court two years back to stop the sale of land resumed by the government which Mafatlal had mortgaged to various banks and financial institutions that had advanced loans to the company. Following the liquidation of the erstwhile industry in 1999, the financial institutions, including Kotak Mahindra Bank Ltd filed suits in the High Court for recovery of dues and got a court receiver appointed for the company land including the plot which was resumed by the government. When the court receiver made an application for selling the land, the court directed the Thane Inspector of Land Records to survey the land in 2003 which was when the government came to know about the deal.

Heading: Edison Challenge: A platform for young talent to come to fore - Indian Express
Content:
Despite existing laws on the right to accessible polling locations, people with disabilities are unable to exercise their franchise during elections.

However, with the Lok Sabha elections round the corner, activists for disability rights from across the country — 40 non-governmental organisations along with 15 Human Rights Law Network (HRLN) lawyers —congregated in Mumbai for the launch of a nationwide campaign. A two-day seminar to provide information to people with disabilities about their voting rights as well as facilities that exist to enable them to vote with ease kick-started the campaign.

Representatives from Kashmir, Kerala, Madhya Pradesh and many other states participated in the seminar, except the hilly regions where elections for the general public is itself an issue."

As per the conservative estimate, seven per cent of the Indian population is disabled which is a sizeable number. However, scant regard is given to them both by the political parties and the government when it comes to implementing Supreme Court directives to enable them to vote.

Elections have come and gone but each poll leaves a familiar aftertaste for the disabled - denial of their basic right to vote due to inadequate arrangements and facilities," said Rajiv Ratouri, National Director, HRLN. Disability right groups have laid down various strategies for the campaigns in their states.

"In the year 2007, in his letter to the Supreme Court, the Election Commissioner had given an assurance that all the necessary arrangements will be made.

He had also issued notices to all the state election commissions to implement the law. We have filed right to information application to monitor the work in progress. At the national level we have urged individual state NGOs and human rights activists to file RTIs and Public Interest Litigations," said Ratouri.

According to the Bombay High Court orders and other high courts, every polling booth should have ramps, Braille for visually impaired to cast their votes. Persons with disabilities will not be required to stand in queues, disabled voters will be allowed facility of a companion of their choice to assist them in entering the booth and in casting their vote and assistance should be provided by the staff on duty to escort the voter on a wheel chair inside the booth.

Casting one's vote takes very little time but this act has great ramifications on the disabled - it is all about being visible and being involved about the issues that affect them, and finding elected officials who would make our inclusion and participation in society a reality," said Nilesh Singit, coordinator, Disability Rights Initiative.

Heading: Petroleum shop robbed in broad daylight - Indian Express
Content:
The competition will assess innovations, potential impact of ideas, quality of presentation of students

In an effort to help provide solutions to some of India's pressing issues, the General Electric (GE) has launched an all India science and engineering contest — the GE Edison Challenge — inviting participation from the science and technology students from across the country to 'test the power of their ideas'. Aimed at tapping the best science and engineering talents, the competition will gauge innovation and novelty, feasibility of ideas, potential impact of the ideas, commercialisation and quality of presentation of the students.

The programme invites the students to provide innovative solutions in four different areas. The students can prove their skills in designing a self-cooling engine that's an efficient truck diesel engine, an early disease detection system which is rapid and accurate —with accuracy greater 90 per cent— and diagnoses TB in the early stage, and a mystery train which is actually a communication device that will capture all essential knowledge about a train that is passing by.

The programme will also have a category in which students can design a home energy solution that can reduce power consumption by the household appliances like television sets.

Dr Guillermo Wille, managing director, John F Welch Technology Center (JFWTC), Bangalore, that is organising the competition said, "We feel that this contest will provide an opportunity to students to shape tomorrow's technologies. This contest will provide invaluable exposure and insights into the real world of engineering and research, where problems are far more complex and multi-dimensional."

The final round of the competition will be held at the JFWTC in Bangalore on November 6 and 7. According to the organisers, participants will vie for a prize of Rs 5 lakh and will have an opportunity to interact with eminent jury members, including leading scientists and engineers in the industry. "It was very clear from the very beginning, when the GE set up its R&D centre in India, that the talent in the country is simply outstanding. Today, the best and brightest in the country are innovating for the world," Dr Willie said.

Heading: Blast victim identified after 2 months - Indian Express
Content:
Four unidentified men robbed a shop dealing in petroleum products and also a franchisee of Western Union money transfer services. They entered the shop carrying a weapon and threatened the three employees inside. They pushed the employees into a cabin, locked them up and asked them about the money.

The employees told them that money was kept in a safe in the other room. They disconnected the phone wire and escaped with the cash. According to eye witness they escaped in a black Maruti car. "There have been several robberies in the area, but this is the first time an incident has taken place in broad daylight," said assistant police inspector Aroon Hazare. "The robbers forgot to take the phone wire and as soon as they left the employees called up their proprietor who rushed to the spot. Since they had taken the keys with them, the cabin's lock had to be broken. We don't think the men could have been locals as they came by car. We are combing the area for the car ," added Hazare.

Heading: SIMI training: If caught, call media - Indian Express
Content:
It is almost two months since the July-26 serial blasts rocked the city. For most of the affected people, life has slowly returned to normal.

They have mourned their dead, performed the last rites and accepted whatever fate has offered. All this when a corpse lay in the Civil Hospital mortuary, awaiting the last rites.

On Sunday evening, however, his mortal remains were consigned to flames. The body of Vipul Bhikhabhai Patel (31) was identified by his brother Mukesh when he saw his photograph published in a local newspaper.

Vipul had lost touch with his family members after he had married a girl from the slums of Raipur Chakla. Their divorce five years later left Vipul all alone, said Inspector Ajiz Sindhi.

"Vipul had last visited his family about a year ago, and was living alone. This is why no one tried to look for him. He was not employed and had taken to drinking after the divorce. He occasionally visited his family when he needed money. His brother identified his photograph in a local daily," said Sindhi, who accompanied Mukesh for the identification of the body. The body was immediately taken for the last rites, as it had decomposed.

Vipul was brought dead to the hospital from the blast site at Hatkeshwar Circle in Ramol area. Dr Jayanti Satapara, the Police Surgeon and CMO said: "We have had no visitors to identify or claim the body ever since it was found. In special cases, we have waited for relatives for much longer before disposing of the corpse. We were waiting for the police report, as the case was under the crime branch."

Heading: Saffron brigade flexes muscle against AMC demolition of roadside temples - Indian Express
Content:
It Appears perfectly natural for the parents of an alleged terrorist to approach human rights groups, or call the media to project their side of the story. But the Ahmedabad police believe it could easily be a ploy to put pressure on the police and mould public opinion, as they were tutored in the SIMI training camps.

The Detection of Crime Branch (DCB) of Ahmedabad police, the investigating agency in the case, said on Sunday that SIMI ideologue Safdar Nagori had himself conducted special training sessions for the members of the organisation about the working of mediahouses and how they could be used for their benefit.

"Nagori has a master degree in journalism and mass communication from a prominent university and understands the media industry inside out. He, along with Usman Agarbattiwalla, who also had done a course in journalism, used to conduct these special sessions during the SIMI training camps," said Joint Commissioner of Police, Ashish Bhatia.

During the training camps, Bhatia said, they were taught that when caught, they or their family members should immediately seek help from the media and NGOs. "This, with an intention to put cops under pressure and mould public opinion," he said.

Recently, the family of Abdul Subhan Qureshi alias Tauqeer, the alleged mastermind of the Ahmedabad and Delhi serial blasts, went on television with statements such as "hang my son if he is guilty" soon after he was named. Bhatia said, "It makes for good reporting, but can even be a Trojan horse."

He added, "We have statements of SIMI activists in our custody who were briefed during training camps about the importance of building public pressure on the authorities through media."

Investigations by the Ahmedabad police had revealed that SIMI training camps were organised at Halol near Vadodara and Wagamon jungles in Kerala.

"Along with mountaineering, swimming, rock climbing, pistol firing, map reading, motorcycle riding and swimming, these members were also trained on how to mislead the police investigation if caught and approach human rights organisations and media using relatives, friends and other contacts to put pressure on the police," DCB said.

SIMI activists from Gujarat, Maharashtra, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Jharkhand, Karnataka, Kerala and Uttar Pradesh had attended these camps.

Heading: Modi will stay in Gujarat, says BJP - Indian Express
Content:
About ten years ago, the Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation (AMC) had tried to remove a roadside temple near Delhi Darwaja for widening the important city road. But thanks to the furious "public reaction" it evoked, the authorities had to beat a hasty and humiliating retreat. The temple still stands tall. The road remains as it was.

The then municipal commissioner, B K Sinha, had ordered the demolition of a small temple built in a garbage dump behind Jamalpur flower market. He had to face the ire of the trishul-weilding Vishwa Hindu Parishad (VHP) and Bajrang Dal men who stormed AMC's Gandhi Hall when a general board meeting was going on. Sinha had to be evacuated through the backdoor of the Mayor's office. The temple was restored and expanded further.

On September 18, the AMC removed a few roadside temples to make way for the Kankaria Lakefront Development Project. The saffron brigade went on a rampage and ransacked offices of the mayor and standing committee chairman on Saturday to register their protest over the demolitions and demand for restoration.

The question is, will the temples be restored, or, for a change, the AMC will have its way? Only time may tell. Against this, part of a mosque near Jamalpur char rasta was demolished by AMC after persuading the trustees.

Also, poet Vali Gujarati's tomb was razed by an irate mob in March 2002. The AMC never cared or dared to restore it. AMC acted quite firmly while razing a mosque near Paldi Bhattha, which was restored after rioters had demolished it. No one talks about it anymore even as the saffron brigade accuses AMC of going soft on mosques and dargahs.

The AMC's tryst with development has been fraught with such incidents and every time, it has lost face despite adopting tough stances. Kankaria lakefront is just a beginning. There are over a dozen roadside temples and a dargah that come in the way of Bus Rapid Transit System. The AMC will have to face major protests or compromise on development.

The VHP, which has accused the AMC of targeting temples only, is demanding restoration of the demolished temples. It has threatened to launch an agitation if the demand is not met. It has pointed out that a number of dargahs are obstructing traffic in Narol, Sarkhej, Danilimda and Behrampura areas, "which the BJP can't dare to touch". Its city general secretary Ashwin Sharma has termed AMC's demolition of temples a matter of shame for the ruling BJP.

"Nothing doing," says AMC standing committee chairman Asit Vora. "Whatever roadside encroachments come in the way of development projects will have to be removed. The VHP's demand for restoration is their own issue. Nobody has approached us so far," he said.

Meanwhile, Mayor Kanaji Thakor has said that the matter would be "left for the municipal commissioner to decide about the future course". "We have been discussing about providing alternative sites to them (temples) and ask the municipal commissioner to find a way out," Thakor said.

Heading: Generation Y ready to welcome Navratri with open arms - Indian Express
Content:
BJP has sought to put to rest all speculation about Chief Minister Narendra Modi's shift to national politics in the near future. Senior party leader and former party president Venkaiah Naidu has clarified that Modi will complete his tenure as Gujarat CM before taking up any new responsibility in New Delhi. Modi was reelected as Gujarat CM in December last year.

"One should be sure that Modi will complete his tenure as the Chief Minister of Gujarat and he has plans to take the state to greater heights," Naidu told reporters after chairing a meeting of the party's election management committee on Saturday.

Naidu's statement appears to be aimed at addressing the concerns of the BJP allies in view of their apprehensions following the Godhra aftermath.

There is an apprehension in the BJP that bigger projection of Modi would hamper its search for new 'friends' essential for the party to strengthen the National Democratic Alliance (NDA) ahead of the Lok Sabha elections.

When asked if Modi would be at South Block or North Block in the probability of an L K Advani-led regime coming to power after the Lok Sabha polls, Naidu said, "He would neither be in the North nor in the South. He would be in the West, in Gandhinagar. He has to fulfil his responsibility as the Chief Minister of Gujarat."

Speculation was rife that Modi will be brought to Delhi before or after the Lok Sabha polls. Modi's profile in the party has grown ever since he led the saffron party to a third consecutive victory in Gujarat, a state that is described as BJP's Hindutva laboratory.

The Hindutva poster-boy of the party has gained prominence in the recent months and had even made a special intervention on the political resolution of the party in the recently concluded National Executive in Bangalore. "We are determined to carry on the battle, both against terrorists and those who stop us from fighting terror," said Modi on the occasion.

Modi's suggestions and interventions formed a major chunk of the final resolution of the party in the three-day conclave. Kick-starting his Vijay Sankalp rally in Bangalore last week, Advani had projected Modi as an example for others in the fight against terror.

Modi is also slated to address a series of anti-terror rallies organised by different BJP state units that began with a public meeting in Delhi on Saturday.

The Gujarat strongman is projected by the party as an answer to UPA's alleged 'soft handling of terror and terror elements' and 'indecisiveness in taking steps to ensure National security'.

Heading: ‘Road’ to creation: NID students learn lessons from street artisans - Indian Express
Content:
With Navratri just nine days away, youngsters are busy preparing for the festival and concerned parents are trying to make sure that their children are safe.

Navratri generally becomes a platform for the young crowd to meet and make friends. However, the festival along with its usual fervour also acts as an agent of depression, peer pressure, sexual worries, social rejection and monetary problems for the young minds.

"Youngsters have a huge craze for Navratri. They want to look good and enjoy the festival to the maximum. The ones with fewer friends and limited budget undergo a stressful period, as they have limitations to enjoyment. We often get cases of depressed individuals who cannot enjoy Navratri like their peers," says Jigar Shah of Mind Management, a counselling centre in the city. According to Shah, ugly incidents during the festival often lead to depression in majority of the girls. Cases of sexual abuse or exploitation are high due to which girls develop a fear psychosis.

"I never had the confidence to go for a dandiya ras with my friends. I had a fear of not being able to dance properly. I had some inferiority complex about myself. I never moved out of the house during Navratri. After getting the counselling, I was more confident to accept myself the way I am. This year, I am taking classes from a dance instructor of Sanban Group. I am ready to dance and enjoy with my friends," says Sangita (name changed).

Parents are often under more pressure than the kids themselves. Excessive parental control is often seen as a reason for many youngsters to break rules.

"Generally, parents are more traditional. The generation gap and sometimes the identity crises between the parents and children often lead to communication problems. The more conservative parents coerce their kids for small things. This makes them rebellious. I believe parental counselling and behaviour therapy is equally necessary," says Dr Mahesh Panchal, a city psychiatrist.

Navarati has almost become synonymous with promiscuity and abortions in the city. Although the scenario hasn't changed much, the rate of abortion has certainly gone down to an extent.

The city-based gynaecologist, Paras Shah, explains, "Today's generation is smart and aware of sex and its consequences. The use of contraceptives is wide among them. The fad of emergency contraceptives has risen considerably, but then complications are always there. Sex education is vital for youngsters."

According to Dr. Mahesh Panchal, parents should be open-minded. Often the hesitation among parents and children to discuss sex issues leads to less information among youngsters. "The youngsters should be told the difference between sex and emotion. The girls need to be on the guard and manage emotions well. The youngsters, due to peer pressure and the fad of considering themselves 'cool', indulge in sex without knowing its implications. Although the festival has been stereotypically considered a meet-up joint for youngsters looking for fun, the training centres for garba and dandiya in the city are thriving to promote the festive spirit in every generation. The training institutes welcome people from all age groups. The training starts one to two months before the festival. The students spend anything between Rs 300 to 3000 to learn various dancing styles viz. Ras garba, Dodhia, Poniya and Kathiyawadi.

"Every year, we receive many entries for training. But this time, we have a large percentage of non-Gujaratis coming in for classes. Even the corporate sector is taking keen interest in training their employees for the event. It is fad among NRIs to learn new styles of dancing," says Chetan Dave, instructor in Panghat Performing Arts.

The 10-day festival is an occasion for youngsters to flaunt their best. An average person spends about Rs 15,000 to 20,000 for the costumes, accessories, training classes and passes to their favourite dandiya joint.

Heading: Govt extends Amrita Patel’s tenure as NDDB chief - Indian Express
Content:
The National Institute of Design (NID), Ahmedabad, is the country's premier design institute. Sophistication, technology, elegance — it has got everything. But when it comes to creativity, NIDians are game to hit the road in its pursuit.

On and off, you might spot an NID student on the pavement outside the Kochrav Ashram in Paldi, sitting by Ishwar Solanki, a bamboo craftsman, while he is busy crafting something.

While most of the time it is due to interest, at times it is out of a compulsion placed by the craft documentation course that every student at NID has to undergo after studying a craft.

Solanki is proud of it.

"NID students keep coming over to learn from me. Sometimes they offer me money also, but this being an art I don't take any," he says.

While Solanki makes a living from making bamboo items such as show pieces, mats, baskets, furniture and huts on order, he has about five to six NID students every two months who come to study his art.

Similarly, Suresh Kataiwala who lives on the roadside outside Gujarat College has students learning intertwining designs from him.

Meera Narula, a student of Textile and Apparel Designing who has been to the artisans to study the craft says: "My course coordinator had referred these bamboo artisans for a comparative study of the lifestyle and techniques followed by them at different places where the craft of warp twining and Chik making is practised. After seeing their work, I had asked them to teach me their technique and offered a reasonable price. I got a miniscule model made for my understanding."

Faculty members at the institute believe in making the modern designs and contributions relevant to the local artisans. Aditi Ranjan, a faculty member at the institute says: "While we have documented around five to six hundred crafts, a few individual artisans' profiles have also been studied. We refer our students to study these artisans, as we feel it is necessary for our students to be sensitised to the rich tradition and technique of craftsmanship. At times, modernisation wipes out valuable traditional techniques. We need to save them before they are wiped out of the streets as well."

Heading: Seven blast suspects still at large: Gujarat Police - Indian Express
Content:
National Dairy Development Board Chairperson Amrita Patel's tenure has been extended by another five years. The board acts as a policy-making body in the dairy sector.

The Cabinet Committee on Appointments (CCA) has approved the extension and a notification regarding this would be issued soon, a government official said.

Patel's five-year tenure was to end on November 30 this year. This is the second extension that she is getting.

Patel was handpicked by Verghese Kurien, father of the White Revolution, to head NDDB in 1998. But both fell apart after some time and later, Kurien was removed from the chairmanship of Gujarat Co-operative Milk Marketing Federation (GCMMF), the body that owns the Amul brand.

After becoming the head of NDDB, Patel initiated some changes by forming joint-venture marketing companies with state-level cooperative dairy federations.

She also allowed cooperatives to expand their operations, as Amul, which was earlier confined to Gujarat, started selling milk in Delhi where Mother Dairy is the leader.

Heading: Cops order sandbag pickets for police stations - Indian Express
Content:
Even as the Delhi Police added names of Zia-ur-Rahman and Mohammed Shakeel to the list of accused in the Delhi and Ahmedabad blasts cases, the Gujarat Police say that at least seven more unidentified suspects are still at large.

"We know that they are Hindi-speaking and may be from Uttar Pradesh," said Ashish Bhatia, Joint Commissioner of Police, Detection of Crime Branch (DCB). He said the DCB of Ahmedabad police are in constant touch with the Delhi police. "In fact, one of our teams in Delhi is also questioning Rahman and Shakeel, arrested by the police there," he added.

Assistant Commissioner of Police, DCB, H R Muliana had disclosed on Saturday that Atif alias Bashir and Sajid, killed in the Delhi Police encounter on Friday, and Mohammed Saif, arrested the same day, were also involved in the July 26 blasts.

"The three were among the six who had stayed in bungalow number 10 in Al-Ahemadi society in Nabinagar near Narol circle," Muliana had said.

The DCB had found that the trio had used their cell phones in Ahmedabad between the second week of July and July 27.

Delhi Police on Sunday said that during interrogation, Zia and Shakeel confessed to have planted a bomb in Chief Minister Narendra Modi's constituency, Maninagar on July 26. A total of five bombs had exploded in Maninagar that day.

Sources in DCB said that Zia and Shakeel, along with some others, had traveled in an AC compartment of Ashram Express to reach Ahmedabad in June. "Atif had booked their tickets and arranged for other expenses. Later, Atif came to Ahmedabad and then left for Delhi on July 27 with 12 people," the source said.

Earlier, the DCB had released names and photographs of five suspects identified during investigation. They were Qayamuddin Kapadia, Abdus Subhan Qureshi alias Tauqir, Abdul Raziq Mansuri, Mujib Jamil Sheikh and Aalamzeb Maksood Afridi.

Heading: Waste disposal under pollution board scanner - Indian Express
Content:
The City police have instructed all the police stations to put up sandbag pickets near their gates and keep armed guards behind them. All police stations have been asked to use drop gates at all the barricade points within their jurisdiction during red alerts.

The instructions were radioed to all the 34 police stations across the city by the police control room two days ago. The police stations have been asked to comply with the instructions within seven days of the message. A sample of the drop gate has been displayed at the police headquarters in Shahibaug area for police stations to follow suit.

When contacted, Deputy Commissioner of Police, Control, D B Vaghela said the message was transmitted to all the police stations under the orders of Ahmedabad Commissioner of Police O P Mathur.

"These (the safeguards) are necessary for the protection of police stations, as they also house arms and ammunition and other valuables. These things have to be guarded in the situation of red alert," Vaghela said.

He refused to answer further queries over the issue and asked to contact Mathur, who could not be contacted.

Satellite police station has already put up such a picket along with an armed guard outside. "I think it is necessary for the safety of police stations. There are many agencies that employ such safeguards for the protection of their offices. I consider it a good initiative," said Inspector J J Patel.

Many police officers are, however, apprehensive about the order.

"Such an order sends a wrong signal among the public about their safety. If the police station itself has to be guarded, what about the safety of the citizens?" said a police inspector. He said such an order can damage the reputation of police in public mind.

"The criminals should have the dread of police in their minds. This order does exactly the opposite and gives a contrary impression," he added.

Another police inspector who is not happy with the order said, "The terrorists must have joked about the latest police order. The sandbags will become a blot on the reputation of the Ahmedabad police. It can be salvaged only by cancelling the order," he said.

Heading: Whistle Blower Scheme just an eyewash - Indian Express
Content:
The Technically Safe Disposal Facilities (TSDFs), set up to fulfil the requirement of Hazardous Waste (Management and Handling) Rules, 1989, framed under the Environment (Protection) Act 1986, have come under the scanner of Gujarat Pollution Control Board (GPCB) due to heavy rains in the state during the last few days.

The issue came to light when the police, along with the GPCB officials raided the Ashray Enterprise Trading Farm in Panoli region last Monday, on charges of it being a dumping ground for solid wastes from the Ankleshwar Industrial estate.

V R Gadge, Regional Officer GPCB, Bharuch, said the waste material samples have been sent to Gandhinagar for a detailed analysis.

B R Naidu, Zonal Officer Central Pollution Control Board, Vadodara said: "The TSDFs have been constructed to dispose of solid waste generated by industries in an environment-friendly manner."

As per rules, the industries are required to store all the solid waste generated inside their premises for a period of 90 days during the rainy season. Also, a makeshift arrangement like a shade with a cover over it, is constructed near the TSDF to temporarily store the waste. But as it happens, storing solid waste for nearly three months is proving to be an expensive affair for the 'not-so-green' industries in Gujarat.

At present, there are seven operational TSDFs in Gujarat catering to about 18,00,000 MT of solid waste, with four more being developed.

Narendra Bhatt of Bharuch Enviro Infrastructure Limited, said: "We have witnessed a clear rise in dumping cases during the rainy season."

Gadge added: "If we find solid waste dumped on un-designated sites, we immediately send the samples for finger printing to trace the source. The industries must make arrangements for the mandatory 90-day storage."

Heading: Raw deal for differently-abled in job sector - Indian Express
Content:
It seems that the Whistle Blower Scheme put in place by the Gujarat Pollution Control Board (GPCB) has failed to live up to its real purpose. Under the Whistle Blower Scheme, introduced in December 2005, any organisation or individual, who provides authentic information on illegal disposal of effluent by any industry, is to be given a monetary reward ranging between Rs 1,000 and Rs 5,000. However, only one reward in nearly three years has put GPCB's method of implementing the system under scanner. The issue came to light after GPCB, in reply to an RTI query, stated that in little less than three years, only one person has been awarded. Paryavaran Mitra, an organisation working on environment issues, which filed the RTI, termed the scheme a mere eyewash. Mahesh Pandya of Paryavaran Mitra said: "GPCB started this scheme under a directive from the High Court. There are several cases of vigilant and alert citizens catching illegal disposals. However, none of these individuals are getting reflected in GPCB's database."

Taking serious note of this, the Gujarat Information Commission directed the GPCB to issue public notices in all major newspapers relating to the particulars of the Whistle Blower Scheme so that the public is aware of the system. The notice must also specify that in order to stake claim to the reward, the concerned citizen/organisation should state that the information is being provided under the Whistle Blower Scheme.

Heading: BCA, police spring into action ahead of Irani Trophy - Indian Express
Content:
Only about 25 per cent have found work for themselves and are economically independent

"I wanted to be a professor in a university. But a minister told me that no university would take me just because I was blind," said Bhaskar Mehta, who worked hard to become the Disability Commissioner of Gujarat.

There are 10,45,500 differently-abled people in the state at present, amounting to 1.9 per cent of the total population. Of this, only 25 per cent are employed. The reluctance of Indian recruiters in employing the differently-abled has worsened their condition in our country.

The central government has reserved five per cent seats for them in government and public sector jobs. Private sectors have also reserved three per cent for them. But these reserved posts usually lie vacant. Last year, the Gujarat government had sanctioned 5,200 self-employment loans to the differently-abled. The Gujarat Minority Finance Development Corporation had given them a loan of Rs 1 crore and 25 lakh. But their number in big companies did not rise.

"The Gujarat government has been working hard to give amenities to the less privileged people. I have requested the education minister to ensure that out of every 300 people employed in colleges, there should be at least 10 differently-abled lecturers. The secretary of Science and Technology has promised that any software required for their training will be provided," said Mehta at a seminar organised to discuss employment opportunities for the differently-abled.

Private sector companies are growing swiftly in the state, but the number of job opportunities for the differently-abled has not increased.

"Disability remains a stigma. But we are ready to employ anyone who has the required skill, irrespective of his disability. We have 11 visually challenged and 10 hearing impaired," said Meenu Bhambhani, CSR Manager of Mphasis.

Shanti Raghavan, Founder and Managing Trustee of EnAble India, said, physically challenged people can work anywhere as far as things are accessible to them. People with cerebral problems should be given brain work. Visually impaired people should be given more office jobs and paperless activities. Mentally ill people have a high level of skill, but are often underestimated. A job where data entry is done is suitable for them. Developing confidence in them is vital, she added.

Jayaram Balsubramanium, whose vision is low, said: "I am a Chartered Accountant. I agree that this is a field of numbers and graphs, but there are options such as taxation, revenue or legal advising where I can work. But whenever I appeared for interviews, I was asked casual questions and turned away. At times, we are exploited at work place. We are not given the entitled salary. We also have to suffer ruthless behaviour".

"Companies need to have respect for their disability. They are educated and trained to perform certain jobs," said Raghavan, adding, "People with disabilities are trained in skills according to their interests such as computers, language, data entry, personality enhancement and the likes".

There is three per cent reservation in educational institutes for the differently-abled. But accessibility to schools is often a drawback in their development.

"We do not have special schools, but have made arrangements in normal schools for them. Classes for them are held on the ground floor, and half-an-hour extra is given to them to complete the exams. In rural areas, we organise camps to find out the disabled people and give them facilities according to their disability," said education minister for state, Ramanlal Vora.

Heading: ‘Top VMC officials involved in land scam’ - Indian Express
Content:
The Baroda Cricket Association (BCA), along with the city police, has made strict security plans ahead of the Irani Trophy match between Ranji Trophy Champions Delhi and Rest of India.

BCA has earmarked an amount of Rs 2.45 crore taking the security scenario of the city into consideration.

"We have installed 30 Closed Circuit Television system (CCTVs) in the stadium to ensure maximum security. Several other measures have also been taken," said a BCA official.

The Irani Trophy match will be held between September 24 and 28 at the Reliance Cricket Stadium in Vadodara.

Mahendra Singh Dhoni and Mohammed Kaif arrived in Vadodara on Saturday. However, Sachin Tendulkar has decided to opt out of the match to recover from his elbow injury.

The batsman has been advised a week of rehabilitation to recover completely from the injury.

Heading: Fake currency racket kingpin in Bangladesh, says SOG - Indian Express
Content:
High-level inquiry committee formed; VMC asked to maintain status quo on the entire issue

Bharatiya Janata Party Legislator Yogesh Patel has accused top officials of the Vadodara Municipal Corporation (VMC) of being involved in a land scam to the tune of Rs 300 crore.

Patel has sent a letter to Chief Minister Narendra Modi regarding the issue. A high-level inquiry committee has been formed to look into the matter and the VMC has been asked to maintain a status quo on the entire issue. Modi's principal secretary K Kailashnathan will head the inquiry, Patel said.

According to the letter, the city's timbre market, popularly known as Lakkadpitha, caught fire several times between 1960 and 1970. Taking the safety of the local residents into consideration, the authorities decided to shift the entire market to a different place outside the city.

"As per the decision, 25 lakh sq ft of land was purchased in Danteshwar, which is in the outskirts of the city. Sixty three timbre merchants were given 8 lakh sq ft of land to run their business. The remaining 17 lakh sq ft of land was given to Baroda Timbre Association Co-operative Industrial estate. VMC had bought the land from the farmers for Rs 6,34,375. However, in 1984, the farmers approached the court and an additional amount of Rs 68 lakh was paid by the VMC."

However, Patel has alleged that many of the timbre merchants have not let off their ownership rights at Lakkadpitha and are still operating from there. Moreover, not only did the VMC fail to make formal land documents, it did not take any steps to relocate the timbre merchants in Danteshwar.

"In 1997-98, one Jayanti Panchal of Narayan Housing Finance Company managed to change the use of land in the records available with the Vadodara Urban Development Authority and collected money from 49 timbre merchants through cheque," Patel alleged.

When contacted, VMC commissioner M K Das said: "All the details in the case have been submitted to the inquiry committee. The matter has been taken up by the standing committee as well as the general board several times."

Heading: City to have two more railway flyovers - Indian Express
Content:
Sometime back, the Vadodara Special Operations Group (SOG) had arrested a few operatives of a fake currency network bringing in bogus currency from Bangladesh via West Bengal. Following that, an SOG team headed by Sub-Inspector A D Parmar conducted a joint operation with the West Bengal Police in West Bengal to nab the kingpin.

However, the alleged kingpin of the network, Mohammed Ikram Ali Sheikh, probably crossed over to Bangladesh. The SOG team returned home recently, empty-handed.

"It looks like the accused crossed over to Bangladesh. We could not arrest him. But the fact that counterfeit notes are coming from Bangladesh has been established," said Inspector Karim Polra of the SOG.

Earlier, Mohammed Nazrul Sheikh (22) and Abdul Majid Sheikh (32) were arrested at Vadodara Railway Station with crockery and other items purchased with fake notes. During the course of investigation, SOG had found that Mohd Ikram Ali Sheikh from Baghmara Village in Malda District had given the notes to the two for circulating them in the country. The duo had around Rs 1 lakh in the form of 500 rupee notes, sixty thousand of which were fake.

Heading: Dahej-Bharuch SEZ expected to begin soon - Indian Express
Content:
In order to tackle the choc-a-bloc traffic that is generated at bottleneck junctions of the city, the Vadodara Municipal Corporation (VMC) along with the Western Railway, has prepared a proposal for the construction of two more railway flyovers at Kalali and Soma Talavdi.

The project, with an estimated budget of Rs 57 crore, comes under the Jawaharlal Nehru National Urban Renewal Mission (JNNURM). Three more railway flyovers are already under construction in Vadsar, Jetalpur and Navayard.

The increasing road traffic causes serious hindrance to the rail traffic as well. The frequency of the traffic in these areas is about one lakh vehicles per day, while there is one train passing the line every three minutes. If we keep the railway crossing gates closed for a longer time, the road traffic suffers. Thus, the railway flyovers are the only option to avoid such situations," said Suhas Kumar, Divisional Railway Manger (DRM).

"The Western Railway has already identified over 40 such spots in the city which require an alternative to maintain the free flow of traffic. Some of the spots have already got the sanction. The Western Railway is eager to have more railway flyovers to ease the traffic," Kumar added.

K B Jaiswal, additional city engineer, said: "We have prepared a Detail Project Report (DPR) which will be submitted to the state government for the sanction."

Heading: India must explore alternative energy to overcome energy crisis - Indian Express
Content:
With the construction of Dahej-Bharuch broad gauge expected to begin next fortnight, a new approach in the Indian Railways is quietly changing the sector.

The conversion, from the narrow gauge railway line, is being done on Private-Public Participation model with the help of Special Purpose Vehicles dedicated to cater to railway freight traffic from the proposed Dahej Special Economic Zone (SEZ).

Suhas Kumar, divisional manager, Western Railways, said the Private-Public concept has worked out well and will not only reap benefits for private players investing in the transportation, but also railways.

Giving details about the major stakeholders of the project, Kumar said Bharuch Dahej Railway Company Limited (BDRCL) was formed in 2005, after a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) was signed involving the Railway Vikas Nigam Limited (RVNL), Gujarat Industrial Development Corporation (GIDC) and Gujarat Maritime Board (GMB). "GMB was involved because Dahej has port facilities," said Kumar.

Private players were roped in later with investments coming through equity shares. "The major shareholder in this project is RVNL with Rs 25 crore in investment which forms about 29.5 per cent of the total investments made along with both government and private players," said Kumar. Other private players include Dahej SEZ, Adani Energy, Gujarat Narmada Valley Fertilisers Corporation Limited (GNVL), Birlas, Jindal and Hindalco industries.

However, it took two years to actualise the investments, as payments from some of the private players were not coming through. "Finally, the MoU was signed on January 2007 and all the paper work was in place on June 16, 2008," said Kumar. On the other hand, Kumar said that unlike political decisions of narrow to broad gauge conversions, the Private-Public model takes less time. "RVNL tendered for construction in June. The work would begin from October as monsoon recedes by then. It would be completed by March 2010," he said.

Meanwhile, Kumar added that the railway track would be extended till the dock to bring the freight from the ships. Two local passenger trains would also be introduced for the workers of SEZ. These trains would run twice a day, he said.

Heading: Cybercrime expert to educate MSU engineers on ‘Gen Next Terror’ - Indian Express
Content:
"Apart from nuclear energy, other alternatives also need to be developed," says nuclear scientist Dr M R Srinivasan, member of the Atomic Energy Commission while in conversation withANUPAM CHAKRAVARTTY;Excerpts from the interview:

Ques: According to a paper presented in a recent conference, the electricity generated in India is lower than the total primary energy in the country. Where do you think nuclear energy stands in this context?

Of the total energy consumed in India, 25 per cent is produced from cow dung and firewood, while 75 per cent is produced from coal, petroleum and other hydrocarbons. About 40 per cent of this 75 per cent is used for electricity. Nuclear energy is important in the context of society's dependence on electricity. As compared to India's 40 per cent, the ratio of electricity to total primary energy is around 60 to 70 per cent in countries like Norway and Canada.

Ques: Apart from nuclear energy, other alternatives such as wind energy have not been explored completely. Is going nuclear the only option left?

Wind and other alternatives have been explored. I would say that these non-conventional and comparatively cleaner forms of energy lack consistency in production. However, Gujarat and Tamil Nadu have been forerunners in developing these forms of energy. I would say that apart from nuclear energy, other alternatives must be explored equally.

Ques: In one of your papers, you have also talked about hydro initiative, targeting the year 2017. Could you elaborate on it?

Hydro initiative belongs to the time when the large dam projects were proposed to produce hydro-electricity during the 1960s. However, we were unable to keep up with the pace of the growing population and their energy requirements. There was a need to develop the existing coal and thermal power resources. Moreover, we could not plan dams for the rain-fed rivers, as there were drought threats. Rivers in the Northeastern states such as Arunachal Pradesh and Sikkim, and north Indian states such as Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand are good sources of hydroelectricity. Even as Sardar Sarovar Narmada Nigam Limited is considered to be successful, Medha Patkar and other members of the Narmada Bachao Andolan point at the flaws of rehabilitation of displaced people. Therefore, hydroelectricity production needs careful assessment, not just from the point of power generation but also from the perspective of those who will be affected by it. There is no single answer for the country's energy needs.

Ques: There is a plan to set up a new nuclear facility in Gujarat. What are your thoughts on this?

The Nuclear Power Corporation of India has examined new sites near the Gujarat coastline. Construction work at two units in Kakrapar near Surat is likely to begin from next year. Each unit would be producing 750 MW.

Heading: Kingfisher Airlines axes 300 jobs - Indian Express
Content:
"Hacking is my passion," says 20-year-old cyber-crime expert, Sunny Vaghela, who has been helping the Mumbai Anti-Terrorism Squad (ATS) and Ahmedabad Crime Branch ever since the Ahmedabad serial blasts and the ensuing threat e-mails sent to various organisations. Now, he is taking hacking and issues of cyber security to new heights by educating young MSU engineers from the Faculty of Technology and Engineering in Vadodara.

In a talk titled 'Gen Next Terror', Vaghela plans to address at least 30 colleges across the state, educating students about the ways in which many terrorists in the recent times have been using SMSes and emails as a weapon to spread fear.

"Since the private licencees of various mobile service providers and some of the Internet service providers have secure networks, it becomes easier for the terror operatives to send such messages," said Vaghela, an ethical hacker who was recently honoured with the Rajiv Gandhi Young Achiever's award for his contribution to police departments in Maharashtra and Gujarat.

He added: "As most of the internet service providers do not maintain a real time log of the events in form of emails and message exchanges, terrorists find it very easy to penetrate the networks and leave the same without a trace."

Vaghela said that although Gujarat is well equipped to handle terror, there is a lack of trained staff. "There are systems in place to tackle such situations, but the police need more staff to handle these machines," he said.

Meanwhile, Vaghela baffled most MSU students by hacking government websites in seconds. "Most of the government websites have loopholes. They immediately give out confidential information or allow access to the servers, which can be penetrated by anyone who knows basic hacking," he said. Vaghela has solved many interesting cyber crime cases, including a fraud case wherein an Ahmedabad based man was cheating a US-based company by sending fake emails to its customers. "I went along with the Ahmedabad Special Operations Group to get him arrested," Vaghela said.

Heading: Can the $700 bn bailout fix US economy? - Indian Express
Content:
In an effort to tide over rough weather that has gripped the aviation industry, Vijay Mallya-promoted Kingfisher Airlines is cutting 300 jobs, besides returning surplus aircrafts.

"As part of a concerted company-wide effort aimed at minimising the impact of the ongoing turbulence faced by the aviation industry, Kingfisher Airlines has, over the last six months, embarked on a series of restructuring measures designed to achieve cost savings and rationalisation and operational efficiencies," a company spokesperson said.

"As a result, a set of 300 employees have chosen to move on and have parted ways with the company and/or put in their resignations," he added.

The carrier is also returning surplus aircrafts to lessors, which are now redundant consequent upon route rationalisation, he added.

"We have already returned two aircraft and are closely monitoring aircraft utilisation," the spokesperson said.

Elaborating the reasons behind downsizing of staff, he said as the process of integration of the two entities (Kingfisher and Simplifly Deccan) nears completion, the carrier examined the complete organisation structure of the airline and mapped the skill sets of the existing talent pool with the projected talent requirements of the company.

"Many employees were counselled on their career path progression and best utilisation of their individual skill sets," he said.

As a token of goodwill, the carrier is offering all these employees a severance package equal to two months gross salary for every completed year of service (subject to a minimum of 3 months pay-out), the spokesperson said.

Kingfisher Airlines currently operates 424 domestic flights and two international flights with a total of 86 aircrafts.

Heading: Alitalia may lose license, invites offers - Indian Express
Content:
The best test of whether the government's $700 billion check will be enough to save the US economy is how much of that money flows back to consumers and companies.

Even if the government gets Congressional approval this week to buy bad debts off banks' books, satisfying some of their cash needs, the financial sector will still need to raise money -- and investors haven't exactly been lining up to help. Unless banks can find funding somewhere, they won't be eager to resume lending, and that will leave the economy sputtering.

The good news is, outside of the financial sector, Corporate America is remarkably cash-rich with some $620 billion sitting on the books of large firms, so companies should be primed to spend once confidence is restored.

But household wealth has taken an unprecedented double hit from the real estate and stock market shocks, and it could be years before consumers feel flush again -- particularly if credit conditions remain tight.

Treasury Secretary Henry Paulson argued on Sunday that opening up federal coffers to Wall Street would benefit Main Street by preventing a deeper economic downturn.

"Last week as the credit markets were frozen, the capital markets were frozen, we had a situation where American companies weren't able to borrow money," Paulson said on ABC's "This Week". "This could ultimately affect small banks, loans to businesses, loans to farmers, jobs, people's retirement."

US companies have cut more than 550,000 jobs this year, sending the unemployment rate up to a five-year high of 6.1 per cent in August. Those figures are likely to worsen in the coming months, with or without a bailout.

The housing market is at the root of the year-long financial crisis, and some members of Congress -- expressing concern that Paulson was taking a roundabout route to helping homeowners -- are expected to push for more direct mortgage assistance when they hammer out terms of the bailout legislation this week.

"I've talked to Secretary Paulson, and I've told him that while his plan is a foundation and we certainly have to do something, we need changes in it relating to housing," New York Sen. Charles Schumer said on Fox News Sunday.

Federal Reserve "Chairman (Ben) Bernanke -- no less than he -- said if you don't solve the mortgage crisis, you're not going to solve the financial crisis. We need to put the taxpayers first, ahead of bondholders, shareholders, executives," Schumer said.

Lawmakers and the administration will get the latest readings on the housing market this week as they hash out the Paulson proposal. Sales of both new and existing homes likely fell in August, according to Reuters polling data, and the pace of transactions remains near the slowest in more than a decade.

HOUSE REPAIRS

Shoring up the housing market means ensuring that would-be buyers can get mortgages, and that means banks will have to find a way to keep lending. Even before this latest bout of financial market unrest, a Federal Reserve survey of senior loan officers showed that credit conditions were tightening, even for borrowers with good credit histories.

"The US banking system needs a lot more capital," said Jan Hatzius, chief US economist at Goldman Sachs. "Capital infusions are needed to avert a sharp contraction in lending."

Hatzius said three things needed to happen in order to resolve the crisis. First, banks must figure out the true value of assets on their balances sheets; then they must raise more capital; and finally, home loans needed to be restructured.

The government's bailout plan in effect addresses the first point by establishing a price for hard-to-value assets, and Congress may tackle the third issue this week. Raising more capital won't be easy.

Lehman Brothers failed last week because it couldn't find investors. Getting $700 billion in bad debts off banks' books will certainly help, but it remains to be seen whether that will be enough to convince investors that it is safe to put their money in financial firms.

If the government's money succeeds in helping Wall Street strike a healthy balance between fear and greed, US companies are well-positioned to fund a strong recovery once they are confident that the economy is on the mend.

The Standard & Poor's industrials, a group of 368 large companies that excludes banks, insurers, utilities and transportation firms, held about $620 billion in cash and short-term securities as of June 30, according to data compiled by S&P analyst Howard Silverblatt.

That was roughly the same amount that they had in March 2007, before the financial market crisis mushroomed. Since then, companies have cut back on dividend increases, share repurchases and expansion, essentially hoarding cash because of concern about the state of the economy.

"They've got money," Silverblatt said. "They're not spending it yet."

Heading: Auctions may be only option for US bailout - Indian Express
Content:
Aviation authorities may withdraw Alitalia's license in 3-4 days if the administrator making a last-ditch attempt to sell it off does not present emergency cost-cutting measures at a meeting on Monday.

After the withdrawal of an Italian rescue bid because of opposition by pilots and cabin crew, the government-appointed administrator made a last bid to attract offers for Alitalia, although previous attempts to find a foreign buyer have failed.

Flights continued as usual but the state-controlled airline faces being grounded, and its assets liquidated, if there is no last-minute decision by dissident unions to accept the job cuts and slimmed-down contracts that the CAI consortium had offered.

"Alitalia is flying with a provisional license," the head of aviation body ENAC, Vito Riggio, said ahead of talks with the airline's special administrator at 10 a.m. (0800 GMT).

"If the (cost-cutting) financial plan doesn't arrive in 3-4 days the license will be suspended," Riggio told local radio.

Suffering from the high fuel prices and an economic downturn that have hit the airline sector globally, Alitalia has been on the brink of collapse for years as political interference and labour unrest bled it of cash and caused it to pile up debt.

Prime Minister Silvio Berlusconi, who made an election vow to rescue the airline, acknowledged this weekend that no foreign airline would step in and Alitalia may be doomed to bankruptcy.

NO OFFERS

Administrator Augusto Fantozzi invited offers of interest in all or part of Alitalia by Sept. 30, via the company's website.

"The only significant offer ... was withdrawn," Fantozzi said in the statement. "Therefore, the special administrator intends to verify the existence of other interested parties."

Fantozzi told one newspaper on Sunday that the tender would just "formalise what I have been doing -- without any results so far despite all my efforts -- regarding the main assets".

The only interest has been in Alitalia's heavy maintenance, cargo, handling and catering units and call centre. Fantozzi has contacted Air France, Lufthansa and British Airways, but said: "Nobody has stepped forward."

A tender for the state's 49.9 percent stake by the previous centre-left government attracted 11 bidders who all pulled out.

A second attempt led to Air France-KLM being picked as buyer but the deal fell down on opposition by unions and Berlusconi, who was campaigning for office and said Alitalia must stay Italian.

The media mogul returned to power in May promising to rescue it and used his influence to rally 16 investors in the CAI consortium.

But CAI withdrew its offer last Thursday and has said it will not modify its offer to make it more acceptable to unions.

The government rules out further state aid or, as some leftists propose, the renationalisation of Alitalia. Italy is already in trouble with the European Commission over a 300 million euro ($435.2 million) loan to keep the airline flying.

Heading: Nomura clinches Lehman's Asia business - Indian Express
Content:
The US government may have little choice but to use an auction process to price up to $700 billion of toxic mortgage debt it is buying from financial institutions, even if the formula has its snags.

The Bush administration sent a proposal for the unprecedented bailout to US lawmakers this weekend to tackle the nation's worst financial disaster since the Great Depression.

The government has a tightrope to walk. It wants to buy assets cheaply enough to make sure taxpayers don't lose too much money, and perhaps even make money when markets stabilize, but at a high enough price to avoid hurting banks any more than necessary.

An auction process would make sense, because it would allow the banks with the best information about the securities to determine the price, said Peter Cramton, a professor of economics at University of Maryland who has set up auctions for governments globally. But competition among sellers would prevent banks from setting too high a price.

Cramton believes a "reverse descending clock auction" is ideal in this situation. Through that process, the government would announce a target for how much of a particular security it is seeking to buy in dollar terms, and an initial buying price.

Sellers would indicate how much they would sell at that initial price, and if there were too many sellers, the government would lower its price until the amount of securities that banks are willing to sell equals the government's target.

"I've conducted dozens of these auctions for assets valued at billions of dollars, and they are extremely effective in determining a competitive market price," Cramton said.

DRAWBACKS

But there are drawbacks. A reverse descending clock auction would work best for securities held by multiple banks, but not as well for securities that are owned by just one or two institutions, Cramton said.

In that case, there would be less competition to sell. The price might be higher than the assets end up being worth, costing the government money.

Banks believe there are differences among their securities. For example, Merrill Lynch & Co Inc agreed in July to sell $30.6 billion of repackaged debt known as collateralized debt obligations at 22 cents on the dollar. That is well below where Citigroup Inc marked its securities in the second quarter. If Citi embraced Merrill's pricing levels, the bank could have another $7 billion of charges in the third quarter, Deutsche Bank analyst Mike Mayo estimated this summer.

And if auctions do attract a large number of sellers, competition may push prices down to low levels, forcing other banks to write down the value of their mortgage bonds to those prices.

Those write-downs could force banks to seek new capital, which has difficult to raise in the current environment. If raising capital proves too hard, more major banks could fail or get pushed into shotgun marriages, potentially worsening the financial crisis.

"Recognition (of losses) brings capital shortfalls into the open," wrote Jan Hatzius, an economist at Goldman Sachs, in a note on Saturday.

NEVER BEFORE

Also worrisome is the speed at which this auction will be set up, because of the complexity of the securities being sold.

"Nothing on this scale has ever been done before," said Eric Maskin, professor at the School of Social Science at the Institute for Advanced Study, who won a 2007 Nobel Prize for economics and has conducted extensive research into auctions.

But even with these concerns, such an auction can likely be done, and there may not be another choice, Maskin said.

Banks must purge bad assets before they can raise the new capital they need, or find other institutions willing to buy them. After the failure of Lehman Brothers Holdings Inc (last week, investors have grown increasingly suspicious of US financial institutions.

"You might not like the consequences of an auction, but it seems like the least of all evils," said Lawrence Ausubel, a professor of economics at University of Maryland.

Heading: CEO beaten to death in Noida - Indian Express
Content:
Nomura Holdings, Japan's largest brokerage, has reached a deal to buy the Asian operations of Lehman Brothers, a source familiar with the matter said on Monday.

British bank Barclays Plc and Standard Chartered were also said by sources to be vying for the unit. No price was given for the deal.

Lehman Brothers last week filed for bankruptcy protection after collapsing from exposure to risky securities backed by subprime mortgages.

Barclays last week struck a $1.75 billion deal to buy Lehman's core US investment banking business.

Heading: Marriott bombing: Al Qaeda, affiliate suspected - Indian Express
Content:
The Chief Executive Officer of a company was on Monday beaten to death by a group of dismissed employees inside office premises after a meeting, called to resolve dispute between them and management, failed.

L K Chaudhury, the CEO of Gradiano in Udyog Vihar of Greater Noida, was killed when the agitating workers turned violent and beat him up, Senior Superintendent of Police (Noida) R K Chaturvedi said.

As the clash erupted, Chaturvedi said, a security guard opened fire in air.

About 20 people were injured in the clashes.

Chaudhury was rushed to Kailash hospital where he was declared brought dead. There were about 200 former employees inside the premises when the incident took place.

They were dismissed two months back for some reasons and were since then protesting against it.

Heading: McCain in 'trouble' over foreign cars - Indian Express
Content:
A suicide bomb attack that killed 53 people at the Marriott Hotel in Pakistan's capital bore the hallmarks of an operation by al Qaeda or an affiliate, Pakistani and US intelligence officials said on Sunday.

Searchers combing the burnt shell of the hotel found more charred bodies after the blast on Saturday evening ignited a blaze that swept through the hotel, part of a US-based chain and a favourite haunt of diplomats and wealthy Pakistanis.

Four foreigners were killed including the Czech ambassador, his Vietnamese partner and two American Defense Department employees. An American State Department employee and a Danish diplomat were also missing, spokesmen said.

The Interior Ministry said 266 people were wounded, 11 of them foreigners, after the bomber blew up a truck packed with 600 kg of explosives including artillery shells,

mortar bombs and shrapnel.

Internal security in nuclear-armed Pakistan, a country vital to the war against al Qaeda and other Islamist militant groups, has deteriorated alarmingly over the past two years.

"The sophistication of the blast shows it's the work of al Qaeda," a Pakistani intelligence officer told Reuters.

Pakistan's army is in the midst of an offensive against al Qaeda and Taliban fighters in the Bajaur region on the Afghan border. The United States has intensified attacks on militants on the Pakistani side of the border, alienating many Pakistanis.

Militants have launched bomb attacks, most on security forces in the northwest, in retaliation. Security analysts said the militants wanted to show they could strike anywhere unless the government changed its policies.

"(It) underscores the ability of these groups to really challenge the authority of the state in the heart of the capital," said Riffat Hussein, a professor of defence studies.

An al Qaeda video, released to mark the seventh anniversary of the Sept 11, 2001, attacks in the United States, included a call for militants in Pakistan to step up their fight.

ATTEMPT TO DESTABILISE PAKISTAN

"They want to destabilise the country. They want to destabilise democracy. They want to destroy the country economically," Prime Minister Yousaf Raza Gilani told reporters.

A civilian government led by Gilani was sworn in six months ago after nine years of rule by former army chief and firm US ally Pervez Musharraf. It is also facing an economy on the verge of collapse.

The attack will be a big blow for foreign investment and will lead to further weakening of the rupee which is already trading at a record low, dealers and analysts said.

The attack was staged hours after new President Asif Ali Zardari, widower of assassinated former prime minister Benazir Bhutto, made his first address to parliament, a few hundred metres from the hotel, calling for terrorism to be rooted out.

Zardari called the bombing cowardly.

"This is an epidemic, a cancer in Pakistan which we will root out," he said in a televised address.

Army chief General Ashfaq Kayani said the army stood with the nation in its resolve to defeat the forces of extremism and terrorism.

HUGE CRATER

Saturday's attack was the worst in the capital.

The blast left a crater 24 feet deep and 59 feet wide, ministry official Rehman Malik told a news conference.

Malik showed security camera footage from the front of the hotel, which had been bombed twice before, showing a truck trying unsuccessfully to force its way through security barriers.

A small blast could be seen going off in the truck cab, apparently as the bomber blew himself up with a grenade, which started a fire. Minutes, later, after a guard tried to put out the fire with an extinguisher, the truck blew up.

Flames and smoke poured out of the 290-room, five-storey hotel located in a high security zone. Dozens of cars were destroyed and windows shattered hundreds of metres away.

Survivors said hotel security men had warned guests to move to the back of the building shortly before the bomb went off.

Most people managed to flee from the fire before it spread but a Reuters photographer saw a body lying on a top floor balcony on Sunday morning.

Malik suggested the investigation would end up pointing to al Qaeda and Taliban militants based in the Federally Administered Tribal Areas (FATA) on the Afghan border

"In previous attacks, all roads led to FATA," he said.

The United States was ready to assist with the investigation if requested, said US embassy spokesman Lou Fintor.

Some Islamabad-based expatriates were considering leaving, after shrugging off smaller blasts in the city.

"I'll be speaking to my boss tomorrow," said Steve, a Briton working in Islamabad who did not want to give his full name.

Zardari, who won a presidential election this month, left for the United States on Sunday and is scheduled to meet President George W Bush in New York on Tuesday before the UN General Assembly.

Heading: Scandal-hit Israeli PM Olmert resigns - Indian Express
Content:
US Republican presidential nominee John McCain was in for more trouble after Democrats accused him of 'betraying' US auto workers after it was reported that his family owns a fleet of 13 cars, including several foreign models.

McCain had in an earlier interview said," I've bought American literally all my life, and I'm proud." But 'Newsweek' reported that McCain and his wife Cindy, an heiress to a lucrative beer distribution company, owned 13 vehicles, not all of them from American manufacturers.

The 71 year-old Republican presidential hopeful, who earlier faced criticism over his property boasting of seven houses now received flak from the United Auto Workers union (UAW. They accused him in a conference call organised by Democrats of not telling the truth, as his family fleet reportedly includes a Lexus, a Honda and a Volkswagen.

"John McCain wasn't straight with the people of Detroit in fact, John McCain owns 13 cars, including a foreign made Lexus, a Volkswagen, and a Honda Sedan- on top of the Toyota Prius that he bragged about last year," UAW president Ron Gettelfinger has said.

" We need a President who's committed to rebuilding the auto industry in America, not a President who buys foreign cars and then lies about when he thinks autoworkers are watching," he added.

'Newsweek' said that Obama and his wife Michelle own a single car, a Ford Escape Hybrid, which Gettelfinger called a "green machine".

Heading: Mbeki resigns after prolonged power struggle - Indian Express
Content:
Israeli Prime Minister Ehud Olmert handed his resignation to President Shimon Peres on Sunday but the scandal-hit premier could stay in office for weeks or months until a new government is formed.

"Prime Minister Ehud Olmert submitted his resignation to me tonight," Peres told reporters at his Jerusalem residence.

Olmert, who faces criminal indictment in corruption probes, said earlier at the weekly cabinet session he was stepping down "in accordance with good governance" and history would judge the achievements of his administration.

Peres said he would hold talks with all of Israel's 13 parliamentary factions before formally asking a consensual faction leader to form the next government.

Olmert was replaced by Foreign Minister Tzipi Livni as leader of the ruling Kadima party in an internal election on Wednesday, raising her chances of becoming Israel's first woman prime minister since Golda Meir in the 1970s.

Olmert's spokesman Mark Regev said the outgoing premier would stay on as interim prime minister until a new prime minister was sworn in.

"There cannot be a power vacuum," Regev said.

Olmert met with Livni and promised her his full support.

The political uncertainty has dimmed even further prospects of an Israeli-Palestinian peace deal which the United States had hoped Olmert and Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas could achieve this year.

Peres will on Sunday hold talks with leaders of the four largest parliamentary factions -- Kadima, Labour, Likud and Shas -- and on Monday he will meet the remaining factions before he flies to New York to attend the 63rd opening ceremony of the United Nations General Assembly.

Olmert had promised to resign once a new Kadima chief was chosen.

If Livni, Israel's chief negotiator in peace talks with the Palestinians, gets the nod from Peres to try to form a new government, she will have up to 42 days to put together a coalition.

Failure to build a coalition would lead to an early parliamentary election.

Livni appeared to face an uphill battle to retain a political partnership with Defence Minister Ehud Barak's Labour Party.

In a snub to Livni, Barak met opposition leader Benjamin Netanyahu of the right-wing Likud on Saturday to discuss the political situation.

Political commentators said it appeared both men were trying to work out a deal for an early election and by keeping Olmert on as caretaker prime minister, freeze Livni out of the top leadership spot before a national ballot.

Opinion polls predict Netanyahu would win a general election, amid speculation he would keep Barak as defence chief.

Heading: Pak troops fire at US helicopters in N Waziristan - Indian Express
Content:
Capping a prolonged power struggle within the country's ruling ANC, South African President Thabo Mbeki announced his resignation on Sunday but denied the charge of interfering with justice in a corruption case to nail his challenger for the top post Jacob Zuma.

In a nationally televised address, President Mbeki told the nation that he had decided to resign after he was asked to do so by the national executive committee of the ruling ANC.

In an unemotional and measured tone, he "categorically" denied that he had interfered in the work of prosecutors. He said that included "the painful matter" of his former deputy.

Mbeki rejected firmly recent accusations by some members of the ruling ANC that he and the Cabinet had been responsible for the fraud and corruption prosecution of Zuma.

"Fellow South Africans since the attainment of our freedom in 1994 we have acted consistently to respect and defend the independence of the judiciary. For this reason our successive governments have respected all judicial decisions, including those that went against the executive," he said.

The president said the "central approach we adopted has always been to defend the judiciary rather than act in a manner that would have had a negative impact on its work".

He said "we have never done this and therefore never compromised the right of the NPA on whom it decides to prosecute or not to prosecute".

"This applies equally to the painful matter relating to the court proceedings of the president of the ANC, Comrade Jacob Zuma.
