Heading: One bitten, other shy - Indian Express
Content: National Conference leader Omar Abdullah was a trendsetter when he took to blogging. But in recent times, he suspended his blogging, tied down by the Valley's competitive politics. Now, the grapevine has it that Omar may soon resume his blog. After all, with the ever-expanding community of netizens, this a great way to reach out.

Heading: Aiyar books Doner news - Indian Express
Content: In a brilliant stroke, a faction of the Haryana BJP has introduced the mob as a key player for settling an internal issue, much in the style of Shakespeare's Julius Caesar. BJP president Rajnath Singh had a brush with a highly- motivated mob recently. About 50-odd youths surrounded him, demanding a tie-up with Kuldeep Bishnoi, even going to the extent of threatening a mass suicide if the BJP aligned with Om Prakash Chautala. Now, a meeting of the state executive is slated to be held at Sonepat on September 26, where former party president Venkaiah Naidu is scheduled to be present. And he is understandably worried.

Heading: Arjun’s new Man Friday - Indian Express
Content: Publicising their achievements is something that comes almost naturally to ministers. But Panchayati Raj and Development of North Eastern Region (DoNER) Minister Mani Shankar Aiyar is all set to go a step further. Aiyar is learnt to be getting a compilation done of all the newspaper and magazine reports on the Northeast that have appeared during his tenure as the DoNER Minister. The plan is to get these clippings published in a coffee-table book showcasing the "minister's involvement" in the region. Needless to add, DoNER Ministry officials are busy fishing out news clippings, particularly those with a picture of their minister.

Heading: HRD clears air on RTE - Indian Express
Content: Not many people know that Arjun Singh and Syed Sibte Razi, the Jharkhand Governor, get along very well. Razi is an old Congress mate of Singh, a self-acclaimed minority champion. Whenever Razi comes to Delhi, he makes it a point to visit Singh's 17, Akbar Road residence. So, it is not surprising that when Singh was looking for a bureaucrat to run the show at the HRD Ministry, he picked Amit Khare, a 1985-batch Jharkhand cadre officer. Khare has been Razi's secretary for the past four years.

Heading: Ringtone too bold for NACO officials - Indian Express
Content: With politicking on the Right to Education Bill continuing and the legislation failing to get Cabinet approval, fingers are once again pointed at Human Resource Development Minister Arjun Singh. The minister, however, took umbrage at allegations that he was stalling the Bill. To clarify, he is said to have written to heads of all political parties, reiterating that he was all for the RTE Bill and would do all to ensure it is tabled in  Parliament this session.

Heading: No time for film fests in poll year - Indian Express
Content: For all the kudos that the National Aids Control Organisation (NACO) may have earned for its bold campaign on promotion of condoms with its signature 'condom' ringtone, its officials seem to be quite embarrassed about the whole affair. So even as NACO advertisements on TV channels belt out the "jo bola wahi sikandar" tagline to promote openness about contraceptive usage, officials at NACO are seen switching their phones to silent mode to avoid much noise and "embarrassment" owing to the condom ringtone on their handsets.

Heading: An elephant for Laura Bush - Indian Express
Content: With just about two months to go for the annual film festival, the Directorate of Film Festivals was desperately trying to augment its strength to make the necessary arrangements. DFF director was aggressively poaching on officers working in other media wings of the Government to get the work done. But in a sudden move last week, the Government decided to effect a change at the top level of DFF, bringing the director to the PIB. That has also put paid to the plans for strengthening the DFF for the time being. With the elections approaching, publicity for the Government is obviously much more important than organising film festivals.

Heading: Nitish reads from Lalu script - Indian Express
Content: Just the perfect Indo-US bonhomie season for Minister of State for Higher Education D Purandeshwari to address an education conclave in New York this week. The high-profile event will see the minister rub shoulders with no less than Laura Bush. Purandeshwari has taken gifts for the US First Lady, and it seems she has ensured it goes well with the current US election mood. She will be gifting Laura a wooden carved elephant prepared by the artisans of Madhya Pradesh — just the right animal to choose for the Republicans whose party symbol is the elephant.

Heading: Split over Pay panel - Indian Express
Content: Unlike rival Lalu Prasad Yadav, Bihar Chief Minister Nitish Kumar is known to be a serious and no-nonsense politician. However, during his recent visit to New Delhi to meet Nepal Prime Minister Pushpa Kamal Dahal "Prachanda", Kumar deviated from his script. Asked if he would have loved to have got an invitation from the Centre to participate in the official-level talks with Prachanda over water management, Kumar replied: "What loved? I continue to wink at the girl, and the girl does not reply."

Heading: Armed Forces vs babus - Indian Express
Content: The revised Pay panel has come under flak from the Armed Forces over perceived anomalies in salary for the officer cadre. The service chiefs have already decided that the revised pay will only be disbursed after all anomalies are rectified. However, they seem to be ignoring a large fraction of the forces that are not too happy with the whole affair. Personnel Below Officer Rank (PBOR) — the soldiers who form the fighting force of the services — are concerned that due to the delay, the new salaries and arrears will not be distributed before Diwali. With accounting departments of all three forces yet to work on the new salary structures, discontentment is spreading through the lower ranks.

Heading: Sachin Pilot’s Meena votebank - Indian Express
Content: The Armed Forces have always been at loggerheads with financial advisors given their strict adherence to the written word. At a recent seminar, the Vice-Chief of Navy Staff seized the opportunity of the recent flood relief operations in Bihar to take a dig at the Ministry of Defence accountants. The senior officer said that when the Navy was called in for relief, the formal orders did not immediately come in from the Government and the financial advisors refused to release funds for the rescue work. He said that the Navy had to use non-public funds — from sources like the welfare corpus and canteen funds — to send in teams for relief operations.

Heading: Behind the scenes at NSG - Indian Express
Content: Dausa MP Sachin Pilot is the most sought-after person among Meena community leaders in Rajasthan nowadays. Unbelievable though it may sound given the long-drawn violent Gurjjar-Meena clashes not long ago, but that's how the matrix of caste and politics sometimes works. There are 24 reserved seats for Scheduled Tribes in the state. Going by how political parties work, all of them are likely to put up ST candidates — over half of them are likely to be Meenas — for each of these seats, thereby neutralising one another in terms of caste advantage. Gurjjars could, therefore, have the decisive role in determining the winners and losers among Meena candidates. This will be the case in at least nine districts of the state — Tonk, Karauli, Sawai Madhopur, Bharatpur, Alwar, Dausa, Ajmer, Bhilwara and Bundi — where Gurjjars have a sizeable number. That explains the crowd of Meena leaders stalking Pilot wherever he goes. The same, however, is not applicable to Gurjjars who are OBCs and do not get any reserved seats. Pilot, who has been striving hard not to lose his good rapport with the Meena community even after Gurjjar-Meena clashes, is, for obvious reasons, being seen as a big threat by powerful and influential leaders including former Chief Minister Ashok Gehlot.

Heading: What Tata, Reliance have in common - Indian Express
Content: While the US works hard on the concluding stretch of the nuclear deal, some little known details have come to light about the huge effort in the Nuclear Suppliers Group earlier this month. For one, the Austrian Government had taken a Cabinet decision to oppose the exemption being sought for India in the NSG, which explains its steadfastness until the very end. The only person who can overturn a Cabinet decision in the Austrian system is the Austrian Chancellor, and that is exactly what happened after White House got in touch with the Chancellor. Another little known fact was the role of NSA M K Narayanan, who was not in Vienna, but was singularly instrumental in pushing through the statement on disarmament in a flat 24 hours after the Netherlands came up with the suggestion. It was he who personally monitored the drafting and convinced Prime Minister Manmohan Singh and External Affairs Minister Pranab Mukherjee to go ahead with it. The result: a split in the group of six opposing the exemption.

Heading: Raining on Cabinet parade - Indian Express
Content: Nira Radia, promoter of public relations firm Vaishnavi, has staged a coup of sorts. After handling PR and corporate affairs for the Tata Group for seven years now, she has worked her 'magic' on India's biggest private sector company, the Mukesh Ambani-owned Reliance Industries Ltd. Vaishnavi has, in fact, floated a new subsidiary, NeoUCom, for managing the RIL account to ensure there is no conflict of interest while managing the reputation of the country's two top conglomerates. Her Magic Airlines venture may have bombed, but clearly, she has expanded her core PR business in an incredible fashion.

Heading: Patil’s ‘phone-a-friend’ - Indian Express
Content: Last week's rainfall in the Capital played spoilsport for the special Cabinet meeting. Several Cabinet ministers, including Pranab Mukherjee, Ambika Soni and Raghuvansh Prasad were caught in a traffic jam that ensued because of the downpour. While Raghuvansh guided his driver towards an alternative route through Bihar Bhavan to reach 7 RCR, Soni, who had cut short her visit to Hyderabad to attend the meeting, was held up. Those who managed to reach on time waited for about 45 minutes, after which the Prime Minister decided to begin the proceedings. Pranab Mukherjee only managed to reach after the meeting was well underway.

Heading: Home alone - Indian Express
Content: Apart from facing criticism from his colleagues over the failure of his department to check terror attacks, Home Minister Shivraj Patil also got a lesson on how terrorists use cellphones to trigger bombs, during the special Cabinet meeting. Minister for Commerce and Industry Kamal Nath came to Patil's rescue when some colleagues asked him whether he knew how cellphones are used to trigger bombs. When Patil looked blank, Nath quickly pulled out his mobile phone and demonstrated how it was done.

Heading: In Orissa’s ‘liberated’ zone, two villages take on the Maoists - Indian Express
Content:
Dempo Sports Club became the first Indian club to enter the AFC Cup semi-finals when they defeated Singapore's Home United 4-3 in an away match at the Jalan Besar Stadium in the island-nation on Tuesday night.

In an edge-of-the-seat affair, Dempo took the lead before the home team, egged on by a vociferous crowd, made a comeback only to see Beto score in the dying moments to give the Indian team a historic win.

The I-League champions were off to the perfect start with Mboyo Iyomi scoring in the first minute, but Peres De Oliveira cancelled it out 12 minutes later. Dempo once again took the lead in the 24th minute through Roberto Mendes Silva Beto. Home United were dealt another blow when Valery Hiek was sent off for a second bookable offence in the 28th minute. However, it didn't stop them from searching for another equaliser.

It came in the 36th minute when Kengne Ludovick was brought down in the box and though De Oliveira's penalty was parried by Abhijit Mondal, Indra Sahdan was on hand to tap home the rebound from close range.

Two minutes later, Indra put the hosts in the lead for the first time as he converted a Ludovick cross from the right. The Goans upped the ante and were rewarded when Climax Lawrence got the better of United goalie Lewis in the first minute of injury time.

The first leg match between the two at Gachibowli Stadium in Hyderabad had ended in a 1-1 draw. With the score tied at 3-3 at half-time in this return leg encounter, Dempo had the away goal advantage. United had no option but to go all out for a win. Indra and Ludovick constantly probed the rival defence, but to no avail. Dempo coach Armando Colaco preferred to play the waiting game and tried to hit United on the break. The move paid off seven minutes from time as Beto, who had an excellent game, collected a loose ball and put things well beyond the hosts. Ludovick put the ball at the back of the net for United a minute later, but referee Fareed Ali Mohamed Almarzouqi from UAE disallowed it for an infringement.

Heading: Shinde: I'll be happy to see Pawar PM - Indian Express
Content:
Armed with an axe, Rukmani Majhi, 45, of Gatibeda village in Sunabeda wildlife sanctuary area, takes a break from household chores every evening to take position on a "morcha" (a fortified platform), along with other men and women of her village, all armed with traditional weapons like bows and arrows, to watch out for Maoists.

For the first time since 2008, when Maoists set up base in the area, two villages on the Orissa-Chhattisgarh border, Sunabeda and Gatibeda in Nuapada district — a part of the "liberated" zone — have taken up arms against them. The two villages together have a population of around 4,000, mostly belonging to the Chakotia Bhunjia tribe.

While no district administration official or local police would venture into the area earlier, the Central Reserve Police Force's (CRPF) CoBRA and Orissa Police's Special Operations Group (SOG) personnel have been camping in the Sunabeda forest rest house since December.

Officials said the change was due to the successful elections in Chhattisgarh. The Maoists had threatened to disrupt the Chhattisgarh polls. But other than some minor incidents, the elections were conducted successfully. According to officials, after the Chhattisgarh polls, people in the two villages started to stand up to Maoists, refusing them food, shelter or any other help.

"This is the first time that we are seeing such resistance against Maoists anywhere in the country. Not everyone wants to help them, but they were doing so till now out of fear. After the Chhattisgarh elections, we got information that locals were rising against the Maoists. It was a conscious strategy to set up camps there, they have to be protected too," said Dilip Trivedi, DG, CRPF.

"When news of the successful polls reached other states, it was taken as a failure on the part of the Maoists. These two villages started resisting the Maoists and also put up a fight against them with bows and arrows," said a senior officer.

"We had been going to these areas for combing operations, but this is the first time that we have set up a base there. This would not have been possible without local support," said another official.

Since the two villages are located on the border with Chhattisgarh, they have often provided a safe refuge for Maoists in the past. In fact, the top Maoist leadership reportedly conducted their fourth central committee meeting in February last year in a village called Kodinga in Sunabeda area. While there are 50 other Naxal-affected villages in the area, they are yet to put up any resistance.

Trivedi said the Maoists are now being seen as "outsiders", as most of them hail from either Andhra Pradesh or Chhattisgarh. "The villagers don't see any gain in siding with the Maoists. We are hopeful that there will be resistance in other areas too," he said.

"One grouse among the villagers was that Maoists were taking their children away. This has given them enough reason to put up a resistance," said an officer.

For Maoists, Nuapada is strategically important as it is the gateway to western Orissa districts of Bargarh, Sambalpur, Bolangir and Kalahandi. If they can dominate Nuapada, it will be easy for them to build a seamless red corridor in western Orissa that connects Bastar in Chhattisgarh to Saranda in Jharkhand.

"When we first entered the area last month, we found several villages around the sanctuary that were not even on the Survey of India map. The villagers had no option but to support the Maoists," said R Jaykumar, a CRPF commandant in charge of the area.

The CRPF has sent a detailed report to the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) on the new developments. "We have started by deploying a small team there. After reviewing the situation, we will deploy more men," said an officer.

Heading: Thousands spoil durbar debut - Indian Express
Content:
Just days ahead of the AICC session on January 17, where the Congress is expected to make its stand clear on party vice-president Rahul Gandhi's candidature as its prime ministerial candidate, Union Home Minister Sushil Kumar Shinde on Saturday was quoted as saying that he would be "happy" to see NCP president Sharad Pawar as the Prime Minister.

"I would be happy if Sharad Pawar becomes the Prime Minister. He is my political guru, I must admit I entered politics because of Sharad Pawar. He brought me to politics in Maharashtra," Shinde was quoted as saying at an interaction with the media in his constituency, Solapur, in western Maharashtra.

"Everyone has ambition. He has been trying (to become the Prime Minister) since 1992... I believe Pawar has been a victim of Delhi politics... There is no reason for harbouring two views about my support to Pawar as Prime Minister. I have said this many times, even on the national platform," he was quoted as saying.

When contacted by The Sunday Express, Shinde did not deny the remarks, but claimed that he was quoted out of context. "My support to Pawar as Prime Minister was in response to questions asked by mediapersons. It was not as if I was pitching Pawar's candidature. It should be seen in the right perspective and not projected wrongly," he said. "My support will always be for Rahul Gandhi as Prime Minister," he said, asserting his loyalty to party president Sonia Gandhi and Rahul.

In Delhi, AICC general secretary in charge of Maharashtra Mohan Prakash refused to comment, saying he was unaware of the context in which Shinde made the observations. Party spokesperson Meem Afzal claimed Shinde had already denied the remarks, and hence he had nothing to add.

But a senior Congress minister in Maharashtra said, "It does not augur well for the party which is pitching Rahul Gandhi for the post". Some Maharashtra PCC leaders indicated a "ploy" to streamline the party's strained relationship with the NCP. "Shinde is a seasoned Congress leader. He would never make a mistake. There is a definite ploy," said a party leader.

"Shinde's support to Pawar has a hidden political agenda — to mend fences with the NCP in his own constituency," said a senior AICC leader.

The NCP, meanwhile, said Pawar was not in the race for the top job. "We all know Sharad Pawar is the most capable leader to become the Prime Minister. But he is not in the race. The NCP understands its political limitations. The party contests limited seats in the Lok Sabha which makes it difficult to stake claim for the top post. The arithmetic is not in our favour," said party chief spokesperson Nawab Malik.

"Shinde's statement is his personal view. What he meant was that if Pawar becomes the Prime Minister, he would have liked it as he is a leader from Maharashtra. But he also indicated that he would like to go by the party's decision," said MPCC spokesperson Ratnakar Mahajan.

"Shinde's open support to Pawar as PM is to ensure NCP helps him in Solapur. The 2014 Lok Sabha elections will be crucial for Shinde as he faces unrest from farmers in the region," said another MPCC leader. The NCP is known to have some strongholds in his Solapur Lok Sabha seat.

"Moreover, the AICC is already exploring the possibility of picking Shinde as one of the probable candidates for the top post in order to consolidate the Dalit vote bank in its favour. Even if it doesn't declare Shinde as the candidate, it wants to use his No. 2 position at the Centre to retain its Dalit vote bank," he added.

\"Shinde has supported Pawar's candidature as Prime Minister. It was shown on television channels, so how can we deny what appears in public. Moreover, he has spoken extensively on Pawar and not just made a passing remark. However, we don't doubt Shinde's loyalty to Rahul's leadership," said another state Congress leader.

Shinde and Pawar are known to share a close friendship. During the 2009 Maharashtra Assembly elections, Pawar and his daughter Supriya Sule launched the campaign of Shinde's daughter, Pranati, in Solapur Assembly constituency. Pawar also campaigned for Shinde during the Lok Sabha elections.

"Pawar and Shinde have always been friendly despite the Congress and NCP often being at loggerheads," said a senior NCP leader.

Meanwhile, the BJP said Shinde's remarks showed the Congress has accepted that Manmohan Singh's successor will not be from the party. "In a way, Shinde has already conceded that no Congress leader will be the next Prime Minister. He may daydream about who should be the Prime Minister, but the people have already reposed their faith in Narendra Modi's leadership," said BJP spokesperson Prakash Javadekar.

with inputs from Delhi

Heading: Six dud firms to transfer money to Virbhadra, family - Indian Express
Content:
The first of Arvind Kejriwal's planned daily janta durbars collapsed an hour after it started Saturday, after a heaving crowd of over 20,000 people threatened to physically swamp the chief minister and his cabinet colleagues, and the meeting teetered on the edge of disintegrating into complete chaos.

Kejriwal and Urban Development Minister Manish Sisodia were forced to retreat into the secretariat building about an hour after the durbar started at 9 am, leaving the other ministers attempting to hear the people's complaints.

The chief minister said he was in danger of being crushed by the crowd, and announced that the durbar was being suspended until the government was able to plan better and put proper arrangements in place.

Standing on the roof of the reception wing of the secretariat, Kejriwal told the crowd behind police barricades: "I accept that there were problems with the arrangements. I am deeply sorry that we could not listen to all your problems. People climbed on to the chair and table at which I was seated, and I could have been crushed if I had not left... We will come back to you with full arrangements and have another janta durbar in four to five days."

"When the crowd became unmanageable, there were two options before me, either to resort to a lathicharge or to talk to the people. I chose the second option. Next time we will have the janta durbar at a stadium," he said.

The chief minister had announced that the entire cabinet would sit outside the Delhi secretariat every Saturday to listen to the people's grievances, and would attempt to solve the urgent problems on the spot. Every weekday, a minister would receive grievances from the public.

A large proportion of the people who thronged the road outside the Delhi government headquarters were contract workers seeking permanent jobs.

Kejriwal said: "I realise that the maximum grievances are among contractual workers from BSES, Asha workers, teachers. I assure you that we have taken note of your complaints.

"On Monday I will ask all departments for data on the number of contractual staff, and why they cannot be made permanent. They will submit a report in a week, and I will try to take a decision in a month. You have waited for so many years, give me this much time."

He also requested them not to come back at the next janta durbar, so that other complaints could be heard.

The chief minister and six cabinet ministers sat in the open outside the secretariat along with senior officials, as people began handing in their complaints. Health Minister Satyendra Jain, whose mother passed away on Saturday morning, was not present.

Each person was given a slip to confirm the receipt of his complaint. Officials at the help desk said those who had supplied their mobile phone numbers would receive a confirmation SMS. \"All written complaints will be put up on our web site and the status of action taken on the complaint will be constantly updated," an official said.

Barely 15 minutes into the durbar, however, the crowd — Kejriwal said there were 5,000 people against an expected 500, while police sources said at least 20,000 people had turned up — turned unruly. Delhi Police and Sashastra Seema Bal (SSB) personnel struggled to manage the crowd, which broke the barricades at some places. The entire stretch of road from ITO to Rajghat was closed, and barricades were erected on the divider so that people could occupy one carriageway.

Some 300-400 police personnel were present outside the secretariat. "There was seating arrangement for 1,000 people outside the secretariat, but a much larger crowd turned up, leading to the chaos," a police officer said.

Several people returned disappointed. "I had come here in the hope of getting relief from my problems. But I was pushed around, and I am leaving after having waited for five hours. I wanted to meet the CM to seek a job for my physically handicapped son. There is no one to look after his needs after I retire," said M S Kaushik.

The BJP accused the AAP of promoting anarchy. "This is definitely promoting anarchy. It is a sign of bad governance," senior BJP leader Harshvardhan said.

Heading: After telling Delhi to sting, AAP wants Lokpal to snoop - Indian Express
Content:
The web of financial transactions between Himachal Pradesh Chief Minister Virbhadra Singh, members of his family and controversial businessman Vakamulla Chandrashekhar involve money transfers from him to the CM and his family via at least five companies that ceased to exist. And, in one case, money moved back and forth between the two sides.

This is revealed in an investigation by The Indian Express based on Registrar of Companies records and bank statements, including the one made public by Leader of Opposition in the Rajya Sabha, Arun Jaitley.

As per that statement, on January 10, 2012, Chandrashekhar received Rs 49.99 lakh in his personal account from Maple Destinations, a company owned by the CM's son and daughter, Vikramaditya Singh and Aprajita Kumari, respectively. The very next day, this amount was transferred to Tarini International, a company of Chandrashekhar's Tarini group. As per RoC records, in the financial year 2011-12, Maple received Rs 49.99 lakh from Tarini Sugar and Distillaries Ltd, another company of the Tarini group.

No one from the CM's family responded to questions from The Indian Express on this transaction and others and involving companies that didn't exist. Chandrashekhar denied any wrongdoing and said he was "open for any investigation at any levels".

Between November 4 and November 21, 2011, Chandrashekhar, as per his bank statement, received inflows into his personal account amounting to Rs 1.6 crore from six companies. During the same period — November 4 to November 29 — a total of Rs 1.75 crore was transferred to the accounts of Chief Minister Virbhadra Singh, wife Pratibha Singh and son Vikramaditya Singh.

Consider the nature of these transactions:

* One of these six companies is Punjab Foods Private Ltd. On November 21, 2011, Punjab Foods deposited Rs 45.5 lakh into Chandrashekhar's account and four days later, Rs 40 lakh from here was transferred to Vikramaditya Singh's account.

Incidentally, six months earlier, on April 18, 2011, Punjab Foods had filed an application before RoC, Chandigarh, to wind up its operations.

That application stated, "Pritpal Singh (director of the company), informed the members the company is not having any business activity for the last 10 years. Further company is having neither any assets nor any liabilities, therefore Easy Exit Scheme 2011 is opted for the closure of the company".

The company was officially wound up on April 20, 2011. Yet, Chandrashekhar's account showed a deposit of Rs 21.50 lakh from Punjab Foods as late as July 24, 2012.

Speaking to The Indian Express on January 2, Chandrashekhar had said he received money from Punjab Foods against agricultural produce he sold.

* On November 4, 2011, Chandrashekhar had a balance of Rs 4.05 lakh in his account. Over the next five days, Rs 92.90 lakh came into it from Kesari Nandan and Co (Rs 17.99 lakh), Shiva Stores (Rs 15.01 lakh), Jai Durga Impex (Rs 12.25 lakh), Laxmi Enterprises (Rs 7.65 lakh), Siddharth International (Rs 26 lakh) and one Suraj Singh (Rs 14 lakh). On November 11, Chandrashekhar transferred Rs 65 lakh, in two transactions, to Virbhadhra Singh's account.

According to the RoC records, Jai Durga Impex, Shiva Stores, Kesari Nandan and Co and Siddharth International all had ceased to exist before any of these transactions.

From Chandrashekhar's account, a transaction of unknown value failed on November 15, due to "insufficient funds".

* Between November 17 and November 21, Chandrashekhar's account received Rs 45.5 lakh from Punjab Foods and Rs 53 lakh from from one "V Chandra Shekhar". Four days later, Rs 71.80 lakh in two instalments of Rs 40 lakh and Rs 31.8 lakh was transferred to CM's son Vikramaditya Singh from Chandrashekhar's account.

Subsequent to this transfer — and some minor transfers not related to the CM's family — Chandrashekhar's account balance became Rs 55.05 lakh on November 25, 2011. On November 29, 2011 two instalments of Rs 25 lakh each were transferred to Pratibha Singh and Virbhadhra Singh.

His balance after these transactions was Rs 4.73 lakh, marginally higher than what it was when the transactions began.

When asked about the transactions with the CM and his family, Chandrashekhar said: "These companies are vendor companies with whom we have had trade relationships. We have done all transactions legitimately through banks. Whether they are doing business still or not, I am not competent to answer as it is purely their business."

Despite telephone calls and text messages Vikramaditya Singh was not available for comment. Jaitley has accused Virbhadra of granting an extension to Venture Energy and Technology, promoted by Chandrashekhar, for executing a hydel project.

Asked about the money received from Maple, Chandrashekhar said: "I and VVikramaditya Singh together wanted to do a construction project in 2010-11. Accordingly, my part contribution of Rs 2 crore was made to Vikram. Since the project did not take off, he returned the money through Maple. Where is the illegality?" He added: "Shri Virbhadraji is a very noble person and worthy of friendship...I am open for any investigation at any levels."

Heading: Delhi businessman overtakes Vadra’s car, booked for rash driving - Indian Express
Content:
After urging citizens to sting corrupt government officials, the AAP government is pushing hard to pass its version of the Jan Lokpal Bill in Delhi. While the process to draft the bill is already underway, Chief Minister Arvind Kejriwal has announced that the Bill will be passed in a special Assembly session by February.

"A committee has been formed to draft the law. The committee under the chief secretary will include secretaries of the departments of home, urban development, law, finance and advocate Rahul Mehra," Kejriwal said on Thursday.

"We will all meet at Ramlila Maidan either in the last week of January or first week of February," he said.

The Bill, he said, would be discussed with the "people of Delhi" at Ramlila Maidan for consent.

A Lokayukta will head the new body to combat graft with powers to conduct its own investigations, surveillance and even tap phones.

"As in the AAP's model Jan Lokpal Bill, the head of the body, in this case the Lokayukta, will have powers to tap phones, conduct independent investigations and surveillance against those who face corruption charges," Urban Development Minister Manish Sisodia said.

According to Kejriwal, the Lokayukta would function as an independent body. "Today if I am accused of corruption, there is no independent body which can investigate me but this will happen once the law is drafted," he said.

Heading: Does AP mean Ahmed Patel, asks prosecutor in Italy court; middleman says don’t know - Indian Express
Content:
A Delhi businessman was penalised by traffic police for "rash driving" after his car overtook the cavalcade of Robert Vadra, son-in-law of Congress president Sonia Gandhi.

A police officer, who did not wish to be named, said the car of Saurabh Rastogi, a businessman who lives in Paschim Vihar, was chased and intercepted by police after Vadra's securityman called the police control room and complained that a car had driven past "dangerously".

The officer said Rastogi was headed towards Lajpat Nagar from the Modi Mill flyover in Okhla at the time of the incident.

"Rastogi was in a Maruti Ritz and Vadra's cavalcade was ahead of him. We were told he had been honking continuously. In a bid to overtake the cavalcade, he accelerated and sped past Vadra's car. It was then that a securityman travelling with Vadra made a PCR call. The traffic police were also informed," the officer said.

Rastogi's car was chased by traffic policemen and intercepted near Amar Colony in south-east Delhi. "He was issued a challan for dangerous driving under Section 184 of the Motor Vehicles Act and let off," the officer said.

Heading: ‘Maoists’ gun down CPM member in Birbhum - Indian Express
Content:
Prosecutors in an Italian court Thursday asked the key middleman in the IAF's VVIP chopper deal whether the initials 'AP' in an alleged "budget sheet" for bribes to politicians referred to Ahmed Patel, the political secretary of UPA chairperson Sonia Gandhi.

The middleman, Guido Haschke, who has consistently denied bribing Indian officials or politicians, replied that he did not know who or what 'AP' stood for.

As first reported by The Indian Express, Italian prosecutors had last month produced a handwritten document they alleged was a "budget" drawn up by two middlemen — Haschke and Christian Michel — which purportedly lists initials of Indian politicians and designations of bureaucrats and IAF officers who allegedly had to be "handled" to fix the Rs 3,546 crore deal.

The alleged "budget sheet" detailed how kickbacks of 51 million euros would be divided and under the heading "POL" — Haschke has claimed this referred to Indian politicians — there is a reference to "AP" against which "3 million euro" has been listed.

Another amount of 15/16 million euros was listed against "FAM" which is said to be "Family". Haschke has claimed the note was dictated to him by British consultant Michel during one of their meetings in 2008.

On Thursday, Italian prosecutor Eugenio Fusco asked Haschke during a court hearing in Busto Arsizio near Milan whether "AP" in the note was a reference to Ahmed Patel.

In his reply, the middlemen said he did not know what AP meant when he wrote it down. Haschke also denied any bribes were paid for the contract and said that the "budget sheet" was just an imaginary note drawn up and was never acted upon.

He also said the budget sheet was merely bragging by Michel about his Indian contacts and that Haschke tried to disassociate himself from the Briton.

Strongly denying any wrongdoing in the deal, Haschke also claimed to Indian interrogators in the court that no bribes were paid for the contract and that the money he received from AgustaWestland - in excess of 24 million euros - is justified as fees for engineering consultations.

Italian prosecutors also produced another note in court Thursday - a March 2008 fax by Michel to Peter Hulett, said to be the then head of region, govt sales at AgustaWestland's India office. The fax said that among the politicians who would use the choppers once acquired by India would be UPA chairperson Sonia Gandhi and her senior advisors, including Ahmed Patel.

However, Sonia is not entitled to use government helicopters. She can use VIP aircraft only when she flies with the PM, President or ministers who are officially entitled to the aircraft. This fax by the British middleman has also been shared by the Italian side with the CBI team that is in Busto Arsizio for the hearing.

Michel has been elusive and no investigative agency has been able to reach him.

Haschke, who is facing a case in Italy for being part of a conspiracy to bribe Indian officials to ensure the AW 101 chopper was picked by the IAF, faced several questions from the Indian side and denied any irregularity.

But the Indian side did not ask Haschke to explain what AP, FAM or any of the other acronyms in the note - "DS", "JS AIR", "AFA", "DG Acquisition", CVC" etc - referred to, source said.

The middleman, who was quizzed about his association with former Air Chief S P Tyagi - named as an accused in the CBI case in the deal - denied that any money had been paid to the retired Indian officer. Haschke, sources said, admitted that he was in regular touch with three cousins of Tyagi who have also been named in the case.

In response to a question from the Indian side, Haschke said he was not aware if any money was paid to S P Tyagi.

The UPA government had come under pressure in connection with the alleged kickbacks last month after The Indian Express report on the budget sheet of the middlemen. The opposition BJP had demanded the government reveal what or who "AP" and "FAM" stand for. The party also said that it wants a detailed discussion in Parliament on "alleged payments to persons close to the ruling establishment" in connection with the controversial chopper deal and has accused the government of "running away from discussions".

The discussion did not take place as the Parliament session was abruptly called off midway.

Heading: Three infants die, relatives allege negligence - Indian Express
Content:
A CPM zonal committee member, Nandalal Mistri (51), was murdered by suspected Maoist cadres on Monday morning at Rajnagar in Birbhum.

"Following the incident, the police have sealed the district's border with Jharkhand. A relative of the deceased has lodged a complaint at the local police station. Investigations are on but no one has been arrested so far," said Laxmi Narayan Meena, SP Birbhum.

Mistri, the headmaster of Agayabandh Primary School, was on his way to school. Around 11.30 am, three youths fired three rounds at him from close range near Mohisapuri forests, killing him on the spot.

Subsequently, Additional SP, Birbhum, Farhat Abbas, reached the spot with a large police contingent.

Police recovered a few Maoist posters strewn around the body. The posters were printed in Burdwan. CPM district secretariat member Sadhan Ghosh said, "The district police has failed to provide security to the people."

On April 22, another CPM local committee member Sridam Das (45) was killed on his way to school in the same area. Even that time, three youths — suspected to be Maoist members — had shot dead Das from point blank range. Maoist leaflets were seized from the spot.

Heading: Bloc follows Trinamool steps, opposes German giant - Indian Express
Content:
Three infants died at the Institute of Child Health, a private hospital in the Park Circus area, on Monday. Their relatives have alleged medical negligence and said there was no senior doctor to attend the babies at the hospital.

Nearly a month ago, forty-day-old Mom Chatterjee was admitted to the hospital with an acute stomach disorder. Initially, her condition was critical and she was admitted to the neo-natal intensive care unit. Mom was under the supervision of two doctors, Dr Nupur Ganguly and Dr Priyanka Pal.

"Her condition started deteriorating after Saturday morning when she was taken out of the intensive care unit without our consent. She was shifted to the general ward and there was no senior doctor to attend her," said Pinaki Chatterjee, father of Mom Chatterjee. "On Sunday, she was put on a ventilator in a critical condition. Her mother repeatedly pleaded with junior doctors to consult their seniors, but they did not pay any heed," Chatterjee added.

Hospital authorities, however, have a different take. "Mom was suffering from acute diarrhoea.

We tried our best to save her but could not," ICU incharge Dr Keya Ghosh said.

Seema Pal's baby, who was brought to the hospital from Nabadwip for treatment, died after seven hours of her birth. "She was a premature baby and was suffering from an acute respiratory disorder. We could not save her," Dr Ghosh added.

Another two-and-a-half month-old baby, Parambrata Nandi, suffering from convulsion, died on Sunday night as he, too, was allegedly left unattended by senior doctors.

"It is not possible for us to deploy senior doctors all the times. The babies did not die due to medical negligence," director of the institute Apurba Ghosh said.

Heading: Board exams: be prepared for viva in English, maths - Indian Express
Content:
More trouble is on way for the CPM. Its ally, the Forward Bloc is singing Mamata Banerjee's tune of opposing big industries.

State Agriculture Minister Naren Dey said he was not concerned whether Metro Cash & Carry left the state or not. Since the state agricultural marketing department is sitting on the application of the German wholesale giant for renewal of its licence, the company has warned that it might consider the option of quitting the state.

"I am not concerned whether they stay here or not. The issue will be discussed at a meeting between the CPM and the Forward Bloc on September 28," the Bloc minister said on Monday.

The Bloc is opposed to the big private players entering the retail field and it apprehends that the German company will gradually move into the sector. The CPM, however, is in favour of corporate houses getting into retail business and is putting pressure on the Bloc to renew the company's licence.

Managing Director of the company, Martin Dlouhy is coming to meet Dey on Tuesday and will meet the chief minister on Wednesday.

Minister for Sunderban Affairs Kanti Ganguly had met Dey two days ago and urged him to renew the licence. "If the company leaves the state, 400 employees will lose their jobs," Ganguly had said.

Heading: Teenagers commit suicide - Indian Express
Content:
Besides introducing the grading system in Madhyamik examination from 2009, the West Bengal Board of Secondary Education (WBBSE) is also introducing viva examination in mathematics and English. Although teachers feel that a 10-marks viva in English is justified, the concept of conducting an oral in mathematics appears strange to them.

The board has so far not issued any guidelines about how the schools and the teachers should go about conducting the viva examination, and is expected to come out with the guidelines next week. "The measure has been taken to enhance the mental alertness of the students," said Mamata Roy, the president of the WBBSE.

"We can ask the derivations of formulae in the mathematics viva. If students can prepare a project report on Pythagoras theorem, they can also be asked questions on the project," said Partho Ray, secretary of the board. "There are many formulae in class X that can be asked," said Uttam Dalui, a teacher of mathematics in the Hindu School.

As per the seven-point indirect grading being introduced by the board from 2009, each student has to secure grade C, which is 25 marks in each subject, to pass the examination. More than 700,000 students are expected to appear for the written Class X Board examination in the last week of February, 2009.

"Statistics has shown that most students fail in mathematics. This is an attempt as per the 'no-detention policy' of the Board to pass all the students. Students can secure good marks in the viva and they can easily overcome the 25-marks barrier," said Biswajit Das, the secretary of Secondary Teachers and Employees Association (STEA).

Vishnupada Bari, mathematics teacher of Durgapur High School at Dum Dum, said, "The students will not benefit from this. This is just to award marks to all the students and reach 100 per cent pass percentage".

The introduction of viva in English, meanwhile, was welcomed by all teachers, who feel this will help the students develop communicative skills in the subject.

Heading: Nine months on, Nandaram market not ready to douse flames - Indian Express
Content:
Family of the boy refused to accept the marriage

Two teenagers committed suicide by jumping in front of a Sealdah-bound Dankuni local train between Dakshineswar and Bali railway stations on Sunday night.

According to the police, Lakhi Naskar (17) and Soma Bhuinya (14), both residents of the railway colony at Dakshineswar, got married on Sunday evening, but decided to end their lives after the Naskar family refused to accept their marriage. While Soma was a class IX student, Lakhi was a school dropout.

Lakhi and Soma were engaged for the last two years and decided to tie the knot at the Dakshineswar temple on Sunday. But when Lakhi took his newly-wedded wife to his house, his father Swapan refused to accept the marriage saying that both were minors.

Lakhi's father has admitted that he had scolded his son, following which, the couple left the house at 9 pm. According to D Chakraborty, investigation officer of Belur GRP, the bodies of the duo were discovered around 1 am.

"It was difficult to identify the bodies," Chakraborty said. The bodies were later taken to Belur GRP where family members identified them.

Heading: Stagnant water in premises? KMC will cut off water supply - Indian Express
Content:
Nine months have passed since the worst fire in living memory gutted Nandaram market in Burrabazar. But till date, the market authorities have not implemented the basic recommendations of the Fire and Emergency Services department.

The report of a survey conducted by the divisional officers of the fire department last week has revealed that the market authorities have not installed even the basic fire-fighting equipment till now.

A 111-page report, which a state-appointed committee had prepared and submitted to chief secretary Amit Kiran Deb, had highlighted the fact that rampant violation of all established fire norms was the main reason behind the 100-hour blaze at Nandaram Market in January.

In a meeting held last week and attended by the Deputy Commissioner (central), DG (building), Director (fire and emergency services), Municipal commissioner and representatives from CESC, it was decided that electricity supply to the market would not be resumed because the market authorities had not implemented the basic recommendations.

"We had recommended that they change wiring, install new pipelines, construct deep tube wells, sprinklers, wet risers and an extra staircase. But nothing has been done," said a divisional officer. He added that according to the recommendations, the market authorities were supposed to bore a deep tube well with a capacity of 1 lakh litres. But the deep tube well that they have constructed is of a 60,000 litre capacity. The officer added that even the new cable that had been laid from the ground floor to the basement was faulty.

Kolkata Municipal Corporation authorities also agreed that the market authorities had not adhered to the fire safety norms.

"Unless all the fire-fighting norms are maintained, electricity supply cannot be resumed," said Director, fire and emergency services, Gopal Bhattcharjee.

The market authorities, on the other hand, said work was on and they were gradually installing the firefighting equipment.

Heading: State government introduces new health scheme for its employees - Indian Express
Content:
With 624 cases of malignant malaria already been reported this year, the Kolkata Municipal Corporation (KMC) has finally decided to act tough against the owners, whose premises hold stagnant water. MMiC (Health) Subodh Dey said: "If stagnant water is found at any place, be it a household, a police station or a government office, a notice will be served for clearing it. And if the order is not complied by in 24 hours, we will disconnect the water-supply line under the KMC Act 1980."

There is, however, a directive of the High Court that supply of water and electricity, the two basic amenities, cannot be discontinued.

The KMC Act, on the other hand, says that if the notice for clearing stagnant water is not complied within seven days, then the civic body can file a case against the offender at the municipal court.

Mayor Bikash Ranjan Bhattacharya said: "We are not going against the High Court order that stated that water connection will not be cut off due to the non-payment of taxes. The KMC Act authorises us to take action against the guilty in other cases."

The civic body will dump the unclaimed tyres, where rainwater usually gets stagnated, in the Dhapa ground. The KMC will also seize old vehicles which hold stagnant water, if their owners do not take immediate precautionary measures.

The KMC has asked health workers to perform their duties effectively.

"Stringent action will be taken against health workers if they are found guilty of slackness. Services of the contractual doctors can be terminated and permanent doctors will be suspended," Dey said .

Heading: Reliance Retail plans new format - Indian Express
Content:
The West Bengal government has introduced a new health scheme for the state government employees, by which they can receive medical treatment in private hospitals and nursing homes. The cost of the treatment will be borne by the government.

This was announced on Monday by Finance Minister Asim Dasgupta at Writers' Buildings. At present, the employees get Rs 100 as medical allowance every month and they get medicines up to Rs 1,000 if they get admitted to a government hospital. 

"Now the employees will be given the option of either availing the present facility or foregoing the Rs 100 and avail medical treatment either in government hospitals or those private hospitals which will be identified by the government," Dasgupta said. For this the financial burden on the state government will be Rs 50 crore every year.

The state government will also pay Rs 1,000 as exgratia to the 2 lakh workers of closed factories and tea gardens and Integrated Child Development Services' employees. For this, the government will spend Rs 20 crore.

Regarding the recent violence at the Writers' Buildings , the minister said the government had to initiate departmental proceedings against seven employees under compelling circumstances.

"The incident of September 5 in which some employees misbehaved with a senior officer of the finance department was shown on TV channels and reported in the dailies the next day. The Left Front government never wants to take action against its employees but we had to initiate departmental proceedings against those employees," Dasgupta said. State Government Employees Federation based at Writers' Buildings, meanwhile, on Monday launched a signature campaign among employees of the state secretariat, demanding the cancellation of the pay commission and revision of pay scales in line with the Central employees.

Heading: Students to hold hunger strike over teacher’s transfer - Indian Express
Content:
Amid resistance from Left Front partners against the entry of retail giants, Mukesh Ambani's Reliance Retail is keen to rollout new stores in West Bengal.

According to sources, Reliance Delight stores, scheduled to be launched after the Pujas in October, will sell fresh fish, frozen chicken and meat. They will also sell frozen, ready-to-cook, foods of other companies.

"They (Reliance representatives) have held a preliminary talks with us for the Delight stores," said a supplier.

The group had made an entry into the city in August by forging an agreement with Keventers Fresh. Sources say the company is bent on opening more stores in Kolkata. So far, Reliance Fresh has opened four stores at — Swabhumi, Rajarhat, Budge Budge and Bangur.

According to industry sources, while Reliance Fresh caters to the vegetarian segment, Reliance Delight will cater only to the non-vegetarian customers.

Earlier, in 2007, Reliance Retail shelved its plan to create 1,62,000 sq ft of retail space in the city and adjacent areas due to violent protests from the Left Front partners.

It, however, did not deter the plans of the company to make a foray in the state.

Heading: Kanjilal case: HC rejects convicts’ bail petitions - Indian Express
Content:
Students of the Regional Institute of Printing Technology at Jadavpur will hold a relay hunger strike from Tuesday to protest against the transfer of a teacher, Bhola Nath Ghosh of planography department, to the Birla Institute of Technology.

The students of the polytechnic allege that the teacher was transferred because he raised his voice against irregularities in the college.

As the authorities have not allowed the students to hold the protest in the college, therefore, they will erect a stage outside it to hold the strike. "I am teaching printing technology here. I don't know what I will teach at BIT. It is the love of the students that they want me in the college," Ghosh said.

The protesting students also met the Director of Technical Education and Training, Parijat De, to submit a deputation on the issue.

"The director threatened our representatives that if we did not withdraw the strike he will close down the college," said Supriyo Sur, a third year student of the institute. The director, however, refused to comment on the issue.

Heading: Miles To Go: wake up call to science students - Indian Express
Content:
A division bench of the High Court comprising Justices Amit Talukdar and P S Banerjee on Monday rejected bail applications of Aditi Kanjilal and three others, who were convicted for the unnatural death of Dr Swapan Kanjilal. Dr Kausik Chakraborty, Dr Subrata Das and Pulak Roy are the other convicts, who had filed the bail petition in the court.

Dr Swapan Kanjilal and seven others had gone to the Kangsabati Dam in Bankura district on a picnic on September 16, 1990, where Dr Kanjilal had drowned while taking a bath in the river. His body was recovered from the river after 68 hours.

The police had filed a chargesheet in the case in 1993 and the Additional Sessions Court at Bankura had awarded them life imprisonment to convicts on April 19, 2008. The four convicts had filed an appeal in the High Court challenging the judgment, following which, their bail petition came up for hearing on Monday.

Advocate Asimesh Goswami, public prosecutor, however, moved a plea before the Bench that Dr Kanjilal was a good swimmer and he had sought help from Pulak Roy when he was drowning.

Heading: Stick to one-skipper policy, Amarnath tells CAB - Indian Express
Content:
The Indian Institute of Chemical Biology (IICB) has taken a unique initiative to take the help of a documentary film to lure students to pursue research in basic science.

The 35-minute docudrama Miles To Go, which has been completed, is the first of its kind by a scientific research institute to attract students to take up research as their area of specialisation. The film, made by Gautam Ghose, has been partly funded by the IICB and Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR).

"We need to check brain drain. There is scope for research in science within the country. However, students are attracted more towards IT than basic science. This is a rare attempt to popularise science," former director S Pakrashia, said.

IICB had approached Gautam Ghose, an eminent filmmaker of the city, a year ago to direct the film showcasing the work done by the institute, as well as highlighting its different research wings.

"Work started a year ago when we decided to bring out information about our institute and research through a film in order to attract young talents to science. The documentary will enable us to showcase our work to the nation and present facts about IICB," said its director Siddhartha Roy.

"The film is shown through the eyes of a family that had approached us to know if one of their children was suffering from optic nerve disease, glaucoma," said deputy director, Ashish Sen.

"I was approached by IICB to make a documentary film that will let people know about the vast research that the scientists of the institute do," said Gautam Ghose. "We spun the film around the true story of a family. The documentary stars IICB scientists and has been shot inside the institute premises," added Ghose.

The documentary sketches the varied research work like applying modern technology to check diseases like gastric ulcer, cancer and prosthetic issues. Research areas like chemistry, biochemistry, cell biology, molecular biology, neurobiology and immunology have been highlighted in the documentary, as the script familiarises one with scientists working on exploration of bioactive substances from natural sources as potential drugs.

IICB has decided to take the rights of the documentary. Though the film is in English, the institute will soon dub it in Bengali and Hindi and it will be screened on different channels and shown in schools, colleges and universities to attract students.

"It is a good way to encourage students. It will surely arouse interest among us to pursue basic science research in future," said Mira Nandi, a undergraduate student of physics.

Heading: Ghanaian Villas lights up Chirag United camp - Indian Express
Content:
While the debate over who should lead the Bengal team is raging on, Mohinder Amarnath has categorically suggested the CAB bosses to pick a single skipper for the full season instead of picking separate captains for the four-day and one-day matches.

Allrounder Laxmi Ratan Shukla, skipper of the team last season, is the favourite to get the top job this time as well, but there is stiff competition from young turk Manoj Tiwary.

The duo has sent certain sections of the CAB wondering if it's a good idea to make Shukla lead the team in the shorter format and hand over the reins to Tiwary for the four-dayers.

"Having taken a good look at these players, I think this team should have a single skipper for the entire season. That will be the right approach," Amarnath told reporters after a long session with CAB president Jagmohan Dalmiya at the Eden Gardens.

Amarnath, who is the consultant to Bengal cricket for a one-year period, spent a week with the senior Bengal probables and will return to Kolkata on September 29.

Heading: Rahul storms into twin prequarters - Indian Express
Content:
Subrata's changed style gets players' support

Chirag United have got a boost ahead of their I-League campaign. On Monday morning, Ghanaian defender Patrick Villas joined their squad and impressed one and all during his half hour training. This was despite the fact that he reached here from Ghana only last night.

The player has an impressive CV. He represented his country in the Athens Olympics. Also, played in the Under-20 World Cup in 2001.

United's Brazilian physical trainer Diego Garcia was all praise for the newcomer. "The players — Solomon Opoku is the other one — barely had any rest after a long flight.

"Naturally, they had a light training this morning. They will take a little time to settle down. Still, Villas was very impressive. He has got a very good technique," he told The Indian Express.

Another overseas player, Kelvin from Cameroon has also arrived for trial. The team already has two foreigners in Muritala Ali and Lewis who played in the Calcutta Football League (CFL). The team management will have to decide in next 48 hours who will be their overseas trio in the I-League. Villas, however, appears a certainty. United will start their I-League campaign against East Bengal on September 26.

Meanwhile, coach Subrata Bhattacharya seems to be in sync with his players. There is a definite change in his approach that has the players' support. Maybe, a couple of inauspicious seasons with East Bengal and Mohun Bagan have prompted Bhattacharya to change his style.

Earlier, Bhattacharya used to be predictable with attacks from the flanks and a mix of a long ball game in between. Now he is keen on playing more ground passes a la modern way.

Said a few senior team members: "We are playing about 30-35 passes to build an attack from our defensive-third.

"Also, Bhattacharya is giving stress on playing more incisive passes in the penetrative zone and cracking the opposition defence in two to three touches. It makes the game exciting. Crowd will love it."

Heading: Double trouble - Indian Express
Content:
Delhi's Rahul Singh advanced to the pre quarter-finals of both the Boys' Singles Under-14 and Under-16 beating seeds at the AITA Talent Series Tennis Championship 2008 at Jamshedpur.

Rahul first ousted fourth seed Ishank Ravi of Bihar 4-2, 5-4 (7-4) in the Under-14 category, and then went on to beat third seed Bengal boy Sattwik Sinha Ray 4-2, 5-4 (7-5) in the Under-16 circuit.

Mohammad Kamran Ali of Bengal ousted eighth seed Purushottam Dash of Orissa 4-1, 4-2 in the Boys' Singles Under-16 event. Innocent Lalrindika of Bengal ousted seventh seed Ishank Ravi of Bihar 4-2, 4-1.

In the Girls' Singles Under-14 category, Sushmita Paul, Suchi Smita Pani and Srishti Smriti Burh of Jharkhand, and Adya Sinha of Bihar, reached the quarter-finals.

Today's results: Boys' Singles Under 16 Final Qualifying Round (Best of 17 Games): Arjun Patnaik (AP) beat Ronak Das (Ori) 9-1; Md. Kamran Ali (WB) beat Balbir Singh (Bih) 9-5; Innocent Lalrindika (WB) beat Gulshan Kumar (Bih) 9-2; Rahul Singh (Dli) beat Sangam Raja (Bih) 9-2; Abhishek Singh (Bih) beat Sachin Gopalka (Dli) 9-2; Ritwik Bhriguvanshi (Bih) beat Qasim Masumi (Bih) 9-5; Shantanu Soumya (Bih) beat Kaushal Bhangar (Bih) 9-3; Vipul Jain (Dli) beat Tilak Raj (Bih) 9-6.

Boys' Singles Under 14 First Round (Short Sets): Shukrit Guha (1) (WB) (55) beat Varun Nayar (Jha) (LL) 4-0, 4-0; Ratan Soren (Jha) (Q) beat Yash Jaiswal (Jha) (WC) 4-1, 4-1.

Heading: Trail of a City - Indian Express
Content:
With Kolkata resident Kaushik Dutta bringing the queasy issue of bigamy to the forefront, it's time to find out Bollywood's take on it

When Behala resident, Kaushik Dutta bound himself in holy matrimony with sisters Jhuma and Soma this Sunday, he unwittingly joined a list of Bollwood and Tollywood greats. Dutta's bigamous ways may have raised a number of eyebrows, but on screen, Bollywood and Tollywood idols have practised and indeed, endorsed bigamy.

In the 1980s and early 1990s, a period that is considered to be the darkest of Bollywood history, filmmaker Saawan Kumar Tak earned himself the title of "souten specialist", because of his uncanny knack of manufacturing polygamous tales of different permutations and combinations—two women, one man, one woman, two men etc. While the Rajesh Khanna starrer Souten, dealt with the problem of other woman by making her to be a martyr, his next film Souten ki Beti was like the icing on the cake. The film deals with the sensitive topic of the fate of children born out of wedlock. Jeetendra has a daughter with Rekha, his mistress, while being married to Jaya Prada. And pray what does the wife do when she gets to know about her husband's philandering ways? Bring the mistress and the child home and give her the status of the "second wife"!

Then it was the turn of director David Dhawan and his series of gharwali-baharwali films, which made a mockery of the institution. Being married to more than one woman at that time seemed to be the favourite pastime of heroes like Govinda and Anil Kapoor in these regressive comedies. While the legalities of the situation may make most men think twice before taking the plunge, for these men the consequences were always happy. In Sajan Chale Sasural Govinda happily bounces from one woman to another with the ease of an olympic gymnast. In between, he also manages to crack a few ribald jokes at the expense of his unsuspecting wives, Tabu and Karisma Kapoor. The problem, which seems a little more than a logistical one for our hero, is resolved with what is supposed to come naturally to most Indian women — you guessed it — acceptance.

Presumably, women in Bollywood of the 1980s had no choice but to accept a man who has been less than loyal to her. If she revolts, like Rekha does in the Jeetendra starrer Ek Hi Bhool, she is a shrew who has to be tamed. Another exercise in regression was the Jeetendra-Rekha starrer of the late 1980s, Mera Pati Sirf Mera Hai. The film literally had the kanjeevaram clad heroines literally clawing each other to keep the man who both can stake claim to!

More recently in David Dhawan's Gharwali Baharwali, the hero has no choice but to indulge in bigamy, we are told. On a business trip to Nepal, Anil Kapoor falls in love with a nubile Rambha, hides the fact from loving wife (Raveena Tandon) before things finally come to a head. Again, it is the wife who is guilt tripped into accepting the other woman.

Closer home, in Tollywood, the treatment of bigamy has thankfully been more sensitive. In Rituparno Ghosh's 2005 film Antarmahal, the oppressive zamindar (Jackie Shroff) marries a much-younger Soha Ali Khan, after his first wife (Rupa Ganguly) fails to give him an heir. The wives are both allies and rivals in this complex tale of exploitation.

Heading: Coming Full Circle - Indian Express
Content:
A new film on Delhi looks at the future, laments the losses

Filmmaker Krishnendu Bose angles his camera at the Yamuna and sees a vision of the future. "This will be Delhi's hippest address. On the flood plains of the Yamuna will rise a Manhattan of the future, with undulating series of high-rise buildings and the best condominiums that money can buy," he says, referring to the state's urban blueprint. The ribbon of the Yamuna and its 22-km-stretch flood plains form the integral part of the 47-year-old documaker's new film, Delhi: Work in Progress.

Bose's camera doesn't stop roving; he travels with it to the other extreme of Delhi's landscape — at Bhawana, 40 km away on the Haryana border, where evicted slum dwellers have been "dumped". He takes it to a series of urban planners who paint fantastical pictures of the future, to social experts who sound warning notes and perches him atop flyovers that look out onto depleting tree cover.

"The film is a Dilliwalla's tribute to the only city he can call home," says Bose. His shelves are lined with trophies — his last film Tiger, the Death Chronicle won an award at Montana in May — but Delhi: Work in Progress, he stresses, is straight from the heart and documents the Capital's rapid transformation into "what politicians call a world-class city" and the cost of development. "At Bhawana, I was frightened by the level of anger. Around 2,000 people were moved to the jungle from their slum in Vikaspuri. They lost their jobs, have no sanitation and there's only darkness at the end of the tunnel," he says. The anger of the displaced runs through the film — and it espouses Bose's fear that soon the city could see a social backlash by the displaced. "They form 70 per cent of the population who are getting increasingly frustrated by the day," he says.

The 38-minute film, made over a period of one year on a budget of Rs 3 lakh that was largely met by the WWF, progresses as a linear narrative on a series of issues ranging from civic values to Delhi's couldn't-care-less attitude. For the students who watched the movie, the effect was scary. "Delhi: Work in Progress started as a five-minute campaign film on tree-felling in the Capital. I had no idea it would end up as a horror movie instead," says the filmmaker.

Heading: Draw We Have Coming to Dover - Indian Express
Content:
After recording with Carlos Santana and making music in LA for over a decade, composer Sanjay Divecha is all set to release his first album exploring Indian sounds

In a musical career spanning over two decades, guitarist and composer Sanjay Divecha spent 15 of it in Los Angeles. And every time he composed a song, the sound of India went missing. But all of that was until 2003, when 40-something Divecha decided to return home to Mumbai, explore the sounds of Indian languages and compile it all in an album, Full Circle. The album, brought out by Blue Frog, releases on September 24.

"This album, as the title says, is a sum of all my musical influences over the years. And the Indian sound, which was absent in my earlier compositions, is present here and that has made it special, giving me an identity," Divecha says about the 11-track set. The lyrics are in Hindi, Tamil and English, apart from a smattering of Sanskrit shlokas, and the sounds are myriad — Hindustani folk and Carnatic rhythms, apart from Latin American and African sounds, R&B, jazz and gospel rock.

Divecha, who has strummed the acoustic guitar with Carlos Santana for the Beninese singer Angelique Kidjo, and with others such as drummer/composer Dave Weckl and renowned bassist Louis Johnson, has also played the guitar for the soundtrack of Penelope Cruz starrer Woman On Top and scored for films like Leela. He has been busy in Bollywood as well, having worked with music directors such as Vishal-Shekhar and Salim-Suleiman and playing in the forthcoming Ru Ba Ru by Arjun Chandramohan Bali and Aashayein by Nagesh Kukunoor.

This time, for the album, Divecha has collaborated with 20 musicians, including Kailash Kher, Kunal Ganjawalla, Ranjit Barot, Karl Peters and Vivek Rajagopalan. "Collaborations are common, but my compositions have got the artists to do something they have never done before," says Divecha, who has composed and produced all the tracks in the album. Artists like Kher, for instance, have taken to a westernised singing style.

"The journey of making this album and exploring India has been a learning experience and even a lifetime doesn't seem enough. This is what I will continue doing," he smiles. He has indeed come a full circle.

Heading: Chargesheet filed in Rizwanur murder case - Indian Express
Content: Last year, when Daljit Nagra brought out his slim volume Look We Have Coming to Dover!, rapping in verse about his mother with "mustard-oiled trail of hair, brocaded pink sandals and the smell of curry" and Every immigrant in the UK, he was feted as the brave new voice. Now the publishing house Westland has floated a contest called "Djinn and Tonic" in collaboration with the British Council, inviting artists, designers and illustrators to send in their creations based on the debut collection of the British poet of Indian origin. At the end, a limited-edition 2009 calendar with Nagra's poetry and a dozen winning images would be published. "Nagra's poetry is very visual. It fitted the format of the contest perfectly. Since verse does not sell like fiction does, this will give a boost to poetry," says Priyanka Chowdhury, head (publicity), Westland. The contest is open till September 30.

Heading: Pranab hopeful of nuclear pacts with France, Russia - Indian Express
Content:
While the Gujarat Police believe that the Indian Mujahideen, which claimed responsibilities for the recent blasts in e-mails sent to media houses, is "nothing but a faction of the outlawed Students Islamic Movement of India (SIMI)", the Delhi Police are of the opinion that they are two separate entities with different ideologies.

The two police departments also differ on who was the mastermind behind the blasts. The Delhi Police say it was Atif, whom they killed in an encounter last week, the Gujarat Police say the Ahmedabad blasts were mastermined by Mufti Abu Bashir Kasmi, who is in their custody at present, and Mumbai-based Abdul Subhan Qureshi alias Tauqeer. The Gujarat Police also claim that it was based on their intelligence and a list of some "suspected" cellphone numbers they passed on to central agencies, that the Delhi Police carried out the Jamia Nagar encounter.

Heading: Mamata lends a hand to teachers - Indian Express
Content:
Union External Affairs minister Pranab Mukherjee on Monday said that there was a great possibility of signing a bilateral deal with France and Russia for supply of nuclear fuel, apart from the much talked about Indo-US Civil Nuclear Cooperation Programme.

Speaking at a seminar titled 'Indo-US Civil Nuclear Cooperation and Its Future Impact' organised by the Rajiv Gandhi Development Institute in the city, Mukherjee vociferously defended the deal and accused the Left and BJP of joining hands in opposing it.

Mukherjee said that while India was likely to sign a bilateral agreement with France for supply of nuclear fuel during Prime Minister Manmohan Singh's forthcoming visit to that country, a similar deal is also likely to be signed with Russia during Prime Minister Vladimir Putin's visit to India. He also said India would sign the NPT if it became non-discriminatory and universally viable.

Mukherjee hoped that the US Congress will ratify the 123 agreement on September 25 but clarified that though US ratification was pending, it would not prevent India from entering into a bilateral agreement with other countries for supply of nuclear fuel.

"An India-specific safety agreement is just a passport to enter into nuclear trade with any country. We now need a visa," he added. Referring to criticism that the 123 agreement would compromise India's sovereignty, Mukherjee said, "there is nothing in that agreement, nor in the India-Specific Safeguard Agreement, nor in the waiver by the NSG, that can compromise India's decision making".

Mukherjee said the nuclear deal was absolutely essential for meeting the country's energy requirement.

Reiterating that India's independent foreign policy would not be compromised by the nuclear deal, he pointed out that India had protested against the US invasion of Iraq.

Heading: High Court postpones hearing of 2002 riot accused till September 26 - Indian Express
Content:
Trinamool Congress chief Mamata Banerjee will join the protests of students and diploma-holders of the Primary Teachers Training Institutes (PTTIs) in the state. The state government is keen to set up a Primary Service Commission that will recruit primary teachers, marking abolition of the existing PTTIs. To protest against the move, the students will launch a protest from the third week of October that will be supported by the Trinamool.

The institutes were recognised by National Council of Teachers Education (NCTE) and diploma-holders of the institutes were eligible for recruitment in primary schools of the state. In 2006, a petition was filed in the Calcutta High Court accusing the institutes of poor governance, following which the court derecognised the diplomas. As a result, the recruitment of primary teachers in the state came to a halt and thousands of the teachers have not been able to get jobs since then.

The teachers have been protesting against the decision since then. On Monday, a delegation of their representatives met Trinamool chief Mamata Banerjee.

"A senior Trinamool leader called me last week, asking me to visit Trinamool Bhavan. We held meetings with senior leaders, including Mamata Banerjee, and they promised us all cooperation," said Pintu Parui, the leader of the West Bengal Primary Teachers Training Institute Students' Union.

The union had earlier sought the support of the Forward Bloc, a constituent of the Left Front. With no support coming from the Bloc, it turned to the Trinamool.

The union has also been asking the government to go for an out of court settlement of the case. Since the court proceedings are likely to linger on for long, the union favoured to resolve the issue through negotiations. "Last month, we met the CPM state secretary, Biman Bose. We were ready for talks but the government turned down our plea," Parui said.

Heading: Two injured in accident - Indian Express
Content:
The Gujarat High Court has postponed the hearing on the bail plea of Bhavin Patel, one of the accused in the Deepada Darwaza mass massacre case of the 2002 post-Godhra riots, till September 26. Justice M R Shah pronounced the verdict on Monday.

Patel was among the eight accused booked for burning alive 11 people in a house in Deepada Darwza area of Visnagar town in Mehsana district in March 2002. Although he was granted bail by the High Court along with the other accused, another FIR was registered against him in March 2004 for threatening and intimidating complainant Iqbal Baloch to withdraw the case.

On Baloch's complaint, Patel was arrested again, but subsequently released by the Mehsana district court. However, when the Special Investigation Team (SIT) was constituted to probe the 10 most heinous cases of the 2002 riots including Deepada Darwaza, Patel was arrested again in July this year.

After his bail plea was rejected by the Mehsana district court, Patel moved the High Court.

Heading: A bank in dire need of ready cash - Indian Express
Content:
Two persons were injured in the Sardarnagar area on Sunday night when the driver of an AMTS bus lost control following an attack of seizures.

The wayward bus then collided with an auto-rickshaw and injured the passengers inside.

The Sardarnagar police lodged a complaint against bus driver Kamlesh Dave for rash driving on the basis of a complaint by the auto-rickshaw driver, Vinod Sewani.

In his complaint, Sewani said the incident occurred on Sunday night when he was driving his auto-rickshaw with his family members inside it. Near Noblenagar, the AMTS bus speeded recklessly towards his auto-rickshaw. Two of his family members sustained minor injuries in the accident and were shifted to Ahmedabad Civil Hospital, he said.

Investigating Officer, sub-Inspector S R Rawat said: "Prima facie it seems that the accident occurred due to the seizure attack. The driver was also taken to the Ahmedabad Civil Hospital for treatment. He was later discharged and we are yet to record his statement."

Heading: New policy to make state industries globally competitive - Indian Express
Content:
Depositors of GICB rush to take back their money

The account holders of the Gujarat Industrial Co-operative Bank (GICB) assembled outside the bank's head office at Bhagal in Surat on Monday morning to withdraw their savings after they learnt that the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has declared that the bank does not have enough liquidity. The bank has 1.52 lakh account holders in Surat.

RBI officials had earlier visited the GICB in Ahmedabad on Saturday. After checking the balance sheet they had declared that the bank is low on liquidity. The RBI officials also claimed that the bank had too many NPA (Non Performing Assets), which had led to low liquidity.

The bank has three branches in Surat city, nine in entire south Gujarat and overall 20 branches in the state. The account holders rushed to the bank's branches for withdrawing their cash from their accounts. Some of them had saved money for their children's marriage and other purposes and were seen crying.

Mahidharpura police rushed to the GICB head office at Bhagal and took control of the situation before anything untoward could occur.
