Praveen Mehta, the bank's regional manager, later allowed the customers to withdraw only Rs 1,000 from their accounts. Administrators have been appointed at the bank to look after the day to day transactions.

Mehta said all the 20 branches in the state have Rs 458 crore of deposits; Rs 252 crore advances (loans and other facilities); Rs 14 crore of assets; Rs 152 crore as net reserve; while Rs 64 crore are with government securities.

On Monday, the banks in Surat had Rs 5.48 crore as cash on hand, Rs 334.34 crore as total deposits and Rs 147.80 crore as advances. Mehta added that Rs 31 lakh was given to the account holders on Monday.

Heading: Right connection: AUDA to link 33 more waterbodies - Indian Express
Content:
To be announced before global summit, the policy will focus on a single window system, environment friendly projects

The state government appears all set to announce its new industrial policy ahead of the biennial Vibrant Gujarat Global Investors' Summit on January 12-13, 2009. A draft of the industrial policy has been readied and is in the process of finalisation.

Several new incentive schemes are envisaged for the proposed new industrial policy. There are also plans to modify some of the existing schemes in the present policy announced in 2003. While preparing the draft document, the government has ensured that its new policy should make the state's industries "globally competitive."

Minister of State for Industries Saurabh Patel told Newsline that the government will make an all-out effort to announce its new industrial policy at the earliest.

"We plan to encourage environment-friendly industrial projects and also introduce a single window system for early clearance of applications by private investors," he said. He, however, declined to divulge further details of the new policy, saying that the government was still in the process of finalising it.

An internal document prepared by the department, however, suggests that under the proposed policy, the government plans to provide substantial interest and capital subsidies to industrial units, with special focus on encouraging micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) in backward talukas of the state.

The document contains recommendations by five separate task forces recently set up to evaluate the performance of the various schemes in force under the present industrial policy and suggest modifications so as to make them more outcome-oriented for the new policy. According to a senior official, most of these recommendations are being incorporated in the proposed policy.

A task force on enhancing the competitiveness of MSMEs has recommended a full interest subsidy for micro enterprises, and 5 per cent interest subsidy for the small and medium ones, with maximum Rs 25 lakh per annum for next five years. In addition to interest subsidy, MSMEs in the 30 undeveloped backward talukas (mainly having tribal populations) will be provided land at concessional rates in industrial estates.

For MSMEs, the task force has also recommended 50 per cent grant with a limit of Rs 1 crore for acquiring new technology. The assistance to be raised has been fixed at 80 per cent for training and 75 per cent for other components, with a ceiling of Rs 10 crore for cluster development in 3-5 years.

According to the document, the large units producing raw materials and promoting auxiliary units will be encouraged to develop industrial park for accommodating minimum 30 units. Small and medium enterprises in this park will be provided 10 per cent investment subsidy with a limit of Rs 20 lakh in addition to the interest subsidy.

To encourage industries to implement environmental protection measures, it is proposed to provide 50 per cent subsidy (upto Rs 1 lakh) per plant for energy and water conservation measures, besides a provision of Rs 2 crore per project for MSMEs for setting up desalination plants through cost effective innovative technology. It has also been recommended to provide Rs 15 lakh per plant for creating waste information and exchange centre (eco-industrial networking).

The government also proposes to provide Rs 2 crore per project for technological up-gradation to existing facility through clean innovative measures and also Rs 25 lakh per plant for using clean efficient and innovative air pollution control equipment in industries. Besides, an assistance of 25 per cent with a ceiling of Rs 5 lakh will be provided for setting up environment management cell within the industry.

It is also envisaged to give assistance of Rs 25 lakh for reducing green house gas emission and obtaining carbon credits through CDM as seed money per cluster of minimum 50 industrial units, and another Rs 50,000 for reducing the carbon foot print.

At least one industrial estate is also proposed to be set up in each of the 30 under-developed and backward talukas for the promotion of cottage/small industries and generation of employment for the locals.

To attract investment in textiles and apparel industry, the government also proposes to provide 10 per cent credit-linked subsidy for cotton spinning, knitting and machine carpeting, besides a provision of duty exemption on power tariff for 10 years.

There are also proposals to build parks in and around all major cities of Gujarat, besides a weaving park for cotton textiles at Ahmedabad, Rajkot and north Gujarat.

Initially, an exclusive technical textile park for small/medium units will be set up in South Gujarat. It is also planned to provide assistance with a ceiling of Rs 5 crore for cost of machinery and equipment for setting up a textile testing and development centre by a Trust or an industry association in the PPP mode.

Heading: GU overlooks its own rulebook - Indian Express
Content:
Storm water management programme to work as model project for water harvesting in the city

After the initial linking of 11 lakes in the city, the Ahmedabad Urban Development Authority (AUDA) is now poised to link 33 more waterbodies across the town as a part of its storm water management programme. The new policy is being projected as a model for water harvesting at the city level.

A sum of Rs 104 crore has already been sanctioned for connecting the waterbodies under JNNURM, which has placed a proposal of Rs 108 core for the preservation of these water bodies. The linking of the water bodies is expected to be over by 2011.

Of the 33 lakes, 26 are in the western part of the city while seven are in the east. The western lakes include Gota Lake, two lakes at Sola, Thaltej, Khoraj and Bodakdev, and lakes at Ambli, Prahladnagar, Makarba, Motera, Chandkheda Jaspur, Chharodi, Chenpur, Ognaj, Hebatpur, Shilaj, Mohmadpura, Okaf, Sarkhej, Tragad and Jagatpur. In the east, the water bodies to be linked are Nikol, Vastral, Ramol, Hanspur, Kathwada, Singarwa and Bilasia.

"We have already linked Memnagar, Vastrapur, Thaltej, Bodakdev, Prahladnagar, Makarba lakes with Sarkhej Roja in the west and Kali, Ranip, Chandlodia lake with the one near RC Technical Institute in the east, which subsequently flows into Gota Gadavi canal," said HN Thakkar, Deputy Town Planner, AUDA.

"While Vastrapur Lake has been fully developed, we are now developing the other lakes in similar fashion and hope to complete them within a year," he added.

While the lakes already connected are being used as a means to recharge the ground water level, AUDA is also mooting to expand their capacities.

"We are trying to ensure that the storm water in the catchments area of a lake flows to the lake and recharges the groundwater level. Once that is done, the excess water will flow to the other lake and so on, and subsequently reach the Sabarmati river or the Gota Gadavi canal to be used for irrigation purpose," said Thakkar. He added that AUDA is also mooting to connect the lakes with the Narmada Canal to make them perennial.

"We also need to ensure that the sewerage water does not get mixed up with the lake water," said D Thara, Chief Executive Authority AUDA. "Ideally the sewerage lines need to be laid first before laying the pipelines to link the water bodies. We are also laying sewerage pipeline network in these areas apart from setting up two sewerage treatment plants at an expense of Rs 300 crore under the JNNURM," she added.

Heading: A life dedicated to a cause — in letter and spirit - Indian Express
Content:
In a mess created by the Gujarat University (GU) itself, the varsity has allowed self-finance affiliated colleges to enrol 1,261 excess students for the academic year 2007-08.

Forgetting the rules it had once created, the GU has allowed admissions in BCA and BBA courses, putting in jeopardy the career of the students.

As per the 2007 circular, a self-financed college must be fined for three years besides paying a penalty of Rs 1 lakh if it gives excess admission.

In the last academic year, seven self-financed BBA colleges gave excess admission to 490 first year students, while 11 self-financed colleges of BCA gave excess admission to 771 first year students.

Despite being aware of it, the GU authorities took no step against the colleges. GU's Controller of Examination J C Lilani admitted that there were excess admissions. He said: "I do not know why no step has been taken against them." Vice-Chancellor Parimal Trivedi refused to comment on the subject.

As for the losses, GU will lose a minimum loss of Rs 4,93,95,000 if the colleges are not penalised for their action in the academic year 2007-08.

Apart from the penalty per student, GU will also lose on the additional fine up to Rs 1 lakh per self-financed colleges.

An Admission Council member of GU said on condition of anonymity: "The students' admissions can be questioned if the matter goes up to the level of the Chancellor. The GU had asked for Rs 120.31 crore grant from the UGC for the next Five-Year plan. At the same time it is losing crores of rupees because of its lethargy, while the self-financed colleges are minting money."

Heading: Anganwadis indulge in ‘private’ talk; take out mass rally against privatisation - Indian Express
Content:
80-yr-old Mahadevbhai Joshi 'Ashk'to be honoured for his services to Kachchhi language

On any day, organising eighty reading sessions is no mean feat, especially if they are in a rare dialect like Kachchhi. But the state government is willing to do it to honour Mahadevbhai Joshi 'Ashk'—the man who has dedicated his life to develop the language—on his 80th birthday.

The Kachchhi Sahitya Academy set up by the state government some years ago is organising the event. The dates are yet to be finalised though, according to Kirti Khatri, president of the Academy. "Ashk has been conferred with the Gaurav Puraskar for his lifelong service to the development of Kachchhi. He has been working all these years for getting recognition for Kachchhi as a state language," he said.

Born in 1929 in Karachi, Ashk moved to Kutch in 1947. After finishing school, he joined the Kutch police in 1948 and worked for 10 years. Ashk, whose social work earned him the sobriquet, 'Gandhi of Kutch,' thereafter took to poetry. In later years, he started Kunjal ji Koonkaar (Voice of Crane), a magazine in Kachchhi, which has completed fifteen years now.

"It is my dream to see Kachchhi in the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution of India. For this, we are constantly trying to get the state Assembly to pass a resolution demanding the Centre to take necessary action for this," said Ashk, who wants the language to remain linked with Gujarati through the common script.

Ashk has published two collections so far. The first being Laheriyoon (Waves), which was very popular and 3,500 of the 5,000 copies published were sold in no time in 1989. His other collection came out in 2005 with the title Sambhren Munke Sen (I Miss My Dear Ones). His first collection Phoolan (Flowers) had come out in 1951.

According to Narayan Joshi, convener of the event, as many as eighty sessions will be held at Nakhatrana, Anjar, Bhuj and other towns in the state over a couple of months during which participants will recite Kachchhi poetry. The top three performers in each town will be sent in for a final round where the best five contestants will be given certificates, said Joshi.

"The idea is to inculcate a love for Kachchhi among the young generation and attract them towards their mother tongue," he said.

Heading: Two Lebanese men arrested for selling uncut diamonds - Indian Express
Content:
Anganwadi workers across Banaskantha district have been bearing the brunt of privatisation of the anganwadi centres in rural, town and city areas for over a year now, as administration in the anganwadi kendras in Sigori and Bhabar talukas has gone haywire.

On Monday, over 5000 anganwadi workers from the district took to the streets of Palanpur. A rally originating from Palanpur Civil Hospital passed through Kirti Stambh, Gurunanak Chowk and reached the district collector's office, where the workers submitted a petition against the privatisation of the centres to the collector.

Balkrishna Jirala, president of the Anganwadi Karamchari Sabha said, "We have had complaints from several anganwadi workers unhappy with the NGOs and trusts that have taken over a few centres. These organisations are here just for making profits. As it is, these workers get a meagre wage of Rs 1000. Many workers are exploited mentally and physically as well. After the privatisation of a few centres about a year ago, we have seen many ill results, which is why we had to take to the street."

While Integrated Child Development Scheme (ICDS) targets poor children, complaints about nutrition-less food infested with insects and stones provided to the children at these centres have been registered by the anganwadi association.

Anganwadi workers are also upset about being exploited by the private players and are scared of their future. While salaries of many workers were kept on hold for six months at a stretch, at times their entire monthly salaries were cut for taking a day off, allege anganwadi workers.

The Banaskantha District Collector, R J Patel, to whom the petition was handed over at the end of the rally, said: "They (anganwadis) have come to me with a petition regarding privatisation and other issues. They are not happy with the private trusts and NGOs and are demanding that the administration should not be handed over to them. They want a salary raise as well."

When asked what would be done about their demands, he said, "They keep coming up with such demands. I am just a messenger. I will send the petition across to the Health Department."

Heading: One arrested for assaulting and stripping woman - Indian Express
Content:
Receptionist of a local hotel worked as their conduit, say cops

The Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI), Surat has launched a search for the unidentified diamond merchant who was allegedly helping two Lebanese men in selling uncut diamonds. The officials have learnt that a receptionist of the hotel acted as an interpreter in the business deals.

In a joint operation by the DRI officials of Ahmedabad and Surat, Hotel Beleview near Surat railway station was raided on Saturday. The officials apprehended two Lebanese nationals Yusuf Oselli and Robar Hussain from the hotel and found rough diamonds worth Rs 3.85 crore, which they said they had brought from Zimbabwe. The duo failed to produce a Kimberly Process Certificate and other necessary documents of the rough diamonds weighing 3600 carats.

The men confessed before the police that from Zimbabwe they flew to Dubai and finally landed in India at Mumbai on September 15. They came out of the airport with the diamonds, undetected . Through their local ally, they had already hired an office in Arpan Complex at Rampura in Surat and booked their room in Hotel Beleview near the railway station.

Thereafter, they started meeting interested buyers through their aide. The hotel receptionist, Mansi, was acting as a conduit.

After primary interrogation, they were produced in court and sent to judicial custody. The officials also recorded the statement of Mansi. Investigation is on to trace the local diamond merchant.

An officer on condition of anonymity said that the police were on the case for the last six months. Without any local link one cannot do diamond trading in Surat. We will seek permission from court to take custody of both the foreigners to interrogate them further to find more leads in the case.

Heading: Dharavi redevp plan amended & revived - Indian Express
Content:
A lady was allegedly assaulted and stripped at Giyod village in Gandhinagar district on Saturday, just because her son had married a girl he loved. Police have arrested one Kesha Chaudhari in this connection.

Jasiben Chaudhari was beaten up outside her house along with son Jignesh and husband Ganda Chaudhari, after Jignesh had married one Bhavna Chaudhary, the daughter of Velji Chaudhary, a neighbour, about a week ago. Velji disapproved of the marriage, following which a group of about 50 people came to Jasiben's house on Saturday and assaulted her after an altercation. An FIR has been lodged at Barad police station in this connection.

According to Barad PSO Takhuji Chavda, while the FIR names 15 people, it also speaks about a mob of 50 others. Police are now looking for them. Meanwhile, Jasiben and her son have been admitted to Gandhinagar Civil Hospital.

"We are looking for the accused, but everyone in the village including the sarpanch is absconding," said Chavda.

Piyush Patel, Superintendent of Police, Gandhinagar, said: "We have carried out a combing operation in the village and posted security at Jasiben's house. She was beaten up outside her house by the group, which had some women as well. In the process, some of her clothes were torn; but the other women present immediately covered her with clothes, so there is no question of parading her naked, as it is now being alleged."

Illegal bungalows demolished

After a lot of political pressure, officers of Surat Municipal Corporation started demolition work on Monday of the 12 illegally constructed bungalows at Ramjikrupa row house, near Gajera School in Kartargam.

Armed with bulldozers and police officers, they continued the demolition work till late evening and may continue it till Tuesday.

The bungalows were constructed by Vasant Gajera and Dhiru Gajera, loyalists of Keshubhai Patel, the rebel BJP group opposing Narendra Modi.

"They had obtained plan of the construction of 92 bungalows in Ramjikrupa Row house at Katargam," sources said. The SMC had demolished four bungalows a year ago.

Heading: Mumbai Metro on wrong track: Delhi Metro chief - Indian Express
Content:
Suggestions from stakeholders incorporated; 300 sq ft homes for dwellers; work from next year

After running into a series of roadblocks, the Rs 9,300-crore Dharavi Redevelopment Project is finally back on course with the government finalising a revised schedule for the much-delayed bidding process.

According to MHADA vice-president Gautam Chatterjee, also officer on special duty for the project, the tentative timeline has been approved, in principle, by Chief Minister Vilasrao Deshmukh as well: The 19 shortlisted consortiums of global realty majors will be issued amended bid documents by the end of September; will present their masterplans by mid-October; following a deliberative process regarding each bid's technical merits, financial bids will be opened before November-end.

"If we can adhere to this timeline," said Chatterjee, "we should have the winning bids in a month from then." Work would then begin by early 2009.

The project aims at rehousing 57,000 slum families in free homes, to be built by investing real estate developers who then exploit the FSI of 4 for commercial realty development.

"We have managed to build consensus among all stakeholders," said Chatterjee, referring to a series of meetings held with various opponents and critics of the project, including former bureaucrats, architects, planners as well as political parties.

"The last couple of months have seen intense interaction between the Slum Rehabilitation Authority, Dharavi Redevelopment Project and stakeholders, which has yielded some very positive results," said project management consultant Mukesh Mehta.

Some details of the scheme have now been tweaked: The minimum size of all flats for slumdwellers is now 300 sq ft; those who currently own more than 300 sq ft will be eligible for 400 sq ft homes if they pay construction cost for the excess 100 sq ft.

Also, to mitigate the widespread fear that the monthly outgoings on a flat in a highrise would be unaffordable, the government will match the Rs 20,000 per flat to be contributed to the maintenance corpus fund by the developer with another Rs 20,000. "This will help create greater resources at the start — Rs 40,000 per flat — for maintenance," Chatterjee added.

The amended bid documents also make it mandatory for bidders to demarcate spaces for economic activities — Dharavi is a hub for manufacture of leather goods, food products, clothing, artificial jewellery and a large recycling industry. Also incorporated in the amendments are a conceptual masterplan, technical specifications of amenities and mandatory infrastructural development.

In a slum large and congested, the government will permit only minimal residential space development in the non-rehabilitation component. That means the largest chunk of the new Dharavi's realty development will contribute to creating commercial space. "These too will be on the periphery of Dharavi, and will be located closer to transportation hubs and nodes," said Chatterjee.

Heading: Lightning strike kills city doctor working with Bihar flood victims - Indian Express
Content:
Expressing concern over the government's endorsement of the Build-Operate-Transfer (BOT) model for all future Metro rail projects, Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC) managing director E Sreedharan has sent a letter to the Planning Commission, saying the progress on Mumbai's first Metro rail corridor has not inspired the "required confidence".

In the letter to the Planning Commission Deputy Chairman, Montek Singh Ahluwalia, he stated that all further Metro projects operationalised under the BoT model would run into serious problems. To support his argument, Sreedharan cited the examples of the first route of Mumbai Metro and Hyderabad Metro projects. "Worldwide, the experience has been that no metro project has succeeded so far on BoT basis. There are many instances where metro projects started on BoT basis had to be finally taken over by the Government for public good," the letter, a copy of which is available with Newsline, stated. The letter added, "Our sole example of Mumbai Metro has not still given us the required confidence in the BoT route. Even after agreeing to a viability gap funding (VGF) of Rs 650 crore plus 26 per cent equity, the project is moving at an extremely slow pace. The private sector efficiency expected from a BOT model is certainly absent."

Earlier, the Mumbai Metropolitan Region Development Authority (MMRDA) had mulled switching to the government-funded model, but later backtracked and proceeded on BoT model for its second corridor too.

A DMRC spokesperson confirmed that the letter was sent to the Planning Commission on September 11. "The intention of the letter was to draw attention to the fact that if a centralised form, a government-controlled system, is put in place, the advantages of a standardised system is possible, ultimately bringing the cost down," the DMRC spokesperson told Newsline .

On the criticism by Sreedharan on the pace of Mumbai's first metro corridor, a senior bureaucrat said, "It's always been his argument since he claims government-funded models progress faster than PPP models."

Meanwhile, senior government officials in the state feel it's extremely tough for a city like Mumbai to get Central funds for Metro projects unlike the case with the DMRC. "Mumbai never gets the treatment that New Delhi gets in terms of funding. Earlier, Sreedharan had come to Maharashtra and convinced everyone for a government funded model. Later, the Government of India declined to fund 20 per cent of the VGF and also refused to process the loan from a financial institution and asked us to go back to the public-private partnership (PPP) model," a senior official, requesting anonymity, said. The official added that the state government, after the Centre's declination, offered to fund another 20 per cent, but Sreedharan felt the Centre's involvement was mandatory in the venture. "He (Sreedharan) argued that the Centre's presence would isolate the project from local manipulation and interference."

The Metropolitan Commissioner, Ratnakar Gaikwad, agrees with Sreedharan's claim that Metro systems on BoT model haven't been successful. "But there are also arguments against public-funded models that we don't possess the technical expertise to implement such huge projects and the issue of time comes into the picture."

He added, "We went ahead with the PPP model on the second metro corridor Charkop-Bandra-Mankhurd despite constituting the Mumbai Metro Rail Corporation as we had already started the tendering process and it would have been unprofessional (not to go ahead). For the model of implementation for the remaining corridors, the government will take a call."

Heading: Former Dawood aide acquitted in JJ Hospital shootout case - Indian Express
Content:
Dr Chandrakant Patil (24) was walking barefoot when a thunderstorm struck the area

As A medical student of the preventive and social medicine (PSM) department, Chandrakant Patil eagerly volunteered to be a part of the first team offering medical relief to victims of Kosi floods in Bihar. But barely a week in his stay at a flood-hit district of Bihar, the 24-year-old doctor met with an untimely end after he was struck by lightning late on Sunday night. His body was brought to Mumbai on Monday to his hometown in Dhule.

Additional Municipal Commissioner R A Rajeev, who was appointed by the state to co-ordinate Mumbai's assistance to Kosi flood measures, announced a compensation of Rs 5 lakh to Patil's family on Monday.

The incident occurred around 10:30 pm in Saupol District, Bihar where a team of 40 doctors from Mumbai's health department was assisting in medical relief operations after a call for help from Bihar government. "There was some distance between their place of residence and tent which held all the equipment. While they were walking towards the tent last night, there was sudden thunder storm and he was struck by lightning. He was not wearing any footwear at that time," said Dr Amit Nohwar, Patil's batchmate at the civic-run King Edward Memorial Hospital, Parel.

A native of Dhule, Patil was a "bright student" having secured a good rank in both the SSC and HSC examinations. Patil completed his MBBS degree from B J Medical College, Pune and joined KEM hospital three months ago in PSM department.

"His death has come as a shock to his parents, as he was the main bread earner in the family. His mother is now in hospital because of the shock," said Anil Dudhabhate, general secretary of the Maharashtra Association of Resident Doctors (MARD).

Patil's family friend from Dhule, Pramod Bet said that both his parents were in shock. "We are trying to support them and prepare for the last rites," Bet said.

"He was a very friendly and hardworking resident doctor with a keen interest in social work — something he planned to pursue in future," Dudhbhate recalled. Patil's father Umakant works in a mill in Dhule while his younger sister is studying for HSC examination.

The 40 resident doctors from Nair Hospital, KEM Hospital and Sion Hospital were sent to the six worst affected districts in Bihar to help with flood relief operations. Five of them returned on Monday evening, while the rest were scheduled to leave by tomorrow evening. "The entire team is in shock. They are coming with the body now. Our current priority is to ensure that the body reaches his residence and the last rites are duly performed. Details of compensation and other matters will be determined by the BMC officials in due course," said Dr M E Yeolekar, dean of the KEM Hospital.

Meanwhile, MARD which had supported the team's visit and stay in Bihar is planning to appeal to the state government to offer some relief for Patil's family.

"The deans of the BMC hospitals along with other officers will be discussing the matter and we will see that something definite is done," Dudhabhate added.

Heading: Bomb on campus? Remark sparks panic among parents - Indian Express
Content:
A special TADA court on Monday acquitted former aide of Dawood Ibrahim, Brijesh Singh, in the 1992 JJ shootout case due to lack of evidence.

Arguing that the prosecution was only relying on the confessions of the co-accused, Subhash Singh Thakur and Shamkishor Garikapatti who were tried separately, Singh's lawyer Sudeep Pasbola told the court that beyond the confession of the co-accused there was nothing to prove Singh guilty. "As per provision under Section 15 of TADA, the confessions of accused can be used only if they are tried jointly. Confession when the case is separated does not stand valid," said Pasbola. The discharge application also stated that none of the witnesses identified Singh.

While Thakur was sentenced to life by the apex court in 2001, Garikapatti was sentenced to 10 year RI. Their co-accused, Surya Rao, former Bhiwandi-Nizampur Municipal Council chairman, was sentenced to 7 years RI. Six others were given benefit of doubt and acquitted.

On January 23, the Delhi police's special cell had arrested Singh from Bhubaneshwar. Singh, who has over 100 criminal cases against him, was missing since 1992. Out of a total of 41 accused only nine were brought to trial. The others were either discharged, absconding, or killed by rivals. One of the witnesses, sub-inspector Thakur, turned hostile.

According to the prosecution's case, on September 12, 1992, an AK 47 was used by the underworld don in the JJ hospital to kill Shailesh Haldankar of Gawli gang to avenge the murder of Dawood's brother-in-law, Ibrahim Ismail Parkar. Gawli was admitted to the hospital and was in ward number 18. Two policemen, P G Javsen and K B Bhanavat, were also killed in the firing.

Heading: Pay redevp tax late, shell out extra interest - Indian Express
Content:
A late night altercation between a security guard of Podar World School (IB) and a passerby on Monday led to a major panic among the parents of students of all five Podar schools in the vicinity. The security guard was asleep on duty at 3 am on Monday when a man driving by asked him what he was doing there. When told he was a security guard, the man became irate and and asked him, "What if someone drops a bomb here?" He then drove off.

The security guard informed the school authorities of the incident. Recognizing the possibility of a threat, the school authorities alerted the officers of Santacruz police station who rushed to the spot along with a bomb disposal squad and declared the threat to be a hoax.

"We got a complaint at 8 am by the school authorities and came here with a bomb squad. We searched the school premises for any signs of blasts," said API S Chauhan of Santacruz police station. "The security guard told us that the man who fought with him was in a black Maruti Swift but he hadn't seen the number. Had he done so we would nabbed him and saved a lot of time and panic," he added.

Soon after the incident, TV channels reported a bomb threat been received by Podar School. Panic-stricken parents flocked to the school to get their wards out. Stressed teachers attempted to calm parents while trying to make students exit in an orderly fashion. The panic in the air was palpable as teachers were informed that students would only be allowed to leave with their mothers or fathers and no relatives were allowed. "This panic is media's fault as the threat was in the IB school and not ours," said a member of the staff at Podar ICSE school. A visibly scared mother said, "We are not panicking. We are just worried that our children will be scared."

A similar incident also shook Shardashram School in Dadar where a hoax caller led the Dadar police and a BDS squad to the site to verify it. "The hoax call was made to police control and has been traced to a Public booth in Dadar," said Senior Police Inspector M Sankhe of Dadar Police station.

Heading: Man shot at on NC Kelkar Road - Indian Express
Content:
Enforcing developers to pay 100 per cent taxes before starting a re-development construction project on municipal tenanted land, the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation has revived its policy on capitalization value. Developers delaying payment of the tax on re-development projects will have to pay the tax with 18 per cent interest.

Builders redeveloping properties on BMC land have to pay 'capitalised value', which is calculated on the basis of ready reckoner rates, to the BMC. Ten per cent of this has to be paid once the commencement certificate for the project is issued while the remaining 90 per cent is paid after the project gets an Occupation Certificate. However, many developers evaded the taxes by avoiding the OC.

The civic administration has now suggested changes. Henceforth, developers will have to pay 20 per cent of the capitalization value before getting the Letter of Intent and the remaining 80 per cent at the time of getting the Commencement Certificate on the saleable component of the construction project. "This way, BMC will ensure that the money comes before the project begins. Since the saleable component of the building is most profitable to the developer, he will have to pay the amount so that the project can begin," said joint municipal commissioner (improvements) V Radha.

The civic administration had earlier proposed that the BMC gets built-up area equivalent to the amount due from a builder. However, it was rejected by the improvement committee. This provision has now been scrapped and in turn a new provision of 20 per cent: 80 per cent has been tabled with the improvement committee.

Under the existing guidelines, the BMC charges 10% of the capital value of a property based on the ready reckoner rates before the start of a project. The remaining 90% is to be paid in the next two years or on completion of a project, whichever comes first.

Two months ago, the estate department served stop-work notices on 16 builders who owed the civic administration Rs 138 crore, of them around 10 developers have paid the amount and the remaining are yet to pay. The builders failed to pay the balance 90% within two years.

Heading: Cafeteria Talks to guide young corporate employees to healthy living - Indian Express
Content:
A driver on his way to fetch school children was shot in the shoulder by two motorcycle-borne persons at Dadar's busy N C Kelkar road on Monday afternoon. The victim, 37 year-old Prakash Amre who was conscious when the police arrived, identified one of the accused as Baba alias Pradeep Gude. He alleged that a dispute over property had triggered the attack.

The Shivaji Park police have registered a case of attempt to murder against both the accused. Deputy Commissioner of Police Milind Bharambe who visited the spot said, "Gude has a criminal record and has over ten offences registered against him ranging from assault, extortion and illegal usage of arms dating back to 1997."

Amre was rushed to the KEM Hospital. According to Amre's relatives, he was operated upon and is now out of danger. Ravi, Amre's cousin said, "Around 4 years ago Amre and his family were residents of the De Silva wadi in Prabhadevi. However, when a local builder proposed to buy the plot of land on which the wadi stood for development, Gude had offered to help him evict all the residents for a commission. However during discussions with the builder Amre suggested that they would be willing to move if given a lump sum in return. Eventually the land was cleared without a middleman and Gude who had to forego his commission held Amre responsible for it."

Amre, his wife and two children had shifted to Worli but Amre continued to receive threats from Gude and his henchmen.

Heading: As global institutes look at Lavasa, a new education hub takes shape - Indian Express
Content:
Assochem, Piramal health group come together to spread awareness among youth about prevention of major chronic ailments

Soon a team of doctors will be seen talking to staff at office cafeterias and explaining them the prevention for the 'big five' chronic ailments — diabetes, heart disease, blood pressure, hypertension and arthritis — that are estimated to take millions of lives and cause a huge burden to Indian economy.

Waking up to this 'sleeping' threat to the economy, the Piramal Healthcare Ltd has launched a healthcare awareness campaign called Help Your Body, and is taking the project ahead with the ASSOCHAM. The campaign aims to spread awareness about prevention of the chronic ailments and tie-ups with hospitals and diagnostic setups for regular checkups.

"Members of ASSOCHAM will be starting with what we are calling Cafeteria Talks at their workplaces. ASSOCHAM will draw from our large team of doctors to give lectures on the big five ailments," says Swati Piramal, chairman of the Piramal Group.

The mission to start an awareness campaign was launched after one of their internal surveys threw up startling ignorance about health indicators among the young employees, and a global survey estimated that the cost of chronic diseases will be one per cent of GDP by 2011. "One of the largest tasks would be to re-orient health systems towards prevention. The Small Steps campaign was such a success in UK when they drafted the Euro vision. We need to see what we can do on the same lines," Piramal adds.

Assocham and Piramal Group have tied up with hospitals and diagnostic centres for the Help Your Body campaign. "With newer range of diagnostic tools available, there is a small change towards the preventive tests. Majority of them are still on recommendation of doctors. However, corporate organisations are tying up for whole-body checkup for their employees once a year," says Dr Avinash Phadke, who runs a diagnostic lab in Dadar.

The first phase of the project targeting diabetes, arthritis and heart ailments has already started, while the second phase with cancer, depression and addiction will start next year.

"The problem is too large and the government or any other single body cannot single handedly change the situation. We are making a start — hoping to make a difference.

There is a scientific approach to prevention which needs to be told to people," says Piramal.

Heading: Job-priority proposal for Marathis shot down by BJP - Indian Express
Content:
Though most campuses will be operational only in 2010, the city is expected to have a large, cosmopolitan student population, and planning for facilities are already in progress

Mumbai's students are set to get a variety of international and Indian educational institutions in what is growing to be an educational hub not far from the city.

For, institutions ranging from London's Oxford University to Symbiosis Institute Pune are setting up campus in the upcoming hill station of Lavasa, located in Pune district. Also coming up in Lavasa is the NSHM Knowledge Campus, an offshoot of the premier institute set up in Kolkata. As part of the Knowledge Campus, a retail, media and 'thinking management' institute will be also be set up, offering courses on Merchandising, Supply Chain Management, Inventory Management, and Customer Relationship, among others.

"The Retail Institute will include a gamut of courses, which can be from three months to two years duration," says Cecil Anthony, NSHM Chief Mentor.

A Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) has also been signed with Oxford University to start a centre for research and executive education in India, which will start by 2010. The course will be akin to an exchange programme, with students from London coming down to study in the Pune campus for three months, along with faculty members, who will be provided accommodation on campus itself.

The UK-based Girls Day School Trust is another institution that has shopped for space in Lavasa. The Trust is over 100 years old and was set up to promote women's education, and though it runs co-education schools in a number of places, this is the first time Indian students can avail of their educational facilities. "As many as 27% of the students from GDST go on to Oxford or Cambridge, and we can now offer that quality of education," says Nathan Andrews, executive vice-president of Lavasa Co. The Girls Day School Trust will eventually set up a residential International Baccalaureate (IB) school, which will offer A-levels and the ICSE syllabus, and will be ready by 2010.

Two autonomous universities- Symbiosis from Pune, and Christ from Bangalore — will also have new campuses here. The Ecole Hotelier de Lausanne (EHL), a Swiss hospitality school has already signed and started constructing its institute, with the first intake planned for 2009.

The educational institutions will cater to different sections of society, according to the planners. "All the verticals will have options for all economic levels. While one school might be expensive for some, others can find it a good option. We are also looking at 2 other schools- one, a world class for a lower income group and another, a school that offers CBSE syllabus," says Andrews.

Though most campuses will be operational only in 2010, the city is expected to have a large, cosmopolitan student population, and planning for facilities are already in progress.

"Apart from the facilities provided by the institutions themselves, there are going to be common facilities as well, so that every institute needn't replicate facilities but can concentrate on creating better in-house laboratories," says Andrews. Faculty for the institutes will be brought from universities and institutions in and around Pune and Mumbai, and will be housed within the campus itself.

Heading: No relief for slum-dwellers in Mafatlal, govt land case - Indian Express
Content:
The Bharatiya Janata Party has slammed corporator Vishwanath Maske for demanding 70 per cent job priority for Marathi manoos. The party's city unit has turned down Maske's take on 'job priority for the sons-of-soil.' Under pressure from the contractors lobby and non-Mahrashtrians comprising a large portion of the party's vote bank, the party has asked him to withdraw the notice from further discussion in the general body meeting.

Accordingly, Maske abstained from discussion on his notice on Monday, and the controversial issue died its own death. BJP-Mumbai unit chief, Gopal Shetty, said that although the party supports the cause of 'sons-of-soil', but there were discrepancies in Maske's proposal.

"We are with the Marathi people, but will not do anything outside the law. Maske had moved the proposal in individual capacity without taking party's opinion," he said.

BJP's unit in the BMC had earlier said that it supports the job priority demand. Shetty said that Maske's first line of the proposal, "Mumbai is the capital of Maharashtra and belongs to Marathi manoos," was objectionable. He added that anyone who is a domiciled citizen of the state is a Maharashtrian.

"We, therefore, asked him to withdraw the notice. The issue was in cold storage, after MNS raked it up. So there was no point in bringing it up," he said. Mumbai Newsline, last week had reported on how the BJP had jumped onto the Shiv Sena-MNS bandwagon in demanding job priority for Marathis. In his notice, Maske said, " Migrants are coming into the city everyday due to which the locals are deprived of job opportunities."

He has asked the BMC to give priority to the Marathi population, while recruiting staff in civic administration as well as other bodies like BEST, while distributing stalls in civic markets and even while appointing contractors for various projects. However, Maske said that he would raise the issue once again."There is nothing wrong with whatever I had demanded. Job priority is the only solution if the pride of Marathi manoos has to be sustained. At present, when the existence of the locals is in danger, how can one think of the pride," he said. He added that former corporators from BJP and other party leaders have also supported his stand. "Even if this time, the issue has been put aside, I will move another notice again," Maske said.

Heading: Five Pardhi gang members arrested - Indian Express
Content:
The Bombay High Court on Monday refused to grant interim relief to slum-dwellers who had encroached upon Mafatlal as well as government land in Kalwa.

The encroachers had moved an appeal before the division bench of Chief Justice Swatanter Kumar and Justice A P Deshpande against an order passed by a single judge on Friday. Justice RY Ganoo had earlier directed the Thane Municipal Corporation to demolish only those structures that have been constructed on Mafatlal Company's and government land which is over 60 hectare.

Justice Ganoo had adjourned the hearing till September 30 to decide on the issue of the remaining encroachments.

The encroachers had sought a stay on the order citing certain provisions of the Bombay Provincial Municipal Corporation Act.

They contended that they had documentary evidence to show that they had certain rights on the land owned by Mafatlal.

The division bench, however, observed that neither was any document attached to the appeal nor any document placed before the single judge.

Assistant government pleader GW Mattos reiterated his stand that demarcation cannot be made unless the encroachments coming in the path are removed.

Mattos submitted that demarcation is necessary to identify the land that belongs to the government and the company.

Taking an overall view of the matter, the court refused to grant any interim relief and adjourned the court till Wednesday, after the advocate for the encroachers stated that they had to attach certain other documents. "The court has adjourned the hearing as we have to file certain documents," said SM Oak, advocate for the encroachers.

Friday's order came in the wake of Thane Inspector of Land records' report which said that the actual demarcation of boundaries at the ground level is yet to be completed due to the presence of encroachments on Mafatlal land and partly on the government land.

According to the slum-dwellers there are around 9000 structures. However, Mattos last week pointed out a 2003 report filed by the TMC stating that it had removed around 21,000 structures on the Mafatlal land, but apparently all these were reconstructed following demolition.

Heading: Ambala: Water recedes after SYL canal repaired - Indian Express
Content:
Acting on a tip-off, Bhayandar police on Saturday arrested a gang of five robbers belonging to the Pardhi community from Osmanabad.

According to the police, the accused were responsible for a spate of robberies and dacoities in the rural Thane belt.

The robbers arrested from Osmanabad belong to the gang of Rajendra alias Raja Kale, one of the state's top five daocits, whose gang has committed around 11 dacoities in the past three months in the Vasai-Virar and the Mira-Bhayandar area.

According to Thane SP Naval Bajaj, due to a spurt in incidents of robberies and dacoities in the Mira-Bhayandar and Vasai-Virar belt, a special task force was appointed to nab the dacoits.

Bajaj said, "We got the breakthrough after we gathered information about the whereabouts of the robbers at Paltan. Based on this information, Local Crime Branch unit arrested these men from Paltan. These robbers belong to the 'Biscuitya' gang."

"After interrogating them, we received information on the whereabouts of the Kale gang that they were somewhere in Osmanabad,"added Bajaj.

Based on the tip-off, police sent a team of officials to the said location and arrested 5 members of the Kale gang, including Kale. They have been identified as Hirabai Kale (32), Surendra Shinde (25), Mohan Kale (19), Laxman Kale (26) and Balu Pawar (25). "We are also looking for other three members of the Kale gang, identified as Bhima Pawar, Kalya Kale and Parshu Kale who are wanted in Osmanabad also," added Bajaj.

According to Bajaj, the Thane rural police are also going to conduct inter-state conferences with police personnel of other states to combat the gangs of robbers operating from different states like Gujarat, Maharashtra and Karnataka.

"These robbers move between states and operate with impunity. Joint effort has to be made to fight them and we are working on it," he said.

Heading: Retired Armyman murdered in Zirakpur, cops clueless - Indian Express
Content:
Repairs were carried out today to stem the 60-feet wide breach of the Sutlej Yamuna Link (SYL) canal, which occurred downstream Punjab-Haryana border (between Sarala and Khaira villages under Ambala) on Sunday.

An Army team, headed by Col S K Vidyarthi, worked round-the-clock to plug the breach. Ambala Sub Divisional Magistrate M K Ahuja supervised the repair work.

About a dozen villages under Naggal police station were flooded on Sunday, endangering about 800 acres of standing paddy and other crops, after water was released from the SYL canal. The floodwater receded after the embankment was repaired.

Ambala MLA and former minister Vinod Sharma visited the spot to assess the damage to standing crops. Residents of Khaira village informed him that they had repeatedly requested the authorities to construct a siphon to divert rainwater to the Tangri river but their pleas had fallen on deaf ears. They had also demanded a 6-km channel be dug from Khaira to Tangri (parallel to the SYL canal) to dissolve the risk of flooding.

MLA Sharma promised the villagers that a survey will be conducted to assess the viability of the proposals. He also assured the farmers that they will be compensated (girdawri) for the damaged crops.

The residents of the affected villages also demanded that the Haryana government take up the issue of the SYL breach with the Punjab government.

The paddy crop was, meanwhile, damaged by floodwater from the Markanda river in Barara block. Tandwali village was flooded after rainwater, blocked by the Dadupur Nalvi canal, caused a breach in the bandh. The breach was, however, quickly plugged by the Barara sub division administration.

Heading: Bull’s death: MC employees ask councillors to join stir - Indian Express
Content: A day after a retired Army havildar was found dead inside his Preet Nagar Colony residence, the police were still groping in the dark for clues. A case has already been registered under Section 302 of the IPC. As per reports, 88-year-old Gurdial Singh, a native of village Retgarh in Yamunagar, was alone in the house when he was murdered. His son, Balbir, an employee with HMT Pinjore, was in Patiala to pay obeisance at the Dukhnivaran Sahib. When Balbir returned, he found the doors bolted from inside. After breaking it open, he found his father dead on the bed with sharp forehead injuries. Police say the murder took place late on Saturday night. His son ruled out robbery as the motive behind the death. DSP Jatinder Singh Khaira said the accused could be a known person and did not rule out property as a motive behind the act. Gurdial owned 11 acres of land in his native village. The body, meanwhile, was handed over to the victim's family after autopsy on Monday.

Heading: Scientists find a natural way to control mealy bug - Indian Express
Content:
The employees of Mohali Municipal Council (MC) continued their indefinite strike on the third consecutive day on Monday and permanently closed public entry to the MC Bhawan in Sector 68. The striking civic staffers once again deferred their ultimatum to snap essential services like power and water supply and cleanliness services in the entire city till Wednesday.

Moving a step forward, the agitating employees sent written requests to all 31 municipal councillors of Mohali, asking them to join the dharna and protest with them from Tuesday in their effort to pressurise the Administration for fulfillment of their demands.

Today, hundreds of agitating MC employees again held a massive protest rally and staged a dharna outside the MC Bhawan seeking cancellation of an FIR lodged against the stray animal catching staffers of the MC over the death of a stray bull near bus stand in Phase VIII here on September 17.

The employees had threatened to suspend indefinitely the essential services from Monday but they agreed to extend the deadline for two days following an assurance from Deputy Commissioner Rahul Bhandari.

A delegation of the MC employees again this afternoon met the DC, who assured them of fulfilling the demands till Wednesday, said councillor Harman Preet Singh Prince, who has put his weight behind the ongoing stir of the civic staffers.

"Now, the unions of all government employees of different departments have extended support to the agitating MC employees and agreed to abide by their call to snap power and water supply as and when necessary," said Prince, while quoting the MC employees.

Besides seeking cancellation of FIR against MC employees on the charges of causing death of a stray bull after subjecting it to cruelty while catching, the MC employees were demanding arrest of those residents of Lambian village, whom they had accused of assaulting the MC employees and obstructing them from discharging their official duty.

Heading: Three-day heritage festival at Pinjore to promote tourism - Indian Express
Content:
The farmers, especially cotton growers, will soon be able to control the pest attacks without using pesticides.

The entomologists at HAU have come up with a natural control for the mealy bug- a pest of cotton crop which destroys crops every year.

"We have identified two insects that can kill the mealy bug. These insects can be reared and multiplied in the laboratory and then set free in fields to check the population of deadly insect," said HAU Director of Research, Dr B.S. Chillar.

A team of entomologists comprising Dr Pala Ram and Dr R.K. Saini identified two hymenopterous parasites (parasitoids), during survey of cotton crop. They reported that the parasites are widespread in the cotton belt of the state. Field monitoring and laboratory rearing of the pest further indicated that the parasites killed 47 per cent mealy bugs on an average, which is quite significant.

"This is the first report of mealy bug parasitisation from Haryana," he claimed. During the next fortnight the extent of parasitisation of mealy bug by these insects is likely to increase, thus checking the growth of these pest. According to him the major nymphal parasite accounting for higher mealy bug mortality is aphelinid wasp while the other one is a small encyrtid wasp. These parasites attacked mealy bug present not only on cotton crop but on other host plants such as congress grass and palpottan as well.

"The mealy bugs harden and turn dark brown in colour and can be easily recognsied on the plant," he said.

Dr Chillar said the surveys showed the damage by mealy bug was not so high this year, as compared to last year. No patches of dried cotton plants were found by the survey team.

"Preliminary studies show these parasitoids can be easi ly reared in the laboratory. Therefore, there is a greater scope and hope for using these parasites for biologi calcontrol of this pest," he added.

Heading: Backward classes to hold rally - Indian Express
Content:
After declaration of Kalka-Shimla railway track as World Heritage Site by Unesco, World Tourism Organisation will market Yadavindra Gardens, Pinjore as a major tourism destination, said Kiran Choudhry, Minister of state for Tourism and Forest.

Addressing a press conference here today to announce a detailed programme of the 3rd Pinjore Heritage Festival from October 3 to 5, Kiran Choudhry said Yadavindra Gardens are ready for more number of tourists.

The three-day 3rd Pinjore Heritage Festival will be inaugurated by Union Minister of Tourism and Culture, Ambika Soni.

Chief Minister Bhupinder Singh Hooda will preside over the inaugural ceremony and Governor Dr A R Kidwai will be the chief guest at the closing ceremony of the function.

This year the festival would showcase handloom and handicrafts items made by the Haryana craftsmen. Cultural evenings would be organised on all the three days, she said.

It will now be a calendar event like Surajkund festival and it will be organised on the same dates every year.

She said with the World Heritage site status for the Kalka-Shimla railway track, the inflow of tourists at Pinjore would increase and it would become an ideal destination for tourists before they move on to places such as Kalka, Solan and Shimla, she added.

She said Bhima Devi museum is almost complete and it would be inaugurated with the dedication ceremony of the toy train. Haryana tourism would develop Kurukshetra-Pehowa-Haridwar as a pilgrim circuit and request the Union government for the funds.

In view of the forthcoming Commonwealth Games, Haryana would provide about 9000 rooms by the year 2009. The shooting event of Commonwealth Games would be held at the CRPF range in Gurgaon and the efforts are on to hold the kayaking event in Hodal, said Kiran Choudhry.

Keshni Anand Arora, Secretary Tourism and Satwanti Ahwalat, Managing Director Tourism were also present.

Heading: Excess water flow in rivers play havoc in state - Indian Express
Content:
A "Pichda Warg Kranti Rally" is being organised by members of Backward Classes (BC) of Haryana on October 5 at Rajiv Gandhi Sports Complex in Rohtak. The rally is being organised to express gratitude to Chief Minister Bhupinder Singh Hooda for his decision to allot residential plots of 100 sq yards to the Backward Classes and families living blow the poverty line free of cost, said convener of the rally, Dr Ram Prakash, Member Rajya Sabha. Hooda will be the chief guest and president of Haryana Pradesh Congress Committee Phool Chand Mullana would preside over the rally.

Phool Chand Mullana would visit the districts of Panchkula on September 24, districts of Karnal and Panipat on September 25, Faridabad, Palwal and Mewat districts on September 26 and districts of Gurgaon, Rewari and Narnaul (Mahendergarh) on September 27

Heading: Shiksha Adhikar Yatra wins approval from UN - Indian Express
Content:
With both Yamuna and Ghaggar rivers in spate in Haryana, several villages including those in Ambala, Sonepat, Karnal, Yamunanagar and Kaithal have been inundated. At least five people have died due to floods. Heavy rains in the past few days have damaged standing crops and vegetables. Release of 5.10 lakh cusecs of water from Tajewala Head Works in Yamunanagar in the last four days caused flood in

Yamunanagar, Karnal and Panipat. Excessive water from rivers in Himachal Pradesh too had created problems in Haryana.

As many as eight villages of Yamunanagar district and 11 of Karnal have been affected due to excessive water flow.

The Ambala district administration had to seek help of the Army to repair the breaches in the Satluj-Yamuna Link canal that submerged 1,000 acre of land.

According to sources, release of water in the incomplete SYL canal from Punjab caused problem in Haryana. The breaches occurred at a distance of 4 km and 4.5 km from zero point of Haryana-Punjab border. About 10,000 cusecs of water is flowing in this incomplete canal.

Also 3000 cusecs is flowing in the main canal.

Meanwhile, Haryana Irrigation Department has submitted a Flood Protection Scheme amounting to Rs 190 crore to the Ganga Flood Control Commission for its approval and funding so that the embankment of Yamuna river from

Yamunanagar to Palwal can be strengthened, besides undertaking other flood protection works.

Haryana Irrigation Minister Captain Ajay Singh Yadav said due to discharge of excessive water from Tajewala Head Works parts of the state have flooded.

He said on September 20 the water flow from Tajewala Head Works was 4.09 lakh cusecs which has decreased to 32,000 cusecs today. Such a level of water was recorded in Yamuna on October 17, 1998, with 5.41 lakh cusecs. Yadav said unless Renuka, Kishau and Lakhvyar Beasi dams, are constructed, no permanent solution of this problem can be found. Chief Minister Bhupinder Singh Hooda met the Union Minister of Water Resources, Prof Saif-ud-din-Soz for construction of these dams. Capt Ajay Yadav said Hooda assured the farmers whose crops had been damaged would get appropriate compensation.

Heading: HARTRON to diversify outside Haryana - Indian Express
Content:
Shiksha Adhikar Yatra (SAY), organised by the Haryana Prathamik Shiksha Pariyojana Parishad and conceptualised by the Centre for Alternative Dalit Media (CADAM), has won approval from the United Naitons Millennium Campaign. Its success would be presented as a case study at the UN General Assembly session, which starts from September 25 in New York. This drive aims at persuading those children who have dropped out of schools and their parents to enroll them back in regular classes.

The results have been highly encouraging. The number of children of school-going age who are not attending schools in Haryana has decreased from 1,47,913 to 64,185. This impressive decline of 57 per cent has been achieved in just a few months as this programme was launched in 2007.

This initiative has also won approval from the officials of Department of International Development (DFID), Government of the United Kingdom, which is one of the international funding agencies of the Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan.

The entire state was covered by 20 teams, with each team covering one district. Sustained community mobilisation, recruitment of women teachers to convince parents to send girls to school, emphasis on modernisation of madrasas, opening up of Kasturba Gandhi Balika Vidyalayas and creating links between various departments in the district were some of the measures taken to persuade parents to send children back to school.

The drive ensured that many children of migratory labour who had come to work in mining, stone crushers and rice mill areas of districts of Ambala, Karnal and Mewat got the chance to join the school. In Mewat, for example, there is a yearly addition of 30,000 to 40,000 children of school-going age every year. But most of them are either unable to go to school or drop out after attending it for a few years. Sustained awareness drives and interactions with parents, enabled the Shiksha Adhikar Yatra to put them back in school.

Heading: UHBVN comes up with innovative way to detect power theft - Indian Express
Content:
The Haryana State Electronics Development Corporation (HARTRON) is planning to diversify its operations into newer areas and is scouting for business opportunities outside the state. The corporation which, so far, has been taking up projects like voter ID cards or smart cards now wants to expand its portfolio in the power and other sectors by supplying equipments, providing managed services/facilities and extend the e-governance initiatives to other states.

V. S Kundu, Special Secretary and Director IT, Haryana said, "Apart from piloting the smart cards project in the state of Haryana, Hartron is planning to take up projects in the power sector as well through channel partners in other regions. The board of directors has given the clearance for channel partnerships. We have already bid for computerising a power utility's billing system in Uttaranchal in partnership with Techlabs, which has experience in computerised billing. "Research is going on at the HARTRON's Electronic R&D centre in Ambala to develop new software for distribution management, networking and grid monitoring for the power utilities. Kundu said, "We had only done the voter ID card projects in the states of Punjab, Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh and Chandigarh. But now we are thinking of going ahead with new initiatives like smart cards in other states as well. The smart cards project in Haryana is likely to cost around Rs 150 crore and will be complete within 15 months of approval.

Heading: Voluntary disclosure scheme by DHBVN - Indian Express
Content:
In addition to the existing system of detection of power pilferage, the Uttar Haryana Bijli Vitran Nigam would now detect the theft on the basis of consumption data available with each operation sub-division. A spokesman said here today the current electricity bills issued by the Nigam also have the details of units consumed during the cycle of last six bills by a particular consumer. It would help in ascertaining the consumption trend as well as variation in the electricity units consumed.

Consumer data in each operation sub-division has been updated which would help identify the consumers with suspicious consumption record. The number of power units supplied by a particular feeder and number of units being billed during that particular period is also being examined. Special teams would be deployed to check the consumers fed from the feeders with maximum loss.

The Nigam had fixed targets of detection of theft cases for each operation sub-division. Superintending Engineers have been instructed to send a weekly progress report to the head office. Simultaneously, checking has been started on the basis of information received under the theft informer scheme of the Nigam.

The identity of the informer is kept a secret under the scheme and an award of Rs 1000 is given immediately after detection of pilferage of power.

Heading: Rahul begins Punjab visit with a surprise - Indian Express
Content:
Dakshin Haryana Bijli Vitram Nigam has decided to introduce Voluntary Disclosure Scheme (VDS) of load for agriculture consumers. This scheme will be effective up to December 31. A decision to this effect was taken keeping in view the persistent demand by the farmers and the feedback from field officers, said a senior DHBVN official. Under the VDS, the farmers who have raised the capacity of their motors without permission can declare it voluntarily by submitting an "application and agreement" form. They need not submit any fresh terms and conditions or affidavits.

Their load shall be regularised without charging any penalty, said officials. However, the consumers will have to deposit advance consumption security and submit a test report for the extended load. The unauthorised extension in load shall be regularised with the existing system.

If the existing system cannot take the additional load declared by the consumers, then the existing equipment will be augmented by the Nigam. Farmers who have extended existing electricity supply to new bore may also declare the extension voluntarily.

Heading: Army observes Dograi Day - Indian Express
Content:
Arrives in Amritsar without any notice, pays obeisance at Golden Temple

All-India Congress Committee (AICC) general secretary and Congress MP Rahul Gandhi today began his three-day Punjab tour with a visit to the Golden Temple. Accompanied by the SPG men in plain clothes, Rahul Gandhi's unexpected visit took many, including the local police, by surprise. "We had no idea about his visit," said IG Border Range Rajpal Meena. Harpal Singh Bhatia, member, Punjab Pradesh Congress Committee (PPCC), who accompanied Rahul Gandhi, said Rahul was supposed to head straight for Chandigarh after Amritsar.

He is the first male scion of the Gandhi family to have visited the Golden Temple after the assassination of former prime minister Indira Gandhi. Sonia Gandhi had visited the Golden Temple in 1999 and, as in the case of Rahul Gandhi today, was not offered a siropa by the SGPC.

Attired in his characteristic white kurta pyjama and saffron headgear, Rahul took a round of the parikrama of the Golden Temple. The employees of Shiromani Gurdwara Parbandhak Committee (SGPC) led him to the sanctum sanctorum of the shrine, where he spent at least half an hour listening to the shabad kirtan.

He later partook the langar and evinced keen interest in the various innovative methods used to prepare the langar. He wanted to visit the Sikh museum, but was running short of time. He was also not given a siropa usually given to VIPs visiting the shrine.

Addressing mediapersons on this occasion, Rahul said he had paid obeisance here to seek blessings for the success of his visit to the state. "It has always been my heartfelt desire to visit the shrine, which has been fulfilled today," he said. Rahul Gandhi later paid tributes to the martyrs of the freedom struggle at Jallianwala Bagh, apart from paying obeisance at the Durgiana Temple. During his visit to the state, Rahul Gandhi is likely to launch an awareness campaign regarding the Indo-US nuclear deal, besides holding road shows in Patiala, Fatehgarh Sahib and Sangrur with a view to boost the ongoing recruitment drive in the Youth Congress ahead of the Lok Sabha elections next year.

Heading: Vigilance grills Chahal about Amarinder’s assets - Indian Express
Content:
The Indian Army on Monday observed the Dograi Day at the Dograi War Memorial at New Amritsar Military Station at Khassa. This day commemorates the famous battle of Dograi which was probably the hardest fought battle of the 1965 Indo-Pak War.

Major General PS Paul, General Officer Commanding, Panther Division; Colonel OJS Khangura, Officiating Commander, Dograi Brigade, and other senior officers of Dograi Brigade paid homage to the martyrs at the Dograi War Memorial.

The JAT battalion was conferred with the Battle Honour of Dograi.

Heading: Residents, leaders pour out their problems to Rahul - Indian Express
Content:
The Punjab Vigilance Bureau today sought to know the sources whereby former Punjab chief minister Capt Amarinder Singh funded his lavish parties while serving as the CM.

Taking investigations ahead in the disproportionate assets case against the former CM, Punjab Vigilance sleuths today grilled his former media adviser B.I.S. Chahal on how

Capt Amarinder used to fund his high-profile parties during his tenure as chief minister.

The former chief minister's media adviser was questioned for more than two and a half hours, during which the VB officials are also learnt to have asked him the details of Amarinder's assets, especially those accumulated during his tenure as chief minister. Chahal was also asked about the extent of his association with the former chief minister.

Chahal is believed to have stated before the VB that part of the money spent on Capt Amarinder's parties "may have come from the party fund". He, however, did not divulge any specific details of Capt Amarinder Singh's personal assets, maintaining that he had nothing to do with them.

Sources reveal that the Vigilance team had prepared a list of questions pertaining to Capt Amarinder Singh's assets, that were to be addressed to Chahal in connection with the disproportionate assets case registered against the former CM.

Though Chahal answered most of the questions raised to him during the questioning, he did not answer specific queries relating to Amarinder's assets

Chahal was earlier summoned by the Punjab Vigilance Bureau at its Patiala office, where he is reported to have cooperated with the VB team carrying out the investigations against the former chief minister.

A team of more than six Vigilance officials, headed by VB Patiala's SSP Shiv Kumar Sharma, questioned Chahal in the morning today. Sharma, when asked about the interrogation, did not give much details. He, however, said that Chahal had cooperated with the team during his questioning.

When asked specifically if Chahal would be summoned again, Sharma said, "We would first verify the information provided by Chahal and then ascertain whether he is to be summoned and questioned again." Chahal, when asked about his questioning, said his meeting went off "cordially".

The Punjab Vigilance Bureau had earlier registered a case of disproportionate assets against former chief minister Capt Amarinder Singh and had charged him with possessing assets disproportionate to his known sources of income during his tenure as chief minister of Punjab. Amarinder Singh has already been questioned once by the VB in Patiala for one full day.

Heading: Low basmati prices spell doom for farmers - Indian Express
Content:
The tussle between the members of the Chandigarh Territorial Congress Committee (CTCC) and UT Administration reached its zenith when the Congress leaders poured their hearts out to All-India Congress Committee General Secretary Rahul Gandhi.

An interactive session was organised with Gandhi and the members of Youth Congress of Chandigarh and Haryana as well as the leaders of CTCC, at the PHD Chamber of Commerce on Monday. Issues from land being acquired at throwaway prices by the Administration to the lack of importance given to the leaders — the list of grievances was long.

CTCC spokesperson Amarjeet Sethi while putting forth the sentiments of the Congress leaders stated that the functioning of the Administration was at an "all-time low". "We have no say in the decisions being taken. The Administration is treating us like opposition," he alleged.

Similar sentiments were expressed during a meeting of the Congress leaders held a few days back. The leaders had decided to go to meet UPA chief Sonia Gandhi to complain against the functioning of the Administration as well as UT Administrator Gen S F Rodrigues (Retd). The leaders said that the Administration was functioning in an arbitrary manner with no accountability or transparency.

The issue of land acquisition was also taken up. Chandigarh Territorial Youth Congress president

H S Lucky said that the Administration was acquiring land at Rs 7.5 lakh per acre and villas costing Rs 6 crore were being built on it.

"During the auctions organised by the Municipal Corporation, the land was sold for Rs 30 crore or more, the farmers are being cheated of their rightful due. The farmers need to be given appropriate compensation," said Lucky.

Besides, issues like the non-issuance of SC/ST certificates in the city were also discussed at length. The certificates have not been issued since 1996.

Former Mayor Kamlesh said that it is the residents of the city who are suffering. Those who come from other states have the certificates. Due to this benefits like admissions in educational institutes or other schemes started by the Central government cannot be availed.

The residents of Dadumajra submitted a memorandum asking for some action to be taken for removal of the garbage dump from the area. They stated that due to the non-functional Solid Waste Management Plant, the garbage was not being lifted yet. This was proving hazardous for their health. A few weeks ago, the residents had submitted a letter to UT Administrator.

Gandhi assured the leaders that their grievances will be looked into and action will be taken soon.

Heading: 45-yr-old held for rape, murder of minor girl - Indian Express
Content:
Farmers will probably have to wait for mid-October to get a decent price for their harvest

A crash in the prices of basmati has once again hit the much-touted diversification plan of the state. In its bid to remove area from under water-guzzling paddy to basmati varieties which need much less water, the state government had motivated farmers to grow basmati under a special campaign, but now when the farmers are ready to harvest the crop and take it to the mandi, they are discouraged by the low prices.

What's worse, the farmers will probably have to wait for at least mid-October to get a decent price for their harvest.

Notable here is that the area under basmati in Punjab has doubled to one lakh hectares as compared to last year, with the most commonly grown basmati varieties in Punjab being RH-10 and 1460.

Ravi Inder Singh, a farmer from Jainagar village near Patiala, says, "I have ripe basmati crop standing on 85 acres. I had sown basmati as I wanted to shift from growing normal paddy. But now the price that I am getting for my crop is just Rs 1,100 per quintal or at the most Rs 1,300 per quintal, whereas this price should at least be around Rs 2,000 per quintal." Ravi Inder is to begin harvesting his crop in the next couple of days and rues, "The price of basmati is likely to pick up around mid-October, but then I do not have the space to store a harvest of 85 acres."

Similarly, Kishan Mohinder Singh Saini, another basmati grower from Sunainheri village, says, "There is no minimum support price for basmati and if the state government wants us farmers to grow paddy, then they should give

us some kind of safety net.

The traders are fleecing the farmers claiming that the export of basmati is still not open and they pick up basmati at throwaway prices."

Another basmati grower, Karmveer Singh Sidhu of Sheetanwali village, says,

"No company sells basmati below the rate of Rs 100 per kg. If we calculate this way, the price for each quintal comes to Rs 10,000, whereas farmers get just Rs 2,000 per quintal and that, too, if the trader is ready to part with some profit. The state government should look into the prices of basmati too and see that the farmers get their fair share of price or else we will have no option but go back to sowing traditional paddy. We pay a higher price for seed and our input costs for maintaining basmati are much higher, but our returns are comparatively poorer."

Heading: Badal for a stronger state police force - Indian Express
Content:
A father of five children was arrested for raping and killing a 10-year-old girl after kidnapping her from his neighbourhood. The accused, Madan Lal, 45, has been sent in police custody.

Reportedly, the accused first tried to rape the mother of the deceased girl, but the woman managed to free herself from his clutches.

Pawan Kumar, the father of the deceased girl, alleged that yesterday night Madan Lal came to his house in his absence at 10 pm when his wife and three daughters were sleeping. The accused tried to rape his wife, but she managed to run out of the house and raised an alarm. "By that time, I also returned and entered my house along with other neighbours, but Madal Lal had already left the house and taken my daughter with him," said Pawan.

The police were informed and a search operation was launched immediately. The accused was nabbed from Phillaur bus stand today morning. During questioning, he told the police that he had killed the girl after raping her. The police recovered the body of the girl from some bushes close to the railway line.

Heading: Eight-yr-old attacked by dogs; injured - Indian Express
Content:
Chief Minister Parkash Singh Badal has announced that the state police would soon be given new and sophisticated weaponry to fight any instance of terrorism. Badal, who was speaking at Gubaya village while laying the foundation stone of a primary health centre, said, "A scheme is being devised to upgrade our state police and at the same time, new recruitment in the understaffed police department will also be done soon."

The Chief Minister added that the Centre should devise a strong policy to combat terrorism and a meeting of all chief ministers should be called for it.
