Stating that there is no threat to the life of Member Parliament Rahul Gandhi till the time he is in Punjab, Badal said the claims of the Congress that they had to cancel Rahul Gandhi's visit to some parts of the state owing to security reasons are false, as "it is our duty to provide full security to any VIP visiting our state".

Addressing another major issue concerning this part of Malwa, Badal said, "Water logging is a major cause of concern and for this the state government has decided to remodel drains, canals and other water channels. The entire project will cost around Rs 3,243 crore. This project will result in farmers of this area getting 30 per cent more water for irrigation purposes." The Chief Minister also added that the state government is consulting experts from the World Bank and others to find a solution to this problem.

During his tour of the area, Badal also attended a function to mark the death anniversary of Akali leader Nardam Singh Virring at Karunj village. Badal was accompanied by Chief Parliamentary Secretary Sher Singh Gobaya and Irrigation Minister Janmejah Singh Sekhon.

Baba Farid Aagman Purb to get status of heritage festival

Baba Farid Aagman Purb would be given the status of a "heritage festival" on the lines of festivals held at Amritsar, Kapurthala and Patiala from next year, said Chief Minister Parkash Singh Badal on Monday. Presiding over the 23rd Baba Sheikh Farid Rural Sports and Cultural festival, Badal said the Punjab government, in its next annual plan, would make provisions for celebrating the festival on a large scale.

Heading: Police keen on pvt security in public places to minimise security threat - Indian Express
Content:
An eight-year-old boy, Rahim, of Railway Colony near Guru Nanakpura, was attacked by stray dogs on Sunday evening while he was playing with other children. Rahim went to pick up his ball when three to four stray dogs attacked him. The dogs pulled the boy towards a lonely place and tried to bite pieces of flesh off him, said an eyewitness. Fortunately, some people noticed the incident and rushed to rescue the boy, who has been admitted to the Civil Hospital for treatment.

This is not a stray incident; children have been a target of ferocious dogs in the city in the past as well, but the Municipal Corporation Jalandhar (MCJ) has turned a blind eye to the stray dog menace in the city. In fact, three children have been attacked by stray dogs on three different occasions in the past.

It may be recalled that when the last incident took place, the MCJ authorities had conducted meetings to appoint dog catchers, but nothing was done on ground.

Heading: Despite expulsion, official website still has Capt’s name in list of MLAs - Indian Express
Content:
Not leaving anything to chance after the recent blasts, Punjab Police has directed its officers to ensure that in public places such as malls, markets and residential societies, private security is deployed. Directions have also been issued that without identity proof, nobody is allowed to use the internet cafes.

Enquiries reveal that the migrant labour working in the state can also be the target of the militants. Sources say that in a recent meeting, DGP NPS Aulakh instructed the officers that in order to minimise the possibilities of any untoward incident, people should be encouraged to to engage private security in markets, malls, multiplexes, places of worship, schools, residential societies etc. Efforts should be made to ensure that such places are not left unguarded, he said.

Confirming this move, Aulakh told The Indian Express, "The directions have been issued for the protection of the people, as the police cannot be present everywhere." The officers have been told that to increase police presence in busy places and on vital roads, police check posts (nakas) should be placed accordingly.

The officers have also been told to increase their intelligence gathering.

According to a senior official, the owners of these malls and other such places will be told to install CCTV cameras, to keep a tab on the movement of individuals. The field officers have been told that the internet cafes in their areas should be under a 'tight' watch.

The persons running these cafes must maintain a register and note down the credentials of each individual using the services. To rule out fake information, owners of cyber cafes must keep a photocopy of the identity proof provided by the users, to be used by the police if required.

Jalandhar Police had recently arrested Harjant Singh, and recovered a pistol, two magazines and other stuff from him. During his interrogation, Harjant revealed that migrants from Bihar who are working as labour in the state are their target. The blast at Shingar Cinema in Ludhiana some months ago also targeted Bihari migrants. The movie being screened at the cinema hall was Bhojpuri.

"Harjant told us that along with narcotics that are smuggled from across the border, there are also directions to smuggle weapons. The stuff is coming in through Ferozepur area in Punjab, Jammu belt along the international border and Rajasthan,'' said an officer.

In its recent seizures, BSF found that the smugglers were carrying weapons along with drugs. The total seizures this year are likely to be much higher than last year, and there has been a big jump in smuggling activities too, says an officer. "The smuggling of weapons with narcotics is a worrying factor for us," said an officer.

Heading: Mid-day meal scheme faces teething troubles in Nawanshahr - Indian Express
Content:
His expulsion from the Punjab Assembly and the subsequent legal battle launched by him notwithstanding, former MLA and former Punjab chief minister Capt Amarinder Singh still figures as a member of the 13th legislative assembly on the official website of the Punjab government.

While Amarinder's name as an MLA to continue on the official website of the state Congress may be termed "justified" (he does figures as MLA there) for the simple reason that party has been backing him and condemning his expulsion, his name on the official website does raise eyebrows.

It is an open secret that both Badal and Amarinder are sworn political opponents.

Information and Technology Director R.K. Verma, when contacted, said that updating the website was the responsibility of the respective departments. "In this case, it is the Vidhan Sabha Secretariat. I am not sure about their schedule of updating the contents," said Verma. "It is negligence. The website should have been updated and the name of Amarinder removed from the list of MLAs," said Dr Daljit Singh Cheema, political advisor to Punjab Chief Minister. "I will ensure that same is done immediately," Cheema added.

Heading: Govt apathy forces Olympian to consider immigration - Indian Express
Content:
Complaints regarding the packed midday meal, launched by Punjab Education Minister Upinderjit Kaur on September 16 in Nawanshahr district, have been pouring in almost from day one.

Sources reveal that hundreds of schools are missing the delivery of packed food daily in the district. Records of the Education Department reveal that from September 17 to 20, food could not reach over a hundred schools in the district. The information for

September 22 is yet to be compiled by the authorities.

Sources add that two schools in the district received packed food for just one day in the last seven days. School authorities in Balachaur and Mubarakpur say that in the last week, they received food only on September 18.

Daily, the children have been leaving school disappointed, after waiting for food. Interestingly, both schools are within four kilometers from the kitchen established for preparing packed food schools in the entire districts.

A common kitchen to prepare midday meals was set up in Barnala village. An NGO, Stri Shakti, has been given the task of preparing food.

When contacted, Ashok Mehta, District Co-ordinator of Sarav Shiksha Abhiyan, who is also looking after the midday meal scheme, said, "At present, there are some hiccups, and it will take some time to solve the problem."

Some schools have also been complaining about poor quality of the food. Mehta said that the food sampling is done by the Health Department.

Heading: HC permits felling of only ‘dangerous’ trees - Indian Express
Content:
Says despite having an appointment, she was virtually kicked out when she went to meet CM Parkash Singh Badal

Alleging indifference and discrimination on part of the Punjab government towards her sporting talent, Harwant Kaur, a discus throw player from Sabrawan village in Tarn Taran, who recently participated in the Beijing Olympics, has set her eyes on greener pastures abroad, particularly Australia.

Harwant, who went to meet Chief Minister Parkash Singh Badal in Patiala on Sunday, has alleged that she was treated very shabbily and not allowed in despite an invitation to meet the CM.

"I was virtually kicked out of the venue though I had prior permission to meet him," she said. She maintained that her counterparts in other states, who had returned after representing India in the Beijing Olympics, had been richly rewarded, but the Punjab government was yet to give her any recognition. "I am fed up with this indifference and am seriously considering going abroad, which I may do shortly," she said.

Harwant, who claims to have represented the police department in the National Games in 2001, said she was posted as an assistant sub inspector (ASI) in the police, but was reverted in 2005. "I was working with an insurance company, but left the job at the behest of the government, who promised me the post of a DSP when I was recruited in the Punjab Police," she said.

She added that she has also participated in the sixth Junior Asia Cup in 1996, seventh Junior Asia tournament in Bangkok in 1997, eighth Junior Asia Tournament in Singapore in 1999, Track and Field Senior Asian Championship in 2002, Asian Games, Busan, 2002 and Afro-Asian Games, 2003.

Hardev Singh, Harwant's father, a farmer by profession, said he had virtually sold his agricultural land to facilitate his daughter's dream of becoming a sportsperson, but said the state government had been insensitive towards her talent. "If encouraged, she has great talent and capability to do India proud in international sporting tournaments," he said.

Heading: Many parts of state battle for normalcy after heavy rain, water supply, power affected - Indian Express
Content:
Striking a balance between the issue of public safety and preservation of forest cover, Himachal Pradesh High Court today allowed the state government to fell only precariously dangerous trees in Shimla.

The court also directed the government to ensure that cutting down of trees be suitably compensated by plantation of at least four trees, in lieu of each tree felled in the larger public interest. The orders were issued following on a special petition filed by the state government seeking the High Court's permission to fell trees which have become dangerous and pose threat to public life after last week's heavy rains.

A division bench comprising Chief Justice Jagdish Bhalla and Justice Deepak Gupta heard the petition and closely examined the report of the three-member committee constituted by the Cabinet on Saturday. It granted only conditional permission for cutting down about 60 trees.

The court refused to go by the report and allowed felling of trees on case-to-case basis, supported by evidence and photographs of the trees to ensure that they were dangerous to human life.

Two tough conditions which the High Court has imposed are that four new trees will be planted at the site of each tree felled, and there will be no further construction permitted at the site of the tree that is felled.

The court categorically told Advocate General RK Bawa, Principal Chief Conservator of Forests (CCF) Pankaj Khullar and Conservator of Forests, Shimla SK Sharma to ensure planting of four new trees in lieu of the tree that has been felled. There is also a strict ban on granting permission for construction at the site of the each tree felled. The trees that are planted must be protected, the court has told the government.

Even though it was Sunday yesterday, the High Court held a special sitting to consider the government's plea for allowing felling of dangerous trees. It asked the government to provide details of the trees required to be felled in view of the threat to public life after the heavy rains.

As the case came up for hearing, the court expressed displeasure over the non-serious attitude of the government. The court noted that an official of the Forest Department was not present for the hearing of the case, taken up in the afternoon.

The Forest Department and the government came under fire for being unable to put forth its point convincingly, particularly about the exact number of trees required to be felled. The bench examined the photographs submitted by the government. It granted permission only for felling of those trees which are dangerous for humans now.

It also asked Principal Chief Conservator of Forests Pankaj Khullar to have a personal look at some of the trees to be felled, before any follow-up action is taken. The private individuals in whose premises the tree will be felled should also be informed about the conditions, the court observed.

Heading: SCA prez Shikha Chauhan attacked - Indian Express
Content:
Two days after the state witnessed the havoc caused by heavy rain, which claimed 38 lives, many areas continue to battle for normalcy.

The government has stepped up efforts to evacuate the stranded people at snow-covered Sarchu and Chhatru areas of Lahula-Spiti district. Helicopters are making regular rounds to airlift people, and also drop essential food items and medicines.

Several parts of Shimla are still going without drinking water and power supply. Mobility on the road within the town and upper-Shimla belt, popular called the apple belt, remains affected. The loss to the public and private property has exceeded Rs 400 crore. This includes 12 bridges. Among these, Bethal bridge near Rampur is vital.

All stranded students of Law College Shimla, who were staying at HPTDC hotel at Kharapathar, today reached Shimla. Over 800 students who had gone to Sarahan for a tournament are safe now.

The death toll in the state during past three days has exceeded 50, though officials put the toll at 45. This morning, Chief Minister Prem Kumar Dhumal held a meeting with top government officials including Additional Chief Secretary Parminder Mathur, who heads the team on disaster management.

Principal Secretary (Revenue) Prem Kumar, Principal Secretary (Home) Subhash Negi, Secretary PWD Balram Sharma and Secretary Revenue Rakesh Kaushal, and DGP BS Gill attended the meeting. They briefed the Chief Minister about efforts being made to rescue stranded persons, and to open the blocked roads.

Later this evening Mathur briefed the Chief Minister about the progress regarding evacuation of stranded persons in the Lahaul-Spiti district. The Chief Minister has gone to reached Delhi to meet central leaders and get relief for funding the restoration works.

During the day, helicopters could not land for airlifting persons stranded in Lahaul. Ten persons who were held up at Sarchu were brought to Keylong. Two of them were found to be suffering of jaundice, and are now being treated at Keylong.

Mathur said Deputy Commissioner C. Paul Rasu is camping at Sarchu to coordinate the efforts. BJP MLA from Lahual Spiti Ram Lal Markandym, who was in Shimla, provided vital information about the stranded persons.

The CM said that teams of Border Road Organisation and PWD are working overtime to open the road through Baralacha pass to Sarchu, so that the stranded people can be evacuated by road. These people had earlier been shifted to safer places towards Sarchu by the rescue teams of Mountaineering Institute, Manali.

The road clearance machinery of PWD will move towards Kunzum La today to connect Spiti with Lahaul. About 280 HRTC buses are stranded due to road blockades all over the state. About 180 buses are in Shimla district, and all passengers have been evacuated to safer places.

Dhumal also emphasized the need for taking up issue of disrupted communication network with the BSNL authorities, which is hampering communication with the affected areas.

Heading: More time sought for PTA inquiry into appointments - Indian Express
Content:
President of Student's Central Association (SCA) of Himachal Pradesh University, Shikha Chauhan, has registered a complaint with the police that four persons attacked her on Sunday evening.

Shikha complained that these persons, who were in a Maruti car, blocked her way and dragged her along the car. The number of car, she said, is HP-51A-0315. Shikha said she could not identify those persons, but they threatened her "with dire consequences" if she reported to the police, said the complaint.

Police have arrested two of the four persons who were in the car when the incident took place. The incident took place on the road leading from tunnel number 103 to Phagli, at about 5.45 pm on Sunday. Sunil Kumar, a taxi driver, was arrested from Krishna Nagar. His accomplice, Gulla, was arrested from Lakkar Bazar. Gulla is unemployed. Police said the hunt is on for the other two persons, who are likely to be arrested by late evening.

Police said they will be interrogated on their intention for the attack. Police have registered a case.

It is learnt that after the incident came to the light, Chief Minister Prem Kumar Dhumal had called up Shikha and assured her that the miscreants would be arrested soon. Shikha sustained no major injuries. She is the first woman president of SCA, and was elected to the post as an SFI candidate. The incident has sent shock waves among the students on campus.

Talking to The Indian Express, Shikha said, "I have never been attacked this way earlier. Almost immediately after the attack, the Chief Minister assured me of strict action against the culprits, so I have faith that they will be taken to task."

When asked if there was any student politics angle to the incident, Shikha said she had not thought of it yet.

CPIM has condemned the incident. Coming out in support of its student wing, Secretary CPIM Rakesh Singh claimed that the assailants attempted to kidnap Shikha. "The party apprehends a deep conspiracy in the attack on the first elected girl president of SCA, and political intentions cannot be ruled out," he said.

Heading: Mankotia to head Kangra Coop Bank - Indian Express
Content:
The deadline for submission of inquiry report of teachers appointed through the Parents Teachers Association (PTA) during term of the Congress government ended today, but the inquiry committees at many places have asked for more time to complete the process.

In April this year, the BJP government had ordered case-by-case inquiry of all complaints against the PTA teachers in colleges, senior secondary schools and middle schools, by three separate committees. When contacted in this regard, Education Minister ID Dhiman said, "At many places the inquiry could not be completed due to several reasons. We are giving them a week more to compile the reports".

Principal Secretary Education PC Dhiman said that reports from many places have reached his office. Reports from some other areas, he said, may take a few days more. "We are compiling the figures of cases where action is recommended against teachers for irregular appointments. Such teachers still have time to appeal against this decision before an appellate authority specially appointed for the purpose," Dhiman said.

Throughout the state, over 3,000 complaints were received against PTA teachers at various levels. Inquiry reports were then sought from the institutions where they are working.

Each complaint committee has three members. At the college level, the members are supposed to be the Deputy Commissioner, Additional Deputy Commissioner or Additional District Magistrate, Principal and the subject expert. At the senior secondary school level, the members are the ADC, ADM or Sub-Divisional Magistrate (SDM), Principal and a subject expert.

The members of the committee at the middle school level are the SDM, the senior-most teacher or Head Master, and a subject expert.

Heading: Uhl-III hydel project, started by BJP govt in its previous tenure, is still a distant dream - Indian Express
Content:
Rasil Singh Mankotia and Bhagwan Dass have been elected unanimously as chairperson and vice-chairperson respectively of the Board of Directors of Kangra Central Cooperative Bank today.

While Makotia is considered close to Chief Minister Prem Kumar Dhumal, Bhagwan Dass is close to Irrigation and Public Health Minister Ravinder Singh Ravi. Mankotia, who hails from Hamirpur district, had defeated sitting chairperson of the Board Prithipal Singh, once considered close to the Chief Minister.

Bhagwan Dass was Mandal Pradhan of the Thural Assembly constituency, represented by Ravi. The elections for the bank's directors had generated much heat, because many BJP workers were in fray.

Ravi was the observer for the election of the chairperson and the vice-chairperson. Talking to mediapersons, Mankotia said that a transfer policy would be formulated for the employees. He added that the Board will review the functions of all the branches, and consider closing the uneconomical branches, if required.

Mankotia added that part-time water carriers who have completed ten years of service will be made daily wagers and regularized, according to the state government policy. About cases of alleged irregularities which are under investigation by the Vigilance department would be discussed by the Board, he stated.

Heading: High Court upholds city school’s disciplinary action against student - Indian Express
Content:
Despite being one of the few pioneering projects that the BJP government headed by Shanta Kumar took up for execution in the private sector in the early 90s, the Uhl-III (100 MW) hydel project located at Jogindernagar of Mandi district stands nowhere 18 years later.

The execution of the project remains affected for the past five months, after Himachal Pradesh State Electricity Board (HPSEB) abruptly cancelled the contract for construction of a 9,258-metre head race tunnel (HRT) in April.

The construction of the HRT, earlier estimated to cost Rs 70 crore, is crucial for commissioning of the project and its power house.

But, after M/s Satyam Shankar Joint Venture (SSJV) — the company building the tunnel — was told to pack up just a few months after the BJP's return to power, the work has been hit adversely, raising doubts about early resumption of the project execution.

Also, the HPSEB is likely to pay a heavy cost for withdrawal of the company. The remaining work, costing barely Rs 20 crore, may finish at not less than Rs 50 crore, even if one goes by conservative estimates.

Admits Ajay Gupta, Managing Director of Beas Valley Power Corporation (BVPC), a Special Purpose Vehicle formed for the project execution, "Tenders for Rs 50 crore for the head race tunnel have been called, but no final decision has been taken yet by the Board. The work will start only after the firm for construction of the head race tunnel is selected."

HPSEB officials say the grounds for cancellation of SSJV's contract was basically non-performance and delays. But, they also add that instead of abrupt cancellation, the company could have been asked to speed-up work.

Company officials maintain that more than 73 per cent of the tunnel excavation was complete before the contract was cancelled. Only 2,403 metres of the remaining work was left and the company had made a representation to the HPSEB for resolving some pending issues like revised rates of steel and payment for installing additional dewatering pipe. Instead of giving a thought to these issues, the company was dumped.

The project, as per revised estimates, is expected to cost over Rs 800 crore and is unlikely to be commissioned by its target date of 2010. Initially estimated to cost less than Rs 500 crore if completed by 2005, the project has already been delayed by over three years.

Revenue Minister Gulab Singh Thakur, who hails from Jogindernagar, is understood to have already conveyed his displeasure to the government over the state of the project. "The project would have been commissioned long back. Even now its progress is not very satisfactory because the tunnel work has stopped," he said.

When contacted, Yogesh Khanna, chairman of the State Electricity Regulatory Commission, said he had asked the HPSEB to look into the causes of the delay and cost overruns at Uhl-III. "I will wait for the Board's report about the reasons before taking any action," he added.

Only last week, Khanna had ordered a probe into the time and cost overruns at the 12-Mega Watt Khauli project. Earlier, a similar inquiry was also ordered for the 126-Mega Watt Larji project, where it was found that gross financial irregularities were committed in the execution of the project, which cost the HPSEB over Rs 1,200 crore.

Heading: Taskforce focuses on solution to Tibet issue - Indian Express
Content:
Justice Jayant Patel of the Gujarat High Court on Monday upheld the decision of the St Xavier's High School, Loyola Hall, not to allow Simardeep, a standard XII student of the school, to attend classes but allow him to appear as an internal candidate of the school in the final board examinations. The school would also make arrangements for 'internal examination' of the student.

Simardeep, who had been suspended from school for misbehaving with two teachers, had earlier moved the civil court levelling religious bias against him. The court, however, appointed the district education officer (DEO) as an arbitrator in the matter. The DEO ruled in favour of reinstating the student.

The school, however, did not implement the DEO's order, owing to the serious nature of allegations levelled by him. Meanwhile, Simardeep moved the high court requesting that the decision of the DEO be implemented. The school also moved the court saying that it will not allow the student to attend classes.

In the meantime, both parties came to a mutual agreement. While Simardeep did not insist on being allowed to attend classes, the school agreed to allow him to appear as an internal candidate of the school in the board examination to ensure that his career is not in jeopardy.

Heading: Rock On! - Indian Express
Content:
A Three-day meeting of the Task Force on Negotiations (TFN), set up by the Dalai Lama, began here on Monday. The taskforce will chalk out a strategy for the next round of talks with the Chinese authorities, being held to find a mutually-acceptable solution to the Tibet issue.

The taskforce was established especially to assist the envoys of the Dalai Lama, who are participating in the talks.

Though the dates for the next round of talks is yet to be fixed, it is likely to be held in October, as was stated by Kasur Lodi Gyaltsen Gyari, special envoy of the Dalai Lama.

Prime Minister of the Tibetan government-in-exile Prof Samdhong Rinpoche said that the taskforce reviewed the outcome of the negations held earlier with the Chinese authorities. "We will also deliberate that the issues to be taken up during the eighth round of talks,'' said Prof Rionpoche.

Rinpoche said the eighth round of formal discussions between the envoys of the Dalai Lama and the representatives of the Chinese government will focus on implementation of national regional autonomy in Tibet, as stated in the constitution of the People's Republic of China.

Apart from the Prime Minister, the representative of the Dalai Lama in New Delhi, Kesang Y. Takla, Minister for the Department of Information and International Relations of the Tibetan government-in-exile, Kasur Tashi Wangdi, Envoy Kelsang Gyaltsen, Thubten Samphel, Secretary for Information, Sonam Dagpo, Secretary for International Relations, Tsewang Phuntsok and Bhuchung K. Tsering were also present at today's meeting.

Gyari could not attend the meeting due to some reasons. Ngodup Donchung, Minister for the Department of Security, Chhime R. Chhoekyapa and Tsegyam, secretaries to the Dalai Lama, Tenzin Geyche Tethong, former secretary to the Dalai Lama, were also present at the meeting of the taskforce.

Heading: Moment Of Honour - Indian Express
Content:
Most bands are born in school and here are some finding their voice in the city

If you thought 'Rock On' was just a movie, well, for some it was a reflection of the fact of life that music can be life but you can't make life out of music! Most rock bands take birth at school. We caught up with a few bands who have started small in the city schools, playing in basements but have an amazing talent looking for a platform to showcase it all.

St John's School in Sector 26 is proud of its band heritage. Michelangelo Francis, the art and music teacher of the school recalls his past and derives the need of a band in a school. "I was always very passionate about music but somehow never had the opportunity to be a part of a school band. When I was in college I was keen to be a band member only to realize that the lack of one in school had an impact on my skills. Upon return to the school, I wanted to set up a band which happened in 2000 with Soaring Eagle and now Wingspan." His opinions regarding studies being affected is contradictory to what almost everyone thinks. "Everyone encourages students to participate in sports. No one understands that this is also precisely the same thing. You have to create time to do anything in life. Music is no different."

The eight-member band 'Wingspan' is proud of its capabilities. "We were invited to be a part of inter-school competition in a local school. Since we all knew each other as musicians, we decided to put together a band and were fortunate enough to stand first there," informs the lead guitarist Mihir Riana. Nods Vibhav, the backbone of the band who plays the keyboards. "Music was a passion for all of us," he says. The band boasts of custom made limited edition shirts and they hope to stick together for long!

Elsewhere, escaping the teachers' eyes, we met Die-bollix, from Bhavan Vidyalaya. Cherish, the lead guitarist and also the founder of the band says, "Our weekend jamming sessions are paying off, and we are evolving." Though pretty new on the rock streets, these lads have high hopes and wish to cut an album soon. "We are holding auditions for a vocalist but nothing has been finalised so far." What about girls since it's a co-ed school? "See when it comes to rock, a female voice won't suit much, In case someone fits the bill, we will be more than happy," tells Shaleen the drummer. "Everyone needs to understand that music is a great platform today and support is needed," adds Vyom, the bass guitarist. "Our compositions are in place and we also plan on buying new equipment by December and hope for the best," informs Shivam, who plays the rhythm guitars.

But the situation is not the same everywhere. Renu Puri, the vice-principal of Vivek High School shares her thoughts, "I feel that any form of music can be extremely distressing for the mind and can stimulate the mind set, which is why we have different activities for the children, music being vital. Our school has an active orchestra which performs at the various school functions and a rock band as well." Neeraj Bakshi, the band manager and the school music teacher further adds, "The band plans to launch an album very soon. Most of the members are bright in academics and are passionate about music, which helps them see a future in music as well." And they are called 'Crossbow'. "We had won the under-16 category in the inter-school rock competition recently," informs Japreet, the drummer of the band who however rues, "Studies end up taking a lot of time leaving little time for practice." But we hope to hear them all soon.

Heading: GEM OF AN IDEA - Indian Express
Content:
Monday saw the Chandigarh Administration felicitate teachers who have helped make a difference. Here's meeting those who got the national awards & the life-time achievement award

We are turning a corner in so many ways. The education system for starters is trotting at express speed. The road blocks not withstanding, the system is taking under its wings novel courses, is building more industry relationships and is making studying interesting. Saluting those who spearhead this revolution and bring about the change was the Chandigarh Administration which held an honouring ceremony of 'Outstanding Teachers for 2007-2008 session' at Government College for Girls, Sector 11 on Monday. We bring to you those who have been awarded the national awards and the life-time achievement award.

Class Apart

If teachers want to take a lesson or two in how to teach the students, there can be no better mentor than Jasmine P Jakhar. Awarded the national award for her excellent ways of teaching, this English lecturer at Government Model Senior Secondary School, Sector 35, surely knows the tricks of the trade. "To love and understand students," she chirps and says that when it comes to her students she has never felt the age difference or the generation gap. "We all feel like one and work with mutual respect," says Jakhar, who started her career in 1990 from GMSS-35, was posted to GMSS-33 in 1998 and now is back to her first school. "While this award has only been given to heads of various institutions in the past, its an honour to get this award after just 18 years of service," she says that it's only when one works with honesty that jigsaw puzzle of life begins to fit in. Owing her success to her Army parentage and the value system imbibed from the missionary nuns of Sacred Heart, Dalhousie, Jakhar says that to teach the students one must not condemn them but adapt and amend the young psyche with a smile, touch of love and an extended helping hand." Well said!

She embodies success with casual panache. Her style is about celebrating an educated India. Her self-designed path is a reflection of ingenuity and perfection she strives to reach in her work. She is after all the life-time achievement awardee. Thirty years on and still on the mission, "to provide quality education," Pritpal Kaur, Mission Co-ordinator, Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan, has been on a roll. From initiating and promoting vocationalisation of education, forming courses for Central Board of Secondary Education to giving Class XII its present status, "I have been a part of it all," she smiles, amidst a round of congratulations from well-wishers. Having started her journey in 1971 as a lecturer in a Government Secondary School, she moved on to the State Institute of Education, Sector 32, in the research department. Pritpal is among the few who has helped education in the city shape up the way it has. "The counseling cell at SIE conceptualized by us got appreciation from all corners including the Central Advisory Board of Education," she tells us that the first comprehensive household survey in 1985-86 was also undertaken by them. "It was the result of the survey that five vocational courses were decided on. These were textile designing, dress making, stenography, food service and auto mill technology. The number of which has increased to 21 by now," she reels. Working with a focused mind and dedicated approach, even after her retirement from the post of Deputy Director in Department of Education in 2005 she continued to work for the cause. "And will do so till the end of time," she signs off.

Suppoting victory

It's not everyday that one gets a President's award. But when one does it surely is a happy moment. "And 15 scouts and guides prepared by me have got it," Dharam Pal Sharma tells us, as he receives the national award for outstanding work in education. Now, the Headmaster of Government Model High School, Sector 37, "I started teaching at GMHS-10 in 1978 as a Sanskrit teacher and since then have taught in GMHS, Manimajra, Sector 23 and Sector 32," he recalls. Boasting 100 per cent result throughout his career and been the Assistant State Trainer Commissioner, Bharat Scouts and Guides, UT, "I have also been the Stage Secretary of UT Education Department for State awards and other functions for the last 15 years," tells Sharma, who has to his credit about 100 poems and five plays. "I love literature and try to promote the same,"he states. Always going ahead of his duties, "my latest venture involves going to students' houses and knowing them better," he says to understand their interests is half the job done.

Heading: Talespin - Indian Express
Content: It seems to be the season of high fashion. The city's seen a host of shows this month and the latest saw PC Jewellers bring in a bevy of models to showcase their designer gold and diamond jewellery. The show titled 'Antragni' saw the likes of Tina Chatwal, Krishna Somani, Himani Thapa take to the ramp wearing the new wedding collection both in terms of ensembles and baubles. "Not many are aware that we also have under our wing a brand called 'Mangal Vasan' which brings in a wide range of ethnic dresses for all occasions for men and women. We decided to showcase the same through this show," mentioned Balram Garg, the managing director of PC Jewellers. With the wedding season fast approaching, the fashion show is well-timed. "We will present various collections such as 'Yuva' for young girls, 'Saumya' collection of lehengas, a range of gowns all complemented with jewellery. The highlight will also be our Daamini range of diamond jewellery," added Garg.

Heading: Small Talk - Indian Express
Content:
The best, as the cliché goes, was saved for last

The last two days of the India Couture Week, could well be termed as those that belonged to the genius of the four most popular designers—Tarun Tahiliani, Rohit Bal, Manish Malhotra and Varun Bahl.

There's reason why the front-row fashion editors left the room stating "Varun Bahl is India's best designer". The 32-year-old designer's collection was a lesson in fusion wear; he teamed lavish velvet tailcoats with opulent sequined gold lehengas, balloon hem kurtis, achkans, embroidered slips under net saris, and created garments that looked like they had walked out of a costume museum.

Easily the most awe-inspiring line of the week, Bahl's jewel-tone colours (emerald greens, ruby reds and deep blues) added to the Elizabethan-meets-Moghul touch. Vintage meets contemporary at its most delicious. His front-row comprised Prahlad Kakkar, Vidya Malvade, Urvashi Sharma and the delectable Randeep Hooda.

This was followed by yet another magnificent couturier, Tarun Tahiliani, who got Shilpa Shetty to be his showstopper in red brocade with semi-precious stones. The coy wannabe bride walked down with boyfriend Raj Kundra and sister Shamita Shetty hooting for her. Elegant extravagance is Tahiliani's 77-piece collection in two words. Be it the ivory chikan and gota empire line Moghul kurtas, Swarovski body suits or the chiffon gown or the printed kaftans. He went a little offbeat with jersey tops worn over biker pants. Couture demands perfection and this he proved with a line that couldn't be overpowered even by his sultry showstopper.

Manish Malhotra's show was high on couture quotient too. Strangely, the man roped in for his Bollywood clout, xmade his paparazzi-fodder friends stay away. His palette was an interplay of rich peacock blues, greens and pinks, in velvet and crushed silk. However, we thought that some of the embroidery on his clothes was straight out of his films. After a dismal show at LFW earlier this year, he seemed to be redeeming himself at couture week.

Rohit Bal closed his collection to a standing ovation from all. Exquisitely crafted with painstaking detail, each garment was a labour of love and dedication. Infinite layers, quirky cuts and tons of volume made his show a cut above the rest. The first batch of whites gave way to robust colours in rich velvet, silks and organzas. Called 'Cheshma Shahi', the collection stood for a maverick sensibility, far from designs dictated by current trends. Bal had something for everyone who'd kill to be wrapped up in such flamboyance.

Heading: Taking Stock - Indian Express
Content:
Strings Attached
In this workshop, a blend of theatre & puppetry give children a unique perspective

Here there's freedom to go beyond clichés and let creativity rule. The issues of the plays, Global Warming and Girl Child, may be serious, but the 27 children of the Navodaya Vidyalya, Sector 25, are giving the concerns an imaginative look and treatment. They are all set to present these at the upcoming regional competition of the Vidyalayas at Mandi and are these days rehearsing hard at the month-long theatre and puppetry workshop, being spearheaded by Anupama Neogi.

It all began with some theatrical exercises to build the children's confidence, improve their communication skills, sharpen their memory and then followed brain-storming sessions on the issues for developing scripts. "Once the mental kick was given, students were divided into small groups and were taken towards dramatization and gradually I weaved in the process of theatre from within and asked them to verbally voice their opinions on both the topics,'' explains Anupama. The penning of the scripts, agree the students, was the most stimulating and challenging process, with many a draft written and rewritten and puppetry being brought in to make the act more live and engrossing. Making puppets, connecting them with characters, changing scripts according to characterization, voice modulation, "it was all engrossing and stimulating for the children, who are all set to put their best on stage for the regional meet and then go on to the nationals,'' smiles Anupama.

Heading: Hundreds wait for hours only to get a glimpse of their leader - Indian Express
Content:
"Bahut ho gaya, chaddo tussi. Thankfully I am no longer playing the character of a Punjabi woman. I think it's time I started exploring other roles," chuckles actor Kirron Kher, 53, who plays a Bengali character in her latest movie, the delightfully titled Saas Bahu Aur Sensex. Kher along with co-star Masumeh Makhija and director Shona Urvashi (of Chup Ke Se fame in 2003) dropped by at Spice World on Thursday for the premiere of their film. The plot is based on middle class aspirations juxtaposed against the regular fluctuations in the Stock market. The star cast may not be too impressive, but there is consolation since it is the first Hindi film Warner Brothers is representing in India.

Kher plays a middle class woman, Binita Sen, from Kolkata who lives in a Mumbai neighbourhood with her daughter played by Tanushree Dutta. She wants to start life afresh but she lives in a flat with saas bahu serials obsessed women. So is she a fan of the Kyunkis? "No way. There is already so much drama in real life," smiles Kher. The stock market angle is provided by veteran actor Farooque Shaikh, who is a broker in the film and educates Kher on the stock market. "I am clueless about the stock market. I keep away from such things. Working with Farooque was a pleasure since he is a complete ladies man," says Kher. Will it work? It just might, considering Bollywood can be as unpredictable as the Sensex.

Heading: Tantrik’s tricks land him in jail - Indian Express
Content:
Hundreds of Hallomajra residents waited for hours on Monday in anticipation of the arrival of All-India Congress Committee general secretary Rahul Gandhi. The cavalcade arrived soon but left sooner before anyone could catch a glimpse of their hero.

Rahul was received at the airport by Mayor Pardeep Chhabra, president of the Chandigarh Territorial Youth Congress, H S Lucky, and president of Chandigarh Territorial Congress Committee, B B Behl, among others.

With tight security arrangements in place, people along with CTCC workers started gathering near Hallomajra with a list of their demands as early as 8.30 in the morning.

"To meet Rahulji, we can wait for hours. I am sure he will hear our grievances with patience and find a solution. I have come with other members of the Kabadi Market Labour Colony to talk about rehabilitation of those whose shops had been destroyed in fire," said Sanjay Kumar.

As the cavalcade arrived, Gandhi rolled down the window glasses of his car and waved at the crowd.

A Congress worker managed to hand over a file containing a memorandum to Gandhi following which the cavalcade moved towards the PHD Chamber of Commerce.

President of the Territorial Youth Congress H S Lucky explained that the stop over at the city was inserted in Gandhi's itinerary at the last minute. So he could not spend much time.

Memorandums to Gandhi

The Deep Complex Welfare Association submitted a memorandum to Rahul Gandhi highlighting the lack of facilities in the area. The residents stated that basic amenities like roads, electricity and water supply were not available.

Another memorandum was presented by the All India Safai Mazdoor Congress as they asked for the issuance of SC/ST certificates which, they claimed, were not being issued for a long time.

The shop-owners at the Manimajra Janta Rehri Market stated that even after their shops had caught fire several times, no permanent booths were being constructed for them.

Heading: Industrialists say Admn has ‘dual policies’ on land transfer, demand uniformity - Indian Express
Content:
A tantrik who befooled several people with his tricks was arrested from his Sector 22 office in Chandigarh on Monday. Sartaj was nabbed from his office — Baba Bengali — after a complainant lodged a complaint with the police after being allegedly defrauded of Rs 16,000.

Lured by an advertisement on a local channel, the complainant, Anju Sharma, a resident of Manimajra, had approached the 'baba' to solve her problems.

Sartaj told her that she was ridden with a bad omen (ullu ka saaya), the solution of which would cost Rs 16,000 that could be paid in installments.

With the help of Anju, the police raided SCO 2408 in Sector 22-C and unearthed various electronic and magnetic gadgets with the help of which he apparently performed his deceiving 'magic'.

Anju claims to have been shown a pot moving with high intensity as a sign of the 'omen' which, she realised later, had electronic gadgets beneath it.

Sartaj also reportedly threatened the complainant of killing her if she disclosed the conversation they had or the amount involved in the transaction.

A case of fraud and threatening under Sections 420 and 506 of the IPC has been registered with the Sector 17 police station.

Heading: Kabaddi kicks off Rahul’s maiden visit to Punjab - Indian Express
Content:
Be it the local politicians, councillors or the city industrialists, the Chandigarh Administration is inviting the wrath of people for its various policies, which are either being labeled as biased or 'not in the interest of the common man'.

A delegation of industrialists has recently submitted a memorandum to the UT Administration accusing it of indulging in 'dual' policies. Placing on record a list of their demands, the industrialists' delegation has asked the Administration to ponder on the issue of different policies for the freehold and leasehold industrial plots.

While the industrialists mentioned that it had been a long-pending demand, asking the Administration to convert their leasehold plots to freehold on payment of nominal charges, which should cover for ground rent, but the Administration is yet not clear on the rules.

While more than 90 per cent of the industrial plots in the city are transferred by way of GPA, the Admn is yet not framing an adequate policy to deal with the same. The industrialists even mentioned that in the wake of the exorbitant transfer rates, nobody in the industry has so far opted for transfer of plots.

While the transfer policy for freehold plots was in existence from decades ago, the tentative policy for leasehold plots was announced recently. The differences between the two policies are many. While the freehold industrial plot is transferred for ever, the leasehold plot is transferred only for the remaining lease period. While the 1,000 square yards freehold plot is transferred by way of registry, the same area leasehold plot is only transferred in terms of transfer of leasehold rights and that also for the balance lease period. While the freehold plots are being sold and transferred by way of registry; the freehold plots are though sold but not registered.

Demanding that the Administration should also allow transfer of leasehold plots but at reasonable rates, the delegation of industrialists had even met Home-Secretary Sanjay Kumar.

Vinod Mittal, Chamber of Chandigarh Industries, said, "There was a meeting held under the chairmanship of Secretary Industries. We gave him a presentation saying that the UT Administration, while transferring freehold industrial plot (measuring 1,000 square yards), gets revenue of approximately Rs 17 lakh by way of registry charges. Similar area plot, if it is a leasehold plot, gets transferred at Rs 95 lakh. The Home Secretary sounded quite responsive and has assured us a speedy solution."

Pawan Aggarwal, Industries Association of Chandigarh, said, "Transfer of leasehold plots should be allowed at nominal charges. While there is a lot of response from the market in freehold plots category, there are almost no takers for the leaseold plots — all thanks to the Administration's exorbitant rates. If the Administration allows the same on nominal charges, I believe many people would come forward."

On the other hand, when asked, the senior Administration officials mentioned that they were looking into the matter and would come up with a solution shortly.

Heading: Contempt notice to editor of Rohtak newspaper - Indian Express
Content:
All-India Congress Committee general secretary Rahul Gandhi today began his three-day maiden Punjab tour by paying obeisance at the Golden Temple in Amritsar. Then, the 38-year-old scion of the Nehru-Gandhi family flew straight to Chandigarh and made a dash to Mohali in a black BMW to catch a kabaddi match under the scorching sun.

Clad in traditional white kurta-pyjama and black leather slippers, Rahul said it felt good to be in Punjab.

The young leader addressed the gathering for barely a minute during his 45-minute stay in Mohali. "Main tin din Punjab ka daura karunga, main aap se milunga, aap se baat karunga, aapki samasyaen sunuga aur unka samadhan karunga (I will tour Punjab for three days, will meet you, talk to you, hear your grievances and solve them)," was what he said. Contrary to all speculations, the Indo-US nuclear deal (Rahul was supposed to launch an awareness campaign about the issue in Punjab) did not figure in his speech at all.

Punjab Congress Affairs Incharge Margret Alva, Punjab Congress chief Mohinder Singh Kaypee, Punjab Youth Congress president Vijayinder Singla and Kharar Congress MLA Balbir Sidhu accompanied the AICC general secretary. Congress legislature party leader in the Punjab Assembly, Rajinder Kaur Bhattal, was conspicuous by her absence.

Around 11.20 am, Rahul stepped onto the field and met the young kabaddi players. He sat on the field to see a match between Sahibzada Ajit Singh Jujhar Singh Academy of Chamkaur Sahib and Mauli Sports Club of Baidwan village.

Taking a keen interest in the game, Rahul opined: "Punjab's kabaddi is different from that of Uttar Pradesh's."

After watching the match for about 20 minutes, Rahul went ahead to greet the rural folk, lined around the field, with folded hands. But the cheerful Congress leader seemed in no mood to talk — ignoring reporters as well as the public.

Skipping the roadshow scheduled to boost the ongoing recruitment drive of the Punjab Youth Congress ahead of the Lok Sabha elections, Rahul's next stop was Morinda. Earlier, Rahul addressed Congress leaders from Chandigarh and Haryana at the PHD Chamber of Commerce and Industry (PHDCCI) in Chandigarh.

Heading: Ram Niwas is UT Home Secretary - Indian Express
Content:
I hereby call upon you to show cause, within ten days of receipt of this communication, as to why should I not set criminal proceedings against you at your own risks and costs. This is no judicial order but a classic legal notice sent by a litigant to an Additional District and Sessions Judge (ADJ).

Taking strong note of the objectionable language used by the litigant, the Punjab and Haryana High Court has issued contempt notices to one Prem Kumar Gupta, a resident of Rohtak.The notices were issued on two separate letters written by the Magistrate and the ADJ to the Registrar General.

In a letter written to the Registrar General of the High Court, Additional District and Sessions Judge, R C Godara from Rohtak, highlighted the 'objectionable' notice issued by Gupta, editor of a daily newspaper published from Rohtak.

The judge stated that a civil appeal titled Prem Kumar Gupta versus UHBVNL Limited was assigned to his court by the Rohtak District and Sessions Judge (DSJ). The case was to come up for hearing on May 21. For some reasons, however, the case was adjourned to May 24.

The case could not be heard on May 24, since the judge was busy holding a Lok Adalat, read the letter written by the ADJ. As a result, the case was adjourned to May 26. Gupta used to appear in person in the Court. The case was called several times on May 26 but Prem Kumar did not appear, therefore, the case was dismissed in default.

Terming the contents of the notice scandalising and lowering the authority of the judicial set up, the judge stated in his letter that the logo of the letterhead is abusive. "Prem Kumar Gupta has committed criminal contempt" reads the letter written by the ADJ.

Heading: Corbusierian euphoria could not be understood by city - Indian Express
Content:
Putting an end to all speculation, 1985-batch IAS officer (Haryana cadre) Ram Niwas has been appointed as the UT Home Secretary. A letter pertaining to the posting, sent by the Ministry of Home Affairs, was received at the Punjab Raj Bhawan on Monday evening.

Ram Niwas confirmed the appointment. "I will, most likely, join on Wednesday. The routine procedure of relieving the Haryana state and joining Chandigarh will take a couple of days."

The post was lying vacant since 175 days ever since Krishna Mohan was repatriated to Haryana on March 31. At present, UT Finance Secretary Sanjay Kumar holds the additional charge of UT Home Secretary.

Ram Niwas is one of the three officers, who had actively lobbied for the coveted post. The other two officers in the panel were R R Jowell (a 1986-batch Haryana cadre IAS officer) and R P Chandra (a 1984-batch Haryana cadre IAS officer).

Heading: P’kula gangrape: Son of Haryana govt official arrested - Indian Express
Content:
Hardly a day passes when one does not confront one or the other statement made in reference to the city's master plan that Le Corbusier had envisaged more than half a century ago.

Times, particularly since the early nineties, have changed considerably, and are now changing rather fast. No wonder that the city of Chandigarh could not retain its pristine Corbusierian look for long.

Slow-moving old timers like me often wonder at the fast speed of the changes that occurs everyday, or say ev`ery minute. A seemingly latest gadget launched today becomes outdated in a week's time.

Unlike the old generation, today's youngsters cannot think, even in their wildest dreams, of wearing and flaunting their grandfather's "once branded watch".

Today, the new socio-material changes, crowned by a flooded growth of money that gets displayed rather brazenly, have apparently made Le Corbusier lose his relevance, particularly in relation to Chandigarh.

In fact, this downslide began much before these changes started occurring. Perhaps, the Corbusierian euphoria, being alien to the local socio-political environment, could not be understood by the city. Or maybe, it was cursed by those who once inhabited this place and were displaced from their homes rather unceremoniously.

It is stated, though I am sceptical about the statement, that the city was visualised to "settle refugees from the newly created Pakistan". It is funny indeed, to settle refugees after dislocating others.

No wonder that the city, long ago, started accepting, though meekly but for good, the topping of religious buildings with antique Mughal domes and medieval pyramidal structures; the unplanned (but in no way ill-planned) Rock Garden and the construction of the multi-storied housing flats. And all this against the basic concept of Chandigarh, that Corbusier had once visualised for the city.

It is not strange that the once popular plain-looking Corbusierian cubicle constructions are today being replaced, as quickly as the changing times, with structures that have triangular fetish facades and are pale copies of American-Baroque architecture.

This change infact followed an earlier changing trend that one saw in the form of kitsch-looking heavy metallic entrance gates, in eccentric black and gold. The latest addition, to this growing changeover, has been that of the Baroque-styled lamp posts, which in no way look ugly or out of place.

True to the changing times, even the city's Tagore Theatre had to be changed, for better, to accommodate the new dramatic needs and advanced theatre technologies.

What Corbusier had "okayed" half a century ago cannot be taken as the Gospel truth for a lifetime; and remember that today, even a "lifetime" (validity), in modern mobile lingo, is for a limited specific period!

Since there is no denying the fact that today the city has come a long way from the old Corbusierian concepts, they need to be 'laid to rest in peace' in museums only.

And with the rapidly changing times in every field of human endeavour, it is foolish to keep crying, every now and then, over his dated plans and concepts.

Let us continue moving ahead, with the same pace as that of the changing times.

Heading: Bansal spoke to an HC judge 13 times before his surrender - Indian Express
Content:
Aman Ahuja, the 21-year-old son of the Assistant District Transport Officer of the Haryana government, was arrested today from his Sector 10 residence for allegedly raping a 17-year-old girl.

Aman, pursuing a BSc degree from Chandigarh, was produced in the district court today and sent on one-day police remand. He is one of the five persons who allegedly gangraped and tortured the girl.

The police officers say that the five were blackmailing the victim for the past one year. A resident of Sector 15, Panchkula, the victim had alleged that the she was gang-raped and tortured by five persons, including a girl, on September 16. On September 18, an FIR was registered against the five accused. A student of Class XII, the victim had stated in her statement that one of her former senior student, along with four boys, abducted her and took her to a Punjab village where she was gangraped and tortured.

"It was revealed during investigation that Aman was involved with the victim a year ago and had made a CD of her. The five were thus blackmailing the girl and called her repeatedly. The picture will be clear after further interrogation of Aman," said a police officer on condition of anonymity.

The victim claimed that her senior asked her to join her for some work in Chandigarh while she was in Sector 12A. It was from there that she was taken to a village. Sources said the victim was under depression for the past one year and was undergoing counselling.

Heading: Construction of airport at Mohali to begin next month - Indian Express
Content:
At the General House of the High Court Bar today, Anupam Gupta, senior standing counsel for the UT Administration, alleged that Sanjeev Bansal, former Additional Advocate General of Haryana and prime accused in the cash-at-judge's-door scam, had spoken to a Punjab and Haryana High Court judge 13 times over the phone before his surrender.

Without disclosing the name of the judge, Gupta said he (the judge) had called Bansal's mobile from his landline phone six times while the accused called him seven times. The duration of the calls was between 113 seconds and 47 seconds. The first call was made at 9:01 pm on August 13 and the last call was at 6:35 pm on August 16. The calls were exchanged during the period Bansal was absconding. "Was it mere curiosity that impelled the High Court judge to call Bansal so frequently?" asked Gupta.

Gupta clarified that the judge in question does not reside in Sector 11, Chandigarh, where the amount was "wrongly" delivered.

The General House, meanwhile, passed a resolution today stating that a narco-analysis test of Delhi-based hotelier Ravinder Singh, another accused in the case, be conducted at the earliest. The members also demanded that the CBI be allowed to interrogate Singh.

The speakers also criticised the order of the Special CBI Court, Chandigarh, wherein a counsel was allowed to be present during Singh's interrogation. Mincing no words, Gupta said: "The court should not have passed such orders, especially when the anticipatory bail application, had already been dismissed by the High Court last week."

Gupta highlighted the need of sustained custodial interrogation. "There is no substitute for custodial interrogation. Let the CBI interrogate Ravinder Singh and get the details of all the places he visited in the one month before his surrender. They shall also find out all about the parties organised by a High Court judge for his colleagues and that the catering was provided by Bansal," he said.

Terming the judge-bribery case as a tragedy, advocate P S Hundal said the Bar should ensure that the guilty are penalised. "This case is a blot on the judicial system. It is our responsibility to remove this stain at any cost," said advocate Dinesh Kumar.

Heading: Sahara India Pariwar held guilty of deficiency in services - Indian Express
Content:
The construction of the International Airport at Mohali will begin next month with the Airport Authority of India spending Rs 550 crore on the project. A joint venture company would be formed for the project between the AAI and Punjab and Haryana governments.

PricewaterhouseCoopers would be the consultants for the project. The work will start with the construction of a boundary wall and levelling of the 306-acre land. These decisions were taken in a meeting on Sunday and the Haryana government was asked to pay Rs 230 crore as its share in the project.

The Haryana Urban Development Authority (HUDA) would pay this amount to the Greater Mohali Area Development Authority (GMADA).

Punjab Chief Secretary Ramesh Inder Singh told Newsline: "The PWC has been appointed as the official consultant for the project. The total land acquisition cost was Rs 460 crore, which the Punjab government has already paid. The amount that the AAI will spend will be used for construction of terminal buildings and other infrastructure."

Highly placed sources said the custom and immigration authorities have agreed to allow the start of international flights from the current set up before the new terminal is functional. The Punjab government has deputed 10 police officials for the purpose.

Heading: We have lost our position in society:  LS speaker - Indian Express
Content:
The District Consumer Redressal Forum has directed Sahara India Pariwar to allot a penthouse to the complainant in Chandigarh at the same price at which it was advertised by them in 2003-04. If the company fails to carry out the order, it would be liable to pay to the complainant Rs 5 lakh for increasing the prices of similar houses besides the deposited amount of Rs 1,00,004.

The complainant, Balwinder Singh Gill, a resident of Bathinda, in response to an advertisement of Sahara India Pariwar became a member of the swarn/rajat yojna and deposited Rs 1,00,004 towards it.

It was averred that the scheme was projected to be an exclusive opportunity for the members of the scheme and would remain open up to February 28, 2005, with the booking for general public open from March 1, 2005, as per the advertisement.

On personally visiting their office, the complainant was told that he would be informed accordingly as and when the allotment procedure would start.  However, when the complainant again visited the office, he was told that allotment of houses for Chandigarh is over and he would be provided a house in Amritsar. It was asserted that as per the advertisement all the provisional members, who could not get the allotment of house, would get back the booking amount by April 15, 2005, and in case of allotment, the booking amount will be adjusted in the price of the house.

It was asserted that Sahara India Pariwar neither allotted a house to the complainant nor refunded the booking amount, thereby illegally retaining the amount with them. The complainant also said that the prices of houses in the surrounding of Chandigarh have escalated many times now than it used to be in 2004, thus he suffered harassment.

Sahara India, in its reply, stated that the complainant opened the account under Sahara Swarn Yojna and could not convert the account into Sahara City Homes Scheme and as such no question of allotment of housing unit to the complainant at Chandigarh arises.   It was pleaded that the scheme was tentative and was subject to various other visible points and terms and conditions contained in the brochure and passbook-cum-certificate.

The forum found Sahara India Pariwar guilty of deficiency in services.

Heading: Mansa Devi residents take charge of repairs as councillor fails to act - Indian Express
Content:
I am shocked that things have come to such a pass that the examination of two High Court judges by the CBI had to be allowed by the Chief Justice of India. It is a matter of great agony that the working of the judiciary is under the scanner now.

Expressing concern over the goings-on in cash-at-judge's-door case, Lok Sabha Speaker Somnath Chatterjee said: "I am sorry to say that the reputation of the legal profession has declined. So many 'unfortunate' developments are taking place due to which we have lost our position in society." He was addressing members of the High Court Bar around 2:30 pm on Monday.

But what shocks him most is that despite all such developments, nobody in the country is shocked.

Highlighting the role of lawyers in society, Chatterjee said: "It is their solemn duty to perform and safeguard human rights. Unfortunately, the judicial system is not working the way it should be."

The speaker added: "Everyone, who is a part of the executive, judiciary, media or citizens of this nation, should do some introspection. Inequality, hunger, unemployment plague our society. As the speaker of the Lok Sabha, I am the unhappiest person. It pains me the most."

Highlighting the squabbling, almost synonymous with politics now, Chatterjee said: "While a terrorist attack becomes a cause of concern for the party in power, the same issue is ground for criticism for the opposition. Such incidents are a common problem and no one should try to gain mileage from such issues."

Heading: HC to Admn: Examine feasibility to frame scheme for freedom fighters - Indian Express
Content:
With the councillor of the Mansa Devi Complex (MDC) having failed to act, the residents of the area took charge and themselves filled all the potholes in the area.

"It has been over four months since we have been noticing the poor condition of roads in the Mansa Devi Complex. After rains, the number of potholes in the area has increased and driving on these roads has become difficult," said Mohan Verma, a resident of the area.

Another resident of the area, on condition of anonymity, said, "It was after we found that despite several requests, councillor Laxmi Devi has failed to act that we went ahead employing our own labour to get the various pot holes filled. The lack of attention by the councillor has resulted in the entire area turning into a village."

The MDC councillor Laxmi Devi was, however, not available for comments. The officials of the Panchkula Municipal Council, meanwhile, subscribe to the universal answer — "repair work would start soon".

Talking to Newsline, Ravinder Rawal, president of the Panchkula MC said, "It is the rains that have stopped us. The tenders for road repair worth Rs 89 lakh have already been allotted and we are just waiting for the rains to stop."

Heading: ICICI to pay up Rs 50,000 compensation for unfair trade practice - Indian Express
Content:
The Punjab and Haryana High Court directed the UT Administration on Monday to examine the feasibility of framing a scheme for providing free medical treatment to surviving freedom fighters living in the city within a period of two months. A similar scheme is already in place in other parts of the country including Pondicherry.

As per the Pondicherry government's scheme, the freedom fighters and their spouses are entitled to (i) Free medical facilities in state and central government hospitals, and are entitled to 'A class' ward when admitted; and (ii) Free bus pass applicable in all buses with a Pondicherry registration number.

In a PIL filed by Advocate H C Arora, he had submitted that there are few surviving freedom fighters residing in the city, most of them being above eighty years and suffering from various ailments, but the UT Administration was not giving them any medical facility.

The Administration had stated in its reply that there are no rules or instructions for providing free medical facility to freedom fighters. The government's counsel submitted before the Bench today that none of the freedom fighters had submitted any representation to the government seeking free medical treatment.

"We fail to understand why a scheme providing free medical treatment to freedom fighters cannot be framed by the government when such a scheme has already been framed by UT Pondicherry, which is also under the same Central government," observed the High Court. "If the UT Administration decides to frame a scheme, it should also issue appropriate instructions to the concerned hospitals," the Division Bench further observed while disposing of the PIL.

Heading: City’s ‘first teacher’ wants Jan 4 as Education Day - Indian Express
Content:
The District Consumer Disputes Redresssal Forum has directed the ICICI Bank and ICICI Lombard General Insurance to pay a sum of Rs 50,000 as penalty for indulging in unfair trade practice and making unsolicited call at the house of a complainant causing him mental, physical harassment and financial loss.

According to the complainant —- Thandi Ram — he had an account with the ICICI Bank and was also a holder of its credit card. He alleged that through the bank statement, he came to know that apart from the audit debit of EMI of a loan taken by him, the bank was auto debiting a premium for an insurance cover, mounting to Rs 1,773, through ICICI Lombard, without his consent. He claimed neither he nor his wife had ever applied for the insurance cover or had ever signed any document for it.

He approached the bank who then kept on delaying the matter. He then got his insurance cancelled. He was again taken aback, when he saw that Rs 6,188 had been auto-debited for the insurance. Ram claimed that when he approached the bank, they "refused to refund the EMIs".

ICICI Bank, in its reply, stated that the amount was auto debited on account of EMI towards the loan. They claimed that Rs 1773 was not debited towards the insurance as alleged but towards the previous balance of the credit card.

The forum found that unsolicited calls were made to the complainant by the bank when he was not at home. It was proclaimed that the wife of the complainant had consented for taking insurance policy. "We think that for making this unsolicited call the OP Insurance Company should be penalised to pay compensation to the complainant," the forum said.

The forum also said the copy of the insurance policy has not been supplied to the complainant.

Heading: Farmers dry grains on road, block traffic, cops ‘unaware’ - Indian Express
Content:
With moist eyes and an overwhelming feeling of pride, 89-year-old Kawar Babu Singh, the first teacher to be employed by the Education department, sat upright in his chair as the UT Administrator General Rodrigues stepped down from the stage to felicitate him.

Singh was felicitated at the Teachers' Day function held in the auditorium of Government College for Girls, Sector 11, on Monday. With several state, national and other awards in his kitty, Singh is still dedicated towards the cause of education in the city and wants it to grow by leaps and bounds.

He also wishes January 4 to be celebrated as Education Day as it was on that day that he had started his long and fruitful journey with the first government institution way back in 1952 with just three students, he told Newsline.

The 'pioneer of education' in the city, he feels that education in the city has gone a long way since he received the first state award in 1968. Going down nostalgia lane, he says, "When I started teaching, there was no infrastructure. I used to take classes under a mango tree. Later, the Administration arranged for tents in Sector 27 and it was many years before a proper classroom was constructed". Singh states that education is one thing that an individual should never be satisfied with and should go to the extreme to attain the highest level of knowledge.

He recalls Prof R C Sobti, now Vice-Chancellor of Panjab University, to be his favourite student. "Over 70 students of mine are IAS and IPS officers in Haryana, Himachal and Chandigarh," he says proudly. Adding a word of advice for students, he says, "Once you take up a task, one should never look back. Also it is only determination and hard work that takes an individual to the top".

He also said that with a surge in infrastructure and resources, the Education department should look for more ways and means to help students come forward, especially from the socially backward segments, "as they are the ones who deserve it the most."

Heading: World Peace Day celebrated at Bhaddal - Indian Express
Content:
Grains scattered everywhere, roads blocked for commuters while the Panchkula police enjoy their 'nap' completely unaware — Sector 20 in Panchkula has stood witness to this unusual drama over the last three days.

As farmers at the Panchkula Kisan Mandi went about drying grain on the road, commuters were inconvenienced as traffic had to be diverted to ease out the traffic jam.

For the farmers, this has been a process continuing for the last three days, the traffic police officials appeared unaware of the traffic diversion made by the farmers.

"It has been three days now since the wet grain is being dried on this road. In fact there is not enough space for farmers to spread their grain in the sun in the Kisan Mandi premises, so we thought it better to use the road for the same", said Mohan Singh, one of the farmers.

He added that though no traffic police official was informed about the diversion, a wooden ladder had been kept indicating the road is closed for traffic.

The commuters, meanwhile, are irked with the "unofficial traffic diversion". Sameer Narang, a resident of Sector 21, said: "While the traffic has been diverted on this road, there is hardly any police official to assist commuters. As this particular road directly meets the National Highway-73 (Zirakpur- Kalka), the entire patch has become accident prone."

The problem has been aggravated with big potholes on the entire patch after heavy rains lashed the city.

Talking to Newsline, a traffic police official, on condition of anonymity, said, "We are not aware of any diversions made on the road and have not received any information regarding the issue. If such a diversion has been created and the road been blocked by the farmers, we would look into the matter immediately."

Heading: Shift dairies and cattle out of Kharar, orders civic body - Indian Express
Content: International Day of Peace was observed at the Institute of Engineering and Technology (IET), Bhaddal. Rupnagar ADC Kavita Mohan Singh Chouhan was the chief guest on the occasion and asked students to come forward and contribute something concrete for the prevalence of world peace. IET CEO Ravinder Singh recited a poem along with his presentation depicting the agony of war and its impact on the coming generations.

Heading: A day of honour and rewards at GCG-11 - Indian Express
Content:
The Kharar Municipal Council (MC) has asked the local residents to shift their dairies, cattle sheds and cow dung heaps out of the municipal limits within a month, failing which it will use force and act against the defaulters.

MC Executive Officer (EO) Sunil Kumar Gulati served the ultimatum to the residents while acting on the order of Punjab and Haryana High Court.

Allowing the writ petition filed by a Kharar resident, Baljit Singh, the division bench of the High Court, comprising Justice Ashutosh Mohunta  and Justice Rajan Gupta, had had directed the MC EO on August 12 to initiate action against all those persons who were keeping cattle in residential houses or plots for commercial purposes.

Baljit had moved the High Court seeking action for shifting of dairy and cattle shed with 15 buffaloes, removal of high velocity diesel engine and heaps of cow dung in respect of dairy or cattle shed being run by one Raja Singh behind his house.

Responding to the petition, Raja's counsel submitted that there were a whole lot of other dairies functioning from residential areas and no action was being initiated by the MC against the other dairy owners or persons who were maintaining cattle in their houses.

After hearing counsels for the rival parties, the High Court judges said that running a business of dairy farm from residential houses and maintaining cattle shed as well as 15 buffaloes, as has been done by Raja Singh, was not only creating nuisance to the petitioner in particular but also to the other residents of the locality.

A perusal of file on record also showed that numerous complaints have been filed before the MC EO to remove the nuisance as the entire atmosphere was vitiated on account of the smell as well as decomposed cow dung, which was lying in the plot and providing a breeding space to mosquitoes and flies.

The High Court directed Raja to stop the business of dairy farm and remove the cattle within a period of two months from the issuance of the order. "In case he does not stop the business, then MC EO is directed to take steps to remove the nuisance," the High Court had ordered.

Confirming the action, the MC EO told Newsline that besides making public announcement to shift dairies, cattle sheds and cow dung heaps out of municipal limits, a final notice was served to Raja to comply with the High Court order within the stipulated time period, failing which the MC will take action.

Heading: Patiala gangster held with Rs 3 lakh fake currency - Indian Express
Content:
The UT Education department on Monday celebrated Teachers' Day at the Government College for Girls, Sector 11, in a unique way by inviting awardees of all the previous years. The important guests for the day, besides the awardees of this year, were the old familiar faces who were honoured in the past, but now are a forgotten tale.
