The officials present at the function included UT Administrator S F Rodrigues, Director Higher Education Raji P Srivastava and Director Public Instructions (Schools) S K Setia.

The function began with the General Rodrigues giving away the Lifetime achievement award to Pritpal Kaur, coordinator for SSA.

The national awards were presented to Jasmine P Jakhar, Dharam Pal Sharma while state awards were given to Rita Batra, Manoj Kumar Sharda, Dr Anil Gugnani, Preeti Garg, Sweety Behl, Pushpa Rani, Dalvinder Kaur, Gyan Chand, Narinder Shastri.

Commendation certificates were given to Seema Malhotra, Parkash Kaur, Amita, Padma Rani, Rajesh Kumar, Manjeet Jauhar and Neeta Monga.

Talking to Newsline, Pritpal Kaur said, "I have been awarded for my work and the same has motivated me to continue with more zeal and enthusiasm."

Jasmine Jakhar added, "I am happy and the award has motivated me to do a lot better."

Besides schoolteachers, many NGOs were also awarded for their commendable work towards society.

The Durga Das Foundaton, Kusum Arora Memorial trust, Society for meritorious students, Saupin's community service organisation and a few others were a few among those awarded. Some were also honoured for their volunteering work. Among them, Dr Manjeet Paintal, who is working for the dropouts, says, "The award means a lot to me and I am glad to have received it."

Speaking on the occasion, General Rodrigues called upon the teaching community to be innovative and reorient the learning processes to encourage children to achieve academic brilliance.

He said the programme has three major elements relating to basic human values, with the focus on a personal value system, the inculcating of a sense of responsibility towards society and ones duty to the state and the nation.

S K Setia, DPI (Schools), in his welcome address highlighted the activities and achievements of the Education department.

Heading: ‘Inflation has taught us to spend money judiciously’ - Indian Express
Content:
In a major breakthrough, the Kharar police arrested a notorious criminal of Patiala on Monday and claimed to have recovered counterfeit currency amounting to Rs 3.7 lakh from him.

Elated over the catch, Kharar Station House Officer (SHO) Dalbeer Singh hoped it was the record recovery of counterfeit currency in this part of the region.

The SHO told Newsline that Rajwinder Singh of Ghumar Nagar in Patiala was on his way to supply fake currency notes of Rs 500 and Rs 100 denomination to his clients in Mohali and its vicinity when a police party intercepted his Chevrolet Tavera on the Kharar-Banur Road near Santemajra village in Kharar this evening.

"During preliminary interrogation, he admitted having much more counterfeit currency stock at his own printing unit somewhere in Patiala," the SHO said, adding the accused was facing charges of dacoity, rioting, charges under Arms Act, cheating and other crimes in different parts of the state.

Rajwinder, according to SHO, was arrested for the second time this year with counterfeit currency after his first arrest in Rajpura early in 2008.

"He confessed to be in this business for the past almost a decade, during which he was able have a well-knit network for printing and supplying fake currency notes," the SHO said.

The SHO said besides impounding Rajwinder's printing unit and confiscating stocks of his counterfeit currency, his entire network will also be unearthed with the identification of his links, clients and all others involved in the illegal trade, causing great loss directly to the country's exchequer.

In his mid-40s, Rajwinder was booked under Sections 489-A and 489-B of the IPC and will be produced before a local court on Tuesday to procure his police remand.

Heading: MCM row: Rival groups reach compromise, final report by Sep 29 - Indian Express
Content:
When the entire nation is in the grip of soaring inflation, we, who are credited with being the most spendthrift of the lot, cannot be but affected. I and my friends have generally been unmindful while spending money but now that the prices are rising and pocket money decreasing, we too have to restrain our expenditure and if possible, save a little. 

Saving has never been the mantra of the young. Like my other friends, I too believe in party today, think tomorrow, for tomorrow may or may not come. But the innovative lot that we are, after much deliberation, have come up with a novel way of having fun without feeling a pinch in the pocket.

So the smoothies at Café Coffee Day and Barista have been replaced with the good ol' nimbu pani at Stu-C. We no longer consume the Darjeeling tea at some high end coffee shop, instead we savour the local tea in our department's canteen. I and my friends have also given up on late night party hopping to the latest restaurants as that too burns a hole in the pocket. But we are still having fun. Some of my friends, who had never tasted roadside food from a dhaba, now swear by it. Some of us have even taken to cooking so that we do not miss out on various cuisines. 

So the bottom line is that no matter how expensive things become, one can find one way or the other to enjoy student life. In fact, the thrill of having fun with friends lies not in a loaded wallet but in a mind brimming with ideas to make the most of whatever life offers. These few months have also taught us the valuable lesson of being content with whatever one has. Often, we tend to forget that the money we spend is actually the hard-earned money of our parents that we thoughtlessly squander away. Though inflation has definitely forced us to cut down on our expenses, but at the same time, it has also taught us to spend judiciously.

Heading: ‘In Army, lead a life of honour, status’ - Indian Express
Content:
The issue pertaining to a brawl between the two rival groups at the MCM College in which one student was injured, was settled on Monday as a compromise was made at the Sector 36 police station.

Priyanka, the victim, had earlier lodged a DDR against the girls from the college. Priyanka's parents, however, were not too convinced with the decision and met Director Higher Education Raji P Srivastava.

Srivastava immediately summoned the college principal, Puneet Bedi, who was asked to explain her position and directed to take corrective action as soon as possible.

After giving a patient hearing to Priyanka, who wants the college to mark an inquiry into the matter, Srivastava demanded a complete report from the committee, formed to look into the matter latest by September 29.

A member from the Education department will also be included in the committee to review the entire issue.

The college has also been directed to work in coordination to improve the relations among students.

Dr Puneet Bedi, principal of MCM DAV, however, said:

"A committee was formed the very next day after this brawl took place. We were to submit the report today but we received a report from the police saying that both the parties have entered into a compromise. So nothing was left to us. We will relook into the matter and try to do something."

The Education department, meanwhile, is also working with the police to beef up security outside the college premises so that such brawls can be avoided in the future.

The issue in the college has been going on for quite some time now after there was a fight between two students groups represented by Geeta and Hemani as presidential candidates during the elections.

The rivalry between the groups, however, could not be resolved as the Education department had decided to do away with the elections this year.

Heading: Delhi Police claims question probe by UP police - Indian Express
Content:
A lecture to apprise the students about the Indian Army and to motivate them to join the military services was organised at the campus of the Doaba Group of Colleges (DGC) near Kharar on Monday. Brig Sanjay Aggarwal from the Ambala Cantonment visited the college along with his team comprising of Lt Col R S Dhir and Lt Col Sanjeev.

"One gets the opportunity of not only serving the country but also earning well and leading a life of status and honour," he said encouraging the students.

Brig Aggarwal also informed the students about the selection procedure and the qualities required in candidates to make it to the highly prestigious defence service.

He said that for BTech graduates, it was easy as they don't need to appear for the written test. "They are just required to appear for the medical test and Service Selection Board (SSB) interview," he said.

The students were also shown a documentary which helped the students get a feel of the adventure and grill in the Armed Forces. Several of the queries of the students relating to career opportunities in the Army were also answered.

Chief Administrator of Doaba Group of Colleges, Jeet Singh proposed a vote of thanks to the guests.

Heading: Maya replies to Rajeswar remark - Indian Express
Content:
The Delhi Police claims that the Indian Mujahideen module busted last week was responsible for some of the recent terror attacks in Uttar Pradesh. But this puts a question mark on the investigation carried out by the state police.

The name of Indian Mujahideen figures nowhere in any of the chargesheets filed by the state police. A completely different set of people have been named altogether. And no connection has been established between the people named by the state police and the ones named by the Delhi Police.

In every case, the HuJI tops the wanted list of the state police. And besides other accused, some Bangladesh nationals have been named — all of whom remain untraced.

In contrast, those named by the Delhi Police as members of the IM module are all from Azamgarh.

Asked about the contradictions, UP's Additional Director General of Police Brij Lal said: "Investigation into these cases is still on. A team of Anti-Terrorist Squad has been dispatched to question the persons arrested by the Delhi Police. Let's see what details they provide to our team".

Admitting that none of the 13 people named by the Delhi Police figured in the state police investigation, Brij Lal added: "We did not put any accused to narco examination. Perhaps that's why other names did not came out during investigation".

The cases: Blasts in Lucknow, Faizabad and Varanasi courts: November 23, 2007 (13 killed) Trial on in Faizabad blast case. Chargesheet filed in Lucknow case UP police claims:

* The blasts were carried out by HuJI activists. Four arrested for the Lucknow and Faizabad blasts.

* Mohammad Tariq Qasmi, a Unani doctor, led the team carried out the Faizabad blasts. He has ben arrested.

* Mohammad Khalid Mujahid, a madrasa teacher who has been arrested, exploded the bomb in Lucknow court.

* Two other accused, Sajjar Rehman and Mohammad Akhtar, were arrested from Jammu and Kashmir.

* For the blast in Varanasi, Sajjad and Raju alias Mukhtar had planted the bombs. Also, Mukhtar alias Raju, who is based in Bangladesh, had orchestrated the blasts in the three courts and arranged for the explosives. Three other accused — Zahid, Qadir, and Imran Guru ¿ are absconding.

Delhi Police say:

* Bomb in Lucknow was planted by Arif and Junaid, both are absconding.

* In Faizabad, bombs planted by Shahzad and Shadab alias Malik, both absconding.

* Varanasi bombs planted by Mohammad Saif and Sajid. Saif arrested after the Jamia Nagar encounter, Sajid was killed.

Blasts in Varanasi's Sankatmochan temple and cantonment railway station: March 7, 2006 (20 killed)

Trial on UP police say:

* HuJI member Waliullah, the imam of a mosque in Allahabad's Phoolpur, was the mastermind.

* The blasts were executed by three persons with whom Waliullah had studied at Deoband. They are Bashiruddin, Mustafiz and Zakaria, all from Bangladesh. None of them have been arrested.

"Waliullah took them to Varanasi and purchased pressure cookers, which were packed with explosives and used for carrying out the blasts", said Investigating officer, TN Tripathi, who is now posted in Bahriach.

* Chandauli resident Shamim, who is absconding, arranged the logistics.

Delhi Police say:

* Atif, who was killed in the Jamia Nagar encounter, Saif, Malik and Junaid carried out the blasts. Saif has been arrested while Malik and Junaid are absconding.

Gorakhpur blast: May 22, 2007 (Six injured)

No chargesheet yet.

UP police say:

* Mohammad Tariq Qasmi, arrested in court blasts case, is the prime accused. "During interrogation, Tariq confessed to having planted the bomb in Gorakhpur. He even told the sequence of events leading to the blast and names of two other accused," said Investigating Officer Vishwajeet Srivastava.

* Chhotu and Raju alias Mukhtar — had executed the blast, they are absconding. The explosives were arranged by Raju.

Delhi Police say:

* Blast carried out by Atif, Saif and Salman, who is absconding.

More flak

In case of the serials blasts in courts, the state police have faced considerable criticism.

* Families of Qasmi and Khalid came out with facts that question the circumstances of their arrests. Following this, the government appointed a one-man inquiry commission. The report is awaited.

* Police had to release an accused — Kolkata Electricity Corporation employee Aftab Alam Ansari, after failing to find evidence against him.

* For the Faizabad blasts, 13 of the 18 witnesses refused to identify the accused in court. Two witnesses said they had seen the accused before, but they were not planting bombs

Heading: Police handed pointers to curb terrorism - Indian Express
Content:
In a retort to Governor T V Rajeswar's remarks on "frequent" transfer and suspension of officials in the state, Chief Minister Mayawati has shot off letters to the Raj Bhavan as well as President Pratibha Patil.

In the letter, Mayawati maintained that the transfer and posting of officers will continue as and when needed and lax officers will be penalised. The Chief Minister said she was surprised over the Governor's observations, as such remarks were never made during the previous Samajwadi Party regime.

Rajeswar, at a conference of Governors in New Delhi last week, had reportedly said the transfers were ordered in the state as frequently as the previous Mulayam Singh regime, and suspensions were ordered on flimsy grounds.

He also criticised the manner in which Centrally-sponsored schemes like National Rural Employment Guarantee Act were being implemented in the state.

"After coming to power, we have formulated a transparent transfer policy. Transfers and action against officers for slackness in performance is taken, as the government has been making efforts to improve the law and order situation," read the three-page letter.

"I am unable to understand your comments when a majority government led by a dalit ke beti is pursuing the agenda of accelerating the development of the state and improving the law and order situation and striving hard to eliminate the menace of terrorism in the state," said Mayawati.

"The Governor should have ascertained the factual position before making such comments on the government in the presence of the President," she added.

The main task of IAS, IPS and PCS officers is to maintain law and order and supervise the implementation of development schemes.

For various reasons, mid-session transfer of officials is deemed necessary and in some cases the officers are also punished, said Mayawati.

According to her, transfers were done only under "unavoidable circumstances" and action was taken against officers who failed to discharge their duties.

The state has a civil services board for the transfer of IAS and IPS officers and the system was being strictly followed, she said.

Heading: JE vaccines unfit due to fault in cold storage - Indian Express
Content:
With Azamgarh firmly placed on the terror map, Chief Minister Mayawati sent a strong message on Monday to nip terrorism in the bud.

Addressing a law and order review meeting, Mayawati said: " After the Delhi serial blasts, a number of terrorists, having a UP link were arrested. If immediate steps are not taken, it could cause huge destruction of life and property."

Govt's stance

The government will take all possible steps to curb terrorism. Mayawati said: "My government's stand is clear on this issue and terrorists will never be allowed to flourish in the state."

In no way terrorism should be linked with any religion, as terrorists are an enemy of the civil society.

The terrorist organisations were spreading their tentacles in the state, as there were some shortcomings in the law enforcement agency and the administrative machinery, said Mayawati.

Message to cops

The chief minister warned the police officers of stern action if any terror incidents or activity is reported from any district. She directed the officers to ensure that no innocent person should be implicated in terror investigations and action should be taken only on basis of concrete evidence. Shea also asked the police officers to "ignore pressure exerted from the top and act independently against the guilty."

"If anyone puts pressure on you to let off any criminal, just ignore them, be it the chief secretary, Director General of Police or the cabinet secretary. You are free to call me and tell the name of the person putting pressure on you," said Mayawati.

While dealing with communal situations, Mayawati told the officers to refrain from balancing act by arresting equal number of persons from different communities and target only the guilty. " If found guilty, the officers would be dismissed," she added.

Tackling violence

On violence triggered by the incidents of cow slaughter, Mayawati said such incidents occur only due to lapses on the part of the administration. She directed the officials to ensure action as per the law after investigation.

The Chief Minister directed the officials to maintain a special vigil for the safety and security of all historical monuments and statues of eminent personalities.

While acknowledging improvement in the law and order situation in the state, Mayawati said a lot more needs to be done. Prosecuting the guilty should be faster and investigation should be more efficient.

Heading: Census conducts digital survey of metros - Indian Express
Content:
It is official now: the stock of 4.5 lakh vaccines for Japanese Encephalitis (JE), which had already suffered a loss of potency was due to the fault in maintaining the cold chain at the Government Medical Store Depot (GMSD) in Karnal.

This comes after a team from the Union Health Ministry had conducted an inspection of the cold storage at the GMSD.

The team found that the stocks sent two months ago to states like UP, Tamil Nadu and West Bengal was in Stage I, which indicated that the fault occurred only after the stocks were dispatched.

Following these initial reports, experts from the ministry will once again reinspect the Karnal unit to find out further details so that action could be taken against the errant officials of GMSD.

"It is now clear that the fault existed at the Karnal unit itself and it occurred in the past two months. But in order to find out how and when this fault did occur, a team of experts will soon visit the unit," said a senior official of the Health Ministry.

Following the controversy over the vaccine in the state, the Centre has decided to withdraw the supply and replace it with the fresh stock. The previous stock will be used for the JE vaccination campaign rather than the routine immunisation programme.

"We will not use this supply in any case for the children in the state. The vaccine sent by the Centre was to be used under the routine immunisation in the most sensitive areas for JE. Thus, any reduction in the potency could be lethal for the children," said Dr M L Khatloiya, the Director General, Medical and Health Uttar Pradesh.

The Centre, however, is yet to decide as to which state will eventually receive the present supply of the vaccine, which is lying with UP.

"It is true that the JE vaccine lying with the UP government has lost some of its potency. But our experts, who had visited the state, have found that it can still be used within the next two months," said a senior official, Infectious Disease wing, Union Health Ministry.

"It is for sure that we cannot use the present stocks for the routine immunisation programme. But it can be used for the JE vaccination programme," added the official.

It was learnt that Bihar, which is going to start the JE vaccination campaign from December, is one of the probable states that could receive this stock.

Heading: Abduction case filed against boxer’s father - Indian Express
Content:
You can now know all the minute details of your city. To collect accurate data for Census 2011, the Survey of India and the Census of India is conducting a digital survey of 35 major cities across the country. Since the digital maps will carry detailed information about each household in a city, these will provide proper estimate for the Census.

Dr Prithvish Nag, Surveyor General, Survey of India, told The Indian Express: " Besides providing information related to population, the data will also be helpful for conducting research in various fields. Presently, the survey is going on in 35 major cities of the country. Later, we may conduct it in smaller towns also." He, however, added that for any data to be useful in future it must be regularly updated.

"The purpose of satellite mapping is to ensure complete coverage for the Census 2011. We want accurate details. We are holding talks with various states in this regard," said a senior official of Census of India.

After the data is digitally mapped for the Census, it will also be made available to the public. One can access details like the number of members residing in a house, name of the house owner, whether the house is single-storeyed or double or kutcha or pucca.

By providing an accurate picture of the city, the digital mapping will prove to be an essential tool for assessing the framework of urban areas and providing proper identification of their denizens. The geographical limit of a city will be marked, its population will be accurately assessed, and individual houses can be tracked.Digitisation will ensure that there will be no omission or duplication of data.

At present, the survey is going on in Lucknow. "We asked the Lucknow Municipal Corporation to depute their tax officials of each ward for collection of the data. Since we have to complete the work by December 31 and there has been no word from the civic body yet, we are planning to rope in more people to meet the deadline," said Pradeep Kumar, Deputy Director, Mapping Department, Directorate of Census.

Heading: High fares, odd hours, Kanpur-Delhi flight hits breakers on runway - Indian Express
Content:
Aakansha Tiwari says mother missing

Following a complaint by the state boxing champion Aakansha Tiwari, a case of kidnapping under Section 364 of the IPC was registered against her father Vinod Tiwari at the Nazirabad police station on Monday.

Neelam, the mother of Aakansha, has been missing for the last four days. On Sunday, the boxer had filed a complaint with the police, alleging that her father had murdered her. Vinod Tiwari was called in, but the police said he was not questioned as he was inebriated at the time.

Aakansha told The Indian Express: "My family had tried to locate her at all the places where she could have gone, but have not been able to find her. My father is well aware of my mother's whereabouts, but the police have been soft on him."

"With the police not extending any help, we are just praying that she is still alive," she added.

Vinod Tiwari, meanwhile, has denied the allegations. "We used to have heated arguments on various issues, but I have not abducted or murdered her," he said. He added that his family members were conspiring against him. "I often scolded my daughters and son. So they are now trying to settle scores with me," he said.

He said this was not the first time Neelam has gone missing. "In 2001, after an altercation, she had run away from home and had returned after a few days."

Nazirabad Station Officer AK Singh said: "We have recorded the statements of the family members and the investigation is on."

Heading: Krishnanand murder case: HC stops judge from hearing appeals - Indian Express
Content:
While Minister of Home for State Shriprakash Jaiswal has fulfilled his promise of launching a flight service between Kanpur and New Delhi, the project has failed to meet a positive response from commuters.

Owing to the frequent change in flight timings, high fares, odd flight hours and recurrent cancellation of flights, people prefer taking train to Delhi.

In 2005, following the efforts of Jaiswal, a flight service was launched after a gap of nearly two decades.

But due to poor flight occupancy, the service was discontinued after 18 months.

The project was relaunched on September 20, 2007.

In the last one year, the flight schedule has been changed eight times, nine flight managers have been posted and later transferred from the Ahirwana Airport and the flight has been cancelled on more than 18 occasions.

Nearly eight to ten passengers take the daily flight from Kanpur and many times, the number drops even further. Worst, on three occasions, the flight had not carried a single passenger and on six flights, the number of passengers was below five.

The flight from New Delhi arrives in Kanpur at 2:55 pm and the return flight departs at 5:15 pm. Local industrialist Micky Manchanda said: "Earlier, it used to be a morning flight and it was convenient to finish work and return to Kanpur in the evening." But now that the timings have been changed to afternoon, people prefer taking a train to Delhi, he added.

Admitting that a morning flight can draw more passengers, Jaiswal said, "we are planning to start a morning flight".

High fares have also affected air traffic. Travel agent Shariq Alvi said: "The Kanpur to New Delhi air ticket costs Rs 4,400, whereas the Lucknow to New Delhi ticket stands at Rs 3,100. Therefore majority of the passengers prefer catching a flight to New Delhi from the state capital."

Heading: Another first for Allahabad: technical institute to set up SAARC digital library - Indian Express
Content:
The Allahabad High Court has restrained an additional district magistrate of Ghazipur from passing any order in the murder caseof BJP legislator Krishnanand Rai.

Justice Vinod Prasad said Additional District Judge Shaileshwar Nath Singh will only pass the remand orders of the accused.

ADJ Singh, who was present in the court following a showcause issued on September 18, has been directed to file a reply in the case.

The court has, however, exempted him from personal appearance in the case.

The court has also directed the accused — Ramu Mallah and Rakesh Pandey — who were granted bail in violation of the Supreme Court order, to be present in the court on October 17, when the case will come up for hearing.

The High Court's order came after the CBI moved an application before Justice Vinod Prasad, seeking cancellation of the bail of the accused.

According to the CBI, the Supreme Court had passed an order that only the bail application of SP leader Afzal Ansari be considered by the ADJ, but he had granted bail to the other accused as well.

BJP legislator Krishnanand Rai was murdered near his native village Goundour in Ghazipur on November 29, 2006, along with seven others.

Following the incident, his brother RN Rai had filed an FIR at the Bhawarkol police station against mafia-turned-politician Mukhtar Ansari, Samajwadi Party leader Afzal Ansari and several others.

Heading: Jamia to provide legal help to two arrested students - Indian Express
Content:
For the first time in the history of South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC), all significant literary, artistic and scientific works of mankind will be digitally preserved and made freely available for every member country. And the work will be done in Allahabad, the the Union Ministry of Human Resource Development, has decided.

The idea is to promote and exchange science and technology among the SAARC countries.

The work has been entrusted to the Indian Institute of Information Technology, Allahabad (IIIT-A), which is already setting up an Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN) — India Science and Technology (S&T) digital library.

The decision was taken in a high-level meeting attended by senior officers of Ministry of Information Technology, Ministry of External Affairs and HRD ministry meeting on September 18.

The proposed SAARC—S&T digital library will be in accordance to the Preamble of SAARC, which advocates educational and cultural exchange among the member countries. "The member countries have already agreed on issues like sharing and safeguarding the   expertise and traditional knowledge. The premiers and ministers of the SAARC countries have expressed their willingness for cooperating in this direction," said sources.

After several rounds of meetings, the IIIT-A was selected as theresource institution for the project, said Dr M D Tiwari, Director, IIIT-A.

"In a thousand years, only a few of the paper documents that we have today will survive the outright destruction. With no more than 10 million unique books and document editions before the year 1900, and perhaps 100 million since the beginning of recorded history, the task of preservation has become much larger," said Tiwari.

Dr Tiwari said the proposed S&T digital library will cost around Rs 3-4 crore. The groundwork for the proposed digital library, which includes networking of available resources of various universities and technical institutes of SAARC countries, is being initiated on a priority basis, he added.

Heading: ‘If he were a really terrorist, would he have slept at home?’ - Indian Express
Content:
In an unexpected turn of events, Jamia Milia Islamia on Monday evening decided to provide legal help to its two students arrested for alleged connection in Saturday's serial blasts across the Capital.

Mohammad Shakeel, a second-year MA student, and Zia-Ur-Rehman (third year BA) were arrested on Sunday.

Jamia Vice-Chancellor Mushirul Hasan told Newsline in the evening that he would take steps to look into the "well being" of his students.

Jamia's media coordinator Rakhshanda Jalil told Newsline, "The university has now decided to provide legal help to the two students caught on Sunday." Since the two are students of Jamia, "the university feels it is a responsibility to safeguard them until they are proven guilty."

The announcement came soon after the university had announced suspension of Shakeel and Rehman.

A large section of the faculty and students' community in the university was earlier rumbling over the varsity authorities' refusal to take a stand on the arrests. What made matters worse, several teachers and students said, was the fact that the university does not have a students' union.

"Jamia does not have a students' body that can fight for the students' rights," an agitated professor had told Newsline this morning. "After Friday's encounter, no one can now speak openly about the students, or the incident at Jamia Nagar, since they feel they might be the next target of the police, in which case the university will not come forward to help them.

"Everyone is afraid of a crackdown."

The teachers and students were concerned about the fact that on Saturday the university had refused to acknowledge that the two were studying at Jamia.

On Friday morning, Jamia had issued a statement saying, "On the basis of prima facie information the University will consider initiating disciplinary action against these students."

Asked why the university did not immediately come out and say Shakeel and Rehman were enrolled in the university, media coordinator Jalil said the police never contacted the university directly. "All our information was filtered from the media," she said. As for Atif, "we could not verify him earlier because he was enrolled under the name of Mohammad Atif Amin."

Jamia will hold a peace march in and around the areas surrounding the university at 4 pm on Wednesday. Students, teachers, staff members and residents of Jamia Nagar are expected to join the peace rally.

Heading: CEO was ‘afraid’ of assault on family - Indian Express
Content:
A strange silence pervades the usually boisterous area of Shaheen Bagh in Jamia Nagar from where 23-year-old Saquib Nisar was arrested on Saturday. Described by the Delhi police as one of the key members of the Indian Mujahideen, Saquib was sleeping at home when he was rudely awoken by the police.

"It was his 23rd birthday and he was fast asleep when the police arrived. If he really is the terrorist they describe him to be, do you think he would have stuck around at home where they could easily find him? He could have easily run away," says Saquib's younger brother, 16-year-old Shakir Nisar resolute in his belief that his brother is innocent.

As Nisar's many neighbours begin to crowd around, one thing is clear - not one of them believes Delhi Police's allegations against Nisar.

"He was a good boy, a gold medalist in Economics who appeared for the UPSC examination in 2006. He wanted to rid the country of corruption," says M A Kamal, Saquib's neighbour. "He worked with a firm in Nehru Place and was also doing his MBA through correspondence from Sikkim Manipal University. Where did he have the time to go around plotting bomb blasts?" he asks.

There is also a sense of fear within the community. "The police have not told the family on what evidence Saquib was picked up. We who lived next to them have known the family as extremely god-fearing. It almost feels like young Muslim boys are being targeted," another neighbour Abu Karim chips in. Saquib's father is busy looking for a lawyer who will represent his son when the case finally goes to trial.

"Right now, we don't even know our brother is being held but my father is sure that justice will be served, he is looking for a lawyer," says Sharik Nisar, Saquib's 18-year-old brother.

"The police said when the blasts took place, my brother watched the scenes of bloodshed on TV and celeberated. But we don't even have a TV at home. My brother has not been out of Delhi for the last two years, how can they blame him?" asked Sharik.

The Nisars have been living in Shaheen Bagh for the last 20 years. "Saquib was an NCC cadet in school," Kamal says. The boy who has been described as "good-looking, popular and charming" by the Delhi Police is described as "decent and god fearing" by the family and neighbours.

Saquib's father, Nisar Ahmed Azmi, a scientific equipments supplier to educational institutes said that his son has only been arrested because he had the number of the boys involved in the encounter on his phone.

"Like us, those boys were also from Azamgarh. Just because Saquib had their number doe not mean he is a terrorsit. By this logic, if I take your number now and cause a blast tomorrow, will you be arrested just because your number was on my phone?" he asks.

Heading: Shahi Imam attends burial of ‘terrorists’, families stay away - Indian Express
Content:
Lalit Kumar Choudhary, the country head of Italian multinational Graziano Transmissioni, had not come home for the last few days, except for one or two brief visits to check on his family.

He wanted to make sure everything was alright at home while he worked out a package that would be acceptable to the agitating workers of his company. He had even put additional security for the family at their A-103 house in Noida's Sector 30, fearing the staff may attack them.

But as fate would have it, Choudhary lost his life on Monday afternoon — at the hands of his workers. He had called them to find a solution to the demands.

At their bungalow, wife Ratna — senior lecturer at the Kirori Mal College — sat quietly surrounded by relatives and neighbours. Teenaged son Keshav hovered around silently, trying to console his mother. Ratna's colleague at Kirori mal Rajeev Ray said she was finding it difficult to believe that Choudhary should be killed by the employees.

Ray added, "Ratna's mother died a year ago. She was just picking up the pieces when this horrible tragedy happened."

Choudhary's neighbours remember him as a thorough gentleman. "The family shifted into the neighbourhood four years ago and has been very courteous," said neighbour Anil Sharma.

Another neighbour Shruti Sabherwal said the entire locality had been taken aback by the viciousness of the attack. "His death is sudden and untimely," she said. Many others felt it was no way to go, to be a victim of irrational violence.

Choudhary is also fondly remembered by the locality's children. Fourteen-year-old Keshav Aggarwal said, "Uncle had gifted me a German Shepherd pup two years ago when I let out that I was fond of dogs."

The guard posted at the bungalow said Choudhary was very worried the dismissed workers might harm his family.

"He barely came home from office in the last three or four days. His visits were brief. He had come very late last night and left in a hurry in the morning by 8.30 am," the guard said.

Heading: Govt pushes installation of security system at Delhi Secretariat, Chief MInister’s office - Indian Express
Content:
Their birth might have been occasion for a celebration for their families but in death, Atif and Sajid, the 'terrorists' gunned down by Delhi police in an encounter last Friday, received a hush-hush farewell.

Their families could not accompany them on their last journey. Sajid's brother Imran (name changed) and Atif's brothers Akram and Muzammil (names changed) were the only representatives.

A long wait at the Batla House Qabristan was futile as friends and family members had to move to the Panj Peeran Qabristan in Hazrat Nizamuddin, where the bodies were finally buried late this evening.

After the Delhi Police's intimation, family and friends had prepared the graves for the two alleged terrorists at Delhi Gate, Mehrauli and Batla House graveyards as well. Initially, the plan was to bury the dead at the Batla House graveyard. It was later decided that the last rites will take place at Nizamuddin instead.

Police sources said the shift was necessary because the atmosphere was tense at Batla House. The burial was delayed as the bodies were not released on time from hospital after the autopsy.

Hamanatullah, a friend of Atif's brother, alleged that the authorities were harassing the family without any provocation. A friend said, "The families had expected that the police will allow the bodies to be taken back to their native village in Azamgarh. However, the police asked us to bury the two here for security reasons," said a friend of the alleged terrorists. The bodies were brought in and given the ceremonial bath amid media glare.

The Shahi Imam of Jama Masjid, Ahmed Bukhari, attended the burial.

Brothers of the two deceased were too shocked to comment.

Heading: Yuvraj Singh pads up for DLF residents, hits the road - Indian Express
Content:
Spurred by the serial blasts in the Capital on September 13, the Delhi government has directed the agency concerned to speed up the installation of the high-security system in the Delhi Secretariat and the Chief Minister's office. Following a review meeting, officials said merely ten per cent of the Rs 20-crore project has been executed in the last four months.

The Electronic Corporation of India (ECIL), a PSU, was awarded the work in May this year. The project involves a 24-hour electronic video monitoring on every floor, in ministers' rooms and outside the building. The government has now directed the ECIL to set a time-frame to execute the project which is set to provide security cover to the 'highly vulnerable' building at the ITO in Delhi.

"The PSU has been asked to set a definite time-frame within which the entire security system will be commissioned and made functional at the Secretariat as progress regarding supply, installation and commissioning of security gadgets has been very slow," an official said.

The government has also directed the ECIL to install CCTVs on priority basis at more sensitive levels including the first, second, third, ninth and tenth floors apart from constituting a four-member team for regularly monitoring internal security by inspecting various levels and floors of the building. So far, apart from the regular frisking carried out by CISF officials, there is only one X-ray machine, meant to scan bags at the enterance.

Heading: Double murder: Electrician stabs to death fiance, sister - Indian Express
Content:
Cricketer Yuvraj Singh has extended support to residents of DLF City protesting against the continuous dumping of garbage close to residential areas around the Aravalli range.

Yuvraj joined around 100 other DLF residents in a protest march near the DLF I- Faridabad crossing on Monday. "He owns a house in DLF Phase I's F block. He readily agreed to support our cause after some residents approached him," Ambika Agarwal, a resident of G block, said.

The issue of illegal garbage disposal has been in the making for over two years now. Residents say the Haryana Urban Development Authority (HUDA) dumps over 325 metric tons of untreated garbage within an 800-metre radius of residential complexes. They say innumerable appeals to the civic body, and litigation against the Gurgaon administration regarding the need for proper disposal in the area, have failed to have an effect.

"The stench, rodents and insects, and the consequent health hazards, have made life hell and despite our efforts to check this practice, the authorities are simply ignoring the issue," Rohit Sarin, another resident, said. "Huda authorities have no alternate site. They do not wish to shift the garbage to the earmarked site in Badhwari, as they are planning a state-of-the-art landfill there," he said.

Officials say an efficient solid waste management plant will soon come up at Badhwari village. "It might be another two years before the plant starts working," P Kumra, HUDA superintendent engineer, said.

Heading: Kendriya Vidyalayas ‘punish’ teachers for bad results - Indian Express
Content:
A 24-year-old electrician on Tuesday allegedly stabbed his fiance and her sister to death before committing suicide in Bindapur area of west district. According to the police, the incident occurred around 11.30 am when Yashpal, who hails from Ballabgarh in Haryana, went to the residence of his fiance Deepa,18, at Bindapur in West Delhi to meet her.

"The couple was talking to each other when they suddenly started shouting after a heated argument," the police officer said. Hearing noises from the room, Deepa's elder sister, Geeta, 26, went to their room to sort out the matter.

However, angry Yashpal bolted the door from inside and allegedly stabbed the two sisters with a knife he had brought with him, the police alleged. The police added Yashpal stabbed both sisters' dozens of times as several stab marks were found on their bodies.

"From initial investigations, it seems to be a pre-planned murder as he had specifically brought a knife from his house which he had hidden in his socks," a senior police officer said.

After murdering the sisters, Yashpal hanged himself from the ceiling fan in the room. The door was later broken when the neighbours and other family members heard screaming sounds from the room. "By the time we could break the door, the three of them had died," one of the neighbours said. They were rushed to a nearby hospital where doctors declared them brought dead. Investigators said that Yashpal got engaged to Deepa about six months back and Yashpal wanted to marry her as soon as possible. "We suspect that an argument over the marriage resulted into the incident," the police said. However, the police have said that the exact motive behind the whole incident is still not clear.

A senior police officer said family members of the sisters are being questioned in connection with the incident. "The mother of the two girls, Ramkali and their three brothers are being questioned about the incident," the police added. Their father had died few years back, the police added. A case has been registered at the Bindapur police station and further investigations are on.

"Our teams have gone to Ballabgarh to interrogate Yashpal's family members about the reason behind the incident," the police officers said.

The three bodies, meanwhile, have been sent for postmortem.

Heading: Utsav Bhasin moves HC seeking anticipatory bail - Indian Express
Content:
The management of the Kendriya Vidyalayas has sent censure notices to nearly 2,500 senior teachers and has even held back the annual increments of many because some of their students did not fare well in the Boards this year.

The operating body of these schools — the Kendriya Vidyalaya Sangathan — rated the teachers' performance against the regional average of successful candidates in the respective subjects they taught.

A teacher from Delhi has been chastised for 'lack of devotion to duty' because 95 per cent of her class passed the subject in the Boards, whereas the average pass percentage in Kendriya Vidyalayas for that subject was 96. This teacher said: "They did not check my past record — 100 per cent for the five years preceding this one. This is demeaning and unfair."

Another teacher, who has been served the notice — for 'lack of devotion' — has only one failed student in her class of 66.

Some letters were harsh. One admonishes a Class XII teacher of 'misconduct' because 90.9 per cent passed the boards in the subject she taught. The regional average of success was 95.1 per cent.

General Secretary of the All India Kendriya Vidyalaya Teachers' Association S S Malik said: "This punishment is illegal. The schools' director Rangalal Jamuda had said in September 2005 there would be no penalty imposed on teachers based on performance."

However, the management's Joint Commissioner (Administration) Pragya Richa Shrivastava said, "Teachers should be punished for poor results. The Sangathan has every right to chargesheet them after analysing results."

However, the Sangathan will reconsider the penalty of those teachers who have shown good records consistently though their wards might have not done well this time. "These teachers can appeal to us," said Assistant Commissioner, in-charge of Delhi region, Sachikant Rai.

Teachers are very upset, some also because of the way these letters were handed to them. A senior teacher in Delhi said: "A peon brought the letter to me, while I was teaching a class. Will the children respect us anymore?"

There may be many reasons behind a student's failure, teachers said. "One of my students could not write the Boards because there was a tragedy in her family. Not all students are weak in studies, some are just disinterested," a teacher said.

Heading: Nanda moves High Court against ‘trial by media’ - Indian Express
Content:
Utsav Bhasin, denied anticipatory bail by a trial court for allegedly mowing down a man with his BMW car on September 11, on Monday moved the Delhi High Court seeking anticipatory bail.

Filing the bail application through his lawyer Ramesh Gupta, 19-year-old Bhasin, son of industrialist R K Bhasin from Bahadurgarh, Haryana, challenged the September 18 order passed by a trial court dismissing his bail petition. He said he was falsely implicated by the police in this case as it was a case of accident that took place due to an error committed by drivers of either of the two vehicles involved in the incident.

Informing the court he was ready to join the investigation, he said there is no evidence to establish that he had any motive to kill the victim Anuj Singh, who was travelling on a bike.The bail application is listed before the court of Justice Veena Birbal for hearing tomorrow.

Heading: Model city in shambles: crumbling infrastructure holds up Gurgaon growth - Indian Express
Content:
Sentenced to five years in prison for ramming his BMW into six persons in 1999, Sanjeev Nanda, grandson of former Navy chief S M Nanda, on Monday appealed before the Delhi High Court against his conviction by a trial court "swayed by publicity in the media".

"The conviction was swayed by the coverage in the media and is on the basis of presumption and not on the evidence on record," Nanda stated in an appeal to be heard by Justice Kailash Gambhir tomorrow.

Nanda's stand is diametrically opposed to the conclusion arrived at by the additional sessions court on September 5 — that the trial was one in which the entire criminal justice system had crumbled and "the hope for justice remained because of the watchful eyes of the vigilant Fourth Estate".

To make his point clear that his was a "trial by media", Nanda quoted from a Supreme Court decision that says the "media does not know what harm it is doing by having a parallel trial... Judges are also human and when hue and cry is made by the media it is possible that the equilibrium of a judge is also disturbed".

Nanda highlighted the good work he had done during his stay at Tihar Jail, where he taught English to other inmates and took active interest in setting up a library in the prison. "He had shown genuine interest in the welfare and upliftment of the inmates," the appeal states. "He also gave counselling on various issues to them."

Nanda criticised the trial court's "implicit reliance" on the testimony given by witness Sunil Kulkarni, even though the defence had produced enough evidence to show Kulkarni was "in Mumbai on the accident date". Moreover, Kulkarni, the appeal submits, had "categorically stated that Nanda was not the driver of the car". Nanda stated the court also ignored the fact that he had paid a total compensation of Rs 65 lakh to victims and their families. He said he had shown good conduct during the trial that was not considered by the judge.

Apart from Nanda, the trial court on September 5 also sentenced co-convict and businessman Rajeev Gupta to one-year rigorous imprisonment for destruction of evidence. Two of Gupta's employees, Bhola Nath and Shyam Singh, were, however, awarded six month jail terms each for washing off blood stains and pieces of the victims' flesh from the vehicle after the incident.

Heading: Singur in Delhi? Farmers gherao DC’s office, court says ‘serious’ - Indian Express
Content:
Gurgaon seems to be caving under its own growth. Indiscriminate real estate development, non-existent infrastructure and official apathy — the list is endless. Pitched as the "model city" in the beginning, one that "all other cities in India would aspire to emulate", the state government had worked overtime to market the city as the perfect investment destination. The lack of civic infrastructure, however, began creeping in soon after.

Almost non-existent storm-water drains and sewage system, frequent power breakdowns, traffic congestion, dismal public transport system — in a city that generates almost 40 per cent of Haryana's earnings.

What is more, many upscale residential complexes in the township are yet to get regular power connections years after full occupancy and the city is yet to get a designated spot to dump the 375 tons of solid waste it generates everyday.

"Residents are facing many health problems and several cases of dengue have been reported in the area. All this is happening because of the negligent and callous attitude of municipal authorities," Rajat Dogra, a resident of DLF city, said.

Upscale residential societies like Belvedere Towers in DLF Phase II and West End Heights lack a proper sewage system linked to the city line, and are forced to pump out their waste in open drains.

Rohit Sarin, a member of the DLF Residents' Welfare Association, said the authorities initially acknowledged the issues. When residents complained about the illegal dumping of garbage, HUDA had contended that the dumping could not be stopped immediately for they had no alternate site.

If civic authorities are to be believed, the situation will improve soon for they are "doing their best".

The new commissioner of the Gurgaon Municipal Corporation, Rajeev Sharma, said all issues are being looked into. "For instance, repair work on some stretches has already started despite the fact that the roads have not been handed over to the corporation," he said.

"Residents should be patient and cooperate with us," G Anupama, HUDA administrator, said. "We are making all possible efforts to sort the grievances of the residents and are very much on schedule," she said. "HUDA has identified an ultra-modern waste management system, which will cost around Rs 60 crore. A detailed report on the system will be submitted to the Chief Minister next week, after which tenders will be issued for the project on a build-operate-transfer (BOT) basis," she said.

Anupama also said efforts were being made to solve the immediate problem of garbage disposal.

For conveyance, the city primarily depends on autorickshaws and a few private city buses. The administration is, however, ready with a solution to all this anguish — the 2010 Commonwealth Games.

HUDA officials said higher authorities in the state government have issued special instructions to the body for completing all major infrastructure projects in time for the Commonwealth Games. These infrastructure projects have already started taking shape on the ground and work on laying the master sewage lines is in its last stages.

"Work on the 150-metre-wide Northern Peripheral Expressway, connecting NH-8 with Dwarka, is about to begin; while that on the Southern Peripheral Expressway has already begun. We will also start work on the solid waste management facility soon," Anupama said.

Heading: Lakra leaves it to his mates - Indian Express
Content:
Days after the Delhi Cabinet decided to hike compensation rate for farmland acquired for infrastructure projects, farmers of six villages in Northwest Delhi, including Kanjhawala, have kept up their agitation demanding a further hike in rates.

Their protests have now forced a city court to intervene. The court's intervention comes after Sub Divisional Magistrate (SDM) of Sarswati Vihar Ranjit Singh brought up the issue of problems in moving files required by his office as a large number of farmers have been staging a sit-in protest outside the deputy commissioner's office at Kanjhawala for 11 days now.

SDM Ranjit Singh submitted before Additional District Judge Kamini Lau that the files could not be taken out of the office because the premises are forcefully shut since September 11. The agitators, Singh told the court, turned violent whenever officials tried to enter the building.

Despite an FIR against them, the protestors have not budged and the police are shying away from stern steps to avoid a flare-up, the SDM informed. "The deputy commissioner is presently sitting in the office of chief electoral officer at Kashmere Gate; I have (also) done a makeshift arrangement for work," Singh said.

ADJ Lau noted that the situation is of "serious concern" since the protestors have forced all work to be halted, besides forcing officers to abandon their place of work. "A serious note is required to be taken as entire revenue records of the area and other government documents are inside the building," the court said. "They cannot be moved due to the agitation, thereby affecting justice."

Observing that the stir is holding up routine works, ADJ Lau said, "The constitutional right of a citizen is to (hold) peaceful protest — under no circumstances can any person or group be allowed to take law into their own hands and hold the entire system to ransom."

Since Chief Minister Sheila Dikshit and concerned government departments are aware of the issue, ADJ Lau said it is not for the court to advise the administration. But the court observed that it is "desirable" that necessary steps are taken on "immediate basis".

Sending a copy of the order to Delhi Chief Secretary, the court urged the government to look into the matter immediately so that records required by it for deciding a civil case could be brought on the next date of hearing.

The Delhi government had acquired 1,450 acres of agricultural land on August 25, 2005 through a notification. The government revised the compensation rate from Rs 15.7 lakh to Rs 17.5 lakh per acre within four days of the notification.

In a meeting last week, the rates were again revised to Rs 75 lakh per acre but the farmers continued to protest: they claim market price of the land is now nearly Rs 3 crore per acre.

Heading: DDCA sports committee re-elected - Indian Express
Content:
Anup Lakra is aware he hasn't scored a goal for two years now, despite the fact that his position as a midfielder does present him with opportunities. Instead, he remains satisfied with drawing himself back from the edge of the opponents' box and letting Shyam Bankira, Shankho Marandi and Bhada Tudu take the honours.

This in no way disheartens Orissa coach Surendranath Padhy who had seen an 'engineer' in 11-year old Anup four years ago and dragged him back to the midfield from the forward line. But there were more reasons to this than just his seniors hanging their boots, according to the coach. "His job is that of an engineer, a distributor. He is the most important member of our team, it doesn't matter if he fails to score," says Padhy.

Anup, then a striker, joined the Sundargarh Sports Hostel as a class VI student in 2004 under Padhy's coaching, and the first thing the tutor noticed in him was his short height compared to others of his age group. But what made him different from the rest was his intelligence. "He understands his game better than all others. He identifies the striker who's at the best position to score according to his strengths. He doesn't have the height, but has the brain," says Padhy. Orissa's highest scorer in the Subroto Cup, Bhada Tudu with seven goals, reiterates his coach's observation.

"I move in from the right and he is just behind me on the same line. That's why I get most of the passes from him (Lakra). At least three of the first five goals were scored from through balls forwarded by Lakra," says last year's Subroto Cup stipend winner. Behind Lakra's favouritism, there are priorities too. "Tudu is the fastest of all our strikers, this is why he can reach the through balls in time. I have made him score the most number of goals," he reinforces.

Sankho Marandi joins the conversation, and says, "If he misses a game it reflects on the result. Our midfield looks bleak without him."

To balance his short stature that prevents him from reaching the aerial balls, the team has a specialist in Umesh Kuju. "Umesh is in the midfield to receive high balls and head them on to Lakra," says Sashi Poppo, another forward.

While Padhy feels his 'intelligent' ward is irreplaceable despite the goal drought for more than two years now, Lakra keeps scoring many when there's a hockey stick in his hand. "I'm scared of the cricket ball. I play hockey whenever I find time and score many goals as I play as a striker," adds Lakra.

Heading: Sharma’s last case before shootout: cracking teen’s abduction - Indian Express
Content:
The existing DDCA (Delhi & District Cricket Association) Sports Working Committee led by Vinod Tihara renewed its term for the 2008-09 season with a comprehensive victory over their rivals, led by Ashok Sharma. The elections were held Monday afternoon following a postponement from August 25 due to legal bindings.

Vinod Tihara, who swept 81 of the 109 votes, however, wasn't surprised by his fifth term in a row and said it was the result of good work over the last year. "You can see the faces in the Indian team. Apart from that, we won the Ranji Trophy after a span of 15 years, that too with players like Ishant Sharma, Virender Sehwag, Virat Kohli and Ashish Nehra sitting out," Tihara said. "We had camps for the middle-order batsmen, openers, spinners, pacers with the likes of Terry Jenner, Shivlal Yadav, Gundappa Vishwanath and Wasim Akram. We have also been providing financial help to the clubs under our affiliation. After all this, we were expecting this victory. ."

As the new committee was assembling for its first meeting, Tihara gave a glimpse of the things to come this year. "We have planned five cricket academies for Delhi players -- four zonal (East, west, north and south) and the main academy--- that will cover the whole city. The DDA complex, Yamuna Sports Complex, Siri Fort Complex, Rashtriya Sports Khel Parishad, Pitampura and Shivaji College have been fixed as the venues and the paper work is almost complete. NCA and first-class level coaches will be appointed for the programme and the top brass from these camps will be absorbed into the main camp," he added.

It was another landmark for Anil Chaudhary, who got his tenure extended to a record 15th year. However, Chaudhary wasn't present during the elections as he is currently in Bangalore attending a camp for umpires.

Members of the Sports Working Committee for 2008-09: Vinod Tihara (LB Shastri Cricket Club), Vijay Bahadur Mishra (SBI), Anil Chaudhary (Darling Cricket Club), PS Chauhan (Pusa Youngsters Cricket Club), Ashok Katyal (GG Dutt Cricket Club), Naresh Sharma (Young Cricketers), Ramesh Sachdeva (Friends Club), Surya Prakash Sharma (Gemini Sports), Ahmed Tameen (Ajmal Khan Cricket Coaching Centre) and Pradeep Aggarwal (Kranti Star Cricket Club).

Heading: Nagaland boys blank Sikkim 5-0 - Indian Express
Content:
Inspector Mohan Chand Sharma was tracking the case of a teenager's abduction from near his house in North Delhi when the serial blasts occurred on September 13.

According to sources in the Special Cell, Police Commissioner Y S Dadwal specifically gave the case to Sharma and his team since the inspector had an exceptional network — both within the Capital and in neighbouring states. The FIR was initially lodged at Keshav Puram police station.

A senior officer Keshav Puram police station said the FIR was lodged on August 18. The businessman (names withheld to protect identity) reported that his 17-year-old son had gone missing while on way to a nearby colony for his tuition classes, the officer said. "The complainant said the family received ransom calls."

Sharma's team in the Special Cell got the investigations on August 20, the source said.

One bullet, 20 injuries on Atif body
Doctors at All India Institute of Medical Sciences which conducted the autopsy on Atif, a suspected terrorist, recovered one bullet from his body. "There were 20 injuries on his body including entry and exit points of the bullet. His heart, lungs and liver were ruptured," said a doctor. The other suspect Mohammad Shahid had several head injuries. Two bullets were recovered from his body, which had 11 injuries, including the entry and exit points of the bullets. The bullets have been given to the police and will be sent to ballistic experts.
— ENS

Heading: BMW sting: Apex court says HC was lenient to senior lawyers - Indian Express
Content:
Riding high on a hat-trick by Tingnyek (22nd, 29th and 31st) Green Wood Hr Sec School,Nagaland thrashed Namchi Sports Hostel, Sikkim 5-0 while St Ignatius High Sec School defeated Govt Kolasib High School 2-0 in the quarter-final matches of Sub-juniors (U-14) of the Subroto Cup at the Ambedkar Stadium on Monday. Green Wood boys dominated the match right from the start and had better ball possession and they drew the first blood in the 9th minute itself with Wasadplung netting in the ball from a cross from the left flank.

Four minutes later Nyuhenlo netted in to give his team a 2-0 lead. Though Namchi Sports Hostel boys got a couple of opportunities but they failed to capitalise on the chances that came their way. Then it was the chance of star performer of the day, Tingnyek, to show his football skills. He netted in thrice in a span of ten minutes to seal the fate of the game in his team's favour even before the first half.

In the other sub-junior match, Mahender Munda and Pradip Lakra scored a goal each in the 19th and 57th minutes respectively.

Later in the day Vasant Valley School, went down fighting to Sports Authority of India, Kolkata 2-1 and Town High School, Orissa defeated Govt. Model Sr Sec School, Chandigarh 2-1 in the junior (U-17) quarter-final matches.

Heading: Spaced Out - Indian Express
Content:
The Supreme Court on Monday observed that the Delhi High Court, which has held senior advocates R K Anand and I U Khan guilty of criminal contempt of court in the BMW hit-and-run case, dealt the matter "rather leniently". The court also refused to stay the HC's judgment.

While refusing to accede to a plea by senior advocates Rajeev Dhavan and P P Rao, appearing for the two convicted senior members of the Bar, the court refused an interim stay on the high court judgment.

"The High Court has dealt with the matter quite leniently," a Bench comprising Justices B N Agarwal and G S Singhvi observed, as Dhavan, arguing for Anand, said the High Court had exceeded its jurisdiction and did not follow the due process of law by holding summary proceeding in the matter.

But the Bench observed: "Had it been a case of an ordinary person, there would be a different yardstick but it is a case of a member of the Bar."

The two senior advocates challenged the high court decision dated August 21, debarring them from practicing in the high court and subordinate courts. Arguing for them, their lawyers submitted before the apex court that the High Court did not consider their applications and delivered the final judgement.

The court also issued notices to the respondents, seeking their responses. It even agreed to give them an expeditious hearing on their appeals by admitting the petitions in this regard and called for case records from the High Court and posted its hearing before an appropriate Bench on October 14.

Heading: Tastes Different, Looks Different - Indian Express
Content:
Art finds a place in the streets of high fashion — at best, it is an intelligent foil to bling, at worst a distraction

The guests won't be the usual aficionados thronging high-profile art galleries, appreciating a Tyeb Mehta or an F.N. Souza. But when the Lakme Fashion Week takes off in Mumbai in about a month's time, the National Centre for the Performing Arts (NCPA) will be host to an art studio organised by city-based gallery Jamaat, designed particularly to give fashionistas a taste of art, up close and personal. "All over the world, designers use venues away and apart from the usual ramp set-ups, and they are almost always art studios. We thought we could do it a little differently. We have commissioned a set of 20 artists to give expression to their notion of fashion which we shall put up at the foyer and the lounge," says Anil Chopra, adviser, Lakme.

At the just-concluded HDIL Couture Week in Mumbai, the Grand Hyatt too saw an art lounge put up by the city-based art gallery Tao, where works of Krishen Khanna, Arpana Caur and other established artists were on display. It was at best a foil to fashion, at worst an intelligent distraction. "The presence of the works helped tone down the high-octane bling and glamour at the week," says Sunil Sethi, president, Fashion Design Council of India, adding, "We had two shows every day and there was a waiting period of two hours between them. The works proved to be absorbing. In fact, when it rained in between we had the paintings insured rather than close down the lounge."

International fashion has already seen a proliferation of big brands going on an art trail, with regular showings and interactions with artists in their retail space. Salvatore Ferragamo, for instance, holds regular shows at its museums in Florence, New York and Seoul. Levis has, in the past, showcased works by Damien Hirst, but this is arguably the first time that fashion events in India have come forward to collaborate with serious art spaces. "The response was overwhelming, probably because it was unexpected," says Kalpana Shah, director of Tao. Meanwhile, Pravina Mecklai of Jamaat says the ArtStudio at LFW could create a dynamic synthesis of art and fashion.

In fact, Sethi says, buoyed by the reception the art studio got at the Couture Week, the FDCI has received similar offers from three leading galleries in Delhi and the NCR for the fashion week next month. "But since we are focusing more on the business of fashion, we would prefer to collaborate with individual artists rather than with galleries in Delhi," he says.

Of course, not everybody is convinced that the collaboration augurs well for serious art. "The presence of art at these shows contributes to the ambience. The works are peripheral to clothes. For serious interactions, galleries will remain the place to go to," says Delhi-based artist Amitava Das, whose work The Galaxy was showcased at the couture event in Mumbai. Sethi, though, has a counter-argument. "The same people who appreciate luxury are into collecting art as well. So, it is a good platform for all," he says. Shah agrees. "The purpose of the whole collaboration was to provide interested people with a trailer of sorts of our catalogue. We told everybody who contacted us to come back to the gallery, and many people have," she says.

Heading: Shootout and the lead-up reconstructed - Indian Express
Content:
Foreign designers add glitz to some of the new restaurants in town

When the Taj was planning to set up its Japanese fine diner Wasabi in the Capital, they wanted the interiors to go with Masaharu Morimoto's menu that went all out contemporising Japanese cuisine and brought out such things as tenderloin steak tossed with wasabi-coated tiger prawns. So they rang up Mario and Theo, a UK-based design firm. Mario and Theo Nicolaou had worked for major airlines like the British Airways and the Virgin Atlantic, and the Taj thought the Nicolaou brothers would be ideal to create a look that would make anyone from Tokyo, New York or New Delhi feel at home.

"The first impression of a restaurant should stimulate the palate even before a morsel is served," says Theo, 40. He and younger brother Mario, 35, lit up Wasabi, which did not have enough natural light, with dramatic lighting — a mix of concealed LED lighting, coffered ceiling zones and flute chandeliers — and clad the walls with dark timber panelling to create a rich and moody backdrop. They contrasted it with a carved wall finished in white. Yin and yang, perfect to quaff mildly warmed sake.

The Taj, impressed with the brothers, got them to go OTT for Varq, their Indian restaurant at the Taj Mahal Hotel, as well. Mario and Theo say they wanted the entrance to Varq to resemble the opening of a giant trinket box that unveils a surprise within. It was to this effect that they made a black, lattice frame that encases circular, beveled, glass apertures with ruby red glass in the hollows. And to go with the name Varq, meaning edible gold or silver foil, they decked up the ceiling with gold leaf patterns. "For both the restaurants, we wanted a design that could marry Indian and international aesthetics. It is partly due to their design that our restaurants are running successfully," says Digvijay Singh, general manager, Taj Mahal.

Priya Paul, chairperson of the Park Hotels, which is one of the early players to work with overseas firms, says sometimes a foreign hand is essential. Three years ago, she had got the UK-based design firm Conran and Partners to give the restaurants a youthful facelift. "We had to give the Park property a vibrant look representing emerging India. We incorporated it through our choice of colours, patterns and use of traditional Mughal screens," says Richard Doone, managing director, Conran & Partners, who admits the task was challenging.

While it is not unusual to find foreign designers working for hotel chains, it is rare to find them doing up standalone restaurants. Restaurateurs argue that the exorbitant fees of a foreign design firm acts as deterrent. "Very few standalones hire foreign talent. In the case of a hotel, they have to maintain a certain class and they go all out hiring the best," says Manav Sharma, owner of Ploof. The upcoming lounge bar, Mannekin, at Greater Kailash I, owned by restaurateur Mandeep Kohli, is an exception — but then it is designed by Kohli's close friend, the American architect Michael Janson. Better known for designing the cigar outlet Cingari at The Oberoi. Janson, 38, is combining exotic materials like seashells and compelling photographs, offset by trendy furniture. "When someone dines out, he is looking to mentally travel the world," says Janson, who took two years to finalise the concept. A year ago, he had designed Kohli's French fine dining restaurant, Café De Paris, inspired by Le Corbusier's Notre Dame Du Haut chapel, at Ronchamp, France. Eat from these foreign hands.

Heading: Post-Office Hit - Indian Express
Content:
Two alleged militants dead, two more arrested, and a blood-spattered room after 33 shots fired from both ends — this is the story of those few minutes on Friday morning at L-18, Jamia Nagar, which left Delhi Police's "best" encounter expert dead and left a nation shaken. Here's how it happened:

Thursday: A commotion ensues in the first-floor office of Special Cell on Lodhi Road after Mohan Chand Sharma's team gets conclusive evidence about whereabouts of suspects in September 13 serial blasts.

2 am, Friday: The day's operation in Jamia Nagar charted, Special Cell encounter cops, led by Sharma, retire for the day.

7.30 am, Friday: A team goes on one last reconnaissance to give final touches to the plan. Inspector M C Sharma, then with his son (down with dengue) at Kalra Hospital in Moti Nagar, West Delhi, gets a call.

He leaves for office immediately.

10.10 am, Friday: Sharma leaves office in an Indica. His destination: Jamia Nagar, where his team is waiting for the go-ahead to bust the "terrorists".

10.30 am: Dressed in formals and posing as a Vodafone salesman, sub-inspector Dharmender knocks on the fourth-floor flat of L-18. From inside comes the yelp: "Kuchh nehin chaiye." Dharmender peeps in and finds two men. He gives a missed call to Sharma: a signal to come up.

Within minutes, Sharma sprints up with a team of six officers, while two others guard the building's exit. "We barged in, with Sharma-sir leading us," an officer with the team says. "We overpowered the two but there were more men — we had earlier failed to spot them."

The three men in the other room suddenly rush in and open fire at Sharma. As Sharma falls down, the bullet aimed at him hits Constable Balwant Rana.

As the shootout goes on, Dharmendar and Constable Sandeep pull out Sharma, now bleeding heavily, and take him down. Propped on the two, Sharma limps some 50 steps to the gray Indica that takes him to Holy Family Hospital.

11 am: NSG commandoes troop in — they were called by Joint Commissioner (Special Cell) Karnal Singh, after Sharma had informed him minutes before barging into L-18.

By then the area is crawling with men in khaki.

Heading: Sound of Music - Indian Express
Content:
Shreyas Talpade on turning letter writer for Benegal

The last time actor Shreyas Talpade wrote letters was in 2004. Then only his wife-to-be in London, Deepti, came to know of them. This time, by writing letters for a riot of villagers in Shyam Benegal's movie Welcome to Sajjanpur, Talpade has got a bigger — but an equally encouraging — response.

"The role has been the toughest and most gratifying till date," says Talpade who was in town with co-star Amrita Rao (right) to gauge the audience's reaction to the movie, the second comic film by Benegal after the 1975 flick Charandas Chor. "I had to learn to speak in Bhagelkhandi, a dialect spoken in Madhya Pradesh. It wasn't easy and I was assisted by my scriptwriter who had a fair grasp of the language."

While Talpade's character Mahadev relives the ambitions of being a writer by jotting down letters and sending text messages, the movie becomes a light-hearted comment on rural India, not quite the favourite location of new Bollywood. Talpade confesses that he had some reservations when he was offered the project. "I was taken aback when I heard Shyam babu was doing a comedy. But when I heard the script, I realised that only he could come up with such a plot. There was romance interwoven with a strong message about rural India. I approached the project with a blank slate and followed Shyam babu's directions," he says.

Working with Benegal proved to be a learning curve. "Shyam babu gave us a free hand. He was disciplined, but not strict. He helped us in improving our shots but let us experiment," he says.

With so many comic flicks under his belt, has comedy become second nature to him? Not quite, admits Talpade. But funnies are not far away. After the horror flick Click, he comes back to slapstick with Golmaal Returns. For now, the distance between post office and box office is reduced.

Heading: No chargesheet yet in last year’s Jamia violence - Indian Express
Content:
There's no time to be sad when you're singing. That's what 30-odd children from two NGOs, Salaam Balak and Bal Sahyog, found out when they began working on an album of songs inspired by their lives. Called Chand Taarey Jeb Mein, the album is conceptualised by Delhi-based singer Rene Singh. While Singh is in talks with labels to release the album, the children will give a glimpse of it at a stage show on September 23. "I've never been on stage before and I'm so nervous," says Asha, a Class VIII student. Her friend Roshni, from Paharganj, adds that she packs in an extra hour's practice everyday between housework and homework.

The album will include eight songs, inspired by dreams, poems and conversations with the children. Singh, who composed the lyrics, says the stress is on optimism because "we didn't want to highlight the negative aspects of life". The musical journey has paid off for Anju, a timid teenager who is now choreographing the piece Man hai ki manchala hai.

The show will be held at the India Habitat Centre on September 23 at 7.30 pm.

Heading: ‘My son cannot make a bomb’ - Indian Express
Content:
Exactly a year ago — as today — Jamia Nagar was wrapped in a blanket of khaki after local residents went on a rampage, attacking the police and posts following a rumour that an officer had desecrated a copy of the Quran.

Officers investigating the case had said certain criminal elements had provoked the locals to attack the police. Twenty two people, including 15 officers were injured, and nearly 30 arrested by the Crime Branch after it could identify these rioters from video footage.

All of them are reportedly out on bail and several still absconding.

The police did not meet the 90-day deadline either to file chargesheets. In fact, a whole year has passed and no chargesheet has been filed yet. Deputy Commissioner (Crime Branch) Neeraj Thakur said: "The investigation is still pending. I don't know the exact status of that case."

It began around 7 pm on the evening of September 21, 2007 and continued till the early hours of the next day. Locals from Batla House — put up to it by criminals — confronted the police for several hours. In these few hours, major parts of Okhla, Sarita Vihar and New Friends Colony turned a battleground. Two police posts, those in Jamia and Shaheen Bagh, were attacked and burnt by a mob. Files were destroyed and property damaged.
