Four police officers, including the additional station house officer of New Friends Colony Akhilesh Yadav, were also seriously injured, prompting the authorities to post a strong contingent of police and paramilitary forces to guard the area for weeks after the incident.

Within a week, Police Commissioner Y S Dadwal handed the case to the Crime Branch.

Two FIRs were registered, one each at the New Friends Colony and Sarita Vihar police stations against unknown people on charges of violence, destruction of public property and assaulting public servants on duty. But since then, the case has not moved an inch.

There has, however, been one upshot of last year's violence — the Jamia post was made into a full-fledged police station in two months.

Heading: Principal Thampu wants elite tag off, more Stephen’s across India - Indian Express
Content:
His mother lies on a small bed in the verandah of her house D5/130, Sangam Vihar. Her eyes are moist and she is waiting for her son to come back home. "I know my son is innocent. I know he cannot make a bomb," says Wakila.

Wakila is the mother of Md. Shakil, the man who had made bombs for the blasts that shook the Capital on September 13. "I want to know why Allah has done this to our family," says Wakila as she looks up at the sky.

"My brother could not kill an ant. How can he make a bomb? Because we are poor and we are Muslims we are easy prey," adds Shakil's sister Tabbassum.

Both Shakil's sister Tabbassum and Shabana say their brother was very reserved. "He would help ammi in household work before going to office and would never be late from college. He did not have the habit of loitering around after college. He loved to spend time with family," said his elder sister Shabana. Both Shabana and Tabbassum want people to know their brother is innocent.

Their house has not been swept for the past two days and the family has not had a proper meal. The used utensils lie in one corner of the verandah and the clothes are waiting to be washed.

"How can the house function properly when one member of the family is behind bars? We have not had a proper meal for the past two days," adds Shakil's younger brother Farooq. Farooq is worried because his father has had a high blood for the last two days and his mother who has undergone two heart surgeries is facing some complications.

Even his neighbours feel Shakil is innocent. "He seemed to be a decent boy. We never saw him arguing with anyone," said a neighbour.

"Once Shakil had thrown his garbage in front of our lane. I just told him not to do so. He apologised and never did the same," said another neighbour. "He was a decent boy," adds the neighbour.

The family owns two houses in the colony and the nighbours do not seem to know what exactly is going on. "Shakil's father works in a printing press. And the sons are studying. And they have two houses," said another neighbour. "Nobody knows what is going inside the house," adds the neighbour.

The family worried about the bad name that it has earned over the past few days. "We have our in-laws. There are going to be so many questions when we go back to our homes," said Shabana.

"We are a middle-class family. We don't know what is going to happen to our brother. But for a middle class family like ours, the family reputation once gone, is gone forever," she said.

Heading: Anand Vihar and Sarai Kale Khan ISBTs to be restored - Indian Express
Content:
Reverend Valsan Thampu, the new St Stephen's College principal, now plans to open branches of the renowned college across the country, and at the same time maintain its "academic vigour".

"Our infrastructure on the Delhi campus is severely restricted. I want to open many branches of St Stephen's and I am seriously mulling how to do it and raise funds," he told Newsline. I would also like to explore the options of having new streams."

Primarily an arts and science college, Stephen's does not offer Commerce courses. Over time, it has not even launched popular arts and science courses that are taking other campuses by storm — like sociology, journalism or biotechnology.

The expansion, Thampu said, would be done without compromising on academics. To give academics a boost, Thampu, as Officer on Special Duty (OSD) in 2007, introduced the post of a Dean (Academics), currently held by Prof Vijay Tankha. "This post is dedicated to problems and issues related to academics. It is meant to encourage and create excellence in academics."

Thampu had come under severe criticism when, as OSD, he had introduced a separate 10-per cent quota for Dalit Christian students for 2008 session. The college alumnus had alleged that the move would dilute academic standards, since it meant 40 per cent seats would be for Christians.

But Thampu said he is anything but a "religious fundamentalist". "Contrary to claims that I am a religious fundamentalist out to destroy academic excellence, I have picked the best people for academics in this college," he said. "We have a new internal management committee, too, which looks at administrative issues. I am a gold medallist in academics, and I would never dilute academic standards of the college.

"I still get threatening calls from those who want nothing in this college to change. But I am firm in my beliefs and don't do anything without the college supreme council's assent."

Thampu said he would review performance of students admitted this session through the Dalit Christian quota. "We admitted 10 very poor children last year. We want to sensitively explore whether such children would require any help or extra classes in future. I want to open doors of the college to academically bright students who wouldn't get a chance otherwise.

"One Scheduled Caste student we admitted from Rajasthan went on to score 50 out of 50 in Logic."

Thampu also wants to rid Stephen's of the "elite" tag. "Higher education is completely isolated from the realities of this country — each institution is hermetically sealed off. These are given the title of elitism. This is not academic elitism but social elitism.

"In my interviews (with students during admission), no one is asked his grandfather or father's name. It's all about the student."

Heading: Foolproof security plans Games 2010 - Indian Express
Content:
The Delhi Cabinet on Monday approved redevelopment of the Inter-state Bus Terminals (ISBTs) at Sarai Kale Khan and Anand Vihar.

The Delhi Integrated Multimodal Transit System (DIMTS) is developing the new ISBTs at Dwarka and Narela.

A Delhi government official said Anand Vihar ISBT was commissioned in 1993 and the one at Sarai Kale Khan in March 1996 — both as temporary structures. Now, they need to be redeveloped to handle the increasing volume of passengers. Dwarka and Narela ISBTs are being developed to decongest the existing terminals ahead of 2010 Commonwealth Games.

The re-development plans for terminals at Narela and Dwarka have scope for establishing restaurants, hotels and a multi-level parking lot, officials said.

More depots okayed
Looking to increase the city's bus fleet by about 6,000 before the Commonwealth Games, the Cabinet on Monday approved a proposal seeking to cover drains and building bus depots on them. The Cabinet sanctioned Rs 500 crore in the first leg of the scheme, as the Delhi Transport Corporation (DTC) has projected a requirement of 27 depots in addition to the existing 35. Officials said DTC is already constructing seven more bus depots with a parking capacity of 700 buses. These depots will be double-storey buildings, meant to accommodate 200 buses each.

With at least five acres required for each bus depot and land not easily available in Delhi, officials said 44 new sites would be developed on drains to construct the depots to accommodate 4,400 buses to be run by private operators. The proposal seeks to cover the drains at Janakpuri, Barapullah, Lodhi Road, Shahdara Industrial Area and Rohini.

The Cabinet approved the idea of private bus operators introducing AC buses.

Heading: City gets a new master plan - Indian Express
Content:
Following the serial blasts in the Capital last week, a wary Delhi government is endeavouring to go hi-tech and implement a foolproof security system for the 2010 Commonwealth Games. "Under the new regime, a strong vigil will be kept on sensitive spots through satellite and entry to games village and sports venues will be strictly through electronic I-cards. All roads and crossing leading to sports complexes will be kept under electronic surveillance," Delhi chief minister Sheila Dikshit told Newsline.

As per the plan, a 'games village management and crowd management system' will be in place ahead of the Games. A hi-tech traffic management centre will be a part of the programme as part of which a fleet of helicopters will monitor traffic movement during the mega event spanning October 3 to 14, 2010.

"To control the flow of visitors, a crowd management system will be in place. An electronic ticketing system network will link metro stations, bus stands and select taxi stands. The government has already placed orders to foreign suppliers for the latest surveillance mobile cameras," Dikshit said.

"More than a 1000-strong workforce is busy in developing the whole system. All state government departments are being linked through Wide Area Network (WAN). Some strategic spots will become Wi-Fi zones. A 10-kilometre area around the Commonwealth Games village will be covered under Wi-Fi system. To provide Internet facility to visitors, about 500 cyber cafes will be set up," Dikshit added.

The government will soon invite bids from reputed IT firms to showcase sports, cultural activities, shopping and tourist spots and health facilities. The information will be given through large display boards.

The whole idea is to instill a sense of security in Delhiites and visitors who have been left insecure following two major terror attacks in less than three years.

Around 20 call centres will be set up in Gurgaon and Noida. These will be used to provide information about tourism, sports, ticketing and health. To provide the latest information, more than 2000 information kiosks will also be set up.

A portal is being prepared through which information will be received at the click of a mouse.

The government will launch a forceful campaign to ensure prevention of terrorist strikes through public participation.

Heading: Power board employee shot dead - Indian Express
Content:
Units in Shimlapuri, New Shimlapuri get 10-year grace period to relocate

Finally, city's master plan has been approved.

The move will benefit more than 6,000 industrialists in the Shimlapuri, New Shimlapuri areas, who have been given 10 years as the grace period to move their units out of these colonies.

The master plan also enlists no further expansion of these industrial units. The officials in the district Town Planning wing say that as the sudden uprooting of these units is not possible, hence the industries have been given ample time to shift out. However, the Small Scale Industries Association General Secretary Gurwant Singh said the traders wanted to meet minister Hira Singh Gabria as they were little confused about the statement of the chief minister that dense industrialised areas will not be uprooted in the years to come.

Town Planning wing, however, has categorically stated that so far they have not received any communication about such an issue from the higher authorities. But if the municipal corporation gets the residential town planning schemes dropped (which are more than 15) from these areas by following the proper procedure, only then traders will be benefitted.

Apart from this, even the government-approved residential colonies having commercial activities are also in the line of fire as according to the new master plan no commercial activity is allowed in such colonies.

If one goes by the new master plan, the city will get parking facility in all the market places.

Areas near Sangeet Cinema and Janta Nagar have been declared for mixed-land use but the residents of these areas had given representations to change them into residential use only. Here too, the residents have been left high and dry.

Though the plan has been approved, industrialists are making last ditch efforts to alter the plan as per their interests.

Line of change

* Kohara and Machiwara have been declared for industrial use. These areas were earlier converted into residential category on the demand of industrial houses.

* Husianpura near Jalandhar bypass has been converted into residential area from the mixed-land use catergory.

Heading: Is PAU going slow over sexual harassment complaint? - Indian Express
Content:
Gurmeet's Singh body found near Alamgir : Car missing but cellphone found broken

An employee of the Punjab State Electricity Board (PSEB) was reportedly shot dead late last night by some unidentified assailants. The accused have reportedly sped away in his luxury car after killing him. His body was found in the Sarinh village, near Alamgir, on the Malerkotla road.

Gurmeet Singh, in his mid 30s, was a resident of the Dhandra road in the city. He was posted as assistant lineman with the PSEB at Mandi Ahmedgarh. Though, the deceased was an assistant lineman, he hailed from a rich background.

According to the police, Gurmeet Singh had last spoken to his daughter Amanpreet Kaur on Sunday evening around 8.30pm while coming back home after work. He told his daughter that he will reach home in about half an hour and asked her to keep the food ready. When he did turn up till 10.30 pm, his family again called him but his phone was switched off.

At this, the family got apprehensive about his wellbeing and informed the police.

Sources said that around midnight, a party from Sadar police station found his broken mobile phone near Sarinh village and then the bullet-pierced body of the victim was found at a distance. The police have yet to trace his car, the police said.

After conducting the post-mortem at the local Civil Hospital, the body was handed over to his family. According to the police, there were two bullet marks on the body of the deceased.

The Sadar police have registered a case under sections 302 (murder) and 397 (robbery or dacoity with attempt to cause death) of the Indian Penal Code (IPC) against unidentified persons and have started investigations.

However, no arrest has been made so far in the case.

Heading: Ex-serviceman held for duping jobless youths - Indian Express
Content:
Though it's has nearly been a week since the Punjab Agricultural University's senior officials were handed over a written complaint by a student alleging sexual harassment, the university is yet to initiate a formal inquiry into the matter.

Dean Postgraduate Studies Dr S K Mann, who is looking into the matter, said, "Vice-Chancellor Dr M S Kang has given me the charge to look into the complaint but I have yet to go into the details of the issue. The issue is very sensitive and hence I need to study the complaint critically." When asked if the Director Students Welfare Dr Dulcha Singh Brar, against whom this complaint has been lodged, has been called to join the inquiry, Dr Mann said, "I have no written orders to summon Dr Brar. I have been verbally asked by the V-C to look into the matter. As the kissan meal is going on, I could not go through complaint. The issue will be tackled as soon and possible," added Dr Mann.

Meanwhile, unrest amongst the women students on the campus is spiraling owing to the inordinate delay. A student on condition of anonymity said, "It all depends on the university officials to handle the case fairly so that it acts as a deterrent for others."

Heading: Jake’s life will be a testimony of new-age medical marvel - Indian Express
Content:
The Ludhiana police have arrested an ex-serviceman for allegedly conning unemployed youths on the pretext of giving them jobs in the Army. The police have also seized some fake rubberstamps from him.

Rajinder Singh Thakur (47), a native of Kangra district in Himachal Pradesh, was a constable in the Army. He was dismissed from the services in 2000 on disciplinary grounds.

Addressing a press conference today, SP (Detective) Gurpreet Singh Toor told mediapersons that Thakur was arrested near the Baddowal ammunition depot on September 19. Posing as a top Army officer, he used take between Rs 30,000 and Rs 50,000 from jobless youths on the pretext of giving them jobs.

SP Toor said that the police had received many complaints that a conman impersonating as a top Army officer was duping unemployed youths.

Toor said that after arresting Thakur, the police found the accused had been arrested thrice for conning unemployed youths hailing from Kangra, Chandigarh, Haryana and Punjab.

SP Toor said that further investigations are on in this case.

Heading: One-way answer to traffic chaos - Indian Express
Content:
Jacob Pastel is like any other 18-year-old from Santiago in the USA. He likes to listen to music, watch movies and spend time with friends. And most of all, he loves to play guitar. But sadly, he can't play the guitar anymore.

Jake (as he is fondly called) is presently undergoing treatment for brain cancer at Sibia Medical Centre (SMC) in the city, with the help of what is dubbed as Cytotron therapy — the technology which is based on Rotational Field Quantum Magnetic Resonance.

"Earlier, I was scared about why it happened only to my son. Then after much introspection, I figured out the reason. If he survives, he will spread the message of the utility of this new technology which is not available back home," said his father Daniel.

Cytotron therapy is a new technology developed indigenously by the researchers of the Institute of Aerospace Medicine in Bangalore. It has shown promising results during clinical trials, which brought the father-son duo in the hope of curing the brain cancer. The technology is still not used in the USA as it does not fall under FDA Rules.

Two year ago, when the Pastel family was to celebrate Daniel's 50th birthday, he had to tell his son that he had brain tumour.

As fingers of Jake's left hand gradually stopped obeying the signals of his brain which was later diagnosed with inoperable brain tumour, Daniel became more and more firm in his mind of one thing — there has to be a solution to it.

"I was looking for information on the treatments of brain cancer on the Internet when I stumbled upon this new technology. Unfortunately, many big hospitals or doctors in the US were not even aware of it," Daniel narrates their journey to India.

"When I researched some more, I discovered that it was being offered in India and Malaysia only. I sent an email to this centre in Ludhiana and got a positive feedback and we landed here on September 3," he adds.

"By now we had exhausted all forms of possible treatments like radiotherapy or chemotherapy, and it all did not seem to work. The tumour would sometimes increase, or get smaller with medicine like Avastin. When it got worse one day, I asked Jake if he was ready to come to India and he agreed," he goes on. Daniel has been documenting every single day of his treatment on a blog www.jakepastel.blogspot.com.

Dr SS Sibia said it (Cytotron therapy) is still in its nascent stage as only a handful of hospitals across the world are using it. "Nevertheless, the results of the therapy have been very encouraging as seen in the six patients we have treated so far," he said.

"Till 2007, we had been using it only for patients of arthritis in order to increase the growth of cartilige. Later, we also started using it on cancer patients as it has no known side effects at all," Dr Sibia said.

"The treatment here will last for another 11 days as the therapy is first used for a 28-day session and the results are seen through MRI. We are hoping that the results are better so that we confirm the reason of our visit to India," Daniel tells with moist eyes.

Heading: MNS to Sena and back again, led by Satpute - Indian Express
Content:
If it works on Solapur Road, why not elsewhere, ask civic activists

In a city plagued by frequent jams, traffic managers need not long farther than Solapur for inspiration. A one-way system on Solapur Road, which is in the Pune Cantonment Board (PCB) area, has worked wonders in decongesting traffic.

With 20 days to go for the Commonwealth Youth Games (CYG), traffic is more chaotic than ever. Civic activists say the solution to the traffic problems in the Pune Municipal Corporation (PMC) area could lie in replicating the Solapur one-way system, instead of building expensive and time-consuming flyovers.

Jams on the stretch from Golibar Maidan to Pulgate started to ease after it was converted recently into a one-way zone. Vehicles from Swargate to Solapur Road now take a left turn from the PCB office and follow a circular route to reach Pulgate or farther ahead.

"There was some opposition from local residents after the stretch was made one-way. But most people now welcome the move. Commuters have also praised the initiative," Deputy Commissioner of Police (traffic) Manoj Patil said.

Civic activist S C N Jatar, a retired major general, said, "Converting two-way roads into one-ways is perhaps the easiest and the easiest way of tackle the chaotic traffic. Though the PMC undertook such measures on some roads in the past, it is not considering this option any longer, as it should. In fact, instead of building expensive roads and flyovers, it should first try this method at bottlenecks."

PMC additional engineer (projects) Srinivas Bonala said, "Such initiatives need to come from the traffic police, as it is their prerogative. As a civic body, we can support these decisions and facilitate its implementation."

The DCP (traffic) said the traffic police would continue to take such measures. "We have been holding talks with the authorities of the PMC and the PCB." Bonala said the PMC is holding talks with the traffic police on traffic problems at places such as Sangam Bridge, Dengle Bridge and Fergusson College Road.

Stressing that one-way roads are an excellent solutions to the disorderly traffic, activist Vijay Kumbhar said, "More than the civic bodies or police department, such measures should be supported by citizens. Many times, such positive moves are shelved following pressure from local politicians and organisations."

Heading: Development rules in force 10 km into city fringes - Indian Express
Content:
With Lok Sabha polls just a few months away, the political climate has begun to hot up in Pune as well. On Monday, Ganesh Satpute, Maharashtra Navnirman Sena (MNS) convener for western Maharashtra, led a dozen local leaders back to the Shiv Sena. The return of the MNS leaders to the Shiv Sena fold was officiated by leader of the Opposition Ramdas Kadam and party MP Shivajirao Adhalrao-Patil.

The MNS leadership put up a brave face, claiming it was no major loss. "Satpute was not contributing much to the party's growth," said MNS leader Ravindra Dhangekar.

According to political analysts, Satpute had been keeping a low profile recently and did not take part in any of the party's recent agitations. Also, Satpute did not get along with Deepak Paigude, a known confidante of party supreme Raj Thackeray.

"There were speculations about the end of the Shiv Sena after Raj Thackeray and Narayan Rane left the party. However, around 95 per cent of the party cadre that followed the two leaders have rejoined the Shiv Sena," Kadam said at a ceremony held to welcome the prodigals back.

"Some of the original Sainiks got carried away and went in wrong directions, but they have now realised the importance of the Shiv Sena. Many more party leaders and activists will rejoin the party in the next few days," he added.

Kadam said the party is growing under the leadership of executive president Uddhav Thackeray, who has shown a big heart to accept those who left the party in the past.

"I had taken the decision to quit Sena in haste and have now realised the mistake of quitting the party which I had served for 20 years. It is only the Shiv Sena that fights for the cause of Hindutva and Maharashtrians," Satpute said after announcing his resignation from MNS and re-joining the Shiv Sena.

Kadam accused other political parties of trying to highjack the issue of Marathi nameplates and compulsory use of language in office, which was first raised by him in the state assembly.

"I had made the speech raising the issue in state assembly last year and the state government had given assurance on it," Sena leader said adding he would soon make public his speech and the government reply on the issue of compulsory use of Marathi nameplates in shops and use of Marathi language in the court.

Others office-bearers of the local MNS unit who rejoined the Shiv Sena were Mahesh Mahale, Ramesh Gogawale, Machindra Gadade, Palash Shriram, Ajay Bhuvad, Nitin Bhujbal, Rajesh Palaskar, Vickrant Vaidya, Atul Dighe, Anil Kolhe, Sunil Thube and Madan Gade.

Heading: Villagers give conditional OK to Dow unit - Indian Express
Content:
The State government will enforce Pune's development control (DC) rules to areas up to 10 kms from the civic limits.

The government issued a notification in the last week of August. Congress MLA Chandrakant Chhajed, who had raised the issue during the Assembly session in April, provided a copy to reporters on Monday.

They had alerted the government that since DC rules were not applicable beyond the municipal limits of Pune and Pimpri-Chinchwad, the fringes were developing haphazardly. Following this, Minister of State for Urban Development Rajesh Tope announced a plan to bring these areas under DC rules.

The notification says: "Government has sanctioned the Regional Plan for Pune district through a notification, which has came into force in February 1998. The DC rules for the Pune Municipal Corporation (PMC) and Pimpri-Chinchwad Municipal Corporation (PCMC) limits and the adjoining areas are not uniform. The DC regulations for the areas within these municipal limits have been modified from time to time but the DC rules for areas within the Pune region have not been modified in respect of height of the building and parking provisions... It was therefore felt necessary to have a homogenous development of the areas adjoining these municipal corporation limits and to have proper planned development of the areas within 10 kms distance from the boundaries of PMC and PCMC," says the notification.

The assistant director of town planning would prepare a proper road network plan, which developers and landowners will have to incorporate in their development proposals.

Heading: Mayor Bhosale among judges at world leadership meet - Indian Express
Content:
In a sudden, apparent thaw in the Dow Chemicals imbroglio, a section of people from Shinde village, the proposed site for the research and development unit of the company, expressed a willingness on Monday to give the green signal to the unit, but with a rider attached.

They met District Collector Chandrakant Dalvi and demanded that the company enter into a written agreement with the Gram Panchayat, promising not to violate any pollution norms. They want a monitoring committee comprising villagers and Dow Chemical officials to regulate the proceedings.

They said if the company abides by the terms and conditions, they would give up resistance to the project.

The villagers have been protesting against the company since January and have blocked the road to the construction site.

Dalvi will now meet Dow Chemical officials to take forward the villagers' demands. "During discussions, the villagers expressed anxiety over the project. They said if a written agreement is made by the company and the monitoring committee is set up, they would not mind the project in their village," he said.

The villagers also want an assurance that the company would conduct only research and development work at the unit and would not enter into any kind of production. The villagers also wanted the company to ensure that the river nearby is not polluted.

The villagers said they were tired of the agitation, on since January 16. In the last nine months, there have been several agitations and many villagers have been arrested. "The villagers are not living in peace," they told the collector.

The villagers had blocked the road to the construction site. The blockade has been on since January 16 and in July, some construction material at the site was burnt down after the High Court gave an interim order to resume construction. On September 17, some officials of the company were attacked and their vehicle was set on fire.

Getting tired of the volatile situation, the village representatives including sarpanch Gorakh Temghire, former sarpanchs Tanaji Kendle and Datta Temghire, decided to meet Dalvi to chalk out a solution.

But there seems to be a division among the villagers. Some villagers and representatives of Lokshasan Andolan said the majority of the villagers did not want the project to come up. Vilas Sonawane of the Lokshasan Andolan said, "We want all the arrested people to be released. We are clear that we do not want the project in the village."

Heading: For villagers beyond Manchar, treatment is never closer than 50 km away - Indian Express
Content:
Mayor Rajlaxmi Bhosale has been invited to join an elite panel of judges for the World Leadership Forum award for 2008-09, a year after a PMC project won an award at the meet. "I have been invited as one of the panelists," Bhosale told The Indian Express.

The World Leadership Forum is a non-profit NGO that promotes leadership by highlighting the work of exceptional leaders and achievers in a host of disciplines and stimulates debate on leadership issues.

"This is in recognition of the good work carried out by the PMC," she said, adding that she would send her acceptance letter to the forum.

The civic body would once again compete for the award with similar bodies across the world by sending entries on various projects. Bhosale said one of these would be the Self Help Group (SHG) project for women's empowerment.

In December 2007, the PMC had bagged the World Leadership Forum award for developing a special software for automatic scrutiny of building proposals, beating competitors from Los Angeles and Lagos in the architecture and civil engineering category. A team of civic officials, together with Mayor Bhosale, had made the final presentation on the Auto DCR software before the panel of judges in London. The software helped in standardisation while ensuring transparency for a work that used to be done manually.

Heading: Don’t use public money for publicity: Pawar - Indian Express
Content:
When four members of a family in Bharadi village, about 10 km from Manchar, took ill on Friday night, they were taken from one hospital to the other, covering four hospitals in Narayangaon and Manchar areas.

The four villagers had dinner together and started vomiting at around midnight. But none of the hospitals could offer them treatment for food poisoning. They were told to rush to a hospital in Pune city or Pimpri-Chinchwad, 50 km from Manchar.

By the time they were brought to the Yeshwantrao Chavan Memorial Hospital in Pimpri, two of the patients were frothing from the mouth and the condition of the other two had also deteriorated. They had lost six crucial hours running from one hospital to another in Narayangaon and Manchar.

But the saga did not end there. There was a shortage of beds at YCMH and only two of the patients could be accommodated in the intensive care unit. They other two had to be taken to a private hospital in Chinchwad.

The patients, Dagdu Khilari, Chandrakant Jambhle, Ramesh Khilari and Yogesh Y belong to a below poverty line (BPL) family.

Dagdu Khilari, recuperating at YCMH is a marginal farmer and this year he has been facing a terrible time. "I sowed peas in April. Since the rain was delayed, there was no yield and hence no income," says Khilari, tears in his eyes. Kisan Jambhle, the head of the family, says they are hard-pressed as they had to pay Rs 20,000 at Chinchwad hospital. "Where do we bring the money for treatment?"

All the four are stll in the ICU of the two hospitals and are out of danger, but the incident has once again brought to fore the need for better medical facilities in rural areas of the district, especially for those who cannot afford costly treatment in private hospitals.

For patients from Chakan, Rajgurunagar, Manchar, Narayangaon to Ale Phata, there are only two government hospitals with less than 50-beds.

These areas have a population of 10 lakh and 30 per cent of them poor. Most emergency cases are rushed to the 700-bed YCMH. It takes nearly two hours to reach Pimpri-Chinchwad and then there is no guarantee of finding a bed as YCMH has a heavy inflow of patients. Transporting the patients to the hospital is another headache.

Medical superintendent of YCMH Dr Anand Jagdale said every month around 150 patients from Chakan, Rajgurunagar, Manchar, Narayangaon, Junnar and Ale Phata are admitted to YCMH. This month alone, 159 patients from these areas had been admitted. "Most are critical cases like accident victims, complicated delivery cases, snake bites, paralysis and food poisoning. They need to be admitted to ICUs. We have 24 beds in two ICUs. When there is no space, patients are advised other hospitals."

Kalpesh Pagaria, an entrepreneur from Pimpri-Chinchwad recalls that around 10 years back his father had met with an accident at Ale Phata. "We had to bring him to Pune for treatment. It took over two hours. By the time we reached the hospital, he had passed away. On the way, he was talking to us. Had there been a hospital nearby, my father would have survived."

The four patients from Manchar too may have met with the same fate, had there been any further delay, said Dr Jagdale.

Shiv Sena MP Shivaji Adhalrao Patil, in whose Khed Lok Sabha constitutency the areas of Chakan, Rajgurunagar, Narayangaon, Manchar, Junnar and Ale Phata fall, says he has been pressing for a hospital like the 700-bed YCMH or the 1,100-bed Sassoon Hospital, but in vain. "The Union Health Ministry has rejected my proposal, arguing that my area falls in rural parts," he said.

Heading: Gujarat cops visited city for blasts probe, keep mum - Indian Express
Content:
Coming out in support of the decision of the NCP local unit in the Pune Municipal Corporation (PMC) to freeze the Rs 19.5-crore promotional plan for the Commonwealth Youth Games (CYG) starting on October 12, NCP chief Sharad Pawar on Monday said that public money should not be used for publicity as it can be done by raising money from private sponsorship.

It was improper to spend public money for publicity purpose and the public money should be used properly, Pawar told reporters while justifying the stand of the ruling NCP, Shiv Sena and the opposition BJP in PMC.

The NCP chief said that the money for publicity can be raised from sponsorships from private companies.

If the public money is spent on cultural function then it would be difficult to run the civic body, Pawar said.

The civic administration had proposed sanctioning of the funds for cultural programmes during the youth baton relay and promotional hoardings, special mobile vans for publicity and advertisement in the media. The proposal was turned down in the standing committee with the NCP, Shiv Sena and BJP voting against it while the Congress and MNS voting in favour.

Heading: Intel India joins hands with University of Pune - Indian Express
Content:
A team of Gujarat police was in the city for investigations of the serial blasts in Ahmedabad. Investigations have revealed that members of sleeper cell of Student Islamic Movement of India (SIMI) in Pune and Hyderabad cities have provided logistical support for the terror outfits.

Speaking to The Indian Express, Joint Commissioner of Gujarat police Ashish Bhatia confirmed that their team was in Pune for investigations into the Ahmedabad blasts.

"Our team had visited Pune a few days back," Bhatia said, but refused to reveal more details about the investigation.

Sources however said that Gujarat police was on the look-out for Abdul Subhan Qureshi alias Tauqeer, the suspected mastermind behind the recent serial blasts.

Tauqeer reportedly visited Pune sometime in 2005-2006 and held secret meetings with SIMI activists. After the Ahmedabad blasts, Tauqeer went to Bharuch in Gujarat. Then he went to Akkalkua in Nandurbar district and from there to Nanded. Since then Taqueer has been untraceable.

The Gujarat police had earlier arrested Dr Mohammed Salim Honali, a former professor of dentistry at M A Rangoonwala College of Dental Sciences and Research Centre at Azam Campus.

Honali was arrested at his native place Vijapur in Karnataka. Now that investigations into the Delhi blasts have revealed that explosives for the recent serial blasts had come from Karnataka, the Guajrat police and Maharashtra state Anti Terrorism Squad (ATS) are investigating the role of Honali in supplying explosives.

Intelligence agencies believe that Honali was proficient in bomb technology and had trained some youths in a camp at Dharwad in Karnataka.

When contacted, inspector Peter Lobo of Pune ATS unit said, "We have no idea about the Gujrat police team coming to Pune. They have not contacted us for any support. Anti terrorism squads in all states are working in co-ordination with each other." Sources from intelligence agencies said that interrogations of top terrorist leaders including SIMI chief Safdar Nagori and Abu Bashar have revealed that Pune was considered as an important "logistic support". Sources from ATS said that sleeper cell in Pune conducted a reiki of IT companies in Pune.

Members of the sleeper cell were trying to indoctrinate more educated youths into jihadi ideology. Investigative agencies believe that Pune, with its educational and infrastructure facilities, provided a good training base and logistic support for SIMI.

The Pune ATS had arrested a SIMI suspect Feroz Pathan from Makka Tower in Ghorpade Peth and Imtiyaz Baba Mia Sheikh from Thane with possession of jihadi literature and CDs.

A top operative of Pune's sleeper cell Bilal Kagzi, a graduate from A A Khan Law College in Pune, who was arrested from Gujarat by the Mumbai crime branch in connection with an extortion case had provided the jihadi literature to Pathan and Sheikh for distributing it in Pune. Kagzi indoctrinated Ayaz Khan and Nadim Sheikh into the SIMI ideology and got them involved in circulating the Jehadi literature.

Heading: Family drama: Man tries to kill wife, surrenders - Indian Express
Content:
The University of Pune (UoP) along with Intel India on Monday announced a joint initiative aimed at creating a specialised work force for the semiconductor industry.

The UoP-Intel Higher Education Program is the first of its kind aimed at MSc students. The idea is to bring industry-specific knowledge to the classroom exposing them to emerging newer technologies in semiconductor development and design.

Speaking at the press conference, Dr P.Vidyasagar, professor, UoP said, "The course will lay the foundation for other such interactive programmes and will also enable the students to pursue career in science."

The main aim of our program is to train post graduate students and enable them to be on par with the engineering students. In the last few years the need for interactive electronic designing has gone up and it has a huge demand now. We are hopeful that this course will provide the same, he added.

The program will offer a complete course work on the VLSI (Very Large Scale Integration) Layout Technology and develop training facilities for the students. Biswajeeth Chaterjee, of Intel India said, "The main aim of our collaboration with the University of Pune is to bridge the gap between demand and supply. This first of its kind innovation is only a step forward and we hope to have many more such ventures with other colleges in the city."

Subodh Manav of Intel said, "The pilot program that was introduced last year received a good response with all the students in the program getting placed."

Heading: Concern over rising cost of education - Indian Express
Content:
A dispute over finalising the terms and conditions for divorce took an ugly turn when Rajesh Shinde (38), a businessman and a resident of Nyati Meadows in Wadgaon Sheri, attempted to kill his wife Bhavana by firing at her with a country-made revolver near India Bulls mall in Shashtri Nagar on Monday morning. Bhavana was saved as the bullet missed the target and hit the road. Rajesh immediately surrendered at the Yerawada police station, near which the incident took place.

The police have seized a country-made revolver from his possession. "Rajesh married Bhavana in 1997. It was a love marriage. They have two children — a son and a daughter. About six months ago, things turned sour between the couple and Bhavna left his home. She is staying on rent in the Maharashtra Housing Society in Yerawada," said Deputy Commissioner of Police (Zone IV) Jalinder Supekar.

"They were about to file a mutual divorce petition in the court on Monday. But there was a dispute over the terms and conditions for divorce. Rajesh wanted Bhavana to sign the divorce papers. But for the last 15 days, Bhavana was not responding to him. She did not attend his phone calls either," Superkar said.

"On Monday, Bhavana left for office on her two wheeler. Rajesh began chasing her in his car at 11.15 pm. He dashed his car on her vehicle in front of the India Bulls. As she fell down, Rajesh fired a bullet at her. But the bullet missed her," Superkar said.

A team of Yerawada police, led by senior inspector Prasad Hasabnis and inspector Sunil Deshmukh, rushed to the crime scene. The police have recovered an empty cartridge and a splinter from the spot. "Rajesh does not have a gun licence. "We have booked Rajesh under Section 307 (attempt to kill) of Indian Penal Code and Arms Act. We are investigating how and where he got the revolver," said inspector Deshmukh.

"Rajesh is director of Rushat International, a company manufacturing musical instruments. He is also a consultant for Joel Immigration and has his office in Clover Centre at Pune Camp. Bhavana was working at a educational centre in Koregaon Park," Superkar said.

In the wake of the rising number of murder cases in the city, the Pune police, led by Additional Commissioner of Police (crime) Rajender Singh, had conducted a study earlier this year. According to the study, every three days a murder happens in the city. And domestic dispute emerged as the reason behind majority of the murders.

Observes Dr Ulhas Luktuke, a reputed psychiatrist, "if a person turns violent to the extent of killing a close family member, it is mainly due to emotional inadequacy. "Tackling frustration is not included in our education syllabus. Many people are unable to tolerate frustration due to domestic disputes. It is called emotional turmoil due to which a person turns violent and behaves unintelligently that he ends up killing the opponent," Luktuke said.

Heading: Act One - Indian Express
Content:
The Arya Samaj and Public Concern for Governance Trust (PCGT), an NGO, have raised concern about the huge expenses involved in admission procedures in metropolitan cities.

"These days, education has become a business and a very expensive commodity for one to buy. With promises of posh amenities, distinguished faculty and claims of lucrative job placements, institutes are indirectly forcing students to pay lump sum amount in form fund or donations," said S C Nagpal, former chief commissioner of income tax and managing trustee of Arya Samaj, Pune, at a meet organised to discuss the issue of "Ethics in education" on Saturday.

"In the name of development and building funds institutes go on collecting such huge amounts for years together, and the surplus, which exceeds crores of rupees, goes unaccounted. Any kind of amount paid to these educational institutes must be accounted for," said Nagpal while talking on the ethical dimensions and emphasising on the need to end such corruptions. "It's the parents and students who must raise their voice against such malpractices and help the education, police and income-tax department in uprooting corruption," he said.

Parents attending the seminar also discussed their good and bad experiences while getting admissions for their wards at different levels, from kindergarten to postgraduate courses. While Col Ajit Palekar spoke on procedures laid by the state government for giving approval to technical and medical education institutes, B G Deshmukh, chairman of PCGT, summed up the proceeding and said that apart from being good human being, people must come together and a joint voice must be raised so that this movement turns into a crusade against corrupt practices.

Heading: Work it out - Indian Express
Content:
As BMCC registers a grand success in Purshottam Karandak, students get into future planning mode

Registering a dramatic success, it was the Brihan Maharashtra College of Commerce (BMCC) team that bagged the coveted Puroshattam Karandak title on Sunday. Struggling their way through the final round, BMCC team defeated nine other teams to prove themselves as best, peaking at just the right time.

The winning team had acted on a story, named Don Shoor, which was based on a Russian book by Anton Chekhov. Giving the details about the story, the co-ordinator of the team, Saroj Gangurde says that the story revolves around two men, one is city-based and is going to the village, he misses his bus and has to travel by the bullock cart. He is afraid but still projects himself as a calm and composed person. The 40-minutes play is only about the journey.

"Students have taken special pain to actually go to the nearby forest at night and get the experience as how it feels and what expression of fear they would have to bring when on stage. The victory was the right reward for the effort," says Gangurde.

The team comprises of 12 students, while three of them acted, rest helped. Aalok Rajwade, second year student, directed the play and also won the best director award.

Talking of his experience in directing a play for Puroshattam Karandak, Rajwade says that he has been acting and directing plays since last two years but this was his first experience with Puroshattam Karandak. Rajwade plans to take up acting and direction both in his future ventures.

Among the actors, Abhay Mahajan played Sudhir Khirsagar, who is a city-based youth and is going to the village. Abhay was also awarded consolation prize in acting. "This was the most challenging role I have ever performed. The expression was tough to get, as I had to portray both fear and composure. The character was of an insecure and conscious person. The story was based in a forest so we all had to create that fear element which was difficult."

This 19-year-old has also worked in Marathi feature films, one of which was released recently in Atlanta. And this is his fourth Karandak venture. He plans to take up acting full time, but refrains from saying what is more interesting – theatre or films – given his limited experience.

Om Bhutkar, who won the best actor prize, played the character of the villager, who is misunderstood as a dangerous person by the city-based youth. When asked what similarities he finds in the character that he played and himself, he says, "The characters are taken from real life only so there has to be some similarity. But here I'm very opposite to what I played."

The 17-year-old Bhutkar feels it is too early for him to decide a career for himself and he believes in justifying everything he does.

Another actor-in-making, Akshay Tanksale, could manage a small but important role in the play, which brought him a consolation prize for acting. A second year student of BCA, Tanksale says, "Acting is my hobby and this was my first experience with Karandak. Though I plan to take up computers as my career, acting would remain my interest and I would love to do more such."

The team was a happy lot; as they had put in a lot, right from making the bullock cart to creating the forest feel on stage. But like they say all's well that ends well. And this is one story with a really happy ending for BMCC.

Heading: Wine Wine situation - Indian Express
Content:
While fitness experts Susanna Backman Boman feels a healthy lifestyle matched with any form of exercise is the answer, Marie Carola Solem advocates Yoga as the right way

From celebrities to students, everyone seems to be bitten by the fitness bug these days. Health is not the only reason for it though. Beauty and fashion has also become reasons for one to shed those extra kilos. Medications, surgery, diets and exercise — while there are many ways to do so — it has always been known that exercising is the most safe and effective way to lose weight. It not only helps reduce fat but also improves your endurance and stamina.

"Exercising is not important only when you are fat. Even if you are in good health regular workouts are important to keep you going. These days obesity is a common problem everywhere. It can give rise to a number of health problems and everyone looks for a quick and effective way to lose weight. But we should always remember that it is important to adapt a healthy lifestyle and enjoy whatever form of exercise we indulge in," suggests celebrity fitness trainer Susanna Backman Boman, who was in city recently to inaugurate Tushar's Fitness Studio on NIBM Road.

The monotonous regime of weight training is passé. Power yoga, kickboxing, fusion dancing and so on have also been inculcated in the workout regimes now. "Exercise may be done in any form, be it sports, dance, yoga, walking or simple stretches, the most important thing is it must be accepted and enjoyed by your mind and body," says Boman, adding, "Walking is the most significant and easiest way to burn your fats and tone the body muscles."

Cardiovascular exercises like jogging, walking, stair climbing, cycling or rowing, are the basics for any workout. "Cardiovascular exercises improve and increase the body's metabolism. Your warm-ups start with such exercises. They are very good especially for the elderly; it keeps their heart rate in check and also keeps them healthy," shares Boman.

But Marie Carola Solem, who had earlier been a personal trainer for 13 years, discovered yoga as her way to healthy life. "After I found yoga I stopped weight training. Yoga is the best and the most steady way for exercise and relaxation. I practice Ashtanga yoga six days a week. Now, I am a full time yoga teacher, teaching Ashtanga Vinyasa yoga and Hatha yoga in Sweden," says Solem a fitness model and personal trainer.

Heading: Radio rules - Indian Express
Content:
Maturing well in its third year, the Pune Gourmet Club plans to take its next wine festival to a new high along with introducing the open source restaurant concept in the city

Just a toddler in the year 2007, the first ever-wine festival in the city in its 2nd year matures to shed the tag of just another wine tasting festival. As the members of Pune Gourmet Club announce the highlights of festival on club's second anniversary the hopes of the festival making it big this time soar high. So get ready to witness another complete wine tasting festival. And this time the festival has a lot more to offer than just 'pairing which wine with what food' lessons. With eight more wineries to add to the seven in the first festival and over six gourmet stalls (last year there were three) the festival, scheduled in December this year, will inveigle wine lovers showcasing city's international and eclectic cuisine.

And it's not only the stalls and wineries, which will undergo a change. Apart from the usual attributes the festival had last year, this festival in an effort to make it an experience of a lifetime adds the international touch by coming up with the concept of open source restaurant. " It's a concept which will give enough freedom to the people to be themselves. They can come at the festival, cook food, which they like on their own, pair it with the wine and just have a gala time. It is will be fun as well it will make them put to use whatever they grasped at the festival," says B Shakarnarayan, moderator, Pune Gourmet Club. Like last year every one visiting the festival will be equipped with a `wine tasting kit' comprising a wine glass, a tasting card and a wine companion (students from Nashik) so that the consumers can use a reference point in the future. But apart from these, this time they will be also accompanied with a blue tooth enabled environment. "Every one will have to vote through their blue tooth enabled phones for wine rating and then the best wine will be selected," shares Shakarnarayan.

The festival apart from cultivating the love of wine amongst people also aims to promote Indian wines across the country. "In this one year the wine scenario has experienced a tectonic change. Lot more new wineries have come up apart from Sula, Vinsura, Nira, Century and other usual names that dominate the Indian wine scene. We encourage new wineries to showcase their wines at the festival. This time too we are doing the same," says Shakarnarayan. Providing a platform to the new wineries across India the festival will feature seven new wineries across the country. " Deccan Plateau is a small boutique winery to whom we have requested to launch their wine in this festival," says Shakarnarayan who remains hopeful about wineries from Karnataka participating in the festival. "I am expecting the wineries there to participate because of the change in the tax equation recently," shares he.

Meanwhile the second anniversary celebrations of PGC hosted at Silk Route in Koregaon Park on September 21, was a resounding success with over 70 members in attendance. An assortment of Indian wines combined with exotic Latin American cuisine dished up by members themselves made the Sunday afternoon a memorable one, as did Chef Parag Kanhere's much-appreciated guidance to the band of enthusiatic cooks. All in all an event worth raising a toast to for sure.

Heading: Ladies Only - Indian Express
Content:
Radio veteran Ameen Sayani gets candid on the new era radio

Changes are inevitable but the art lies in keeping pace with the change and at the same time not losing the heritage as well," feels radio veteran, Ameen Sayani. He was in the city to attend the national radio meet organised by Symbiosis Institute of Mass Communication.

Despite his advancing years and illness that had taken hold of the ever-energetic Sayani, there was no sign of weariness in his magical voice that was a treat for both the youngsters as well as the other guests, who grew up listening to him.

And despite the feebleness nothing could stop the legendary icon from attending a programme that's about radio. Speaking in his signature style Sayani said that he cannot imagine himself out of media and is still working on some projects.

For more than 50 decades now Sayani has been the voice of radio, and he firmly believes the radio that has once again come up as strong medium, is capable of bringing in a sea change in the society.

Given the strong presence of radio in everybody's life, Sayani says that today the medium is even more active and is satisfactorily catering to the demands of its audience. When asked about radio being used for bringing about a social change by including serious programmes Sayani says, "The ideal thing will be to sandwich the community programme with entertainment so that it retains the interest of the audience and at the same time gives a socially relevant message. People look at radio as one medium of entertainment and a compromise on that is incomprhensible."

Expressing his content on radio's progress, Sayani says that radio has certainly made a strong comeback and is here to stay given the busy schedule of people, who find radio a very handy entertainment.

However, taking care of the commercial aspect of the industry, he says, "Radio has to sell. We cannot turn serious by compromising on entertainment. Our first priority is to meet people's demand, only then can we maintain our presence in their lives. Like any other profession this is also a profession where people need to earn. So the commercial aspect is equally important. Throughout my career, in all my radio programmes I have used social relevance as an undercurrent for entertainment. And I can say that unless it is a balanced blend of humour, commercial interests, education and many other factors, the programme may not be appealing enough to draw audiences from all sections."

Giving example of popular programmes of past, Sayani points out that a programme is hit when people are involved. "A programme by the Kashmir station of All India Radio, Zoona Dab, which raised social and civic problems faced by the people of Kashmir, witnessed immense popularity but later had to be taken off air. Another was Chauraha where villagers use to meet and discuss their problems, this was also a big hit in the history of Indian radio."

Commenting on the current working style of radio, he suggested that more emphasis should be given to recorded programmes so that the content could be managed.

Heading: Spotlight shifts from N-deal to Wall St crisis - Indian Express
Content:
The presence of some glittering Bollywood faces in Anamika Khanna's guest-list breathed some life into the otherwise slow-paced proceedings. And when the beautiful Sonam Kapoor sashayed down the ramp, the applause we heard was the loudest. The surprise entry of the evening was Sanjay Leela Bhansali with his mother who clapped for his protégé. Also applauding their daughter were Anil and Sunita Kapoor who were both playing hosts. The front rows were sprinkled with more stars in the form of Twinkle Khanna, Madhur Bhandarkar, Karan Johar, Surily Goel, Seema Khan, Rita Dhody (looking better than the models) and Pooja Shetty.

Khanna's choreography was the least dramatic but thanks to the wide ramp, the models were almost walking into our laps. This had to be Khanna's weakest collection to date. Leotards under chiffon tunic dresses, overlaid kurtis and ruffled skirts, aren't anyone's definition of haute couture. Every ensemble looked like a pared-down version of something far more beautiful, ironic since her ready-to-wear shows are far dressier. That said, her cutwork styles were the highlight, especially a red, rose-motif coat.

Pallavi Jaikishan's well-heeled family, Roohi and Chetan Jaikishan, Yogesh and Priya Jaikishan and Bhairavi Jaikishan were present to applaud her. The SoBoites and star wives after exchanging hellos witnessed what can be termed as the shortest couture show so far. Queenie Dhody dressed in a Jaikishan saree, Avanti Birla, Kaajal Anand, Haseena Jethmalani, Anju Taraporewala, Bhavana Pandey, Rita Dhody, Nitasha Nanda, Ekta Raheja, Tanya and Arvind Dubash, Maheep Kapoor, Chhaya Momaya and Bonita Bulchandani applauded the designers work.

The ramp was a French garden with an artificial lawn, plants, vines and exquisite benches and the choreography was dramatic to say the least. A male model dressed like a French nobleman with a white wig served chocolates to the models sashaying down the ramps and guests seated on the front row. Jaikishan's clothes too had a European influence with Duchess satin and lace lehengas made to look like ballroom gowns with French tape embroidery, crystal embellishments and embroidered flowers and accessorised with stoles. But the kalidaar lehengas and bandhini sarees took away from the European feel.

Heading: 'Mayawati has kept Rs 6,500 cr for LS polls' - Indian Express
Content:
With just two days to go for Prime Minister Manmohan Singh's White House visit, there still seem to be no clear indication on the status of the Indo-US civil nuclear deal with both the US administration and the Congress bogged down over the financial crisis in the country.

The focus has shifted to bail out the country from the economic turmoil and the administration is trying hard to iron out the parameters and specifics of the nearly USD 1 trillion package that is being put through to stabilise frightened markets.

One of the legislative strategies being discussed recently is that of attaching the Financial Package to the 'Continuing Resolution' that is needed to fund the government past the end of the month.

Some are hoping that the civilian nuclear deal will also be attached to this resolution so that the Congress can pass one Omnibus measure prior to its adjournment for the season.

However, the Bush administration is pressing hard to form an "acceptable framework and language" to get the deal approved with parleys going on till late Monday evening at the aides level between the Senate and the House of Representatives on the Text of a Resolution of Approval of the nuclear agreement.

Administration officials were at one time quite hopeful that the India agreement would be ready to get through the Congress prior to the adjournment of September 26, perhaps even readying themselves for a signing ceremony at the time of the Bush-Singh meeting scheduled for September 25.

Congress will have to pass a Continuing Resolution to fund Federal Government beyond September 30, as most, if not all, of the spending bills have not been passed.

At this time, it is maintained in many Congressional quarters, the civilian nuclear agreement can only be attached to a larger 'Continuing Resolution Package' as there will be no time for it to be addressed as a 'Free Standing Legislation'.

"I don't see the likelihood of any free standing proposal would have any opportunity for consideration" the Acting Chair of the Senate Foreign Relations Committee, Christopher Dodd told media persons on Monday.

"The Indo-US civilian nuclear deal will pass" remarked a Senior Congressional aide working for the Republican minority.

Indications suggests that if Congress cannot come to terms with the Financial Stabilisation package then they are probably going to have to sit for another week; and if the work is still not finished then the President can ask for a Lame Duck session of Congress that will probably start in the first week of December.

One of the first substantive moves on the civilian nuclear deal could come in the Business Session of the Senate Foreign Relations Committee this afternoon when law makers on the Panel could decide to Mark Up the India Agreement to the senate floor for action.

The Senate Committee has listed a number of things on their agenda including the approval of several nominations; but the Indian nuclear agreement is not one among the items. Foreign Relations Committee headed by California Democrat Howard Berman is yet to schedule a hearing.

"Chairman Berman is considering the matter with the congressional leadership, with his colleagues and with the Administration," the Spokeswoman of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, Lynne Weil said.

"He is discussing legislation that will waive the 30-day requirement but it must be legislation that strikes the right balance to attract sufficient congressional support, and he is working out the details," Weil said.

Senior Congressional aides on the House insist that there will have to be additional legislation to waive the thirty day continuous session requirement on the civilian nuclear deal.

"The Hyde Act and the Atomic Energy Act stipulate the thirty day requirement. It is the law, not a rule. Additional legislation is needed to waive that legal requirement" a top aide said.

Heading: Post-Godhra riot accused sent to judicial custody - Indian Express
Content:
Charging BSP supremo Mayawati with amassing huge wealth through unfair means, the Samajwadi Party on Tuesday alleged she had kept nearly Rs 6,500 crore for her party for contesting the coming Lok Sabha election in Uttar Pradesh.

Ever since her name was floated by Left parties for Prime Ministerial candidate, Mayawati's main focus was on amassing wealth for the Parliamentary poll, SP president Mulayam Singh Yadav said in Lucknow.

The UP Chief Minister "has no concern for welfare of farmers and traders and for development of the state ever since Left parties threw her name up for the post of Prime Minister," he said.

With an eye on the election, her only aim was to amass wealth through unfair means, the SP chief said.

He alleged Mayawati had kept aside nearly Rs 6,500 crore for contesting the Lok Sabha election in Uttar Pradesh alone.

Yadav claimed he had specific information that Rs three crore changed hands for scrapping the high-powered committee set up to grant no objection certificates in the higher education department.

"Decisions such as hiking VAT rates are aimed at increasing the revenue," he said and asked "but, where is the money going and how it is being spent?"

The former Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister alleged the money was being squandered on setting up parks and memorials in the state.

Alleging nothing was being done to provide relief to flood victims, farmers and students, Yadav said a meeting of party district unit chiefs would be held on October five to chalk out SP's strategy in this regard.

Terming the Ganga Expressway project as unnecessary, he said he was told the government plans to keep the acquired land even if the project falls through as "huge sums have been paid as commission".

Yadav said this would not be allowed at any cost.

Heading: Guj cops tracked cell trail to Atif, shared it with Delhi in Aug - Indian Express
Content:
Seventeen people, accused in three separate post-Godhra riot cases of 2002, were sent in judicial custody on Monday by a court in Ahmedabad.

All 17 were produced before the Metropolitan Magistrate after the end of their police remand on Monday.

The accused were arrested last week by the Special Investigation Team (SIT), constituted by the Supreme Court to re-investigate the Godhra train burning and 10 riot cases.

Of them, seven have been arrested for their alleged involvement in the violence at Gulberg Society here where 38 people, including ex-MP Ehsan Jafrey, were killed.

Six are accused in the Naroda Gam case in the city, where 11 person were killed.

The other four have been arrested in the Naroda Patia case where 84 people were killed during the riots, triggered by the Sabarmati train burning, six years ago.

Heading: '4 held for Delhi blasts were behind Jaipur explosions' - Indian Express
Content:
As early as August 20, investigators from the Gujarat Police and the Intelligence Bureau probing the Ahmedabad blasts, handed over a series of cellphone numbers, including the one used by Atif alias Bashir, the alleged mastermind of the Delhi blasts and one of the two men killed in the Jamia encounter last Friday. Intercepts of Atif's phone number indicate there were 12 people in his house the night before the encounter since Atif's phone was used to order dinner for a dozen.

Sources have detailed the sequence of events to 'The Indian Express' that led to the encounter in which Inspector Mohan Chand Sharma lost his life.

Gujarat Police was told by the landlord of a house in Vatva, Ahmedabad, which was used by terrorists for the serial blasts in Ahmedabad on July 26 that one of the SIMI cadres used telephone number (9712398204) to call him for renting the house.

Tracing this number, Gujarat Police found that five pre-paid SIM cards had been purchased, including the above number, using fictitious identities. Investigations showed that this number was used by main accused Abu Bashar for a while.

Checking on the above number revealed that it received two calls from eastern UP from number 9415835341. This phone number went dead before the Ahmedabad blasts.

Working on the eastern UP number, the Gujarat Police found calls from 9811004309, which was being used by Atif.

Gujarat Police handed over Atif's number for surveillance at a senior level to both the Delhi Police Special Branch and to the Intelligence Bureau. This is confirmed by DCP Alok Kumar.

On September 17 — four days after the Delhi blasts — when Abu Bashar was brought to Delhi by Ahmedabad crime branch inspectors Zankat and T S Patel, Atif's number showed it was operating in four locations, including Jamia Nagar. The other three locations are still under verification.

While the Delhi police claim that there were five people in the house at the time of the encounter, telephone intercepts suggest that Atif's number was used to order pizzas for dinner for 12 persons. However, as pizzas were not available, the person using the phone said that the "food (delivered) should be enough for 12 persons." Besides, the four persons arrested on Sunday by the Delhi Police were apprehended after a call — lasting six to seven minutes — made to a landline from Atif's number.

Heading: BJP never encouraged communal politics: Rajnath - Indian Express
Content:
Cementing the theory that SIMI and Indian Mujaheedin were behind the string of terror attacks in the country, Rajasthan police on Monday claimed Atif, one of the four militants arrested in connection with Delhi blasts, was the mastermind of the serial explosions in Jaipur in May.

The Special Operation Group of Rajasthan police investigating into the May 13 blasts in Jaipur said Atif, Sajjid, Mohd Saif and Junaid, who were held by Delhi police after recent blasts in the national capital, had carried out the serial blasts in the Pink City in a planned manner along with Khalid, Arif, Sahadab, Bada Sajjid, Salman and two others.

SOG DIG A Ponnuchamy said the attacks in Jaipur were jointly carried out by SIMI and Indian Mujaheedin.

The mastermind of this entire conspiracy was Atif who was a member of Indian Mujahiddin, A Ponnuchamy said.

Giving details of the planning and execution of Jaipur blasts, he said that on May 11 all the 11 boarded a Rajasthan Roadways Volvo bus from Bikaner House in Delhi at 0800 hours and reached Jaipur's main bus stand at Sindhi Camp at 1300 hrs.

Thereafter, they constituted a three teams--two of three members each--and another of four members comprising Salman, Safiq and another unidentified person. The group was headed Atif.

The second team constituted of Sahabad, Khalid and the other unidentified person and the third team consisted of Sajjid, Saif and Chotta Sajjid.

Both Chotta Sajjid and Atif were killed in an encounter with police encounter in Delhi on Friday.

Heading: Govt says Noida CEO death a warning, India Inc in shock - Indian Express
Content:
BJP condemns any form of violence that are on communal lines and the party never encouraged communal politics, party President Rajnath Singh said, in Mumbai.

Terrorism has to be contained at any cost, Rajnath who visited the victim Amit Singh of serial train blast of July 11, 2006 who is in coma at Jaslok hospital in south Mumbai, said.

He described his visit as part of the rehabilitation work that has been carried out by his party when replying to a query on the reason for his visit soon after the Delhi serial blasts.

He donated Rs two lakh to Amit's parents as part of rehabilitation work, the party has been doing for the last two years.

Rajnath also inaugurated a mobile medical van at suburban Bhandup.

Heading: Shun politicians who seek to divide: Aamir Khan - Indian Express
Content:
India and Pakistan on Monday agreed to start trade across the Line of Control (LoC). The cross-border trade is expected to start from October this year.

This was decided at a meeting of the joint working group on cross-LoC Confidence Building Measures held in New Delhi. "The modalities of cross-LoC trade were finalised," said the joint press release, adding that the meeting had been "cordial". The modalities relate to trade on the Srinagar-Muzaffarabad route and the Poonch-Rawlakote route, while a third one, the Kargil-Skardu route, is still under consideration.

While the Indian delegation was led by the MEA Joint Secretary (Pakistan) T C A Raghavan, the Pakistan side was headed by Foreign Affairs Ministry Additional Secretary (South Asia) Aizaz Ahmed Choudhary.

While cross-LoC trade had been first mooted in 2005 after the bus service was started, the steps required to implement it had not been agreed upon so far, with Indian officials contending that Pakistan was stalling the move.

Foreign Secretary Shivshankar Menon had expressed his disappointment on Friday, when he regretted Pakistan's dilly-dallying over reciprocating India's gesture of sending businessmen from the Indian side of Kashmir.

India had hoped that trade could begin from October 2—just in time for Eid—but Pakistan is yet to send a delegation of businessmen from Muzaffarabad for talks.

A delegation of the Chambers of Commerce from Muzaffarabad is expected to undertake a visit to Srinagar and Jammu next month to discuss various aspects related to the trade, the sources said.

The meeting of the chambers of the two sides is essential as it is they who actually have to engage in trade. In July, foreign secretaries of both countries had exchanged lists of commodities with zero tariff regime and agreed to indicate the items they were willing to receive.

Heading: Cops conduct search ops in Atif's village - Indian Express
Content:
Actor Aamir Khan on Sunday plunged unexpectedly into the Marathi manoos controversy, dismissing it as a non-issue and advising fans to shut out those seeking to 'divide us on the basis of language or culture'.

The actor-turned-director made his political stand known at a press conference meant to celebrate the selection of Taare Zameen Par (TZP) as India's official entry for the Academy Awards.

Without taking names, he said: "We should be wary of any politician who wants to divide us on the basis of language or culture. If a politician does that, then he's not for the country but for himself. We should support leaders who are positive thinkers, who can bring people together, promote peace and brotherhood."

He called himself a Marathi but struck a nationalistic chord: "Any film, be it Hindi, Tamil or Telugu, has a right to be released anywhere in the country, even in Maharashtra. It's one country and this is a non-issue. We should respect all the languages and cultures."

On his film, Khan unveiled a massive campaign strategy aimed at helping TZP achieve what Lagaan and Rang De Basanti could not. On the agenda are screenings for Academy members in Los Angeles and New York, besides roping in the services of an LA-based PR company to create a media buzz.

"Since I'm the producer-director, it's my responsibility to create awareness. We'll advertise the film and tell members how TZP has played an important role in creating childcare awareness in our country. I'm sure the film will leave a strong impact on members; it will at least make them cry," he said.

Heading: SC hands over UP PF scam probe to CBI - Indian Express
Content:
A joint team of Delhi police and Uttar Pradesh Anti Terrorist Squad (ATS) on Tuesday conducted searches in Delhi serial blasts main accused Atif's native village in Azamgarh district, official sources said in Lucknow.

The team reached Sanjarpur area in Saraimeer village in the wee hours and questioned relatives and conducted searches to find clues relating to the blast case, ATS sources said.

The team, the sources said, has succeeded in tracing a bank account of Atif in Pawai branch of a nationalised bank through which transactions of over Rs three crores were done in the past six months.

The bank manager will also be questioned besides relatives of the accused, they said.

A chopper was also flown from Lucknow to Azamgarh to facilitate arrest, if any, so that those nabbed could be flown to Delhi or Lucknow, they said.

The ATS sources said the Delhi police had got some leads during interrogation of those arrested after an encounter in the capital on Friday about the links of terrorists in Azamgarh.

Heading: BMW hit-and-run case: HC issues notice on Nanda plea - Indian Express
Content:
The Supreme Court on Tuesday handed over to CBI the investigation of the Uttar Pradesh provident fund scam in which the names of some judges from the higher judiciary, including one from the apex court, have cropped up.

The apex court granted three months time to the investigating agency to place the status report relating to the probe in the case.

However, a bench headed by Justice Arijit Pasayat said though three months time have been given, CBI shall not in any way be stopped from going ahead with filing of the final report earlier.

The bench said "the court before which the final report/chargesheet will be placed will deal according to the law".

The apex Court said CBI shall nominate an investigating officer to be incharge of the probe who can take the assistance of the state government officials.

The UP government will provide all manpower and infrastructure facilities to the CBI for carrying out effective investigation, it said.

The court said all the documents relating to the case will be microfilmed and deposited before it, the copies of which will be handed over to the CBI and the Uttar Pradesh government.

The documents already collected by the UP police and the reports prepared by it will be handed over to the investigating officer, it said.

Heading: I will marry soon, says Rahul Gandhi - Indian Express
Content:
The Delhi High Court on Tuesday issued a notice to the city police on a petition filed by Sanjeev Nanda challenging a lower court's decision to sentence him to five years' imprisonment in the BMW hit-and-run case.

Justice Kailash Gambhir sought a response from the police after briefly hearing the contentions of Nanda.

Sanjeev Nanda, grandson of ex-naval chief S M Nanda, approached the High Court against his conviction and quantum of sentence awarded to him by the lower court.

Senior advocate Mukul Rohatgi, appearing for Nanda, contended that no incriminating circumstance appeared against him and the trial court had wrongly convicted him due to publicity in the media.

Seeking bail from the court, Nanda contended that the trial court has accepted the testimony of controversial prosecution eye-witness Sunil Kulkarni which is not reliable as he was in Mumbai and not in Delhi at the time of accident.

Heading: Amarinder has full support of Congress: Alva - Indian Express
Content:
I will get married soon, said Rahul Gandhi, the 38-year-old scion of the Nehru-Gandhi family.

He was replying to a question at a roadshow in Bathinda on Tuesday on whether he has any plans to tie the knot.

Gandhi, without giving any details, just said "I will get married soon".

The Congress General Secretary, who is on a three-day visit to the state, met families of at least ten persons either killed or injured during the Punjab panchayat polls in May.

He listened to the family members and assured them of "maximum help" after he returned to Delhi.

The young MP also heard grievances of people who complained of "atrocities" during the present Akali Dal-BJP rule.

Congress workers in Bathinda told him about the alleged political vendetta against them unleashed by the ruling combine in the state, party sources said in Bathinda.

Gandhi also met inmates of a local drug de-addiction centre run by the Red Cross society.

During his interaction with people the young Congress leader sought to woo the youth to join the party.

Heading: Singur row threatens to overshadow Durga Puja - Indian Express
Content:
