Khan is hoping his previous experience with the Oscars will help: "Maybe some of the jury members will give TZP more attention if they recognise me from my earlier films," he said.

Yet, for all the hype, Khan claims that the golden statuette is not high among his priorities. "I don't need an Oscar to tell me that my film is good. I make films for the audience; if they like a film then that's my award. It's just that international forums provide a platform for filmmakers to address a larger audience," he said.

Asked whether he has put behind him 'Lagaan's' loss to 'No Man's Land', Khan said that in his eyes Lagaan didn't lose. "After the ceremony, about 40 members came up to me and told me that they were disappointed that Lagaan didn't win since they had voted for it. It's just that all five films that year were great. Lagaan didn't lose."

As to why an Indian film has not won an Oscar till now, Khan delivered a parting shot: "That's because the other films are better." He'll be hoping to change that this time around.

Heading: Indian art offering 'safe haven' at turbulent time - Indian Express
Content:
The countdown has begun for the two biggies that are slated for release this Idd: 'Drona' and 'Kidnap'. A lot is riding on these two films. In terms of economics, both are expensive films. Plus, the careers of Abhishek Bachchan [Drona] and Imran Khan [post Jaane Tu… Ya Jaane Na] are at stake. Will 'Drona' live up to the humungous expectations?

"It's my biggest and best film so far," Abhishek Bachchan tells me. He's supremely confident this time. "I don't speak like this, do I? But Drona is different. It's the most expensive film I am associated with. Besides, Goldie [Behl; the director] has executed the subject remarkably," he states.

Abhishek and Goldie have got together after more than seven years ['Bas Itna Sa Khwab Hai' was released in July 2001]. In between, in 2006, Goldie had plans of making a thriller with Abhishek, but decided on making an adventure fare instead. "Goldie was disheartened after his debut film failed. Later, he diversified into television; he wanted to make his company secure before he announced his next film," Abhishek reminisces.

Abhishek credits his directors for the [sterling] performances he has delivered in films like 'Yuva' and 'Guru' [Mani Ratnam] as also 'Sarkar' and 'Sarkar Raj' [RGV]. "If at all Drona works -- and I hope it does -- Goldie should get the credit for it. He has worked very, very hard. I am sure, the Indian audiences haven't seen an adventure film like Drona before," he says confidently.

Abhishek has worked in the 'Dhoom' series as also 'Sarkar' and its sequel. There's talk that a sequel to 'Drona' is in the offing. "Oh yes! Goldie has written so much in the intervening period that he's ready to take the 'Drona' series forward. In fact, the possibility of a sequel can easily be explored," he adds.

Heading: Now, an all-in-one guide for aspiring Romeos - Indian Express
Content:
Indian art might be just the solution for investors seeking a safe haven at a turbulent time.

Take a vivid landscape by avant-garde artist Francis Newton Souza hanging on a wall in Indian art dealer Ashish Anand's New Delhi gallery. With a price tag of $400,000, the painting might not seem like a bargain but Abnand says it will probably be worth $2 million within the next two years.

Art dealers and experts say the Indian art market is still undervalued and there is money to be made in local art for those with the means to pay the six figure prices that works by some of India's leading artists fetch at auctions.

"I think Indian art is a one-way bet in the long term. That's why I will allocate money to it," said Philip Hoffman who runs the Fine Art Fund based in London.

"If you look 50 years down the line, what you pay now is peanuts compared to what you will have to pay for the great Indian artists," he told Reuters at an Indian art summit in New Delhi in August.

The prices of Indian art have gone up considerably but not at the levels of Chinese art, which has seen prices soar due to enormous interest at home and abroad. Dealers believe Indian works have plenty of room to appreciate, especially as South Asian art begins to draw a Western audience.

"The growth potential is huge," said Hugo Weihe, Christie's international director of Asian Art.

"The Indian art market is particularly strong within India and that's different from the Chinese contemporary. You have that component plus we are now reaching out to an international component every season."

Often depicting vivid and colourful scenes of Indian life and culture, Indian art has long been popular among wealthy Indians, whose ranks are growing rapidly in a booming economy. Yet until recently Western collectors had not taken much interest in classical and contemporary Indian artists.

That is starting to change. Weihe predicts that sales of Indian art at Christie's auctions might reach $30 million this year, compared with $680,000 in 2000.

SKYROCKETING VALUATIONS

Asia's art scene has blossomed in the past five years driven by the continent's rapid economic growth. Valuations have skyrocketed as Asian art has become an investment for speculators and a symbol of affluence for a growing pool of local collectors.

The record for a contemporary Indian art work was set in June when Francis Newton Souza's piece 'Birth' was sold for $1.3 million pounds ($2.3 million).

The figure was, nevertheless, significantly lower than the $9.7 million record price for Chinese artist Zeng Fanzhi's piece 'Mask Series 1996 No. 6' sold at an auction in Hong Kong in May.

Works by famous Indian artists such as Maqbool Fida Husain and Syed Haider Raza currently go under the hammer for anywhere from $200,000 to $1 million.

Yet industry players expect prices to shoot up to between $5 million to $10 million in the next few years.

Neville Tuli, a manager of a $400 million art fund in India, believes that Indian art will appreciate by between 18 to 25 percent per year in a climate in which art is increasingly seen as a secure investment.

"Financial institutions and their HNIs (high net worth individuals) are recognising the inherent stability in the art object as a capital asset," said Neville Tuli, a manager of a $400 million art fund in India.

"Hence given its low correlation to economic circumstances and other related factors, the proportion of art within the alternative asset allocation is increasing significantly," he added.

HOT MONEY CANVASES ART

But as with all investments, there are risks. The Indian market is vastly different from the Western art markets because in India, art is viewed more as a financial investment rather than a collectors item, art fund managers said.

"It has gone up 200 times in five years," said Hoffman, of the London-based Fine Art Fund, adding that the Indian market consisted of 70 percent speculators and 30 percent collectors.

This trend of rapid buying and selling, makes it difficult to predict long term value.

"Let's say you've got a Gupta," Hoffman said, referring to Subodh Gupta, one of India's hot new artists whose pieces sell for between $800,000 to $1 million. "It's a financial commodity like a stock," Hoffman said.

"You need the Bill Gates of this world to say I want a Gupta and I don't give a damn how much it cost. It's going into my collection and it's not for sale," he added, saying a growing pool of collectors will give the market stability.

Art experts would like to see more people like Kusam Sani, a wealthy fashion consultant based in Delhi, who is one of the few art collectors who keeps the art they buy.

"I have a 40 foot dining room and it's covered with work, but I can't buy anymore because I've got no more space," said Sani, who has been collecting paintings since she was a teenager.

Greater government investment in art infrastructure and museums will give the market stability in the long term, experts said, although they noted that so far the Indian government has shown little political will to support such projects.

There are also bureaucratic hurdles such as permits to export works of art and requirements to register antiques with government bodies that turn acquisitions of Indian art into a headache for dealers and collectors abroad.

But despite the market's shortcomings, art dealers, Weihe and Hoffman are bullish on Indian art.

"The Indian market will mature when the real collector base is grown up and put the money is put to one side," Hoffman said.

"In the long run, all these artists are going to be global, they just happen to be local at the moment."

Heading: Sacked staff of Italy-based firm lynch CEO in Greater Noida - Indian Express
Content:
Struggling to woo women? Well, help is at hand -- thanks to a new all-in-one guide to romance which offers tips from the first act of chivalry right through to the knot.

Yes, the Debrett's Guide for the Modern Gentleman has everything from what to say and how to say it, to making your all important first move -- perfect for all aspiring Romeos, 'The Daily Telegraph' reported.

According to the guide, holding the door and being prepared to pay for the meal are a given. However, giving up your seat isn't necessary for those looking for love – unless you are trying to attract a pregnant or an elderly woman.

Your conversation should be a fine balance between talking and listening, and avoid talking about the three principal passions killers -- money, illness or death.

First date rules include drinks or lunch, that way having to avoid wasting an evening if you hate each other. Try to compliment her and come the end, if all's gone well, try to kiss her but don't try to get her into bed.

For those dating with children, advanced warning that the little darlings are coming along is vital, and never ignore your kids or choose solely adult activities to impress your target.

Blind dates should be avoided but if you find yourself set up, stick around for at least two drinks. In fact an early departure is "humiliating and ungentlemanly", according to the new guide.

If dating online, don't fall into the temptation of trying to be funny with your profile picture. Use a flattering one, but make sure it is realistic. Remember, chat up lines are no substitute for eye contact and good humour.

Flowers make a splendid present, but there are pitfalls. Mixed bouquets can look cheap if not a decent size and well arranged, and bulk up the flowers with greenery.

While proposing, timing, location and confidence are all things you should prepare. Get down on one knee, she will love it (and if a look of horror spreads over her face you can always pretend you're tying a shoelace).

And when it comes to choosing a diamond ring, remember the four Cs - carat, clarity, colour and cut. If disaster strikes remember to keep your dignity and never grovel, lose your temper or try to change her mind.

Heading: Gujarat Police tracked cellphone trail to Atif, shared it with Delhi in August - Indian Express
Content:
Sacked employees of an Italian auto-parts maker bludgeoned the chief of the company's India operations to death following a violent disagreement with the management on the firm's premises in Greater Noida's Udyog Vihar on Monday afternoon.

Lalit Kumar Choudhary, Chief Executive Officer and Managing Director of Graziano Transmissioni India Pvt. Ltd was allegedly beaten with iron rods. He was declared dead on arrival at Kailash Hospital in Greater Noida. He is survived by his wife and a young son.

"A total 40 injured from both sides have been admitted in the hospital. Half a dozen are in the Intensive Care Unit," said Dr Mahesh Sharma, Chairman and Managing Director of Kailash Hospitals.

Police said the incident happened around 12.30 pm, when the dismissed employees met the management to resolve a dispute that had been continuing for the last five months. "The employees wanted a raise and permanent jobs with the firm," SP (Rural) Babu Ram said. "The standoff took a serious turn two months ago, when the agitating employees ransacked the company's offices, and the management retaliated by dismissing around 300 people for misbehaviour and rioting."

A Graziano official said the sacked employees were told to give an undertaking not to launch any movement. . "This was a precondition for getting their jobs back. This led to an argument, which turned violent," the official said.

Bhanu Pratap Singh, IG (Law and order), said a large group of employees waiting outside got restive after rumours spread that a scuffle had broken out between the management and union leaders inside the meeting.

A worker who was injured in the scuffle with company guards told The Indian Express from his hospital bed that the employees had met the management with a written apology.

Graziano's officials said they had informed the Circle officer, Dadri and Station Officer, Bisrakh about the clash but the police took too long to reach. "When the security guard was beaten by the dismissed employees, we called up the police. However, the agitating employees got violent and hit the managing director with an iron rod," said the company's production manager.

Police have lodged FIRs against 119 employees and arrested 63. "Cases have been registered under sections pertaining to rioting, clashes, attempt to murder and murder. The Station Officer of Bisrakh police station, Jagmohan Sharma, has been suspended for dereliction of duty," SP (Rural) Babu Ram said.

(With ENS, Lucknow)

Heading: To help Bush push n-deal up the Hill, Delhi signals it can wait - Indian Express
Content:
As early as August 20, investigators from the Gujarat Police and the Intelligence Bureau probing the Ahmedabad blasts, handed over a series of cellphone numbers, including the one used by Atif alias Bashir, the alleged mastermind of the Delhi blasts and one of the two men killed in the Jamia encounter last Friday. Intercepts of Atif's phone number indicate there were 12 people in his house the night before the encounter since Atif's phone was used to order dinner for a dozen.

Sources have detailed the sequence of events to The Indian Express that led to the encounter in which Inspector Mohan Chand Sharma lost his life.

Gujarat Police was told by the landlord of a house in Vatva, Ahmedabad, which was used by terrorists for the serial blasts in Ahmedabad on July 26 that one of the SIMI cadres used telephone number (9712398204) to call him for renting the house.

Tracing this number, Gujarat Police found that five pre-paid SIM cards had been purchased, including the above number, using fictitious identities. Investigations showed that this number was used by main accused Abu Bashar for a while.

Checking on the above number revealed that it received two calls from eastern UP from number 9415835341. This phone number went dead before the Ahmedabad blasts.

Working on the eastern UP number, the Gujarat Police found calls from 9811004309, which was being used by Atif.

Gujarat Police handed over Atif's number for surveillance at a senior level to both the Delhi Police Special Branch and to the Intelligence Bureau. This is confirmed by DCP Alok Kumar.

On September 17 — four days after the Delhi blasts — when Abu Bashar was brought to Delhi by Ahmedabad crime branch inspectors Zankat and T S Patel, Atif's number showed it was operating in four locations, including Jamia Nagar. The other three locations are still under verification.

While the Delhi police claim that there were five people in the house at the time of the encounter, telephone intercepts suggest that Atif's number was used to order pizzas for dinner for 12 persons. However, as pizzas were not available, the person using the phone said that the "food (delivered) should be enough for 12 persons." Besides, the four persons arrested on Sunday by the Delhi Police were apprehended after a call — lasting six to seven minutes — made to a landline from Atif's number.

Heading: Via phonetap, 3 held for Hurriyat man’s killing - Indian Express
Content:
Downplaying speculation that the 123 agreement would be concluded during Prime Minister Manmohan Singh's visit to the US, top officials said there was no "immediate urgency" on the Indian side to rush matters over the next few days. Sources said India could wait till the US completes its domestic processes and there was "no pressing need" that the agreement has to be concluded when Singh meets US President George W Bush.

Broad indications from Washington are positive with the Bush Administration making an extra effort to see the agreement through in the current session of the Congress which could be extended by a week given the situation arising out of the financial meltdown. The view in the government is that given the anti-deal noises being made by some on Capitol Hill that the Bush Administration is letting India get away with way too much, the prudent option — now that the NSG waiver has been secured — is not to precipitate matters.

But one concern for India is that the agreement should not attract amendments — or accompanying resolutions — during it passage through the Congress. So the effort by House International Relations Committee (HIRC) chairman Howard Berman to include a resolution containing contents of a letter written by the State Department is seen as disturbing. It's in this context that the Prime Minister will speak to Democratic Presidential candidate Barack Obama if they cannot schedule a meeting.

Sources said India may not also needlessly object to broad-based resolutions relating to non-proliferation on the lines of the statement by External Affairs Minister Pranab Mukherjee. However, a clear picture was still not available to the Indian side which was anticipating a meeting of the Senate committee on Tuesday to decide the procedures for Congressional approval.

Among the options: tag the 123 agreement to the legislation on the financial bailout package that needs to be cleared immediately; both chambers agree to a joint resolution on the 123 and pass it together; Speaker Nancy Pelosi may bring the 123 to the House without the HIRC deliberating on it.

Heading: First reply to Sachar in: Muslims missing in institutes run by Arjun Singh’s HRD - Indian Express
Content:
Almost 40 days after the killing of Hurriyat leader Sheikh Abdul Aziz during the massive protest march along the Srinagar-Muzaffarabad road on August 11 — in which three other protesters were killed in police and CRPF firing — the J&K Police have arrested three neighbours from Baramulla for their alleged role in Aziz's killing.

They are: unani doctor Tariq Ahmed Teli; salesman at a shoe shop Irfan Akhoon; and a former militant Ashraf Akhoon, who now runs a poultry farm. They were arrested six days ago after late-night raids at their homes in Khanpora, Baramulla.

Incidentally, the first casualty in police firing that day was Manzoor Akhoon, cousin of prime accused Ashraf Akhoon.

According to a report based on Ashraf's interrogation — a copy of which is with The Indian Express — Ashraf's cellphone was under surveillance right through the rally from 9 am to 11.45 pm. The report says Ashraf had four SIM cards and used only one (9469289255) to talk to Furqan, a militant commander based in PoK. As many as 31 conversations between him and Furqan that day were recorded by the police.

In one of these, Furqan, the report says, told Ashraf to hand over the phone to Hurriyat leader Shabir Shah who was with Aziz in the march that day. Shah is in jail under the Public Safety Act and there are no details in the report about any conversation between Shah and Furqan. The report is also silent on why there was no immediate action if Ashraf was being tapped throughout. The report says the killing happened at least half a km away from Chahal which contradicts the official version that Aziz was injured in Chahal itself. When asked about these, senior police officers declined to comment. The report says the pistol allegedly used by Ashraf was kept "at (his) home for 15 days" and then given to a released militant. It's yet to be recovered.

Heading: Atif, Saif used same aliases to buy tickets, cycles in Jaipur - Indian Express
Content:
The number of Muslims employed in some of India's biggest and best-known state-run educational institutions is abysmal, data available with the government and accessed by The Indian Express, shows. The skew is most pronounced at the higher levels, the data shows.

Just 26 of the total 361 Groups A, B, C and D staffers at IIM-Ahmedabad (7.2%) belong to minority communities. The numbers are worse for IIM-Calcutta: there are 19 minority community staffers among a total 346 (5.5%), none among 85 Group A officers, and only 2 among 48 Group B employees.

Assam University has 6 employees from the minorities out of a total 245 (2.4%), and Banaras Hindu University 237 out of 6,202 (3.8%). Minority institutions like the Maulana Azad Education Foundation (17%) and National Commission for Minority Educational Institutions (28.5%) fare somewhat better.

The figures constitute the first bits of data coming in to the Department Of Personnel & Training (DoPT) and the Ministry of Minority Affairs after they asked all ministries to put together numbers of employees from different communities.

The effort at compiling the community-wise database followed the Sachar Committee recommendation that a National Data Bank be created, tabulating all information on the socio-economic and educational status of communities. Sample data is now available from some of the 119 educational institutions under the HRD Ministry.

The most glaring gaps are seen in Class A and B employees, which include gazetted officers of the rank of Deputy Secretary and above, and the equivalent of an Under Secretary respectively.

The University of Hyderabad has 33 minority community staffers against a total 376 Class A employees; BHU has 83 out of a total 1465; IIM-A 3 out of 30. The National Institute of Industrial Engineering, Mumbai has 1 out of 54, and the National Commission for Minority Institutions, none.

"While the low representation of minorities in Class A and B can still be explained citing lack of educational qualifications, what is the rationale for the abysmal representation even in Classes C and D?" asked a senior official. "Class C staffers are assistants to Section Officers, and Class D employees are sweepers, peons, drivers etc. This is a cause for worry," the official added.

The Sachar Committee report focused on two critical issues: under-representation of Muslims in government jobs, and the duty of the government as the 'ideal employer'.

Heading: UP cops blame HuJI, Delhi Police say IM - Indian Express
Content:
In a major breakthrough in the May 13 Jaipur serial blasts probe, the Rajasthan Police have collected crucial evidence corroborating the involvement of Saif, who was arrested in Delhi on September 19, and 10 others.

The police said Saif and 10 others bought cycles that were used in the blasts, placed the bombs in the predetermined sites and escaped to Delhi the same day. According to the police, the aliases the suspects used matched the names under which they purchased bus and train tickets from Delhi to Jaipur and back.

"Saif and ten others came to Jaipur on May 11, in a Volvo bus from Bikaner House in Delhi, and conducted a recce in the city. They left for Delhi after placing the bombs on May 13," said Rajasthan Special Operations Group (SOG) Deputy Inspector-General A Ponnuchamy.

The police said those involved in the blasts were: Saif, Atif and Bada Sajid (who were killed in the Delhi encounter), Junaid, Sajid, Khalid, Arif, Shahbad, Salman and two others whose names are yet to be determined.

According to Ponnuchamy, Saif and the others used aliases during their trip to Jaipur. "They purchased the cycles, train tickets and bus tickets under the same aliases. The names on the bills from the cycle shops, the bus reservation system and the train tickets corroborate this. We cannot reveal the aliases at this moment," he said.

While Saif is in Delhi Police custody, efforts are underway to apprehend the others. Sources said this information was garnered after interrogating Saif, who reportedly laid bare the Jaipur terror plot.

On reaching Jaipur's Sindhi bus camp on May 11, Saif and the rest split into three teams. Sajid, Shahdab and Atif selected the bomb locations, while the others chose the shops in Kishenpol, in the walled city area, from where they would buy the cycles. The suspects stayed in Jaipur on May 11, returned to Delhi on May 12, and came back to Jaipur on May 13, when they bought the cycles, placed the bombs and caught the 5.50 pm Shatabdi to Delhi.

Heading: Police get flak for ‘Arabic’ scarves of blast suspects - Indian Express
Content:
The Delhi Police have blamed the terror attacks in Uttar Pradesh on the Indian Mujahideen (IM) module that they busted last week, raising questions on the investigations carried out by the state police here. While the UP Police have chargesheeted different persons in these cases, the IM does not find mention anywhere. Instead, the HuJI has been blamed for the blasts.

Asked about the contradictions, UP's Additional Director General of Police Brij Lal said: "Investigation are still on. A team of the Anti-Terrorist Squad has been dispatched to question the persons arrested by the Delhi Police. Let's see what details they provide to our team."

Blasts in Lucknow, Faizabad and Varanasi courts

Thirteen persons were killed in these blasts on November 23 last year. The UP Police blamed HuJI activists, and arrested four suspected activists. Trial has begun in the Faizabad case, while the chargesheet has been filed in the Lucknow blast. The Delhi Police have said the bomb in Lucknow was planted by Arif and Junaid — both absconding; in Faizabad, it was Shahzad and Shadab alias Malik — both absconding; and in Varanasi, it was Mohammad Saif and Sajid. While Sajid was killed in last week's encounter, Saif was arrested.

The UP Police, however, named Sajjad and Raju alias Mukhtar of West Bengal as accused in Varanasi court blast. They said Mukhtar alias Raju, who is based in Bangladesh, had orchestrated the blasts in the three courts and arranged explosives. Mohammad Tariq Qasmi, a Unani doctor, was said to have led the team in Faizabad, while Mohammad Khalid Mujahid, a madrasa teacher, was suspected to be behind the Lucknow bomb. Both have been arrested. Two other accused—Sajjar Rehman and Mohammad Akhtar—were arrested from Jammu and Kashmir. The UP Police said three other accused—Zahid, Qadir and Imran Guru—were absconding.

Varanasi blasts

Two blasts took place in Varanasi on March 7, 2006 — one at the Sankatmochan Temple and the other at the Cantonment railway station. As many as 20 persons were killed. The UP Police have filed a chargesheet, and the trial is on. The Delhi Police said Atif, who was killed in the Jamia Nagar encounter, Saif, Malik and Junaid carried out the blasts. But the UP Police claim that HuJI member Waliullah, Imam of a mosque in Phoolpur town of Allahabad district, was the mastermind, and the blasts were executed by three persons with whom he had studied at Deoband. They were identified as Bashiruddin, Mustafiz and Zakaria, all from Bangladesh.

Gorakhpur blast

Six persons were injured in a blast in Gorakhpur on May 22, 2007. The police haven't filed a chargesheet yet. According to the Delhi Police, the blast was carried out by Atif, Saif and Salman. The UP Police, however, named Mohammad Tariq Qasmi, one of these arrested in court blasts, as a prime accused. "During interrogation, Tariq confessed to having planted the bomb in Gorakhpur. He even told the sequence of events leading to the blast and names of two other accused," said investigating officer Vishwajeet Srivastava.

Heading: Gujarat, Delhi police differ - Indian Express
Content:
The Delhi Police is being severely criticised for covering the faces of the three blast suspects—Saqib Nisar, Mohd Shakeel and Zia ur Rehman— with 'Arabic' scarves with many terming the act as "partisan" and "an attempt on the police's part to hint at a link between Islam and terror".

The police usually covers the faces of criminals, whose identity cannot be revealed, with a towel or a black cloth. However, when the three suspects were produced in court yesterday, their faces were covered with scarves usually sported by imams and religious leaders of the Muslim community.

Senior Congress leader Salman Khursheed told The Indian Express that such depiction was "unfortunate and created an impression of a stereotype at a time when images flashed by the media was being closely followed by the public".

Islamic scholar Dr Khwaja Iftekhar Ahmad, too, termed the use of the scarves as "offending". "It appears to be a design to malign the whole Muslim community and the Arab world. Making criminals wear such a scarf sends out a wrong message to other religions as well," added Ahmad.

The Delhi Police, however, maintained that it had no code of conduct as far as covering the faces of suspects go. "We do provide cloth to suspects to cover their faces with. But there is no code of conduct for it as such. The cloth could be red, black or white," said Delhi Police spokesperson Rajan Bhagat.

"A terrorist should be severely punished. But to depict a suspect in a way that can be recognised as 'Muslim' is wrong. This scarf is usually slung on the shoulder or used to cover the head during prayers," says Firoz Bakht Ahmed, who runs an NGO, Friends for Education, and teaches in Modern School, Barakhamba Road.

Interestingly, police had said that Indian Mujahideen mastermind Atif had instructed his companions to remain without beard and dress in modern clothes in order to escape a "typically Muslim look".

The Urdu Press has also lashed out at the Delhi Police for this. The Hindustan Express has carried an editorial, 'Dilli Police Ka Arbi Roomal', criticising the police's action in its Monday edition.

Heading: Lead anti-terror discourse: Advani to Kalam - Indian Express
Content:
Union External Affairs minister Pranab Mukherjee on Monday said that there was a great possibility of signing a bilateral deal with France and Russia for supply of nuclear fuel, apart from the much talked about Indo-US Civil Nuclear Cooperation Programme.

Speaking at a seminar titled 'Indo-US Civil Nuclear Cooperation and Its Future Impact' organised by the Rajiv Gandhi Development Institute in the city, Mukherjee vociferously defended the deal and accused the Left and BJP of joining hands in opposing it.

Mukherjee said that while India was likely to sign a bilateral agreement with France for supply of nuclear fuel during Prime Minister Manmohan Singh's forthcoming visit to that country, a similar deal is also likely to be signed with Russia during Prime Minister Vladimir Putin's visit to India. He also said India would sign the NPT if it became non-discriminatory and universally viable.

Mukherjee hoped that the US Congress will ratify the 123 agreement on September 25 but clarified that though US ratification was pending, it would not prevent India from entering into a bilateral agreement with other countries for supply of nuclear fuel.

"An India-specific safety agreement is just a passport to enter into nuclear trade with any country. We now need a visa," he added. Referring to criticism that the 123 agreement would compromise India's sovereignty, Mukherjee said, "there is nothing in that agreement, nor in the India-Specific Safeguard Agreement, nor in the waiver by the NSG, that can compromise India's decision making".

Mukherjee said the nuclear deal was absolutely essential for meeting the country's energy requirement.

Reiterating that India's independent foreign policy would not be compromised by the nuclear deal, he pointed out that India had protested against the US invasion of Iraq.

Heading: Uma’s best MP show, says BJP won’t return - Indian Express
Content:
After zeroing in on Gujarat Chief Minister Narendra Modi as the party's mascot for its anti-terror plank, the BJP on Monday hoped that A P J Abdul Kalam would help build a national consensus on terror and the need to effect stringent anti-terror laws.

"I was happy to read media reports about your concern over terrorism, which has assumed such serious dimensions that it has not only gravely imperiled India's national security and national unity but also threatened the safety of the common man... I feel that a person of your eminence can help in elevating the discourse on terrorism to a level where it can be discussed as a national problem requiring broad national consensus unimpaired by narrow electoral considerations," said NDA prime ministerial candidate L K Advani in a letter to the former President.

In his recent interventions, Kalam has stressed for a "unified intelligence agency" and a "national mission to eradicate terrorism". "I believe, time has come, apart from our multiple agencies forecasting and handling of the terrorist activities, we need to evolve an aggressive mission called National Campaign to Eradicate Terrorism (NCET), with mission oriented integrated management structure, duly passed as a Bill by Parliament," he had said last week. Kalam also called for a law "to provide stringent punishments and faster justice to the perpetrators of the crime in a time bound manner" and "national citizen ID cards for all".

Many of these ideas have been mooted by the BJP in the past. While Advani, as former Union Home Minister, wanted to implement a national ID card scheme for the country, the BJP holds the Centre responsible "for halting Gujarat's crackdown on terror agents by its refusal to give its nod to the GUJCOC Bill, passed by the state Assembly some four years ago". The party in its recent National Executive said that the "Congress was communalising the war on terror."

While the BJP chose to look the other way when attempts were being made to give him a second term as President, or when he rooted strongly for the Indo-US nuclear deal more recently, Kalam, nonetheless, has always been the "Ideal Indian Muslim" for the saffron party and the RSS.

"Like you and millions of ordinary citizens in the country, I am extremely concerned that an issue of such national and global importance is being ignored by a section of the political class," said Advani in his letter, in an obvious reference to the Congress position on terror.

"Therefore, your statement has come as a great relief. It holds out a hope for building a national consensus for initiating effective measures, including stringent laws, against terror. My intention in writing this letter is to request you to lead this initiative in a manner you deem fit. I assure you the cooperation of my party and that of the National Democratic Alliance in this effort," concluded Advani's letter.

Heading: Salwa Judum debate to dominate polls in south Bastar - Indian Express
Content:
The Bharatiya Janshakti turned in its best public performance till date in Madhya Pradesh on Monday as thousands crowded into the Lal Parade ground to hear Uma Bharati target her former party and L K Advani. With elections round the corner, the rally had attracted a lot of attention if only to find if the former BJP chief minister packs any punch. Though the BJP dismisses her as a spent force in public, the Congress hopes to gain from her presence in the fray.

At the same venue on March 15, 2003, Advani had projected her as the chief ministerial candidate, a chair she went on to occupy on December 8 that year, only to step down a few months later when a court issued a non-bailable warrant against her in a case of hoisting the Tricolour in Hubli.

On Monday, her two-and-a-half-year old party coined a new slogan: "Ram Se Dhokha Uma Se Chhal Ab Kabhi Nahi Khilega Kamal", accusing the BJP of dumping the Ram temple issue and Bharati once the purpose was served.

Projecting herself as a victim, Bharati took recourse to Mahabharata comparing herself with Arjun and the BJP with Kauravas. "In this battle, I have to decapitate my own people," she said.

There is no second leader with his own following in her party as the BJP has managed to win back those who had some support. Bharati said the BJP had heaped insults on her in the past three years, and ruled out her return at any cost. She admitted that she was surprised by the turnout.

According to her, only 5,000 dalals (brokers) had turned up recently at the Lal Parade ground where the Hindi version of Advani's book was released at a grand function. "Should not you be dubbed an agent of Mulayam Singh Yadav when you project him as prime minister," she asked Advani and lashed out at him for praising Jinnah.

While accusing the BJP of indulging in rampant corruption after her departure, she also targeted the Congress by referring to Afzal Guru and Sonia Gandhi's foreign origin.

Heading: Centre to send high-level team to K’taka - Indian Express
Content:
Controversial anti-Naxalite movement Salwa Judum is all set to become a poll issue that could make or break the prospects of both the BJP and Congress in South Bastar and even revitalise the Communist Party of India (CPI) in this tribal area in the next Assembly elections.

While the BJP is supporting Salwa Judum, describing it as a spontaneous movement against the Naxalite violence, local Congress leaders are divided over it. But the CPI has been opposing the campaign since it began in June 2005.

"BJP's success in South Bastar will depend on the fallout of the Judum movement. If there is a vote in favour of this anti-Naxalite campaign, the BJP will be benefited not only in Dantewada, Konta and Bijapur constituencies but also in other tribal areas where Maoists have a presence," said a senior BJP minister.

"It's for the first time that Assembly polls are taking place after the Salwa Judum began. It could make or mar the prospects of the ruling party," he said, adding the BJP was hopeful of getting support of tribals who were fed up with the Naxalite violence.

Ever since the movement turned violent and Maoist rebels began attacking those who participated in the anti-Naxalite campaign, the Congress has been divided over whether to support the Salwa Judum.

While leader of the Opposition Mahendra Karma, who represents Dantewada Assembly seat, is among those in the forefront of this anti-Naxal campaign, former chief minister Ajit Jogi and his supporters, including two Congress legislators from South Bastar, have been opposing the manner in which the Salwa Judum is being run.

Despite mounting pressure from a section of Congress leaders, Karma stuck to his stand of supporting the movement. "As far as the issue of campaign against Naxalite menace is concerned, I am at a point of no return, irrespective of its consequences," he said.

With the BJP supporting the movement and the Congress undecided, Communists see it as an opportunity to make a dent in the support base of both these parties in the elections.

The CPI, which had represented two Assembly segments of Bastar in the undivided Madhya Pradesh Assembly, has a strong support base in the region. In the state's maiden elections in December 2003, its candidates had finished second in Dantewada and Konta constituencies while they were third in Bijapur and Chitrakot constituencies.

"CPI is the only party which always stood with the local tribals who were caught between Salwa Judum activists and the rebels," says Communist leader and former legislator Manish Kunjam.

He told The Indian Express that his party had been opposing the way in which the Salwa Judum campaign was being carried out as it resulted in armed conflict, leading to tribals' exodus to neighbouring Andhra Pradesh and Orissa and forcing 56,000 people to desert their native villages and take shelter in the state Government-run relief camps.

"The mood of the locals is against the present form of Salwa Judum because of the atrocities being committed by the anti-Naxalite campaign activists and the destruction

it has caused to South Bastar villages," he said, adding locals could extend their support to the CPI in the elections.

Meanwhile, Maoist rebels have called for boycotting the Assembly elections in Bastar and are now circulating pamphlets and posters in the remote villages.

Police sources said there were intelligence inputs suggesting that the CPI(Maoist) cadres were holding meetings in the remote villages in Dantewada, Bijapur and Narayanpur districts to discuss their poll strategy as they consider that Salwa Judum had caused damage to the Naxalite movement in the area.

Heading: Governor rejected ex-CJ’s candidates for HC judges - Indian Express
Content:
Two days after it directed Karnataka to crack down on miscreants indulging in violence against the Christian community in the state, the Home Ministry has decided to send a team of senior officials to Bangalore to assess the situation.

M L Kumawat, Special Secretary (Internal Security) in the Home Ministry and A K Yadav Joint Secretary (Human Rights) have been asked to visit the trouble torn areas in Karnataka on Tuesday and will meet Karnataka Chief Secretary and other senior officials of the state government to discuss the steps that are being taken to contain the violence.The team will also visit Mangalore and Udupi, two places that had seen a number of churches being attacked by right-wing mobs protesting against alleged conversion drives by some Christian organisations.

Despite the Centre's stern message on Friday asking the state government to take immediate steps to ensure that peace and normalcy is restored, Karnataka has continued to witness violence against the Christian community.

Meanwhile, the Home Ministry made another appeal to the state governments to strengthen their intelligence apparatus and fill up the large number of vacancies in their police forces.

Heading: SC puts brakes on Punjab judicial appointments - Indian Express
Content:
Just before he retired, Punjab and Haryana High Court Chief Justice V K Jain recommended names of six District and Sessions Judges for elevation to the high court, a move strongly opposed by Punjab Governor Gen (retd) S F Rodrigues.

In his recommendation, Jain said that the senior-most judge, Justice J S Khehar, had reservations about some of the names, while the judge second to him in seniority, Justice Mehtab Singh Gill, felt no more appointments should be made in view of the lack of requisite infrastructure. However, he didn't include a written record of their views.

Neither did Jain put in writing the views of the next two judges in order of seniority, Justice K S Garewal and Justice Ashutosh Mohunta, who he claimed agreed with his recommendations.

General Rodrigues also felt that when Jain was on his way out and Tirath Singh Thakur was set to take over as the new Chief Justice, he should not have made these recommendations.

As per procedure, in case of the Punjab and Haryana High Court, which is common for the two states, the written recommendations of a collegium headed by the Chief Justice are sent to the senior of the two states' governors. In this case, that is A R Kidwai, the Governor of Haryana. The senior Governor then passes on the recommendations to the other governor after giving his opinion.

The recommendations are then sent to chief ministers of the two states, which give their individual opinions. The opinions of both the governors and the chief ministers are then sent along with the list of recommended names to the Law Ministry.

According to sources, of the six names recommended for elevation by Jain, Justice Khehar objected to K K Garg, G K Rai (from Punjab) and S K Sardana (Haryana). Jain's list also included Gurdev Singh (Punjab), R K Gupta, and M S Sullar, Haryana. Khehar reportedly took into account Rai's annual confidential reports as well as opinions of other judges advising him to reject his name, while a pending inquiry went against Sardana. Views of other judges and reliable quarters allegedly also went against Garg.

Heading: MBBS student kills girlfriend - Indian Express
Content:
The Supreme Court on Monday asked the Punjab and Haryana High Court not to issue orders giving judicial postings to candidates selected for subordinate judiciary in Punjab through entrance examinations between 1998 and 2001, following allegations of corruption in the conduct of examinations.

Issuing a directive restraining the HC, the bench of Chief Justice K G Balakrishanan, Justices P Sathasivam and J M Panchal stayed the High Court order allowing appointment of some candidates who were allegedly not tainted.

Acting on a petition filed by the HC Registrar, the court also issued notices to the Punjab Government and Punjab Public Services Commission seeking their responses to the pleas raised before it.

Heading: DMK offers to share power with Congress, adds rider - Indian Express
Content:
A final-year MBBS student of Gandhi Medical College has reportedly confessed to killing his girlfriend in his hostel room and disposing of her body in Pachmarhi, about 175 km away.

Chandresh Maraskole, 28, killed his girlfriend on Friday, kept the body in his room the entire night before heading for the hill station in a car owned by his senior.

The car driver had found the MBBS student's conduct suspicious and knew something was fishy when he found the bedding kept in the car missing. Chandresh had asked the driver to go away on some pretext and rolled the bedding — in which he had kept the body — down the hill in his absence.

After returning to Bhopal, the driver shared with the car owner, Dr Hemant Varma, what happened at Pachmarhi. While asking for the car, Chandresh had told Varma that he had urgent work in Hoshangabad. After reaching Hoshangabad he asked the driver to drive on towards the hill station.

Varma got in touch with the police who did not take long to make Chandresh speak. He confessed to strangling Ritu who had been staying with him in the hostel room for some time. Apparently, the two had an affair and she was pressing for marriage.

Chandresh alleged that the girl was suffering from a psychological disorder and was under treatment. Though she had rented a room in the city she used to stay with Chandresh, who hails from Balaghat. It's unclear how they got in touch with each other.

The body was found only on Monday afternoon after a protracted search involving the local police.

Heading: Actor claims DMDK men attacked his house, files case - Indian Express
Content:
Tamil Nadu chief minister and DMK leader M Karunanidhi on Sunday signalled his willingness to consider the request for power sharing in the state with the Congress, on whose support his government depends. However, he followed this up with a set of riders which would in all probability put paid to the possibility of any such arrangement.

DMK, with 96 members in a house of 234, is dependent on the support of the 36-member Congress for continuance in power, but had steadfastly refused to entertain demands of power sharing, made overtly and covertly by many State level Congress leaders.

Taking part in a public function at Tiruchy on Sunday, Karunanidhi said that the general council and executive committee of DMK would consider the demand if a request for power sharing was put forth by the Congress High Command, which effectively takes the State unit of the party out of the picture. Speaking after receiving the Periyar Award instituted by DMK for his contribution to the growth of the party, Karunanidhi said that the Congress high command was yet to make such a demand and that he had become aware of this through the media, indicating that the demand was mostly from lower level leaders. Putting another precondition to considering the request, Karunanidhi demanded a quid pro quo of sharing power in the Union Territory of Puducherry where there is a role reversal between the two parties. The 11-member Congress Government is dependent on the support extended from outside by DMK with seven members in a House of 30 members. Incidentally, even while the Puducherry Congress Government had been facing a severe crisis following internal squabbles, Karunanidhi had directed the DMK unit to stay away from the 'internal matters' of the Congress party and uptill now had never sought a share of power.

Ever since the DMK came to power in Tamil Nadu 26 months ago, many Congress leaders in Tamil Nadu had been angling for a share of power, though DMK had refused to entertain any such overtures. It was as a result of this arrangement that Opposition leader J Jayalalithaa, in all her press statements since 2006, had taken to describing the State Government as the 'minority DMK Government'.

Heading: Doon shocked as Catholic priest, aide murdered - Indian Express
Content:
The political war between various parties has entered Tamil filmdom with popular comedian Vadivelu filing a complaint against DMDK founder and matinee star 'Captain' Vijayakanth and his supporters, alleging that his party cadres had pelted his residence and office with stones on Sunday, a charge that the latter has since denied.

Both actors have been having a running feud for about a year after Vijayakanth floated his party, the DMDK.

In the latest incident, a bike-borne gang of about 40 persons allegedly attacked Vadivelu's house here on Sunday in what is termed as a continuation of the unresolved issues between the two. The comedian was to depose at one of the courts here on Monday in connection with the case registered last year.

However, addressing a hurriedly called press meet on Monday morning, Vijayakanth alleged that the entire attack was a drama enacted by DMK and that the veteran actor has become a pawn in the hands of the ruling party, "which is afraid of the rising clout of the DMDK".

Vadivelu, meanwhile, announced that he would take on Vijayakanth in the coming elections. "My patience has been tested by these continuing attacks. In the coming elections, I will contest against Vijayakanth as a nominee of all other political parties and defeat him," said an agitated Vadivelu at the court premises on Monday.

Heading: Soumya Reddy cremated - Indian Express
Content:
The murder of a Catholic Priest and a lady volunteer in Chhota Rampur area of Dehradun district has sent shock waves amongst the Christian community in Uttarakhand.

The priest Sadhu Astey and the volunteer, identified as Mercy, were found strangled in the two-room Smarpanalay Home in Chhota Rampur on Monday morning. While Astey was in his mid-fifties, Mercy was in her early thirties. The home was being run as a prayer centre, which also used to provide medical assistance to the needy.

The police said that prima facie it appeared to be a case of robbery. Circle Inspector Harish Verma told The Indian Express, "the home was ransacked and belongings scattered when the police reached the spot. A local informed the police after he noticed no movement at the home for the last two days. It appears that the murder was committed two days back."

Astey had been running the home for over 15 years in the Muslim dominated area. Verma said the bodies have been sent for post mortem and the police are taking the help of the dog squad to gather clues.

Heading: Village funeral for 800 storks - Indian Express
Content: The body of Soumya Reddy, who was shot dead by an unidentified assailant in the United States last week, was cremated here on Monday. A number of relatives and friends attended the ceremony at the Bansilalpet crematorium. Family members took Reddy's body from the Rajiv Gandhi International airport to their residence in Padmaraonagar in Secunderabad on Sunday night.  Soumya (23) was pursuing a post-graduate course in electronics engineering at the Southern Illinois University. Meanwhile, the body of Vikram Reddy, a cousin of Soumya,  is likely to be brought to Hyderabad later.

Heading: Mining: DAE official holds talks in Meghalaya - Indian Express
Content:
Five days after nearly 800 open-billed storks were killed as an old banyan tree collapsed in a temple complex in a remote Assam village, the residents not only cremated the birds in their typical Buddhist way, but also organised a prayer meeting seeking eternal peace for the departed souls.

The birds died when all the branches of the banyan tree, believed to have been planted when the village was established in 1835 by a group of Man-Tai people migrating from Upper Myanmar, collapsed on Wednesday due to the increasing weight of their nests.

"It was indeed a tearful event for the 300-odd residents of Banlung village. At the prayer meeting, five monks, led by Bichitra Mahathero, chanted from Buddhist scriptures written in Pali script and prayed for eternal peace of the departed souls," said Arup Ballabh Goswami, honorary wildlife warden of Golaghat, who was present at the prayer meeting.

Banlung village, though inside Karbi Anglong district, is closer to Golaghat. People also came in from four other Man-Tai Buddhist villages nearby to attend the funeral and the prayer meeting. In the village monastery where the banyan trees are located, people resolved to plant more banyan and simul trees so that the increasing population of storks could be dispersed and the load reduced from the existing trees.

Banlung, about 300 km east of Guwahati, is located close to the Kaziranga National Park, as well as to the Nambor and Garampani wildlife sanctuaries.

In Guwahati, the state chief wildlife warden has called for a detailed report from the district officials so that the residents of Banlung could be recommended for some kind of an award or recognition for the service they rendered to save the birds.

"We have got preliminary reports about how the villagers rescued the birds working round the clock," M C Malakar, chief wildlife warden, told The Indian Express here on Monday. "It is a case of community involvement in wildlife conservation," he added.

While, over 100 birds rescued from the disaster site are undergoing treatment at the Wildlife Rescue and Rehabilitation Centre at Kaziranga, vets from Karbi Anglong and Golaghat are also attending to the injured birds.

Heading: Assam remembers unsung heroes of 1942 - Indian Express
Content:
Department of Atomic Energy (DAE) Principal Advisor V P Raja, sent to Meghalaya by the Centre, on Monday held discussions with Chief Minister Donkupar Roy, Deputy Chief Minister Hopingstone Lyngdoh and others on the uranium mining issue.

Large deposits of uranium ore have been found in Wahkaji-Mawthabah in West Khasi Hills district of Meghalaya.However, it is facing opposition from the Khasi Student's Union (KSU) and political parties like the Hill State People's Democratic Party (HSPDP) due to fears that it will lead to radiation which can endanger the health of local people and cause irreparable damage to the environment.

Emerging from the meeting with Roy, Raja said: "The meeting went off well." Raja's visit comes a month after Union Cabinet Secretary K M Chandrasekhar and Atomic Energy Commission (AEC) Chairman Anil Kakodkar visited Meghalaya and held wide-ranging discussions on the mining issue with pro and anti-mining lobbies.

According to DAE officials, the uranium deposit in West Khasi Hills can take care of as much as 16 per cent of the estimated need for uranium for power generation. Raja told reportes that the Centre had worked out safeguards and there was no need for apprehension.

Heading: New AGP chief predicts Cong rout in elections - Indian Express
Content:
A begger and a sanyasi figure in the list of people who had laid down their lives while trying to hoist the national flag on police stations in Assam in September 1942. But though these two persons have remained unidentified throughout the past six decades, they are finally to be officially recognised as martyrs by the Government.

"It is tragic that these two persons, who were among 13 courageous souls who took the bullets of the British police while trying to hoist the tricolour atop the Dhekiajuli police station on September 20, 1942, neither have been declared as martyrs nor have their statues been included in the Dhekiajuli memorial," said Ramesh Chandra Bora, a senior citizen of Dhekiajuli in Sonitpur district, as the town observed the day on Saturday to recall the great sacrifice made by the 13 persons. Bora,the president of a public committee that maintains the martyrs' memorial in Dhekiajuli, moved a resolution at a public meeting on Saturday for installing the statues.

13 persons were officially recorded as killed in the worst-ever police firing in Dhekiajuli during the 1942 movement, with official records referring to the two heroes as "one bhikhari and one monk."

Heading: Lightning kills Mumbai doctor at relief camp - Indian Express
Content:
The Asom Gana Parishad (AGP) would wipe out the Congress in the next Assembly elections in Assam, apart from taking away most of the Lok Sabha seats in the next polls, Chandra Mohan Patowari, the newly-elected president of the regional party, said here on Monday.

"The AGP has been growing stronger and with the unification of all the breakaway factions that is expected to take place in a month's time, the party is marching towards unseating the Congress from the state," said Patowari, who was unanimously elected to the top post. He succeeded Brindaban Goswami, who had taken over from Prafulla Kumar Mahanta in 2001 after the AGP suffered a crushing defeat at the hands of the Congress in the Assembly elections.

Patowari, also leader of the Opposition in the Assembly, hit out at the Congress for trying to keep the insurgency issue alive for petty political interests. "The Congress does not want an honourable solution to bring the curtains down on insurgency. This is evident from the fact that the UPA Government headed by the Congress had discontinued talks with the ULFA which were going on in the right direction," he added.

The new AGP chief vowed to prevent a split in anti-Congress votes. "We are working with various parties, including the BJP, to prevent the loss of anti-Congress votes in the next elections," he said.

Heading: CM blessing, love in time of flood - Indian Express
Content:
As a medical student with the Preventive and Social Medicine Department, Chandrakant Patil (25) eagerly volunteered to be a part of the first team offering medical relief to victims of the Kosi flood. Barely a week into his stay in Bihar, the 24-year old doctor met with an untimely end after he was struck by lightning late on Sunday night at the relief camp being run by film director Prakash Jha in Kataiya. His body was being brought to Mumbai on Monday on its way to his hometown in Dhule.

"There was some distance between their place of residence and the tent which held all the equipment. While they were walking towards the tent last night, there was a sudden thunder storm and he was struck by lightning. He was not wearing any footwear at that time," said Dr Amit Nohwar, Patil's batchmate at the King Edward Memorial hospital in Parel. He was part of a team of 40 doctors from Mumbai's health department was assisting in medical relief operations after a call for help from the Bihar Government.

Inmates of the camp said Dr Patil suffered serious burn injuries and was taken to the Referral Hospital at Simrahi where he was declared brought dead. Lab technician Ramchandra also suffered serious burn injuries. Patil had been treating patients at the relief camps in Raghopur, Simrahi, Birpur and Kataiya for the past week.

Patil was a "bright student" having secured a place in both the SSC and HSC examinations. Patil's father Umakant works in a mill back home. Patil completed his MBBS degree from B J Medical College, Pune and joined KEM Hospital three months ago.

"His death has come as a shock to his parents. His mother is in hospital," said Anil Dudhabhate, general secretary of the Maharashtra Association of Resident Doctors (MARD). "He was a very friendly, hardworking resident doctor, with a keen interest in social work, something he planned to pursue," Dudhbhate remembered.

The 40 resident doctors from Nair Hospital, KEM Hospital and Sion Hospital were sent to the six worst affected districts in Bihar, to help with flood relief operations. Five of them returned on Monday evening, while the rest will come back on Tuesday evening.

"The entire team is in shock. We will come to know if the team is returning in an hour as they are coming with the body now. Our current priority is to ensure that the body reaches his residence and the last rites are duly performed. Details of compensation and other matters will be determined by the BMC officials in due course," said KEM Dean Dr M E Yeolekar. MARD which had supported the team's visit and stay in Bihar is planning to appeal to the state government to offer some relief for Patil's family.

Heading: SC stays Madras HC ban on explicit visuals for condoms - Indian Express
Content:
After the chaos and pain unleashed by the Kosi river, it was time for love and marriage at the Ghelar mega relief camp in Madhepura last week.

Sanjay Kumar Sada, 22, a resident of Katawan in Madhepura and Darun of Patarghat in Saharsa met each other at the relief camp, where they were staying the adjacent tents. Their parents had no objection to the marriage of Sanjay and Darun, both from the Scheduled Caste Mushahar community. Soon, the elders finalised a date for marriage. Three days ago, the marriage was solemnised without any fanfare. The camp management has alloted a separate tent for the couple. Sanjay, an illiterate petty worker who lost his house to the flood waters, said he had never expected to start his new life this way.

On Monday, Chief Minister Nitish Kumar, who was on an inspection tour of relief camps, learnt of the marriage and sent for the couple. The newly weds sought the CM's blessings amidst applause by other inmates. He directed his personal secretary to give the couple "all possible help". "Always remember that you met and got married in difficult times. Be there for each other in happiness and sorrow. Calamity has united you and hence, nothing should set you apart now," the CM told the couple.

Heading: Khanduri orders probe into death of 5 porters - Indian Express
Content:
The Supreme Court on Monday stayed a Madras High Court order which had said that condoms could not be marketed with explicit visuals either printed on the wrappers or in advertisements.

The Bench of Chief Justice K G Balakrishnan, Justices P Sathasivam and J M Panchal also stayed an order directing all condom manufacturers to seek permission for their promotional activities from the Advertising Standards Council of India (ASCI), a self-regulatory voluntary organisation of the advertising industry.

It also issued notices to the Centre, the Tamil Nadu government, ASCI, the Central Board of Film Certification and several condom manufacturers like TTK-LIG, Hindustan Latex Ltd (HLL), Pashupathi Seohung and JK Ansell.

Taking up the appeal filed by the state-owned HLL, the Bench even sought a response from C Ravikumar, the petitioner on whose PIL the High Court gave its order.

Heading: The Other Lama - Indian Express
Content: Uttarakhand CM B C Khanduri has ordered a probe into the death of five porters who were part of the two trekking contingents that had been trapped amidst the heights in Chamoli district over the last weekend. A team of Snow Commandoes of the Indo-Tibetan Border Police had successfully rescued 39 trekkers, including seven Austrians, who had been trapped on the Bhatwari-Kalindi Khal-Arbatal-Ghastoli-Mana route on Saturday. Those rescued also included noted historian from Uttarakhand Shekhar Pathak and renowned photographer Anup Sah. Khanduri has asked District Magistrate D S Gabaryal to get the incident investigated and ensure punishment for those guilty of laxity. He has ordered that trekking teams should be provided with all facilities by the state.

Heading: Deaths may fail to put brakes on Assam’s gravy trains - Indian Express
Content:
Eight years after Ogyen Trinley Dorje, the 17th Gyalwang Karmapa, made a sensational escape from China, this leader of the Kagyu school of Tibetan Buddhism is making his presence felt here.

The Karmapa is the third most respected leader after the Dalai Lama and the 'missing' Panchen Lama. For a long time after his escape he retained a low profile, living in the shadow of the Dalai Lama. Even today, he lives at the Gyuto Monastery in Sidhbari near Dharamsala, which belongs to the Dalai Lama and the Gelugpa school of Tibetan Buddhism. But with the Dalai Lama ageing and the need for a future leader for the Tibetan movement being felt, the Karmapa seems to be staking his claim.

This year, he visited the US for the first time. On September 9, he also undertook his maiden Dharma tour to Ladakh, Lahaul & Spiti and Kinnaur. On Sunday, he and 13 followers were airlifted from Lahaul after the region was rendered out-of-bounds following more than 48 hours of snowfall.

Helping Karmapa in his endeavour is Pema Tonyo Rinpoche, the 12th Tai Situ Rinpoche, who the Kagyu School deems to be the next Buddha and the man who recognised Ogyen Dorje as the 17th Karmapa.

At Sherab Ling monastery near Palampur, the seat of the Kagyu sect, there is frenetic activity these days. Usually, the Tai Situ preaches only twice a year to two batches of 300 disciples each. Each session lasts about a week. But the lectures this year have prolonged. They are being imparted to a congregation of 2,000 disciples comprising monks, children and foreigners.

A luxurious guesthouse is coming up in the monastery complex. With 350 rooms, this facility would significantly increase the existing capacity of providing lodging for disciples. The old guesthouse could accommodate only 20 people. Also being developed is an old age home. "The new guesthouse is so luxurious that we call it the Sherab Ling, Hilton," jokes one of the disciples. Sanam, one of the officials at the monastery, adds, "All these facilities will ensure that Sherab Ling gains the eminence of the famous Nalanda university of ancient India."

The Union Government doesn't give the Karmapa the permission to visit the Sherab Ling monastery. A new guesthouse is being constructed exclusively for him at the Gyuto Monastery itself. Tai Situ regularly visits Gyuto to give lessons to the Karmapa. After all, the Karmapa is still very young (he turned 23 this year) and it is felt that he still has to learn many things. As Tenam Lama, spokesperson of Tai Situ, says, "Tai Situ takes care of the Karmapa's education and the Karmapa himself is aware of his responsibilities as a leader of the Tibetan people. As regards the construction activity, these facilities are meant for the comfort of disciples whose numbers are gradually increasing."

However, in Dharamsala, Samdung Rinpoche, PM of the Tibetan government in exile and the man selected as the representative of the Tibetan movement by the Dalai Lama, says, "The Karmapa has lot of appeal and a large following among the Tibetans. But I think it would be inappropriate and bit too premature to suggest that he is emerging as the heir apparent to His Holiness the Dalai Lama."

Heading: Yo Ho Ho and a rummy battle - Indian Express
Content:
An organised crime that has operated in the shadows for a long while in Assam was brought to light last week when 15 people died while trying to pilfer refined petroleum products from a train in Karbi Anglong district.

According to the police, over 150 people had come to steal oil from a train travelling from the Numaligarh Refinery in Upper Assam to Mughalsarai in UP on Friday night. They struck when the train was stopped at the Rangapahar Siding station, about six km from Dimapur, an important commercial town on the Assam-Nagaland border.

The train was kept hostage from 11:55 pm to 1:10 am, as the miscreants who came with pumps, pipes and drums opened several of the oil tankers and removed a huge quantity of oil, until some of them collapsed due to suffocation caused by lack of oxygen. While the Karbi Anglong police (on the Assam side) picked up eight bodies from the spot, the Dimapur police (in Nagaland) is said to have found seven bodies.

"Such incidents of gangs forcibly stopping a train and looting petroleum products, mostly petrol and diesel, seem to be going on here for quite sometime. The Railways have complained of such thefts and pilferages on many occasions in security coordination meetings," said K K Sharma, SP, Karbi Anglong.

Two bodies recovered by the Assam Police were identified as NSCN (IM) cadres, and they said this confirmed the involvement of the rebel group in the pilferage. "We have earlier arrested several persons from the same area," Sharma confirmed.

On Saturday morning, the police seized 504 drums from the area, some filled with petroleum and others empty. And going by the capacity of each drum (200 litres), the miscreants would have robbed at least 100,000 litres of oil that night itself. Most of the oil is believed to reach Dimapur's clandestine petroleum market.

Local reports said the gang that had carried out the operation at Rangapahar Siding that night offered local labourers up to Rs 1,000 to pilfer the oil.

"We have been asking the Railways to ply oil-transporting trains through that area only during the daytime, but there has been hardly any response," complained Sharma. The Railways, however, put the onus on the police, saying it's a law and order problem.

"The Railways have been asking the police to provide adequate security in that area, but we have not got any support," retorted Sameer Goswami, Chief Public Relations Officer of the Northeast Frontier Railways in Guwahati. "If miscreants come in large numbers, hold our staff hostage, and remove oil from the trains, what else can we do but ask the police for security cover," Goswami said.

While 15 persons died on the spot and several others fell unconscious during the robbery, the Railways, surprisingly, moved the goods train at 1:20 pm from the spot on its onward journey. "The goods train was moved after some minor repairs and it has reached its destination," confirmed Goswami. The police admit that they have few clues to go on. "We have no scope to carry out detailed investigation because we have not inspected the train," rued Sharma.

The theft of crude oil from the oilfields in Upper Assam is yet another major organised crime in the region. "Organised gangs stole huge quantities of crude oil from oil collection stations in the Upper Assam districts till a couple of years ago, until we managed to arrest two top kingpins," said Bhaskar Jyoti Mahanta, Inspector-General of Police, Assam.

Mahanta said incidents of thefts had come down drastically after the arrest of Putul Gogoi and Kajal Khan. The latter is a former ULFA militant. These gangs are suspected to have had links with employees of oil companies. Mahanta said most of the crude oil used to find its way to tea gardens and brick kilns, where it was used as furnace oil.

Heading: Ahead of polls, Maya back to basics - Indian Express
Content:
Eighteen Indians have been held hostage at the Somalian port of Eyl after the Hong Kong-owned Stolt Valor, coming from the Suez Canal and bound for Mumbai, was hijacked by pirates in the Gulf of Aden on September 15. On Sunday, Greek freighter Captain Stephanos with 19 crew members on board was attacked by pirates off the Somalian coast — the 13th ship to fall into the hands of the Somalian pirates this year. The International Maritime Bureau reports 50 such attacks this year in or near the Gulf of Aden, considered one of the most dangerous stretches of waters in the world. Without an effective central administration since the 1991 civil war and plagued by factional fighting, Somalia located at the entrance of the Gulf of Aden continues to be a haven for pirates. Beyond the stereotypical notions of the bandana, the black patch, the skull-and-cross-bones flag, the peg leg, and the nagging parrot — nurtured by fiction and film — these fishermen are armed with automatic weapons and hand-held rocket launchers:

The strategy

According to a recent BBC report, off the Somalian coast, the hotspot of piracy attacks, only seven to 10 pirates, armed with heavy weapons and cruising in speed boats board the ship and make the initial attack. After the ships are captured, they are taken mostly to the port of Eyl. Once the vessel is seized, it has been reported, 50 pirates stay on board while 50 more wait on the shore to see that nothing goes amiss. At Eyl, the pirates treat their hostages well in expectation of a huge ransom amount. No hostages have been reported killed in Somali pirate hijackings. The crew of the hijacked ships is fed at special restaurants that have sprung up in the area. And though the country has not had a stable government in 17 years, plush houses and fancy cars dot the town. According to one estimate, money made by pirates from ransom payments was higher than the annual budget of Puntland last year. Lately, pirates have changed their tactics with heavily armed attackers operating simultaneously in the Gulf of Aden and on the eastern coast of Somalia, extending their range by operating from larger vessels. They use a mother ship as a mainstay of their attacks, from where they launch smaller boats to attack vessels.

The ransom amount

Gone are the days of Stevenson's Long John Silver, of pirates decamping with buried treasures or lugging treasure chests. Today when ships are attacked and captured, a tall ransom changes hands. On an average, today most captured ships fetch a ransom of anything between $300,000 and $1.5 million. If Danish-owned Svitzer Korsakov captured off Somalia's northern semi-autonomous Puntland region was freed after the payment of a ransom of $700,000, a Spanish fishing boat captured by Somali pirates from Spain's Basque region in April 2008 was released within a week's time after the Spanish government reportedly paid a ransom of $1.2 million. Somali pirates released a German operated ship in September 2008 after a ransom of $ 1.1 million was paid, while $1.5 million reportedly changed hands for the release of Japanese tanker MT Irene, captured on August 21, 2008. With shipping companies agreeing to pay huge ransoms, the frequency of attacks have gone up.

The law

Piracy is considered a breach of a conventional international norm that states must uphold, a crime against nations instead of any particular nation. Those guilty of the crime of piracy are considered by sovereign states to be enemies of humanity. In English law, piracy was considered petit treason, while during the reign of Henry VIII it was redefined as felony.

The complexity of the laws

Pirates attack ships mostly outside the territorial waters of a state, making it difficult for the sovereign states to prosecute them. Their prosecution on high seas contravenes the conventional freedom of the high seas. However, because of universal jurisdiction, action can be taken against pirates without objection from the flag state of the pirate vessel.

UN and piracy

The UNCLOS (The United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea) came into existence as a result of the third United Nations Conference on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS III), which began in 1973 and concluded in 1982. The convention, nevertheless, came into force only in 1994, a year after the 60th state Guyana ratified it. It defines the rights and responsibilities of nations in their use of the world's oceans, establishing guidelines for businesses, environment, and management of marine natural resources. The convention also assumed significance as it set limits of various areas and classified areas of jurisdiction. This includes internal waters (the coastal state reserves exclusive rights over them; no right of passage for foreign vessels); territorial waters (extends up to 12 nautical lines from the baseline; foreign vessels permitted right of peaceful passage); contiguous zone (beyond the initial 12 nautical miles, another 12 nautical miles where the respective coastal states can continue to enforce laws regarding activities such as smuggling or illegal migration); exclusive economic zones (extends upto 200 nautical miles from the baselins, with the coastal state given exclusive rights over the use of natural resources); and continental shelf (natural prolongation of the land territory to the continental margin's outer edge, or 200 nautical miles from the coastal state's baseline, whichever is greater).

In its efforts to combat escalating piracy off the coasts of Somalia, the UN Security Council in June 2008 unanimously passed Resolution 1816 which authorised foreign warships to enter Somalia's territorial waters with the Government's consent. But the resolution is yet to be implemented. A multinational taskforce has also been operational in Djibouti in recent months to patrol parts of the Gulf of Aden and the Red Sea, where a pirate mothership is believed to be functional.

The role of IMB

The International Maritime Bureau (IMB) assists in the suppression of piracy and armed robbery against ships around the world. In view of escalating piracy, the IMB, in 1992, established a Piracy Reporting Centre in Kuala Lumpur the job of which was to raise awareness of piracy hotspots, detail attacks and their consequences, investigate incidents of piracy and armed robbery at sea and in port.

Piracy hotspots

As per High Risk Areas 2008, as reported by the International Maritime Bureau, these are Nigeria, Indonesia, Tanzania, India, Bangladesh

Heading: BSY in damage-control mode - Indian Express
Content:
Expanding the BSP's appeal to 'Sarvajan Samaj' may have won her one election, but with the Lok Sabha polls round the corner, party chief Mayawati is reinforcing her core base of Bahujan Samaj. After a carefully picked up Cabinet and a balanced secretariat to broadbase her appeal, the BSP supremo is now concentrating on keeping her original vote bank intact and wooing the Muslim community by standing firmly against the nuclear deal.

Whether it's opening the state's coffers for scholarship for backward community students or starting Gautam Buddha University in Noida that promises SC students stints with foreign universities, with the Government bearing the cost, Mayawati is fulfilling the Bahujan agenda of her party. In fact, each decision of her government taken off late seems to be aimed at sending a positive message to the original vote bank of the party.

A case in point is the withdrawal of UPCOCA (UP Control of Organised Crime Act) Bill 2007, the terror law that had attracted strong objections from the Muslim community.

Early this month, Mayawati brought about a sudden, but major, change in the Chief Minister's Secretariat. About a dozen officers were either brought in or shunted out. What amazed everyone was the posting of senior bureaucrats J N Chamber (a Schedule Caste IAS officer) and Anis Ansari (a Muslim IAS officer) as Principal Secretary to the CM and Agriculture Production Commissioner (APC), respectively.

Chamber had been shown the door by Mayawati when his daughter, Disha, was handpicked by Rahul Gandhi to play an active role in the Uttar Pradesh Congress Committee. Disha led a demonstration against the state Government and thereby caused much embarrassment for Principal Secretary (Home) J N Chamber. It was only after Disha surrendered her primary membership of the Congress that Mayawati rewarded him by bringing him to the CMO.
