Acclaimed as India's first and biggest mountain bike race, the Mountain Biking Himachal 2008 Championship will have over top 80 international and Indian riders taking centrestage. Participants from across the globe - South Africa, Australia, USA, UK, Germany, Dubai, and Pakistan, apart from India, will compete in this year's event for total prize money of Rs 6 lakhs.

"Events such as these help put Himachal on the world tourism map. The event has grown in stature and we are confident of assured success in the years to come," said Manisa Nanda, Himachal Pradesh tourism secretary here.

Heading: 50% posts in health centres vacant: ASSOCHAM survey - Indian Express
Content:
The Jama Masjid Precinct Plan, which aims to redevelop and beautify the area around the Jama Masjid, has missed its deadline, and still remains on paper. The project was to be completed by May this year, but till date the concerned files have just been changing hands between the MCD and the Delhi Urban Art Commission (DUAC). In the last couple of years, the MCD has submitted its plan report to the DUAC four times. The DUAC has sent back the file every time with its observations and suggestions for amendment. The project at present still lies in the initial planning stages.

In the last meeting of the DUAC on August 19, it had observed that the Jama Masjid is not a heritage monument and development work within 100 metres of the monument is not prohibited, or requires permission from the ASI. However, in September, it directed the MCD to take ASI's approval, since the Sunehri Masjid and the Red Fort lie within 300 metres and hence prior approval from the ASI is required. It also observed that as the monument falls in the vicinity of World Heritage Sites, any development project would also have to be scrutinised by international conservation agencies.

The DUAC had also observed that the ASI was preparing a Comprehensive Conservation Master Plan for the Red Fort as per Supreme Court orders. The Jama Masjid Precinct Plan would have to take cognizance of this fact that any proposal in the vicinity of a World Heritage Site should be in consonance with that plan.

The meeting of DUAC took place more than a month ago. Till date, however, the MCD says that it has not received any official correspondence from the DUAC allowing it to proceed with the project. "We have heard about the DUAC observations from the DUAC website and the press. Nothing has been confirmed to us officially," said the MCD project coordinator Vijay Singh.

Singh informed that the MCD would write to the DUAC soon seeking an official confirmation on whatever has been reported so far.

MCD sources alleged that each time the MCD has submitted a report the DUAC has been putting forth new observations.

"The project was to start some time last year, but till now we have not received a clearance from the DUAC. We have asked the DUAC to give us specifications, but nothing concrete has happened," added Singh.

However, the DUAC denies any delay on its end. "We can only give observations. We are no experts in giving specifications as to what needs to be done. That is for the agency to decide," said DUAC chairperson KT Ravindran.

Ravindran also said the DUAC has never caused the delay of any government project, specially development projects. "Besides the Jama Masjid project, there are several other projects for Commonwealth Games that have come to us for approval. We make sure that each project is studied and submitted within a period of three months. There has been no delay from our side," he added.

Features of the Jama Masjid Precinct Plan

* Jama Masjid Precinct covers an area of 46 acre

* The project is to restore the area around the mosque

* The height of the area around the mosque is to be raised to the level of the mosque and created into a Mughal Garden

* Two-tier underground parking be created on an area of 19,100 square metres within the restored area

* The existing Meena Bazar to go under the restored area with 650 air-conditioned shops of uniform size.

* Art gallery, heritage museum, heritage library, recreation centre and a tourist information centre to be made according to the new plan.

* Recreation of exteriors of mosques and darghas in the precinct as per Mughal architecture

* Community hall and indoor sports complex spread over 7,800 square metres for residents around the mosque

* New road and traffic management plan for the area to make approach to the precinct easy.

Heading: CEO cremated, family in a daze - Indian Express
Content:
The dispute between the management and labourers, which left Graziano Transmissioni (India) CEO L K Choudhury dead on Monday, began in the last week of November 2007, company officials said.

A company statement issued today stated that it was enforcing a partial lockout against the striking workers.

The police claimed a "small dispute" between the management and one of the employee representatives snowballed into a major crisis as workers thought the employee was being attacked.

Company officials said that some 350 disgruntled employees staged the first sit-in strike last November. They were protesting dismissal of some fellow labourers.

That was the first time the factory in Greater Noida was locked out, "partially, for a few days," Graziano India's personnel manager L K Gupta said. "But we struck a settlement with them (labourers) within three days."

This January, Gupta said, the workers joined All India Trade Union Congress (AITUC) and sent a list of demands, Gupta said: "The union demanded a salary hike of Rs 7,000 per month. This meant a huge financial burden on the company."

Gupta said the management and the workers finally settled on a monthly hike of Rs 3,000 on a three-year contract, "with conditions attached." He said, "We asked them that they would not create any nuisance and would abide by the company's law and decision." But the union, Gupta said, later refused to abide by the agreement.

Meanwhile, the labourers disputed company officials' claim that Monday's attack was a planned one. "No one (in the management, or among officials) was ready to hear our case, not even the Labour Commission," Rajendra Singh, one of the labourers who were injured in yesterday's clash, said.

According to Singh, yesterday (September 22) was the last day of submitting the request letter to reinstate dismissed workers. "We went inside but the security guards misbehaved with us," he said.

This acted as the trigger, police officials said, for other workers to barge in.

Deputy Labour Commissioner B K Singh said the company recruited around 400 contract employees in January, and the workers soon started demanding permanent status. "In a meeting on September 16 the management agreed to reinstate all dismissed employees, barring 15 who were terminated for grave indiscipline and misconduct," he said.

But the employees, B K Singh said, kept up their demand: reinstatement of all employees. At this point the company increased salary by Rs 2,000, with incentive of another Rs 1,000 per month, Singh said.

137 workers held for CEO's death

A Noida court sent 63 employees to Dasna Jail on charges of murdering L K Choudhary. Another 74 have been sent to prison on charges of rioting, assault and unlawful assembly. "Initially we filed FIR against 19 workers and have sent 137 dismissed employees to the court. They have been sent to Dasna Jail on 14 days of judicial remand," SP (Rural) Babu Ram, transferred later in the day, said.

SP (Rural) moved out

SP (Rural) Babu Ram was transferred to Bulandshehr. SSP R K Chaturvedi said Monday's incident was one of the reasons that led to the transfer. Bulandshehr's Superintendent of Police Surendra Verma would take over from Ram, it was announced. — ENS

Heading: Rampaging mob came with a clear plan to kill: eyewitnesses - Indian Express
Content:
Family, friends and colleagues of Lalit Kishore Chaudhary — who was murdered on Monday by a group of enraged former workers of the Italian auto parts company he was heading in India — was cremated on Tuesday at the Nigambodh Ghat in Delhi.

With Chaudhary's life cut short at the hands of the former workers of the company that he was heading, his family is still in a state of shock. He is survived by wife Ratna and 16-year-old son Keshav.

According to Chaudhary's relatives, his wife has just gone silent.

"We still don't understand what has happened and how. What was the need for such barbarism? Ratna has not reacted to the news. Keshav had just been sitting next to his father's body since morning and was initially not letting anyone take it away," said Jaya, Chaudhary's cousin.

Keshav is a Class XI student of Modern School, Barakhamba Road.

Senior Personnel Executive of Graziano Transmissioni India Pvt Ltd, Avneesh Kumar, could not hold back his tears as he remembered his CEO and recounted the gruesome incident.

"He was not only a good manager, but a great boss as well. When he was attacked, I was away and could not save him," he said.

Mahasingh Yadav, working with the engineering department, who joined the company only a month after Chaudhary, recounted that the growth made by the Italian company, which had more than doubled in the past decade, owed largely to the hard work of Chaudhary.

"He started the company in 1998. The company has grown so fast only due to Chaudhary's leadership. He was a father figure for us all. We had stayed together for nine months when we went to Italy for a training programme," said Singh.

Chaudhary's relatives said they were aware that some problems were going on relating to the factory and the workers, but no one had any idea things could take such a violent and terrible turn.

"He was young and had a long way to go. No one is able to talk about the incident at present," said Sunil Chaudhary, another cousin brother of the deceased.

When Newsline visited Chaudhary's A-103 residence in Noida, the family was not available for comment as relatives said that no one was in a position to talk to the media.

Heading: No interim relief for Nanda, Bhasin - Indian Express
Content:
Lalit Kishore Chaudhary, IIT Kanpur alumnus and Graziano CEO, was killed on Monday after being attacked by a group of expelled workers on the company premises in Greater Noida. As the protesters took law in their own hands and attacked the company premises, they also attacked all the other employees of the company who were working in the factory at the time.

According to sources, 55 employees were injured and there were around 80 employees in the factory. Twenty-four employees were later admitted to Kailash Hospital in Greater Noida with skull injuries and bone fractures.

While six employees, including S Sarkar, Vice-President (Operations) of the company and second in command after Chaudhary, are admitted in the Intensive Care Unit, the condition of two of them is said to be critical. Sarkar was hit in the head with an iron object and has 25 stitches.

Sudhir Kumar, the guard on duty at the main entrance at the time of the incident, said: "They were over 200 people who wanted to get into the company premises. I stopped them because we did not have permission to allow them inside. Then somebody hit me on the head with a rod from behind, after which some six to seven people started beating me up and threw me in a ditch outside the company gate and I fainted after that." According to sources, after the workers allegedly went on a rampage in the company, Chaudhary had come down from his office, but was attacked by the mob.

Ashwani Kumar, the company driver, who came to rescue Chaudhary, was also beaten up mercilessly. He now lies in a critically injured state at Kailash Hospital. While Chaudhary lost his life in this battle between the management and workers, Kumar is still unconscious. His skull is injured and his both arms broken.

"They had all come well-planned with the intention to kill everyone inside the office. They just wanted to murder. I was hit with a very hard object on the back, head and legs. But I managed to escape and was later brought to the hospital," said Saroj Kumar (38), who works with the company's Quality Assurance department.

Yashpal Sharma (45), working with the logistics department, could not talk much as his face was swollen after being hit on the eyes and nose. His arm was also broken in the rampage.

KK Sharma, administrator of Kailash Hospital, said that a majority of workers have been discharged. "Only seven injured now remain with us, two of them critical," Sharma added.

Heading: ‘Terrorists’ were regular college boys, fun-loving and good in studies - Indian Express
Content:
The Delhi High Court on Tuesday issued a notice to the police on an appeal filed by Sanjeev Nanda, the grandson of former naval chief S M Nanda, sentenced to five years' imprisonment for ramming his BMW car into six persons in 1999. Justice Kailash Gambhir passed the order on the first day of hearing of Nanda's appeal, directing the Delhi Police to respond by October 3.

In his appeal, Nanda contended that the court had found him guilty despite not having any incriminating evidence against him. Justice Gambhir refused to grant any interim relief to Nanda, noting that the accident was indeed a "serious" offence.

Senior Advocate Mukul Rohatgi, appearing for Nanda, contended that the trial court had wrongly convicted him due to publicity in the media and he should not be given more than two years of imprisonment.

"The court relied on the Alistair Pereira case where the accused was given three years of imprisonment for mowing down people sleeping on the pavement. In this case the accident happened because of the victim's fault as they were standing in the middle of the road in the early hours," Rohatgi said. "Nanda's offence stands on a lower footing as compared to Pereira and he should not be given more than two years of imprisonment," he submitted. To this, the court asked the counsel, "Do you want to say that the car accident is not a serious offence? People standing on the road were run over by the car".

The Delhi High Court on Tuesday refused to give any interim protection against arrest to Utsav Bhasin, a Haryana industrialist's teenaged son, accused of killing one person with his BMW car in South Delhi. "I am not giving any protection. I will hear the case (Bhasin's anticipatory bail plea) tomorrow," Justice Veena Birbal said while rejecting his plea to restrain the police from arresting him till tomorrow. Bhasin had approached the High Court for anticipatory bail in the case after the city police imposed additional charge against him under a harsher penal provision under IPC section 304 (culpable homicide not amounting to murder). He was earlier denied anticipatory bail by a trial court on September 18. — ENS

Heading: HC quashes traders’ petition challenging eviction - Indian Express
Content:
'Even as the Delhi Police describes Atif, Md. Shakeel and Zia-ur-Rehman as the men behind the Delhi blasts, students and teachers at Jamia Millia Islamia, where the three were studying, described them as serious students who were "normal" in every aspect.

Atif, who was killed in the encounter, was doing his MA in Human Rights, Shakeel was doing his MA in Economics and Zia-ur-Rehman was a final year student of BA.

Describing Shakeel, his old time friend says that he was a fun-loving boy who would speak nicely to all his friends. "He was an outgoing student, very simple and sober. I cannot imagine that the police have arrested him as a terrorist. Nothing about him ever suggested that he can be anything else but a normal student."

Shakeel had done his schooling and graduation from JMI and was enrolled in MA. The head of the department, MS Bhat, refused to comment on Shakeel. Friends said he was a good student. "Shakeel would not have got admission in Jamia if he was not a good student. But, during graduation, Shakeel had to repeat his papers in second year due to attendance problems," said a friend.

Teachers at the Human Rights department say Atif had done his schooling and graduation from Uttar Pradesh before he came to Delhi. "He was a serious-looking bearded boy and had been coming for classes for the past two months ever since the university opened for the new session," said a teacher on condition of annonimity. According to him, Atif never gave any signs that he could be involved in any other activities but the curriculum of the college.

Teachers of Zia-ur-Rehman, however, refused to comment. Rehman was doing his graduation from the Political Science department.

Heading: Bikes to rev up firemen’s response time - Indian Express
Content:
According to the 37-year-old Public Premises Act — a Parliamentary law to authorise "speedy eviction" of illegal occupants — the New Delhi Municipal Council (NDMC) fails to exist. Fourteen years after the NDMC opened shop, the statute is yet to take note of it as a municipal body — a fact the Delhi High Court considers as "casus omissus" (case of omission) by the Parliament.

The matter was brought to the notice of Justice Vipin Sanghi by 16 shopkeepers facing eviction from their Gole Market premises on the orders of the estate officer of the Municipal Council. The estate officer, had, late last year cancelled their shop allotments and issued a notice for their eviction under the Public Premises Act.

Traders challenged the eviction order in High Court with the argument that the Public Premises Act does not apply to NDMC areas as the statute fails to even acknowledge the very existence of the municipal body.

A reading of Section 2 of the Act shows that the statute is only applicable to "public premises" in areas under the "Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD) or any municipal committee or notified area committee".

"The petitioners (traders) have a very interesting argument that the Public Premises Act does not apply to NDMC premises," said Justice Sanghi, "and so the estate officer has no jurisdiction to proceed to either evict or levy damages on them under the Act".

The court noted that the Parliament had continued to chug along with the predecessor body of the Municipal Council — the New Delhi Municipal Committee — which had ceased to exist when the former was christened on May 25, 1994.

The Committee had been administering New Delhi area as per a law that dates back to 1911, borrowed from Punjab till the Parliament decided to "harmonise all laws governing municipalities" with a Constitutional Amendment on June 1, 1993.

"The Parliament considered it necessary to form the Municipal Council for New Delhi due to increase in population and more area falling in its jurisdiction," explained the court. But "though the Committee ceased to exist," the Bench added, "the Parliament continues to use the expression Municipal Committee and not Municipal Council."

However, the Bench dismissed the petition of the shopkeepers by ruling that the Municipal Council, as the successor of the Committee, would automatically inherit all the powers and properties earlier possessed by the former.

"The New Delhi Municipal Council has been constituted to carry out local self-governance in the area known as New Delhi. It is therefore a municipality," said the court, directing the estate officer to "expeditiously conclude" the eviction process.

Heading: 30-year-old man killed by friend - Indian Express
Content:
The Delhi Fire Service is to launch a special wing, comprising motorcycle-borne firemen, to tackle fires in congested areas of the city, particularly in the Walled City.

Chief Fire Officer R C Sharma said the service would initially comprise ten motorcycle-borne personnel equipped with special fire fighting equipment. Each of the motorcycles will carry nine litres of water, along with gas cylinders that will be used to produce mist, or a mixture of pressurised air and water, to extinguish fires.

Sharma said the fire service came up with the idea of using motorcycles to reach crowded areas of the city, since fire tenders are often unable to enter and negotiate the narrow by-lanes of the Walled City and other congested parts of the city like Sadar Bazaar.

"Often small fires spread to become major ones. The motorcycles are intended to help firemen act speedily to control small fires in their initial phase," he said.

This method is already in use in the US and the UK, from where it is being imported. Around ten such bikes are to be introduced before March 2009, each costing approximately Rs 3.5 lakh, with the possibility of more being introduced if successful.

These plans are also directed towards the Commonwealth Games, with fire engines being deployed in all major event and practice venues. Two more fire stations are also being added at the Commonwealth Games Village and at Mayur Vihar, to allow faster response to any potential fire mishaps.

These measures follow several other steps aimed at expanding and streamlining the Delhi Fire Service. These include the expansion in numbers of fire stations in Delhi, from the current 49 to 70 by 2010. This year, fire stations have been opened at Jwala Heri, Tikri Kalan, Tahirpur, Sarita Vihar, Paschim Vihar and in Sectors 5 and 15 in Rohini. The increase in numbers is slated to reduce the response time of the fire service in various parts of Delhi.

In addition, the computerisation of the control and command communications systems is also underway, which will link various fire stations across the city.

To complement the increase in the number of fire stations, other measures include an increase in the personnel recruited for the Delhi Fire Service from its current number of 2,000-odd service persons. Around 430 seats have been filled so far, with 800 more in the pipeline.

The newly recruited fire operators will be trained at the Training Centre of the Delhi Fire Service in Rohini.

Heading: Lack of FIR cannot bar claim in mishaps: court - Indian Express
Content: A thirty-year-old man was shot dead by his friend in Arjun Nagar area here on Monday night. According to the police, the incident occurred around 10.30 pm when Mahesh, the deceased, had gone to meet a few friends in the area. They had been playing a game of cards when he had a tiff with one of his friends Anil over some issue. Anil allegedly took out a pistol and shot Mahesh four times. Those present at the time have been identified as Ashok, Dhiraj, Sudhir, Shyam and Vijay. Police said all of them had gathered at Sudhir's place for the game when the incident occurred. One of them then called the police, informing about the incident. By the time a police team reached the spot, all of them had fled and Mahesh's body was found lying in a pool of blood, police said. A resident of Bawani Enclave area, Mahesh used to work in a private firm here. He is survived by his wife and two children. A case has been registered against Anil in the city police station under Section 302 of the IPC, and investigations are on. Efforts are also on to nab all the six persons present at the spot at the time of the incident, said Inspector Divinder Singh.

Heading: Animated Response - Indian Express
Content:
An insurance company cannot evade liability to compensate victims of a road accident just because an FIR was not lodged, the Motor Accident Claim Tribunal (MACT) has held. The tribunal awarded a compensation of Rs 9.7 lakh to a man who lost his wife in an accident in 2005.

The tribunal's observation came while deciding the claim petitions of Durgesh Kumar Gupta and his two children, who were injured in an accident on May 29, 2005 while returning to the Capital from Badrinath (Uttarakhand).

Gupta's wife Shankuntala Devi died after the vehicle's driver lost control.

Heading: Moving Pictures - Indian Express
Content:
While a martial arts-loving giant panda from Kung Fu Panda and a dreamer zebra from Madagascar attracted attention at the recent SIGGRAPH Festival in Los Angeles with their star status, Delhi-based filmmaker Charuvi Agrawal cut through the fantasy and introduced demonic television in her 150-second film 10th Avatar. Wings attached to its rectangular body and monstrous eyes popping from the monitor, the idiot box got an animated avatar as the marijuana of the visual world. "This isn't far-fetched. Everyone is hooked to the TV," says Agrawal, 25, about her 3-D animation film.

Nominated in the short film category in several international competitions, including the Santa Fe Film Festival in New Mexico and the South Asian International Film Festival in New York, the film had its first screening in Delhi at the Films Division Auditorium on Saturday. Kamal Haasan would have been amused at this Dasavathaaram-meets-Orwell short, which begins with a group of devotees offering prayers to Krishna and then segues into an illusionary world where the deity descends on the earth as the tenth avatar in the form of a television set. And the new incarnation addresses Its worshippers through mythological serials.

Agrawal, who showed the movie only to select invitees and not a barrage of popcorn-clutching children, does not think animation films are kiddie stuff. "The notion that animation is meant for children is rampant in India. It'll take time for people to acknowledge that filmmakers are depicting mature issues through the medium," she says. Little wonder that Agrawal, who graduated from the Delhi College of Art and did master's in computer animation from Sheridan College, Canada, projected on the screen three films made over the past two years. While 10th Avatar harped on the overarching importance of television, Dream Magic, a four-minute film commissioned by the Canada National Film Board, had animation based on the etchings of documentary filmmaker Alanis Obomsawin, while Dundas n Bathrust depicted the diversity of Toronto in a minute. "Each project was different in theme and treatment," says Agrawal, who often refers to Indian folklore for inspiration. If the storyboard of 10th Avatar has reflections of Mughal miniature paintings, she is planning a mythological narrative in her next.

With animation on the forefront, the fine arts may have taken a backseat but Agrawal hopes to produce another set of miniature 3-D clay caricatures akin to the display at her solo exhibition at the India Habitat Centre two years ago. They had tongue-in-cheek taglines like "Silence — antarman ki aawaz" for Sonia Gandhi and "I am a heavyweight. Don't undermine me" for

J. Jayalalithaa's caricature, but as she goes back to the storyboard, Agrawal assures that the forthcoming exhibition, which will take a jab at film stars, will be better. An animated response is, of course, welcome.

Heading: Clown Act - Indian Express
Content:
What's it like being gay in India? To which artist-photographer Sunil Gupta generally has one answer: "I don't know." Now, with a book of 100 photographs, Gupta hazards a guess, not just about gay life in India but also in Canada, the US and the UK. Called Wish You Were Here: Memories of a Gay Life, the book, to be released on Friday, documents the development of the queer movement in several countries through a personal narrative that starts 40 years ago and ends with Delhi's first Queer Pride a few months ago.

"My family migrated to Canada in the 1970s when I was 15. Later, as I moved from one country to another to pursue the arts, I got a ringside view of the gay movement finally coming into its own," says Gupta, who came out early. Published by Yoda Press and priced at Rs 895, the book follows Gupta's pictorial autobiography Wish You Were Here, published in 2003.

There is a black-and-white shot of a young man at Christopher Street, the scene of the Stonewall riots in 1969. "I didn't visit Christopher Street till a couple of years later, but the historic impact hit you instantly. There was a flourishing gay subculture. Of course, this was before AIDS broke out," says Gupta, who was diagnosed with HIV in 1995. There are several colourful shots of gay beaches, pubs and discos. "The biggest gay disco in the world was Heaven, in London. There would be 2,000 guys any evening and the atmosphere was quite something," he says.

The mood changes from uninhibited bonhomie to a guarded celebration of LGBT rights during the gay parade, called Queer Pride, in Delhi. "When I left India, there was no talk of homosexuality. When I returned to live here in 2004, a movement had begun. However, at the Pride, I noticed that many people had covered their faces with masks," he says. Things aren't always fine for people who choose to come out, he insists. Midway through the book, there is a picture of the Memorial for Matthew Shephard, the gay American student who was fatally attacked in Laramie, Wyoming, as a chilling reminder to the threats faced by Gupta's "kind of people".

The book unfolds through faces — there is Saleem Kidwai, a leading queer rights activist, Sylvie, a celebrity hairstylist who went for a sex change and became a woman, as well as Gupta's friends and family.

Through the three months that Gupta took to sift through photographs, there was one strong thread of caution — "I have left out all the pictures of people who haven't come put openly," he says. When they are ready to walk out of the closet without fear, India would have taken a huge leap. And then, maybe, Gupta will publish another book.

Heading: Bride’s Mate - Indian Express
Content:
I am what I am. The logo hammered in all that Manish Arora stood for — insouciance, attitude and loads of talent — when the maverick designer collaborated with Reebok for his Fish Fry range of shoes two years ago. It's been a while since Arora took the fashion world by storm, but the adulation seems nowhere close to reaching a lull.

Of course, Arora has been meticulous in designing his triumphs. From his incorrigible colour palette to his fascination with all that is kitschy, there's never a dull moment when his collections take the ramp. This time Paris Fashion Week will see Arora take up circus, something he claims has been a long-time favourite, and whips it in another intriguing collection. "This is something I have wanted to do for a long time," he claims, on the eve of his departure to Paris, where he will showcase his Spring-Summer 2009 collection on September 30.

The collection uses hand-sewn appliqué, digitally printed sequins as well as traditional Indian gota embroidery. It also has Swarovski crystals, leather sequins and ostrich feathers as embellishments. "The look is kept very international," says the designer who has had two successful outings in the fashion capital and has a firm finger on the pulse of his international clients.

Arora will interpret scenes from the circus in his signature style in a collection that includes short dresses, mini skirts, trousers, voluminous jackets, ruffled skirts and dresses as well as pieces largely inspired from circus costumes. There are clown pants, bra tops, bat-wing sleeves, multiple bows and jumpsuits. "It is very much me," he shrugs. Post Paris, Arora has more up his sleeve. He is the grand finale designer for the Wills Lifestyle India Fashion Week next month, where he will showcase the same Manish Arora Circus collection. If that is not enough, then the designer is also headed for Paris again, this time for the prestigious Tranoi Fair in October.

Heading: Day after CEO’s death, company is firm: it’s ‘partial lockout’ - Indian Express
Content:
When Divya Gurwaara decided to launch Bridal Asia, it sparked off the trend of wedding exhibitions in town. What started out with just a handful of designers has now expanded into a full-fledged exhibition encompassing not just the trousseau but also the entire bridal brouhaha — wedding planners, honeymoon organisers, make-up artists, chocolate makers, the works. This year, Bridal Asia celebrates a decade and has an impressive line-up of designers. Between October 7 and 9, designers like Tarun

Tahiliani, Sabyasachi Mukherjee, Ritu Beri, Gaurav Gupta, Vineet Behl and Anand Kabra (see picture for his creation) will rub shoulders with their counterparts from Pakistan and Bangladesh at The Ashok Hotel.

Heading: Atif’s 17-year-old cousin picked up, released later - Indian Express
Content:
The dispute between the management and labourers, which left Graziano Transmissioni (India) CEO L K Choudhury dead on Monday, began in the last week of November 2007, company officials said.

A company statement issued today stated that it was enforcing a partial lockout against the striking workers.

The police claimed a "small dispute" between the management and one of the employee representatives snowballed into a major crisis as workers thought the employee was being attacked.

Company officials said that some 350 disgruntled employees staged the first sit-in strike last November. They were protesting dismissal of some fellow labourers.

That was the first time the factory in Greater Noida was locked out, "partially, for a few days," Graziano India's personnel manager L K Gupta said. "But we struck a settlement with them (labourers) within three days."

This January, Gupta said, the workers joined All India Trade Union Congress (AITUC) and sent a list of demands, Gupta said: "The union demanded a salary hike of Rs 7,000 per month. This meant a huge financial burden on the company."

Gupta said the management and the workers finally settled on a monthly hike of Rs 3,000 on a three-year contract, "with conditions attached." He said, "We asked them that they would not create any nuisance and would abide by the company's law and decision." But the union, Gupta said, later refused to abide by the agreement.

Meanwhile, the labourers disputed company officials' claim that Monday's attack was a planned one. "No one (in the management, or among officials) was ready to hear our case, not even the Labour Commission," Rajendra Singh, one of the labourers who were injured in yesterday's clash, said.

According to Singh, yesterday (September 22) was the last day of submitting the request letter to reinstate dismissed workers. "We went inside but the security guards misbehaved with us," he said.

This acted as the trigger, police officials said, for other workers to barge in.

Deputy Labour Commissioner B K Singh said the company recruited around 400 contract employees in January, and the workers soon started demanding permanent status. "In a meeting on September 16 the management agreed to reinstate all dismissed employees, barring 15 who were terminated for grave indiscipline and misconduct," he said.

But the employees, B K Singh said, kept up their demand: reinstatement of all employees. At this point the company increased salary by Rs 2,000, with incentive of another Rs 1,000 per month, Singh said.

137 workers held for company CEO's death

A Noida court today sent 63 employees to Dasna Jail on charges of murdering L K Choudhary. Another 74 have been sent to prison on charges of rioting, assault and unlawful assembly. "Initially we filed FIR against 19 workers and have sent 137 dismissed employees to the court. They have been sent to Dasna Jail on 14 days of judicial remand," SP (Rural) Babu Ram, transferred later in the day, said.

SP (Rural) moved out

A day after the fatal fracas at Graziano Transmissioni, SP (Rural) Babu Ram was today transferred to Bulandshehr. SSP R K Chaturvedi said Monday's incident was one of the reasons that led to the transfer. Bulandshehr's Superintendent of Police Surendra Verma would take over from Ram, it was announced.

Heading: Kashmiri students detained in Delhi while returning from Dhaka - Indian Express
Content:
A seventeen-year-old cousin of Atif — the suspected brain behind the Delhi blasts — was picked up by the Special Cell on Tuesday evening for questioning but later released.

Officers arrived at the family's home in Abul Fazl Enclave around 4.30 pm on Tuesday in search of the elder brother Talim Akhtar, family members said. Their demeanour was rough, the family said, adding that officers took away young Saqib when told that Talim was not at home. When Talim returned to find his brother in custody, he rushed to the police cell where he too was interrogated for a while.

An officer of the Special Cell later said: "Some of Saqib's remarks after the blasts had aroused suspicion. we wanted to know what he had meant. We found after the interrogation that his comments were not in this context."

The family said Saqib had just finished high school while Talim, 27, worked for a courier company.

The boys' mother told Newsline: "Atif is a closed chapter for us. We don't know what he did. But why should the police behave like this?" The family has also lodged an FIR at the Okhla Police Station complaining about the behaviour — detailing that officers had even threatened to break open the door. A close relative said Atif's elder brother also lives with his cousins in the house in Abul Fazal Enclave.

Meanwhile, news of the detentions spread quickly in this Jamia Nagar locality, keeping young men indoors, even after Iftar had been broken.

A resident of the area, 29-year-old Atif Rehman said: "The image of the terrorist has changed today. He is no longer a bearded fundamentalist, but a young, educated boy. But can the police pick up anybody?"

Heading: Jamia to discuss helping arrested duo; V-C says ‘hope they are not guilty’ - Indian Express
Content:
Three Kashmiri students — picked up from the Delhi airport on Monday for a session with the Delhi Police — were finally put on a plane to Srinagar a day later after the Jammu Kashmir Police did a quick background check on the boys and told their colleagues here that these youths were 'not involved'.

The three, Naveed Farooq, Mohammad Zainulabidin and Adnan Firdous Raina, study medicine in Bangladesh and were to take a Jet Lite flight to Srinagar on Monday.

Farooq and Zainulabidin had taken the road to Kolkata from Bangladesh before they flew to Delhi. Their friend Adnan landed in Delhi directly from Dhaka and all three were to leave for Srinagar together.

However, when they were about to board the flight, the airlines staff 'reported' these boys to the Central Industrial Security Force (CISF). A Delhi Police official said: "They CISF checked their passports and came across the visas to Bangladesh. Without checking further, they called us in."

The students were then taken to the Palam Police Station for a long interview — at least five hours. The Special Cell was also informed about the detention.

Meanwhile, the superintendent of the J-K Police's CID (Criminal Investigation Department) wing in Delhi got wind of the incident and shot a report to the headquarters in Kashmir.

The CID did a quick check on their families and found — Farooq's father Mohammad Amin Narchu is a deputy general manager with the Jammu and Kashmir Bank in Srinagar; Adnan is son of Srinagar's tehsildar Firdous Sultan Raina and Zainulabidin's father Mohammad Ayub Dar is also a bank manager in Anantnag.

Kashmiri officers then sent a report to the Delhi Police stating these boys were 'not involved' in anything with a request that they be released immediately. The report also gave details of where these boys lived in Kashmir — Farooq in the Janglat Gali neighbourhood in south Kashmir's Anantnag district, Adnan in Usmanabad Colony in the frontier district of Kupwara and Zainulabidin in Qazipora, Anantnag.

The three students were finally let off, but a long time after their flight had already left for home on Monday afternoon.

Heading: Terror’s code lingo: ‘Book’ is bomb, ‘library’ blast sites - Indian Express
Content:
Jamia Millia Islamia would hold emergency meeting of both academic and executive councils on Thursday to zero in on ways to help the two students arrested in connection with September 13 serial blasts in the city.

Vice-Chancellor Mushirul Hasan had declared on Monday that the university would provide legal help to Mohammed Shakeel and Zia-ur-Rehman.

The academic council would meet at 10 am, followed by the executive council meeting at 3 pm, officials today said.

"We are scrutinising records of the accused and it will be submitted to the academic council for assessment on Thursday," a university official (name withheld on request) said. "The council would forward the report to the disciplinary committee for further probe."

Meanwhile, Prof Hasan, now in Kolkata, is scheduled to address the varsity students on Wednesday afternoon for a "free and frank exchange of opinion" between the student community and the vice-chancellor, in his capacity as a teacher and head of the institution. Hasan is also slated to lead a peace march in the campus the following day at 11 am, Thursday. Faculty members, students and administrative staff are expected to take part in the procession.

Meanwhile, in Kolkata to attend a convocation function at Calcutta University, Hasan said, "The university has already suspended the two students. We hope the two are not guilty."

He said just the fact that they have been arrested does not prove they are guilty — "nevertheless, we have suspended them." Assuring the assembly at Calcutta University that there is peace on Jamia campus, Hasan said it is "unfortunate" that names of Jamia students have cropped up in the blasts case.

"Totalitarian forces seeking revenge through violence are damaging Islam in stronger ways than they are (by) claiming lives," he said while accepting the honour. Hasan was conferred Doctor of Literature by the Calcutta University.

Heading: In post-Beijing fervour to promote ‘other’ sports, cricket stumped - Indian Express
Content:
Atif, the alleged militant killed in last Friday's encounter in Jamia Nagar, had formulated a unique code language to plan and execute the serial blasts on September 13, say police sources. In their code, the blast sites were called "library", Special Cell officials revealed, following interrogation of the five suspected militants.

After interrogating the arrested — Mohammed Said, Zeeshan, Shakil, Zia-ur-Rehman and Saquib Nisar — Special Cell officials said all of them appeared to be discussing books and studies while discussing the blasts. "If they had to talk over phone about crowded places where bombs could be easily placed and they had seen the site, they would say 'library dekh li hai, bhai' (I have seen the library)," a source said. "If Atif was asked about the crowd and the situation at the site, his accomplice would say, 'Main library mein kitaab padhke aa gaya hoon, aachchi hai (I have read books in the library; they are good)."

The bombs were called kitaab, or book. "When Atif procured bombs from Karnataka, he informed his superiors, including Tauqeer, over phone 'kitabein aa gayi hain'," the source said. "For the Delhi blasts, they used the word 'rack' for dustbins.

"When all of them returned after planting the bombs, they informed Atif by saying, 'Maine rack mein kitaab rakh di hai' (I have kept the book in the library rack)."

The codes, sources said, are the same as used in Hindi film Zameen, which is on terrorism. Atif, alias Bashir, briefed his counterparts in other states also using the code, sources said. The suspected militants used the same words when they spoke outside the flat, sources said. They used the code language to avoid interception, for the police were working on some phone numbers, the sources said.

There were more codes in the whole operation, and Special Cell officials said they are trying to crack them. Officials said numbers were also discussed in codes.

According to sources, Atif and his accomplices began using these codes 20 days before the blasts. Sources, meanwhile, said two days of interrogation has revealed that the five do not know much about the alleged blasts mastermind: Abdus Subhan, alias Tauqeer, and Abu Bashar. "They had not interacted with Tauqeer; Atif looked after all the operations," the source said.

Heading: Apple of the eye - Indian Express
Content:
This is one Beijing Olympic after-effect that the city could well have done without, for the sake of sports. While an interest in Olympic sports seem to have finally taken roots, it has knocked off a 38-year-old piece of history from the cricket grassroots Salwan Boys School, Rajinder Nagar, in the bargain.

The school, which has produced first-class cricketers by the dozen over the years, has as good as pulled the shutters down on its cricket team. Reason: the present school management wants to concentrate on disciplines such as athletics, wrestling and others. 

While the school authorities claim cricket has not been cut off its calendar, the team's main players were forced to seek greener pastures — other schools, that is — after school principal Raj Dabas, a physical education teacher who rose through the ranks, retired this May. Dabas's contribution to sports, particularly cricket, saw him occupy the post for the last eight years.

Soon, the school's cricket trainer Sanjay Bharadwaj, who has coached India opener Gautam Gambhir and leg-spinner Amit Mishra among others, was handed the pink slip. Subsequently, the entire school team was disbanded.

"Two days after Dabas-sir retired, new school principal Naresh Kumar called me up and said my services were not needed as they were winding up cricket," Bharadwaj said.

Interestingly, when the new edition of Boost all-India schools tournament was announced this Saturday, Dabas was a special invitee at the function. Under him and Bharadwaj, Salwan had won seven straight titles in the tournament but the defending champions will make only a token representation in the tournament this year.

"Ab kya jeetenge?" Dabas regretted. "They (Salwan) may make it to the second round at the most — most boys have already taken transfers (to other schools). If the principal does not take interest then it's difficult for any sport to survive in schools.

"I feel bad because I had worked so hard over the years."

Students confirmed that coaching and regular net practice has been stopped, and they have been denied leave to take part in matches.

The school authorities, however, denied the charge that the school team has been "disbanded". "The boys were taking too much liberty and not respecting school discipline," a school official (name withheld on request) said.

"We can't allow too many grace marks just because they are cricketers," the school official said. "They don't attend school and, most importantly, they joined the school just to play cricket. Just as they came here, they have migrated to another school now."

Salwan's loss is Vidya Jain School's gain. "Ab kya karen, these boys have to be accommodated somewhere," Bharadwaj said.

Heading: Healthy Combination - Indian Express
Content:
Global initiative Vision 2020 Right to Sight is all set to prepare a strong network of national NGOs to tackle burden of avoidable blindness

In the year 2000, blindness affected 50 million people and this will grow to 75 million by the year 2020 , unless special efforts are taken to arrest and reverse this trend Many organisations have attempted to combat the problem of blindness in the past. Towards this purpose, a global initiative called 'Vision 2020 Right to Sight' was launched as a collaborative movement by World Health Organisation (WHO) and International Agency for Prevention of Blindness (IAPB). Vision 2020 envisages collaboration between governments, WHO, IAPB, funding agencies, international and private non-governmental organisations (NGOs) to prevent and control cases of blindness.

"In our country there are an estimated 12 million blind people, of which over 90 per cent live in rural areas, says Col (retd) M Deshpande," member of National Executive Board, Vision 2020, who is also the senior director (Medical), HV Desai Eye Hospital. With the increase in life expectancy and projected increase in the country's population, this number is likely to increase to more than 18 million by the year 2020.

Blindness is mainly a problem of developing countries, which is preventable in at least 80 per cent of cases. India is committed to reduce the burden of preventable blindness by the year 2020 by adopting strategies advocated by Vision 2020. To align and collate the efforts of different sectors and organisations towards the national plan of action to achieve the goals of Vision 2020 in India, the Right to Sight India was founded in May 2004 as an NGO confederation parallel to the international body.

In his editorial comment in the October issue of the Medical Journal of Armed Forces of India (MJAFI), Deshpande has pointed out that the Armed Forces Medical Services (AFMS) with a country wide network of hospitals can provide a helping hand to the Right to Sight India. It is worth considering that AFMS should be a member of this forum, which will give a great impetus to this national programme on reducing the burden of avoidable blindness.

Vision 2020 organises World Sight Day, Eye Donation Fortnight and others with the active partnership of GOI. The forum is also building a strong network of national NGOs to tackle the burden of avoidable blindness. It facilitates the development of training modules, models, manuals, protocols and guidelines, which are made available to eye care institutions.

Heading: Pentavalent combination - Indian Express
Content:
Combination vaccines reduce the pain for the infant and also cuts down on the visits to the doctor

This is the era of combination vaccines. The number of recommended immunizations during childhood has increased in the past years. Under the immunisation schedule infants receive vaccines against 11 diseases in the first two years of their life and the total number of shots is 37 through six years of age. Sometimes the child may receive as many as five injections at a single visit to the clinic to cope up with the immunisation schedule enabling protection against additional diseases with a single shot. The pain that a child experiences when he is poked is not any less painful for his parents, says Dr Y K Amdekar, former president of the Indian Academy of Pediatrics.

Pain to children can be minimised by the usage of newer combination vaccines with higher safety, efficacy and quality. Combination vaccines merge into a single product, multiple antigens that prevent different diseases caused by various infectious agents like bacteria and viruses. Thus they reduce the number of injections required to prevent major killer diseases. A combination vaccine is a practical way to overcome the constraints of multiple injections, Amdekar points out.

Pentavalent vaccines prevent harmful diseases like diptheria, pertussis (whooping cough), tetanus, poliomyelitis (Polio), and HiB (Haemophilus influenza type B). These combination vaccines have a very high protective efficacy against five childhood killer diseases.

Pentavalent vaccines are usually given in three doses. The three doses are given at six weeks, 10 weeks and 14 weeks of age respectively. After three doses children can receive a booster dose between 15 to 18 months and WHO schedule is utilised for primary series.

Combination vaccines provide prevention against several diseases like Diptheria, Pertussis, Tetanus, Poliomyelitis and Hib simultaneously. They reduce the number of injections required and make the immunization schedule less complex. They aim at greater population coverage and help to reduce disease transmission.

A study, recently published in The Journal of Pediatrics, shows that efficacy or safety is not compromised when clinicians administer a new combination vaccine that streamlines the process of poking the child a number of times for each vaccine separately.

Combination vaccines help to simplify the current immunisation schedule. They decrease the anxiety of the parents and healthcare providers because of perceived reduction in pain for the infant. They also tend to reduce the missed opportunities to vaccinate the risk of needle sticks as a result of handling fewer syringes and improve the record keeping. They are economical for the parents as they involve fewer vaccine administration charges and potentially fewer clinic visits. Therefore, incorporation of combination vaccines into clinical practice will benefit infants, parents, healthcare providers, office managers, and managed care administrators alike, stresses Amdekar.

Heading: Health Corner - Indian Express
Content:
Diptheria mainly affects the throat. It spreads by droplets from the nose or mouth and if complications set in, it can cause breathing difficulties, damage to the heart and nervous system or even death.

Hib causes flu-like symptoms such as sore throat, chest infections and ear infections.Complications such as pneumonia, meningitis or epiglottitis (blockages of the throat) can set in. Symptoms of tetanus (sometimes called lockjaw) are painful spasms of muscle contraction. The disease can be fatal

Polio is caused by a virus. Sometimes it causes paralysis. it can kill people who get it, usually by paralyzing the muscles that help them breathe.

Pertussis is transmitted by droplets from the nose or mouth. It starts in the same way as cold, but the spasms of coughing become more and more severe. The 'whoop' occurs as the child draws breath between bouts of coughing. Severe cases may be complicated by pneumonia, vomiting and weight loss and, more rarely, by brain damage and death. Young babies are most at risk.

Heading: Switching channels - Indian Express
Content:
If only the number of watches one owned had some bearing on the punctuality factor, we could have well changed the dubious reputation enjoyed by Indian Standard Time. For while we may not be a very good nation of time keepers, of late we certainly have become great keepers of the time-telling devices. And all thanks to market that is flooded with classy, stylish yet affordable timepieces.

Gone are the days when special occasions like graduation, SSC, job placement and so on warranted the gift of watch to the recipient. Now is when even a casual movie going experience can double up as a watch buying spree, given the costs involved. Indeed there may be times when the movie ticket may cost more than the watch available at the multiplex! But then who's complaining?

Vishal Pandit is an engineering student who is passionate about trendy fashion accessories and says, "I have a collection of over 12 watches. I like to flaunt a rugged watch on my wrist. Being a student, buying an expensive watch is not possible for me however I get almost all, in fact better designs at much cheaper rates at the roadside shops. And to tell you the truth, since the last one year I don't remember a month when I have not bought a watch."

Muzaffer Shaikh, a salesperson at one of the shops on M G road agrees with the trend. "The market is full of smart and affordable watches. There was a time when buying watches that looked like these was a luxury, but no more.We have people from all sections of the society coming and buying watches from us. And why shouldn't they since these watches give the same look as the expensive ones yet are still available in the range of Rs 100 to 200 and can be used without any problems for at least one year."

The insides of these watches are fabricated and come with fully charged batteries that last for anywhere between six months to one year. Clearing the misconception that the watches are useless after the batteries expire, Shaikh adds, "They do not come with a warranty but then the batteries can surely be replaced. In fact if one maintains the watch properly, these can be used for longer duration as well."

While big, colourful dials with metallic and leather belts along with additional features like stopwatch, tachometer are the characteristics of watches for men, the ones for women display fresh and vibrant colours on delicate designs. Debika Rakshe another student says, "I like trekking and a part of my trekking gear is a sports watch that I brought from roadside shop. I am a rough user and I prefer losing this watch rather than an expensive one."

It is the same trend that has compelled even giants in the field of watches to introduce affordable trendy watches in the market. According to Shabbir Ghadyali who owns a watch shop in Kumar plaza on M G Road, "Brands such as Timex and Fast Track also offer sporty watches at very competitive prices now. For instance, Timex watches start from Rs 400 while Fast Track ones are for Rs 500 and above. The added advantage in this case is the warranty that comes with the brand."

Usually it is difficult to beat the multiplexes when it comes to exorbitant prices, but the affordable watch mania seems to have caught the shopping malls and multiplexes as well. One of the stores in a city multiplex offers attractive watches for as less as Rs 120. The owner who doesn't want to be named says, "We sell minimum 12 to 15 watches a day and the demand for them is very high. Today, what is more important is looking good and people are getting to look good at cheaper prices."

Times indeed have changed.

Ques: What makes these watches affordable?

Expensive watches use high-end materials like steel, titanium for manufacturing the parts. In case of affordable watches, the assembly is made of cheaper material like plastic, which serves the purpose for hosting the gear assembly.

Ques: Where are these watches manufactured?

These watches are manufactured at a number of locations in Mumbai and Pune. However major chunk comes from China. Branded watches are however manufactured in the respective companies.

Ques: The price range

The price for these watches ranges any where between 100 and 1000 depending upon the design. For instance roadside metallic watches cost Rs 100 to 200. Branded watches come with a warranty and the price range is between 400 and 600. The replicas of some of the famous and popular models however, cost Rs 1000 and above.

Ques: Popular designs

Big, rugged watches are in for men. Bright colours are in for women.

Heading: RTO’s ply-by-meter will return to Pimpri, yet again - Indian Express
Content:
Study on to estimate city's capacity for sustaining population

With the city's population growing at 3.5 per cent a year, the Pune Municipal Corporation (PMC) has undertaken a study to estimate the maximum population that can be sustained by the city, with water supply as the defining factor. This will be part of the new development control (DC) rules, which are an annexure to the ongoing process for the new development plan (DP) that will form the backbone of the city's sustainable development for the next 20 years.

Member of the group set up for framing new DC rules, architect Rajiv Raje said as the DP has to be prepared for two decades, the DC rules need to be framed in a manner that could help in controlling the population growth in the city that could be sustained with the available infrastructure.

The population of the city is around 40 lakh and the civic administration has a capacity of 1,031 million litre per day of water supply with approximately a per citizen capacity of 195 litre per day. Against this, the sewage generated by the city is 451 million litre per day.

Now, the civic administration has plans to increase the water supply capacity to 1,500 MLD by 2025 to cater to an estimated 25-lakh growth in population, as Pune will be home to 65 lakh people. It also plans to scale up the sewage treatment capacity to 1,200 MLD.

Even though population growth of any region is a natural phenomena based on various factors, Raje said the Floor Space Index (FSI) can act as a controlling factor for population growth in the residential region. The demand as well as availability of water can give a theoretical picture of the sustainable population of the city, Raje said.

The existing per capita consumption of water and overall availability will help in estimating the threshold growth of the city in terms of population, he added.

According to architect Vikas Bhandari the availability of water, water distribution system, sewerage treatment, transportation and public amenities – all these factors decide the sustaining capacity of any city. While all other factors can be improved, the availability of water has restrictions, he said.

Therefore, the population sustaining capacity within the PMC jurisdiction can be decided by studying the availability of water and its consumption. Thus, the total water supply to the city including ground water would enable in determining the population that the city could sustain, Bhandari said.

For a more accurate estimation, it has been decided to study the sewage received at the treatment plants as an indicator of water consumption that can be compared with the available water supply.

It also has an advantage that the threshold limit can be increased if education of water conservation is imparted among the citizens and per capita consumption is brought down, Bhandari said.

The group is also studying DC rules of Delhi, Bangalore, Hyderabad, London and Singapore for framing the best rules for Pune.

Heading: Secondary school exams after Diwali - Indian Express
Content:
Rule to be mandatory from Oct 5; share-a-rickshaw too makes comeback

For the umpteenth time in the last decade, the Deputy Regional Transport Office, Chikhali, is going to make ply-by-meters compulsory for autorickshaws across Pimpri-Chinchwad. This is the second promise made by Deputy RTO Sarjerao Shelke who had made a similar promise when he took over a year-and-a-half back. The last time he made the promise, it had lasted only a few weeks.

The ply-by-meter scheme will be made mandatory for all autorickshaws from October 5. The RTO is also re-introducing the share-a-rickshaw scheme on 14 roads in Pimpri-Chinchwad.

The routes, where the share-a-rickshaw has been planned are Dapodi to Nigdi, Nashik Phata to Bhosari, Pimpri to Chikhali, Pimpri to Kalewadi Phata, Pimpri to Dange chowk, Bhosari to KSB chowk, Nigdi to KSB chowk, Chinchwad station to Dange chowk and Landewadi to Nigdi.

Officials said that in view of the rising population and rapid expansion of the city, rickshaw stands are being increased. "The number of rickshaw stands will be increased to 157 from 57," he said. The traffic police will crack down on illegal rickshaws from October 5. The decision was conveyed by Deputy Commissioner of Police (Traffic) Manoj Patil to Rickshaw Panchayat at a meeting between representatives of the Rickshaw Panchayat and RTO on Monday.

"The rickshaw drivers have been asked to display their permit numbers and their expiry dates on the rickshaw. Rickshaw capacity should also be mentioned. They have been given 15 days, after which action will be taken," said Shelke.

Contacted, Anand Unavne, secretary of the Maharashtra Rickshaw Panchayat, said the RTO had given them 15 days to get the papers in order. He said the rickshaw drivers should have the original papers with them, otherwise action would be taken. "But drivers cannot keep original papers with them as many rickshaws are taken on rent and the owners refuse to give the papers to drivers," he said expressing opposition to the compulsory meter scheme.

Boards mentioning the trip cost will be put up at share-a-rickshaw stands. The initiative will be of great benefit to thousands of commuters who will now pay a nominal charge, he said. Shelke said around 5,400 rickshaws with permits are plying in Pimpri-Chinchwad. Of them, 1,000 ply in the 18 newly merged villages. Around 600 six-seater ones ply in rural areas.

Heading: Workers fight on...for their dream factory - Indian Express
Content:
The term-end exams of all the secondary schools (class 8 to class 10) in the city will be conducted after Diwali vacation. The secondary education officer of Pune Zilla Parishad has come up with a circular on September 20 in this regard, which will be applicable to all the schools including government-aided, non-aided and private schools.

The Commonwealth Youth Games (CYG) will be held in the city from October 12 to 18 in which many schoolchildren will be participating. Previously, it was decided that the 70 schools participating would conduct their exams after Diwali. "But the other schools in the city also made the request as their students are also participating in the games," Prakash Parab, Secondary Education Officer of Pune Zilla Parishad told The Indian Express .

Parab said that the CYG organising committee also had requested the education department to postpone the term-end exams.

"The baton relay is supposed to take place on October 5, in which many students are participating. According to the timetable, the term-work is officially ending on October 5 and schools are allowed to take exams only after that. But it is not possible as the games are starting on October 12. That is why we have taken the decision to postpone the exams," he said.

Meanwhile, a few English medium schools have already declared their timetable for term-end exams. When asked, what will happen to that, Parab said the schools had not taken permission from our department, which was necessary. "These schools have to cancel the exams and conduct them in November after Diwali vacation," he said.

As the term-end exams are postponed, it is likely that the final exams will also get postponed at least by two weeks. Generally, the final exams start in the last week of March. As the first term-end exams will be delayed, the final exams will most likely be conducted after April 5. "As the official working days of schools are up to April 30, it will fit in the norms," said a senior officer.

Heading: University to keep hawk’s eye on exam centres - Indian Express
Content:
Deadline to deposit Rs 4.5 crore ends today; extension being sought

Former employees of Garware Nylons, Pimpri, who have embarked upon their dream project of setting up the country's first ever "common people's factory," will have to wait a little longer.

The 210 former employees of the company who had won a bid in a public auction earlier in February to take possession of nine acres of land belonging to the company's closed unit in Ahmednagar, have not been able to collect the required deposit amount of Rs 4.5 crore yet.

The Supreme Court had issued orders to deposit the amount in 15 days. With the deadline lapsing on September 24, and the workers unable to raise the requisite amount, they are seeking an extension upto to October 15. Dominic Lobo, representative of workers and president of the Common People's Front, said, "It was too short a notice to raise the amount."

Of the total of Rs 6.01 crore, the workers had initially submitted Rs 1.05 crore. They were to deposit Rs 4.5 crore according to a Supreme Court order. However, the employees are now seeking an extension till October 20 due to funds crunch. Lobo said that the promised funds from different quarters did not come in. "There were many people who promised but in actual we did not get the funds.'' The company had closed its units in Ahmednagar, Pimpri and Sarola on August 28, 1996 and the workers had come together to form their own factory by pitching in some amount, said Lobo. The workers had earlier sold their belongings, mortgaged gold and houses to deposit a whopping Rs 1.5 crore in 15 days. Help came in only through a few philanthropic individuals, said Lobo. The workers managed only Rs one crore. "Some of them are even trying to sell their agricultural lands but it is not possible in this period of 'Pitra Pandharavada.' So we need more time,'' said Pravin Dhole, another worker.

A fresh application was filed on Tuesday in the Supreme Court seeking extension of the deadline till October 15 to deposit the balance. The application is likely to come up for hearing on next Tuesday before a two judge bench. The 'Pitra Pandharavad' end on September 30 and is hindering the sale of agricultural lands of three workers who have committed to sell their lands and help the cause, said Lobo.

Heading: ARI identifies bacteria for oil extraction above 90 degrees C - Indian Express
Content:
From April onwards, all the examination centres of the University of Pune (UoP) will be under the scanner as the university has decided to keep a close watch on the examination process with increased number of vigilance squads and stringent norms to curb the irregularities.

The university has decided to identify officials in every examination centre to fix responsibility if any irregularity takes place. The centres will also be penalised if five per cent of total students in an examination centre are found using unfair means.

The examination department has been mired in controversies this year as several incidences of irregularities have come to the fore. It all started with a paper leak in March. After that as the results were out in June, there were a number of instances where the students were marked absent in their marksheet when they were actually present for the exam.

In this backdrop, Vice-Chancellor Narendra Jadhav had immediately taken action and set up a four-member committee to suggest reforms in the present examination system chaired by Sarjerao Nimse, a management council member. The committee has come up with some stringent norms in its report, which was recently accepted in the board of examination.

The report has stated that the new colleges would be given permission to act as an examination centre only after a detailed scrutiny by a committee appointed by the vice-chancellor. "Presently, the new colleges are given the status of examination centre on their request letters. But now these colleges will be scrutinised by the committee, which will see if there is proper infrastructure in place and approved teachers and principals are there on whom responsibility can be placed," said Babasaheb Sangale, a member of the committee.

If five per cent of the total students are found copying, fine will be levied on the examination centre as a punishment. "Principal of the college and senior and junior supervisors will be held responsible and action will be taken," said another member of the committee. "The suggestions will be implemented from the final year exams to be held in April/May," he added.

There are some other recommendations like hike in the remuneration of members of vigilance squads from Rs 200 to Rs 400 and increasing the number of squads from eight to 12.

Heading: Srivastav wins U-17 pre-quarterfinal - Indian Express
Content:
In what could prove to be a path-breaking discovery for the oil exploration and production business, scientists at Agharkar Research Institute (ARI), Pune have identified environment friendly bacteria that allows extraction of oil at temperatures more than 90 degrees Celsius. Even as microbial enhanced oil recovery (MEOR) methods are being used by oil companies at the commercial level, Oil and Natural Gas Corporation (ONGC) has decided to seize the initiative and go in for field trials by attempting to produce oil at temperature levels above 90 degrees C.

ONGC, having recovered 40,000 tonnes of oil from 100 defunct wells around Ahmedabad and Assam in the last two years, is now contemplating field trials with the new technology. Dr T R Mishra, General Manager, Institute of Reservoir Studies, ONGC, when contacted in Ahmedabad told The Indian Express that the technology devised by ARI scientists was showing success at the laboratory level and soon field trials will be taken up.

"The ONGC has earmarked a sum of Rs 50 lakh for each of the research projects to develop microbial techniques used for the extraction of oil," he said.

P K Dhakephalkar, scientist at ARI, said the institute has developed several consortia that could be suitable for MEOR. These consortia work in a temperature range of 70C to more than 96C. Consortia developed for MEOR at more than 91C are jointly owned by ARI and IRS-ONGC.

At present, the MEOR process for oil reservoir with temperature above 90 degrees C is not available. Since microorganisms involved are anaerobic ones and very few R&D labs in the country have adequate facilities to work on anaerobes, not much work has been carried out on anaerobes based MEOR processes.

Meor is the use of microorganisms to retrieve additional oil from existing wells, thereby enhancing the petroleum production of an oil reservoir. Compared to other oil recovery processes, MEOR becomes even more attractive at low oil prices, Mishra said.

Dhakephalkar, who along with other scientists has been working on anaerobic bacteria for the past one year explained that there was a large amount of viscous and hard oil present underground. Oil companies cannot pump it due to the depth of the wells and they have even used water, gas and other chemicals.

These bacterial clusters will produce gas that will make it easier to locate the oil supply and hence it can propel the oil out of the well. Bacteria have been cultivated in the laboratory and can work well in temperatures in Indian wells that are above 90 degrees C.

Heading: Petit reign supreme in football - Indian Express
Content:
The inter-school tennis tournament, conducted by the Zilla Parishad, is being held at the Fergusson College Tennis courts. In the under-17 boys pre-quarterfinal, Vivek Srivastav blanked out Harsh Thakkar 7-0.

Vivek Srivastav had total control of the proceedings and gave no chance to his opponent. Sagar Shah beat Rushav Runawat 7-4 in a tough match. Both players fought hard and put a lot of effort into their game. Nakul Rawal cruised past Akshay Shekhatkar, defeating him 7-0.

Heading: Junior tennis tournament from Oct 24 - Indian Express
Content:
JN Pet it have dominated the football scene this year, winning five tournaments at the local level and two at the district level. Petit started their reign over Pune football by winning the under-14 and under-17 sections of the National Congress Party football tournament. They then won the under-17 section of the Subroto Mukherjee tournament and went on to win the district level tournament after beating St. Josephs High School, Solapur, in the final. They came third in the state level of the same tournament held at the St. Xavier's ground, Bombay after defeating New English Academic School, Kolhapur. Their under-17 team again won the inter-school football tournament conducted by the Zilla Parishad and carried on their good form. Finally the under-16 team won the inter school SAI tournament and wrapped up a year full of trophies for their school.

Rohan Kadam, Karim Dinani and Shubham Lad all students of JN Petit school have been selected for the under-15 Pune FC team. "Players like Rohan Kadam and Riyan Yadgiri have played a vital role in ensuring success," said Nandu Angirwal, head coach of the JN Petit football team. Riyan Yadgiri represented last year's Pune FC team that went to Chennai to play a tournament. In the current under-19 squad of the Pune FC line up, four players — Nishant Malwinkar, Akash Kamble, Jeevan Nalge and Niket Jain — were once a part of Angirwal's football team.

Heading: Symbiosis eves win volleyball title - Indian Express
Content:
The eighth Baker's Basket Junior Open Tennis Tournament will be held at the Ladies Club Tennis Courts from October 24-November 1. The inauguration will be on October 23. The tournament is a non-ranking Junior Tennis Tournament conducted by 'Sunny Jacob Tennis Academy.' Sunny Jacob is the director of the tournament.

The events are for boys and girls under the ages of 9, 11, 13 and 15 years. The entry forms can be collected from all Baker's Basket shops, located at Aundh Road, Bhandarkar Road, Dhole Patil Road, East Street, Karve Road, Wanowrie, Kalyani Nagar, Polka Dots and Ladies Club from October 23.

Heading: Dark days: Baner residents hit the streets - Indian Express
Content:
Symbiosis girls clinched the title in the under-14 inter school volleyball tournament conducted by the Zilla Parishad at the Azam Campus Volleyball Courts on Tuesday. Symbiosis had no trouble in beating Kataria High School in straight sets 25-23 and 25-15. Urvi Khasnis and Priyadarshani Kokre played a key role in securing a victory for Symbiosis.

In the under-17 section, Bharati Vidya Bhavan boys managed to win the title but the girls were not so lucky. The boys' team beat opponents Symbiosis in straight sets 25-21 and 25-10. Satyajit Deshmukh and Sanket Shitole played a stellar role in the victory while Soham Hudekar and Sankalp Kokare reduced the deficit for the losing team. The Bharati Vidya Bhavan girls team were defeated by Tejaswini Krida Probhodini 25-19 and 29-27 in a tough encounter. Himali Doshi and Sharayu Rao played well for the winners while Rashmi Kadam and Kashmira Patil reduced the margin for the losing team.

Heading: PMC dithers, Ruby Hall Clinic approaches Ajit Pawar - Indian Express
Content:
CYG road work spells nightmare; cable fault, says MSEDCL

Irate citizens in Baner were out on the streets on Tuesday after a third massive power failure owing to the Commonwealth Youth Games roadwork. This was the third such black out over the last week because of the frantic pace with which the Pune Municipal Corporation is undertaking roadwork from Baner to Balewadi to meet the CYG deadline.

The blackout began on Monday evening at 4 pm and continued late into Tuesday night even as Maharashtra State Electricity Distribution Corporation Limited (MSEDCL) officers said that they would provide citizens with backup power. On September 20, there was a massive power failure extending to 65 hours because of the roadwork, on 15-16 September, there was a 25 hour power cut.

Supply to four transformers have been cut off, 300-500 connections are affected. This follows the 65 hour- black out that began on September 20 and a 26 hour power failure on September 15 prior to that.

"What on earth will we do with sports, if survival is becoming difficult?" said Amar Singh, a 70-year-old citizen living at Ujjwal Estate on Baner Road. "This has been happening since the road work began, but it was always repaired in a span of few hours. Without power, water supply has been erratic. Our telephone lines have also been down because of cable faults for a month. The civic body is showing little concern for the senior citizens, little children here for whom life has become difficult," said Singh. "When we complain to MSEDCL, they are asking us to go and lodge protest with the municipal corporation," a resident said.

MSEDCL deputy engineer A G Ghatol said that two cables of 11 kv each had snapped again because of PMC roadwork. "We are trying to get back up feeders till the repair work is undertaken," he said.

Heading: Appoint panel to probe lapses, Mayor directs civic administration - Indian Express
Content:
The lethargic attitude of the Pune Municipal Corporation (PMC) in taking a decision on running its Bharat Ratna Rajiv Gandhi Memorial Hospital in Yerawada with private partnership has prompted the Ruby Hall Clinic (RHC) to approach guardian minister Ajit Pawar. RHC had earlier won a tender floated by the PMC to start the hospital.

The confusion, whether the hospital should be in partnership with a private firm, which is said to be the delay in taking any decision, came after chief minister Vilasrao Deshmukh questioned the need to hand over civic hospitals to private parties.

Ajit Pawar had recently said that those industries that have taken land from the government and not utilising it should surrender the land or immediately start operation. Chief Executive Officer of RHC, Bomi Bhote said he has requested Pawar to use the same rule in this case. "We hope the minister's involvement will speed up the process," he added.
