After the inauguration of Rajiv Gandhi hospital on March 03, 2007, the PMC had floated a tender in December inviting private parties to run the hospital.

"RHC had won the bid and we had paid a deposit of Rs 25 lakh to the PMC on December 19, 2007," said Bhote, However, the PMC has not yet handed over the 170-bed hospital to Ruby Hall and neither have they returned the RS 25 lakh deposit amount, he said.

"I have met the PMC Commisioner Praveensinh Pardeshi at least a dozen times in this regard. However, all I have been getting is assurances and nothing beyond," Bhote said. Frustrated with the lethargic attitude of the PMC, he requested Pawar to intervene in the matter. "He has assured us that he will look into it," Bhote said.

Reacting to the issue, Pardeshi agreed that they had accepted the deposit from Ruby Hall. PMC Chief health officer, Dr Pramod Dhaygude said that the delay was caused after chief minister Vilasrao Deshmukh had questioned the need to hand over civic hospitals to private parties for management. He added that the civic body is planning to run the hospital and an outdoor patient department (OPD) and 25-bed maternity home was started a month ago at the hospital. He said that the PMC would write to the government to permit the PMC to run the hospital with private partnership.

"However, the hospital is supposed to be a super specialty hospital and not just an OPD and maternity home," Bhote said.

According to the bid, the hospital is to have the freedom of sharing their facilities like pathological laboratory, blood bank, radiology clinic and MRI tests. The party can also decide on the number of beds that can be accommodated in the hospital.

Heading: Man booked for bid to kill wife - Indian Express
Content:
Following a row over the negligence of the Pune Municipal Corporation's (PMC) during its general body meeting, including the recent incident of a fire breaking out at biomedical waste plant and impure water being provided to the residents of Uruli Devachi owing to the existence of a garbage depot in the area, Mayor Rajlaxmi Bhosale on Tuesday directed the civic administration to appoint a committee that will probe into these matters and take action against those found responsible for the lapses.

The issue of the health department's disregard for health norms was also discussed during the general body meeting. BJP corporator Anil Shirole asked if the health department had undertaken any precautionary measures to stop the water from getting contaminated before a garbage depot was set up at the Uruli Devachi. PMC health chief Pramod Dhaigude replied that no measures had been taken before the garbage depot came up at the site. "After we observed that the water quality is deteriorating due to the garbage depot, we started taking some measures," Dhaigude said.

Regarding the issue of seven workers getting killed in the accident at the biomedical waste disposal plant, Shirole said, "Despite the fact that seven workers lost their lives in the fire caught at the Kailash crematorium, the PMC has not yet suspended any health department official directly responsible for it." Reiterating this view, NCP corporator Subhash Jagtap said the PMC had not filed a complaint against the contractor responsible for the irregularities.

According to BJP corporator Vikas Mathkari, "The contractor of the incinerator had illegally constructed a godown and also piled up inflammable contents - deodorant-spray. The PMC had constructed this Rs 1 crore plant, wherein the contractor was found bringing in spray-cans from Bhiwandi.

Therefore, PMC health chief should be held responsible for the incident." Municipal Commissioner Praveensinh Pardeshi responded by saying that the PMC was taking a stepwise action in this case.

During the general body meeting, Congress corporators, including Arvind Shinde, Virendra Kirad, Avinash Salve and Siddharth Dhende demanded that the committee report on the school board irregularities, which was expected to be tabled by the civic administration during the GB, but had not been submitted yet.

BJP corpoator Ujwal Keskar said the Congress had no right to demand the report, as the party had never submitted any report on the irregularities of the school board, which happened during the Congress regime.

Heading: PTA hampered by lack of experts: NGOs - Indian Express
Content:
Twenty-year-old Sunitabai Patil was allegedly set ablaze by her husband and in-laws for not getting Rs 2 lakh from her parents as demanded.

The police have filed a case against Manohar Patil (28), Jijabai Patil, Meena Patil of Pune and Pandurang Patil of Dhule on the basis of a complaint filed by Sunitabai with the Sangvi police.

In her complaint, Sunitabai accused her in-laws of harassing her mentally and physically.

She said that on September 15, they took away all the gold jewellery she was wearing before setting her ablaze.

Sunita was first admitted to Yeshwantrao Chavan Memorial Hospital and then shifted to Jawahar Medical Hospital in Dhule.

Inspector Vijay Sawant of crime branch is investigating the case.

Heading: At PMPML: Kumar brakes to a halt, Patil speeds on - Indian Express
Content:
Pointing out the lack of sufficient experts in the Pune Tree Authority (PTA) not providing enough voice in stopping the loss of green cover, non-governmental organisations Pune Tree Watch and Parisar have urged Municipal Commissioner Praveensinh Pardeshi to appoint an expert in the vacant post in the PTA as per the directions of the Bombay High Court.

"There are only few experts of recognised environmental NGOs in the PTA. The lack of commitment from other members of the committee is hampering efforts to curb the loss of green cover," Tasneem Balasinorwala and Sharvari Barve, PTA members and representatives of Pune Tree Watch, said in a letter to the Municipal Commissioner.

The Bombay High court has accorded Parisar to have one of its recommended members in the PTA, they said. The position has been vacant for long.

Since Ajay Vaishampayan, appointed following a recommendation from Parisar, recently resigned. The 30-member PTA has to have at least 15 elected representatives and a minimum of five experts, Balasinorwala said, adding there were actually only three experts on the body now.

Heading: PBAP meet addresses issues in realty sector - Indian Express
Content:
On a day when Ashwini Kumar, former director-general of Yashwantrao Chavan Academy of Development Administration (YASHADA) held his first meeting as the managing director and chairman of Pune Mahanagar Parivahan Mahamandal Limited (PMPML) with his staff, the state government stayed the transfer orders of the previous chief S B Patil. Sources in the state government said that this has been done only till the Commonwealth Youth Games that will be held between October 12 to 18, in the city.

For Ashwini Kumar, this is the third time in the last three weeks that his transfer order has been withdrawn or cancelled.

On Saturday, the state government had transferred him to PMPML as the new head, while Patil had been shifted to Konkan as the divisional commissioner. "It is a temporary stay. I will be continuing at Yashada till I join PMPML," said Kumar.

Three weeks ago he was set to take charge as the Commissioner of Physically Challenged. Sources said that this order was withdrawn after a minister raised objections with the chief minister. A week ago, he was to be posted as the Commissioner of Social Welfare, which was also withdrawn.

"The government felt that that the present incumbent (Patil) would have more experience during the upcoming the CYG. It was felt that the new person might require some more time. The orders have been stayed only for about a month till the CYG ends. Ashwini Kumar will take charge after that," said a senior officer at the office of Chief Secretary. Some people associated with the CYG may have requested for the transfer to be stayed, he added.

Patil confirmed that stay order. "The orders staying my transfer were faxed to my office this morning," he said.

Earlier in the day, before the stay order, Kumar held a meeting with the PMPML staff and a media interaction was initially scheduled for Wednesday morning, which was finally cancelled. When Kumar does take charge next month, he would be the first mechanical engineer to head the bus utility.

He has previous work experience as district collector of Dhule, municipal commissioner of Sangli and Pune Commissioner of Women and Child welfare and Director of Sports, Pune.

Heading: DAPA to hold AGM on Saturday - Indian Express
Content:
The Promoters and Builders Association of Pune in association with Grahak Peth held a talk show on 'Review of Pune Real Estate' on Monday.

The event was participated by Lalitkumar Jain, president, PBAP, Balaji Raghvan, business head-mortgage finance, ICICI HFC and Anuj Puri country head and managing director, Jones Lang Lasalle Meghraj (JLLM).

"The city is witnessing a high growth in terms of education and employment. The attrition rate of employment as compared to other cities is very low thus increasing the sustainability of employees. The real estate scenario is diverse here," said Anuj Puri, analysing the sudden growth in the IT sector.

Raising concern over various issues in the realty sector, Puri said, "As far as the realty scenario in Pune is concerned, the major issues are over supply, poor quality supply and supply to places where there is no demand. These issues have to addressed."

Commenting on the unstable scenario of real estate these days, Balaji Raghvan said, "Even though the sales are low till monsoon, Pune is comparatively stable."

But according to Satish Magar, the big concern at present is the increased cost of raw materials and labour.

The ICICI bank has announced a 10 per cent interest scheme for three days at the PBAP exhibition starting on October 3.

Heading: Satyam launches development centre in city - Indian Express
Content: The 15th Annual Genreal body meeting (AGM) of Defence Accounts Pensioners Association  (DAPA) will be held on Saturday at CDA (Officers) recreation club hall at 9.30 am. The association will felicitate pensioners who have completed seventy-five years of age and will discuss pensioner's entitlements as contained in the Sixth Pay Commision report. BG Joshi, FADS (retired) and SS Savadi, Principal Controller of Defence Accounts (retired) will grace the occasion. H N Kulkarni (president), R Krishnan (vice president), Shailendra Mhaskar secretary and SR Gore Joint Secretary will be present on the occasion.

Heading: CYG: Seminar on e-waste held - Indian Express
Content:
Satyam Computer Services on Tuesday opened a development centre in the special economic zone at the Rajiv Gandhi Infotech Park, Hinjewadi. The state-of-the-art facility, which is spread over 475,000 sq ft, will eventually accommodate 4,750 employees.

Speaking on the occasion, Virender Aggarwal, head, APAC and MEIA regions, Satyam, "Our investment in this centre is an indication that Pune is becoming India's next information technology hub."

Reiterating this viewpoint, Uday Shankar Roy, managing director and chief executive officer, SBI Life Insurance, said Pune was one of the fastest growing IT hubs in the country, posing a challenge to cities such as Bangalore and Hyderabad.

Heading: Shiv Sena to demand public votes for all SEZs - Indian Express
Content:
Under the environmental friendly drive of commonwealth youth games, a seminar was organised at I2IT on the e-waste management by NGO Sarathi.

"E-waste menace is growing at a faster pace and the ill effects have started showing already. Maharashtra is seating at 1st position as far as e-waste is concerned.

The government should take concrete steps towards developing a technology for recycling the e-waste, which is not developed at present," said Sanjay Gandhi, director, Jetking.

He was addressing the students as a guest speaker at the seminar.

Heading: Discount sale at Brand Factory - Indian Express
Content:
After the Congress-NCP led government was forced to seek public votes on the Maha-Mumbai Special Economic Zone (SEZ) in Raigad, the Shiv Sena has decided to demand similar referendum on all the proposed SEZ through out the state.

"There is unrest among the farmers through out the state for the forcible acquisition of their farm land for the SEZ," Sena leader and Leader of Opposition in the state legislative assembly Ramdas Kadam told reporters here on Monday.

He said the state government was forced for referendum due to the agitation by farmers against the Mukesh Ambani promoted RIL's proposed 10,000 hecatre multi-purpose SEZ in Raigad district and the same situation prevails at Maan village as well as Shinde village in Pune district for various industrial mega projects.

"Prime Minister Manmohan Singh, President Pratibha Patil and Congress chief Sonia Gandhi have been urging the government to not to acquire the agriculture land for the industrial purpose, but the Congress-led government in the state is going against it only to maintain the interest of the industries," Kadam said adding the Democratic Front (DF) government in the state has no moral right to remain in power.

There is no sufficient power supply to run such big industrial projects as there has been no addition in the power generation capacity in the state, but the government is engaged in making the farmers landless, he alleged.

The union government was forced to announce a loan waiver package for the farmers after the Sena took a state-wide agitation for it, Kadam said adding there is rampant corruption in implementing it.

The state government is merely cheating the public by giving false assurance as it did through announcement of package for development of Marathwada region, he said.

Kadam said it is the failure of the government to ensure good prices to agriculture produce has led to the debt of the farmers compelling them to commit suicide.

Heading: Now traders up ante against Raj, tell CM they are living in fear - Indian Express
Content:
Brand Factory, the one-stop hub of branded products near Shivaji market in Camp, is organising "biggest discount sale."

The end of season sale from September 15 to October 5, has exciting offers on apparels, footwear, cosmetics, fragrances, herbal products and accessories, stated a press release.

Shoppers will have the opportunity to indulge in shopping spree as they can avail Buy 1 Get 1 Free, Buy 2 Get 3 Free and other great deals on 150 best brands include Flying Machine, Park Avenue, Parx, Arrow Sports, Lee Kids, Bare Denim and Allen Solly, the release said.

Heading: Global architects will compete to design 309-ft Shivaji statue off Marine Drive - Indian Express
Content:
Well over a month after Raj Thackeray's Maharashtra Navinirman Sena members ransacked shops and damaged signboards for not displaying their name in the Devnagari script, the Federation of Retail Traders Welfare Association (FRTWA) has reignited the issue, with a letter to Chief Minister Vilasrao Deshmukh and Deputy Chief Minister R R Patil detailing the damages suffered by shopowners and stating that they are still "living in fear".

Asking for stern action towards maintaining law and order in the city and citing the public statements made by MNS men threatening Joint Commissioner of Police K L Prasad, the letter adds that property worth Rs 7 lakh was damaged in the course of the MNS campaign against shopfronts that did not have Devnagiri names. The letter says the shopkeepers should be compensated by the state government.

Signed by joint secretary of FRTWA Viren Shah, who owns the Roopam stores, the letter lists 15 shop-owners in the city who say their shops were damaged by MNS men. The Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation had set a deadline of August 28 for all shops and establishments to display signboards in Devnagri. The MNS, which had taken up the issue of the Marathi signboards, had directed the shopkeepers to follow the regulation or "face the consequences".

"Thackeray has threatened well-known personalities.. the Bachchan family had no option but to apologise to him. Because of such incidents and the approach of Raj and his party, we as well as the public at large residing in the state are feeling insecure and living under fear," the letter states. The letter asks the state government to take immediate steps to maintain law and order in the state.

Shah, who refused to toe the MNS line and became the face of the protests, said: "We obtained details from around 15 shopkeepers on damages and have requested the state government to compensate them in due course."

Shah's letter states that even after the Bombay High Court order directing Thackeray and his men to refrain from disturbing law and order, some incidents continued. "His party workers have thrown stones and broken glasses of shops, bank ATM centers, autorickshaws and taxis. The state government has failed to take any concrete and cognizable action against them from doing such violence," Shah has said in the letter.

MNS General Secretary Shirish Parkar responded by saying said that the FRTWA itself, and not his party, was to blame for the damages. "If they had not gone against the law, then the shops would have never been damaged. They shouldn't have gone against public feeling and the law," he said, adding that it was also wrong on Shah's part to have arranged a meeting of retailers and traders and "incite" them against following the rule.

Heading: School boy run over by tanker; irate mob damages Best bus - Indian Express
Content:
The proposal for erecting the equestrian statue of Maratha warrior Shivaji in the Arabian Sea will now have architects from all over the world competing to be a part of the ambitious project.

Conceptualised to stand four feet taller than the Statue of Liberty in New York, the blueprint for the statue has already been drawn up by the state Public Works Department (PWD). The state government has now decided to announce an international competition in which architects worldwide will be invited to participate. The first three winners will be given prizes of Rs 2.5 lakh, Rs 2 lakh and Rs 1.5 lakh each.

"Any architect who has carried out work of similar nature globally can participate. By next week we will be issuing the draft for the competition. Once that is done, the architects will be given about two months to submit their proposals that detail the design and technology to be used," said PWD chief architect Bipin Sankhe.

As per plans laid out by the PWD, the Shivaji statue will come up a kilometer into the sea from the Marine Drive, nestled between Nariman Point and Malabar Hill on a 6-acre patch of reclaimed land. The architects will have to submit detailed designs for the statue on a pedestal which would be have a total height of 309 feet.

Located centrally at the base of the statue will be an amphitheatre for light and sound shows on whose periphery will be six foot-high walls with murals on Shivaji's life. Also at the base of the statue will be a cafeteria for visitors, a garden and a museum showcasing the history of the period through literature and relics.

The participating architects will have to base their designs as per the recommendations of the technical committee headed by the chief secretary. Said Thanksy Thekkekara, principal secretary for the General Administration Department (GAD), "We have provided the PWD Rs 1 crore for the competitive international bidding, they will take it forward from here."

The GAD department has estimated a budget of Rs 100 crore for the project this year.

The architect who is declared the winner of the competition will be awarded the contract and paid a percentage of the project cost as his fee.

Heading: Susairaj gets to have half-hour meeting with Emile in court - Indian Express
Content:
A twelve-year-old boy was run over by a speeding tanker on Tuesday at Chembur Naka, which led to an angry mob pelting stones and damaging a BEST bus parked nearby.

According to the Chembur police, Rohit Papardekar, a sixth standard student of the Chembur School at Chembur Naka near the Sion Trombay Road, had just left his school premises when he was mowed down by the speeding tanker. "The impact of the accident was such that Rohit died on the spot after being crushed under the wheels. The driver, Dashrath Sahu (55), was immediately taken in to custody and charged with causing death due to rash and negligent driving," said Senior Police Inspector Balasaheb Pachundkar.

Though the driver did not seem drunk, the police have taken him for a medical check-up. "From the driver's behaviour, he did not seem drunk. But still, we cannot take any chances and so have taken him for medical tests to ascertain if he had consumed alcohol," Pachundkar said.

A few minutes after the incident, an irate mob of around 100-150 people gathered at the spot and damaged the government bus. "Someone from the mob threw a few stones at the tanker, and in the process the front wind-shield of a nearby BEST bus was shattered. But the mob was soon brought in control," said the senior police inspector, adding that no one from the mob was arrested and no one in the bus got injured.

Pachundkar said that the mob was agitated at the fact that the street where the accident took place is narrow and has no speed-breaker or signal nearby. "According to them, this caused the accident," he said, adding, "The mob was demanding that the area near the school should be monitored so that such incidents do not take place." Rohit's body was taken to the Shatabdi Hospital for post-mortem.

Heading: Rupee-a-day scheme for girl students: Few have received the money - Indian Express
Content:
Not even her lawyers could fathom why Kannada actress Maria Monica Susairaj suddenly wanted to meet her fiancée Emile Jerome, the man she has accused of killing television production executive Neeraj Grover.

Susairaj, co-accused in the murder case along with Jerome, recently caught up with him within the premises of the Esplanade court for nearly half an hour. "She suddenly requested a meeting with Jerome. Following her request, an application was moved before the court, which granted her permission to meet Jerome on September 18," said

Susairaj's advocate Murthy Acharya.

Though Susairaj's lawyer G Kannur confirmed the meeting, he refused to divulge any information on the conversation between the two. Susairaj also spent some time with her family members who had come from Bangalore to meet her.

 On May 7, Susairaj and Jerome had allegedly stabbed Grover to death. They then had allegedly dismembered the body and burnt it at Manor in rural Thane district before returning to her suburban apartment to clean up, paint the walls and destroy all traces of the crime. 

 Susairaj has maintained from the beginning that it was Jerome who murdered Grover in a fit of rage at seeing him at her apartment. Her confession to the police also states that Jerome raped her after the crime. Two bail applications moved by her lawyers before the sessions court asked that she be accused only of destroying evidence, not of murder.

Last week, Susairaj's advocate Harshad Ponda also told the court that she was a "victim of circumstances" created by Jerome. The court has earlier rejected her bail plea observing that there was enough prima facie evidence to prove Susairaj's involvement in the murder.

Heading: India Post gets a new logo - Indian Express
Content:
Teachers were asked to submit students' list in March last year but banks didn't come to schools till a few months ago

It was a move meant to encourage more girl children to go to school by giving them a rupee for every day they attend. But plagued by delays and red-tape, the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation's (BMC) initiative has met with little success.

On the eve of the International Day for The Girl Child, it appears that the scheme — launched in June last year and inspired by similar initiatives in other states — is still to act as an adequate incentive to raising the numbers of girl children at school; they usually stay at home or do odd-jobs for the family.

There are 2,16,571 girl students in civic schools around the city, each of whom has a stake in the initiative. While the drop-out rate for students between grades I and V is 5 per cent, the figure for students between the Vth and VIIth grades is 8 per cent. However, the money for the first academic year (2007-2008) is only being disbursed now, after a series of delays.

"In March last year, all teachers were asked to submit a list of students but the people from the bank didn't come till a few months ago," said a teacher with a BMC school, who did not wish to be named. The bank, however, says that since this is the first time that such an initiative has been taken, it will take them a while to iron out some of the finer points.

"We are distributing the money for last year a little late, but that is because there were a number of small details to see to," said Municipal Corporation Bank Director Mahavir Bangar, who oversees education-related affairs. Also, as the money goes straight into the students' hands, they have to be present when the bank representatives visit their schools. But because they are given short notice, the students often end up missing their dues and have to wait for the next visit — which often takes months.

"Sometimes, they only give us the intimation a day earlier and by that time the students have left; so they have to wait till the next time the bank visits the school," pointed out another teacher from a different BMC school. "My daughter is in the IIIrd grade at a civic school but she has not got any of the money due to her so far," said A Arputhraj, a parent." This was despite the fact that that his wife had been to the school when the distribution was to occur, he added.

"We are planning to start giving schools an longer intimation. Sometimes we have a problem too, since we don't have the contact numbers of all the schools," Bangar informed.

Agreeing that there has been a problem of delays, BMC Education Officer A J Thakre said, "This time we are definitely working on how to distribute the money twice a year, at the end of each semester. There were delays last year, because we had difficulties coordinating with the bank. But we are definitely working to make the distribution better."

"We are going to start telling students who miss the distribution to come and claim the money from the bank if possible," said Bangar. He added that he would be submitting a report to the Board of Governors, giving directions for changes to be made in order to implement the scheme in a more effective manner.

Heading: Ayurveda admissions stalled in state - Indian Express
Content:
A move that's part of a larger makeover process in the Postal department, say sources

Taking its first step towards creating a new image, the Postal department unveiled its new logo on Tuesday, a move that is a part of a larger makeover process that is sweeping through the department. While the logo was unveiled in New Delhi on Tuesday morning by Minister of Communication and Information Technology A Raja and Jyotiraditya Scindia, it was simultaneously unveiled by chief postmasters generals in the state capitals and will be on letter-boxes and other post office insignia in the coming months.

In the past few months, the core processes have been overhauled in 50 post offices, a number which is set to rise to 450 by the end of the year. The interiors of the post offices have also undergone a change. The existing logo of India Post was designed in 1995 with the help of the Indian Institute of Technology, Bombay. The department says that the need for a change was felt because of the rapid transformation in the Indian economy and the need to create a newer and more energetic feel for India Post.

The earlier logo was characterised by straight lines, while the new one has a more fluid feel to it. The effect of the wings on the logo has remained unchanged so as to ensure some continuity. "We worked in collaboration with Ogilvy and Mather, and a number of staff- officers and others and designed it," said M S Bali, Chief Postmaster General, Maharashtra Circle.

The construct of the logo is meant to signify India Post carrying emotion across physical distances, and the colours are post office red and orange. Red symbolises the traditional association with post office, along with passion, power and commitment, while orange communicates hope, joy and happiness.

Heading: 3 get 3-yr RI for robbery, assault - Indian Express
Content:
Central Council of Indian Medicine approves only 100 of 200 post-graduate seats this year

Students seeking admissions in Ayurveda colleges in the state are in a quandary as only 100 out of 200 post graduate seats have been given approval by the Department of Ayurveda, Yoga and Naturopathy, Unani, Siddha and Homoeopathy (AYUSH) of the Central Council of Indian Medicine (CCIM), this year.

Earlier last week, over 100 students had protested at RA Podar Ayurved Medical College, Worli and had refused to avail the second round of admissions till all the 200 seats were given approval.

The first round of admissions took place in July after which 22 seats were vacant. The students also protested against the CCIM's decision to give approval to only 8 out of those 22 seats.

Dr Kishan Deshmukh, one of the students, said, "Last year, 240 seats were offered. This year only 200 were offered. Out of that 100 have been removed. This is unfair to the students."

Some of the main reasons cited by the CCIM are shortage of faculty and lack of infrastructure. Dr Jaya Prakash Narayan, vice president, Ayurveda, CCIM said, "According to CCIM norms, there should be 35 teachers for 50 students, a norm that is not being followed in Maharashtra and some other places in India. Only 102 out of 209 Ayurveda colleges in India have been given approvals. CCIM has not de-recognised them. However, the government of India has instructed not to admit students into these colleges."

He added that in Karnataka too, only 28 out of 51 colleges have been given approvals. Dr P Deshmukh, dean of Poddar College, acting director of Ayurveda, CCIM, Maharashtra, said, "Admissions have been stalled. As and when colleges that have not been given approvals get approvals, admissions will begin in those colleges."

"Only five colleges out of around 50 Ayurveda colleges in the state have been given approvals," he said.

Heading: Vikram outplays Sahil - Indian Express
Content:
A sessions court on Tuesday convicted three accused to three years rigorous imprisonment for robbery and assaulting.  Additional sessions Judge N P Dhote convicted Raju Hamal, Satyanarayan Jha and Sanjay Ingle for stealing Rs 12,000 and assaulting a person on August 9 last year.

On the day of the incident, complainant Ram Prasad Tiwari was attacked by three persons at Ghatkopar station and robbed of Rs 12,000. One of the accused, Hamal, had posed to be a commuter and had asked help from Tiwari. When Tiwari helped Hamal, two other accused assaulted Tiwari with a knife. After the police arrested the trio, they recovered Rs 26,000 from them and three mobile phones.         

All three accused have been in custody since the time of incident.

Heading: Gomes 'tricks for Holy Cross - Indian Express
Content:
Junior national champ downs second-seed Vora 3-0 in final

Top seed and under-19 National champion Vikram Malhotra was in rampaging form as he blanked second seed Sahil Vora to lift the men's singles title in the Minute Maid Pulpy Orange Squash Classic 2008, which concluded at the squash courts of Gold's Gym, Oshiwara on Tuesday.

Malhotra was in total control against Vora, his speed and power play brooking no opposition from the senior rival, who has been playing collegiate squash in the US. Malhotra prevailed 11-9, 11-7, 11-6 in just 35 minutes. Malhotra won Rs 7,500 for his victory, while Vora took home Rs 4,000.

The handicap doubles title was lifted by Kunwarpal Singh and Nitin Chauhan of Jindal, who defeated their clubmates Sunil Varma and Laxman Joshi 15-14, 15-13. The doubles winners gained Rs 8,000, with the runner-up pair winning Rs 4,000.

In the semi-finals, Malhotra weathered a tough first game before getting the better of former National champion Akhil Behl 12-10, 11-3, 11-5 , while Vora scored a 11-2, 11-6, 11-6 victory over teenager Mahesh Mangaonkar.

Heading: Amre to inaugurate under-22 trials, starting Wednesday - Indian Express
Content:
James Gomes scored a hat-trick to lead his team Holy Cross United from Kurla to a 3-0 victory over Dadar United in their opening game in the Mahindra Mumbai District Football Association (MDFA) Division I-C at the St Xavier's ground in Parel on Tuesday. The Dadar outfit have had a mixed season so far, but have lots of work on their hands with just one win up their sleeves.

Borovlian Stead Fast also made a winning start to their campaign in Division III this season, by overcoming Western Railway Protection Force (WRPF) 1-0. Abhishek Narkar scored the clincher for Borovlian in the very closely contested III-B encounter. WRPF had started their season with a 1-1 draw, and will be hoping to launch a comeback after their reversal today.

Meanwhile, in Division III-C, Strikers struck out PD Hinduja 1-0 with a strike from Chandras Panchal.

Heading: Ultimate game - Indian Express
Content:
Mumbai Ranji coach and former test cricketer Pravin Amre will inaugurate the 10th edition of the Shalini Bhalekar Memorial Cricket Tournament, which kicks off on Wednesday at the Ramesh Dadkar Maidan in Matunga. The tournament which also acts as the under-22 Mumbai Cricket Association (MCA) selection trial is organized by the Dadar Parsee Zoroastrian (DPZ) Cricket Club and will include four teams, Chandrakant Pandit XI, Lalchand Rajput XI, Hemant Waingankar XI and Dilip Vengsarkar XI this year. Prashant Naik, Omkar Gurav, Sushant Khaire and Siddharth Chitnis will lead the respective teams.

The squads

Chandrakant Pandit XI: Prashant Naik (capt), Bhavesh Patel (vc), Brijesh Puhari (wk), Rahul Lad, Abhishek Raut, Tejas Kalyankar, Sufiyan Rehmani, Sanket Chavan, Oninder Gill, Sagar Mule, Ravishankar Singh, Sagar Krishnan, Skanda Vora, Varun Thakkar.

Lalchand Rajput XI: Omkar Gurav (capt and wk), Shoaib Sheikh (vc), Swapnil Salvi, Pratik Amin, Anand Singh, Swapnil Kule, Hrishikesh Patkar, Vishal Dabholkar, Akshay Jambhekar, Rajeev Mehra, Harshal Nandu, Balkrishna Shirke, Harshal Desle, R Prabhu.

Hemant Waingankar XI: Sushant Khaire (capt), Sachin Wagh (vc),Viral Shah (wk), Pratap Kawdi, Bravesh Shetty, Gaurang Chavan, Ishant Mithbaonkar, Pushkaraj Chavan, Saaish Dhore, Dhaval Parab, Rahul Vengsarkar, Aatish Gavan, Pankaj Tiwari, Vivek Aarothe.

Dilip Vengsarkar XI: Siddarth Chitnis (capt), Sarvesh Damle (vc), Sagar Pawar, Karan More, Kunal Mathure, Swapnil Pradhan, Hrishikesh Shettye, Tejas Narvekar, Sagar Udeshi, R Paranjpe, Viral Patel, Gauda Narsimhan, Prathamesh Mahadik, Pratik Kar.

Heading: Cops raid Atif’s village, study his bank accounts - Indian Express
Content:
Mumbai team gear up for a national frisbee tournament

LITTLE did Gaurav
Kelaskar, 20, a cricket lover, know that he would like another game as much as cricket. These days, playing frisbee on Juhu beach has become a weekend ritual. Giving him company are his fellow-members of the Storm Chasers team.
If you think frisbee is just meant to be played at picnics, read on. While worldwide popularly known as Ultimate, this sport is gaining ground in India too; it has already become popular in Ahmedabad, Chennai and Bangalore, and finally caught the fancy of Mumbai's sport enthusiasts.
Every weekend, Mumbai team Storm Chasers, comprising seven youngsters, are seen diving, throwing and catching frisbee at Juhu beach. It is just three months, since Sanal Nair (26) formulated the team and they are all gung-ho about participating in the first biggest national frisbee tournament—Chennai Ultimate Frisbee tournament this November at Chennai's Marina beach. The event has 11 teams participating.
Nair, the captain of the team and an event manager at VGC sports, says, "Initially, I thought of just creating awareness of the game and started playing with neighbourhood friends but later on when I came to know about the tournament, we formally created a team and started practising on weekends in the mornings and evenings."
The rules being new and the lack of proper coaching have not deterred the spirit of these 20-something players, but what fascinates them is the duration and the vibrancy around the game. "One of our German friends who play the game taught us the basic rules and we also get guidance from the Delhi team that have a majority of foreigners. The rest we learn from the online videos. Hence we are excited to attend the tournament for better exposure," says Rupesh Desai (24). Anand Nanigadkar (24) who feels that this sport has the scope to become as popular as cricket, he s says, "There is no referee and the constant coordination during the game, strengthens the bond between the two teams and creates a healthy competition."
Initial funding is no problem for the team as there is not much investment. Nair says, "Unlike other games which requires a lot of equipment, this one only has a disc, but it has to be imported. We have now got few frisbees from the USA."
What are their plans for creating more awareness? Nair adds, "To start off, we plan to get more people in the team through word of mouth. We will soon be creating a website and will be designing our jerseys. After the tournament, we plan to promote it on the professional front by tying up with corporate companies."

Heading: If SIMI can be banned, why not Bajrang Dal, asks Mulayam - Indian Express
Content:
In an early morning joint operation on Tuesday, the Delhi Police and Uttar Pradesh Anti-Terror Squad carried out searches at various places in Azamgarh district to collect information about the suspected Delhi bombers who are still at large.

The Delhi Police had brought along one of the accused, Shaqib Nisar, who took the team to the homes of other people from the same area who the police say were part of alleged mastermind Atif Ameen's 14-member Indian Mujahideen module.

The police scrutinised local bank accounts belonging to Atif and his associates Saif and Arif, and collected details of transactions made by them. The areas where the search took place were cordoned off by the PAC and local police in a bid to avoid any untoward incident.

Additional DG (Law and Order) Brij Lal said: "The Delhi police had come to Azamgarh in search of the absconding accused. They coordinated with SSP, Azamgarh, before initiating the operation in Sanjarpur area and other places. The police team interrogated one of the wanted accused Asadullah's father Dr Javed Akhtar and five others: Abdullah, Saifullah, Azeem Ahmed, Dr Fakre Alam and Salam Khan."

The ADG also said they would seek custody of Ahmedabad blast accused Abu Bashar and those arrested for the Delhi blasts, if required.

DIG of the ATS Rajiv Krishna said: "Our team was already camping in Azamgarh to gather intelligence about the absconding accused. The ATS team scrutinized two bank accounts and a transaction of Rs 30,000 was found in Arif's account. In other accounts too, there were usual transactions in thousands."

PRO of Delhi police Rajan Bhagat said: "We have no update about any heavy transaction in accounts of any of the accused. The team that went to Azamgargh is still on the job."

The Delhi team, led by the SHO, Okhla, started searches in Sanjarpur around 6.30 am, and visited the homes of Shahdab alias Bhai, Asadullah Akhtar, Arif and Junaid. They collected some documents, including photo albums and CDs, from the houses of Arif and Asadullah. They failed to trace the house of another accused Shehzad alias Pappu, as they were not aware of his father's name and no local person volunteered to help.

DIG, Azamgarh, Vijay Kumar said nothing significant was recovered in the search, or from the bank accounts. The team left for Delhi in the evening, he said.

Heading: Day after CEO’s death, company is firm: it’s a ‘partial lockout’ - Indian Express
Content:
Samajwadi Party (SP) chief Mulayam Singh Yadav demanded a ban on Bajrang Dal on the lines of Students Islamic Movement of India (SIMI) on Tuesday.

"If an organisation like SIMI can be banned for terror activities, why not Bajrang Dal, which was involved in incidents of violence against Christians in Orissa and Karnataka? Whenever SIMI's name is mentioned, there is a hue and cry, then why not against Bajrang Dal?" Yadav said while addressing mediapersons.

Asked if the SP was still opposed to a ban on SIMI, Yadav said: "If the charges against SIMI are proved correct, it should be banned. During my regime, no terror incidents were linked to the SIMI. This fact was conveyed to the tribunal."

Yadav also rubbised charges levelled by Chief Minister Mayawati that terrorism had flourished in the state during the SP regime.

Asked about Azamgarh district having emerged as a "nursery" of terrorism, Yadav said: "A detailed probe will prove this suggestion wrong. There may be a handful of persons who were involved in terror activities but it is wrong to generalise."

The SP chief further said though the state was reeling under floods and power crisis, the farmers were being dispossessed of their land for projects like the Ganga Expressway. "The state machinery was indulging in extortion to fill the coffers of the BSP for the next Lok Sabha election," he said.

Describing Mayawati as the most insensitive chief minister, Yadav said the inadequate flood relief operations in the state were yet another example of Bahujan Samaj Party's apathy towards the people of the state.

Heading: ‘Rampaging mob came with a clear plan to kill’ - Indian Express
Content:
Family, friends and colleagues of Lalit Kishore Chaudhary — who was murdered on Monday by a group of enraged former workers of the Italian auto parts company he was heading in India — was cremated on Tuesday at the Nigambodh Ghat in Delhi.

With Chaudhary's life cut short at the hands of the former workers of the company that he was heading, his family is still in a state of shock. He is survived by wife Ratna and 16-year-old son Keshav.

According to Chaudhary's relatives, his wife has just gone silent.

"We still don't understand what has happened and how. What was the need for such barbarism? Ratna has not reacted to the news. Keshav had just been sitting next to his father's body since morning and was initially not letting anyone take it away," said Jaya, Chaudhary's cousin.

Keshav is a Class XI student of Modern School at Barakhamba Road.

Senior Personnel Executive of Graziano Transmissioni India Pvt Ltd, Avneesh Kumar, could not hold back his tears as he remembered his CEO and recounted the gruesome incident. "He was not only a good manager, but a great boss as well. When he was attacked, I was away and could not save him," he said.

Mahasingh Yadav, working with the engineering department, who joined the company only a month after Chaudhary, recounted that the growth made by the Italian company, which had more than doubled in the past decade, owed largely to the hard work of Chaudhary.

"He started the company in 1998. The company has grown so fast only due to Chaudhary's leadership. He was a father figure for us all. We had stayed together for nine months when we went to Italy for a training programme," said Singh.

Chaudhary's relatives said they were aware that some problems were going on relating to the factory and the workers, but no one had any idea things could take such a violent and terrible turn.

"He was young and had a long way to go. No one is able to talk about the incident at present," said Sunil Chaudhary, another cousin brother of the deceased.

When The Indian Express visited Chaudhary's A-103 residence in Noida, the family was not available for comment as relatives said that no one was in a position to talk to the media.

Heading: President wants better educational infrastructure - Indian Express
Content:
Lalit Kishore Chaudhary, IIT Kanpur alumnus and Graziano CEO, was killed on Monday after being attacked by a group of expelled workers on the company premises in Greater Noida. As the protesters took law in their own hands and attacked the company premises, they also attacked all the other employees of the company who were working in the factory at the time.

According to sources, 55 employees were injured and there were around 80 employees in the factory. Twenty-four employees were later admitted to Kailash Hospital in Greater Noida with skull injuries and bone fractures.

While six employees, including S Sarkar, Vice-President (Operations) of the company and second in command after Chaudhary, are admitted in the Intensive Care Unit, the condition of two of them is said to be critical. Sarkar was hit in the head with an iron object and has 25 stitches.

Sudhir Kumar, the guard on duty at the main entrance at the time of the incident, said: "They were over 200 people who wanted to get into the company premises. I stopped them because we did not have permission to allow them inside. Then somebody hit me on the head with a rod from behind, after which some six to seven people started beating me up and threw me in a ditch outside the company gate and I fainted after that." According to sources, after the workers allegedly went on a rampage in the company, Chaudhary had come down from his office, but was attacked by the mob.

Ashwani Kumar, the company driver, who came to rescue Chaudhary, was also beaten up mercilessly. He now lies in a critically injured state at Kailash Hospital. While Chaudhary lost his life, Kumar is still unconscious.

"They had all come well-planned with the intention to kill everyone inside the office. They just wanted to murder. I was hit with a very hard object on the back, head and legs. But I managed to escape and was brought to the hospital," said Saroj Kumar (38), who works with the company's Quality Assurance department.

Heading: Congress team meets Patil - Indian Express
Content:
As the country faces immense challenges in the field of education, President Pratibha Patil on Tuesday emphasised the need to "expand our educational infrastructure."

Delivering her address at a special convocation at Lucknow University (LU), the President said as per the National Knowledge Commission reports, the country needs around 1,500 universities to cope with the growing demand.

"As we grow it is important to keep in mind that in the quest of quantity, we do not compromise with quality," she said.

The President, who was the chief guest on the occasion, was conferred the honorary DLitt. The university also honoured two of its alumni, Professor R P Rastogi, former vice-chancellor of Banaras Hindu University with DSc and Professor Chandrashekhar Rath with DLitt.

As many as 28 students were awarded gold medals. Since 17 of these went to boys, the President asked the boys to work harder and strive for larger goals.

Expressing her dismay over the decline in the country's research facilities, Patil said there was a need for enhancing productivity on a sustainable basis. "Research facilities in our universities need to be reinforced. Universities must become centres of research and advance research responding to the requirements of the society and various economic sectors such as agriculture and industry," she said.

She said as a society transforms, the education system must also respond to the change. It is only then that it will be relevant. "We have a responsibility to impart proper education to a society comprising 54 crore youths," she said.

Earlier, Governor and university Chancellor T V Rajeswar said: "We are lagging behind from our target of universalisation of primary education especially with reference to the girl child. Violence against women, restriction on women's mobility and traditional division of work and roles continue to restrict a women's choice in education and career."

On the occasion, LU Vice-Chancellor A S Brar listed the achievements of the university.

Meanwhile, Islamic Centre of India (ICI), comprising local Muslim clerics, met President Pratibha Patil on Tuesday. They demanded the setting up of a commission to probe terror incidents during the last five years by a sitting judge of the Supreme Court.

A delegation of the ICI, led by Darul-ulum principal Maulana Saidul Haman Azmi Nadvi and ICI general secretary Maulana Khalid Rashid Firangi Mahali presented an eight-point charter of demand to Patil. The clerics said the President gave them a patient hearing and promised to consider their demands.

The other demands included an end to the arrest of innocent Muslims in terror cases, reservation for backward Muslims, implementation of the Srikrishna Commission report, a separate commission for Muslims within the Planning Commission and setting up of minority institutions like the Aligarh Muslim University in the country.

'Sectarian hatred has no place in society'

In the backdrop of the serial blasts in Delhi and incidents of communal violence in Karnataka and Orissa, the President said terrorism and sectarian hatred have no place in the society as it was against development.

While praising the efforts of police and security personnel who are working against terrorism, the President said it was the duty of every citizen of the country to cooperate in combating terrorism.

She also payed tributes to Inspector Mohan Chand Sharma of the Delhi police, who made the supreme sacrifice during the Jamia Nagar encounter on September 19.

Heading: Suspected Naxal arrested in Maanchi - Indian Express
Content:
The state unit of the Congress submitted a memorandum to President Pratibha Patil, alleging that in the 16-month rule of Chief Minister Mayawati, "transfer and posting of officials had become an industry".

The Congress delegation, led by state president Rita Bahuguna Joshi, told the President that there was hardly a district where the district magistrate and the superintendent of police had completed an year in office.

The party also alleged that not even 10 per cent of the funds released by the Centre to the state for development works were reaching the intended beneficiaries.

The two major poverty alleviation programmes — NREGA and the public distribution system — had become victims of corruption. Funds for afforestation in Bundelkhand had also been misappropriated, the team said.

It also accused the BSP government of favouring private builders and real estate companies at the cost of farmers.

President meets martyr's widow
Rasoolan Bibi, the widow of 1965 Indo-Pak war martyr Abdul Hamid, met President Pratibha Patil and submitted a memorandum, demanding special reservation for her family members in government jobs.

She also demanded the issuance of commemorative stamps on Hamid, development of his parental house as a memorial, a stadium in Bullapur village in Ghazipur district and an Army Recruitment Centre in Ghazipur.— ENS

Heading: Don’t block roads on the pretext of constructing public utilities: HC - Indian Express
Content:
In a joint operation, the Sonbhadra police and the Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) arrested a suspected Naxal from the Maanchi area on Tuesday.

In the ensuing gun battle, one of the armed miscreants was killed while others fled.

The deceased was identified as Mahendra Kharwar, who was carrying a bounty of Rs 5,000.

A self-loading rifle (SLR) and 80 cartridges were recovered from his possession.

The weapon was part of the 15 SLRs stolen by Naxals from a Provincial Armed Constabulary (PAC) camp in Ahiraura area of Mirzapur district in 2001.

Sonbhadra Superintendent of Police Ram Kumar said: "Following a tip-off, the team had laid a trap near Rampur village for a group of Naxals. The officers spotted the group walking towards them. As they were asked to stop, they opened fire."

Heading: Part-time private doctors to strengthen healthcare - Indian Express
Content:
The Lucknow Bench of the Allahabad High Court expressed its dissatisfaction over the state government's decision to block three roads near Ambedkar Memorial in Gomti Nagar for developing a parking area and a police barrack.

In a meeting held on September 6, the Lucknow Development Authority (LDA) had approved the proposal of changing the land use of the two roads adjacent to the memorial from "road transport" to "public utilities".

The Gomti Nagar Jankalyan Mahasamiti filed a Public Interest Litigation (PIL), challenging the blocking of these three roads.

In the last hearing on September 16, a High Court bench comprising Justice Pradeep Kant and Justice Vedpal had summoned the principal secretary (Housing) and LDA vice-chairman to the court.

On Tuesday, the two officials appeared before the court and explained that a parking area was planned on the two roads and a police barrack on the embankment road near Ambedkar Memorial.

The petitioner's counsel B K Singh told The Indian Express, "After hearing them, the bench said that the court was not satisfied with the plan of developing a parking area by blocking the roads."

"The bench also asked the officials to develop the parking area and the barrack anywhere, but not by closing the roads," added Singh.

Singh said LDA V-C gave an undertaking in the court that their plans will be reviewed to find alternative sites. The court gave them two weeks to review the plan and fixed the next hearing for October 14.

Heading: 4 months on, cops yet to start probe in fraud case - Indian Express
Content:
Alarmed by the shortage of doctors, particularly in rural areas, the state government has decided to strengthen medical services in districts by hiring private doctors on part-time basis.

Health Minister Anant Kumar confirmed that the health department has decided to seek the services of private experts and hospitals where government schemes are running.

In compliance with the decision, shifting of government experts from primary health centres and community health centres to district hospitals has begun. They will be replaced by private doctors.

The state has 1,946 vacancies for doctors in the provincial medical services, besides having a shortage of 600 experts in various branches of medicine, sources said.

Allahabad region alone has an alarming shortfall of 256 doctors, and needs a minimum of 100 doctors urgently. Kaushambi needs 56 doctors, Fatehpur and Pratapgarh 56 and 44 doctors respectively.

In the absence of doctors in rural areas, quacks have been ruling the roost despite the High Court directive to the government to keep a check on them.

Heading: More fake currency seized - Indian Express
Content:
Four months after Tera Cap Investment Consultant Pvt Ltd (TCIC) Managing Director Saurabh Mohan Shukla fled after duping investors of Rs 200 crore, the investigation into the case has not even begun. The Economic Offences Wing (EOW) of the UP police, which took up the case a month ago, has not even recorded the statement of the victims.

Neither the police nor the EOW has any clue about the whereabouts of Shukla, who fled on June 25, and his brother Tushar Mohan — another accused in the case. To justify the inaction on the part of the authorities, Inspector General of EOW J L Tripathi said: "As we do not have adequate resources like that of the district police, it takes time. We work in a very steady and in-depth manner, which demands more time."

"Once the matter has come to us, we will take our time and we cannot predict the required time for the investigations; five years, ten years or even more," said Tripathi.

Shriprakash Mishra, who had lodged the first FIR against Shukla, said, "First it was the local police that did not react to our complaints that Shukla was planning to flee and now it is EOW which has refused to perform."

Mishra had also complained to the range Inspector General A K Jain on June 21 that Shukla was planning to flee.

According to Jain, the police kept a watch on Shukla and also raided several places. But the exercise drew a blank. After this, the case was transferred to the EOW, which took two months.

During these two months, no investigation whatsoever took place. Circle Officer of Gomti Nagar Subhash Chandra Dubey blamed the delay on "government formalities".

Heading: Standard Chartered to pay Rs 50,000 as compensation for deficiency in services - Indian Express
Content:
Arrested gangster's printing unit raided in Patiala

The fake currency racket, unearthed by the Kharar police on Monday evening with the arrest of Rajwinder Singh, a notorious criminal of Patiala, unfolded further today.

More counterfeit currency notes, amounting to Rs 24,000, were recovered from Rajwinder on Tuesday.

With this, the total counterfeit currency seized went up to Rs 3.94 lakh as Rs 3.7 lakh in fake currency was recovered on Monday.

The police also raided the printing unit of Rajwinder at his first-floor accommodation in Ghuman Nagar, Patiala, and seized a coloured printer-cum-scanner, ink, paper and other material used to print the fake notes, said Dalbeer Singh, Station House Officer, Kharar.

He added that the counterfeit currency recovered today was in denomination of Rs 100 and printed on a single side.

"The gangster's instruments used to manufacture currency very similar to the real notes. It was difficult to tell a fake from a real note," said Singh.

Rajwinder, who is facing charges of dacoity, cheating, rioting and charges under the Arms Act and NDPS Act, was produced before Sub-Divisional Judicial Magistrate K K Goel today. He has been remanded in police custody till September 26.

Rajwinder will be further interrogated to identify the bookies, clients and other persons involved in the well-knit racket, which was running for over a decade, as confessed by the accused. Rajwinder's area of operation was Delhi and Punjab.

Heading: Two boys die in separate accidents - Indian Express
Content:
The District Consumer Disputes Redressal Forum has directed Standard Chartered Bank to pay Rs 50,000 as compensation for deficiency in services. The bank has also been directed to pay Rs 5500 as costs of litigation.

The complainant, Jagir Singh Saini, availed a mileage cash overdraft of Rs 80,000 against his Maruti car, which was intimated to him on telephone. Thereafter, the said facility was reviewed and reduced to Rs 65,000 for 12 months.

But, the complainant alleged, the bank later recalled the entire loan and directed Saini to pay Rs 58,938, failing which his car will be confiscated. The complainant gave two cheques of Rs 14,000 and Rs 40,979, both drawn on Bank of Rajasthan, Mohali. Both these cheques were cleared by the bank, which was depicted in the statement.

In May 2006, the collection manager, accompanied by three men, came to Saini's office to take possession of the vehicle. On enquiry, he was informed that Rs 54,979 was due against his aforesaid account. Only after repeated requests for the No Objection Certificate, he was issued a duplicate copy.

In its reply, the Standard Chartered Bank said the overdraft limit was revised to Rs 65,000 at the time of renewal (June 2005). It stated that the complainant failed to pay his regular dues as communicated to him vide statement of accounts. Hence, the overdraft facility was withdrawn and a notice was sent asking him to repay the outstanding dues.

The bank denied that any person, as alleged, was sent to meet the complainant. The bank also said that the original NOC was issued in September 2006, and hence, a duplicate NOC was issued. "This was as good as the original for all facts and purposes and for presenting before the RTA," stated the bank.

The forum observed: "The receipt of the duplicate NOC is not disputed but this document cannot serve the purpose as the registering authority requires the original NOC, which was never sent to the complainant. In 18 months, the complainant wrote so many letters to the bank, but they never responded. This by itself is deficiency in service on their part."

Heading: Bull’s death: MC employees’ strike enters fourth day - Indian Express
Content:
An eight-year-old boy was crushed to death by a tractor on Tuesday. Laadi was rushed to General Hospital, Sector 16, in Chandigarh, where doctors declared him brought dead. Police have registered a case against tractor driver Jaswinder Singh.

In another incident, an 11-year-old boy, who was admitted in the hospital after being hurt in a road accident ten days ago, succumbed to his injuries.

Anuj, a resident of Samgoli village had sustained severe injuries after being hit by a truck on September 12. He was admitted in GMCH, Chandigarh.

Heading: The future is here: a modern airport terminal - Indian Express
Content:
Employees of the Mohali Municipal Council continued their indefinite strike and dharna for the fourth consecutive day on Tuesday.

Bringing official work to a halt and restricting public entry to the MC Bhawan in Sector 68, the civic officials staged a massive protest rally to press for their demand — the cancellation of an FIR lodged against MC employees for "causing the death of a stray bull" on September 17.

They are also seeking the arrest of several residents of Lambian village, who allegedly assaulted the MC staffers and obstructed them from discharging their official duty.

Today, the MC employees reiterated their ultimatum to snap emergency public service like power and water supply besides cleanliness services if their demands were not met.

On the other hand, founder trustee of the Chandigarh chapter of People for Animals, Payal Sodhi, demanded the immediate arrest and suspension of all those MC employees and officials responsible for the bull's "murder". She also exhorted the authorities to find a per-manent solution to check cruelty to animals in Mohali.

Heading: Pending projects on NH-22: Govt, NHAI invite court’s wrath - Indian Express
Content:
With the land acquisition and joint venture formalities for the upcoming Chandigarh international airport over, the focus has now shifted to the terminal building. While the new terminal at Hyderabad has considerably raised the benchmark in terms of quality of facilities and infrastructure, the Chandigarh airport, too, promises to be a futuristic one.

A Murugesan, Regional Executive Director of the Airport Authority of India (AAI) assures: "The new airport and the facilities will befit Chandigarh's status as one of India's best planned cities."

It will be an S-shaped building — 135 metres in length and 100 metres in breadth — made of tempered glass. The space between the roof and the floor will vary between 13 and 16 m.

The material for the roof is being imported from South Africa, while three conveyor belts — two for the arrival section and one for the departure — are being procured from Italy.

"As of now we have only one belt, which is antiquated, in the arrival section. There is no belt in the departure section. With an increase in the quantum of traffic, you often find passengers waiting for around half and hour to get their luggage. This is the reason we have provided for two more belts in the arrival section at the new airport, apart for one in the departure area," said an official associated with the project.

The airport will have a new restaurant and eight concessional locations (space reserved for shops, eateries, coffee parlours and internet kiosks). Coffee chains, including Barista and Café Coffee Day, have already evinced interest in opening their outlets. "The final decision will be taken later. We will invite bids first," said a project officer.

This will be one of the very few airports in India to have boarding bridges. This means the passengers — even those boarding domestic flights — will not have to travel to the aircraft from the terminal in a bus. The entry to the aircraft will be directly linked via a bridge. In India, this facility is usually restricted to international flights.

"The building will be fully air-conditioned and we are installing an advanced building management system, which will automatically adjust the cooling and lighting, depending upon the situation. For example, if it is more crowded the intensity of air-conditioning will increase. Likewise, if the waiting lounge is vacant, some lights will automatically switch off. The project will also have imported revolving doors and advanced fire fighting and detection system," said another official.

The parking lot will have space for 500 vehicles and there will be a separate parking area for buses and taxis. Special disabled-friendly toilets are also being constructed. The airport complex will have a rainwater-harvesting plant and a sewerage treatment facility.

The structural work of the project is expected to be complete by February 2009.

While the region is now staking claim to almost half a dozen airports, till recently the aviation rules in India debarred a new airport within 150 km radius of an international airport. "The condition was relaxed in March this year. There is no ban now, but a formal approval has to be taken from a specially constituted committee. Every case is judged on individual merits. This explains why an airport is coming up in Noida despite its proximity to New Delhi. Also, this condition is not applicable anywhere internationally," said A Murugesan.

Heading: Kansal land grab: stay on ’99 FIR vacated - Indian Express
Content:
Defence Secy, Chief of Army Staff, Haryana Chief Secy, NHAI chairman summoned on October 1

The Punjab and Haryana High Court pulled up the State of Haryana, the Ministry of Defence and the National Highway Authority of India (NHAI) on Tuesday for its "lukewarm attitude" towards the completion of various pending projects on the National Highway-22. The court also reprimanded the Haryana government for not acquiring 54 acres of military land for the Pinjore-Kalka-Parwanoo road.

The court was hearing a public interest litigation (PIL), concerning the pending projects. Taking a strong note of the non-fulfilment of promises, the HC directed the Defence Secretary, the Chief of Army Staff, the Chief Secretary to the Government of Haryana and the NHAI Chairman to remain present in the court on October 1, the next date of hearing.

A Division Bench comprising Justice Uma Nath Singh and Justice Daya Chaudhary strongly criticised the conduct of Additional Advocate General (AAG) of Haryana M L Saggar for making an "irresponsible" statement in the court.

Senior advocate M L Sarin, amicus curiae in the case, demanded the process of acquiring 54 acres from the Ministry of Defence be sped up to make the Pinjore-Kalka-Parwanoo road function properly.

Sarin referred to a High Court order dated August 18 whereby it was stated that the 54 acres were required for the project, of which 14 acres were earmarked for widening of certain roads. An assurance in this regard was given in undertaking by the Assistant Solicitor General of India and the Deputy Advocate General, Haryana. The land, however, has not been acquired yet.

The court observed: "The authorities seem to be reluctant to accept the persuasive orders of this court and that is why this project is moving at a snail's pace. NH-22 is the only highway that bears the major traffic load bound for Shimla and other parts of Himachal Pradesh."

Advocate M L Sarin referred to letters dated June 12, 2007 and March 13, 2006, filed on behalf of the Ministry of Defence, which explained the procedures for processing the case for the land acquisition, instead of solving the problem.

"Such a stand appears to be contrary to the undertaking. This is not a project that can be delayed on account of red tape. Any unreasonable delay will further expose the officials to public attention and scrutiny," the Division Bench held.

The court also came down heavily on the AAG for his statement. "The Additional Advocate General, Haryana, makes an irresponsible statement without verification that only Rs 15 crore was deposited on May 2008 by the NHAI, which is strongly opposed by the senior counsel for the Authority, who said a further amount of Rs 16 crore had been deposited on September 19 in the account of the competent authority and the acquisition collector. The counsel submitted that the amount is available for disbursement," the order reads.

The Division Bench held: "We take a serious note of the statement. We are surprised that the assistance of the Advocate General, Haryana, is not available even in important matters like this one. This has also been brought to our notice that a flyover on the GT Road at Murthal and Samalkha, which should have been completed by now as per the statement given by the construction company, is not in place yet, which has made that area an accident-prone zone. In view of the breach of undertaking, and the lukewarm attitude of the authorities concerned, we think it expedient in the interest of justice to direct appearance of Defence Secretary, Chief of Army Staff, Chief Secretary to the Government of Haryana and Chairman, NHAI."

Heading: Big fish to bid adieu to Sukhna Lake - Indian Express
Content:
The Punjab and Haryana High Court has vacated the stay on proceedings in an FIR registered against former Punjab Governor's son Sonum Chhibber in connection with a nine-year-old land grab case. The stay order was issued on September 23, 2007.

Justice Sham Sunder was hearing a petition that sought quashing of the FIR against Chhibber.

In 1999, Puran Singh, a resident of Kansal village, had lodged a complaint with the then Financial Commissioner, Revenue (Punjab), alleging Sonum Chhibber, Randhir Sood and Darshan Singh (naib tehsildar, Majri) had committed forgery, cheating and criminal conspiracy to grab his land in the village. During investigation, the Joint Registrar of Majri found that the accused had forged Puran Singh's signatures on a general power of attorney, will and sale agreement, favouring Chhibber, son of former Punjab Governor General B K N Chibber (retd), and got them registered at the Majri tehsil office.

Subsequently, an FIR was registered with the Mohali police on October 13, 1999 against Chibber, Sood and Darshan Singh. Even after nearly a decade, the Mohali police have not initiated any action against the accused.

In 2005, on a petition filed by Puran Singh, the HC had directed the investigating agency to submit its final report with the magistrate concerned within two months. The police filed a cancellation report in a Kharar court, which refused to accept it and ordered re-investigation. The police, however, still failed to take any action.

In July 2007, the then Chief Justice of Punjab and Haryana High Court, while hearing a PIL concerning illegal grabbing of shamlat land (common land) in Kansal, allegedly by numerous bureaucrats and VIPs, summoned a status report on the FIR. The Punjab Police remained inactive even then.

Randhir Sood, one of the accused in the FIR, meanwhile, reached a compromise with Puran Singh and filed a petition for quashing of the FIR. Though the compromise was executed between the complainant and Sood, one of the accused who was merely a witness in the forged documents, an attempt was made to get the entire FIR quashed. Hearing the petition, Justice Sham Sunder took a serious note of the fact that the petitioner had concealed certain material facts in the plea and ordered to vacate the stay on proceedings in the 1999 FIR.

Heading: City colleges not to implement OBC quota - Indian Express
Content:
Fish more than 40 cm in size will be weeded out; decision follows recent fish mortality

Fish measuring more than 40 centimetres in length will no longer find a place in the Sukhna Lake. The decision was taken after dead fish surfaced in the lake a few days ago.

The recommendation to this effect was made by Director, Environment, and Deputy Conservator of Forests Ishwar Singh to the Fisheries department. The department has been asked to find ways to remove big fish from the lake.

Investigation by Dr M S Johal from the Department of Zoology, Panjab University, had blamed the fish mortality on deposition of silt on gills.

Johal's report said the bigger the fish the more was the need for food, due to which there was a tendency to go deeper into the silt. "This causes deposition of silt on the gills leading to asphyxiation," said the report, recommending a regular review of the aquatic life in the lake.

Sukhna draws a large number of migratory birds every year. More than 10,000 migratory birds had visited the lake last year. They mostly survive on fish.

"The fish that died were around 40 cm in length and weighed around 10 to 12 kgs. The migratory birds cannot pick up heavy fish. They need small fish to eat. We have recommended that the large fish be weeded out. The population of fish in the lake has increased extensively. This needs to be curbed keeping in view its size," says Ishwar Singh.

The ways and means to remove the fish will be devised by the Fisheries department. One of the recommendations is to lay a net that will trap the large fish but allow the smaller ones to pass. People who fish in the lake on weekends will be asked to catch only the big fish and throw the small ones back into the water.

A report by the Chandigarh Pollution Control Committee, meanwhile, ruled out lack of oxygen as a reason for the fish mortality. It found oxygen content of the water to be appropriate.

Heading: Industrial robot unveiled at CIIS - Indian Express
Content:
Colleges in Chandigarh will not be implementing the OBC quota, as announced by the Supreme Court recently.

The Administration that had been silent on the issue for long has finally taken a stand saying that if they implement the quota, it would only be out of concern for social responsibility and that too after they receive a grant from the Centre.

The colleges were asked by the government to submit information pertaining to the infrastructure, faculty etc required for implementing the quota, but there was no response from their side.

Talking to Newsline, a senior official in the UT Administration said: "We have sought legal opinion in this regard and it has been decided that the city colleges are not required to implement the OBC quota."

He added: "Implementing the 27 per cent quota in one go is not feasible, so different institutions have decided to implement the same in a phased manner. Also, if we implement the quota, it would be only out of concern for social responsibility."

Earlier, affiliated colleges were waiting for the Panjab University to implement the quota. However, with the university passing the buck, it was clear that it would be the Administration that would be responsible for getting the quota implemented in the colleges.

Interestingly, the Administration was not clear whether they would be implementing the quota even after a quarter of the academic session had passed.

The UT Standing Counsel, Anupam Gupta, meanwhile said: "The OBC quota is to be implemented under the Central Educational Institutions (Reservation in Admission) Act 2006, but both the university and its affiliated colleges are not covered under the Act. Keeping this in mind, the government has decided not to implement the quota."

The Panjab University, however, has decided to implement the quota in a phased manner for which it has demanded a sum of Rs 300 crore from the Centre. The university would be implementing 7 per cent quota this year followed by 7 per cent and 13 per cent respectively in the next two years.

Heading: Senate results: A few new faces among familiar ones - Indian Express
Content:
A first-of-its-kind industrial robot for training students in robotics and automation was unveiled at the Continental Institute for International Studies (CIIS) campus on Tuesday. The robot has been donated by a Canadian firm, Barrie Welding and Machine Industrial Automation, through the Georgian College in Canada to CIIS.  

Paul Stevens, Associate Director, International Projects, Georgian College, made public the KUKA KR 15/2. Lt Col (Retd) B S Sandhu, president of the CIIS Educational Society was also present during the unveiling ceremony. Col Sandhu expressed joy at the incorporation of the first industrial robot by any educational or industrial institute in the region.

He announced that students from neighbouring engineering colleges, deemed universities and Punjab Technical University would also be able to avail the opportunity of training with the KUKA robot whose incorporation is being claimed as a landmark step in the mechanical engineering domain.

The robot with a reach of 1570 mm and a payload capacity of 15 kg has many advantages in industrial processes, claimed Paul Stevens. 

While the introduction of the KUKA robot is being received with a great degree of excitement in the mechanical world, researchers all over the world are equally glad as the development spells an advanced research resource.

Heading: ‘Exchange of thoughts helps an individual grow in life’ - Indian Express
Content:
The result for the Panjab University Senate elections for the principal and lecturers' constituency, of affiliated colleges, was declared on Tuesday. Most of the present senators were re-elected though a few new faces have also emerged in the Senate.

The counting for the principal constituency of affiliated colleges started at about 9 am. Out of the 13 contestants in fray for the eight seats of the principal constituency, AC Vaid, principal of GGDSD College, Sector 32 and Tejinder Kaur Dhaliwal, principal of Guru Nanak College for Girls, Muktsar were the first to be declared elected. A total of 70 votes were polled in this constituency of which one was declared invalid.

The two new faces that have made it to senate this time are Janmit Singh, principal of Taravati Memorial Degree College, Bringali, Mukerian district of Hoshiarpur and RS Jhanji, principal of AS College, Khanna.

Others elected from the principal's constituency include BC Josan, principal of DAV College, Sector 10, Gurdip Kumar Sharma, principal of GGDSD College, Hariana (Hoshiarpur), HS Gosal, principal of Govind National College, Ludhiana and Satish Kumar Sharma, principal of Lajpat Rai DAV College, Jagraon, Ludhiana.

The declaration of the principal constituency results was followed by the counting for the lecturers' constituency of affiliated colleges that commenced at 11 am. In this constituency, many existing senators were re-elected though three new faces have also emerged this time. A total of 1990 votes were polled out of which 89 were declared invalid.

Mukesh Arora, a lecturer of SCD Government College, Ludhiana got the highest number of votes (307) in the lecturers' constituency. He has been a senator from the graduate constituency last year.

Another senator HS Dua, a lecturer in the Gujranwala Guru Nanak Khalsa College, Ludhiana was re-elected to the Senate after he got 244 votes. Dinesh Talwar was also re-elected with 240 votes.

The new faces elected to the Senate this time are Dalip Kumar, lecturer in Government College for Girls, Sector 42, IS Sandhu, lecturer, DAV College, Abhor and Kuldip Singh, lecturer in Guru Nanak National College Doraha, Ludhiana.

Other senators re-elected to the Senate include RPS Josh, a lecturer of the Government College for Girls, Sector 42 and PS Gill, lecturer in Sri Guru Gobind Singh College, Sector 26.
