The Senate elections this time were special as it saw a female candidate, Rupinder Chatha, a lecturer in the MCM DAV College for Women, Sector 36, contesting from the lecturers' constituency for the first time in the last 25 years but she could not make it to the Senate.

Heading: It’s a case of judicial terrorism: CBI - Indian Express
Content:
With more and more families deciding to go nuclear, children these days are lacking in their moral as well as social responsibilities. I believe that parents should acquaint their children about the society and their social responsibilities.

In the past, joint families were the order of the day, following which, children got an opportunity to interact with many family members.

This helped them open up and also taught them to share. These days, however, children have no exposure and fail to open up. Parents too do not have time for their children, which makes a child shy.

In our school, we hold regular parent-teacher meetings, where we guide parents on ways to interact with their children and make them meet more people. I believe that exchange of thoughts and opinions is very important as it helps an individual grow in life. We also have experts coming in regularly to hold sessions for both students and their parents. These are really helpful as many a times parents get to know their children better.

In the past, I have found that children actually open up to their parents during such occasions.

Going out and meeting new people is also important for adolescents as they need more exposure.

Heading: HC drops contempt charges against inspector - Indian Express
Content:
Cash at judge's door : Ravinder will be in CBI remand till Sept 27

Claiming that the offence committed by the accused involved in the cash-at-judge's-door case to be more serious than that of triggering the serial blasts in Delhi, the CBI special public prosecutor termed it a case of "judicial terrorism".

The prosecutor made the comment twice on Tuesday, while demanding an extended police remand of Ravinder Singh, a Delhi-based hotelier and co-accused in the case.

As defence counsel A S Chahal questioned if the CBI was trying to call Ravinder a terrorist, the prosecutor said: "We never said he is a terrorist but the case is more serious than terrorism." The court today sent Ravinder to CBI custody till September 27.

Citing grounds for sending Ravinder in CBI remand for ten days, the prosecutor said the accused had during interrogation, disclosed some names, in whose presence, he had handed over Rs 15 lakh in cash to Sanjeev Bansal, former Haryana Additional Advocate General, for delivering it to a judge in Chandigarh.

He said the CBI had to confront Ravinder with the people he had met before his surrender, adding that he would be taken to Delhi for the purpose.

On the other hand, the defence counsel said: "There is no incriminating evidence against Ravinder. The CBI has not listed any ground on which they are demanding the police remand."

The court, meanwhile, allowed the application of Ravinder's wife, Mohinder Kaur, seeking directions to the CBI to break the locks put on the second house owned by Ravinder in Delhi by 2 pm tomorrow.

When special CBI Judge Jagdeep Jain came out of his retiring room to pronounce the orders on the police remand, Chahal's junior counsel requested the court to defer the pronouncement by half an hour. The reason: Chahal had gone to the Punjab and Haryana High Court to meet Chief Justice Tirath Singh Thakur.

Mohinder Kaur has moved an application, requesting the Punjab and Haryana HC Chief Justice to request the Chief Justice of India to transfer the case to Delhi.

The Chief Justice reportedly told the defence counsel that it's only the Supreme Court that could transfer the case outside Punjab.

"The case has been described in different ways by the Press. The painful aspect is that the Punjab and Haryana Bar Association has become a party to the case with a view that the accused are guilty" reads the application.

Mohinder Kaur has further taken the plea that the orders passed in this case by various judges are being criticised by the Bar.

"Unfortunately, the names of certain Judges of the High Court are being dragged openly, showing that they are interfering in the investigation. The action of the Bar is a factor to be taken note of. The successive meetings of the General House are unprecedented in the history of the association. All these circumstances are prejudicing my husband's right to defence — he may not get justice from the courts in Punjab, Haryana or Chandigarh," reads the application.

Justice Nirmaljit Kaur questioned

A team of the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) from Delhi questioned Justice Nirmaljit Kaur, who was "wrongly" delivered Rs 15 lakh in cash on August 13, for 30 minutes at her residence on Monday night. According to sources, the agency will examine Justice Nirmal Yadav, for whom was money was allegedly meant for, after sustained custodial interrogation of Ravinder Singh.

CBI officers had met earlier Chief Justice Tirath Singh Thakur, requesting him to let them examine the two judges at their offices or other places of choice and not at their residences. Two days ago, the CBI was intimated that it had to examine them at their residences. "We went ahead with the examination of Justice Nirmaljit Kaur so that the investigation is not delayed," said a CBI officer.

The court is, meanwhile, likely to pronounce its order on the regular bail application of Sanjeev Bansal on Wednesday, if the defence counsel does not seek yet another adjournment.

Heading: Mohali man held for forging registration papers of vehicles - Indian Express
Content:
In a major sigh of relief for Inspector Ram Gopal, the Punjab and Haryana High Court today dropped contempt of court proceedings pending against him.

A Division Bench of the High Court had issued notices to Inspector Ram Gopal asking him to file reply as to why contempt proceedings should not be initiated against him.

The division bench had received a recommendation from Justice L N Mittal who had held that "prima facie a case of commission of contempt is made out against Ram Gopal".

Ram Gopal, who was suspended at that time and had earned the wrath of the High Court for illegally detaining few local residents in the Sector-3 police station, despite their release orders passed by the High Court. The case dates back to 2007, when Ram Gopal was the station house officer (SHO) of the Police Station in Sector 3, Chandigarh.

One Munish Aggarwal, a resident of Sector 40, had moved the High Court demanding release of his friends Narinder Kumar Singhal; Sulabh Singhal and Saurabh Singhal. The trio was illegally detained by Gopal and a sub-inspector (who has also been prima facie held guilty of contempt of court today).

On August 12, Aggarwal moved the High Court alleging that the trio had gone to the police station to register a complaint against one Ashok Kumar regarding a theft which had taken place in a showroom co-owned by Narender Kumar Singhal.

It was alleged that the trio had gone to register a complaint but were instead illegally detained by the SHO and the sub inspector.

The High Court had appointed a warrant officer to inquire into the issue. The warrant officer in his report stated that a mini truck (CH-01-G1-6038) was seen coming out of the police station at the gate with the three detainees along with a sub-inspector. Aggarwal at once identified the trio and told it to the warrant officer.

When Ram Gopal was inquired, he had submitted that the three were not illegally detained. The warrant officer had said that no entry was made in the daily diary report regarding the detention of the trio. Moreover, it was stated by the warrant officer that the FIR registered on the complaint of the trio was also ante-timed by the SHO.

Taking strong note of the misconduct, the High Court had held that prima facie a case of commission of contempt of court is made out against Ram Gopal. However, another division bench today discharged him of the contempt proceedings.

Heading: Forum issues non-bailable warrants to CitiFinancial officials - Indian Express
Content:
The Mohali police arrested Vipin Kumar, a city resident on charges of preparing forged sale letters of vehicles to get them wrongly registered on Tuesday.

SSP Jatinder Singh Aulakh said that acting on a tip-off, a special checkpost was laid in Phase VII, during which Kumar was intercepted in a car, which he had allegedly got registered from the Mohali District Trasnport Officer by forging the sale letter. During investigation, it was revealed that the vehicle was originally a 2006-model, but in the sale letter it was changed to 2007. A case under Sections 420, 465, 468, 471 and 120-B of the IPC has been lodged against Kumar.

Heading: Cockroach in bottle, Coca-Cola to dish out Rs 5,000 as compensation - Indian Express
Content:
Exercising its powers under Section 27 of the Consumer Protection Act, the District Consumer Forum today issued non-bailable warrants against CitiFinancial for not returning the unused cheques of a complainant, after the forum had asked the firm to pay compensation to the complainant in May.

The forum today sentenced the general manager of CitiFinancial and Assistant Manager Gurpal Singh to six-month imprisonment and imposed a fine of Rs 10,000. "If they fail to pay the fine, they will be further imprisoned for three months," it ruled.

Ordering the issuance of non-bailable warrants for arrest on October 24, the execution application was filed for the order dated May 15, in which CitiFinancial was directed to pay Rs 25,000 as compensation and to return the unused cheques to the complainant.

The forum had ordered that if the amount is not paid within 30 days, the company will be liable to pay the same along with penal interest at a rate of 12 per cent per annum from the date of filing of the complaint.

Heading: This doc is all eyes for wheeled beauties - Indian Express
Content:
After a cockroach was discovered in a bottle of Diet Coke by a city resident in May last year, today the district consumer grievances redressal forum directed Coca-Cola to pay Rs 5,000 as compensation for "selling a sub-standard and contaminated beverage to the complainant, which caused him mental tension and harassment". The company has also been directed to pay Rs 1500 as litigation cost.

The complainant, Vineet Kaura, a resident of Sector 21, stated that he had purchased the bottle from Parkash Medical Hall in Sector 21-C. "While hosting a small get-together, I and the guests saw a cockroach floating in the unopened bottle. After that, no drinks were served and everyone left early. Later, I showed the sealed bottle to the shopkeeper but he did not bother to record my complaint. If the guests or I had consumed the beverage, we would have definitely been exposed to the risk of a stomach disorder or disease."

In its reply, chairman-cum-managing director of Hindustan Coca- Cola Beverages, Ghaziabad, stated: "The complainant has failed to disclose the details of the manufacturer of the alleged bottle of Diet Coke nor has he disclosed the batch number, date and time of manufacture and details of the manufacturing unit. Further, the complainant may have tampered with the said bottle as all our soft drinks are manufactured according to the specifications of international standards."

The forum found that the complainant had attached a copy of the cash memo through which the bottle was purchased. "A notice was issued to the company in this respect but it did not reply, which shows that it has nothing to say against the allegations," observed the forum.

Other instances

Citing previous judgments, the forum said a thick plastic string was noticed in a bottle of Maaza by another complainant a few months ago.

Aashish Verma, who alleged that a bottle of Sprite purchased by him contained a dead housefly, was another complainant.

Neeraj Kumar filed a complaint alleging the presence of a white straw in a bottle of Limca.

Last year, Sarika Chadha had filed a complaint alleging that she found a foreign object in a bottle of Limca.

"These complaints show that the Coca-Cola Company is not ensuring up-to-standard cleanliness in their bottling plants. The mere fact that some of these complaints were dismissed on technical grounds seem to have encouraged the company not to bother with hygiene," said Jagroop Singh Mahal, president of the District Consumer Forum.

Heading: Nayagaon lensman ‘beaten to death’ - Indian Express
Content:
Till last count, Dr Rajan Chugh had given a new look to as many as 16 cars. The eye and laser specialist has now his eyes set on a seven-seater SUV. His hands are itching to totally transform it, as he has done with his previous machines. It's a passion that began in childhood and has only got stronger and better with time.

"It reflects my creativity and innovation, which I make ample use of," says Dr Chugh, taking us around his uniquely designed clinic, which he says is a treat to the eyes of his patients.

'Reversing' back to the wheels, the doctor says: "Impossible, is what I usually hear when I propose my ideas, but when we begin work it's a fabulous experience for all." He works closely with carpenters and mechanics to modify his cars to his taste.

He doesn't touch his cars for the first one year after buying them. And then begins the metamorphosis of the interiors, exteriors and also modifications in the engine for better performance. "I love the feel of the changes and of course, the surprised look on people's faces when these beauties hit the road." He spends at least around Rs 1 lakh on each car. The maximum he has spent so far on re-designing a car is Rs 2.5 lakh. He owns four cars at present.

One of his favourite makeovers is the Limousine he created out of a Contessa by cutting it into half, giving it a 28-inch fabrication, support and enlargement!

"This one was a designated picnic vehicle, equipped with a television, fridge, carpet area — The designs are all original, not from any magazine and it's a labour of love, one that gives me as much satisfaction as my profession, precisely why hours in the week are kept aside for car seva," says the doctor.

His latest love is a Skoda. He has painted it in portions, got fancy lights on the bumpers, alloy wheels, made the rear shorter for a better drive and given the interiors a designer touch. "I also studied the engine and changed some fitments and filters for more zip and instead of speakers have membranes fitted to save space and give it an aesthetic look," says Dr Chugh.

His Swift has a wide sunroof so that the children can be in touch with the sky, while the Mitsubishi Gallant is in line for a brand-new look! "And yes, I don't repeat designs between cars and they fetch quite a price when I sell them," winks the whiz.

Heading: P’kula rape: Youth sent to judicial custody for 14 days - Indian Express
Content:
Punjab, Chandigarh police take 7 hours to decide jurisdiction

A 22-year-old freelance photographer died after he was allegedly assaulted by unidentified assailants near Sector 25, Chandigarh, on Tuesday.

Ravi, a resident of Nayagaon, had gone for an assignment in Sector 41, Chandigarh, on Monday. "His parents said he returned home around 5 am on Tuesday, bleeding profusely," Investigating Officer (IO) Harmesh Kumar told Newsline.

Ravi was rushed to a private clinic, from where he was shifted to Government Multi Specialty Hospital in Sector 16, Chandigarh, where he succumbed to his injuries around 2 pm.

Meanwhile, it took almost seven hours after Ravi's death for the Punjab and Chandigarh police to decide on the jurisdiction of the case. Till 9 pm, the officers of Nayagaon and Chandigarh police reportedly kept on asking each other to act in the case. IO Kumar admitted that after a long confusion, the case was finally taken up by Nayagaon police. Only then was the statement of Ravi's parents recorded.

As the cause of death has not been established, inquest proceedings under Section 174 of the CrPC have been initiated. "The autopsy will be conducted on Wednesday. Further proceedings, as and if necessary, will be undertaken as per the autopsy report," added the IO.

Heading: Construction of underpass begins on Zirakpur-Parwanoo highway - Indian Express
Content:
A week after the gang rape of a girl on September 16, Aman Ahuja, the accused was today sent to 14 days judicial custody. The girl was abducted by one of her seniors along with four youths and taken to a village, where she was raped and tortured by them.

"We have questioned Aman but are still to make a breakthrough," said a police officer on condition of anonymity.

Aman is the son of an assistant district transport officer in the Haryana government and was arrested on Sunday. He is said to be one of the five persons involved in the gang rape and torture of the victim.

Sandeep Khirwar, superintendent of police, said investigations are on to nab the other accused.

Heading: Janata rehri market: Shopkeepers furious as booth allotment deferred once again - Indian Express
Content:
Work on the construction of an underpass on the Zirakpur- Parwanoo National Highway 22, started from today. With various diversions and service lanes to facilitate the smooth flow of traffic having been planned, the district traffic police have been requested by the National Highway Authority of India (NHAI) to depute its men on the highway.

The underpass is a part of the bigger Zirakpur- Parwanoo four laning project, taken up by the NHAI.

"The construction of the underpass that started from today is the first of the various structures that will come up under the Zirakpur- Parwanoo four laning project. The underpass will be 13.5 metre wide and 5.5 metre in height," said an official of Jaiprakash Associates, the company handling the project, on condition of anonymity.

He also said that service lanes have been constructed for the smooth flow of traffic.

"Traffic coming from Zirakpur will take the service lane to go towards Panchkula. As the service lane will allow two-way traffic, the ones coming from Panchkula too will use the same road. Those coming from Sector 20 towards Panchkula will have to move towards Zirakpur for a few metres and then take a u-turn to take the service road," he added.

"At an estimated cost of Rs 7.5 crore, the construction work will be completed in a year's time. Also, as there are around six underpasses in all, with four of them for vehicular traffic and two for pedestrians, the construction work will start when the service lanes for the same are complete," he said.

Talking to Newsline, Traffic Inspector Varinder Singh said: "We have received a letter from the NHAI regarding diversions on the highway. Though at present, we have only one traffic official, soon 10 to 15 of them will be deputed to ensure the smooth flow of traffic."

Heading: GMADA to use force to clear encroachment in Jhota Kut - Indian Express
Content:
The shopkeepers, who had lost their illegal kiosks at the Janata Rehri Market in a major fire last year, turned furious when the allotment of concrete booths to 369 eligible claimants was deferred once again on Tuesday.

The Greater Mohali Area Development Authority (GMADA) officials had decided to conduct the draw of lots for the allotments at PUDA Bhawan in Sector 62 in Mohali today. But one of the aggrieved shopkeepers — Waryam Singh — had moved a petition in the Punjab and Haryana High Court claiming that he was also eligible for a kiosk but was eliminated by the GMADA.

As per the High court order — which was pronounced by a division bench comprising Justice Uma Nath Singh and Justice Daya Chaudhary on September 19 — the GMADA was asked to consider the petitioner's claim immediately and dispose of it before the auction. The bench said the petitioner should be given a proper chance to prove his ownership claim.

In view of the court order, GMADA officials decided to put off the today's scheduled allotment and decided to look into the disputed case. But as soon as the news reached the anxious shopkeepers, they got agitated and went berserk .

Market association president Devinder Singh had a heated confrontation with GMADA Chief Administrator Vivek Partap Singh and the angry shopkeepers threatened to damage the PUDA Bhawan and turn their heat on GMADA officials.

Area Councillor Harman Preet Singh Prince, meanwhile, came to the spot and averted the possible clash between the agitated shopkeepers and GMADA officials.

On behalf of Punjab Cooperation Minister Capt Kanwaljit Singh, who was supposed to be the chief guest of the allotment process, Prince assured the shopkeepers that the draw will be held tomorrow at 9.30 am. He also added it was necessary to consider the disputed case first before going ahead with the allotment process.

"GMADA has decided to put off the allotment of single disputed booth until its ownership claim was decided by a court of law."

Heading: Mona Lisa, Smile! - Indian Express
Content:
Illegal occupants turn a deaf ear to court's order

Even after offering three days to voluntarily clear the encroachments at Jhota Kut Colony, several illegal occupants still remained at the colony, one of the oldest slums in Mohali.

Peeved over the betrayal of undertaking given by the illegal occupants to vacate the area within a day, the Greater Mohali Area Development Authority (GMADA) has decided to use "force" to vacate the remaining portion of the total 5 acre of prime land under encroachment in the colony.

"We are left with no other alternative but remove them forcibly as around 14-15 illegal occupants are still squatting on our land," GMADA Chief Administrator (CA) Vivek Partap Singh told Newsline on Tuesday evening.

Following the go-ahead call from the Punjab and Haryana High Court, the GMADA had on Saturday pulled down almost 100 concrete structures in the colony to vacate almost 5 acre of prime land worth several crores in the heart of city, which was under encroachment since 1980s.

The occupants of remaining 300 structures were given a day's time to move out to safely procure their wares.

After the encroachment is removed, the GMADA will carve out around 50 plots measuring 1 kanal and 16 marlas each, besides developing a park in continuity of the development of Sector 71 in the vacated land.

On September 17, a High Court division bench had "dismissed on merit" an Latter Patent Appeal (LPA) filed by R S Sandhu and others against the dispossession of the colony dwellers.

The land was acquired in 1970s for the development of Sector 71 but in 1980s, Jhota Kut Colony surfaced on it illegally.

However, when efforts were made to remove the encroachment, the colony dwellers took shelter of the court and procured stay on their dispossession, which continued till last year.

After the stay was vacated, the colony dwellers filed an LPA before the High Court, which finally ordered them to leave the land.

As per the GMADA plan, some portion of the vacated land will be used in the ongoing project of widening the roads passing through the area.

Heading: Cell of life - Indian Express
Content:
When it comes to cinema, this is (sadly) all that the leading lady in the picture is made & paid to do

Oh, that hurts, we squirmed in pain. "But it's true," filmmaker Onir stuck to his side of the argument...wait, was it an argument anymore? I mean, when we catch those picture-perfect size sub-zero Barbie dolls posing next to their Johnny Handsomes, the chance of any argument is lost! In that very instant, every word My Brother Nikhil's director Onir said made absolute, perfect sense. We are, well most of the times, the victims of our own doings. "Tell me, why do women change their surname after marriage? Why do they give up their identity and tag along with that of their husband's?" It's true, Indian men look at women as homemakers, their shadows, and it's this attitude that trickles down in cinema too. Scan through all the films you've seen, do you recall any powerful woman subject that's hit jackpot at the box office? We've had our Mother Indias and Mata Haris, flicks of desi Lara Crofts and Aaj ki Aurats. Somewhere, in between the spools of film rolls, there was some sense and sensibility in Arth, Mandi, Bazaar, Mirch Masala....(you know the rest), but if we pan to the present, the leading lady is still a lipstick and paint job in Indian Hindi cinema. Hindi because the regional cinema, especially Bengali is doing justice to the entire profession of filmmaking. Meanwhile, Bollywood is all about the boys and boy-bonding. As a result, we have the screen space hogged by men in slapstick comedies, in rock band regalia, doing bank robberies, etc etc. Heck, even scripts on homosexuality are biased towards gays! What do the women have? A box office blunder called Kudiyon Ka Hai Zamana (how can we ever re-create A Sex and the City!) and guy fantasy, Girlfriend.

"I won't lie when I say it's a predominantly male-dominated industry, a place where women are happy playing those lovey-dovey, sob-cry role and standing there like a piece of decoration. In fact, it's a reflection of how society at large treats women," says Onir, who's had his share of trouble while dealing with women-oriented scripts. "Men form a huge chunk of cinegoers, and they don't want to see a woman-oriented film. Even if we ignore this, I've always faced problem over signing up leading actresses for the same role because they are more interested in knowing which hero is opposite them. When it comes to the hero, he gets insecure if the woman's role is bigger than his!" Onir observes that women take up challenging or different roles only when their commercial value comes down. "It's a Catch 22 situation. It's the same world over, in almost every profession. Take tennis, like cinema, the men earn more. Why are the rates that male stars charge higher than what actresses demand?" Good point.

The reason for the inequality, or gender bias per se, is due to the social conditioning over centuries, adman Prahlad Kakar had once made a remark for one of our stories. "Women are made to believe that they are second best, that their place is in the house, that they have to be caretakers!" he said. This has seeped into mainstream cinema. We are keeping the parallel, experimental and art house aside, for they've tried to explore the Indian woman. But then, these guys never sell. It all boils down to viability, commercial saleabilty, market dynamics. "This is a country where people want to see their six-foot tall strapping, muscular handsome hero who can bash a 100 goons in one go. They want to see the damsel in distress," commented Jackie Shroff. In short it's chained Veeru and naach Basanti!

"Films centered around women! First, there are hardly any scripts, and even if there are, there are hardly any takers. If there is a taker, where do we get saleable, leading women actors from? Like the telly, it's all about the 'TRPs', the market dynamics are in place, and everyone will place their bet on a Khan or Roshan for none of the women actors have a market value," director Leena Yadav of Shabd gets candid. As a director, Reema Katgi feels everything depends on the actor. "Even if they say niche small films, the single woman still has to raise money on her own, still look for bankable male/female stars. You want to explore and experiment, but where do you get the finances from?" But she adds that writers are now scripting more well-rounded characters for women. "Let's put it this way, we are not playing just the wife and girlfriend, there's a little more, for instance Debbie's character in Rock On."

When it comes to actors like Gul Panag and Konkana Sen Sharma, they act wise and pick the best out of the lot. "Films are in any case not made that well," Konkana generalizes. As for Gul, all she does is make the most of it and "keep on the lookout for good parts, characters which bring strength to the film. After all, we all can't keep fighting an uphill battle," seems like she's already given up and in.

But we'd like to stick to what director Shona Urvashi has to say: "We are half of the planet and we are treated as if we are the niche market! They have been successful in creating this hype, but world has become a little intellectual. We need to assert more, have our own thought process, find our own individuality." Yeah, may be have an all-girl band that rocks on, a vacation to remember in Goa, just like Dil Chahta Hai, and a girl who dumps three boyfriends before she decides to settle. Yup, Bachne Ae Boys!

Heading: Maiden Innings - Indian Express
Content:
Stem cell therapy is a breakthrough in modern regenerative medicine

It's not a miracle cure, but certainly a technology that offers hope against many diseases. There are many unanswered questions, but stem cells are certainly a breakthrough in modern regenerative medicine. The last one year has seen many couples preserving cord blood stem cells for future disease management of not just the child, but also the siblings and other family members as well.

Nods Hridesh Jaiswal, centre head of of Life Cell International, a pioneer in the concept of umbilical cord blood stem cell banking in India, which has been in Chandigarh since 2005. Since the last one year, mentions Jaiswal, there have been various awareness campaigns regarding the technology, with doctors, counsellors educating to-be parents of various benefits. "We have seen a spurt in the number of people going in for saving the cord blood cells for future use,'' adds Jaiswal.

According to doctors of Life Cell, stem cells have the unique ability to differentiate into a variety of cells and their main potential lies in the ability to generate cells and tissues. Stem cells can also be directed to differentiate into specific cell types, thereby offering possibility of a renewable source of replacement cells and tissues. Across the world, stem cell transplants have been used since the '60s to treat a variety of blood diseases such as leukaemia, inherited immune system disorders, plasma cell disorders and other blood-related disorders. Possibilities, adds Dr R S Bedi, exist in treating spinal cord injury, stroke, burns, heart disease, diabetes, osteoarthritis and rheumatoid arthritis, Parkinson's and Alzheimer's disease. "The success is ongoing and its benefits are mostly for acquired diseases,'' explains Dr Bedi, who confirms that with time, research will yield better results.

Dr Mahesh Hirandani feels the technology should not be presented as a miracle cure for the present and future. "Companies must ensure that people get a clear and true picture of the disease which can be managed with this, the role of genetics, what it cannot cure et al,'' says the pediatrician.

For new and proud parents Natasha and Hitesh Roy, saving cord blood stem cells for their daughter was not a tough decision. The two had read up on the option and also discussed it with their pediatrician, who gave them an honest view. "I know that right now the technology is developing and we are not sure how many disease it will protect the child against, it's all new, but we are sure that technology will only get better and we are going to benefit from this amazing breakthrough,'' smiles Natasha.

Cord blood stem cells are not just for the child but can be of use to the entire family, with siblings having a 25 per cent chance of being a suitable match. Banking umbilical cord blood stem cells is a life-saving alternate to bone marrow transplants. "The procedure is simple, at the time of the child's birth, the cord blood is collected and taken to the cord blood stem cell bank for testing and processing to harvest stem cells. The stem cells are preserved for potential medical use in the future. Whenever the stem cells are required for therapy they can approach the bank,'' explains Jaiswal. "It's a promising technology and in my opinion, more useful for community banking and we need to wait and watch for the technology to grow,'' says Dr Umesh Jindal, an infertility expert.

Heading: Presidential form would be catastrophic for India - Indian Express
Content:
After twirling on her toes last season, actor Sandhya Mridul has moved on to a lethal combination - cricket and dance!

What are the country's two loves? Cricket and films, we can hear you chorus. Making the most of that lethal, if we may say so, combination is Colors channel with its new weekend show 'Ek Khiladi Ek Hasina'. Pegged as India's "first cricket format" show, 'Ek Khiladi Ek Hasina' will see present day cricketing chaps team up with some of television's prettiest ladies and get them together to shake a leg on the floor. And while Sushmita Sen and Wasim Akram will judge the two, stepping into the anchor's stilettos is last season's 'dancing queen' Sandhya Mridul.

The decision to be a part of the show admits the actor was "quick and fast". "Like every Indian I am passionate about cricket and dance too. I was fond of dancing but never really thought I could perform a sequence until Jhalak Dikhla Jaa happened," tells Mridul who has been twirling on her toes ever since. "I have been performing all over the world and loving every bit of it," adds the actor who admits to "discovering" the dancer in her finally! But if you have your expectations high on seeing Mridul sizzle on stage, she's lets out her role. "Actually there won't be much of me dancing, only a bit. I am playing host for once," she laughs admitting to sharing a "wonderful rapport" with the cricketers. Remember she's hosted Extraa Innings on Set Max sometime back. As far as all the cricketing action on this channel goes, there are quite a few dishy players lined up. There's Sreesanth teaming up with Surveen Chawla, Harbhajan Singh with Mona Singh, Irfan Pathan with Ashima Bhalla, Dinesh Karthik with Nigar Khan, Nikhil Chopra with Barkha Bisht and Vinod Kambli with Shama Sikander.

"Who wouldn't love to see cricketers dance? It's an amazing format really," spoke Sandhya who by the way isn't just dancing for now. "I am an actor first and I do have a few films lined up," she tells. Among them is Arshad Warsi's home production and another by Anubhav Sinha that stars Shabana Azmi and Anupam Kher. And while she would love to do an item number, Sandhya is looking to sign up only for "good cinema". "I am not so fussy about the size of the role but it should give me scope to act. Like I loved Farhan's role in Rock On," Sandhya says. Watch out for her!

Heading: Somnath for setting up special tribunal to deal with defection - Indian Express
Content:
Lok Sabha Speaker Somnath Chatterjee today rejected the suggestion for a Presidential form of government for India in the light of several lacunae in the present-day Parliamentary democracy.

Addressing a press conference here today at the end of the 73rd conference of Presiding Officers of Legislative Bodies in India, Chatterjee said the Presidential form of government would be,"catastrophic for the country''.

"There may be limitations in the present form of government and all sorts of questionable mergers and defections, but the Presidential form of government is not suitable for India," he said, while replying to a question whether the Presidential form of government was better suited for India.

With regard to cases of corruption in judiciary, the Speaker said every section of society was amenable to corruption.

As for the role of the media in the functioning of the democracy, Chatterjee said , "Criticise what is wrong, but do also let us know all the good things and provisions in democracy." He said there were no plans to curb telecast of the Lok Sabha proceedings."People should know what is happening in their House,'' he said.

'I have not receipved any resignation letter from Kuldeep'

Somnath Chatterjee categorically denied having received any letter of resignation from Congress MP from Bhiwani, Kuldeep Bishnoi. Bishnoi had time and again claimed that he had sent his resignation letter to the Lok Sabha Speaker, but had not been able to meet him. "Not a single resignation letter was received by me,'' Chatterji said. He said he had also not received any letter for disqualification of Shiromani Akali Dal (Badal) MP S S Libra for for defying the party whip during the recent Trust Vote in Parliament.

Heading: ‘MLAs welcome to undergo training at Lok Sabha’ - Indian Express
Content:
To effectively curb rampant horse-trading and alleged buying-off of MLAs and MPs, Lok Sabha Speaker Somnath Chatterjee suggested setting-up of a special tribunal to deal with matters of defection. The Speaker said that if a special tribunal did not seem viable, the Election Commission (EC) could deal with such a matter.

Participating in a symposium on the topic 'Anti-Defection Law-Need for review', organised by the Haryana Vidhan Sabha as part of the 73rd Conference of Presiding Officers of Legislative Bodies in India, here today, Somnath Chatterjee said that over the years, the exercise of power by presiding officers had caused some controversies owing to their political allegiance.

"This considerably affects the dignity of the high office of the presiding officer. In my view, it is desirable, or rather necessary, that the jurisdiction and authority to deal with matters of defection as provided in the Tenth Schedule need not continue to be exercised by the presiding officers."

"The power should be conferred on some other authority, such as a special tribunal comprised of people well versed in law or an authority like the Election Commission,'' added Chatterjee.

Coming down heavily on the shifting stance of politicians, Chatterjee said political defection among legislators was a matter of great concern. "It affects the stability of the governments and is destructive for the true principles of Parliamentary democracy," he said "With due respect to the judiciary", he said it would be "fit and proper" if presiding officers are not under judicial scrutiny as such scrutiny gives way to avoidable tension between the two constitutional bodies.

Deputy Speaker of the Lok Sabha, Charanjit Singh Atwal, said it was unfortunate that some of the decisions of the speakers had been challenged in the courts of law. He also suggested periodic review of the Anti-Defection Act.

Haryana Chief Minister Bhupinder Singh Hooda suggested more teeth to the Anti-Defection law "to meet the requirements of the changing scenario.'' He said the law did not give any authoritative judicial guidance about the true interpretation of provisions relating to mergers and the correct meanings of the expressions — Legislature party, political party and 'original political party'.

Hooda also called for a discussion on the issue of 'party whip', due to which voting against the will of the party was considered as defection. "This curtails the right to speech and expression of an individual," he said. To curb defection effectively, Hooda said there should be suo-moto initiation of action by the speaker against the erring member.

Haryana Vidhan Sabha Speaker Dr Raghuvir Singh Kadian also called for a need to review the law and said the position of a member expelled by the party too required to be reviewed.

Goa Speaker Pratap Singh Rane suggested that if a member defects, he should not be allowed to contest for at least five years.

Speakers from Assam, Bihar, Nagaland, Meghalaya and Chattisgarh and MLAs from Haryana, including Karan Singh Dalal, Radhey Shyam and D K Bansal also participated in the discussion held on the last day of the conference.

Heading: Desk for International Affairs established at HAU - Indian Express
Content:
Lok Sabha Speaker Somnath Chatterjee today said that newly elected members of the Legislative Assemblies were welcome to undergo a training course at the Lok Sabha.

The Speaker was responding to a suggestion made by Haryana MLA Karan Singh Dalal during a symposium on 'Anti-Defection Law-Need for Review' here today. Dalal said that there was a need to apprise the elected representatives of Legislative and Parliamentary procedures and practices, besides constitutional and legal aspects.

Dalal had suggested the setting up of an institution to conduct orientation courses for elected MPs and MLAs to which Chatterjee said that the Lok Sabha already had such a facility and he would welcome if the speakers of Legislative Assemblies wrote to him to impart such training to their MLAs.

Heading: 38 cases of power theft detected - Indian Express
Content:
The Chaudhary Charan Singh Haryana Agricultural University (CCS HAU) has established a Desk for International Affairs at its Directorate of Human Resource Management (DHRM).

Disclosing this here today, HAU Registrar Dr R S Dalal said that establishment of this desk would facilitate greater exchange of students and staff from CCS HAU with foreign universities. Dr R B Srivastava, Associate Director, Human Resource Management and Incharge of the Patent Cell of the university, has been entrusted with the responsibility of heading the desk .

It may be mentioned that recently, the university has signed MOUs with several foreign universities, including Michigan University and Maryland State University of USA and Weningen University of Netherlands, and the process of signing MOUs with the research institutes and universities of Germany, France and Netherlands are in the pipeline. The Registrar said that the need for the establishment of this cell was being felt in view of the number of intents for collaboration being received from foreign universities.

According to Dr R K Kashyap, Director, Human Resource Management, two batches of students of the final year of Bachelor of Veterinary Sciences (B.V.Sc) have already completed their study tours with the universities of USA. He said the desk would help make travel and boarding arrangements for those going on exchange programmes.

Heading: I’m not in race for PM’s post: Rahul - Indian Express
Content: The Uttar Haryana Bijli Vitran Nigam has detected 38 cases of power theft in Jhajjar district during the first fortnight of the current month and imposed penalty of Rs 3.94 lakh on the erring consumers, out of which Rs 2.45 lakh have been recovered. Giving details, a spokesman said here today that the teams constituted by the nigam conducted surprise checking of 3520 consumer premises in Jhajjar, Bahadurgarh and Beri operation divisions . Most of the consumers found stealing power had tampered with their metres. The connections of the erring consumers were disconnected on the spot, he said.

Heading: ...visits Hussainiwala - Indian Express
Content:
Amidst the slogans of 'Rahul Gandhi zindabad' and hordes of people jostling to have a glimpse of him or touch him, MP and All India Congress Committee General Secretary Rahul Gandhi had his feet firmly on the ground.

Rahul said he was not in race for Prime Minister's post. "This is all media creation. There is nothing like that," Rahul today told The Indian Express in Jaitu, while reacting to the news reports that said he was not averse to becoming the PM.

Under tight security arrangements -- even leader of opposition in Punjab Rajinder Kaur Bhattal was frisked before being allowed inside and SPG tried to stop Indian Youth Congress president Ashok Tanwar from entering the venue -- Rahul today visited the historical place in Jaitu, where Pandit Jawahar Lal Nehru was kept after he courted arrest while protesting against the British government's interference in an Akhand Path in 1923.

Rahul spent about 10 minutes inside the historical place, the surroundings of which, the residents told, were a dumping ground, and the waste was removed a couple of days ago. The stench bore testimony to their claims.

As mediapersons were kept at a distance from the place, they raised slogans and even threatened to boycott the event, but then decided against it.

Earlier, Rahul Gandhi started his day from Bathinda with listening to the grievances of "victims of vendetta politics". The "victims" said Rahul had assured to look into their cases.

He then went to a drug de-addiction centre in Bathinda before starting his road show. His convoy headed towards Behman Deewana village, where Rahul looked into the enrolment drive for the youth Congress. From there, he went to Gidderbaha and had a brief interaction with the people waiting for him.

On his way to Jaitu, Rahul halted at Guru Harkishan Public School, Kot Bhai, and met the students and the staff.

Tight security

Throughout his journey, Rahul was accorded a thunderous welcome. His security guards had a tough time at a number of places, controlling the people who wanted to shake hands with Rahul even while he was on the move. Congress leaders, including MLAs, were seen complaining that they were not being allowed to meet Rahul.

Moga MLA Joginder Pal Jain was allowed entry only after Kotkapura MLA Ripjit Brar came out. Jain had to wait for at least 15 minutes as police turned down his repeated requests. Police claimed that they had an approved list of only seven people and Jain was not among them. "I was insulted at least five times," said Ripjit, while taking along Jain inside.

Heading: State to clear Rs 37-crore  arrears of cane growers - Indian Express
Content:
MP Rahul Gandhi today paid obeisance at the Hussainiwala memorial built in the memory of freedom fighters, Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev and Rajguru.

Rahul reached Hussainiwala in the afternoon from Jaitu. Guruharsahai MLA Rana Gurmeet Singh Sodhi submitted a memorandum to Rahul Gandhi, in which he demanded opening of Hussainiwala border and setting up of big industries for the development of the area.

Sodhi is said to be eyeing ticket from Ferozepur Lok Sabha constituency. The other likely contender is senior Congress leader Jagmeet Singh Brar. "I have submitted the memorandum to Rahul and demanded that the area should be properly represented to usher in an era of development," said Sodhi.

From Hussainiwala, Rahul Gandhi went to Dev Samaj College for Women, Ferozepur, to attend a seminar on female foeticide. On the occasion, Rahul answered different queries of students. Terming female foeticide as a curse, Rahul dwelt upon the need to spread awareness.

Answering a query of a student as to why he was not getting married, Rahul said he was busy serving the country, and was not getting time for it.

To another query on corruption, Rahul said entry of youngsters in politics could go a long way in checking the menace. He termed infrastructure, democratic set-up and education as the three mainstays for leading country on the path of progress.

Rally not allowed

Rana Sodhi said a rally was planned at Hussainiwala, but the administration did not give the permission. When contacted, Ferozepur DC Megh Raj said the only function that was allowed at Hussainiwala was on March 23 every year in the memory of Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev and Rajguru. "We cannot allow any other function. Sodhi has violated the law by putting chairs at the venue without taking permission," DC said.

Heading: Punjab gets award for water and sanitation facilities - Indian Express
Content:
Punjab has decided to clear the Rs 37-crore dues of sugarcane growers before the start of the crushing season in November.

"We have estimated the arrears of the 2007-08 crushing season to be around Rs 37 crore and are trying to generate resources to pay them off," Punjab Cooperation Minister Capt Kanwaljit Singh says.

The department is mooting various proposals to mobilise resources, including raising a bank loan. So far, two out of the nine sugar mills under the Federation of Cooperative Sugar Mills Ltd (Sugarfed), have paid farmers from their own resources. The others are yet to clear the dues ranging between Rs 2 crore and Rs 7 crore, Sugarfed Chairman Pritam Singh Kaunta said.

Witnessing a slump due to crashing of prices worldwide, the sugar industry has incurred huge arrears with the outstanding dues of sugar mills of Uttar Pradesh, the largest sugar-producing state, standing at Rs 600 crore this year. Many cane growers are already moving towards the more secure wheat-paddy cycle, with the area under sugarcane in Punjab this year going down from 1.5 lakh hectares to 1.1 lakh hectares.

Besides clearing the dues, it is important to pre-empt any move by cane growers to opt for private sugar mills.

So far, six cooperative sugar mills have closed down in Punjab, forcing the government to come up with bail-out packages. "We are looking at not just sugar production now. The capacity of the mills will be augmented, and major emphasis will be laid on setting up co-generation power plants of 8-10 MWs in each mill," says Kaunta, adding that there are also hopes of revival of sugar prices, and things will start looking up by the end of this year.

Heading: New Zealand consultants for state road contracts - Indian Express
Content:
Punjab was adjudged the best state in the sphere of water and sanitation in the country at the IBN7 Diamond States Awards ceremony held in New Delhi last evening.

The award was presented by former President Dr APJ Abdul Kalam to Punjab's Information and Public Relations and Water Supply and Sanitation Minister Bikram Singh Majithia.

The awards were given as recognition of the human and social development and evaluation of the standards of governance in the states.

Access to drinking water and toilet facilities were the parameters considered by the IBN Network while evaluating the performance of different states in the category of water and sanitation.

Majithia said the state government was fully committed to provide potable water and quality sanitation facilities, especially in rural areas and urban slums.

He said the state had taken initiatives to provide quality drinking water using reverse osmosis technology in collaboration with Naandi Foundation, an NGO in Muktsar district, which was now being extended to other villages of Malwa. Work on the Rs 1,250-crore World Bank-aided water supply and sanitation project has also been expedited, he added. He said the state's infrastructural shortcomings were being addressed on priority with special focus on health and education.

President of the Shiromani Akali Dal and MP Sukhbir Singh Badal said, "This award was confirmation of the will of the SAD-BJP to provide people basic necessities."

The awardees were selected through a multi-pronged approach, involving independent validation partner, international consultancy PricewaterhouseCoopers that analysed official sources of information and did extensive research based on parameters set up by Network18 editorial board, Outlook editorial board and a jury of eminent citizens of India.

Heading: Markfed to ensure adequate DAP supply - Indian Express
Content:
The Punjab government would soon engage the services of Opus International Consultants Limited (OPUS) of New Zealand to devise a strategy for implementation of output and performance-based road contracts (OPRC) to improve and maintain a portion of its road network in the southern districts of the state through the Punjab Roads and Bridges Development Board (PRBDB).

This assurance was given by Punjab Chief Minister Parkash Singh Badal to OPUS Technical Director Tony Porter, who called on him this morning.

While briefing the Chief Minister, PWD (B&R) Minister Parminder Singh Dhindsa said the works, under phase II of the Rs 1,500-crore World Bank-funded Punjab State Road Sector Project (PSRSP), would be now based on the output of these services likely to be commenced by the middle of next year. The Chief Minister asked the team leader of OPUS Robert Fergerstrom to undertake an extensive tour of Punjab to have first-hand information about the existing roads and suggest constructive measures to improve their quality.

Heading: MC employees’ stir on; Sidhu assures none will be displaced - Indian Express
Content:
The Punjab government has declared Markfed as the nodal agency for supply of DAP through cooperative societies for the 2008-09 rabi season. Out of the total requirement of 3.1 lakh MTs of cooperative sector, 2.6 lakh MTs of DAP will be supplied by Markfed.

GS Grewal, MD Markfed, said farmers who have given their requirements through the societies would get DAP in time for the sowing of wheat as the supplies were expected by October-end.

At present, 1.17 lakh MT of DAP is available with the societies and Markfed is receiving regular supplies from various ports. The stocks are being delivered directly at the doorstep of farmers.

Reacting to the news appeared in a section of press regarding supply of DAP to potato growers, the Markfed MD clarified that the potato-growing districts have been given priority. In the potato-growing belt of Jalandhar and Kapurthala, five more rakes of DAP would arrive soon, he added.

Heading: State to rationalise taxes on cotton - Indian Express
Content:
The work in Amritsar Municipal Corporation remained suspended today and the sanitation work came to a halt as the employees continued to hold protest against the solid waste management project.

Heaps of garbage could be seen in every nook and corner of the city. Various associations in the MC have charged Mayor Shawet Malik with privatising the work of picking up the debris and appointing a private company for it. The protesters feared they would lose their jobs if the project was implemented.

Addressing mediapersons today, BJP Lok Sabha MP Navjot Singh Sidhu clarified that no MC employee would be displaced after the implementation of the project.

"I give my word for it. If anything of this sort happens, we will all resign," he said.

He said efforts would be made to convince the protesters. He claimed other municipal corporations of Punjab have shown interest in the project seeing its viability.

Newly-appointed chairman of Punjab Water Supply and Sewerage Board Baldev Raj Chawla said only 59 per cent of urban population of Punjab has the sewerage system and 86 per cent has facility of water supply.

He said efforts would be made to provide 100 per cent water supply and sewerage disposal systems to the public. He added Rs 1,000 crore have already been sanctioned for these projects.

Heading: Reality check for PAU - Indian Express
Content:
To stop the sale of homegrown cotton outside Punjab, the state government is set to rationalise the taxes levied by the Mandi Board. The board levies 12.5 per cent taxes on every quintal of cotton sold in Punjab, while the neighbouring states of Rajasthan and Haryana charge 7.5 per cent.

Therefore for the farmers, arhtiyas and even cotton buyers, it is more lucrative to sell and buy the crop in the neighbouring states. As per the break-up, a cotton buyer in Punjab has to pay 2 per cent as market fee, 2 per cent as rural development fund, 2.5 per cent as arhtiya fees, 2 per cent as Punjab infrastructure development fund and 4 per cent as VAT. Bhagwan Bansal, president of the Punjab Cotton Factories and Ginners' Association, says, "This year, Punjab will produce about 25 lakh cotton bales, out of which 10 lakh bales will be sold outside the state. Farmers, especially those living in Abohar, have no problem travelling a few kilometres down to Rajasthan to sell their crop. This results into loss to the state exchequer."

Bansal adds, "Moreover, the state government has given tax exemption to spinning mills that have an investment of Rs 100 crore. We want this exemption to be withdrawn to create a level playing field."

Ajmer Singh Lakhowal, chairman of the Punjab Mandi Board, says, "I have brought this matter to the notice of the Chief

Minister, who has agreed to meet the spinners. We suggested reduction in market fee from 2 per cent to 1 per cent and withdrawal of 2 per cent infrastructure development cess. This step will also help in checking evasion of market fees. It is not just the farmers, even the arhtiyas take the crop outside Punjab to sell it."

Heading: HC order: Forest dept prepares to fell trees - Indian Express
Content: While Punjab Agricultural University has been trying to impress upon the state government to levy a cess of 50 paisa for every Rs 100 earned by the farmer, which in turn can be used as funding for the university, Punjab Mandi Board chairman Ajmer Singh Lakhowal has suggested that the state government should even do away with the 2 per cent cess that the state government had levied on cotton buyers for development of research in Punjab. When asked why farmers were not ready to support PAU, Lakhowal said, "Why should only farmers of Punjab pay for PAU. Whatever we grow is consumed by the entire country. Majority of Punjab farmers fall below the poverty line and cannot pay any kind of cess."

Heading: 400 stranded in Lahaul and Spiti - Indian Express
Content:
Three teams formed; trained manpower to help complete operation by end of the week

A day after High Court granted permission to fell 60-odd trees, which have been rendered dangerous, the state government today prepared a strategy to cut down the trees.

The state's Forest Corporation, which will be an agency to cut down the trees, has formed three teams and decided to take the help of trained manpower to complete the operation by the end of the week.

Additional Chief Secretary (Forest) Avay Shukla, who held a meeting with senior forest officials following the High Court order, told the forest officials to mark the trees that the High Court had allowed to be felled on the basis of photographs provided.

As per a survey by the three-member committee, which the Cabinet had

constituted last week, nearly 414 trees were identified

as dangerous.

The High Court, however, had rejected the committee report and decided to allow felling of the trees only on the basis of photographs. Fifty photographs were submitted to the High Court and the Bench examined each photograph. Significantly, the Bench pointed out that some of the trees that the committee had identified as dangerous could be saved by undertaking some protection work.

For over a dozen trees, the court ordered Principal Chief Conservator of Forests Pankaj Khullar to personally visit the spot and take a decision.

Sources, however, said the government proposes to undertake a fresh survey to prepare a separate list of the trees that still pose a danger to life and property.

"The officials will undertake fresh videography of these trees and approach the High Court. For other trees that could be saved from felling, suitable measures will be taken," said Shukla.

Heading: Shanta loyalist quits BJP, joins LJP - Indian Express
Content:
More than 400 persons, mostly tourists, are stranded at Sarchu and Satru following disruption of road communications, even as Shimla and its peripheral areas are limping towards normalcy. Rohtang Pass has been reopened for vehicular traffic after continuous efforts of the Border Roads Organisation teams. The opening of the road will help in movement of the stranded vehicles and persons.

State's Additional Chief Secretary Parminder Mathur, who heads the disaster management group, held a meeting late this evening and reviewed the situation with top officials of the Public Works and Irrigation and Public Health Departments.

"Directions have been given to the Deputy Commissioner, Lahaul and Spiti, to ensure safety of the stranded persons and make arrangements for their evacuation. Officials are also camping at Satru and Sarchu to oversee the arrangements," she told the meeting.

In Shimla and other areas affected by the landslides, Mathur stressed upon the need to open link roads and maintaining drinking water supply. The meeting was also attended by PWD, IPH and police officials.

Reports received from Lahaul-Spiti said nearly 300 persons are stranded at Sarchu and another 100 between Batal and Satru. There have also been reports about a foreigners' trekking group stranded in Lahaul-Spiti. The Deputy Commissioner is understood to have sent a request for pressing a helicopter into service to airlift the foreigners and other stranded persons. About 22 persons who have reached Lossar in Spiti valley are reported to be safe, say reports.

Lahaul-Spiti DC C. Paul Rasu said in a release that snow clearance work on the road between Keylong and Baralacha was still on. One person whose body was found yesterday has been identified as a truck driver, Cheering Dorje, who hails from Leh.

Rakesh Kaushal, Secretary (Revenue), said the total death toll in the state has reached 49, of which 38 are in Shimla district alone.

Heading: Una SEZ gets Centre’s nod - Indian Express
Content:
The BJP today suffered a major setback when staunch Shanta loyalist Subhash Sharma resigned from the party and joined the Lok Janshakti Party along with his supporters. Sharma has been made chairperson of the state LJP parliamentary board.

Sharma, who remained a known employee leader when he was in government service, had joined the party after his retirement. Sharma was considered very close to Rajya Sabha member Shanta Kumar. He was made secretary of the party till the recent Assembly elections, but claims he was later ignored by the party.

"I was not only feeling ignored by the party, but also humiliated,'' Sharma said. "The party bosses invited several party workers who do not hold any office for meetings after the elections, but I was not invited even once. I feel I was used by the party and then dumped,'' an irate Sharma told The Indian Express over phone.

He charged the BJP leadership with ignoring the employees and said the government was not safeguarding the interests of the employees. "The state government has not done justice with the employees who were victimised by the previous Congress regime even after nine months of assuming power,'' he alleged.

Making a fierce attack on the BJP leadership, Sharma said it appeared that the BJP does not need the support of its workers from within the state. "Now the party has gathered the support of outsiders from Punjab, Haryana and Delhi,'' alleged Sharma, adding that there were many others who were "feeling suffocated" in the BJP.

Heading: Campaign against foeticide aimed at reversing sex ratio - Indian Express
Content:
Barely three days after the farmers who will be affected by the proposed special economic zone (SEZ) at Una marched to Shimla, the Centre has granted its approval to the promoter's company — Skil Infrastructure.

The SEZ, earlier cleared by the previous Congress government, was shelved for sometime, but subsequently the BJP government decided to go ahead with the plan and adopt the Gujarat model of SEZs.

The proposed SEZ, coming up close to Gagret, will have an investment of Rs 4,500 crore, of which the major component would be an international airport on the banks of Swan river.

When contacted, Director Industries Manoj Kumar confirmed that a meeting of the committee on SEZ was slated for September 22 and the Skil SEZ project for Una was on the agenda. "Our representatives were also there, but we have no details yet," he said.

But this is not without sharp reactions from the locals, who have already formed a joint action committee called Matrabhumi Sangharsh Samiti.

"We have called a meeting of the samiti on September 28 and next course of action will be announced then. There are 24 villages that will be affected by the SEZ and all families in these villagers are opposed to the proposal," said Narinder Singh Parmar, a leader of the sangharsh samiti.

Heading: Himachal gets environment award - Indian Express
Content:
The latest figures of the government's Sample Registration Survey show that the juvenile sex ratio of Himachal has improved and is now recorded at 903. The figure as per the 2001 Census was 896 girls for 1,000 boys.

Enthused by the outcome, the Himachal Gyan Vigyan Samiti (HGVS) would further accelerate its campaign against female foeticide with direct involvement of the masses.

"The aim is to reverse the trend of falling sex ratio that had put Himachal as the sixth-worse state in the country during the last Census, despite a good per capita income, education and health facilities. It is even possible that the sex ratio turns positive, where there are more girls for every 1,000 boys," said HGVS chairman Kuldeep Singh Tanwar.

During the coming three years, till the next Census survey is conducted in 2011, the state would see a sustained campaign at various levels where every section of the community would be involved in the awareness and direct action plan against ultrasound clinics responsible for violation of the Pre-Conception and Pre-Natal Diagnostic Techniques Act (Prohibition of Sex Selection Act), 1994.

"The proposed campaign would do what the literacy mission did to improve the literacy rate in the 1990s and women's involvement is the only answer for change," said professor Sunder Lohia, a social activist.

Heading: High Court extends gag order on govt, final verdict on Sept 26 - Indian Express
Content:
Himachal Pradesh has been adjudged the best state in the country for environment protection and increase of green cover by a private news channel in partnership with a news magazine in a national-level survey. Former president APJ Abdul Kalam presented the 'Diamond State Award' to Himachal Pradesh Chief Minister Prem Kumar Dhumal at an impressive function held in New Delhi last night.

Himachal Pradesh, in the past eight months, has made a pioneering effort to become the country's first carbon neutral state.The major initiatives taken include introducing technological interventions for reduction of greenhouse emissions in industrial, business, residential, automobile and energy sectors.

Dhumal said on the occasion: "Himachal Pradesh strongly advocates local, regional and global action for reducing greenhouse gas emissions."

Earlier, while participating in the discussions, Dhumal favoured the holding of Assembly and Parliamentary elections simultaneously in the country. "Repeated elections have caused adverse impact on social and economic development and holding of various elections on different occasions diverts the attention of the government from real issues," he added.

Heading: Singur: Guards attacked, Left points finger at Trinamool - Indian Express
Content:
The Calcutta High Court said it will pass its final order on September 26 on the Tata Motors plea for not allowing the state government to disclose contents of the agreement on setting up its small car plant. It also extended the interim gag order till September 30.

On September 12, Tata Motors had moved a plea urging for secrecy of the agreement. Justice Dipankar Dutta had passed an order staying the disclosure of the agreement for two weeks, which will expire on September 26.

Advocate Samaraditya Pal, counsel for the Tata Motors submitted that West Bengal Industrial Development Corporation (WBIDC) had published a part of the agreement in their website on September 12, following a direction issued by the chief information commissioner (CIC). Pal termed the disclosure as "illegal".

On Tuesday, Pal moved a plea saying that Tata Motors should have been given an opportunity to place its objections before the CIC before any order was passed on the disclosure of the agreement.

Counsel for Leader of the Opposition Partha Chatterjee, meanwhile, argued that once the agreement was read out on August 27 in a meeting of the standing committee, the people have a right to know the details of the project.

Heading: Called ‘driver’ by CISF official, Air India pilots stay grounded - Indian Express
Content:
Armed men bludgeoned two guards at the Tata's Singur factory late on Monday night, seriously injuring one and leaving a deeper question mark on whether the company will at all roll out the Nano from the factory's gates.

The assailants are yet to be traced, police officers have said, while the injured guard — Ajit Kumar — continues to remain serious in a private hospital with critical head injuried. The other, S N Sarkar, has been discharged from the Singur block hospital after treatment.

The Singur factory is guarded round-the-clock by 600 private security personnel and an equal number of policemen posted by the West Bengal government. Monday's incident will lend credence to the Tata's demand for a "conducive environment" in Singur, which looks remote now considering the talks between the government and the Trinamool-led protesters are still floundering.

The Tatas have already suspended work in the factory, and are quietly moving out their equipment from this facility.

Meanwhile, guards at the factory have begun to panic. One of them, Raju Kumar, who is posted at a gate, said: "We are all scared. Why are they targetting us? We have to stay on because we have families to feed."

Left Front Chairman Biman Bose was quick to point at the Trinamool for the assault. "In public they claim the agitation is peaceful satyagraha, but in practice they continue to thwart work. They don't want the state to develop. Tatas are clear on when to resume work," Bose said

Trinamool leader Partha Chatterjee dismissed Bose's accusations as a "conspiracy to malign" his party. "None of our supporters was involved in this attack," he said. The convenor of the Singur Krishi Jomi Raksha Committee, Becharam Manna, said: "We are being blamed unnecessarily."

Meanwhile, the search is on for officer-in-charge of the Singur police station Priyabrata Bakshi. "We are trying to zero in on the goons as soon as possible," he said. Officers said nearly seven miscreants were involved in Monday's attack. Armed with iron rods and bamboo sticks, they had sneaked inside the mother plant from the Gopalnagar area. The security guards were at the vendor park, when they were attacked.

Ajit Kumar saw his colleague Sarkar being beaten up and he blew the whistle to alert other security staff. The intruders then turned on him and hit him on the back of his head. They fled when Kumar fell unconscious. Security guards rushed to the spot and took the two to the Singur hospital. Later Kumar, a resident of Patna, was shifted to a private nursing home in Barasat.

Monday's assault follows a familiar pattern. On July 29, plant engineer Manish Khatua was beaten up with iron rods by armed youth. He spent 10 days in a Kolkata hospital before resuming duty.

Eight arrests were made in the Khatua case but later six were released on bail. In two other cases of assault and intimidation of staff, no arrest has been made.

Fifteen cases of theft of building material have also been reported ever since the boundary wall came up on February 4, 2007. Armed men have breached and damaged the factory wall 12 times, set fire at places and exploded bombs. However, Bakshi said: "There have been nearly 50 cases, big and small. But we are only a handful here. We are doing our best."

Tatas might not stay, says Nirupam Sen

"The possibility of the Tatas staying back in Bengal has become very remote," admitted Minister for Commerce and Industries Nirupam Sen on Tuesday. "The Tatas are saying they want a congenial atmosphere for implemention of the project. But you see the ground reality. People are still being beaten up. Then where are we? I don't see any solution," added Sabyasachi Sen, principal secretary, Department of Commerce and Industries. Asked if the Tatas had sent any communication to the government indicating that they would pull out, Sen said: "I don't know. Nothing has come to me." -ENS

Heading: We hope the arrested Jamia students are not guilty: V-C - Indian Express
Content:
Following a brawl between an Air India pilot and Central Industrial Security Force (CISF) officials, members of the Indian Commercial Pilots Association (ICPA) decided not to fly in and out of the city on Tuesday.

The incident took place when an Air India pilot, Captain M K Singh, was heading for the Bagdogra flight around 1 pm. According to sources, there was a tiff between the pilot and a CISF personnel about his cabin baggage at the security check point.

In a fit of rage, one of the CISF personnel allegedly called the pilot a "driver" and did not apologise as was demanded by Singh. According to sources, blows were exchanged and onlookers had to interfere to end the brawl.

The pilot decided not to fly the aircraft and the Bagdogra flight was delayed by more than two hours. Following this, within two hours, members of the ICPA decided not to operate flights in and out of Kolkata.

"One of our captains was assaulted and manhandled by CISF personnel. We have demanded an assurance from the airport management that such incidents will not be repeated in future. We have decided not to fly till the issue is resolved," said R Khiangte, general secretary of ICPA (eastern region).

Though Air India flights were delayed till late in the evening, they were being operated by airport management pilots and co-pilots who were on probation. A Delhi-bound flight had to be cancelled and a Chennai-Bangalore flight had to be clubbed.

However, after a meeting between CISF and ICPA the issue was amicably resolved late in the evening.

Air India will resume its flight opration as per schedule from Wednesday.

On an average, 30 Air India flights operate in and out of Kolkata everyday.

Both captain Singh and the CISF personnel have lodged complaints at the airport police station.

Ealier, in April this year, Air India pilots had threatened to go on a strike after Captain Rajat Rana was allegedly called a "driver" by Kerala parliamentarian PV Abdul Wahab, after the pilot accused him of delaying the flight and refused to fly with him on board.

Heading: East Bengal likely to use Yakubu in midfield - Indian Express
Content:
Moshirul Hasan, Vice-Chancellor of Jamia Millia Islamia University, said law will take its own course in the case of the two students of the university arrested by the Delhi Police in connection with the Delhi blasts.

He was speaking at the annual convocation of the Calcutta University. Hasan, a noted social scientist and Padmashree awardee in 2007, was conferred Doctor of Literature (Honoris Causa) by the university along with 341 PhD students on Tuesday.

The students, Mohammed Shakeel of second year MA, and Zia-Ur-Rehman of third year BA, were arrested last Sunday in connection with the blasts in the Capital on September 13.

"The university has already suspended these two students. We hope the two are not guilty," said Hasan, while addressing the reporters in Kolkata on Tuesday.

The Vice-Chancellor said it is unfortunate that the names of the students of the university have cropped up but he assured that there is peace on the campus. He also said these instances are happening throughout the world and we should not pinpoint one particular place or institution for this.

"Totalitarian forces seeking revenge through violence are damaging Islam in stronger ways than they are claiming lives of the victims," Hassan said while accepting the award.

Meanwhile, presiding over the function, Governor Gopalkrishna Gandhi said: "We need to develop a society where success should be synonymous to goal and not a victory."

Heading: Dazzling Dempo keep Indian flag flying - Indian Express
Content:
Yusif Yakubu could well be the player to watch in the upcoming I-League, albeit in a new role.

The striker, who had won the highest scorer award twice in the National Football League (NFL), is now set to perform the job of a play-maker. East Bengal's newly-appointed coach Stanley Rozario is using the Nigerian as a skimmer and the latter has impressed one and all with the way he has adopted to his new role.

"I was successful as a striker and became the top scorer twice in the NFL. It gave me prominence. Now I will be equally happy if I can set it up for (Sunil) Chhetri and Edmilson. It will be great to see anyone of them emerging as the top scorer of this I-League," Yakubu said.

Coach Rozario is using Yakubu in the central midfield position in a 4-4-2 formation. Mehrajuddin Wadoo will be doing the holding job, while Renedy Singh and Mehtab Hossain will operate through flanks.

Yakubu's team-mates believe that the former will pose a serious threat to any defence in his new position. Skipper M Suresh sounded very hopeful. "If Yakubu clicks in central midfiled then our strikers will rule the roost. They will get lot more balls in the penetrative zone. Yakubu has got a lovely game sense and is pretty adept in sending incisive passes. He can be a nightmare for the opponents," Suresh said.

However, for a 35-year-old, it's not easy to keep the intensity level intact in a marathon championship. Playing as a striker allows some breathing space. But as a midfielder he needs be to always on his toes. Will he be able to handle this day in and day out?

Yakubu appears unperturbed. "Modern day football doesn't allow anybody to play in a fixed position. Only goalkeepers have that liberty. The extra pressure shouldn't be a problem."

Incidentally, former East Bengal coach Subhas Bhowmick had used Mike Okoro in a similar kind of role in 2002-2003. The decision had worked wonders for the red-and-gold brigade who went on to win the Asean Cup and back-to-back NFL titles.

Heading: Rs 1 crore spent on food bill for KKR! - Indian Express
Content:
History was created at Jalan Besar Stadium, Singapore on Tuesday night. For the first time, an Indian football club moved into the semi-finals of the AFC Cup, at the expense of Home United. Dempo Sports Club of Goa, and of course, Indian football, have reasons to celebrate. After India's entry to the main rounds of the Asian Cup, Dempo's triumph today came as an icing on the cake. So, raise a toast to Indian football that is progressing big time.

The match was an edge-of-the-seat affair as the 4-3 scoreline suggests. Mboyo Iyomi drew first blood for Dempo in the very first minute, only to see Peres De Oliveira canceling it 12 minutes later. Dempo once again took the lead in the 24th minute through Roberto Mendes Silva Beto. Home United were dealt another blow when Valery Hiek was sent off for a second bookable offence in the 28th minute. But it didn't stop them from searching for another equaliser.

It came in the 36th minute when Kengne Ludovick was brought down in the box and though De Oliveira's penalty was parried by Abhijit Mondal, Indra Sahdan was on hand to tap home the rebound from close range.

A couple of minutes on and Indra Sadhan was once again in the thick of things, as he drove home a Ludovick cross from the right.

The hosts enjoyed the lead till Climax Lawrance got the better of Home United goalie Lewis first minute into the added-on time in the first half.

The first leg match between the two at Gachibowli Stadium in Hyderabad had ended in a 1-1 draw. With the score tied at 3-3 at half-time in this return leg encounter, Dempo had the away goal advantage. United had no option but to go all out for a win. Indra and Ludovick constantly probed the rival defence to no avail.

Dempo coach Armando Colaco preferred to play a waiting game and tried to hit the opponent on the break. The move paid off seven minutes from time. Beto, who had an excellent game, collected a loose ball and put things well beyond the hosts.

Ludovick put the ball in the net a minute later, but referee Fareed Ali Mohamed Almarzouqi from UAE disallowed that for an infringement.

Heading: Saurav inches closer to main draw of top French meet - Indian Express
Content:
It's been four months now since Shah Rukh Khan's IPL carnival in the city, but the skeletons keep falling off the shelf even now.
