In yet another startling revelation over the much-criticised handling of the IPL's Kolkata episode last summer, hosts CAB are learnt to have spent a mind-boggling Rs 1.1 crore just on food bills for the Kolkata Knight Riders and the organisers for the seven matches held at Eden Gardens.

A top CAB official today revealed that the then administration's (Prasun Mukherjee was CAB chief then) official food expenses bill for the 45-day IPL ran into Rs 1.1 crore, with the expenses covering players, hosting and visiting organisers, and high-profile guests.

The discovery has left the current Jagmohan Dalmiya-led CAB top brass fuming, and the state association has withheld pending payments that are due to be made to the companies that supplied the food for the seven matches IPL matches that were held in Kolkata.

With former CAB chief Mukherjee at the helm during the April-May Twenty20 carnival at Eden, the CAB went on to overshoot its budget by nearly Rs 5 crore. The BCCI had strictly instructed all the eight hosting bodies to limit their IPL expenditure to Rs 3.5 crore, but the CAB went on to spend a whopping Rs 7.26 crore for the 7-match show.

Even as the current CAB administration is up in arms over how to explain the excess expenditure to the BCCI and seek due reimbursement, strong letters were today shot off to members of the Mukherjee-led CAB top brass during the IPL. Unable to explain the massive overspending to the BCCI, Dalmiya & Co now want the then administration to explain how the costs were incurred and find out ways to hammer out a proper explanation.

The sensational Rs 1.1 crore food bill apart, the CAB is also learnt to have spent a whopping Rs 13 lakh on installing an automatic sight-screen for the IPL matches. Questions have been raised on this expenditure, and also over an amount of Rs 1.81 lakh that was reportedly spent on purchasing plastic cups for drinking water for the IPL matches.

Heading: Container marked ‘explosive’ triggers panic at Howrah station - Indian Express
Content:
India's squash sensation Saurav Ghosal — who is going through the form of his life — is now just one win away from making it to the main draw of the all-important Internationaux de France tournament. Ghosal inched close to the coveted title's main draw after he scored a hard-earned five-game win in the qualifying opener in Paris today.

The reigning national champion staved off a stiff challenge from South African No 1 and World No 55 Jesse Engelbrecht 11-8, 7-11, 9-11, 11-3, 11-9 in a 68-minute battle to enter the qualifying finals yesterday.

The 22-year-old World No 45, who clinched his maiden PSA title outside India with the Ornano Open in Bordeaux, carried his form through and capitalised on his opponent's umpteen unforced errors to eke out yet another laudable win.

Ghosal will now take on Mathieu Castaqnet in the qualifying finals after the Frenchman rallied to beat Netherland's Dylan Bennett 11-13, 11-9, 11-6, 11-5 in a marathon 62-minute contest.

"I saw Mathieu play in Bordeaux and I was impressed by his game, he really played well," Ghosal said of his next opponent.

India's national squash champion and a rising star on the international circuit, Saurav claimed the biggest title of his career when he won the inaugural Ornano International Open trophy last week. The Chennai-born youngster, who stays in England, defeated third seed Davide Bianchetti of Italy in the final of the Ornano Open.

It was his third successive big moment in the event after the upsets he scripted in the quarter-finals and semi-finals.

Heading: German wholesale giant to take quit Kolkata decision tomorrow - Indian Express
Content:
Panic gripped Howrah station on Tuesday when an abandoned container marked "explosive" was spotted inside a train compartment.

Business on the station was as usual on Tuesday afternoon when Bagha Jatin Passenger entered platform number 21 and 22 at the new station complex.

Two porters, who were dumping bags in the luggage compartment of the train, first noticed the abandoned container inside the compartment. They immediately informed the travelling ticket collectors.

Maniram Aich and Surai Hembrom, members of the railway bomb disposal squad, were informed and they came with sniffer dogs. The dogs sniffed something inside the box, and it was immediately removed from the compartment.

The railway police, along with RPF, cordoned off the area and requested people to stay away. The incident also led to suspension of some trains, B L Meena, superintendent of Railway Police said.

A thorough search, however, revealed no explosives inside the box. It was found after preliminary investigation that some empty shells were contained in the box, which was supposed to be delivered to Chandipur in Orissa.

Defence Ministry spokesman Group Captain R K Das claimed that the box was booked by an ordnance factory for Chandipur and contained no explosives.

"The box contains no explosives and poses no danger. Had it contained explosives, it would have been booked by road and not rail," he said.

Holding the railways responsible for "leaving the box uncared for", he said there was no need to create a fuss over it.Railway officials said an inquiry has been started in this case.

Heading: Medical board set up to probe infant deaths - Indian Express
Content:
Metro Cash & Carry, a German wholesale giant, which has applied for the renewal of its licence, will take a decision on whether to quit Kolkata or not on September 25.

This was announced on Tuesday by the firm's managing director Martin Doluhy, who along with Heinrich OE Birr, vice-president of international relations of the company, met State Minister for Agriculture Naren Dey.

"Our talks were quite positive. We are going to meet the Chief Minister on Wednesday and will take a decision the day after," Doluhy told the media after the meeting.

Metro, which has built its wholesale outlet on the Eastern Bypass, first got its licence in 2005 from Agricultural Produce Marketing Corporation (APMC) and had it renewed in 2006 and 2007. But this year, the licence has not been renewed yet and the company has said it would consider all options, including pulling out of the state.

Dey, however, said the decision on the licence would be decided at the bipartite meet between CPM and Forward Bloc to be held on September 28. CPM is in favour of the company carrying out its operations in the state.

"They discussed about their operation and services in the state. I have told them that the decision will be taken on September 28," Dey said.

Heading: HC seeks reply from cops for illegal parking in rally - Indian Express
Content:
A medical board has been set up by the authorities of the Institute of Child Health to find out the reasons behind the deaths of three infants on Sunday night.

Although the primary reason behind the deaths appears to be the diseases of the children, the slackness on part of the senior doctors also seems to have played a role.

Since the Institute of Child Health is a Trust hospital and senior doctors work voluntarily, they do not attend to patients after 4 pm. Moreover, no senior doctors are available in the hospital during week-ends.

"We have an acute shortage of trained nursing staff. Since it is a trust hospital, we cannot force the senior doctors to stay overnight, as they work voluntarily. Although these three deaths were not caused by medical negligence, we are trying to strengthen our reporting system," said Dr Apurba Ghosh, director, Institute of Child Health.

A report prepared on the number of fatalities in the last six months in the hospital comes as a shock. Out of 161 patients admitted, 14 have died. Earlier, when there was no Neonatal Incentive Care Unit (NICU), 18 infants had died out of 118 admitted.

Sources have revealed that the protocol in the hospital is such that if the condition of a child starts deteriorating after 4 pm, the nursing staffs contact first-year medical students. If the students fail to handle the case, then second-year students are consulted. If they too fail then third-year students come into the picture. After the long process, if the case continues to worsen, senior doctors are consulted over the phone.

"Sometimes, some cases are found too critical for survival. In some cases, we declare that there is no hope. So, if such cases suddenly start deteriorating, the students do not disturb the senior doctors by calling them," said a medical official on condition of anonymity.

"In today's meeting, it has been decided that the reporting system has to be strengthened. Moreover, the authorities will deploy better doctors who will be available on call," added the official.

Parents of other patients admitted to the hospital feel at least two of the three deceased infants — 40-day-old Mom Chatterjee and 75-day-old Parambrata Nandi — could have survived for a few more days if they were attended by senior doctors when their condition started deteriorating.

Mom was suffering from chronic diarrhoea and she did not have enzymes in her body. According to the hospital authorities, her case was fatal and there was no treatment for her. Parambrata, meanwhile, was suffering from acute respiratory disorder.

"Since there was no hope in these two cases, the junior doctors did not feel the need to discuss the cases with the senior doctors. It is a recurring problem in this hospital. Senior doctors are available only for a few hours in the hospital," said Shipra Maity, mother of the infant undergoing treatment on the bed beside that of Mom Chatterjee.

Heading: Banka murder: Servant gets death sentence - Indian Express
Content:
The Calcutta High Court sought a reply from DC (Headquarters) Vineet Goel of the Kolkata police as to why driving licences and tax tokens had not been seized from buses that were illegally parked around the Victoria Memorial during a CPM rally on January 13.

This was in response to a plea moved by environmentalist Subhas Dutta on Tuesday, which stated that among the illegally parked buses, Kolkata police had registered cases against only 267 of them. In response, the police admitted that owners of 48 buses could not be traced, as their driving licences and tax tokens have not been seized.

The Division Bench of Justices Bhaskar Bhattacharya and R N Banerjee directed Goel to file an affidavit stating why the licences and tax tokens were not seized when all the buses were parked in a particular area.

In another development, Dutta submitted before the Division Bench that five open coal ovens were being used on the premises of the SSKM Hospital, violating a High Court order. On September 28, 2007 a division bench had banned the use of open coal ovens within 3 km of the Victoria Memorial — SSKM Hospital falls within that distance. On August 18, the High Court had directed SSKM to stop the use of open coal ovens on their premises by August 30.

On Tuesday, after Dutta's submission, the Division Bench issued showcause notices to the medical superintendent and vice-principal of SSKM, asking why they should not be held guilty of contempt of court. The case will come up for hearing next Tuesday.

Heading: Titagarh jute mill re-opened after 4 months - Indian Express
Content:
Nearly three years after being arrested for the murder of his employers Tarachand and Sarada Devi Banka, a fast track court on Tuesday awarded death sentence to Kebol Roy. Roy had murdered the elderly couple in their Camac Street flat and had stolen valuables worth nearly Rs 20 lakh.

This is the second death sentence handed down by a Kolkata court within a month. On August 29, Nikku Yadav, another domestic help, was sentenced to death for murdering his employer Ravinder Kaur Luthra.

After the conviction earlier this month, Justice Subodh Batavyal announced the sentence on Tuesday. Public prosecutor Ganesh Maity had cited that the case was in the category of "rarest of the rare" and had recommended capital punishment.

On April 18, 2005, Roy had smashed 68-year-old Tarachand's head with a frying pan and slit Sarda Devi's (56) throat with a kitchen knife in their seventh floor flat in Mansarovar Apartments.

After the murder, Roy fled Kolkata and was arrested from his native village Simultala in Bihar a month later. Valuables stolen from Banka's flat were recovered from his possession.

According to investigating officers, Roy had planned the murder meticulously. He had wiped out his fingerprints from the apartment, but forgot to wipe them from the doorknob while leaving the flat.

Heading: Kashmiri youths intercepted at Bangladesh border - Indian Express
Content:
Even as uncertainty looms over the Greater Noida-based Graziano Transmissioni India Pvt Ltd whose CEO and MD LK Choudhary was bludgeoned to death by disgruntled workers on Monday, Titagarh-based jute mill Loomtex Engineering resumed work after being shut down for nearly four months following the murder of its personnel manager, allegedly by workers.

On May 15, Loomtex personnel manager Apurba Roychowdhury was found battered to death in his office on the mill premises, while the Sangrami Mazdoor Union (SMU) was conducting a "gate meeting" protesting the non-payment of long standing provident fund and gratuity dues. A team from Khardah police station arrested 21 members of the SMU in this connection.

According to Khardah police station Inspector-in-Charge Sukumar Gharai, the SMU had not taken police permission to hold the meeting. "All of them were arrested from the spot. The meeting was illegal. They have been chargesheeted and at present are out on bail," Gharai said.

SMU leader Sharmishta Choudhury, a Centre for Communist Revolutionaries (Marxist-Leninist) activist, alleged the murder was carried out by criminals hired by the management. "We were holding a peaceful meeting at the mill gates when criminals attacked us and tried to disrupt the meeting. We immediately called in the police. Later we heard that the personnel manager had been killed. Among those arrested some were our union's high-ranking members, including the president, secretary and treasurer. How can they be involved in the murder?" Choudhury said.

She said the arrests were aimed at breaking the back of the SMU, which was formed by Loomtex workers early this year. "The workers have not been paid gratuity and other arrears — amounting to about Rs 15 crore — since years. The management has no accounts to show. The existing unions have not taken up the matter properly with the management."

The mill's president (works), Ranjan Majumdar, however, said the SMU was trying to cripple the mill. "The Naxalite union was against the smooth functioning of the mill. Their workers killed the manager. After that, neither the management nor the workers had the confidence to return to work. Finally, after a lot of meetings with local legislators and workers, we arrived at a historic deal and reopened the mill on September 12," he added.

Majumdar said nearly 1,600 workers and representatives of 12 unions met the management on September 11 on the Loomtex premises.

Majumdar said: "The workers were not aware of the figures involved. The mill has been unsuccessfully run by different promoters since 1986. When we took over in 1999, there were a lot of arrears, Rs 11.83 crore in provident fund is being paid to the PF commissioner by us in 50 installments."

"We have already paid Rs 55 lakh in wages to workers for the period since May. Our only condition is that the 24 arrested and absconding workers will not be reinducted. The workers have rejoined without any preconditions or financial promises. Work is going on," Majumdar added.

Heading: Fire department issues guidelines to ensure safety in Puja pandals - Indian Express
Content:
Two Kashmiri youths were intercepted by the Border Security Force (BSF) in Nadia along the India-Bangladesh border on Monday. The youths, who were without any valid papers, entered India from Bangladesh and were on their way to Jammu and Kashmir.

"Hilal Ahmed Mir (27) and Manjir Ahmed (28) were intercepted by BSF on Monday and on Tuesday the duo was handed over to us. We have contacted our counterparts in Jammu and Kashmir to verify the antecedents of the duo. They are now being interrogated," said Harikishore Kusumakar, police super of Nadia.

The two youths were spotted by a BSF patrol while they were trying to cross into Indian territory from Bangladesh at Kumari Border outpost of BSF 200 battalion in the Hanskhali police station area.

The duo was detained and during questioning they said they were residents of Haringandharbal locality, under tehsil Kangan in Srinagar.

"They said they have married Bangladeshi girls and were returning home from there. We are yet to verify their claims. It is still not clear why they ventured into Bangladesh without valid papers," said Kusumakar.

Heading: Tapasi Malik death case verdict deferred - Indian Express
Content:
As Puja pandals have virtually occupied every road and lane in the city, the Fire and Emergency Services Department wants to make sure that all the pandals adhere to the basic fire safety norms.

In 2006, the department had received 3,670 applications for fire clearance from various Puja committees in Kolkata. This year, the department has already received 3,500 applications and the number is expected to rise close to 4,000.

"The number of pandals has gone up in the last few years, but our officials have not increased in that ratio. We are trying our best to deal with the situation," said Gopal Bhattacharya, director of fire and emergency services.

To make the job easier for Puja organisers, application forms to obtain a 'No Objection Certificate' is available at all the police stations of the city. The Puja organisers are required to furnish details of their pandals such as height and width of the entry and exit points, area occupied and materials used to construct pandals in the application forms. The forms should be submitted at the headquarters of the Fire and Emergency Department.

With only 15 fire inspectors to inspect nearly 4,000 pandals in Kolkata, the department has decided to conduct surprise checks between September 26 and October 7.

In 2006, notices were served to 50 Puja committees for violation of fire safety norms, while 874 were given strict warnings. An FIR was also lodged in one case. "This year also we will take strict action against Puja committees who fail to adhere to the fire safety regulations," Bhattacharya said.

DOs

* Separate entry and exit doors in all pandals

* Each door should be 14 feet high and 12 feet wide

* Cloth used for construction should be dipped in fire retardant solution

* Volunteers should be available inside pandals at all the times

* Fire extinguishers, water and sand buckets should be available in side each pandal

DON'T's

* Do not use flammable material for construction of pandals

* Do not allow hawkers to use open fire near pandals

* No cooking or firecrackers should be used within 200 feet of pandals

* Do not let devotees gather inside pandals, especially at peak hours

Heading: Court rejects CU’s admission letter to college - Indian Express
Content:
The sub-divisional court of Chandernagore has deferred its decision on the Tapasi Malik death case till November 1.

Justice Amal Kanti Acharya was to deliver the verdict by Tuesday. CPM leader Suhrid Dutta, prime accused in the case, was the secretary of the Singur zonal committee of the CPM when he was arrested by the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI).

On Tuesday, the judge stated that some parts of the petition filed by the CBI were not legible. "The judge asked us to file fresh photocopies of our petition. We will do so as soon as possible," said Partha Sarathi Bose, DSP of the agency.

The charred body of 18-year-old Tapasi Malik was found in a field inside the Tata factory area on December 18, 2006. Dutta was arrested by the CBI on June 26, 2007 and has since been in custody.

Supporters of both the Trinamool Congress and the CPM gathered in large numbers at the court compound waiting for the verdict. While Trinamool supporters demanded severe punishment for Dutta, CPM cadres spoke about his innocence.

Heading: Six PSEs ready for ‘public service enterprise’ tag - Indian Express
Content:
The Calcutta High Court on Tuesday rejected the letter issued by the Calcutta University, which had asked the Bhowanipore Gujarati Education Society College not to admit more than 300 students in a session.

Delivering the final order, Justice Saumitra Pal observed: "The letter issued by the university was not sustainable according to the law". Justice Pal also imposed a fine of Rs 10,200 on CU, and directed that the amount should be paid to the college as the cost for the court case.

The college admitted 2,304 students in BCom, BBA and MBA for the current session. Pro-Vice-Chancellor (Academic) of the CU had written to the college authorities that the college could not admit more the 300 students in a session.

Heading: Poverty drives 12-year-old Dalit girl to commit suicide - Indian Express
Content:
Top honchos agree to part with 30 per cent of their profit after a marathon meeting at Chief Minister's residence

Responding to the Narendra Modi government's "diktat," the chairpersons and managing directors of six state-run public sector enterprises (PSEs) on Tuesday agreed to set aside 30 per cent of the Profit Before Tax (PBT) for carrying out welfare activities across Gujarat.

Apparently, aware of the resentment brewing among individual shareholders over the government's controversial move, the Tuesday meeting was a closely-guarded secret, kept at the CM's residence rather than at the Sachivalaya. The ministers and senior bureaucrats who attended the meet were tight-lipped, with none of them willing to talk to the media about its proceedings.

Minister of State for Industries Saurabh Patel declined to say anything on the proceedings of the meeting. GNFC Managing Director Sudha Anchaliya, among the first MDs to oppose the government's move, also refused to comment on today's meeting.

On his part, Arvind Agrawal, Commissioner, Bureau of Public Sector Enterprises, GoG, said, "It was a general discussion on the issue."

A senior official in the Finance Department, who attended the three-hour marathon meeting, told Newsline that the CM had instructed heads of the six PSEs to ensure that their respective AGMs, to adopt a resolution on setting aside 30 per cent of the PBT for 'social causes, are held in a peaceful atmosphere.' He said the CM had also asked them to win the confidence of the minority shareholders while adopting a resolution on the same and ensure the protection of the interests of private shareholders.

The official said there were chances of some minority shareholders filing a petition in the court of law against the government's move and the PSE heads were cautioned against this possibility at today's meeting.

Apparently, Modi also "reprimanded" Gujarat Mineral Development Corporation (GMDC) Managing Director Vijya Laxmi Joshi for staying away from the Corporation's AGM at Ahmedabad last week. Angry investors had created a ruckus over the PSEs' proposal to set aside Rs 122 crore for welfare activities as directed by the state government.

A government nominee deputed to handle the AGM was also forced to adjourn the meeting, rescheduling it for Wednesday.

Last Saturday, the Gujarat Industries Power Co Ltd (GIPCL) was the first among the six state-listed PSEs to pass a resolution, by a majority, setting aside 30 per cent of their PBT towards "Corporate Social Responsibility." The company that had recorded a PBT of Rs 140 crore for the fiscal year 2007-08 has decided to contribute about Rs 50 crore for social causes.

The six listed PSEs — GMDC, GNFC, GSFC, GACL, GIPCL and GSPL —had over eight lakh individual shareholders at the end of June. According to official sources, the annual profit of these PSEs are over Rs 2,000 crore, and about Rs 700 crore are paid as corporate taxes to the Centre.

These state-run companies have continued to register a steep decline in their share prices following a "request" by the state government to contribute 30 per cent of the PBT for "social causes."

Heading: Do not table part Nanavati panel report, pleads PIL; HC says no - Indian Express
Content:
A 12-year-old Dalit girl committed suicide by setting herself on fire in the Danilimda area on Tuesday afternoon, following severe financial crunch. The girl has been identified as Kailas Makwana, a resident of Vadhiyar Vaas in Ram-Rahim Nagar, behind Calico Mill in the Danilimda area. The police said the girl was living with her eight-year-old brother, Laxman, and uncle Pravin Makwana (35), a tuberculosis patient.

Investigating officer, Sub-Inspector D I Sindhi, said: "Due to illness, Pravin did not pursue any occupation. Kailas used to earn for the family by doing petty jobs . Many a time, the neighbours also helped her. But she seems to have got fed up of the financial crunch to meet the daily household expenses and the expenses of her uncle's illness, and possibly took the extreme step in disgust."

According to the police, Kailas drenched herself with kerosene and set herself ablaze in the afternoon when she was alone. The neighbours came to know of the incident only when they saw smoke coming out of the house. When the door was opened, they found Kailas lying dead.

The police said, Kailas' father — Muljibhai had died nine years ago. Soon afterwards, her mother, Goriben abandoned her two children, Kailas and the newly-born Laxman, and re-married.

Following their mother's re-marriage, Kailas and her brother started living with their uncle. Goriben's present address is not known to the police.

The Danilimda police have registered a case of accidental death. Further investigations are on.

Heading: Rain God’s ‘benevolence’ leaves Jamka at Almighty’s mercy - Indian Express
Content:
Petitioner had sought quashing of part report, saying the panel should have filed a complete report

A division bench of the Gujarat High Court on Tuesday dismissed a joint Public Interest Litigation (PIL) seeking direction to quash the part report of the Nanavati Commission.

The bench comprising Chief Justice K S Radhkrishnan and Justice M S Shah observed that Section 3 of the Commissions of Inquiry Act did not prevent the Commission from preparing a part report, nor did it say whether a part report could not be filed in the state Assembly.

The PIL was filed by the Citizens for Justice and Peace and the Peoples Union for Civil Liberties and had also sought directions ordering the government not to table the part report in the Assembly during the Monsoon session starting September 25.

Representing the petitioners, advocate M M Tirmizi contended that the Commission was set up to probe the Godhra and the post-Godhra riots and hence could not split the inquiry into two parts. He pleaded that it should be a composite report of the complete inquiry.

He said the first part of the report dealt with the Godhra incident and did not reflect

on the role of the Chief Minister, other ministers and governmental officials in the ensuing riots.

"So, a composite report should be submitted to the state government and tabled in the Assembly after complete inquiry of the Godhra and post-Godhra incidents," he added.

Referring to two Supreme Court judgements, Tirmizi further said: "It is an exercise by the state government for placing the part report of the inquiry of Godhra and the post-Godhra incidents."

He added that the prejudicial role of the state government had been exposed following the Supreme Court order of a re-trial of the Best Bakery and the Bilkis Bano cases outside Gujarat. The apex court had also directed the state government to appoint another public prosecutor in the two cases on the suggestions of the victims, he said. He also referred to affidavits filed by former Additional Director General of Police R B Sreekumar about the role of the state in the post-Godhra riots.

He said the terms of reference appointing the Commission to look into the Godhra and post-Godhra incidents be looked in toto. Tabling one part of the report and making it public was detrimental to the public interest and amounted to splitting the terms of reference into two, he added.

As such, the state government should be restrained from placing it in the House on September 25, he said.

Heading: Now, objections against proposed power tariff can be filed till Oct 13 - Indian Express
Content:
Downpour, sloppy roads cut off Junagadh villagers from rest of the world

Not too long ago, the residents of Jamka village were praying to the Rain God for showering mercy on the village. But now that the village has seen some good rain, they are praying for it to stop. And not for a reason unexplained.

Every year, the village gets cut off from the rest of the world during monsoon season. No vehicle can enter the village as water floods the only road that links it to the other villages. People have to survive on all that they have and wait for days for the water to recede.

This year, one person died as he could not be taken to the nearby hospital for treatment because the road was flooded and vehicles could not ply on it. Two cases of death were recorded last year due to the same reason.

Jamka village in Junagarh district falls between two rivers — Jamka and Bandhukiyo. When the road gets flooded, villagers get isolated from the rest of the world. Even after the water recedes, the road is so sloppy that it is almost impossible for vehicles to ply on it.

Village sarpanch Parsottam Sidpara said: "The river usually flows six feet above the road surface. We usually cross the road by making a human chain. It is very dangerous. The problem aggravates during a medical emergency."

Dipak Dobaria, a member of the Junagadh taluka panchayat, said: "Every year people die because medical service cannot reach them. This has been happening since the time of Independence. Recently, the state government sanctioned Rs 40 lakh for the construction of a causeway. But work on the project has not yet started. This apart, the fund sanctioned is not sufficient. The strong current also makes it important for the structure to be designed properly. Otherwise, it may collapse."

In view of the situation, the two village chiefs have said that the project should be studied properly before it is implemented. "We need a river bridge, not a causeway, as sanctioned by the government," they said.

Heading: Robbery accused attempts suicide by consuming poison - Indian Express
Content:
GUVNL had submitted multi-year tariff petition for April 1, 2008 to March 31, 2011

The Gujarat Electricity Regulatory Commission (GERC) has extended the last date of filing objections/suggestions on the Multi-Year Tariff (MYT) petition filed by the Gujarat Urja Vikas Nigam Ltd. for the first control period of three financial years – April 1, 2008 to March 31, 2011, up to October 13.

This has been done on receipt of representations from the stakeholders/consumer associations, who have expressed concern over the proposed hike.

It may be mentioned here that GUVNL and all its subsidiary companies have submitted a proposal to the GERC for an increase in the power tariff for the above mentioned control period, applicable to all categories of consumers except agriculture.

This has been done under Section 61 of the MYT Framework Regulation 2007, which states that any power tariff to be determined from April 1, 2006 should feature an initial control period of three-year duration for transmission and distribution.

The proposed hike comes when the cost of power in Gujarat is already on the higher side, as compared to other states.

An analysis of the power scenario in Gujarat raises some interesting questions. At present there are 23 power plants in Gujarat that includes 9 thermal, 9 gas based, 4 hydro and 1 nuclear power plant at Kakrapara.

The data provided by the Energy and Petrochemicals Department, Gujarat government mentions the total installed capacity in the state at 10,605 MW and expects to increase it by 100 per cent to 20,725 MW in the next five years. The government also projects the peak demand to touch 14,031 MW by 2012, thus aiming to generate nearly 6,000 MW as surplus.

The claims, however, seem contrary to the power situation in the state. The Monthly Review of Gujarat Economy published by the Centre for Monitoring of Indian Economy (CMIE), Ahmedabad reports the power deficit in Gujarat to be above 15 per cent, which reaches to 21 per cent during the peak demand period.

Statistically, the state required 6,253 million KwH of electricity during May 2008, but only 5,250 million KwH was available, a deficit of 16.04 per cent.

The power deficit in the state also prompted GUVNL to announce the compulsory additional one-day power staggered holiday on high-tension and low-tension non-continuous process industries across the state.

The move was later withdrawn following timely rains and the improvement in the overall power supply.

Incidentally, the CMIE report also records a decline in the overall thermal power generation of the state.

R J Revar, Chief Engineer (Generation), GUVNL refused to comment on the issue and S B Khayalia, General Manager, Commercial was un-reachable.

Heading: 16-year-old caught with stolen bike - Indian Express
Content:
A man accused of robbery attempted suicide by consuming acid in the police lock up in Palsana taluka on Monday. He was shifted to the New Civil Hospital at Surat for further treatment where he is reported to be out of danger.

The police had arrested Ramkaran Soni (25), a resident of Kadodara taluka in Surat suspecting his involvement in providing a tip off to two persons who had robbed one Mahendra Singhvi, the owner of Mamta Dyeing Mills at Kadodara of Rs 13 lakh on Friday.

During interrogation, Soni confessed to have given a tip-off to his friends who threatened Mahendra at gun-point to hand over the cash, while the latter was returning home from his factory.

After the incident, Mahendra contacted the Palsana police station and lodged a robbery complaint.

During investigations, the police found the statements of Soni and the victim's car driver, contradictory, as he was also present at the spot when the robbery took place.

On Monday, the police arrested him and began further investigations. During his custody, Soni went to the bathroom and attempted suicide by consuming acid. The other inmates immediately started shouting when they spotted Soni lying on the floor. Lockup In-charge Bhagwanbhai immediately rushed Soni to the Sanjeewani Hospital at Kadodara and later shifted him to Surat.

Palsana Sub-Inspector Vinod Anand said: "After primary investigations, we found that Soni went into the bathroom and consumed the acid. We suspect he might have done this so that he could be released. We have arrested him under charges of robbery."

Heading: Legal notice to Ram Gopal for ‘promoting’ blind faith - Indian Express
Content:
Boy wanted to sell off bike to pay tuition fees at coaching class

A 16-year-old boy was caught by the police with a stolen motorcycle from the Bhatar area in Surat on Monday evening. The Umra police said the boy was caught following a tip-off by one of the persons to whom he had shown the bike for a possible sale. The police said the boy had confessed to his involvement in the theft.

The police added that the teenager, a resident of Kamrej taluka of Surat district, had stolen the motorcycle to pay for his tuition fees at his coaching class. The boy had completed his Class VIII from Galipara High School in Kathor and had to forego further studies due to his parents' weak financial condition. He had come to the city and was staying at his uncle's house at Bharthana village in Umra for the last five years. He worked at various places, but wanted to pursue further studies, they said.

The police said, on the advice of the Royal Coaching Classes at Bhatar, he decided to appear at the Class X exams as an external student. He made a part payment of Rs 3,000 from his savings but couldn't make further payment as he was jobless.

On September 9, he found a motorcycle parked at the coaching class parking lot. The keys were inside and the boy stole the bike with the intention of selling it off to pay the coaching class fees. Later, he filled up the tank with Rs 300 worth of petrol and showed it to several people, one of whom informed the police.

The police said a check revealed that one Vaibhav Parekh had lodged a theft complaint of a bike at the Umra police station on September 9.

The boy said: "My intention of stealing the motorcycle was to pay the tuition fees. I took admission as an external student in the SSC and also started taking coaching from the tuition class. My uncle's financial position is not good and they cannot help me with the fees. My father Jagdish is a tempo driver and stays in Kamrej after his divorce from my mother Taradevi. My mother took my younger brother Praveen with her while my elder sister Varsha is married and stays in Kathor village. After divorce, my father took me with him and later re-married. Nobody was looking after me and my step-mother harassed me a lot. My father then told me to go to Surat at his brother's house."

Umra Inspector R S Patel said: "We "ill send him to a juvenile home after producing him in the court. This was his first attempt at stealing. He wanted to study further and had stolen the motorcycle for paying the fees. We have informed his uncle about his crime and his arrest. We have found that he is mentally broken as he failed to get support from his family. His parents are divorced and living separately and there is no one in the family except his uncle to take care of him."

Heading: Pure for sure: Lions Club’s ‘Suraksha’ cover for clean water - Indian Express
Content:
Film producer Ram Gopal Varma has been slapped with a legal notice for allegedly promoting blind faith in his latest movie Phoonk.

Jayant Pandya, the chairman of NGO Bharat Jan Vigyan Jatha in Rajkot, has served the notice to Varma for "cheating people by claiming that the film cannot be seen sitting alone in the theatre and for promoting blind faith."

Varma had announced a reward of Rs 5 lakh to anyone who watches the entire movie sitting alone in the theatre.

Pandya said that when he accepted the challenge, the film producer said the reward scheme was limited to theatres in Mumbai only, which proves that Varma was cheating people by such publicity stunts.

The theme is also misleading, as it shows the victory of a tantrik over a doctor, Pandya said, adding that the film can be seen alone in theatre but it is foolish to watch such a movie.

Heading: Four senior Congressmen cry ‘favouritism’, threaten to quit - Indian Express
Content:
The project will cover 50 villages and towns of Saurashtra-Kutch region

With an aim to provide purified drinking water in the remote villages of Saurashtra and Kutch, the Lions Club of Rajkot has begun a new project named 'Suraksha'. Under this, they plan to cover 50 villages and towns where Reverse Osmosis (RO) purified water will be supplied to residents at a nominal cost of just 20 paisa per litre.

The project is the brainchild of members of the Lions Club of Rajkot, Avkar and former district president, Hitesh Kothari. Kothari had conducted several health camps in villages and had found that the water in most of the villages was contaminated and impure.

Kothari said: "Under this project, we will install huge RO plants in villages, where water and electricity is available. We have donors who are willing to give us RO plants with a purifying capacity of 500 to 1,000 litres per hour, which costs around Rs 1 to 2 lakh. We will pay the electricity bill, water bill, bear the maintenance cost of machine and the salary of employees, and in return, people desirous of availing this facility will just pay us 20 paise per litre."

He said in major cities of Saurashtra, private operators supply 20 litre mineral water bottles for Rs 35 and they will provide the same for just Rs 4.

He said they have forwarded this project to their head office for approval, which has now been granted.

"Under this project, we select a village or town, preferably where there is a Lions Club centre. Then, we check for availability of water and electricity connection. After this, the RO plant is installed. Per se a person with a daily water need of 5 litres will have to spend just Rs 1 everday," he said.

At present, the Lions Club has selected 10-12 centres including two areas in Rajkot city, Morbi town, Manavadar, Madhavpur-Ghed, Wankaner, Shaper and two centres in Jamnagar city and Gondal town for this project.

By the end of this year, they plan to cover another 50 villages in the Saurashtra region, he said.

Kothari added: "Many people have approached us with the request for starting such a centre in their village or town, which we will consider after checking the feasibility."

He said the main problems facing the Club is the lack of constant water supply and electricity in many rural areas.

"Though we have not yet approached any government authority with our problems, but once all our formalities are completed, we will approach the authority concerned to help us with our project. We have also decided that if regular water supply is issued at any centre then we will go for underground water source and pump out water for our usage," said Kothari.

"As of now, work has begun at our first centre in Shiromani Complex area near the Karansinhji School in Rajkot. Work at the next centre, at Milpara, will begin soon. Within a month or so, work will begin at the other centres selected by us. As initially, people are hesitant about purchasing water, we are planning to provide home delivery," he added.

Heading: Grey area: Ageing AMTS drivers pose a threat to passengers’ lives - Indian Express
Content:
Two councillors, city general secretary write to Sonia, allege irregularities in filling of party posts

Two sitting Congress councillors and a city Congress general secretary have reportedly conveyed to AICC president Sonia Gandhi about their decision to quit to protest against favouritism in filling party posts.

Saijpur Bogha councillors Dr Krishna Thakar and Dipak Makwana, former municipal school board chairman Dr Ganpat Parmar, and city Congress general secretary Dr Praful Thakar have stated in public that they have quit the party. They have also said that they are chalking out future plans about joining some other party.

The reason for this provocation is the alleged high-handedness of city Congress president Pankaj Shah with Dr Parmar. The latter is known for his outspoken nature and rebellious temper and had an argument with Shah recently over party matters in the city.

The aggrieved leaders have also alleged that their public performance is being ignored by and large, while inactive party workers close to Shah are being accommodated on various posts. Thakar said the city unit president had ignored the hard work done by him, the two councillors and Dr Parmar in taking out the Navnirman Yatra of September 18, as well as their earlier performances.

The state leadership has apparently taken a serious note of this and asked Shah to secure explanation from the dissatisfied group.

GPCC president Siddharth Patel said: "We have not received any resignation from them, but they are free to do so. We will accept it. Their going to the media with threats of resignation is against the interest of the party. I have asked the city unit president to issue them show cause notice." He said the party will take stern action against them for their act of gross indiscipline. Patel said the charges levelled by them had no basis.

Apparently, the four rebels announced their plans to join the Nationalist Congress Party last Thursday.

Thakar and his supporters said that since they were AICC delegates, they sent "conditional resignations" straight to the AICC president and her political advisor "to forewarn them of the imminent debacle of the party in next Lok Sabha elections if the dissension at grassroots level was allowed to continue". Thakar added that the fight was for principles and not for personal matters. It was in protest against favouritism and groupism being allegedly encouraged by city unit chief Shah who is "favouring twin appointment of one Balubhai Parmar as convener and ward president in Saijpur Bogha despite being inactive for long in the party affairs," he added. There is no ward president in Saijpur for the past two years and now there is this move to appoint Parmar to that post, Thakar further said, adding that Shah had dealt in a high-handed manner with Dr Ganpat Parmar when a protest was lodged. He added that the situation was no different in the other city wards.

On the other hand, Shah said he had done as was requested in the case of appointments. As for disciplinary action, it was up to the state leadership to decide what step to take against them, he added.

Heading: HC attempts to check ‘systematic’ exploitation by state government - Indian Express
Content:
Nearly 30 per cent of them are physically unfit, but shy away from fitness tests for fear of losing their job

On Sunday night, two persons were injured when the driver of an AMTS bus collapsed on the steering wheel following an attack of seizure, near Kotarpur.

The accident has posed a serious question over the physical fitness of private bus drivers and their AMTS counterparts.

Sources said that nearly 30 per cent of the 500-odd drivers in AMTS are above 50 years of age. Most of them shy away from physical fitness check-up camps organised for them every two years. Officials believe that the reason for their reluctance is the fear of losing job on the ground of being physically unfit.

Speaking on condition of anonymity, an AMTS officer said the administration should come out with a reassuring mechanism that convinces them that they would not lose job just on this ground.

"We hold medical check-up camps for the crew at regular intervals. Many take part in such camps, but they are apprehensive about their reports," he said.

The driver involved in the Sunday night accident was an employee of a private operator and had suffered seizure while driving the bus on route number 105.

"We sent him to hospital for treatment, but he left the place and has not been traced yet," said traffic department sources in AMTS.

T G Jhalawadia, deputy municipal commissioner and outgoing transport manager, said that the 1,000-odd drivers on the AMTS rolls were younger — in the age group of 40

and 45 years — with an

average of ten years'

service record.

"Private operators are generally not concerned about the health of their staff. They are also lowly paid. We held a camp two years ago where the response was good. It is not that they are sacked in every case," he said.

At AMTS, he added, medical check-up in general, and eye check-up in particular, is a must for drivers who have reached

55 years.

The AMC will have to be extra careful while finalising contracts with private operators to run buses on BRTS routes because this would require persons who can drive fast with their reflexes firmly in place, he said.

Heading: Youth arrested in Pune for kidnapping employer’s son - Indian Express
Content:
Directs to resolve salary issues of Class III, IV contractual employees

The Gujarat High Court has directed the state Government to take appropriate decision in accordance with law in resolving the salary issues of about 50,000 Class III and Class IV contractual employees. The people have been employed at contractual salaries in the range of Rs 1,000 and Rs 2,500 per month.

Gujarat Chief Justice K S Radhakrishnan issued the verbal order while dismissing a PIL filed by the city-based Yogkshem Foundation for Human Dignity, an NGO working for civil rights.

Dr Rajendra Shukla, president of Yogkshem Foundation told Newsline that while the state government has been making such contractual appointments for a period of five years, the wages paid by the state government are less than those prescribed by the Minimum Wages Act.

"The state government systematically appointed people in Class III and Class IV category under a different nomenclature adding the term sahayak to them and started paying them pittance," said Shukla.

"Varg 3 ane varg 4 na samvargo hethan a yojana hethan je nimnuko thai, te nimnukna namabhidhan agan 'sahayak' shabda mukwano rahesha. (The word sahayak is to be affixed before the appointments are made under Class III and Class IV under this scheme)," the notification said.

It may be mentioned that the state Finance Department had issued a notification on February 16, 2006 recommending Rs 1,500 and Rs 2,500 as consolidated salaries for the Class IV and Class III employees, who were to be employed on contractual basis, as per the recommendations of the Dr P K Das committee.

Shukla said: "In the process, about 10,000 vidya sahayaks (teachers) were appointed who were to perform regular duties as teachers in various schools for a measly salary of Rs 2,500 per month for five years. More than 5,000 lokrakshaks (police constables) were appointed on a similar pay scale and condition, while about 10,000 Class IV employees such as cooks, barbers, washers, sweepers and peons were appointed at Rs 1,500 per month, while another 20,000 gram mitras were appointed at Rs 1,000."

He added that they had made two representations to the state government in this connection and asked for the redressal of this discrepancy. He said that even the Supreme Court had on several occasions said that non-payment of minimum wages was a violation of human dignity and right to life.

"While the pay commissions have periodically looked into the salary affairs, with the current rate of high inflation, the unorganised group are in no way protected from rising prices. With this order passed by the High Court, we hope the state government will now initiate at least some steps to redress the discrepancy," he added.

Heading: Three Bangladeshi youths arrested in Limbayat - Indian Express
Content:
Suthar did it to avenge admonishing by the boy's father

The Sabarmati police have arrested Ishwar Suthar, who had kidnapped his employer's 13-year-old son on June 25, from Pune.

The motive behind the kidnapping was to take revenge of an admonishment Suthar was subjected to by the boy's father. Earlier, Suthar had released the boy, Sanjay, from Pune, who had a dramatic reunion with his parents on August 16, almost two months after his kidnapping.

"Those two months were nightmarish for all of us. We did not have any clue about the whereabouts of our son. We didn't even know whether he was alive or not," said Sanjay's mother, Jyotsana.

She said: "Almost all our relatives took an oath for the safety of Sanjay, which was ultimately heard by God. I am least concerned about the punishment the accused gets. I am grateful to God that my son has returned safe."

Sanjay, a Class VII student of Triveni School in Ranip area told Newsline that he was taken to places like Udaipur, Surat, Nasik, Mumbai and Pune during his captivity. Suthar, a carpenter, also made him work during his stay.

"On June 25, he (Suthar) took me saying that we will come back after moving around in the area. Later, though, he took me to different places. He did not answer my queries to go home," Sanjay said. He, however, said that Suthar never beat him up.

Sanjay's father Dahyabhai said his son tried to contact him on the mobile. "But, did not succeed as he did not know to add zero before the mobile number," he said.

According to Dahyabhai, Suthar made Sanjay board an Ahmedabad-bound train from Pune and asked a fellow passenger to drop him at the Kalupur Railway Station. Sanjay informed his father on the fellow passenger's mobile phone of his arrival in Ahmedabad. His father and other relatives then received him from the railway station and intimated the police about it.

Sabarmati Inspector K B Zala said that following the boy's arrival in Ahmedabad and the information that the accused was in Pune, they sent a team there to arrest him after confirming his whereabouts. "In his statement to the police, Suthar said that his dispute with Sanjay's father was the reason for him to kidnap the boy and teach Dahyabhai a lesson," Zala said.

Heading: For Vadodara cops, cricket is as much a threat to peace as guns - Indian Express
Content:
Cops raided a house in Santoshinagar slum at Limbayat area on Monday night and arrested three youths hailing from Bangladesh.

The trio failed to produce documents substantiating their stay in India. They have been identified as Mohammed Riyan, Mohsin Shaikh and Hasibul Shaikh. Police recovered Rs 40,000 cash, three mobile phones and two US dollars from their possession.

Before coming to Surat, they stayed in places like Delhi, Kolkota and Mumbai some two months ago. Police are interrogating them to find out more details.

Heading: With Navratri round the corner, cops, organisers get on their toes - Indian Express
Content:
As major festivals draw to a close, carrying private weapons, gully cricket banned in city

With the festive season around the corner, the Vadodara police have issued a notification instructing all private security guards not to carry weapons, including their licensed weapons, in public places.

Police Commissioner Rakesh Asthana issued the notification in view of the recent terror attacks in New Delhi and Ahmedabad and as a preventive measure to stop any criminal activity during the holy month of Ramzan and Navratri celebrations.

The police notification has also banned firing in the air during celebration time. Further, the ban has been imposed on playing cricket in the bylanes, especially in the sensitive areas of the Walled City. This has been done considering the fact that gully cricket often results in quarrels, leading to major incidents.

The Vadodara police have said that semi-government and government officials with licensed guns can carry their weapons. Asthana has stated in the notification that the ban on private securitymen from carrying weapons has been imposed keeping in mind the past cases that occurred during festivals. "On many occasions, licensed weapons of private security guards have been used to threaten people and demand money," said Asthana. He pointed out that loan recovery agents, many a time, have used privately owned licensed weapons for loan recovery.

Asthana said that the ban has been issued as a preventive measure.

Heading: No smoking deadline gives health dept a high - Indian Express
Content:
As the city decks up for yet another Garba season with Navratri starting next week, metal detectors, breath analysers and CCTVs are being put in place by private security staff at the most happening Garba venues.

Various organisations and community members met Police Commissioner Rakesh Asthana on Monday to discuss security arrangements at the venues.

United Way of Baroda (UWB) Garba, one of the main organisers in the city, will install CCTVs at the venue along with breath analysers to check for alcohol consumption. "We have installed breath analysers especially for men at their restrooms, venue entry and near the food court," said UWB spokesperson Dolcy Simon.

Metal detectors will be installed at the entrance and only people with passes will be allowed entry to the venue, she said.

Additional security personnel will constantly keep a watch over the venue, while private security women would frisk the girls.

Faculty of Fine Arts, which hosts one of the most authentic and traditional Garba in the city, will install metal detectors as part of the security check.

"We will follow the police guidelines and place metal detectors to avoid any untoward incident," said Dean of the Faculty Deepak Kannal.

Additional private security personnel will also man entry points and the venue, he added.

Security for Irani Trophy

The Baroda Cricket Association (BCA), which is hosting the Z R Irani Trophy Test match for the first time, will have two police officers video-graphing the match.

Under the instructions of Police Commissioner Rakesh Asthana, the Bomb Detection Squad will scan the Reliance Cricket Stadium, venue of the match, before and after each day of play. Parking facilities have been extended only to VIPs and police personnel.

Heading: VMC cold to burning issue of fire safety - Indian Express
Content:
District-level monitoring panels to be put in place by September 30

The state Health Department is upbeat about introducing a ban on smoking in public places with effect from October 2.

It is busy charting out plans to organise separate state and district level monitoring committees for the purpose.

The Prohibition of Smoking in Public Places Rules, 2008, is to take effect from October 2 under The Cigarettes and Other Products (Prohibition of Advertisement and Regulation of Trade and Commerce, Production, Supply and Distribution Act, 2003, that was enacted by Parliament.

While the state level committee has already been constituted, the formation of district level committees is expected to be completed within the given deadline of September 30.

The state level committee will be responsible for keeping a tab on the district and local level committees, apart from reviewing the work of authorised officers. It will take decisions on all matters referred to it by the district committees, collect data, recommend and initiate action in specific cases of violations, set up a mechanism for reporting of violations and above all ensure the formation of district committees.

The committee will be headed by the secretary of health and family welfare department as the chairman; commissioner of health as the co-chairperson, and nodal officer for tobacco control in the state as member secretary, who will also hold the position for the district level committees. Among other members are the director general of the state police, commissioner of food and drugs administration, a representative of a leading NGO working in the field of health and tobacco control, an academician, a sociologist and a psychologist (nominated by the health secretary).

The members of the district level committee will be the district superintendent of police or the deputy commissioner of police, district public relations officer and drugs and food inspector. Other members will include one representative of a leading NGO working in the field of health or tobacco control, the principal of a leading college in the district, an academician, a psychologist and a sociologist (nominated by the district magistrate), district supply officer and divisional controller (GSRTC). Though the composition of the committee has been listed elaborately, details of each one's functions are missing.

While Gujarat happens to be one of the first states to have constituted the committee according to the health department authorities, a stringent implementing plan seems to be missing in the resolution to form the committee. The implementing powers of the committee have not been charted out in the resolution to constitute the monitoring committee. When contacted, Parish Dave, nodal officer for the tobacco control initiative said: "If a person is found smoking in public domain, he shall be fined Rs 200 as chalan. Though there has been no mention of the penalty for a person who repeats the act, there is a mention that in case a person is found smoking repeatedly in the same place, the onus of tackling him falls upon the head/owner of the place, according to the condition that may be."

Heading: Bomb hoax at SSG Hospital - Indian Express
Content:
Over 50 per cent of the city's high-rise buildings lack some of the basic fire safety provisions. But, the Vadodara Municipal Corporation has failed to take stern action against those flouting the norms.

Swank and posh from the outside, there are innumerable buildings in the city that have absolutely no system to fight a sudden fire.

According to the fire safety department, around seven per cent of the high-rise buildings in the city lack a fire safety mechanism, and over 50 per cent that have the fire safety system installed, have not got it renewed.

H J Taparia chief fire officer, Vadodara fire and emergency services said: "There are 327 high-rise buildings in the city. Out of this, 15 do not have a fire safety system installed at all. Although 312 buildings have the system, 50 per cent of them do not get them renewed annually."

This apart, many buildings also lack proper implementation of the fire exit system. "All the builders have to follow the norms listed by the General Development Control Rules (GDCR), but most of the structures fail in following the guidelines in some way or the other," said Taparia.

To be in purview of the GDCR laws, the buildings fail on various parametres of fire safety. "Each building should have at least 7.5 metre to 9 metre space for the fire vehicles to be parked within the premises," said Taparia.

The department also complains of builders' apathy in taking care of fire safety from the buildings' outside. "Even after repeated admonitions to the builders, overhead wiring poses a major problem during rescue operations. Lack of space for parking the fire vehicle added to the overhead wires pose a major hindrance in rescue operations when the stairs are to be elevated," said Taparia.

Most of the officials however, are either not aware of the existing problem, or simply turn a blind eye towards it. Town Development Officer C B Patel said, "We are not aware of any such building. The high-rise buildings that do not have fire safety system might be the very old buildings which were built before the norms were laid. As far as other buildings are concerned, we should be notified about them by the concerned department."

Heading: Cong bid to gain cheap publicity demoralising state police: Shah - Indian Express
Content:
Chaos reigned at the Sir Sayajirao General Hospital (SSGH) as the authorities received a letter on Tuesday afternoon stating that the hospital would be bombed if the Ahmedabad-blasts accused Abu Basher was not released.

The Bomb Detection Squad (BDS) of Vadodara police, however, checked the entire hospital premises and found that it was nothing but a hoax.

The police rushed to the spot almost immediately after the letter surfaced at the Resident Medical Office. "The letter posted at the Vadodara GPO the same day stated: 'Free Abu Basher, or else we will bomb the hospital. The letter was written in Hindi'," said Inspector G A Solanki.

Meanwhile, the BDS has told the hospital authorities to get the garbage bins cleaned every hour.

Ironically, the CCTV cameras that were to be installed at the SSGH after the Ahmedabad bloodbath are not yet in place. Hospital Superintendent V P Hathila said: "There is some technical snag in the cameras. They will be installed soon."

The hospital was also supposed to increase the number of security personnel with 25 Home Guards, 20 Gujarat Industrial Security Force and 10 more in-house private hospital guards.

Heading: AMC all set to welcome Red Ribbon Express - Indian Express
Content:
Politicking on the terror suspects is fast gaining ground in the state. Gujarat Minister for State (Home) Amit Shah has reacted sharply to statements by Opposition Congress Spokesperson Arjun Modvadia and said that the latter has been helping terrorists by raising doubts in people's mind regarding the efficiency of the state Police Department.

"There has been no prior intelligence lead on the Ahmedabad blasts from the Intelligence Bureau (IB)," said Shah. He added that Modvadia has been indulging in such statements only to garner cheap popularity. "In the process, the Congress is adversely affecting the morale of the State Police Department," he added.

Shah told Newsline on Tuesday that the report Modvadia referred to does not mention anything about possible blasts in Ahmedabad. "Modvadia has been talking about Safdar Nagori, Kanruddin Nagori and the son of Maulana Naseeruddin, all of whom were in jails in Madhya Pradesh and Karnataka during the Ahmedabad blasts. Even Safdar Nagori has not mentioned anything about the Gujarat blasts in his confessions," Shah added.

He said if Modvadia is really worried about the security of the people of the state, then he should concentrate on ways to get GUJCOC sanctioned by the UPA government.

Heading: Rahul to be in PAU today, officials clueless - Indian Express
Content:
The Ahemdabad Municipal Corporation (AMC) is all set to welcome the Red Ribbon Express (RRE), which will arrive here on Thursday.

The train will showcase an exhibition to spread public awareness on AIDS. It will remain at the Ahmedabad railway station for two days.

Municipal Commissioner I P Gautam told media persons that the number of HIV/AIDS cases in the city had gone down over the years. This, he said, was due to increased awareness and higher number of people turning up for HIV tests in the past five years.

There was a decline among commercial sex workers from 5.79 per cent to 4.23 per cent and MSM groups from 12 per cent to 9.79 per cent in the city over the past two years, he said. At the same time, there are 1,312 full-blown AIDS cases in the state, he added.

During 2007-08, 1.23 lakh people underwent HIV tests at nine blood banks in the city, out of which 299 were found positive. The year before that, 1.18 lakh people were tested, out of which, 302 turned positive for HIV.

The blood samples from 23,391 pregnant women were tested during 2007-08. The tests showed that 57 of them were HIV infected. They were treated accordingly so that their children did not fall prey to the disease.

The municipal commissioner said the AMC will take effective steps to increase the number of voluntary organisations in the city to carry out NACO projects. Once a person is found HIV positive, the responsibility of an NGO increases, he said.

The RRE will be welcomed at the Ahmedabad railway station in the presence of Mayor Kaanji Thakor and other civic office-bearers.

Heading: 35-year-old alleges torture by police - Indian Express
Content:
Interesting it may sound, the reality is that the current regime at the Punjab Agricultural University has no clue about the scheduled visit of Congress leader Rahul Gandhi to the university tomorrow evening.

The Gandhi scion will interact with farmers and hear their grievances. Dr Jagtar Singh Dhiman, additional director, Department of Communications and International Linkages, said, "We have no official information about the visit of Rahul Gandhi. No one has approached us and the university is in no way involved in the meeting."

Meanwhile, the top brass of the PAU officials will leave for Bathinda tomorrow where Chief Minister Parkash Singh Badal will address a kissan mela. Therefore, the university will have no senior official present on the campus to greet the Congress general secretary. The old regime of PAU led by former vice-chancellor Dr K S Aulakh has taken over the reigns of the scheduled meeting. Dr Aulakh said, "Over 80 farmers hailing from various parts of the state will meet Rahul Gandhi at the PAMETI hall in the university. Rahul had made it very clear that he does not want to meet any political leader. He had insisted that he wanted to meet people from the grassroot level."

Dr Aulkh further added, "We have invited farmers from various fields. These include the farmers who sow the usual rice and wheat, farmers who have diversified into other crops, farmers hailing from dairy fishery, floriculture, horticulture and other similar fields."

When asked about the absence of university officials, Dr Aulakh refused to comment stating, "This is not a university show."

Meanwhile Jagmohan Sharma president district congress committee said, "Rahul will land in the city around 3 pm where the workers of the party will meet him at the Amaltas. He will come to PAU and meet farmers and head back to Delhi the same evening."

Heading: Ludhiana residents lend a helping hand to Kashmiri orphans - Indian Express
Content:
Sanjay says he was taken to a private hospital after the assault; police deny charges

A man was allegedly beaten up by the policemen of the Sherpur police post on late Monday evening. The victim had to be admitted to the SPS Apollo hospital following the incident. Meanwhile, the police have denied the allegations.

Sanjay Kumar (35), a resident of Ambedkar colony near Sherpur chowk and who works with a mobile shop, has alleged that he was called to the Sherpur police post on Monday evening in connection with the investigation of the elopement of a girl. The victim had reportedly spoken to the couple on their cellphone.

Sanjay alleged that he was beaten up at the police station. After he fell unconscious, he was taken to the nearby hospital by the police and his family was informed.

Speaking to mediapersons, Sanjay's father Ramdev and mother Savitri Devi alleged that the police forcibly got Sanjay discharged from the hospital. They alleged that the police did so as they were investigating the elopement of a girl with a youth Ravinder Kumar. They said Ravinder had called up Sanjay to get his mobile phone recharged.

Meanwhile, Gurdev Singh, SHO, Focal Point police station, said, "The allegations of torture are absolutely false. Sanjay had been called to the Sherpur police post but he was not beaten up. In fact, as Sanjay was already down with fever, he was let off after questioning. We are investigating the case of elopement of a girl with a youth and when we got the details of mobile calls of that youth, we found that Sanjay had spoken to him. We just wanted to enquire about the whereabouts of the youth."

Heading: A few new faces among familiar names - Indian Express
Content:
Help has started pouring in for the Borderless World Foundation — a non-governmental organisation working for the welfare orphan girls in Kashmir — after the Newsline highlighted their noble task on September 22.

Supriya Kalra, Project Development Manager, Basera-e-Tabassum, a project being run by this NGO, said, "Some city based as well as Chandigarh-based people called up and offered their services in cash and kind.

The first call I got was from Dr Laikra who has offered financial as well as medical aid for the needy children.

A retried army officer from Chandigarh, who perhaps read the news on internet, has also offered his services for the NGO. Jagjit Singh, a city-based manufacturer of woolen socks wants to give socks for children.

I also got a few calls from other residents who have offered help."

With all thanks to these donors, Supriya said, "I heartfelt gratitude for these people who have come forward to help the 59 orphan girls."

Heading: Woman dies as roof caves in - Indian Express
Content:
The result for the Panjab University Senate elections for the principal and lecturers' constituency of affiliated colleges, was declared on Tuesday. Most of the present senators were re-elected though a few new faces have also find their place in the Senate.

The counting for the principal constituency of affiliated colleges started around 9 am. Of the 13 contestants in the fray for the eight seats of the principal constituency, AC Vaid, principal of GGDSD College, Sector 32 and Tejinder Kaur Dhaliwal, principal of Guru Nanak College for Girls, Muktsar, were the first to be declared elected.

A total of 70 votes were polled in this constituency of which one was declared invalid.

The two new faces that have made it to the senate this time are Janmit Singh, principal of Taravati Memorial Degree College, Bringali, Mukerian district of Hoshiarpur and RS Jhanji, principal of AS College, Khanna.

Others elected from the principal's constituency include BC Josan, principal of DAV College, Sector 10, Gurdip Kumar Sharma, principal of GGDSD College, Hariana (Hoshiarpur), HS Gosal, principal of Govind National College, Ludhiana and Satish Kumar Sharma, principal of Lajpat Rai DAV College, Jagraon, Ludhiana.

The declaration of the principal constituency results was followed by the counting for the lecturers' constituency of affiliated colleges that commenced at 11 am. In this constituency, many existing senators were re-elected though three new faces have also made it to the Senate. A total of 1990 votes were polled out of which 89 were declared invalid.

Mukesh Arora, a lecturer of SCD Government College, Ludhiana got the highest number of votes (307) in the lecturers' constituency. He has been a senator from the graduate constituency last year.

Another senator HS Dua, a lecturer in the Gujranwala Guru Nanak Khalsa College, Ludhiana was re-elected to the Senate. He was polled 244 votes. Dinesh Talwar was also re-elected with 240 votes. The new faces elected to the Senate this time are Dalip Kumar, lecturer in Government College for Girls, Sector 42, IS Sandhu, lecturer, DAV College, Abhor and Kuldip Singh, lecturer in Guru Nanak National College Doraha, Ludhiana.

Other senators re-elected to the Senate include RPS Josh, a lecturer of the Government College for Girls, Sector 42, and PS Gill, lecturer in Sri Guru Gobind Singh College, Sector 26.

Heading: A ‘model’ teacher, she does let waste go waste - Indian Express
Content:
A 56-year-old woman died and her 19-year-old daughter got injured as the roof of their room caved in at their Mohalla Ucha Vehra residence on Tuesday morning. The incident took place around 5 am when Charno and her daughter Rajji were fast asleep. Rajji suffered injuries on her head and was rushed to the Civil Hospital.

Khanna SDM Sukhwinder Singh Gill told Newsline, "I have asked the tehsildar to give a detailed report about the loss."

Charno's husband died one and half years ago. The roof of the room was supported by a wooden pillar which hit Charno and resulted in her death. Rajji was taken out of the debris by her neighbours one and half hours after the incident.

Heading: Food riots in Orissa, flood waters lap Taj Mahal - Indian Express
Content:
Science is a practical subject but a few teachers know how to teach it in an interesting way. State awardee Kusum Lata, a science teacher at Government Model Senior Secondary School in PAU, has the faculty of explaining complicated principles in a simple form. Not only her explanations but the models and aids which she uses to teach her topic have been prepared by her from waste material. From syringe to empty shoe-polish box, she has used it all to make students grasp toughest of physics or chemistry problems with an ease.

With an experience of 32 years, she has inspired her students to be more persistent. "Nothing is difficult to understand in science. Acquiring knowledge is a continuous process. I keep on learning with my students. The more questions they ask, the more I feel involved in my subject. Their queries give me inspiration to make simple but effective teaching aids for teaching them. By now I have made dozens of teaching aids and all with the help of trash."

Some of the aids prepared by her includes a working model of 'water is a good conductor of electricity', step down transformer, persistence of vision, working of watermill, magnetic separator, how sound waves travel, pin hole camera and the working of a vacuum cleaner."

Through an old greeting card and a half lead pencil, she explains the 'persistence of vision' theorem. By drawing a parrot on one side and cage on the other, when one moves the half lead pencil (fixed in between the card) like the milk churner, it seems as if the parrot is in the cage. "It is due to persistence of vision which remains in the eye for 1/16 of second and then replaced by the next vision," she explains. She draws a circle with seven different colours and rotates it like a bay-blade having pencil in the middle. The very next moment all the colours give the appearance of white colour. She dutifully elucidates her children about rainbow colours and tells that all these colours are made up of white.

Through a working projector made with the broken badminton racket and a box of cardboard, she shows different slides of biology.

Heading: Rahul praises Prime Minister on N issue, economy - Indian Express
Content:
Officials in eastern India struggled to provide aid to tens of thousands of flood victims after riots broke out on Wednesday, as floodwaters lapped the Taj Mahal compound but posed no immediate threat to it.

Monsoon rains, burst dams and overflowing embankments have unleashed bouts of flooding in South Asia in 2008, killing about 1,500 people, mostly in India but also in Nepal.

In Orissa, tens of thousands were still stranded on embankments and on highways after large areas were flooded when authorities opened sluice gates of a dam on the Mahanadi river after heavy rains last week.

Food riots broke out in many areas after villagers complained they were not getting relief supplies. Hungry victims beat up officials, blocked roads and looted relief materials.

"At least eight people sustained injuries after two groups of people clashed over distribution of relief," police officer Jitendra Kumar Dalai, who was injured, said by telephone from flood-hit Jagatsinghpur district.

Authorities said more than 100,000 people are still marooned and six more deaths were reported overnight, raising the death toll from floods in the eastern state to 35 in the past week.

More than 200 people have died in the past five days in India, most of them in Uttar Pradesh and Bihar, with rising rivers bursting their banks and swamping vast areas of farmland and villages, forcing thousands from their homes.

Officials said they had posted policemen near the famed Taj Mahal to monitor water levels in the swollen Yamuna river.

Flood waters had reached the outer wall of the Taj compound, but posed no danger to the 17th century mausoleum built by the Mughal emperor Shah Jahan on very high ground, officials said.

"Since the monument has weathered many a storm over the centuries, I do not think the rise in the Yamuna level or its increasing current could cause any harm to the structure," said K C Yadav, a police officer.

The flooding in the Yamuna, which also flows through New Delhi, was caused by the release of water from two barrages following heavy rains upstream.

The Taj Mahal, one of the seven wonders of modern world, is already under threat from industrial pollution which is turning its white marble a pale yellow.

Heading: India to seek action against infiltration from Zardari - Indian Express
Content:
Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Wednesday showered praise on Prime Minister Manmohan Singh for his handling of the nuclear and economic issues saying he had 'full faith' in him.

"Prime Minister Manmohan Singh ji has made India proud," Gandhi told reporters in Jalandhar.

"I have full faith in him....I will back him anywhere, anytime on this," the Congress general secretary said referring to Singh's handling of economy and the Indo-US nuclear deal.

Asked about the economic problems, he said, "You are creating a doomsday situation.

"The kind of impact the world economy had recently did not affect India. Inflation is also coming down and will come down.... India is growing at one of the fastest rates along with China," said Gandhi, attributing it to having an 'able' economist as the Prime Minister.

Taking a dig at the BJP, which has been critical of government's performance on the economic front, he said, "Our India Shining friends were not able to deliver on this".
