Once the area is declared eco-sensitive, no industrial unit with the potential to pollute would be allowed in the area. Mining and quarrying will also be out. The proposed 4000-MW NTPC thermal power project too would come under a cloud along with units engaged in the production of pig iron and cement pipes. The casualty would be Rane's capacity to patronise industrialists as well as his image of the man behind the economic transformation of the area.

Prabhu, however, maintained that his petition, far from being targeted at Rane, does not involve any politics at all. "The idea is not to create a controversy," Prabhu told The Indian Express, The 720 sq km Konkan area, he pointed out, boasts of the best variety of mango, Alphonso. The economy hinges on four occupations—fishing, farming, horticulture and tourism. Therefore, nothing should be done which adversely affects their longevity.

When told this could endanger the proposed power plant and industrial development, Prabhu contended, "Let local people decide what they want and let there be a study of the sustainability of what is proposed." Deshmukh's response to the petition, according to sources, was encouraging.

Heading: Cash-in-bag: CBI calls it judicial terror - Indian Express
Content:
Apprehensive that RJD chief and Railway Minister Lalu Prasad Yadav could use his influence at the Centre to indict the state Government, Bihar Chief Minister Nitish Kumar has managed to scuttle an inquiry in the Kosi breach by a central high-level expert committee. A team set up by the Ministry of Water Resources was supposed to go into the cause of the breach besides suggesting remedial measures to avoid a similar tragedy that has affected more than three million people in north Bihar. Now, the team will only suggest long-term measures after visiting the site of the breach.

The state Government raised the issue with the Principal Secretary to the PM arguing that since the state had already constituted a one-man judicial commission under a former chief Justice of the Patna High Court to probe the reasons of the Kosi breach, there was "no need" for a separate inquiry. To press the point, sources say, the state Government did not facilitate the visit of its Kosi Breach Closure Advisory Committee for a week to the site, citing "confusion over overlapping terms of reference" after the Centre constituted its team.

However, given that the breach in Kosi has taken place in the Nepalese territory, confusion remains whether the Nepal Government will allow the inspection of the one-man judicial commission set up unilaterally by the Bihar Government. The concerns that the commission may indict it would weigh heavily on the Nepal administration.

With Lalu and Kumar engaged in a blame game over the Kosi floods, the sparring over the incident is likely to further gain momentum after the state Government's commission submits its report in six months.

Heading: PF scam accused nailed judges in confession - Indian Express
Content:
Claiming that the offence committed by the accused involved in the cash-at-judge's-door case was more serious than that of triggering the serial blasts in Delhi, the CBI special public prosecutor on Tuesday termed it an example of "judicial terrorism".

The prosecutor made the comment twice while demanding an extended police remand of Ravinder Singh, a Delhi-based hotelier and co-accused in the case. As defence counsel A S Chahal asked if the CBI was trying to call Ravinder a terrorist, the prosecutor said: "We never said he is a terrorist but the case is more serious than terrorism."

The court sent Ravinder to CBI custody till September 27.

Demanding a 10-day CBI remand, the prosecutor said the accused had disclosed some names, in the presence of whom he had handed over Rs 15 lakh to Sanjeev Bansal, former Haryana additional advocate general, for delivering it to a judge in Chandigarh. He said the CBI had to confront Ravinder with the people he had met before his surrender. The hotelier would be taken to Delhi for the purpose.

However, the defence counsel said: "There is no incriminating evidence against Ravinder. The CBI has not listed any ground on which they are demanding the police remand."

The court, meanwhile, allowed the plea of Ravinder's wife, Mohinder Kaur, seeking directions to the CBI to break the locks on Ravinder's second house in Delhi by 2 pm on Wednesday. Kaur has moved an application, requesting the Chief Justice for getting the case transferred to Delhi. The Chief Justice reportedly told the defence counsel that only the Supreme Court could transfer the case outside Punjab.

Heading: Church attacks: Central team for ‘more action’ - Indian Express
Content:
On April 28, Ashutosh Asthana, key accused in the Ghaziabad Provident Fund (PF) scam, recorded his statement alleging the involvement of 34 judges—one from the apex court, 10 from the High Courts and 23 district-level judicial officers.

His 29-page statement was recorded under Section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, conferring it legal sanctity to be treated as preliminary evidence against the persons named.

Asthana, 46, worked as the central nazir (chief treasurer) during 2001-2008 — the period when large sums of money were withdrawn fraudulently from the PF accounts of the court's Class III and IV employees. Detailing the modus operandi, Asthana, who began working at the Ghaziabad district courts in February 1993, said the money was withdrawn from the PF accounts of the court employees years before maturity, with the consent of the judges, all of whom had served as district judges in Ghaziabad and were authorised to sign the vouchers.

Asthana also reportedly confessed that a large number of Class III and Class IV employees existed only on paper and bogus PF payments were made to them, with the knowledge of the judges. His statement listed the names of district judges who allegedly sanctioned withdrawal of money from the treasury as well as judges who had received consumer goods from him.

"Goods like TVs, refrigerators, ACs, touch screen mobile phones, furniture and other articles used to be supplied to the judges on a regular basis, and I also used to pay for their tours and shopping," says his confessional statement. "I used to withdraw the fund illegally from the general PF, at the instructions of the judges in charge of Ghaziabad. I supplied goods worth crores to judges named by me on a monthly basis," he said.

Heading: After spat with Sreedharan, AP Govt scraps contract - Indian Express
Content:
Stepping up the pressure on Karnataka Government in the aftermath of attacks on churches, a Central team assessing the situation told the state's BJP Government to take more action and said preventive measures could have been better.

"More action is needed (by the state Government)," Special Secretary (internal security) M L Kumawat told reporters here on Tuesday night in response to questions on whether the two-member team he was leading was satisfied with the action taken by the state Government.

The team visited Mangalore and Udupi, the scene of church attacks, and reviewed the situation at a meeting with officials and met victims.

On his way back to Bangalore, Kumawat said there was "better scope for preventive measures".

"We have advised district officials that those responsible (for the attacks) should be brought to book; they (those who have not been taken into custody so far) must be arrested forthwith and a sense of confidence must be instilled in the people," he said.

To a question on "laxity" of the police department in preventing the attacks, Kumawat said it was premature to make a statement. The team would be meeting state officials in Bangalore on Wednesday. "We cannot arrive at any conclusion without hearing and meeting the officials," he said.

The team would submit its report to the Centre on September 25, he said. A R Infant, ADGP (Law and Order), A M Prasad (IGP Western Range) were among those who accompanied the Central team.

The visit, as also the two advisories that the Centre had sent following the church attacks, has come under fire from Chief Minister B S Yeddyurappa who claimed "law and order situation is very good in the state" and questioned the UPA Government's moves.

Meanwhile, lashing out at both the Congress and the BJP, JD(S) president Deve Gowda on Tuesday alleged the former had failed to contain incidents of communal violence and accused the saffron party of engaging in "state-sponsored atrocities".

Commenting on the incidents of churches being attacked in Karnataka, Gowda sought immediate removal of the BJP-led Government in the state. "It is the failure of the Union Government to take action in accordance with the constitutional provisions. There is no other way. Serving advisories to the state Government is not going to solve the problem, it is just a piece of paper for the state Government," Gowda told PTI after meeting Christian leaders.

Heading: Susairaj gets half-hour meeting with Emile in court - Indian Express
Content:
Rattled by Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC) Managing Director E Sreedharan raising doubts over the Hyderabad Metro Rail, the Andhra Pradesh Government terminated its consultancy contract with DMRC on Tuesday, as the controversial project triggered a political storm in the state.

The DMRC has been the prime consultant for the Rs 12,100-crore Hyderabad Metro project. Although the contract period was for five years, official sources confirmed it has been terminated. "We will immediately initiate the process for selecting a new consultant," the sources said, adding that the process would be completed in December.

The decision came following acute embarrassment caused to the state Government in the wake of Sreedharan's stinging criticism of the project. Dubbing the project as a political scandal in the making, the Delhi Metro chief had raised objections over handing over 296 acres of prime government land to the private developer and said it was tantamount to selling the family silver.

Sreedharan had expressed reservations over the way the Government had awarded a contract to the infrastructure firm Maytas-led consortium and said the private developer would reap windfall profit.

Expressing concerns over the private sector's direct involvement, he warned that BOT (build-operate-transfer) model could backfire.

The issue triggered a political storm with Opposition parties sharing Sreedharan's apprehensions. The TDP, CPI, BJP and Praja Rajyam, demanded that the details of the agreement be made public.

Stung by Sreedharan's charges, contained in a letter he wrote to Planning Commission Deputy Chairman Montek Singh Ahluwalia, the Congress Government has sought an unconditional apology, failing which it threatened to sue him.

In a letter to Sreedharan on Monday, Principal Secretary (Municipal Administration) and Hyderabad Metro Rail (HMR) Chairman C V S K Sarma also threatened to take legal measures for defamation.

Heading: Kerala High Court cancels golf club takeover for now - Indian Express
Content:
Not even her lawyers could fathom why Kannada actress Maria Monica Susairaj suddenly wanted to meet her fiancée Emile Jerome, the man she has accused of killing television production executive Neeraj Grover.

Susairaj, co-accused in the murder case along with Jerome, recently caught up with him within the premises of the Esplanade court for nearly half an hour. "She suddenly requested a meeting with Jerome. Following her request, an application was moved before the court, which granted her permission to meet Jerome on September 18," said Susairaj's advocate Murthy Acharya.

Though Susairaj's lawyer G Kannur confirmed the meeting, he refused to divulge any information on the conversation between the two.

Susairaj also spent some time with her family members who had come from Bangalore to meet her.

On May 7, Susairaj and Jerome had allegedly stabbed Grover to death. They then allegedly dismembered the body and burnt it at Manor in rural Thane district before returning to her suburban apartment to clean up, paint the walls and destroy all traces of the crime. 

Susairaj has maintained from the beginning that it was Jerome who murdered Grover in a fit of rage at seeing him at her apartment. Her confession to the police also states that Jerome raped her after the crime. Two bail applications moved by her lawyers before the sessions court asked that she be accused only of destroying evidence, not of murder.

Last week, Susairaj's advocate Harshad Ponda also told the court that she was a "victim of circumstances" created by Jerome.

The court has earlier rejected her bail plea observing that there was enough prima facie evidence to prove Susairaj's involvement in the murder.

Heading: Boycotting classes must be last resort, says M A Baby - Indian Express
Content:
While nullifying the state government's controversial take-over of the Trivandrum golf club on Tuesday on grounds of procedural violations, the Kerala High Court nonetheless upheld the right of the state government to own the century old-club.

Acting on a petition by the club management challenging the government action, the court said a fresh show cause notice should be served to the management if the government wanted to take back the property. Justice V Giri said the club was denied natural justice by the hasty action of the government.

Though the government had claimed that the club had violated the stipulated norms regarding the use of the property, the notice slapped on the club had not mentioned the reasons for scrapping the club licence, the judge said. If the government wanted to take over the club, a fresh show cause notice would have to be served to the club within a month. Moreover, the charge sheet against the management should be clearly mentioned in the memo and the club should be heard before proceeding with further actions and the entire process wrapped up within four months, the court said.

The club, which counts prominent politicians, business men and bureaucrats among its members is spread over 24 acres of prime land in the city. The May 31 state Cabinet decision to take over the club on the ground that the land belonged to the government had sparked off a furore.

Heading: Left looking for allies in TN, says Raja - Indian Express
Content:
Party central committee member and Kerala education minister M A Baby on Tuesday said classes should be boycotted only as a last resort.

His remark assumes political significance against the backdrop of West Bengal Chief Minister Budhadeb Bhattacharjee's anti-bandh comments and subsequent censure from the party.

While announcing the schedule of school youth festivals this academic year, Baby said he could not agree with students boycotting classes every now and then.

"Boycotting classes is a sharp weapon. It should be taken out only after exhausting all other means of protest. It should be done only for serious issues," advised Baby, who had led many student agitations during his innings as the leader of the Students Federation of India, the student outfit of the CPM.

Baby's "distress call" came in the wake of the loss of several school days this academic year due to agitations by students as well as teachers.

In Kerala, agitations organised by the SFI, the KSU and the ABVP have always taken a heavy toll on the academic calendar.

Heading: Expulsion of MPs: notice to Speaker - Indian Express
Content:
Downplaying the statement made by state secretary D Pandian on an alliance with the AIADMK, CPI national secretary D Raja said the Left parties were exploring the 'fluid' political situation in Tamil Nadu.

While maintaining that the Left was opposed to the Congress, the BJP and its allies, Pandian had said on Monday that the CPI would explore the prospects of alliance with all parties, including the AIADMK. However, according to sources, a relationship with Jayalalithaa's AIADMK is not favoured by all members of the Left front due to her pro-Hindutva stance on many issues in the recent past.

"A non-BJP, non-Congress alternative is the aim of Left parties. Today, the situation for such an alternative is gaining prominence in this multi-party democracy," said Raja. When asked about the buzz surrounding Pandian's comment about a possible alliance with the AIADMK, Raja said. "The situation in TN is very fluid. Within the parameters set by the national leadership, the state leadership can evolve suitable electoral lines and explore all possibilities."

Heading: PM ‘hopeful’ of wrapping n-deal during visit - Indian Express
Content:
The Delhi High Court on Tuesday issued a notice to Lok Sabha Speaker Somnath Chatterjee after two Members of Parliament challenged their expulsion from the House for defying their party whip to vote in favour of the UPA Government.

Samajwadi Party MPs Jai Prakash Rawat from Mohanlalganj and SP Singh Baghel from Jalesar had separately approached the court against their termination.

Appearing for both, Munendra Kumar Singh submitted before Justice G S Sistani that the termination order was in violation of the law of natural justice. "The termination order was issued without giving my clients any opportunity to be heard before the Speaker. This is against the natural justice of law," Singh submitted.

He further said, "However, two others—Raj Narain Budholia (Hamirpur) and Munawwar Hussain (Muzaffarnagar) —were given an extension and opportunity to appear and defend themselves."

Jai Prakash and Baghel were expelled with two others MPs from the party for defying the whip to vote in favour of the UPA Government's trust vote in the Lok Sabha. The party had then moved a petition before the Speaker seeking their termination from the House. The court will hear the matter on November 4.

Heading: Undecided on terror law: Manmohan - Indian Express
Content:
Hours before he landed in New York and on a day when the Senate Foreign Relations Committee is slated to consider mark-up of the 123 agreement, Prime Minister Manmohan Singh on Tuesday said he was "still hopeful" that the Indo-US civil nuclear cooperation agreement could be wrapped up during his visit despite the preoccupation of the US Congress with other issues.

While his officials, including Planning Commission Deputy Chairman Montek Singh Ahluwalia, continued to maintain that New Delhi was in no hurry to burden the visit with large expectations, the PM was particularly confident when asked whether he would be disappointed if the agreement did not come through in this visit.

"In politics, one has to learn to live with disappointment. But I do not think we have reached that point yet. I am still hopeful that it will happen," he said during an informal media interaction on his way to New York. It may be noted that US Secretary of State Condoleezza Rice may visit India in October first week.

On being pressed further, he acknowledged that the US Congress has other important issues to deal with and went on to add: "Let us see what happens. I am not an astrologer".

According to the latest assessments by the PM's energy security panel after the NSG clearance, India should now import uranium for about 20-30,000 MW which will free up domestic uranium for the fast breeder programme and once that delivers, India could generate up to 600,000 MW nuclear power by 2050. Sources said plans were afoot in this direction. Prior to this, the DAE had planned only 200,000 MW by 2050. Singh will be meeting US President George W Bush in Washington on Thursday, where the latter has planned an exclusive dinner for him in the White House. Bush, officials said, has only held about six such dinners in the White House during his entire presidency.

The last time when the two leaders met on the sidelines of the G8 Summit in Sapporo, Singh had conveyed that India would go ahead with the nuclear deal, which led to withdrawal of support by the Left parties. This time Singh will be waiting to hear from Bush about the progress of the 123 agreement in the US Congress. Both leaders have invested large political capital into the nuclear deal and would hope to announce completion as Bush draws closer to the end of his term.

Singh was, however, cautious on his upcoming meeting with newly-elected Pakistan President Asif Zardari on Wednesday. "I will talk about the meeting later... there are enormous challenges in our relations, we have to see how to convert these challenges into opportunities so that peace can be brought by working together."

While the nuclear deal weighs lighter on Singh's head, it is the news about the financial meltdown and its impact on the global economy that has occupied his mind in the last few days. Singh said he used the overnight stopover at Frankfurt to read up on what had been happening in the global financial sector.

He described it as a "very unusual situation" that needs careful studying.

However, when asked whether the current crisis had challenged his belief in the market economy, he felt that there were lessons to be drawn from what had happened. He was clear that the current crisis underlined the need for multilateral monetary institutions to play a greater role in what he called stronger "multilateral surveillance" of money flows.

Heading: Azamgarh: Delhi team conducts raids - Indian Express
Content:
As repeated terror attacks have triggered a debate in the political circles over bringing in a stronger anti-terror law, Prime Minister Manmohan Singh on Tuesday said he was still undecided on the issue and had asked a group of officials to study the report of the Administrative Reforms Commission (ARC), which calls for a new law, and come up with their suggestions.

Having made it clear earlier that his Government was not against a strong anti-terror law, Singh wondered whether a law was the sole answer to the menace of terrorism. "It is not just a question of bringing in a law. There are complex issues involved. In fact, I was just reading British newspapers where (Britain) they have prosecuted many people, but are not able to convict. So, I have not reached any conclusion yet. There is an Administrative Reforms Commission report, which I have asked a group of officials to study and report to me," he said.

After the serial blasts in Delhi, a special Cabinet meeting had been convened where several issues related to countering terror, including a stronger anti-terror law, were discussed but Information and Broadcasting Minister Priyaranjan Dasmunsi had clarified the next day that the Government would not bring back POTA. However, that statement was at odds with the PM's earlier observation of not being ideologically against such a law.

Clearly, there is a churning within the Government and the Congress party on the issue, especially after the ARC report was submitted by Veerappa Moily. But unlike some of his other colleagues, the PM is clear that the Centre has to play a role when it comes to countering terrorism.

When asked about why states should not be encouraged to draw up their own anti-terror laws as law and order was state subject, the PM said: "I am not getting into Centre-State relations here. The Centre has the responsibility to assess and decide whether it needs a law or not. We are there to do all we can to help the states and we will do that."

Singh was non-committal when he was asked about the prospects of holding elections in Jammu and Kashmir on time. "I think that is for the Election Commission to decide." On being pressed further, he added, "Who can say when is the right time (for elections)?" He was equally evasive to a question on whether he planned to contest for Lok Sabha. "We will cross the bridge when we come to it," he added.

On the other pressing domestic issue of rising prices, it was left for Deputy Chairman of Planning Commission Montek Singh Ahluwalia to claim prices would come down soon and that the inflation rate had not been moving up as rapidly as it was doing few months back. "I think we can expect inflation to come back to single digit before the end of this financial year," he added.

Heading: India Post, a new red-letter day - Indian Express
Content:
The Delhi Police and Anti-Terror Squad (ATS) of the Uttar Pradesh conducted searches at various places in Azamgarh district early Tuesday to collect information about the absconding blast accused. Shaqib Nisar, one of the arrested accused brought by the Delhi Police, guided the team to the houses of other absconding Indian Mujahideen operatives. The cops later scrutinised bank accounts of slain terrorist Atif and his associates Saif and Arif. The ATS and the Delhi Police collected details of the transactions.

Deputy Inspector General ATS Rajiv Krishna said: "Our team was already camping in Azamgarh to gather intelligence about the absconding accused. The ATS team scrutinised two bank accounts and a transaction of Rs 30,000 was found in Arif's account. In other accounts too, there were usual transactions." Delhi Police PRO Rajan Bhagat said they did not have any information about major transactions in the accounts of any of the accused.

The areas where the search took place were cordoned off by the PAC and the local police in a bid to avoid any untoward incident.

Additional DG (Law and Order) Brij Lal said: "The Delhi Police had come to Azamgarh in search of the absconding accused. They coordinated with the SSP, Azamgarh, before initiating the operation in Sanjarpur area and other places. The police team interrogated Dr Javed Akhtar, the father of one of the wanted accused, and five others — Abdullah, Saifullah, Azeem Ahmed, Dr Fakre Alam and Salam Khan". The ADG said they would seek remand of Ahmedabad blast accused Abu Bashar and those arrested in Delhi blast case, if required.

The Delhi team led by SHO Okhla started their searches at Sanjarpur around 6.30 am and visited the houses of Shahdab alias Bhai, Asadullah Akhtar, Arif and Junaid. They collected some documents, including photo albums and CDs from the houses of Arif and Asadullah. The cops failed to trace the house of Shehzad alias Pappu as they were not aware of his father's name and none of the locals came forward to identify him.

Azamgarh DIG Vijay Kumar said nothing significant was recovered either in the search or in the scrutiny of the bank accounts, he said, adding that the team left for Delhi by evening.

Heading: Kapil Dev to join Territorial Army - Indian Express
Content:
From the scarlet "Scinde dawk" of the pre-lithograph era to the ubiquitous streetside post box, the colour red has been a lasting leitmotif in the history of the Indian Postal Department. And it will remain so for several years to come. When Minister for Communications and IT A Raja and Minister of State for Communications and IT Jyotiraditya Scindia unveiled the new logo of India Post on Tuesday—a red envelope with three yellow streaks forming 'wings', designed by Ogilvy & Mather—in a not-so-sarkari ceremony replete with dancing laser beams, it was a red-letter event for the largest postal network in the world. A noticeable change in the look and feel of the system, it was felt, was necessary to underline the efforts to redeem India Post from its romanticised antiquity and "perceived inadequacies".

It's a timely endeavour. In an electropolis of 10 million Internet connections and 300 million mobile phone users, the culture of communication seems to thrive on Broadband-enabled e-mailathons, fashionably truncated text messages, and multiple chat windows on every workstation. And for mailing across that occasional, still-indispensable document which cannot yet be broken down into neat little electronic packets of data, there are the 'express' courier services. The raison d'etre of dropping off a handwritten letter in the big red box at the street corner or at a dak ghar manned by sleepy clerks and waiting for at least a couple of days for it to be delivered may be lost on you, but for a village untouched by the telecom revolution, the postal service is still the only window to the world.

The window is now set to open wider, thanks to Project Arrow, a Department of Posts initiative flagged off by Raja last month, which is giving a much-needed fillip to the countrywide network of 1.5 lakh post offices, almost 1.4 lakh of which are located in rural areas. As many as 52 post offices have already been revamped with their performance being reviewed on a daily basis. Corporate branding is the next step.

With over 10 crore money orders a year, 17 crore savings scheme accounts—which also facilitate payment of wages under the NREGS—and deposits of Rs 5,40,000 crore, India Post is more than a snail mail service, it is a system of integration that is ingrained in the social fabric. Offering e-post, life insurance, e-billing, social security schemes and value-added financial services, the post office today is a multi-purpose facility that can potentially plug the gaps in India's growth story.

To tap that potential and effect a smooth transition to a business model that can survive the competition of the day, Raja and Scindia roped in global consulting firm McKinsey. The core precept, Scindia stressed, remains the same: "Service, with a smile, to the one-billion-strong populace". The new corporate identity, however, promises to deliver convenience, rather than letters, with services like micro-credit, computerised banking, standardised one-stop counters, instant money orders, passport application submission, express parcel processing, call centres to track Speed Post and more.

The ambitions are pitched perilously high. A few years ago, someone walking into a post office would not have been referred to as a "customer". Now, when Raja talks of turning India Post into "a parcel and logistics giant, in the domestic as well as the international sector" and Scindia works towards building a "thinking organisation", it does raise eyebrows. But, as McKinsey Partner Gautam Kumra pointed out, postal systems like that of Italy were rescued from bankruptcy in a matter of a few years. A humble beginning has been made. India Post launched its first aircraft last year to ferry Speed Post and mail to the farthest reaches of the Northeast.

Heading: SC refuses to restore Janata symbol - Indian Express
Content:
Starting an innings of a different kind, former Indian cricket captain Kapil Dev is set to join the Armed Forces as an honourary officer. He will don the Army uniform at a glittering ceremony on Wednesday.

The former cricketer has been roped in to join the Armed Forces by the Territorial Army (TA), which is celebrating its 59th anniversary this year, and will be accorded the rank of an honourary Lieutenant Colonel.

Kapil confirmed to this newspaper that he is joining the TA as an honourary officer on Wednesday. Sources said Kapil will get his rank tags and badges personally from Army Chief General Deepak Kapoor at a special function.

While Kapil will not take part in the rigorous training of the regular Territorial Army, a part time "citizens' army" consisting of civilians who act as a reserve force, he will act as a "brand ambassador" for the Armed Forces. The Army, sources said, approached Kapil to join in as an honourary officer earlier this year. "The idea is to get a well-known personality from the sports field and help promote the Armed Forces as a good career choice for youth. Kapil will inspire youngsters to come and join the Army," a senior officer said.

The Territorial Army is part of the regular Army and has various roles, including relieving the regular personnel from static duties and assistance to the civil administration in times of calamities. TA personnel can also voluntarily serve in active duty for short durations and several officers and men have won gallantry awards for exceptional bravery.

Interestingly, the Territorial Army, which has a sanctioned strength of just over 40,000 personnel, was keen on roping in young MPs and MLAs to join its ranks to set an example for youngsters. A presentation was also held at the Parliament house last year but the force did not receive any applications from the elected representatives.

Heading: ONGC cites Rs 24-cr loss, calls against bandhs - Indian Express
Content: The Supreme Court on Tuesday dismissed an appeal filed by Janata Party president Subramanian Swamy seeking restoration of the "Chakra Haldar" election symbol to his party. However, a Bench comprising Justices Ashok Bhan and V S Sirpurkar gave liberty to Swamy to approach the Election Commission for freezing the symbol, whose exclusive use by the Janata Party was forbidden under the Election Symbols (Reservation and Allottment) Order  in 2000. The Election Commission through its September 27, 2000 order had held that the Janata Party could not exclusively use the election symbol after it lost its status as a national party due to its poor performance in the 1996 General Elections. Meanwhile, the Janata Party on Tuesday said the party was actively considering choosing a new party symbol.

Heading: One-time spectrum charge beyond 6.2 Mhz on anvil: Raja - Indian Express
Content:
Though the number of bandhs in Assam have come down recently due to increasingly hostile public opinion, the state still has a long way to go if the state-owned oil giant ONGC's experience is anything to go by. A 100-hour bandh called last month by a local organisation against ONGC in Sivasagar district, where most of its operations are concentrated, has caused a loss to the tune of Rs 24.16 crore. This is in addition to a Rs 3.22 crore loss to the state Government in terms of royalty on crude as well as taxes.

"We want a strong public opinion against bandhs. Look at the loss all of us suffer. It is not just us. The impact trickles down to the local economy too," R S Sharma, ONGC CMD said on Monday. The All Tai Asom Student's Union, a local student organisation had called a bandh last month following complaints that drilling operations within a radius of 125 metres of the Rang-ghar, Asia's oldest amphitheatre built during the Ahom era, had damaged the heritage structure.

Heading: Post office act amendment bill in this Parliament session - Indian Express
Content:
The government will come out with new spectrum charges which could include a one-time fee by the end of October, Telecom Minister A Raja said today. "We are discussing the issue with Ministry of Finance. A one-time charge could be there over and above the adjusted gross revenue of the telecom companies for spectrum above 6.2 Mhz. We expect to take a decision by the end of October," Raja said on the sidelines of a Department of Post function.

The move will raise the cost of spectrum for operators. At present, Bharti, Vodafone, Idea, BPL hold more than 6.2 Mhz of spectrum.

Earlier Trai had recommended a one-time spectrum charge for 2G spectrum beyond 10 MHz for GSM operators and five MHz for CDMA operators. The regulator had suggested that for every additional one MHz beyond 10 MHz in Mumbai, Delhi and category A circles, operators should be charged Rs 16 crore.

But DoT's view is since GSM spectrum allotment beyond 10 MHz is rare, and there is no spectrum allotment beyond five MHz for CDMA operators, no substantial additional revenue would accrue to the government.

Says it's Swan which is to tie up with Etisalat

Telecom Minister A Raja today revealed that the company which was widely speculated to be in the final stages of inking a deal with UAE's Etisalat is Swan Telecom. "I am told unofficially that one of the companies which got spectrum in some of the areas is going to align with Etisalat," he said and when pressed to name the Indian company involved he said it is "Swan". Swan Telecom has got the start-up spectrum in Delhi and in some other states.

Heading: 968 state employment exchanges to be revamped - Indian Express
Content:
Telecom Minister A Raja today said efforts are on to introduce the Post Office Act Amendment Bill, that brings courier companies under the ambit of its regulation, in the forthcoming session of Parliament.

"We have circulated the Bill inputs among the different ministries. We plan to introduce the Bill in the current session of Parliament," Raja said after inaugurating the new logo for a forward-looking India Post.

The government plans to amend the Indian Postal Act to bring courier companies under the ambit of this Act, a move that may hit hard the private players but could prove to be a shot in the arm for the Indian Postal Department.

If approved, this would bar the private courier service providers from carrying packets weighing below 150 grams and could give a major blow to the courier companies which earn a major share of their revenues from letter and packets weighing below half a kilogram.

The government is also planning to bring in a regulator called the Mail Regulatory and Development Authority to monitor this sector better. Every service provider, other than the Department of Posts (DoP), has to be registered.

The Bill also proposes to set up a Universal Service Obligation Fund (USO Fund), to which private service providers with at least Rs 25 lakh annual turnover would contribute 10 per cent of their turnover. The government would use the USO Fund to fulfil its obligation of providing affordable postal service to every citizen.

Heading: Financial closure for 2 mega plants this yr: Rel Power - Indian Express
Content:
The central government has now decided to revamp 968 state Employment Exchanges by way of modernising and upgrading their operations. In fact, the Employment Exchanges will be given a new name to reflect their changing character — Employment Promotion and Guidance Centre.

In an initiative undertaken by the labour and employment ministry, the central government has initiated discussions with all the state governments to modernise such exchanges that require reforms in their functioning. The exchanges will be computerised and connected to a national web portal, called the employment exchange portal. The ministry has pegged the cost of this exercise at Rs 600-700 crore, said a ministry official.

The ministry had earlier asked Hyderabad-based National Institute of Smart Governance to submit a detailed project report (DPR) on the revamping of Employment Exchanges. The report has received the clearance from Directorate General of Employment and Training, but is awaiting the labour and employment ministry's finance department nod. However, the approval is likely to come through in a week's time, told the source.

"The Employment Exchanges will be linked with Industrial Training Institutes, which will provide information about trained manpower available. This information can be accessed by industry to match vacancies," said labour and employment joint secretary and director general (employment and training) Sharda Prasad.

For implementation of the report, which is estimated to take two and a half years, the government is planning to engage reputed IT software companies. Initially, it will implement the scheme on a pilot basis across five states, one each from north, south, west, east and north-east regions. The pilot will be launched in within seven months, said an official. The online portal will enable generation of quick lists of candidates as per the requirement of employers and accordingly call letters could be generated.

It will facilitate online registration of vacancies by employers. Computerised counselling is likely to be made available to unemployed youth through this portal. The Employment Exchange, according to the ministry's estimates, had live registrations of over four crore people by 2005-end.

Heading: HTC comes out of the shadows with Google phone - Indian Express
Content:
Anil Ambani-led Reliance Power today said it will tie up funding of Rs 36,000 crore by this year for two ultra mega power projects of 4,000 MW capacity each in Sasan and in Krishnapatnam.

"We are likely to achieve financial closure for a project of Sasan's size and complexity requiring nearly Rs 20,000 crore worth of investment this year," Reliance Power Chairman Anil Ambani told shareholders at the company's AGM here.

"The financial closure for the project (at Krishnapatnam) is expected later this year," he said. The investment in Krishnapatnam would be Rs 16,000 crore. The company is also gearing up for the nuclear opportunities that would arise after the government opens up the sector for private players. "We have had a dedicated team working on the nuclear opportunity for the past three years, and have conducted a series of discussions with the leading international players in the nuclear power industry," Ambani said. The first private nuclear power project to come up would take up to 8 to 10 years, he said.

The company plans to spend $28 billion on building 28,200 MW of coal-fired and water-based electricity plants in the next eight years.

Company to tap wind, solar power

Reliance Power has said it is exploring opportunities in wind, solar and fuel cell-based power. "We are considering the possibility of setting up a one-of-a-kind 100 MW Grid Interactive Concentrating Solar Power Plant through an exclusive relationship with a technology provider," Reliance Power chairman Anil Ambani told shareholders at the company's AGM.

Heading: Panel to decide on ECB norms for other cos - Indian Express
Content:
When executives from Google and T-Mobile converge on a stage in New York Tuesday to unveil the first mobile phone powered by Google's software, the event will be a coming-out party of sorts for another, far more obscure, but no less ambitious company — HTC.

The Taiwanese electronics manufacturer was chosen by Google more than two years ago to build the first mobile phone based on its "Android" software in large part because of its proven ability to design and build head-turning mobile devices.

For HTC, it amounted to another victory in its efforts to do battle for the high end of the phone market with the likes of the iPhone maker Apple, BlackBerry's maker Research in Motion and others.

"I think we are ready," Cher Wang, a Taiwanese plastics mogul's daughter who helped found the company in 1997 and serves as its chairwoman. "We have a strong customer base of people who want our devices."

A lot of Americans already use HTC phones — they just do not know it. HTC accounted for about one in six smartphones in the United States in the first half of this year, but the overwhelming majority of them do not carry the HTC brand,.

For much of the past decade, the company operated in relative obscurity as a contract manufacturer for companies like Compaq, Palm and many cellphone carriers, who stamped their own brands on the products.

About two years ago, HTC decided to come out of the shadows with an ambitious goal: establish a global consumer electronics brand that its executives hope will become synonymous with quality.

"We are far from being there," said John Wang, HTC's chief marketing officer. But Mr. Wang said that the company is off to a good start. The company sold two million units of the HTC Touch, introduced last year, and in just three months, one million of the follow-on Touch Diamond, a slick and slim device that reviewers have compared with the iPhone.

The Google-powered phone will be the next step in HTC's road to global recognition, he said. (Over all, HTC's revenue, which it reports in Taiwanese dollars, was about $1 billion in the most recent quarter, a 29 percent jump from a year earlier.)

The Google phone, which has been called the HTC Dream and the T-Mobile G1, has a touch screen that slides out to expose a five-row keyboard. It offers easy access to Google's services and to a range of third-party applications.

Many analysts and industry insiders say HTC has turned them into believers. "HTC has been pushing the innovation envelope for quite a long time," said Jeffrey K. Belk, a former senior vice president for strategy at the cellphone chip maker Qualcomm. "It is only now that people are starting to get know to them better."

Still, analysts say that HTC faces long odds in its quest to become a global consumer electronics powerhouse. It is competing against much larger rivals in a market where few niche players have been able to establish themselves.

The company began running ads in the United States this year, but a global marketing campaign could be expensive. And unlike some of its most successful competitors, like Apple and Research in Motion, HTC does not control the software that powers its phones.

"HTC is trying to compete on better hardware in a point in time when more and more of the differentiation of phones is going to be in the software," said James Faucette, an analyst with Pacific Crest Securities.

Heading: As Senators calculate move, Ben & Hank express urgency - Indian Express
Content:
A day after relaxing norms for external commercial borrowings for infrastructure companies, the Government today said a high-level committee will take a call later this month on whether to liberalise the guidelines for other firms as well or not.

"Liberalising ECB norms for other companies is under discussion. A high-level committee will take a call on the matter," sources in the Finance Ministry told PTI. However, they declined to specify whether the norms will in fact be liberalised or not.

Heading: ‘FII equity investment may be hit by global crisis’ - Indian Express
Content:
Federal Reserve chairman Ben Bernanke bluntly warned reluctant lawmakers on Tuesday that they risk a recession with higher unemployment and increased home foreclosures if they fail to pass the Bush administration's $700-billion plan to bail out the financial industry.

Bernanke sketched a scenario in which neither businesses nor consumers could borrow money as US president George Bush and top lawmakers and leaders in both parties voiced hope for agreement within days on a plan to ease the crisis.

With the stock market headed lower, the stakes were unmistakable. Treasury secretary Henry Paulson said Congress must pass the legislation this week. "I understand speed is important, but I'm far more interested in whether or not we get this right," said Senator Chris Dodd, presiding over a hearing by the Senate Banking Committee banking panel where Bernanke joined Paulson in appealing for quick legislation. "There is no second act to this. There is no alternative idea out there with resources available if this does not work," he added.

Bernanke's remarks about the risk of recession came in response to a question from Dodd, who seemed eager to hear a strong rationale for lawmakers to act swiftly on the administration's unprecedented request.

"The financial markets are in quite fragile condition and I think absent a plan they will get worse," Bernanke said. Ominously, he added, "I believe if the credit markets are not functioning, that jobs will be lost, that our credit rate will rise, more houses will be foreclosed upon, GDP will contract, that the economy will just not be able to recover in a normal, healthy way."

Across the Capitol complex, US vice-president Dick Cheney and Jim Nussle, the administration's budget director, met privately with restive House Republicans, some of whom emerged from the session unpersuaded. "Just because God created the world in seven days doesn't mean we have to pass this bill in seven days," said Republican Joe Barton. Added Republican Darrell Issa, "I am emphatically against it."

Dodd and other key Democrats have been in private negotiations with the administration since the weekend on legislation designed to allow the government to buy bad debts held by banks and other financial institutions.

Paulson, seated next to Bernanke at the committee hearing, objected strongly when Senator Chuck Schumer asked if $150 billion might be enough to get the program started, with a promise of more to come. Paulson said that would be a "grave mistake", and would fail to give the markets the confidence they needed to rebound.

Paulson repeatedly fielded questions from committee members asking why taxpayers should accept the burdens of a bailout. "You worry about taxpayers being on the hook?" he replied at one point. "Guess what — they're already on the hook."

Bernanke added that action by lawmakers "is urgently required to stabilise the situation and avert what otherwise could be very serious consequences for our financial markets and for our economy".

Heading: Sensex dips 3% as financial concerns mount - Indian Express
Content:
The US financial crisis is likely to deter foreign institutional investors from investing in India's equity markets, even as debt segment could witness positive response from a section of such investors, chief economic advisor Arvind Virmani said.

So far as FDI is concerned, it would depend on fundamentals of the economy, which have not altered after the financial turmoil, Virmani added.

He said he expected around nine per cent growth of the economy over the next four years and added that despite global uncertainty, there is a solid basis for growth of Indian corporates, given their strong base.

"To the extent that Indian companies, whether for the global operations or for their domestic operations, were depending on equity flows, those clearly would be affected in the rest of this year, at least for the next three months," he said.

Elaborating, he said the US Federal Reserve has increased liquidity to meet the crisis, but even after that, demand for money has gone up because of the turmoil. "So, risk adjusted rate was even higher. It had gone back a little before this stage of the crisis, but it went up again," Virmani said.

Heading: Under watch: Rs 9,000 cr Merrill debts - Indian Express
Content:
Taking cues from the global market, the Bombay Stock Exchange's benchmark index, Sensex, tanked 424.65 points on Tuesday. Uncertainty prevailed in the markets as traders heavily sold IT and banking stocks. Among IT companies, Infosys led the fall losing 5.2 per cent to Rs 1,543.35 on growing worries about outsourcing prospects amid a global financial turmoil. Tata Consultancy Services and Satyam Computer Services shed nearly 6 per cent each to Rs 720.75 and Rs 331.65 respectively.

Market men said that the statement by the US Federal Reserve chairman Ben Bernanke spooked the markets further. Bernanke had told the US Congress on Tuesday that financial markets are under severe stress and urged immediate action to buy up hundreds of billions of dollars worth of tainted mortgage assets.

"Despite the efforts of the Fed, the Treasury, and other agencies, global financial markets remain under extraordinary stress," Bernanke said. "Action by Congress is urgently required to stabilise the situation and avert what could otherwise be very serious consequences for our financial markets and our economy," he said.

"There is increasing concern that the US government's $700-billion bailout package to rescue the ailing financial sector may not be enough to revive the US economy. This apprehension is leading to sell-offs in the technology companies which are to a large extent dependent on the US economy for their business," said an analyst with a broking house. Traders said high oil prices also stoked worries about inflation.

In the banking sector, ICICI Bank fell 5.5 per cent to Rs 599.70, its biggest single-day fall in a week, on concerns high crude prices will diminish the possibility of monetary policy easing in the near term. State Bank of India lost 4.1 per cent to Rs 1,502.75 and while HDFC Bank closed 4.6 per cent lower at Rs 1,237.70.

The 50-share NSE index fell 2.28 per cent to 4,126.90.

Woes continue

Concern that the $700-billion bailout may not be enough to revive the US economy is leading to sell-offs in technology companies

High crude prices could diminish the possibility of monetary policy easing in the near term

Heading: Ramanathan named new finance secy - Indian Express
Content:
Credit rating agency Crisil has placed the ratings of Rs 9,000 crore debentures of DSP Merrill Lynch under watch. "The agency has revised the credit rating of the Rs 30 billion and Rs 60 billion short term debentures P1+ and P1+(so) respectively, which signifies that the debentures are under Rating Watch with Developing Implications," debenture trustee IL&FS Trust Company said.

Recently, US-based investment banker Merrill Lynch was taken over by the Bank of America for $50 billion.

Heading: South Africa calling: India Inc prepares for a big push - Indian Express
Content:
Arun Ramanathan, a 1973-batch Tamil Nadu cadre IAS officer, was named the new finance secretary today. Ramanathan, currently posted as Department of Financial services secretary, succeeds D Subba Rao, who becomes RBI Governor.

Prior to this, Ramanathan had served as secretary in the Chemical and Fertilisers ministry. Throughout his career, he has held positions at various levels, mostly in Tamil Nadu state government's Finance and Industries departments.

Heading: Bank of England injects $40 bn into money markets - Indian Express
Content:
Africa was never seriously on the radar of India Inc for many years. But that could change in a big way in the coming months and years. The Indian industry has discovered that South Africa is the gateway for them to set up base, expand and consolidate their global presence. Nearly 40 Indian companies — from the Tatas, Ranbaxy to the UB group — are present here. That number could go up significantly in the near future. And an equal number of South African companies are active India as well.

What's the strategy for India Inc in Africa? South African industry leaders project that Indian companies can first set up base in South Africa in view of the excellent infrastructure that the country offers and then slowly expand to other African countries, utilising the knowledge and expertise from the South African experience.

Of course, another positive factor is the sizeable Indian disapora present here. "I see tremendous opportunities for Indian companies to invest and expand in South African. So is South African investment. In fact Indian outbound investment almost equals the inbound investment," said former Confederation of Indian Industry (CII) president Shekhar Datta.

In the process, many of the procedural hurdles are being removed. "After the Indian government took up the initiative, the South African government has liberalised the visa regime for Indian businessmen. There has been a big growth in bilateral trade in the last a few years. But there's scope for improvement," said India's Ambassador to South Africa RK Bhatia.

South African companies have started looking at India as a big opportunity, thanks to the country's 8 per cent plus growth and the huge market potential. "I see increasing opportunities in India. There are opportunities and challenges," said Smollan International CEO Doug Smollen. Some companies are looking at India alone disregarding the strong growth of China. "We have decided to focus on India only. We are not looking at China," said Sizwe Nxasana, CEO, banking group, First Rand.

TVS is one among the Indian companies that is looking for opportunities in South Africa. "We see tremendous scope for our products in South Africa. We see opportunities in the rural regions and small towns," HS Goindi of the TVS group said at a seminar on Doing Business with India organised by the CII, with the support of the Indian government in Johannesberg on Tuesday.

Heading: Video-conferencing to replace bureaucrats’ hotline - Indian Express
Content:
The Bank of England on Tuesday pumped another $40 billion dollars into money markets in a bid to ease credit-crunch pressures.

The BoE, which last Thursday began offering the sum on a daily basis, is lending more cash to banking institutions that are facing funding problems due to the worldwide tightening of lending criteria.

Major central banks agreed last week to inject hundreds of billions of dollars into money markets that have been battered by the ongoing financial crisis in order to ensure that banks can access short-term funds.

Earlier on Friday, the European Central Bank had also offered $40 billion for short-term loans.

UAE sets up $13.6-billion fund to help its banks

The UAE Central Bank has set up a $13.6-bn facility to help banks in dealing with the global financial crisis. The Central Bank's board of directors, in a statement released here yesterday, said the bank has discussed the position of inter-bank deposits, which has been affected by the "liquidity constraints" in international money markets and may pump in more money to ease it.

"To remedy this situation, the Central Bank has decided to set up a facility amounting to 50 billion dirhams ($13.6 billion) for banks operating in the Unite Arab Emirates, to be used by these banks if so needed," it said. The bank said it "expects that these funds would meet banks needs for supporting continued financing of economic growth".

Shares continue to slide in Europe, Asia

Share prices tumbled in Europe and Asia on Tuesday, with investors still anxious about a critical US financial bailout now caught in political crossfire in Congress. Fears that the rescue package, drafted by Paulson over the weekend, could be stalled or undermined by Democrat-Republican political wrangling depressed market sentiment.

The London FTSE 100 index lost 1.91 per cent to close at 5,136.12 points while in Paris the CAC 40 fell 1.98 per cent to 4,139.82 points. The Frankfurt the Dax shed 0.64 percent at 6,068 points. In Asia, Hong Kong shares plunged 3.9 per cent, Sydney shed 1.9 per cent and Shanghai dropped 1.56 per cent. Japan's markets were closed for a public holiday.

Crude oil prices slip after historic one-day gain

World oil prices dipped slightly on Tuesday in choppy deals as traders banked profits, one day after New York crude had soared more than $16 for its biggest-ever daily jump. The massive price surge on Monday was driven partly by hopes that a US plan to buy tainted mortgage-related assets would save the global economy from collapse and thus maintain strong demand for energy.

The rally was also driven by technical factors because the contract for New York oil deliverable in October had expired on Monday. On Tuesday, New York's new main contract, light sweet crude for November delivery, shed $2.10 to $107.27 a barrel.

Heading: Labour, Fin ministries disagree on EPF rates - Indian Express
Content:
The use of RAX phones by top bureaucrats may soon be a thing of the past. All the secretaries at the centre and state chief secretaries can soon have virtual meetings every day as the centre has begun implementing a programme worth Rs 1.5 crore, introducing desktop video conferencing to enable them take quick decisions and expedite the response time. The project is expected to be completed within two months.

"The government is according high priority to various e-governance initiatives. For improving e-governance, communication is a key ingredient and that is why we have decided to connect secretaries of the central government and chief secretaries of the states through Executive Video Conferencing System (EVCS) over internet protocol involving less communication cost as it would enable them to take decisions expeditiously," Secretary, Planning Commission Subas Pani said.

The entire concept has been mooted by the commission and is being implemented by the National Informatics Centre (NIC) whose internet protocol will be utilised for the purpose. An expenditure of about Rs 1.5 crore would be incurred for the programme. The secretaries currently use the RAX system, which is a hotline between them for communicating in times of need. The new system will enable virtual meetings between them and ensure a quick response during crisis situations like natural disasters. The government had initially decided to install EVCS for the union secretaries, but after a review it decided to extend the same to state chief secretaries, Pani said.

The project would be executed by NIC and the existing Internet Protocol based network infrastructure-NICNET will be used for providing high-speed bandwidth needed for good quality video-conferencing which can be simultaneously carried out in eight EVCS at a time. A key advantage of the system is sharing of data in video conferencing mode. The RAX system will continue to be used by the ministers. A total of 120 desk-top video conferencing hardware would be installed as of now at the centre besides in all states and union territories. As of now one such hardware has been installed in the office of the Orissa chief secretary.

The basic objective of installing EVCS is to enable quick action in times of natural disasters like the recent flood in Bihar and ensure fast response to minimize loss of lives and livestock. Expanding the ambit of the EVCS network would depend on the success of its initial phase.

Heading: Lehman re-opens in North America under Barclays ownership, offers 10,000 jobs - Indian Express
Content:
The differences between the Labour and Finance Ministries over increasing the interest rate for the Employees Provident Fund is deepening with Labour Minister Oscar Fernandes on Tuesday saying that the entire corpus invested in the Special Deposit Scheme (SDS) may be withdrawn and parked elsewhere.

The Labour Ministry has been pushing for hiking the interest rate for the Rs 53,000 crore of EPFO money invested in the SDS to 8.8-9.0 per cent from the present rate of 8 per cent, but the Finance Ministry is understood to be disinclined to any upward revision of rates.

"We may take back our entire corpus invested in the SDS if the finance ministry does not agree to an upward revision of the interest rate under the scheme," Fernandes said. A major portion of the EPFO corpus is parked in the SDS.

The Labour Minister along with a delegation of the Central Board of Trustees (CBT) met Finance Minister P Chidambaram last week and sought an upward revision of the interest rate arguing that banks offer 10 per cent interest on fixed deposits.

"The Finance Minister approved the idea of withdrawing money from the SDS and investing it in other government securities or instrument where the EPFO can get better returns. We would give reasonable time to the Finance Ministry to take a call on it before taking a decision," the Labour Minister added.

Trade union leaders claimed that the Finance Ministry considers the SDS a liability and has been putting pressure on the Labour Ministry to take back the EPFO corpus and invest it elsewhere, particularly in private equities.

Heading: Lehman bond holders likely to loose $100 bn - Indian Express
Content:
Lehman Brothers' North American operations, which were acquired by global financial services major Barclays, has reopened under the new ownership and over 10,000 employees have been offered jobs in the combined entity.

These actions follow the Bankruptcy Court for Southern District of New York's approval for Barclays acquisition of Lehman Brothers' North America operations which include fixed income and equity sales, trading and research, prime services, investment banking, principal investing and private investment management businesses.

The integration process for the combined businesses began immediately after the court's decision, Barclays said in a statement last night.

However, the process is still continuing, thus Lehman's sales and trading business was not able to conduct business yesterday, while the capital markets and trading businesses would become fully functional shortly, it added.

"Employment offers have been made to all employees of the Lehman Brothers businesses that have been acquired by Barclays Capital, including Lehman Brothers Private Investment Management business, transferring to Barclays Wealth, the wealth management arm of Barclays PLC," the statement said.

The combined firm would use Barclays Capital name, while the financial major has also purchased rights to use Lehman Brothers name and would consider opportunities to do so.

"Barclays-Lehman Brothers partnership is now a reality. With all that our combined firm has to offer, we have a great business to tell our clients about. We have been delighted by the enthusiastic response of the senior Lehman brothers executives to whom we have offered leadership positions in our combined firm," Barclays PLC President Bob Diamond said.

Heading: Hong Kong investors may sue bond sellers - Indian Express
Content:
Bondholders of the beleaguered Lehman Brothers may loose $110 billion (about Rs five lakh crore) on account of decline in the asset-value of the fourth-largest investment bank in the US, media reports say. The value of the bonds of Lehman Brothers has witnessed a major fall, the Financial Times report said adding, "further losses on its derivatives positions, which are still being unwound, could leave even less on the table for bond investors." Loomis Sayles vice-chairman Dan Fuss has said, "I don't know how this will play out for bondholders, but I doubt if its going to be good."

Nomura to buy EU, Middle East operations

A day after announcing the deal to acquire Lehman Brothers' Asia-Pacific business, Nomura said on Tuesday it would acquire the European and Middle Eastern equities and banking operations of the now-collapsed American investment banking major. On Monday, the Japanese firm entered into an agreement to buy the battered US bank's entire franchise in the Asia-Pacific region including Japan and Australia, a deal which would help about 3,000 employees of the collapsed bank in the region. Nomura said the buyout would provide a market leading equities and investment banking platform in the region.

Heading: De jure, defecto - Indian Express
Content: Hong Kong investors who bought complex financial products backed by collapsed US investment bank Lehman Brothers were considering suing the institutions who sold them, a lawmaker said today. Investors argued that the banks who sold the instruments guaranteed by the failed Wall Street titan did not fully explain the high risks associated with the products. "The investors are considering mounting legal action against the banks for misrepresentation," Albert Ho, chairman of the Democratic Party and a lawyer, told AFP. Many of the investors, who paid a total of $1.63 billion, had been sold mini-bonds which are based on derivatives linked to major firms' stocks but are worthless if the guarantor goes bankrupt.

Heading: LA’s fine, but the sun doesn’t shine - Indian Express
Content:
As the presiding officers' annual conference draws to a close, a major topic of discussion is the need to review the anti-defection law. Of course, the law is being reviewed the umpteenth time; no previous review has produced rational results. It has been used often since being introduced in 1985; and yet there appears to be no consensus on how to control its deleterious side-effects, including the proliferation of political parties by splits and mergers, the use of money to encourage mass defections such as are protected by the law, the naked incursion of courts into what should be the domain of various speakers, and, above all, the freezing of Parliamentary creativity, innovation and excellence by heavily constraining the freedom of speech of legislators inside and outside legislatures. The presiding officers need to think about a few points in particular, pertaining to how far the law and its implementation have drifted from the original intent of those who framed it.

The 52nd Amendment to the Constitution contained a single, pure declaration: "This Bill is meant for outlawing defection." Nobody anticipated that it, in the course of time and events, would outlaw instead freedoms of speech and vote of legislators. The key question now is how to reform the anti-defection law to outlaw defections without stepping on the freedoms of speech and vote of members.  

The most abused provision in the anti-defection law is the disqualification of members on ground of voluntarily giving up membership of their political parties. Courts have provided nebulous interpretations of the phrase; and speakers and chairmen have construed the meaning of the words "voluntarily giving up membership of a political party", with political factors firmly in mind. This is the provision that unacceptably constrains the freedom of members of legislatures to speak in, and outside, the House. Outlawing defection is not inextricably linked to constraining freedom of speech. Freedom of speech and of dissent against party authority inside and outside the legislature has, therefore, to be restored to end the enslavement of Parliament unknowingly created by the law over the past two decades. 

The central mistake is that the law does not realise that what it wishes to contain — political instability — is caused by voting, and not by speech in the House. Curbing legislative coups must be correlated to the casting of votes for those coups; but if every time members vote they are constrained by a whip, the point of individual members would be lost. Such whips should be issued only on confidence motions; governments' stability should never be tested on any other motions, such as Cut Motions and so on. If the demands for grants are cut or increased by the House it should never be deemed as censure of the government. So long as governments believe budgets have to be passed untouched by legislatures, the sad spectacle of governments controlling the Houses instead of the Houses controlling the governments will continue.

The present law does a bad job of addressing its own objectives. In particular, it does not rule out the possibility that defectors might first cross-vote and then be disqualified — while their vote stands. (This is in spite of the Supreme Court ruling in Rana vs Maurya that orders of the speakers and chairmen under the Tenth Schedule needed to be retroactive.) The law, as it stands, acts counter to stability: if a member votes even once against his party whip, even on innocuous motions, he stands disqualified for the term of the whole House. Thus, instead of dealing with his cross-vote, the law is dealing with the member. Instead, to effectuate the original intent of the law, cross-votes on confidence and no-confidence motions should be ignored; cross-votes on other motions must be respected.

Consequently, political parties must be allowed to split and merge outside the legislature in accordance with the election commission's standard procedures and not the whims of the presiding officers of legislatures. The authority on the party status of a member should be the EC.

Thus reform is necessary, and must be deep. It should restore constitutionally guaranteed freedom of speech, action and association of legislators; it should reduce and rationalise the regulation of their votes; it should act on votes retrospectively, and the EC should be restored to paramount status.

The writer is secretary of the Goa legislative assembly & author of 'Ideas for an Alternative Anti-Defection Law' express@expressindia.com

Heading: How do you value risk? - Indian Express
Content:
If there's one thing the native residents of Los Angeles can't stand, it's condescending New Yorkers... Here they come, the Tina Feys, the Jon Stewarts and the New York Times reporters, sneering at LA's non-existent public transportation, its incomprehensible freeway system and its bed-before-nine suburban-ness, before jetting back to their glittering, never-sleeping Manhattan playground... I think Angelenos should just relax. So what if New Yorkers think LA is unbearable? [New York] may have the edge on excitement, but it's also noisy, filthy, crowded, rapaciously expensive and by turns too hot and too cold...

Alas, this view puts me in a minority in LA. Angelenos want to compete. [Hence] the reason why the city's most famous architect, Frank Gehry, put his name to a $3 billion mega-development to transform LA's historic but unloved downtown area (the financial district) into a mini-Manhattan... The Grand Avenue Project [was] conceived to give LA nothing less than its very own Central Park. A similarly ambitious project, the $2.5 billion LA Live complex, was also devised for the other side of downtown. Its goal? To give LA nothing less than its own Times Square. In many ways, all this is great news for LA. [But] the timing of LA's decision to out-New York the New Yorkers has been terrible... And for Angelenos, utterly infuriating. After all, everything would be fine if not for those catastrophically overextended bankers on Wall Street. New Yorkers, in other words.

Excerpted from a comment by Chris Ayres in 'The Times'

Heading: Rupee, afloat - Indian Express
Content:
India is at a cusp. More accurately, it is at what mathematicians call a point of inflection. At a point of inflection, a curve changes shape. For instance, an accelerating rate of growth becomes decelerating, or vice-versa. Around 2003, the trend rate of GDP growth changed from 6.5 per cent to 8.5 per cent, perhaps even 9 per cent. So that was one point of inflection. GDP growth is down to 7.5 per cent now, perhaps even 7 per cent. Hence, we are at another point of inflection. Lest we forget, the UPA's National Common Minimum Programme (NCMP) promised us 7 to 8 per cent rate of growth and no more. So that promise has been kept.

However, this isn't about downturn in the economic cycle alone. It is also about downturn in the policy cycle. Elegies, and they aren't eulogies, have begun to be written about the UPA. Newsweek is an instance. The short point is there have been zero reforms under the UPA, the nuclear deal doesn't count. What second generation economic reforms have been implemented? Incidentally, historians often count a generation to be 25 years. Hence, if we count from 1991, we should expect second generation reforms in 2016 and not before. Partial VAT is a legacy, as is the road programme (though procedures have improved for Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana) or improved school enrolment indicators. Adherence to deficit targets is a sleight of hand.

The diluted Right to Information Act is like an old man without dentures. The less said the better about pensions, banking, insurance, privatisation/disinvestment, labour market (not the Industrial Disputes Act alone), education (including skills), health and improved efficiency of public expenditure. Other than the Pay Commission, we have added many large vessels to the fleet of so-called flagship programmes and tax reform has retreated from avowed goals. The public sector has an uncanny ability to convert every asset into a liability and, with its blind belief in the public sector, the UPA has done no better.

Consequently, India's track record in cross-country surveys isn't laudable. The World Bank's "Doing Business" and "Economic Freedom of the World" are two recent examples. These typically have ranks, as well as scores. In general, India's ranks have dropped, implying other countries have done better. When India's scores have improved, they have done so at slower rates, the point of inflection again.

Beyond numbers, reforms are also headed south. What is worrying is the feeding in of global developments into reform scepticism. First, least important of the lot, we are unhappy with China's behaviour at the NSG. So let's dump anti-dumping and safeguard measures on Chinese imports. True, this may be knee-jerk and transient. Also true, this protectionist stance in trade policy is partly neutralised by the FTA with Asean. Second, WTO talks are headed nowhere in a hurry and that trigger is missing too. Third, imported inflation through oil, commodities and food (less important for India in an imported sense) has reinforced protectionism (such as for agro exporters), though those pressures are easing now. Fourth, we have US developments, liable to be misinterpreted.

But before that, let's ask a few questions. First, why is there such hype over the Sensex, if it is not representative of the entire capital market? Second, why can't there be greater supply of shares through disinvestment? Third, why do promoters hang on to so many shares? Fourth, why has the debt market not developed? Fifth, why is the capital market (especially the Sensex segment) so sensitive to purchase and sale by foreign investors? India is a large country and sources of growth are primarily internal. India's trade/ GDP ratio is 30 per cent and will never be much over 35 per cent. (China is an outlier.) For example, a large chunk of India's trade is inter-state. Like Europe, had these states been individual countries, India would have appeared far less insular. In a similar vein, why isn't the Sensex primarily driven by domestic investors and when will that shift occur? Sixth, why is the Sensex behaviour so distorted, at a zenith of 20,000-plus or a nadir of 10,000-minus? Answers to such questions underline the need for more reforms, not less.

Most discussion of the US financial sector meltdown and its impact on India has focused on macroeconomy and individual sectors (infrastructure) and companies (those that wish to borrow abroad or have forex assets). Unlike the financial sector, India's real sector is more insulated and the trade basket diversified. Therefore, the impact on GDP growth or BOP (balance of payments) can't be much. Any adverse impact on BOP because of FII pull-out and the reticence to invest in emerging markets will be more than neutralised by FDI inflows and reduced oil imports (in value, if not volume), thereby easing downward pressures on the rupee.

The more serious impact will be on mindsets and policy stances, somewhat reminiscent of 1997/1998. Stepping out on the road involves the risk of being run over by a BMW or Blueline. Shopping in a market involves the risk of being torn apart by a bomb. One takes risks because the gains are more than commensurate and the existence of risks is no argument for risk aversion and playing safe. There is risk in voting in a new government too. You never know what it will do. Similarly, globalisation brings risks, both because the economy can no longer be insulated and is susceptible to external shocks and because policy-making loses degrees of freedom.

One loses a little bit of one's independence, so to speak, a bit like getting married. Why should that be an argument against marrying, stepping onto the road or going shopping? However, the US meltdown is likely to be interpreted as an argument against globalisation and opening up. Let's impose controls on capital flows. The US has an enviable financial architecture. If information gaps, corporate mis-governance and regulatory failure can occur in such a developed country, how can we afford to liberalise financial sectors in a developing country? There is worse. Witness government bail-outs of Wall Street firms: clear proof that one can't depend on markets. State intervention is necessary. Unwarranted comparisons are being drawn, not just with 1987, but with the Great Depression years. Those years led to Keynes, government intervention and the New Deal, a far cry from the down-sized government of the '80s.

In pedagogy, there is always a problem with lessons learnt and morals drawn. Usually, people don't learn what is taught. Instead, they learn what they wish to learn. Consequently, the US experience will be interpreted in Marxist imagery, the demise of market-driven capitalism rather than the withering away of the state. And this reinforces the anti-reform straws in the wind mentioned earlier.
