The government will offer a maximum of Rs 5 lakh as capital subsidy, which will amount to 25 per cent of the total project cost.

"We have already received 158 applications from places like Sultanpur, Kabirnagar, Hardoi, Chitrakoot and Agra and are in the process of launching advertisements to draw more entrepreneurs," said Ojha.

With this, traditional cooking in these villages will get a facelift as chulhas will be replaced by modern stoves and clean fuel.

A single biogas plant with a capacity of 100 cubic metres consumes 1,875 kilograms of agro-waste to produce 80 kgs of methane gas per week. Agro-waste includes cowdung, kitchen waste, water hyacinth and other biodegradable household waste. Methane produced per week by one such unit per village will be sufficient for all its households to cook for seven hours daily.

The mission has also designed a superior biofuel generator — "Gram Urja". Yet to be patented, the generator accepts any agricultural waste, not just cowdung. It produces biogas within a week, at one-tenth the speed of other biogas units. Claiming to be an improvement on contemporary models such as the KVIC and Deen Bandu, Ojha said it also addresses the burner jamming issue by the introduction of burners with larger holes.

The project will be rolled out in two phases. In its first phase, the project will aim to deliver gas for cooking and lighting gas lamps. The next stage will involve the setting up of electricity generators at the village level.

Socio-economic outcomes of the project could include direct and indirect employment, sustainability, as well as self-reliance. Each plant will become a hub of economic activity, providing employment to four youths.

Compost produced from drying the slurry obtained as a by-product can be sold for Rs 4000 per tonne. Farmers will also be given carbon credits under the Kyoto Protocol norms, said Ojha.

The Bio-Energy Mission has already tested the "Gram Urja" at Kanpur, Mishrawallia village in Ballia district, and at Mullahikhera located in the outskirts of Lucknow.

Heading: Industrialists in Greater Noida: ‘accidents’ like Monday not new - Indian Express
Content:
The recent hike in the Value Added Tax (VAT) and the imposition of entry tax have made some items the costliest in the state.

These include tea, cellphones, TV, computers, laptop, air conditioners, refrigerators, electrical and electronic goods, steel, iron and steel. The difference in tax rates between Uttar Pradesh and the neighboring states on most of these items is as high as 8.5 per cent.

Now, the business and industry are up in arms against the government's move and the traders' organisations have called for a statewide bandh on October 4.

Terming the government's decision "retrograde", the traders said the high tax rates will inflict damage on the state's economy as business will be diverted to other states.

"The hike will not only cause a huge loss to business, but will also accelerate the process of migration of industries to neighboring states that provide a better tax structure," said Praveen Sadana, president of the Indian Industries Association (IIA). Rohit Kohli, president of the UP Computer Dealers Association, agreed: "Instead of buying a laptop or a computer at 12.5 per cent tax, the buyer will prefer getting it from neighboring states where the tax is 4 per cent."

Those involved in manufacturing transformers are also making dire predictions. "The tax on the cheapest transformer will be Rs 17,000, which will make our products uncompetitive. If the hike is not rolled back, then we will have to shift our units to Uttarakhand," said S K Rungta, president of the UP Transformer Industries Forum.

The Indian Cellular Association (ICA) — an apex body of the mobile industry comprising manufacturers, brand owners, distributors, retailers and consumers — has, meanwhile, urged the state government to reconsider its decision of increasing the VAT on mobile phone sets from 4 per cent to 12.5 per cent.

In a memorandum to the government, the ICA said the hike would only lead to smuggling of cellphone sets from the adjoining states and even Nepal where the tax rate is 4 to 6 per cent.

Pankaj Mohindroo, ICA national president, said it may also lead to the emergence of a grey market, where the consumer will purchase the sets without giving any tax to the government. "With the hike in the taxes, mobiles sets ranging in price between Rs 1,500 and Rs 30,000 will be costlier by Rs 127 to Rs 2,550," he said. The government has, however, defended the hike saying that the traders did not pass on the benefit of its original decision to cut VAT to 4 per cent to consumers.

"The VAT has been increased only on those goods and products which were charged at the rate of 7 to 11 per cent under the old trade tax regime," said Govindan Nair, principal secretary of tax and registration.

Heading: Graziano yet to decide on future course of action - Indian Express
Content:
Two days after L K Choudhary was killed by employees at Italian firm Graziano International, the mood among industrialists in the city is one of apprehension. "Accidents" like that on Monday are not new to the industrial hub, they say.

Vinod Kumar Vajpayee, president of the Noida Phase-II Industries Association, said: "There are many other companies that have seen violence over the last few years."

Workers of Jaypee Greens in Greater Noida attacked the company's office in 2004 and killed one person. Similarly, employees at Daewoo attacked the office of the company after it went bankrupt. Some 125 workers and 10 policemen were injured in the clashes.

"Largescale rioting like that on Monday (when Choudhary was killed and 34 others were injured) is a troubling phenomenon," Vajpayee said.

Hindon Rubber, another company that was based in Noida, wound up operations after similar protests by employees earlier this year.

Most clashes in the past, industrialists say, have been because of expelled or suspended employees. Graziano had expelled 192 of its regular employees on July 1 and opted for contracted workers, a practice opposed by the Mazdoor Sangh leaders.

Virender Singh Sirohi, secretary of the Uttar Pradesh unit of Hind Mazdoor Sabha, said: "We had taken the issue of workers to the president and all concerned authorities; the rioting is condemnable but there are issues that need to be addressed."

Sirohi alleges that officials at Graziano had agreed to their demands in an earlier meeting and later refused to implement the steps promised. "The frustration had been building up," he said.

Industrialists, however, allege gangs that operate among the labourers are involved. Sahdev Sharma, chairman of the Greater Noida Industries Association, said: "We have reported about the involvement of bad elements and a few workers in the past; meetings between employees and owners have also been arranged."

Sharma alleges the police and administration have been neglecting the situation in the area. "Assurances have been given and some action taken but this incident goes to show that all is not well."

Sharma and members of other associations held a meeting with District Magistrate Shravan Kumar and Senior Superintendent of Police R K Chaturvedi on Wednesday to discuss security arrangements in the industrial area.

After the meeting, Sharma said: "We do not want Gautam Budh Nagar to lose its image as an industrial hub; stern steps will need to be taken in this regard."

Till then, he says, some people might choose to keep away from Noida and Greater Noida and some might wind up their businesses as well.

Heading: Congress list of 34 seats in state stumps SP - Indian Express
Content:
Graziano Transmissioni, the Italian auto-parts manufacturer whose India head L K Choudhary was allegedly lynched by dismissed workers on Monday, is "yet to decide" on the future course of action in the country.

Marcello Lambert, segment chief executive officer of the company who reached Delhi on Wednesday, said: "My priority is to see the injured get proper medical care and all help is extended to the grieving family of Choudhary."

Lamberto met the family members of Choudhary at their residence and expressed condolences. He also went to the Kailash Hospital and met the injured officials of the company. As many as 34 employees had sustained injuries in the Monday attack.

Later, Lamberto held a meeting of the officials amid heavy security at the factory in Greater Noida.

Factory manager L K Gupta said: "It was an internal meeting. The factory has been restarted for a check. Further decisions will be taken on Monday."

Choudhary was allegedly beaten to death at the company's plant in Greater Noida by a group of dismissed employees after a meeting called to resolve dispute between them and the management had failed.

Heading: SIC orders govt to give data on CM Discretionary Fund - Indian Express
Content:
With the Congress handing over a list of 34 seats it wants to contest in Uttar Pradesh, the Samajwadi Party (SP) is in a quandary over stitching an alliance with the national party to counter Mayawati's rise in the state.

What has added to the SP's worries is the adamant attitude of the Congress in claiming seats held by the SP while conceding none of its seats.

Senior party leaders wonder whether the party can accommodate the Congress in its scheme of things when the party chief has instructed its negotiators to concede less than half the seats being demanded.

In the last two rounds of negotiations, the SP has agreed to all 12 seats demanded by the Congress — Rae Bareli, Amethi, Varanasi, Hapur, Mathura, Bansgaon, Aligarh, Dharaura and Kanpur, held by the Congress, along with Khurja, Domariaganj and Bareilly, where the Congress vote share was more than the SP.

It is the remaining seats, many of which are held by the SP, that have become a bone of contention.

While the Congress wants Rampur, Farrukhabad and Pratapgarh seats for its state leaders Noor Bano, Salman Khursheed and Ratna Singh respectively, it has also set its eyes on Muradabad in western Uttar Pradesh, Banda and Jhansi in Bundelkhand, and Salempur and Padrauna in East UP, most of which are held by the SP.

The Congress also wants to contest from Sultanpur near the Gandhi family bastions of Rae Bareli and Amethi, though showing willingness for a friendly fight in Pratapgarh.

Senior SP leaders said party negotiators Amar Singh and Ram Gopal Yadav had been instructed by party chief Mulayam Singh Yadav to concede only about 15 seats to the Congress.

At best, half a dozen more seats could be conceded, they added.

According to sources, both the parties would sit again to finalise their seat-sharing agreement later this week.

Heading: Woman asked to return to first husband after 14 yrs - Indian Express
Content:
Acting on an appeal by Congress spokesperson Akhilesh Pratap Singh, who had sought detailed information regarding monetary assistance from Chief Minister's Discretionary Fund, the State Information Commission (SIC) has asked the government to provide the desired information within a months time.

The commission has also asked the government not to charge any money from the applicant as document fee, as the information had not been provided to him within the stipulated time of 30 days.

The commission, taking a cue from the High Court, has asked the government to post all information relating to expenditure incurred from the Discretionary Fund on the department website.

In June 2007, Singh had asked the Chief Minister's Office to provide him with a list of all those people who had been given financial assistance of over Rs 1 lakh from the fund.

Singh had asked for the complete details of these beneficiaries along with their addresses and the amount received.

On being refused from the Chief Minister's secretariat, the applicant filed an appeal before the commission, which ordered the Chief Minister's office to provide the applicant with the desired information within 15 days.

Acting on the order, the secretariat prepared 336-page document and asked Singh to pay an amount of Rs 5,040 at the rate of Rs 15 per page.

The Congress leader's plea was that since the information was not given to him within 30 days, he could not be charged with any money.

The commission has upheld his contention.

Heading: Activists cry foul as UP Information Commission drafts regulations - Indian Express
Content:
A community panchayat has directed a woman to return to her first husband, who was missing for the last 14 years and appeared just a week after she had remarried in the Meerut district.

The panchayat, convened on Tuesday in Kulganj village, supported Abid's claim that he had not yet divorced Shabana and she was still his wife. On Wednesday, Islamic seminary Darul-Uloom Deoband said the case should be referred to a Shariat court.

Abid had married Shabana 17 years ago. After three years of marriage, he went missing and returned early this month.

"To marry again, a married woman can seek a divorce from her missing husband in the Shariat court. So, both parties should approach the court," said Mufti Ahsan Kashmi, deputy-incharge Fatwa Department of Darul-Uloom Wakf Deoband.

Mufti Zulfiqar, president of the Uttar Pradesh Imams Organisation and a member of the Shariat court, said: "A married woman can seek a divorce from her missing husband only after approaching Shariat court."

In 2004, the Gudiya case had grabbed the headlines.

Gudiya's husband Arif, who went missing soon after the Kargil war, was repatriated from Pakistan.

By then, Gudiya had married another man and was pregnant. She was, however, forced to return to Arif and died a few months after giving birth.

Heading: Usmani was wanted by Mau cops in auto-lifting cases - Indian Express
Content:
The UP State Information Commission has formulated some regulations for the implementation of the Right to Information Act, which, activists allege, are contrary to the spirit of the law enacted to facilitate availability of information.

"The regulations of the state commission are the copy of the Central Information Commission (CIC) rules and regulations, which reject 60 per cent cases on technical grounds," said Arvind Kejriwal, who was actively involved in the formation of the RTI Act.

The commission has not sought public opinion while formulating the regulations. But since the matter was posted on the commission website, it has attracted suggestions from various quarters.

Chief Information Commissioner Wajahat Habibullah clarified that the states have the authority to form regulations for the implementation of the Act in its true spirit. But it is better to seek public opinion while drafting the regulations, he added.

The activists from across the nation have now come together to oppose the regulations and have demanded several amendments.

Social worker and RTI activist Urvashi Sharma from RTI Mahila Manch has raised the issue by writing an open letter to the officiating state Chief Information Commissioner, Gyanendra Sharma. Copies of the letter have been sent to the President, besides the

Governor and the Chief Minster of Uttar Pradesh.

Urvashi says the rules are meant to make the process so complex that it acts as a deterrent, and forces the applicant to seek legal help.

"The law was passed after a people's movement. It was drafted by civil societies. Its rules should also be made through public discussions," she said.

Gyanendra Sharma said the regulations were basically for the functioning of the commission, but still he got them posted at the commission website.

"We are going through all suggestions and will incorporate whatever is feasible before implementing them," said Sharma. He however, denied that the regulations had been sent to the government for its approval.

"The question of sending the regulations to government does not arise as they are an internal matter."

Some of the points in the SIC regulations and the counterpoints of the activists:

* Rule 6 mentions a flexible two to four-week summer break and a two-week winter break. Activists say: This lacks clarity. Besides, this is unjustified when over 10,000 cases are pending with the SIC.

* Rule 8(1) (a) makes it mandatory for the appellant/complainant to furnish his personal details, apart from name and address.
Activists say: Personal details are not specified.

* Rule 11(5) (b) says that the registrar can cancel cases that are not maintainable due to "some" reasons.
Activists say: The word "some" is ambiguous.

* Rule 12 dealing with filing of counter by the public information officer gives a bunch of relaxations to the PIO as it says, "after getting the complaint/appeal, the PIO shall submit his counter (if there is any) along with related documents.
Activists say: Why the words "if there is any" when according to Rule 10, the complainant/appellant has to send a copy of complaint/appeal to the PIO and compulsorily furnish attested copies to the SIC while filing the complaint/appeal

* Rule 12 says during hearing in commission, "generally" the PIO shall present his view.
Activists say: Why is this not mandatory?

* Rule 15(5) says the commission shall pass order on the merits of the case.
Activists say: The term "speaking order" has not been used, which is mandatory as per Section 4(1)d of the Act.

Heading: Sops for hotel projects in backward blocks - Indian Express
Content:
Afzal Mutalib Usmani, one of the five Indian Mujahiddin (IM) operatives arrested in Mumbai, has been wanted by the Mau district police since September 2. He was allegedly the kingpin of an auto-lifters' gang operating in the area.

The name of Usmani, a native of Delai Ferozpur village of Madhuban area in Mau, came up after two youths arrested with Bolero, Tavera and Tata Sumo cars named him during interrogation.

The duo had told the police that Usmani orchestrated a gang of auto-lifters in Maharashtra and used to send the stolen vehicles to Mau for disposal.

Mau Superintendent of Police Mahesh Mishra said: "We have traced Usmani to Maharashtra, near Geeta Vikas Mandir in Govindi (East). Two of his brothers, Faiz and Fazal Ahmed, run a bakery in Bhiwandi."

He added: "During a raid, we found Usmani's house locked. All his relatives had disappeared after his name came up as the leader of the auto-lifters' gang."

Usmani's in-laws' house at Fatehpur Mando village in Mau was also raided, but the relatives feigned ignorance about his whereabouts, he said.

The SP said that the police were also looking for Usmani's friend Siraj Ahmed alias Sultan, who used to provide him shelter during his stay in Mau. A team was sent to Maharashtra in this connection, but Sultan could not be traced. "His brothers were also not able to give any information about Usmani," Mishra said.

Deputy Inspector General (DIG), UP Anti-Terror Squad (ATS), Rajiv Krishna said: "The case with the Mau police will help in seeking Usmani's remand. We could retrieve more details from him about other IM suspects wanted in the UP blasts."

Heading: Paddy, bajra arrival picks up in state mandis - Indian Express
Content:
In an effort to promote tourism in the backward areas of the state, the state government has decided to dole out special incentives for entrepreneurs setting up hotel establishments in the areas identified as backward blocks in terms of tourism.

The notification in this regard has already been issued by the Department of Industries last week, according to sources. However, to avail of these benefits, the industrialists would have to put in a minimum investment of Rs 3 crore in the project.

The Minister of state for tourism and forest, Kiran Choudhry, said financial assistance and an interest-free loan repayable after five years from the date of the launch of the concerned project are some of the incentives to be given to such industrialists.

She said it was the state government's endeavour to promote tourism industry not just in the national capital region (NCR), or places with historical and religious importance, but in those areas as well which had remained backward so far. There are 95 identified backward blocks in the state which have been designated for tourism and hotel projects.

Choudhry also revealed plans of the Tourism Department to promote adventure sports at Morni, among some other places.

Some incentives are also planned to be given to mega projects with investments of Rs 100 crore or more in the backward blocks. The incentives could also be availed by those industries employing more than 500 workers or more, irrespective of the amount of their investment in the hotel.

Keshni Anand Arora, Secretary, Haryana Tourism, said the government had recently added seven more blocks in the list of industrially backward areas designated for tourism and hotel projects. These include Thanesar, Jagadhari, Pehowa, Bhiwani, Panipat, Hisar and Rewari.

In its recent meeting, the Haryana Tourist Development Council, approved in principle that the Tourism department would develop an integrated resort at Kalesar in Yamunanagar district for long term lease on nine acres of land with public private partnership.

The council has also recommended setting-up of integrated tourism resorts and spas at Mallah in Panchkula district and Madhogarh in Mahendragarh-Loharu area. It was also suggested that the Tourism Department should develop various places of religious and historical importance, including Kurukshetra, Pehowa and Hodal.

Heading: Rahul praises Manmohan for nuclear deal - Indian Express
Content:
The arrival of paddy and bajra in the mandis of Haryana is picking up with over 12,000 tonne paddy and 78,247 metric tonne bajra having arrived already.

A spokesman of the Department of Food and Supplies said that out of the total paddy arrival, 3560 tonnes has been procured by government agencies at the minimum support price fixed by the Central Government and the remaining 8,574 tonne has been purchased by private millers and traders. Kurukshetra district is leading with the arrival of 4,735 tonne, followed by Karnal with 3,777 tonne. As for bajra, out of the total arrival, 63,857 metric tonnes has been procured by government agencies and the remaining 14,390 metric tonnes by private traders. He said that Rewari district is leading with the arrival of 15,402 metric tonnes from there, followed by Sonipat at 14,336 metric tonnes.

Heading: State loosens purse strings for private schools, tightens fist for govt institutions - Indian Express
Content:
Putting to rest all speculation, AICC general secretary Rahul Gandhi today clarified that for him, Dr Manmohan Singh was the next Prime Ministerial candidate and being a young member of the party, he fully supported the person who has put the country on the fast-track of economic growth.

Rahul, while talking to mediapersons, said he supports the Prime Minister on every issue, including Indo-US nuclear deal. "Nuclear deal has raised country's status in the world, besides it will meet our huge energy needs. And, Prime Minister Manmohan Singh should be given credit for this," said Rahul Gandhi.

Without taking the name of the NDA, he said, "Our 'India-shining' friends were not able to deliver much. They compromised, and were ready to sign the worse nuclear deal with the US."

About the economy, he said inflation rate was coming down and due to the able Prime Minister, India did not suffer the worst economic shocks, which other countries faced.

When asked about the re-implementation of the POTA, he said it was a failed law and India needs stronger legislations to deal with terrorism.

"When POTA was in force, Parliament was attacked, IC-814 was hijacked and the then government gave in to the demands of the terrorists," he said.

Regarding attack on the Christian community in several states, Rahul said attackers should be dealt with severely.

When asked for his take on the idea mooted by Lok Sabha Speaker Somnath Chatterjee on the right to recall the non-performing elected representatives, Rahul said, "It is a robust idea. Though I don't know much about it, I have full faith in the Speaker."

Without mentioning Singur, Rahul said in Orissa, poor farmers were not given adequate compensation for their land, but he appreciated Haryana, where farmers were offered equity in the project for which their land was acquired.

Replying to a query on the deteriorating law and order situation in Uttar Pradesh, Rahul asked, "No one can comment on law and order situation in UP."

Heading: School closed as SAD opened arms for Panjoli - Indian Express
Content:
The state government's "largesse" in disbursing funds to private schools and colleges in Punjab comes in stark contrast to the aid that the government institutions got in the last one year.

Out of the total funds that were distributed by the Chief Minister, cabinet ministers and chief parliamentary secretaries from their discretionary quota in 2007-08, about 70 per cent went to private schools and colleges.

Punjab Health Minister Laxmi Kanta Chawla tops the list. Sources said she gave Rs 36 lakh during this period to 23 schools in the state, 22 of these were private institutions, which received Rs 34 lakh. While the CM can spend Rs 3 crore out of this quota, cabinet ministers are empowered to give Rs 1.5 crore every year.

Minister Sucha Singh Langah too comes close to Chawla's record. He disbursed funds to 10 schools, out of which nine were private, said sources. Overall, out of the total 371 schools and colleges in Punjab that received Rs 4.28-crore funds, as many as 252 were private institutions.

Punjab Education Minister Upinderjit Kaur seems to be an exception. She gave out more grants to government schools. Sources said Upinderjit disbursed discretionary quota funds to 23 schools, out of which only five were private schools.

Chief Minister Parkash Singh Badal distributed funds to four schools in the state, of which three were private. Out of the total over Rs 10 lakh that the CM distributed from his quota, the government school got only Rs 51,000.

BJP ministers too have been magnanimous with private schools, which got 90 per cent of their funds.

Similarly, Chief Parliamentary Secretary Harish Rai Dhanda gave funds to 20 private schools out of the total 37.

Education Minister Upinderjit Kaur could not be contacted despite repeated attempts.

When contacted, BJP minister Tikshan Sud said the government schools get various grants from the state and the private institutions also need aid as they too further the cause of education.

Heading: Punjab’s new pride: top-heavy babudom - Indian Express
Content:
Using their political clout, members of the Shiromani Akali Dal today bent all rules to hold a political function at Government Secondary School, Panjoli Kalan, and the students had to go without a day of study.

The function was organised by SGPC executive member Karnail Singh Panjoli, who joined the SAD in the presence of party president Sukhbir Badal. Sources said the decision to hold the function on the school premises was taken a few days ago, and information was given to the authorities. Today, the 20 teachers and approximately 350 students did not come to attend the school, the foundation stone of which was laid by Tohra in September 1977.

When contacted, District Education Officer (Secondary) Vijay Kaushal said political functions could not be held in the school after declaring a holiday. "I am not aware of the function," he claimed.

A few students playing on the nearby road said there had been many policemen in the school for the last two days. The villagers, meanwhile, were not too happy with the state of affairs. They said while CM Parkash Singh Badal has made tall claims of improving the standard of education in government schools, his own party declared a holiday for a function.

"Politics mein sub kuch hota hai, bacchon ki kise parwah hai (Everything is allowed in politics, who cares for the students)," a villager said.

The function started in the morning, but Sukhbir arrived two hours late.

Fatehgarh Sahib DC Surjit Singh said he was not aware if permission was taken to hold the function. Interestingly, he himself attended the function. "I was there, but I am not aware if a holiday was declared. Sukhbir had to lay the foundation stones for some development works," the DC said.

Heading: No teachers for remedial classes in Jalandhar district - Indian Express
Content:
The babudom in the state is becoming top heavy, with the Punjab Government's decision to promote the 1992 batch of IAS officers as secretaries. The state will now have 62 officers as secretaries, 30 officers as principal secretaries and 8 officers in the Chief Secretary grade.

There are only 42 departments in the state. Ironically, there is an acute shortage of state service officers and excise and taxation officers, who bear the maximum responsibilities. Sources say CM Parkash Singh Badal has recently cleared the file that the 1992 batch of IAS officers be promoted as secretaries. Now, a meeting of the Departmental Committee for Promotions will be held. The process will take about a fortnight.

In the 1992 batch, there are nine officers. Sarabjit Singh, who is on deputation to the Central Government, is posted as General Manager FCI at Chandigarh. Raji Srivastva, on deputation to Chandigarh, is Additional Finance Secretary. KAP Sinha, on deputation to the Centre, is Private Secretary with Union Minister of State for Industries Ashwani Kumar.

The others are Jaspal Singh, HIS Grewal, Ravinder Singh, Kirandeep Singh Bhullar, Samir Kumar and Ashok Kumar Gupta. With their promotion, there will be 62 Secretaries in the state. The effective strength of Secretaries, though, will stand at 51, since 11 officers are on deputation. From the 1984 batch of IAS to the 1992 batch, all officers will be in Secretary rank.

From the 1974 batch till the 1983 batch of IAS officers, all 30 officers are in the rank of Principal Secretary or Financial Commissioner. Among them, four are on deputation to Central Government. So their strength in the state stands at 26.

Recently, officers of the 1983 batch were promoted as Principal Secretary. These include Suresh Kumar, NS Kang and Jagpal Singh. There are eight officers in the rank of Chief Secretary, from the 1972 batch of IAS officers to the 1974 batch. The present Chief Secretary, RI Singh, is from the 1974 batch.

JS Maini, also of the 1974 batch, is on Central Government deputation. This year, two officers who are in CS grade will retire. These are Robin Gupta, who will retire at the end of this month, and Vijay Kain, who will retire in November. SK Ahluwalia and KBS Sidhu, in the Secretary rank, will retire in September and December respectively.

Meanwhile, there is shortage of officers in Punjab State Civil Services (PCS). While the sanctioned strength is 288, there are only 188 PCS officers in the state, with 100 posts lying vacant. The recruitment was last done in 1998.

There is also a shortage of ETOs in the state. While their sanctioned strength stands at 315, the state faces a shortage of 105 officers. There are only 80 tehsildars in the state.

As a senior officer points out, "Many PCS officers have been given two to three charges. They double up as the SDM and also the DTO. In some cases, they are the SDM of two sub-divisions. The same is the case at the headquarters.''

In Haryana, there are five officers in Chief Secretary grade, 26 principal secretaries and 40 secretaries. In Haryana too, all officers till the 1992 batch officers have been promoted as secretaries. In HP, there are three officers in CS grade, 19 officers in Principal Secretary rank and 25 in Secretary rank. In Himachal, all IAS officers till the 1990 batch have been promoted as Secretaries.

Heading: Employees ensure customers’ comfort - Indian Express
Content:
First they avoided the English test and now the remedial coaching classes. It seems the government schoolteachers are not interested in improving the education system.

The aim of the remedial classes for students of classes VI to VIII with less than 55 per cent marks was to help them in science, mathematics and English subjects. The scheme, which started a month ago under Sarv Shiksha Abhiyan (SSA) and will continue till December 16, has not been implemented in many schools. It was started after noticing poor performance of students in class VIII in the last academic year.

A large number of schools in the Doaba region have not appointed qualified teachers for the scheme. In Jalandhar, 429 schools were to be covered, but a large number of them are yet to start it.

The head teachers of schools were supposed to decide the subjects in which students required coaching and appoint them on Rs 1,800 per month. Ironically, a grant of over Rs 31 lakh for the district for four months has already been released. "Head teachers have shown inability to find good teachers. This sounds like a lame excuse in a state with lakhs of unemployed qualified youths," said a senior officer at the Education Department.

DEO (Secondary) Harinder Sahni said the scheme has not started in some remote areas, and the classes would start

as soon as the teachers were appointed.

Heading: Govt loses lakhs as bigwigs dodge land registration fee - Indian Express
Content:
Locked gates greeted the public on the first day of the all-India public sector banks' strike on Wednesday. The two-day strike, called by the United Forum of Bank Unions (UFBU), will continue on Thursday.

Today, hundreds of bank employees took out a rally from State Bank of India's local head office in Sector 17, Chandigarh, to the Bank Square in Sector 17, Chandigarh. Addressing the gathering, the union leaders resolved that another indefinite strike will be undertaken in November or December if their demands are not met.

For the disappointed account holders, the ATM machines acted as lifesavers. "The employees can go ahead with the strike if they ensure support for the customers. Bank transactions are an integral part of everyone life's today. I, as a businessman, am really affected by such unwanted events," said Ravi Sharma.

"We have filled enough cash in the ATMs to cater to the customers for two days. Certainly, the strike will inconvenience the public but they must understand that this is our last resort," said T K Dutta, a member of the All-India Bank Employees' Association.

Over 10 lakh bank employees all over the country are opposing the privatisation or merger of public sector banks and demand the immediate implementation of the MoUs regarding pension options, compassionate appointments and wage revision.

In Ambala, a demonstration was held outside the UCO Bank in Rai Market, Ambala Cantonment. Leaders of the All-India Bank Officers' Association and Haryana Bank Employees' Federation addressed the rally.

Heading: Rs 40 lakh stolen from shopkeeper - Indian Express
Content:
69 influential citizens evaded stamp duty or paid less than mandated

Even as the common man, despite paying the full levy, struggles at the tehsil offices to get his land sale deeds registered, it seems that the city's high and mighty are making short work of it. How? By simply evading stamp duty and the requisite registration fee in connivance with revenue officials.

On scrutinising the revenue records, Newsline found that at least 69 influential citizens got their land registered for free or paying less than mandated leading the state exchequer to suffer a heavy loss. These cases were detected from August 1, 2006, till March 31, 2008, at Majri sub-tehsil in Mohali district, which covers major parts of the Chandigarh periphery falling under Punjab, during different audit inspections.

"The number of actual violations could be much higher as during audit, the records are checked at random — each and every registered land deed does not come under scrutiny," said a retired Punjab Civil Services officer, who had served as a sub-divisional magistrate in the area. "It amounts to criminal offence and the Vigilance Bureau should take note of the issue," he added.

The evasion ran as high as Rs 4.5 lakh in a single case — Amrita Jhajj of house number 16, Sector 2-A, Chandigarh, evaded this fee (the maximum stamp duty) in a land deal registered on January 3, 2007.

A senior Indian Police Services officer and his son are also among the defaulters with evasion and shortfall amounting to Rs 5.73 lakh in four land deals during the scrutiny period of 20 months.

The rules
According to the norms, the collector (Deputy Commissioner) fixes the minimum rates of registration of land in different parts of the district, which is around 8 per cent as stamp duty and 1 per cent as registration fee payable on the total amount of land deal. For women, the government offers 1 per cent concession in stamp duty.
The tehsildars are supposed to recover the full fees before registering any land deed. In case, the tehsildar suspects that the amount shown in the deed is less than the prevailing market price, he can impound the said land deed under Section 47-A of the Indian Stamp Duty Act and send it to Additional Deputy Commissioner for adjudication.
The official records, however, fail to mention how the 69 land deals were registered without recovering the full stamp duty and registration fee. Also, the records are silent on the action taken after the audit.

But...
So far, the district administration has remained a mute spectator to the violations for "obvious" reasons. After the widespread grabbing of shamlat (common) land, this seems to be the tip of another major land scam in the Chandigarh periphery, where top bureaucrats and politicians own prime chunks of land.

Heading: Women have the last word in consumer court - Indian Express
Content:
Three unidentified men allegedly fled with a bag containing around Rs 40 lakh in cash from a wholesale shop, Mahavir Enterprises, in Kajheri on Wednesday. The shopkeeper, Mahavir Singh, said the men asked him to donate wheat flour to an orphanage.

"I went upstairs to get the items. When I returned, the bag was missing. I was about to go to the bank to deposit the cash when the incident occurred," said Singh.

"A case of theft has been registered against the unknown accused, though the exact amount stolen is yet to be ascertained. Investigations are on," said Devinder Sharma, Station House Officer, Sector 36 police station.

Heading: Encroachment is normal: UT official - Indian Express
Content:
Number of women complainants has increased from zero to 20 per cent in the last decade

The feminist movement has evidently pervaded all spheres today, including the district consumer grievances redressal forum. The number of women complainants has increased to over 20 per cent from being almost negligible in the last decade.

Whether fighting for insurance after her husband's death, problems with a defective fridge or taking the neighbourhood gym to court after the promised kilos were not lost — women are making their presence felt as alert consumers.

"The number of women complainants at the consumer forum is increasing with each passing year. This year, an increasing number of widows have also knocked on the forum's door for getting their insurance claims settled," said Justice K C Gupta, president of the State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission. Most of the women are middle-aged or senior citizens.

A case in point is Neeta Taprial, the wife of a serving defence officer. On September 16, she filed a complaint against Whirlpool, after the vegetable basket in her fridge cracked. The state commission upheld the forum's order directing Whirlpool to rectify the defects and increased the compensation from Rs 5,000 to Rs 10,000.

Another instance — asserting that the dry cleaner had destroyed a velvet suit, a gift from her sister in Canada, Neena Sharma complained to the forum. She was refunded Rs 70 as well as awarded Rs 1000 as compensation.

Another noteworthy case relates to VLCC. In 2006, the forum directed the fitness centre to refund the fees taken from Baljinder Kaur, a resident of Patiala, after her weight stood stable at 90 kgs, even after six months of joining.

Dismissing VLCC's appeal, the forum directed that Rs 20,081 be refunded for the promised 20 kgs she never lost.

"But awareness still needs to be generated in the rural areas. Most of the complaints are filed by urban women," said Justice S N Aggarwal, president of the Punjab State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission.

Heading: Dabwali fire: Committee’s tenure extended by three months for report - Indian Express
Content:
Punjab Police encroaches on Capitol Complex

For the common man encroaching upon a mere feet of area is cause enough to invite a bulldozer at his doorstep, the rules apparently differ for the Punjab Armed Police (PAP).

As highlighted by Newsline on September 14, the 2nd Battalion of the Punjab Police has blatantly encroached upon 14 acres of prime land in the Capitol Complex (behind the Punjab Civil Secretariat).

While the UT Administration had allowed the PAP to pitch their tents in a 6.5-acre area, they have cordoned off more than 20 acres and constructed checkposts at the boundaries of the encroached land as well.

But for UT Chief Engineer S K Jaitley, "encroachment is normal". He said: "We are aware of the fact. Although I was asked to conduct a survey and submit a report, no deadline has been intimated to me for that. Thus, we are taking time to complete the survey."

Meanwhile, a swanky mess, canteens, barracks and even a guesthouse pass off as 'pre-fabricated structures' (UT Administration had allowed the pre-fabricated structures to come up on the land). The mango grove and guava orchards between the Chandigarh Club and Punjab Civil Secretariat have also been encroached upon. An attempt to camouflage the violations is also quite evident — to conceal the unauthorised structures, the Punjab Police has allowed shrubs to grow wild and surround the area from all directions.

Heading: After 25 yrs, lawyer gets a month’s jail term for contempt of court - Indian Express
Content:
In A significant development, Justice T P Garg (Retd), the one-man commission inspecting the Dabwali school fire accident, has submitted his interim report recommending the amount of compensation to be awarded to the kin of the deceased. The compensation to be given to the injured, however, is yet to be prepared and recommended by Garg.

Expressing deep concern over the inordinate delay being caused in finalisation of compensation to be awarded to victims, the Punjab and Haryana High Court today directed Garg to expedite the process.

Justice T P Garg, a retired judge from Allahabad, is inspecting the 1995 Dabwali school fire accident. The report is yet to be handed over to the advocates representing the victims and the Haryana government.

The amount proposed by Garg is a recommendation and not a direction.

The recommendation will be approved by the High Court and then implemented by the Haryana government.

Garg had demanded an extension of six months to prepare the report. Refusing to give six months time, the division bench headed by Chief Justice Tirath Singh Thakur granted

only three months extension. The Chief Justice has made it clear that if Garg demands extension in future, he will have to list reasons for it.

The court also expressed deep concern for the victims of the incident. On the other hand, the counsel representing the Haryana government also averred that the interim report, which is presently with the Registrar General, should be handed over to the Haryana government, so that it could be implemented and compensation can be awarded to the kin of the injured and the deceased. The kin of nearly 400 children and teachers are awaiting the amount of compensation even after the 11 extensions, each of six months, were granted to the one-man commission by the High Court.

A commission was formed on January 29, 2003, to ascertain the amount of compensation to be awarded to the kin of the deceased and those injured in the incident.

Heading: No undertrial to be handcuffed without permission, says High Court - Indian Express
Content:
Twenty five years after Advocate Madan Lal Sharma, a practicing lawyer in the Punjab and Haryana High Court, was accused of contempt of court, a division bench held him guilty and awarded him one month simple imprisonment on Wednesday.

The advocate was issued showcause contempt of court notices by the High Court in 1983 on account of tampering with the judicial record. It was alleged that he connived with his clients to change the date of their case so that its appeal could be filed. The case pertained to a civil dispute concerning possession of a piece of land located in Haryana.

The date was changed since the time within which the appeal could be filed had lapsed. Thus, in order to make the appeal maintainable, the date was allegedly changed. Moreover, the judicial record pertaining to this case had also gone missing. The tampering with judicial record was brought to the notice of the High Court, which issued him showcause notices on March 30, 1983.

The defence counsel for Sharma took the plea that there was no tampering done by him and that there was no evidence against him on record. Refusing to show complete conviction in the stand taken by Sharma, a division bench held Sharma guilty.

"His conduct is also gone into great detail. In the interest of justice, the contemnor cannot be forgiven and he is held guilty of criminal contempt of court," held the High Court.

As per law, a maximum imprisonment of six months and a penalty of Rs 2,000 can be awarded to a contemnor. The court however, awarded one month simple imprisonment to Sharma.

Heading: HC quashes plea to make CM party to Dera case - Indian Express
Content:
To ensure that no undertrial is handcuffed without the prior permission of court, the Punjab and Haryana High Court has issued directions to the Director General of Police, Punjab and Haryana, and the Chandigarh Inspector General of Police to convey the same to their officers.

A Division Bench of the High Court has also directed all the magistrates of Punjab, Haryana and Chandigarh to verify from each and every undertrial produced before them if they were handcuffed by the police.

The High Court has also directed the magistrates to know every detail before granting permission to handcuff any undertrial.

The Court made it clear that the police will have to give a reason if it wants to handcuff an undertrial.

The directions were passed in wake of a public interest litigation (PIL) filed by World Human Rights Protection Council. Its chairman, Advocate Ranjan Lakhanpal, had filed the PIL arising out of a report published in an English daily.

The report had highlighted the pitiable condition of a juvenile, who was booked on charges of murder and was handcuffed with the bed in PGI.

The juvenile, who was undergoing a murder trial in Faridkot was suffering from a heart ailment, as a result of which he was brought to the PGI. Based on a news item, Lakhanpal had filed the PIL which was disposed today with the above directions.

Heading: Shalimar Mall awaits no-objection certificate - Indian Express
Content:
Let us not make a mockery of the law, says court

More than a year after Dera Sacha Sauda Chief Gurmeet Ram Rahim Singh had moved the Punjab and Haryana High Court demanding quashing of an FIR registered against him in the controversial robe case, his counsel on Wednesday vehemently demanded that Chief Minister of Punjab Parkash Singh Badal be made party to the case.

Surprised with the 'sudden discovery' after more than a year, the High Court on Wednesday turned down the request of the counsel. The counsel levelled allegations of malice against the Chief Minister and accused him of playing a pivotal role in getting the FIR registered against the Dera Chief.

Expressing urgency, the counsel even submitted that he will take only one day's time to move an application demanding permission to make Badal party to the case.

Further demanding permission to hear the case on a day-to-day basis, the counsel submitted that notices can be issued to Badal and the state counsels can represent him.

A case was registered against the Dera Chief following a complaint by a Bathinda resident, who had accused Ram Raheem Singh of hurting the religious sentiments of Sikhs by donning the attire of the tenth Sikh guru, Guru Gobind Singh. The proceedings in the trial court have been stayed.

The court sharply reacted to this observing: "Let us not make a mockery of the law. If Badal is made a party to the case, then he is entitled to engage a counsel, file a reply separately, why would only the state counsels appear on behalf of the chief minister. This case is not that important that I give up other cases and devote all the time for this case only."

The court also asked why the case was delayed for over one year in making such submission.

"You filed the petition in July 2007. Till date you have not thought of making the chief minister a party. It is an old case. Before filing a petition, every advocate knows who all to make a party to the case. One can understand if a counsel moves an application for making someone party to the case after a month. But you are coming to the Court after more than a year," the Court observed.

Giving a choice the Court told the counsel: "The court can allow you to move an application to make the chief minister a party but then the stay on the proceedings in the trial court will be vacated."

Finding himself in a fix, the counsel kept requesting the court that stay should not be vacated yet permission to make Badal a party should be allowed. However, the court refused to allow the request.

The HC further observed that mere making Badal a party to the case is not sufficient.

"If there are no allegations against Badal, what purpose will it serve by making him a party? Without any allegations, the case will not succeed. You will have to amend the petition. There is no averment, no allegation against the Chief Minister."

Putting forward newspaper reports, the counsel pointed out certain statements made by the chief minister against the Dera Chief.

The counsel alleged that the FIR was registered against the Dera chief on the directions of Badal. "How does the chief minister comes into the picture? If he was interested in getting the Dera chief implicated, don't you think he will have got him implicated in a much serious offence than this.

Tomorrow you might come up and say that you want to make the Prime Minister a party to the case. You think I am going to allow that?," the court remarked.

Heading: Cholamandalam to compensate harassed customer - Indian Express
Content:
Panchkula Deputy Commissioner Rajender Kataria, along with officials of various departments of the Administration, visited the Shalimar Mall in Sector 5 to inspect the site. The Shalimar Mall has applied to the Administration for a no-objection certificate (NOC), which they claim is the last stage of series of approvals that are required before the opening of the mall. Immediately after the NOC is given, officials of the mall said, that the final date for the inauguration would be declared.

"The DC and Superintendent of Police (SP) Sandeep Khirwar, along with others, visited the mall for a final inspection. The officials including SDM, Executive officer, MC, Estate officer, HUDA, officials of the PWD (B and R) were among the ones who inspected the site," RK Aggarwal, the mall's MD said.

If everything goes well, the mall, with a three-level basement parking and located right in the heart of the city, is expected to open by Diwali this year. "The mall is almost ready and is awaiting the final approval from the Panchkula Administration. The mall would provide a retail mix to accommodate all categories of people, not only from the city but the tricity," added Aggarwal.

With three movie halls to accommodate around 750 persons and capsule elevators, the mall is expected to cater to all needs under one roof. "Our location is one of the major USPs. We also aim to introduce a night life to the city. As for tickling the taste buds, we have 10 to 12 food courts with a capacity double than what others have," said Aggarwal.

Talking to Newsline, Kataria said: "We conducted a preliminary meeting today after which the Shalimar Mall was inspected and certain observations were made which were later communicated to the officials of the mall. There are a number of departments from which the approval has to be taken regarding building, lighting, parking, electricity and security among others." He added that the moment the required instructions are followed, the NOC would be given.

Heading: Pest control company to pay up for deficiency in service - Indian Express
Content:
The District Consumer Disputes Redressal Forum has directed Cholamandalam Finance Company to pay Rs 5,000 as compensation for harassing a customer. The company has also been directed to waive off the bounce charges of Rs 500 of one installment, which were unnecessarily levied on him.

The complainant, Chander Mohan, availed a personal loan of Rs 35,000 from Cholamandalam in 2004. The net amount he received was Rs 31,623 through the Central Bank of India, with a monthly installment of Rs 1,894.

The complainant said he paid 13 installments without any break till June 12, 2008. Only one installment dated November 5, 2007, bounced because of insufficient funds in his account.

The fact came to the notice of the complainant when the collection agent of the company met him. Mohan got a certificate of the payment from the bank in December 2007, that his account had been debited with Rs 1,894 on November 5, 2007, towards clearing the installment.

It was alleged that despite this, the company sent his representative and made phone calls to complainant at odd hours, harassing him and his wife, who is a heart patient.

Mohan was also asked to pay a fine of Rs 500 for delayed payment. He then moved the consumer forum. Notices were issued to the company but no one appeared to contest the complaint or to file the reply; hence the opposite party was proceeded exparte.

The forum was satisfied that all installments have been paid by the complainant, except one, which also stands clear at present. It was found that the fine of Rs 500 has been levied on the complainant without any justification.

The forum also said the company unnecessarily harassed and disturbed him by making calls on phone. "This assertion of the complainant stands unrebutted by the company, as there is no written statement on their behalf. Moreover, it is clear from the complainant's passbook and certificate that his account has been debited with Rs 1,894 on November 5, 2007, towards ECS clearing," said Jagroop Singh Mahal , president of the District Forum.

The company has also been directed to pay Rs 1,500 as litigation charges.

Heading: Revisit your childhood at the International Dolls Museum - Indian Express
Content:
The District Consumer Disputes Redressal Forum has directed J S Pest Control to pay Rs 1,500 as compensation, including the cost of litigation, for deficiency in service that caused harassment to the complainant.

Saudagar Singh, availed an anti-termite treatment for the woodwork in his newly constructed house in 2003 from J S Pest Control and was charged Rs 3,000 with a five-year guarantee.

When the termites resurfaced after only 8 months, the complainant approached the pest control company's agent and was assured that an anti-termite treatment would be conducted. The treatment was again carried out in 2004. Despite that, the termites reappeared within seven months after which another treatment was conducted in 2005. After the termites infested the wooden structures again in the next four months, the doors, windows, wardrobes, cupboards and woodwork on the walls suffered extensive damage.

Alleging huge loss and harassment, the complainant moved the consumer forum.

J S Pest Control, in its reply, stated that the guarantee given by the company excluded the portion of the doors and windows where the termites had caused damage. Sufficient damage had already been done to the woodwork prior to their treatment. It was pleaded that whenever intimation was given to them, they immediately got the complainant's house checked for infestation of termites. During inspection, it was found that no living termites were there and that apart from the old portion of the wood that had already been destroyed before the treatment, the rest of the woodwork was treated.

The forum said it is not possible to arrive at the conclusion that the complainant suffered a loss of Rs 1.50 lakh. "However, it is proved on record that the company gave anti-termite treatment thrice as and when he approached them with the complaint. It is therefore established that the treatment of anti-termite on the woodwork, at the residence of complainant, did not work effectively as assured," the forum ruled.

Heading: MC plan for expansion of water supply system ready - Indian Express
Content:
The International Dolls Museum is a place that will never cease to bring out the child in you. Hundreds of dolls smile back at you at the museum inside Bal Bhavan in Sector 23 and if you have an instant urge to be playful, we won't blame you!

Set up in 1985, the museum, home to more than 350 dolls from 28 countries, was the brainchild and initiative of Rotarian RK Saboo, who would bring back a doll from every country he visited for the children of Chandigarh.

Founded under the auspices of the Indian Council of Child Welfare, the first display generated a lot of excitement and the latest to join the beautiful group are two Arabian dolls — a gift to the museum from visitors who were floored by the collection.

A small note on the place where the dolls came from, the flag of the respective countries and also some paintings initially accompanied the display... "These give us a glimpse into the lives of people of different countries, their costumes, across eras and ages," Tejinder K Bajwa, the former in-charge of the place says as he takes you around the museum.

Dressed in traditional costumes, the dolls come from as far as Argentina, Austria, Belgium, France, Russia, USA, Germany, Finland and Israel. The museum was recently renovated and now wears a new look and feel, courtesy the Chandigarh Industrial and Tourism Development Corporation Limited (CITCO).

An interesting section here is that of dolls representing fairy-tale characters like Aladdin, Ali Baba, Cinderella, Sleeping Beauty and Snow White... all designed and made by local artists and a set of four displays 'tell' a visual story.

"This one is a big attraction for children and we hope to have an area in the near future where children can play with dolls and feel more connected with the place and have fun as well. In fact, we would love to get some rare dolls from the people of the city," says Tejinder while showing tableaux representing mythological and epic tales. These present scenes from the Mahabharata, Ramayana and stories from the lives of the Buddha, Eklavaya, Jhansi ki Rani, Sikh gurus and Christ. It is a great way to introduce children to history, mythology, culture.

The museum also has a special section devoted to the dolls from various parts of India, with a special emphasis on the brides of the country. A must-check here is a toy train presented by the Rotary Club, Ebingen, West Germany and according to Tejinder, the museum's a big hit with school children and foreign tourist and also has a guide for an engrossing tour. "And on popular demand by the children, we hope to add some Barbie dolls soon to the lovely group," smiles Bajwa.

Yes, we have to move with the times!

Heading: Setia all set to go, schools rejoice - Indian Express
Content:
The Municipal Corporation will hire consultants for augmentation of water supply and sewerage system in the city. The consultants will prepare feasibility reports and thereafter, the detailed project report for submission to the Ministry of the Urban Development under the Jawaharlal Nehru Urban Renewal Mission.

The proposal will be discussed in the meeting of Finance and Contract Committee to be held on Thursday.

The consultants will conduct studies in all urban sectors of Chandigarh from Sectors 1 to 56, Punjab and Haryana Secretariat, Vidhan Sabha, High Court. The villages and rehabilitation colonies in the jurisdiction of the civic body will also come under its purview. The other areas to be studied include the Industrial Area, Phase I and II, Manimajra Town and Mauli Jagran Colony.

The team will also study the feasibility of bringing water from Ganguwal Head works to water works at Sector 39 under gravity. This will in addition to exploring the possibility of bringing additional water 40 MGD from Water works at Kajauli under the augmentation water supply Scheme V and VI.

Besides, a study on unaccounted and non-revenue water and improvement in water pressure to supply water for 24 hours in the city will be undertaken. It will take six months from the date of allotment to submit the final report by the consultants. Terms and conditions for engaging the consultants have been framed, sources said.

Heading: To assess available flora-fauna, survey at Botanical Garden soon - Indian Express
Content:
The news of Director Public Instructions (Schools) S K Setia's transfer to his home state, Haryana, has been welcomed with relief by a majority of school principals and teachers. UT Administration S F Rodrigues signed his relieving letter today.

While Setia is tightlipped on the issue, government schools are a happy lot, even if it may be only for the time

being. As per the information available, the Haryana government has asked the UT administration to send Setia back to his parent cadre, citing reasons of shortage of administrative staff. Even in the last month, the State government had requested the UT Administration to shift him to Haryana and had even proposed a panel of officers to decide on his replacement. Samawartak Singh, an HCS officer, who was tipped to join as DPI (Schools) was later given the post of Secretary, Municipal Corporation.

Why has his exit made teachers and principals happy?

During his tenure as DPI, Setia had kept most of the teachers and principals on tenterhooks, mainly because of the 'novel' ideas proposed every now and then. "His mind was always brimming with out-of-the-box ideas, the practical implication of which was doubtful. Since he was in the seat of authority, we could not disagree with him blatantly. But we are glad that finally there will be an end to his arbitrary rule," says a principal requesting anonymity.

"Setia had tried to bring in reforms in schools but before giving ideas, he should have kept in mind that our education system is different from that followed in the West. Providing interactive boards in all the schools when some of the schools lack even the basic infrastructure was not viable," adds another principal on condition of anonymity.

In the one-year as DPI (S), Setia was also at loggerheads with the Sarv Shiksha Abhiyaan (SSA) teachers. "We are happy to know that he is going back to his State cadre. Setia has being detrimental to the rights of SSA teachers. From denying salaries for summer vacations to not giving maternity leave, we have been a harassed lot during his term," says Arvind Rana, an SSA teacher.

Heading: Senate polls: tense moments as counting begins for Graduate constituency - Indian Express
Content:
In a first-of-its-kind survey to be conducted in the Botanical Garden near Sarangpur, a stock of the available flora and fauna will be compiled.

Deputy Conservator of Forests and Director Environment Ishwar Singh said that since the garden was started a year back, flora and fauna have developed gradually. "As the gardens become older, the variety of species increases. Regular monitoring is required to know what kind of plants and animals are making the garden a habitat," says Singh.

The Department of Zoology, Panjab University,

is most likely to be given the task of conducting the survey.

The Botanical Garden, spread over an 88-acre plot, has a number of sections aimed to promote eco tourism. Two lakes, developed in the garden along the Patiala ki Rao, have been designed for rainwater harvesting. Apart from rainwater harvesting, these would also help in recharging underground water aquifers. With heavy rainfall experienced during the monsoon, the filled water bodies have proved beneficial in supporting the flora and fauna.

Medicinal plant gardens and herbal gardens have been developed over 40 acres of land. Over 75 species of medicinal trees and 55 species of medicinal shrubs, herbs and climbers have already been planted in this section.

Heading: There is nothing we can do even if students submit manipulated reports: DSW - Indian Express
Content:
As the counting of votes was on throughout the day at Panjab University, candidates for the Graduate constituency were keeping their fingers crossed, With the first preferences being counted, the names of only five candidates with a considerable lead could be known till the filing of the report.

Only two candidates have crossed the 3,462-vote mark fixed as the limit for declaring a candidate as a winner, while the other three have secured winning position on the reserved seats of which two are for Punjab and one is for Chandigarh.

The counting of votes in the constituency is expected to take another day atleast as votes are counted manually. Having felt the heat with the traditional electoral process employed in the elections, the candidates are talking of a need to bring in changes like revision of voter lists and a mechanism to expedite counting of votes in the Panjab University.

Heading: Punjab sets another precedent in Mohali, allots 369 concrete booths - Indian Express
Content:
With two days to the deadline for student leaders to submit a list of the expenses incurred during PU elections, the students are yet to show any urgency while the authorities appear as helpless as ever.

Rather than taking action against students' laxity, the officials are busy requesting students to submit their expense charts. While the Lyngdoh Committee prescribes an upper limit of Rs 5000 per candidate, the authorities have little option but to accept the lists, even if they are manipulated.

Interestingly, the INSO, one of the student bodies, has submitted similar expenses for all the candidates with the expense break ups corresponding similarly for all its candidates. This particular body was reportedly showing movies and arranging dance parties for students during elections.

DSW Prof Naval Kishore said, "There is nothing we can do even if students submit manipulated expenses. As per the Lyngdoh Committee guidelines, they have to submit a self-attested report of the expenses".

Talking to Newsline, an official from the university

said, "We have to follow students to ensure that they complete the formalities. Even with the Lyngdoh Committees recommendations, there are gaping loopholes that need to be fixed."

Heading: ‘India’s domestic flower market expected to grow to Rs 10,000 crore’ - Indian Express
Content:
Janata Rehri Market: 130 booths ready, tenders for others to be floated shortly

The Punjab government on Wednesday set another precedent in Mohali by allotting 369 concrete booths in lieu of illegal kutcha kiosks, which were wiped out in a major fire at the Janata Rehri Market in Phase 3B1 on June 1, 2007. The government had earlier paid Rs 25,000 cash compensation to all those running the 377 kiosks destroyed in the inferno.

While chairing the allotment process at PUDA Bhawan in Sector 62, Punjab Cooperation Minister Captain Kanwaljit Singh said this was the second bounty by chief minister Parkash Singh Badal to the Mohali residents after paying record compensation of Rs 1.5 crore per acre for over 300 acres of land acquired to set up an international airport in Jheourheri village.

Capt Kanwaljit also reminded that the Badal government had also implemented farmer-friendly Land Pooling Scheme, which entails participation of landowners in the development on the acquired land in Punjab.

Immediately after allotment of booths, hundreds of beneficiaries and their family and friends broke into grand celebrations. They danced to the beats of the dhol and distributed sweets. "It's like a dream come true," said Sohan Lal, an elated allottee.

Manjeet Kaur said the day was a result of her prayers and that she had lost all hopes to get rehabilitated.

"Our area councillor Harman Preet Singh Prince is our saviour," said Ramesh, while offering ladoos to Prince.

Rajinder Singh, another allottee, hoped that after 16 months of displacement, new booths will help them restart their closed business.

"No words can express our gratitude to the councillor, Capt Kanwaljit and the chief minister, who understood our pains and miseries to make us see this day," said Mahesh Kumar, while dancing to the beats of the dhol.

As rescheduled, the Greater Mohali Area Development Authority (GMADA) Chief Administrator (CA) Vivek Partap Singh, Additional CA Balwinder Singh Multani and Estate Officer (EO) Sukhjeet Pal Singh began the draw of lots for allotment of booths according to eligibility established during a survey conducted in 1998.

Capt Kanwaljit, accompanied by councillor Harman Preet Singh Prince, picked the first slip to kickstart the proceedings of booths allotment.

Speaking on the occasion, Capt Kanwaljit said on the persistence of Prince, he had impressed upon the chief minister who agreed to award cash compensation and concrete booths to the fire victims. He also assured that the names of the eight persons, who were left out from the allotment of booths as they were among couples or minor children, who were claiming separate booths in a single family, will also be considered after taking up their cases with the chief minister.

GMADA EO told Newsline that while 130 booths were ready, tenders to construct the remaining 239 booths will be floated shortly to make allotments at the earliest. Though the final decision was yet to be taken, the allottees are likely to be asked to bear the construction cost of booths.

No sooner the allotment process concluded at 1 pm, the beneficiaries turned their way to the market, where they continued celebrating the development till evening.

Heading: Power, water supply in Mohali to be snapped from today - Indian Express
Content:
"New challenges are emerging for India's growing floriculture industry. Even as the domestic demand for flowers is growing annually by 15-20 per cent in major cities, the export growth has struck a bumpy path," said S Jafar Naqvi, president, iFlora and chief co-coordinator, Flora Expo 2008, while talking with media persons today.

In the city to promote the forthcoming expo, which is being organised in New Delhi from September 26 to 28, Naqvi said the latest export trends available from the Directorate General of Foreign Trade under the Commerce Ministry show that floriculture export in 2007-08 was $ 83.67 million.

"It is not a small achievement that India's domestic flower and plant market, now valued at over Rs 1,000 crore is further expected to grow to Rs 10,000 crore in the future," he said.

The International Flora Expo 2008, along with third International Landscape and Gardening Expo 2008 and International Florist and Floral Art Expo 2008, is the third such expo to be held.

The main theme of the event will be to highlight the potential business and investment opportunities and to promote floriculture as a Rs 10,000 crore business opportunity and creating a million jobs.

"Thirty-two countries participated in the expo last year. So far, we have received confirmation from nine countries but expect participation of more than 30 international groups," he added.

Heading: Found in translation - Indian Express
Content:
Bull death: MC employees block traffic, intensify stir

The week-old deadlock between the employees of Mohali Municipal Council (MC) and the district administration on Wednesday reached flashpoint with striking civic staffers threatening to snap essential services like power and water supply, sanitation and streetlight services indefinitely in entire Mohali from Thursday.

As their demand to cancel an FIR lodged against the animal catching staff of the MC on charges of causing death of a stray bull on September 17 was not fulfilled despite repeated assurances, the MC employees today went out on the roads to block traffic, gherao police station, stage dharna and take out massive protest rally in different parts of the city.

Continuing their indefinite strike, which had already suspended work at the MC Bhawan in Sector 68 for the fifth consecutive day, the MC Employees' Union threatened to intensify the stir and spread the strike across the state if their demand was not met forthwith.

Hundreds of striking civic staffers blocked vehicular traffic on main road connecting Chandigarh with Mohali at Phase VII-VIII traffic light point around noon and squatted on the road for almost an hour. Later, they gheraoed Phase VIII police station for almost half-an-hour and then turned via PUDA Bhawan towards Deputy Commissioner's office, in front of which they staged a massive dharna and again blocked traffic on road passing in front of the district administrative complex.

Municipal Councillor Harman Preet Singh Prince, who has put his weight behind the agitating civic employees, said the protesters have called employees of all other government departments in Mohali to join hands with them to extend the agitation to other departments as well. He urged the administration to immediately take note of the situation and arrange for an amicable solution to the impasse before the situation goes out of control.

Heading: Coming Soon - Indian Express
Content:
India's only concert harp has featured in the famous Carmen opera and is an integral part of the Symphony Orchestra of India

From the small town of Watten near Innsbruck in Austria to the hustle and bustle of compelling Delhi, this 1.8 metre harp made of seasoned wood with nylon strings has rendered a dozen sunny performances since it first came to India in 2004. And what sets the little known traditional instrument aside is that it is the one and only concert harp in India. "The harp was gifted to us by Austria-based Swarovski Crystal World in 2004 and we lend it for orchestras and symphonies without any charge. Usually, orchestras and ensembles from abroad borrow this harp," says Munish Bahl, adviser, Press relations and Cultural Affairs with the Austrian Cultural Forum.

In the hands of 33-year-old Austrian harp player Sabine Kraus, the traditional string instrument recreated a composition of Handel in B major in September while in Georges Bizet's famous opera Carmen that regaled Delhiites in April, Lucie Marical from Paris-based chamber orchestra OstinatO lent a lush and forceful fury to the opera with an Indian twist. "The search for the harp began two months before production and I found out by asking musicians in Delhi. For Carmen we required a specifically heavy and old style harp," says Antoine Redon, from the Neemrana foundation. The concert harp was also used for Pearl Fishers opera by Georges Bizet, held in Delhi and Mumbai in summer of 2005.

Currently, the harp is lodged with NCPA for a performance by Symphony Orchestra of India. "This will be the fifth performance with the harp and Magryta from Kazakhstan would perform on it," says Onay, a cellist who is part of the Symphony Orchestra of India. The performance in Mumbai is slated for today. "The harp was played as part of an Italian opera in 2006 and there was a workshop last year with foreign players in Mumbai," says Bahl.

However, the sunniest performance so far with the harp was rendered by Salzburger Saitenklang, an Austrian ensemble this September in Goa, Mumbai and Delhi. Sabine Kraus, part of the three-member ensemble enthralled the audience with her baroque style pieces and the musical jamboree with another string instrument—zither and guitar. "I was not acquainted with this harp and got to tune it just hours before the performance," says Kraus who started playing professionally in 2003. Kraus also conducted a two-hour workshop in Goa with the harp in September. "The group was invited by the Entertainment Society of Goa and the two-hour workshop was organized by Kala Mandir," says Bahl. Up next, the harp will lend its tune in a French opera If I were a King: by Adolphe Adam to be held in November 2009. "We will certainly have the harp for the next French Opera where the action is taking place in Goa next November," shares Redon.

Heading: Fresh Cut - Indian Express
Content: After Indian cricket captain Mahendra Singh Dhoni, it is now the turn of Bipasha Basu to turn designer for sportswear brand Reebok. Basu, who is also a brand ambassador of the label, has worked closely with in-house designers to develop a line of women's gym wear that will hit stores soon. The look of the collection, in keeping with the actor's image, is funky and energetic with a lot of classic colours like blues, pearl whites and blacks. That apart, Basu is also excited about her forthcoming regional film, Pankh by Bengali director Sudipto Chattopadhyay's Pankh, where she plays an alter-ego to a boy going through gender confusion. "It's a delightful role, quite different from anything I have done before in my career. The script was so convincing that I just could not give up the offer," she says.

Heading: Style check - Indian Express
Content:
Punjab's youth, politics and love come together with Hashar-a love story

Thankfully this one's looking at the broader picture than just the 'abroad' theme. With youth and politics at its core Gaurav Trehan's Punjabi flick 'Hashar- a love story' may strike just the right chord with the young audience. "It's a film of the youth not just for the youth," Tarlochan Singh throws light on his story that is "meaningful and entertaining." The team of Hashar met the scribes at PVR Cinemas, Centra Mall. Singer-actor Babbu Mann, who is in the lead role, turns producer for the film launching his banner Mann Films. The Babbu Mann-Gaurav Trehan duo first worked together for the singer's first album.

Amidst spilt popcorn and too few a seats to hold the crew present for the event, Trehan tells us, "It's is a treatment film. We have used the contemporary Punjabi youth as the backdrop to highlight the urban- rural contrast. The film is a journey of a young guy who comes from a village to Chandigarh for studying. Dealing with relations, the movie traces the ups and downs of his life." Part of that is the love triangle completed by the two leading ladies Gurleen Chopra and Mahima Mehta. The film also casts Rana Ranbir and Ashmita Vasudev.The movie has been shot in Panjab University, various parts of Chandigarh and Ludhiana to give it a 'realistic' look. "There were no budget constraints since we wanted real locations. Moreover films are made with passion not money," smiles Trehan. So what kind of homework went into portraying the politics angle? "Most of the student leaders are my friends," Babbu, who seemed drunk with the excitement of the film (literally!) tells that he was constantly in touch with SOPU and PUSU workers (so there is something they can come together for!).
