The September 26 release of the movie becomes significant in light of the recent PU elections and if Prof P S Nirola, who wrote the screenplay, is to be believed, "the MCM catfight could have been avoided if the film was released prior to the elections!" Here's hoping it works well for the next year.

Heading: Mass Movement - Indian Express
Content:
The runway is what sets the pulse racing for the older of the tantalising model twins

It isn't often that we read Tupur Chatterjee's name separated from her sister Tapur. But during the just concluded India Couture Week, Tupur tells us that it was a conscious decision on their part to not do the same shows. "Once in a way, it is nice to see us separately. Only then probably people can see the difference between us," she says, as the make-up artiste does a good job of making her eyes look dramatic for Pallavi Jaikishan's show. But do people confuse between the two? "All the time. But now we are used to it. If you spend a couple of days with us, you will know the difference in our facial structure and also our personalities," she says, as she enters the green room.

The backstage seems to be the centre of all activity right now with make-up artistes and hairstylists getting their act right, caterers serving some diet food, event organisers running helter-skelter to get the stage ready, choreographers doling out instructions, models dabbing on some rouge and gloss and an in-house photographer capturing these moments. For Tupur, who is older by 12 minutes, feels the backstage is a quintessential part of their life because it is here that they spend most of their time dressing up, making friends, practicing their walk and, sometimes, thinking of innovative ways of killing time. Other models, who are doing similar stuff, hover around graciously as Tupur fields simple questions. "In our profession, the waiting period is the biggest drawback. Models make it to the venue at least seven hours in advance. If we could cut down on the waiting period, we would look so much fresher," she says sipping on water.

In spite of being in the profession for eight years, her enthusiasm is still in place. She looks every bit excited even today, about wearing yet another designer ensemble and sauntering down the ramp. "I get very excited but I am never nervous of walking the ramp. If the ramp is slippery or has paper bits, it does get a little scary," says the 28-year-old, while practicing her sequence of steps. And with the couture week being more elaborate in terms of settings, choreography and clothes, the anxiety becomes two-fold.

The sisters have had a firm finger on the fashion pulse of the city. But Tupur, a graduate in Biology, feels that the industry has grown massively over the last couple of years. "Today there are more international designs in the market. There is a Western feel to Indian wear," she says as she points out to the outfit she wears. "Also the fashion shows are more organised now, unlike the earlier days when you did not know what was happening."

But for this granddaughter of Hrishikesh Mukherjee, one of the most revered filmmakers of the industry, Bollywood is still a distant calling. "It is those two minutes on the ramp that make me feel like a queen. Also, most of your dreams of wearing the best clothes available in the country also get fulfilled." No wonder then, that between shouts of 'Hurry Up' and 'Find the damn hair pin' in the green room, Tupur manages to hold on to her nerve.

Heading: Ode to a poetess - Indian Express
Content: After winning critical acclaim their debut production film, Khosla Ka Ghosla, Raj Hiremath and Savita Raj Hiremath of Tandav Films Entertainment Pvt. Ltd. are now producing a video to mobilize masses to stand up in the movement against poverty. And this is not just any video for it will feature renowned celebrities from different fields. A public social advertising (PSA), the video will pan on AR Rehman, Gulzar, Sonu Nigam, Sunidhi Chauhan, Yuvraj Singh, Ranbir Kapoor and 'Khuda Kay Liye' actress, Imaan Ali. Any guesses for who's behind the camera? Meghna Gulzar. Assigned by the United Nations Millennium Campaign (UNMC), Tandav Films, through the video, also aim at educating the masses on Millennium Development Goals (MDGs). The video will essentially focus on the global advocacy campaign called "Stand up and Take Action". In last October, 43 million people across the globe took part in this campaign and set up a Guinnies record. A bigger number is what the UNMC is eyeing on this year and hence the involvement of Indian celebrities. "Celebrities can attract a lot of attention and help in making a differnce. This video will be aired free of cost in major television channels," says Raj Hiremath, the producer of this video. "Starting from advertising to a stage where we are all set to produce many films is a journey which I believe is just an extension to our creativity. Advertising kept us a bit restricted since we had to work on a set brief, while film making is more liberal in many ways. I am glad to have such an opportunity to work with renowned organization like UNMC and I am sure that we would prove them our creativity and credibility," he adds.

Heading: Live Well - Indian Express
Content: The ink has run out of the pen, and the words have come to a full stop. After writing for years, and giving the world of music the famous Pritam Aan Milo, Saroj Mohini Nayyar, wife of late music director OP Nayyar, passed away on Tuesday night in Mumbai. An accomplished lyricist, she wrote the C H Atma/Geeta Dutt song, Preetam Aan Milo, which launched Opee into the big league of Bollywood composers. She was 75 years old and is survived by three daughters and a son. Her nephew is the famous Punjabi composer, Jaidev. Daugther of late freedom fighter, Vir Deva Vir, who was also one of the founders of Bharat Scouts and Guides Movement, one of Saroj Mohini's is Chandigarh-based Rakesh Arora.

Heading: Live it up - Indian Express
Content:
His students call him the King of Yoga, but Dinesh Kashikar happily settles in humility. In Mohali for a yoga course (basic pranayaam and seven-chakra meditation course is meant for the beginners) in Paragon School, the 34-year-old Art of Living yoga instructor is an IIT graduate associated with his 'mission' for the last 13 years. "With Art of Living I can do whatever I want, I lead the course of my life. But in the corporate world everybody is part of a never-ending rat race," Kashi says that while the world is in some search or other he lives a content life.

So why is it that so many young people are turning to yoga? "People today are more open and ready to experiment. They have the courage to do whatever they want to," he replies. Since '95 Kashi has travelled extensively teaching yoga to yoga teachers. "People ask me why I, being so intelligent, have turned to yoga and meditation, I tell them that I'm doing it because I'm intelligent!" he signs off.

Heading: Six companies roped in to harness solar energy - Indian Express
Content:
Pucker up
Nature's Essence has introduced their latest colour range of lipsticks comprising different colours in vibrant and exciting shades. With ingredients which include Honey Wax and almond oil, the lipsticks allow the colour to glide on smoothly and wear comfortably for hours. The lip colour pallette is impressive and is priced between Rs 95 and Rs 1,180.

Think Straight
HAIR styling is an "expression of art", and today the world has woken up to it. One style that is hot in fashion now is straight hair. "Straight hair is simple hair that adds a touch of elegance to the modern women's style statement," says Najeeb Ur Rehman, National Technical Head, Schwarzkopf Professional, "but the key is to use the right kind of treatment & products." Schwarzkopf Professional has launched 'Strait Therapy' with an in-built treatment process which ensures that your hair glows with the shine of good health. And the best part is that you can do it at home. The kit consists of a straightening cream, neutralizing milk and protection spray. With the help of Bonacure Hairtherapy Smooth Control range of products offered by Schwarzkopf Professional, it is now possible to manage sleek strait looks even at home. Also Sparkle and Flatliner, from the Osis range styling products is efficient in de-tangling and protecting your hair, enabling you to style your hair for a perfect finish.

Heading: Kuldeep sticks to claim even as Congress calls him liar - Indian Express
Content:
The Haryana Renewable Energy Development Agency (HAREDA) has signed memoranda of understanding (MoUs) with six Independent Power Producers (IPPs) to generate 12 MW of power from solar energy with an investment of about Rs 240 crore.

The MoUs have been signed with RS India Wind Energy, New Delhi, and Astonfield Renewable Resources, Kolkata, for setting up solar power projects of 3 MW capacity each; with Epuron Renewable Energy, New Delhi, and Azure Power India, New Delhi, for setting up projects of 2 MW capacity each. The investment in the projects with RS India Wind Energy and Astonfield Renewable Resources would cost about Rs 60 crore each and with Epuron Renewable Energy and Azure Power India, about Rs 40 crore each.

The signing of the MoUs will help the state government to harness its abundant solar power generation potential, said Chief Minister Bhupinder Singh Hooda, who was present when the MoUs were signed. The firms would prepare detailed project reports within two months and the projects would be implemented and commissioned by December 31, 2009.

In addition to these, MoUs had also been signed with Omax Auto, Gurgaon and Selecto Systems, Faridabad, for setting up solar power projects of one MW capacity each. These projects are special cases as in these, use of land was not involved and the energy would be harnessed through rooftop installations.

These could be showcased for replication in other industries, said Financial Commissioner, Power and Renewable Energy, Ashok Lavasa.

Heading: Dalai Lama’s security beefed up - Indian Express
Content:
Lok Sabha Speaker Somnath Chatterjee's statement yesterday that he had not received any resignation letter from rebel Congress MP Kuldeep Bishnoi has evoked strong reaction from the state Congressmen.

Haryana Pradesh Congress Committee president Phool Chand Mullana said truth had finally prevailed and Kuldeep Bishnoi was now fully exposed. "No one can doubt the words of Somnath Chatterjee, while one can easily doubt the intentions and claims of Bishnoi," he said.

HPCC spokesperson Ved Prakash Vidrohi said that it was clear now that Bishnoi had not been speaking the truth. "Bishnoi was afraid to face election," claimed Vidrohi. HPCC Media Convenor Pawan Jain urged Bishnoi to quit politics.

However, in a statement issued here today, Kuldeep reacted strongly to Chatterjee's statement. Bishnoi reiterated that he had indeed sent his resignation to the Speaker and anybody could confirm it.

He said the Congress was afraid of his growing popularity and this was the main reason why his resignation was not accepted.

Heading: State BJP to frame ‘Vision-2020’ for govt - Indian Express
Content:
The government has decided to strengthen the security cover around Tibetan spiritual leader and temporal head, the Dalai Lama. A proposal to this effect was sent by the Kangra Senior Superintendent of Police to the liaison office of the Union Ministry for Foreign Affairs situated at McLeodganj, after which the Central government approved it.

Sources said a decision to install at least six close circuit television (CCT) cameras on the premises of the Dalai Lama's official residence at McLeodganj has been taken to keep a close watch. They said the CCT cameras are being installed as there is a large open space between the outer circle and inner circle of security of the spiritual leader.

A control room is being set up in the office of the Deputy Superintendent of Police, who is in charge of the Dalai Lama's security. Besides, the surveillance by the police has also been increased in the limits of McLeodganj police station and a close vigil is being kept on the structures situated around the residence of the Dalai Lama.

When contacted, Kangra SSP Atul Fulzele confirmed that six CCT cameras were being installed in and around the official residence of the spiritual leader to strengthen the security cover. The cameras would be installed within two-three weeks, said the SSP.

"Now we will also have electronic surveillance on the premises of the Tibetan spiritual leader along with the manual one,'' said the district police chief.

Meanwhile, the fifth two-day World Parliamentarians' Convention on Tibet beginning October 20 at Paris has been postponed indefinitely due to cancellation of the Dalai Lama's visit to Europe, said a press release.

The release said, "We offer deep apologies and regret the inconvenience caused to our friends and supporters. The next date of the convention is being worked out and it will be intimated to all concerned at the earliest.''

Heading: New CFL tenders floated for bijli bachat scheme - Indian Express
Content:
During the coming month, the Bharatiya Janata Party in Himachal Pradesh is expected to initiate a core proposal for implementation of the idea of better coordination between the party and government. The party would sit together on October 5 to frame the "Vision Document-2020", with a proposed roadmap for every sector that would be submitted to the government for implementation. Framing of the draft document backed by the party's ideology would be at the core of the agenda of the state executive meeting scheduled for October 4 and 5.

It is learnt that during last month's training session of the party leadership and party cadre conducted in Shimla, national president Rajnath Singh had called upon the party cadre, leaders of frontal organisations and convenors of various cells for brainstorming on important issues such as employment generation, emerging areas of economic development, skill development of youth and scope of tourism development. "The idea is to work out a best possible way of implementing developmental schemes which uphold the party's ideology and are in public interest. The greatest focus would be on employment generation, said a party leader.

Various proposals that were raised for implementation in the state during the recently held national executive meeting in Bangalore would also be taken up for incorporation in the party's agenda and mode of functioning before the Lok Sabha elections.

While in the past only the government departments have been involved in identifying the roadmap for themselves, it is the first time that the BJP is framing a futuristic plan for the state as a suggestion to the government. It is being said that this idea, floated by the national leadership, is also being seen as a helping hand to the government to keep reminding it of its election promises outlined in the party manifesto.

Heading: St Bede’s in trouble, govt denies any bias - Indian Express
Content:
The Himachal Pradesh State Electricity Board (HPSEB) has invited fresh bids from leading companies manufacturing 0.85 power factor (PF) compact fluorescent bulbs under the Atal Bijli Bachat Yojana.

HPSEB chairman R.K. Jain, confirming the move on CFL tenders, said the last date for submitting the tenders would be October 10 and thereafter the HPSEB will go ahead with distribution of the bulbs.

The scheme had run into trouble after the HPSEB had earlier accepted the bids of four companies who apparently had quoted higher prices. The orders were put on hold following a complaint send to Chief Minister Prem Kumar Dhumal by a competitor company, which claimed that it's prices were the lowest.

However, the government appointed a new chairman for HPSEB and asked the HPSEB to take a fresh decision on the CFL supply order. Last week, the HPSEB quashed the earlier

orders to pave the way for fresh purchases. Some of the officials associated with the decision on the CFL supply order were also replaced.

"We want complete transparency in scheme, which should become a model for the entire country," Dhumal asserts.

When contacted, the officials of M/s HPL-Socomec, which had sent the complaint against the earlier supply order, said they will not participate in the tenders this time.

Heading: Cop beaten up in public for ‘demanding money’ from trader - Indian Express
Content:
At a time when new private institutions of higher education are preparing to set up campuses in Himachal Pradesh, Shimla's St Bede's , a leading college of north India, seems to have run into serious trouble.

The fund crunch faced by the college is directly attributed to the state government's decision to reduce the grant-in-aid from 95 per cent to 50 per cent, a notification for which was issued in March. Since then, the college authorities have been trying to seek restoration of the funding, but in vain.

College principal Sister Molly Abraham says, "The crisis, which is a result of shortage of funds mainly due to the state government's decision to cut down grant-in-aid, has made it tough to run the institution effectively. We will be compelled to close down if grants are not restored."

But the government has expressed its inability to bail out one college and leave other aided education institutions, approximately a dozen, in the lurch. "We have framed a new policy to give grant-in-aid to all aided colleges equally.

All are equally affected by the decision," asserts P.C. Dhiman, Principal Secretary (Education).

Dhiman doesn't deny that St Bede's stands out amongst all privately-run colleges and says that's why the government has not deprived the college of its due share in the grant-in-aid. "After all, everyone also knows about the state's fiscal health and mounting debt liabilities. We want the private colleges to become self-reliant and share the government's burden," he says.

The congregation of Jesus and Mary institutions, to which St Bede's College is affiliated, has also been briefed about the situation. The college, Sister Molly asserts, cannot charge high fees from girl students due to the free education policy for girls. The college has already implemented the UGC scales for the staff.

Heading: A day for the girl child, but where is she? - Indian Express
Content:
A constable was beaten up in the main market of Nahan town by traders when he slapped a fruit seller who allegedly refused to pay money to the cop. The constable, Jagat Ram, was allegedly inebriated and not in uniform when the incident took place. When other traders saw Jagat Ram beating fruit seller Irshad and calling him a "terrorist", they gathered in support of Irshad and beat up the constable. Later, they reported the matter to the police.

When contacted, Additional Superintendent of Police Bindu Rani Sachdeva said Jagat Ram was on leave and had been shifted to the Police Lines. She denied that the cop was inebriated and said on medical examination the constable was not found under the influence of liquor. She said it was unfortunate that the other traders attacked the cop when they could have reported the matter to the police.

She said trouble arose when Irshad demanded a higher price for fruit and said there was no complaint of demanding money from traders. She assured to look into the incident.

Heading: Airport’s brand new runway takes off today - Indian Express
Content:
While the Delhi government came out with advertisements in newspapers on the Girl Child Day on Wednesday, requesting people to stop female foeticide, records with the Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD) say child sex ratio in the Capital is getting more skewed by the day.

According to the number of birth certificates issued by the office of the Chief Registrar, Births and Deaths, in 2006, only 831 girls were born against every 1,000 male births in Delhi. In 2001, the sex ratio in Delhi stood at 868. A healthy ratio, according to the World Health Organisation, is 952 girls per 1,000 boys.

"The figures are based on the deliveries that took place in Delhi in these years. The number excludes that of children born outside hospitals," said Dr V K Monga, chairman of the health committee of the MCD.

In 2001, the Capital ranked third among the states with the lowest sex ratio, after Punjab and Haryana. The figures have dipped further over the last eight years, with all nine districts showing a downward trend.

In east Delhi's Preet Vihar, the sex ratio is 750 girls for 1,000 boys — a figure worse than that of Punjab and Haryana in 2001. Punjabi Bagh comes next with a ratio of 820: 1,000. At 850 girls per 1,000 boys, the situation is a little better in Defence Colony and Patel Nagar.

The MCD figures only confirm the findings of a survey of leading hospitals conducted by the Christian Medical Association (CMA) of India last year. "If the first child is a girl, 50 per cent families abort the second foetus if it is a girl again. The sex ratio in such cases is even worse. Our study revealed that only 219 girls were born as a second female child for every 1,000 boys," said Dr Joe Verghese of the CMA.

"We require changes in the existing policies to complement the Pre-Natal Diagnostic Techniques Act. Less school fees and medical care expenses will put the girl child on a better platform," said Dr Indrani Ganguli, member of the Federation of Obstetric and Gynaecological Societies of India.

The reasons for the downward trend may differ from case to case — higher infant mortality rate or foeticide — but the disturbing trend speaks volumes about an urban society that is refusing to get over the age-old preference for the male child. "Our survey found the preference is often as pronounced, or more, in relatively well-off families too," said Dr Verghese.

Heading: Graziano official meets CEO’s kin, injured staff - Indian Express
Content:
The third runway of the Indira Gandhi International Airport, all off 4,430 metres and perhaps the longest in this part of the world, will be operational from 6 am on Thursday.

This decision was taken at a meeting of the Civil Aviation ministry on Wednesday, chaired by Joint Secretary K N Srivastava. The officers also said all arrivals for now would be handled by the existing main runway (28-10) but planes will take off — as many possible — from the new one (29-11). The ministry has also asked all airlines to send a copy of their winter schedule to the Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) for approval.

The Delhi International Airport Limited (DIAL) — the company taking care of the airport's renovation — has been asked to take adequate measures to prevent bird-hits. However, there is one slight hiccup: the planes taking off will spend an extra 15 minutes as taxi time because the runway is a little far from the terminal buildings.

The runway was constructed in 18 months, six months ahead of schedule and tested on August 21 in the presence of Civil Aviation Minister Praful Patel. It is expected to increase the capacity of flights per hour to nearly 70 from the present 40, a ministry spokesperson said. The Capital's airspace is also expected to be clear of too many hovering planes, waiting for a chance to land.

DIAL sources said the load on this runway will be gradually increased, and it is expected to run on full capacity by December. At Wednesday's meeting, DIAL was asked to ensure that the Category-IIIB Instrument Landing System be commissioned by November — well ahead of the fog season. The ministry spokesperson said the Airports Authority of India will also have to put in place the Surface Movement Radar facilities in the next two months.

Heading: Delhi Police to recommend Sharma for President’s Medal - Indian Express
Content:
Graziano Transmissioni, the Italian auto-parts manufacturer whose India head L K Choudhary was lynched by dismissed workers on Monday, is "yet to decide" on the future course of action in the country.

Marcello Lamberto, segment chief executive officer of the company who reached Delhi on Wednesday, said: "My priority is to see the injured get proper medical care and all help is extended to the grieving family of Choudhary."

Lamberto met the family members of Choudhary at their residence and expressed condolences. He also visited the Kailash Hospital and met the injured officials of the company. As many as 34 employees had sustained injuries in Monday's attack.

Later, Lamberto held a meeting of the officials amid heavy security at the factory in Greater Noida.

Factory manager L K Gupta said: "It was an internal meeting. The factory has been restarted for a check. Further decisions will be taken on Monday."

Choudhary was allegedly beaten to death at the company's plant in Greater Noida by a group of dismissed employees after a meeting called to resolve the dispute between them and the management had failed.

Heading: BJP demands dismissal of Jamia V-C - Indian Express
Content:
Delhi Police Commissioner Y S Dadwal has decided to recommend slain inspector Mohan Chand Sharma's name for President's Police Medal posthumously. The decision comes on Sharma's 43rd birthday on Wednesday.

"He was one of the best officers who could track terrorists and find out their exact location through technical analysis. His name will be recommended for the medal and he deserves it," said Alok Kumar, DCP (Special Cell). Sharma died in an encounter with suspected terrorists on September 19.

During his career spanning 19 years, Sharma was part of investigations in all major terror-related cases — like the Red Fort attack, the Parliament attack and the 2005 Diwali blasts. He was considered the "lifeline of the Special Cell".

"He deserves this medal, but this would have been of more importance if he were alive," said one of his colleagues who did not want to be named. The Delhi Police has decided to announce a cash reward for Sharma's family, but the amount has not been decided yet.

The President Police Medal, if approved, will be presented to his family on Republic Day, said a senior officer. Sharma had earlier won two President Police Medals in 2003 and 2007. He also won four Police Medals for gallantry in 2001, 2002, 2004 and 2005. In all, he received around 150 awards, including recommendations and appreciation from different agencies other than the Delhi Police.

On his 43th birthday, Sharma's colleagues and senior officers, including Joint CP Karnal Singh, DCP Alok Kumar, ACPs Sanjeev Yadav, L N Rao and Ravi Shankar, and other officers of the Special Cell remembered him at a gathering on Wednesday evening.

Job for slain cop's wife
The Delhi Police has decided to offer a job on compassionate grounds to slain inspector Mohan Chand Sharma's wife. Sharma's family, comprising his wife and two school-going children, will be given several other special privileges such as liberalised pensionary award, equal to the last pay drawn by the late Inspector, an ex gratia payment of Rs 15 lakh, death-cum-retirement gratuity equal to a year's salary, leave encashment equal to 10 months' salary, Central government employee insurance and benefits under the Delhi Police Welfare Scheme. Sharma will also be entitled to the Rs 3-lakh grant under the Government of India's scheme for terror victims.

Heading: IM banned on Orkut - Indian Express
Content:
The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) demanded the dismissal of Jamia Millia Islamia Vice-Chancellor Mushirul Hasan for announcing legal aid for two students — Mohammad Shakil and Zia-ur-Rehman — who have been arrested for their alleged involvement in the Delhi blasts.

BJP spokesperson Ravi Shankar Prasad said the police were arresting people suspected of waging or aiding "a war against the nation". The V-C, therefore, count not use taxpayers' money for providing assistance to a suspect, he said.

The party spokesperson said it was not the job of an educational institution established by the government to deal with the issue.

BJP Deputy Leader in the Lok Sabha Vijay Kumar Malhotra, who is also the Member of Parliament from the Jamia area, said the position taken by the V-C was "condemnable".

"It is atrocious and anti-national," he said.

Heading: Post encounter: Unsure, frightened Jamia Nagar asks students to leave - Indian Express
Content:
A community by the name of "Indian Mujahideen" (IM) was banned on Orkut, a social networking website, following the serial blasts on September 13. Anti-national remarks had allegedly been posted on the community web page, sources said. The community, which had hundreds of members, allegedly called the recent blasts a lesson for "anti-Islamic" people.

A spokesperson from Google that runs the website said: "Google strongly condemns illegal activities and those encouraging terrorism and violence." Sources said as news about the involvement of Indian Mujahideen spread, the number of visitors to the web page witnessed an increase.

There are two Orkut communities on the Indian Mujahideen — the "Indian Mujahideen Fan club" and "Indian Mujahideen". Both have been blocked. Even as one cannot access the first community at all, as per the profile of Indian Mujahideen, it was formed on July 31, 2008 by a user listed as 'Ummar (Azaad Kashmir) Jihaad', based in Bandipura in Jammu and Kashmir. His profile page is not accessible. The web page carries the message: "Please support Indian Mujahideen. They are fighting for the justice and the enemies of Islam".

Heading: Khan do - Indian Express
Content:
Jamia Nagar's strong student community, mostly those from out of town, are today pleading with their suspicious landlords to allow them to stay on. Most have been asked to vacate, while several have moved out till things cool down.

This area with its affordable rates and its proximity to the Jamia Millia Islamia University has put a roof over students for long. But the recent encounter, backed by raids and a heavy police presence, has shaken the confidence of landlords.

Kolkata's Saugata Chowdhury, who lives in Shaheen Bagh near Jamia, was asked to leave a day after the two suspected terrorists were shot dead. "The landlady was scared the police might question her," he told Newsline. Chowdhury however refused to vacate but moved in with his relatives in Bhajanpura. "I was frightened too and preferred to commute to Jamia from here," he added.

Ali, Farhan and Sahil have shared a flat in Shaheen Bagh for over a year. Their landlord has now asked for fresh details of their identity and has even put a curfew on their movements — you cannot go out after 10 pm. Ali said: "People become suspicious when they hear there are three of us in one flat. Nobody wants to be harassed by the police."

Sahil added: "It is unfair to brand us all just because those boys have been accused of being terrorists. So many of our friends have been asked to leave. Many parents are also taking their children home."

A lecturer of the Jamia said: "In campus, we are on equal footing on terror — whether a student is a Hindu or a Muslim. But students are edgy these days. They are scared to call up friends, they don't talk about the encounter."

On the other hand, life goes on in hushed whispers in Batla House. Namazis gather for the daily prayers at the Khalilullah Mosque. They don't share pleasantries much but talk about what is going on. A heavy force of khaki continues to guard the area.

The lane to house L-18 is still cordoned off, the sixth day now, and many are turned away from the top of the bylane. Tea-stall owners, cyber cafe employees and even those at nearby dhabas refuse to recognise Atif and his friends. "These boys had moved in only a few months ago. We hardly ever interacted," said Iqbal, owner of the locality's provisions store.

Another resident Imran said: "The guards of that building were picked up for interrogation and anyone who claims to have known the boys are being randomly questioned." He added: "Atif and his friends looked like regular students. They had hired a maid, they ate at nearby dhabas and also studied hard."

Residents are also upset with the elected representatives, many of whom have not turned up after the encounter. "We are very frightened. There is police everywhere, but nobody has bothered to speak a word of assurance," said Mohsin Akhtar.

But the Imam of Khalilullah, Mohammad Yakub, is optimistic. "Even in these tough times, there hasn't been a drop in attendance for namaz," he said.

(All names changed on request)

Heading: On Track - Indian Express
Content:
The Khan-daan turned up in full strength for the music launch of Atul Agnihotri's latest movie Hello, at Enigma in the JW Marriott, Juhu, on September 23. Patriarch and father-in-law Salim Khan turned up with his wives Salma and Helen. Also present were Arbaaz Khan (in Barbie pink), Atul's wife Alvira and their daughter Alizeh, and Arpita Khan. Also present were Hello's female leads, Amrita Arora, in a scarlet dress and Gul Panag, in bright red lipstick. Author Chetan Bhagat, on whose book One Night @ a Call Centre, the movie is based, also showed up for the bash with his wife Anusha.

Bummer Salman Khan and It-girl Katrina Kaif did not turn up for the family affair.

Heading: Centurion - Indian Express
Content:
With several independent bands composing for films, Bollywood tunes are set to change

Randolph Correia, of the relatively small electronica duo band Shaai'r n Func, has for the first time composed a full soundtrack, for the movie, Saas Bahu aur Sensex. The movie may have been a dud but Correia feels that it's a headstart for him, since it's his first serious exposure to Bollywood, and towards making mainstream popular music. Though music from the Indian film industry has always been catchy, the predictability of the tracks is about to change, with bands that have focused on creating original sound coming in. "A lot of music from Bollywood sounds exactly the same," says Correia, whose tracks for Saas Bahu.. has a lot of progressive electronic sounds instead of dance and bhangra beats.

Kailasa is another group that has created a separate Bollywood identity for themselves and like to call them the Kailash-Paresh-Naresh trio. Departing from their conventional Sufi sound, the trio is ready to bring in unplugged and acoustic beats with their composition for Sushant Shah's Dus Vidhaniya starring Vinay Pathak and Neha Dhupia.

"The music that we have done for the film is new for us as well," says Paresh Kamath, guitarist of Kailasa, who have recorded their music live. "There's a certain human element that lengthens the songs shelf life when it's live," adds Kamath. The trio has also composed two tracks for the forthcoming Chandni Chowk to China that even includes a quwwali with a twist.

But not all consider Bollywood a progression, though all musicians acknowledge it the fastest way to get noticed and top the charts. "I'm not progressing to Bollywood. In fact it is a step down for me as a musician since it cannot provide any inspiration. But it is a decent money-making proposition," says Correia, who has also produced a track for Drona. Agrees Rahul Ram, bassist, Indian Ocean who says, "Bollywood is not our final bastion. The filmmakers are coming to us for our sound." The band has composed the soundtrack for the recently released Hulla and a film titled Bhoomi is in the pipeline. "The soundtrack for Hulla basically has one main song and three versions of it apart from the background score. But the sound for our films, be it in the past or the future, will continue being the sound that is Indian Ocean," says Ram.

Most of these bands are continuing with their independent work that only benefits from their exposure to Bollywood. "It aligns your creative thought process with what people want to hear which can be a challenge," admits Ram. "Working on a script written by someone else makes us think differently which may not have been possible otherwise," says Kamath.

While Correia is busy with his albums for his groups Shaai'r n Func and Pentagram to take the band to next level, Kailash-Paresh-Naresh turn back to Kailasa to record their third album. And Indian Ocean, which has just released their DVD, Indian Ocean Live in Delhi, is still hoping their fans will go and pick a copy

Heading: Red Fort home of the tricolour - Indian Express
Content:
City theatre expert Ashish Ghosh is celebrating, and it isn't just because his favorite festival, Durga Puja, is round the corner. "My show Agomoni turns 100 in October," he says.Comprising songs drawn from the saints of the 17th-20th century, strung together to tell the story of Goddess Durga, Agomoni was first performed at India Habitat Centre in 1998 — the same venue where the 100th show will be staged.

"It started as a 40-minute show and has doubled in the last 10 years, as bits of other songs and narratives were added," says Ghosh, a former professor of political science at Dayal Singh College in Delhi. Ghosh's solo performance follows in the traditions of the troubadours of Murshidabad and incorporates dance, dialogues and theatre. The show has traveled across West Bengal, Mumbai, Varanasi, Jaipur, Allahabad and Toronto. May the run continue.

Heading: RAIL TRAIL - Indian Express
Content:
Students of Jain Bharati Mrigavati Vidyalaya, Alipur, take part in the heritage walk at Red Fort conducted by The Indian Express in association with INTACH and ASI

A schools' initiative from The Express Group
Quest is a project conducted by The Indian Express in schools in and around Delhi. It covers more than 50 schools in Delhi and NCR.

Quest aims at stirring awareness and opinions. Today, when all that children see are shopping malls and cineplexes, we at The Indian Express want to show a completely different picture of this city to them. Delhi has changed beyond nostalgia and recognition since Independence. How many of these kids know of the 'Seven Cities' of Delhi or the stories of the pigeon fliers of Old Delhi?

The idea behind such an activity is to create awareness about the various structures and monuments that the students do not know about. This is a specially designed programme, which will help the students appreciate the rich culture and background of this city. In association with INTACH and ASI, this is a small effort on our behalf to depict a phase of our national life and the decay of a whole culture, a particular mode of thought and living. The visit is followed by the students sending in articles, pictures, poems, paintings, and collages to express their experiences about the heritage walk.

We invite schools to be a part of this Express Group initiative.

The need to conserve our heritage
Heritage walks help us youngsters understand the great history of India's freedom struggle. They broaden our outlook and add to our knowledge. For the public, a historical monument may simply mean stones ,bricks and cement; but for a student, it is of great educational importance.

I, along with other students of Jain Bharati Mrigavati Vidyalaya, went for a heritage walk to the Red Fort organised by The Indian Express. The Red Fort is of great importance for the nation and is an indispensable part of Indian History.

The fort is made of red sandstone and was built by Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan. Further additions were done by other emperors and the British. Just near the entrance, is a bazaar and after that comes the Naubat or Nakkar Khana. The Nakkar Khana got its name from the musical instrument Nagada. In those days, musicians used to play music on the arrival of VIPs, so that the emperor would be informed. In front of the Nakkar Khana, there is a circular garden with colourful and beautiful flowers. Then there is a building made of red sandstone, built by Bahadur Shah Zafar. We also saw the Diwan-e-Aam and the Diwan-e-Khas, which are the most important structures at the Red Fort. The Diwan-e-Aam was meant for the emperor's audiences with the public. It houses the famous "Peacock Throne" that is beautifully carved and once had inlay work of precious stones. There is the Rang Mahal, meant for entertainment. The Red Fort also has a museum where one can see statues of great persons, guns and weapons used in the 1857 Uprising, as well as pictures and photographs from that period. The Senani Smarak, where the INA trial took place, is also in the same campus. One can also find a collection of writings, clothes and photographs, etc related to Netaji Subash Chandra Bose and his famous trial here.

The need of the hour is to conserve our heritage. Many people continue to litter the surroundings of such monuments and write their names on walls, contributing to their dilapidated condition. As students, we should create awareness about these things because our heritage is indispensable. As Indians, it is our moral duty to protect them because our heritage is our pride.
— SUSHIL KUMAR GOEL, X C

Informative walk
I went for a heritage walk organised by The Indian Express to the Red Fort on September 19. We were divided into three groups and were led by talented and experienced guides from INTACH. They took us to each and every part of the Red Fort. We were shown around the Diwan-e-Aam and the Diwan-e-Khas, where the nobles meet and discussed issues of governance. We were also shown around the Rang Mahal; Khas Mahal; the Moti Masjid built by Aurangzeb; the hammams; and the Savan, Bhado, Shah Bhuj and Chatta bazaars. We were also told about the architecture of the Red Fort. At the museum, we saw photographs related to the 1857 Uprising. The whole excursion brought us close to the history of the Red Fort. We enjoyed the excursion and would like to thank The Indian Express and INTACH for such an informative heritage walk.
— AKSHI SHARMA, X A

A fabulous fort
I went for a heritage walk to the Red Fort, organised by The Indian Express, on September 19, 2008. It was a very interesting and knowledgeable experience. Generally, people just go to see the fort without knowing much about it. But we were accompanied by guides, who provided us with very interesting facts and information. The Diwan-e-Aam is fabulous and beautifully designed. We also saw the Diwan-e-Khas, where the noblemen met. It was once covered in gold and silver but now only the stone remains. As in other Muslim monuments, there is a fountain between four gardens, which looked exactly like heaven on earth. After that we went to the museum, where weapons, dresses and models of the 1857 Uprising are kept. We were all really amazed by the interesting facts about the Red Fort. The heritage walk was indeed great fun.
— SURBHI SHARMA, X C

World heritage site
A heritage walk was organised by The Indian Express on September 19, for the students of Jain Bharati Mrigavati Vidyalaya to the Red Fort, a World Heritage site. The guides from Intach provided very interesting information about the historic fort, unveiled many facts unknown to us previously. The Red Fort museum was full of inspirational photographs and models of the 1857 Uprising, which inspired us to be more patriotic. The rich heritage of India can be seen in the architecture and sculptures used there. Overall, it was a complete expedition, bringing us closer to our heritage.
— ADITYA RATHI, X A

For queries mail to heritagewalks@expressindia.com

Heading: Now, bus accident victims entitled to interim relief - Indian Express
Content:
Stephie D'Souza, the 'Flying Ranee'
Long before the days of P T Usha, Indian sport had a "Flying Ranee", Stephie D'Souza, a member of the Indian Railways and India's top woman athlete in the late 50s and early 60s. At her peak, Stephie had to her credit national records in 100m, 200m, 400m and 800m events. She was the only Indian woman to be selected for athletics at the 1964 Olympics at Tokyo. Earlier, at the Asian Games in Tokyo in 1958, she had won a silver medal.

Not just athletics, Stephie was a double international and captained the Indian women's hockey team that toured Japan and England. After her sporting days, she was a member of the All India Council of Sports.

Stephie's marriage kept her in the athletics and Railway fraternity, as she married none other than Edward Sequeira, who also started his career like Stephie with the Central Railway. Edward stood tall as a middle distance runner. Among his many achievements was a 5th position in the 5,000 metres at the 1972 Munich Olympics.
—J L Singh, retired railway official

Darjeeling and the B Class
Perched about 7,000 ft above sea level and surrounded by the Himalayas, Darjeeling is one of the most popular hill stations in Eastern India. Best known for its tea, it is also known for its Railway or "Toy Train", as its popularly referred to.

Construction of the Railway commenced in 1879, under the aegis of Franklin Prestage, with the sole intention of bringing down travel time between the plains and the hills.

Given the challenges of the Himalayan terrain, the line was built in record time and utilised mountain railway engineering techniques — spiral loops and reversing stations — considered way advanced for its time and type.

The line was opened in 1881 as the "Darjeeling Himalayan Railway Company". The opening of the Railway boosted communication, provided employment and led to the social and economic development of Darjeeling and its surrounding areas.

Today, a road runs parallel to the Railway line and provides a faster way of getting there. But there is no better way to get up to Darjeeling than by taking the train. A ride on the Toy Train is a quintessential part of the whole Darjeeling experience.

A lot has obviously changed since the Railway began operations 127 years ago. One thing, however, has more or less remained unchanged, the charming old "B" Class steam locomotives, some over a century old, which continue to chug up and down the line, day after day.

The "B" Class is a small two-axle saddle tank locomotive, which carries its water tanks on its boiler. Built originally by the English firm Sharpe & Stewart and the Scottish firm North British Locomotive Co, these locos weigh 14 tons and have a 0-4-0 wheel arrangement, with a diameter measuring just 2 feet.

The oldest "B" Class in service today was built in 1889 and the latest one was put on line in 1928. There are 14 "B" Class locomotives in working order today. A lot of them have been preserved as well. One such, No.777, can be seen at the National Rail Museum in New Delhi.
— Bharat Vohra, Rail Enthusiast

Did you know?
* Radio communication between driver and guard was first introduced on the Delhi-Mugalsarai route.
* The first Jan Shatabdi in 2002 ran between Mumbai and Madgaon.
* The first petrol-driven loco manufactured by Kerr Stuart was used in 1905 on the Morvi Railway.
* The first train to be hauled by an electric locomotive from Delhi Junction was the Assam Mail.
* Mobile post office service in trains was first introduced in 1870 by the East India Railway.
* The first railway budget was presented in 1925.
* The first Sampark Kranti Express, flagged on February 8, 2004, runs between Hazrat Nizamuddin and Yashwantpur.
— Vikas Singh, rail enthusiast

Heading: Trains diverted, cancelled as Yamuna crosses danger mark, experts say nothing to worry - Indian Express
Content:
Will contest 'illegal' order in Supreme Court, say bus owners

From today, the Delhi Transport Corporation (DTC) and Blueline bus owners will have to pay "immediate" compensation to victims, and their families, involved in accidents with their vehicles.

They will have to pay Rs 1 lakh in case of a fatal accident and Rs 50,000 if the victim(s) has grievous injuries or permanent or partial disability. The payment will act as a pre-condition for the release of impounded buses. This is the thrust of an interim scheme called the "Scheme for Victims of Accidents Caused By Stage Carriages (DTC and Blueline Buses)", formulated on Wednesday by a Bench led by Chief Justice A P Shah and Justice S Muralidhar.

The court has also directed the Centre to form a high-level panel at the Joint Secretary level to "explore the possibility of devising a similar scheme" and report back within three months. The court has posted the matter for further hearing on November 5.

"DTC and Blueline buses are involved in a large number of accidents. In case of a fatal accident, surviving members of the family have to deal with a lifetime of psychological trauma. Others spend the rest of their lives in wheelchairs," the Bench said.

As per the scheme, the police will send copies of the FIR filed to the local metropolitan magistrate and the Delhi Legal Services Authority. The bus owners shall apply to the metropolitan magistrate for release of their bus and deposit the compensation amount.

The metropolitan magistrate will notify the next of kin or the victim. The victims or their family will also have to give a written undertaking to file a motor accidents claim case in the Special Tribunal for a final decree on the compensation amount.

"This amount is only for immediate help. Final compensation will be given through the insurance claim on the vehicle as ordered by the Tribunal," amicus curae Kailash Vasdev said.

The amount given, as interim compensation will be adjusted against the final amount. "The interim compensation given by the bus owner will be reimbursed by the insurance company after the Tribunal gives its final orders," the court said.

The court foresees a role for the Delhi Police. "The police will immediately notify the Delhi Legal Services Authority, which will provide free legal aid to victims from weaker economic backgrounds seeking compensation," the amicus curae said. The Bench also ruled "all hospitals nearest to the spot of the accident, private or public, will provide immediate medical aid".

Reacting to the court's decision, H S Kalra, president of the Federation of Blueline Bus Owners, said: "The order is patently illegal. We were not given an opportunity to be heard. Nobody wants to be involved in an accident. Improve the infrastructure and there will be no more accidents."

"We will appeal in the Supreme Court," Shyamlal Gola, Dilli Bus Ekta Manch spokesperson, said.

Heading: Greater Noida industrialists: ‘accidents’ like Monday not new - Indian Express
Content:
Even as the Delhi government takes all precautionary measures to deal with the rising water level of the Yamuna, the river reached 205.88 metres (as recorded at the Old Delhi Railway Bridge) on Monday. Following this, almost 140 scheduled trains crossing the Old Yamuna Bridge had to be either cancelled or diverted.

Officials at the Northern Railways, however, confirmed that after the river levels fell to 205.76 metres in the afternoon, regular services were resumed. "This is a precautionary measure undertaken when the river water levels rise beyond a certain danger mark. Therefore, from 3 am on Wednesday morning, we had to cancel or divert quite a few trains. Since 2 this afternoon, however, the water level has fallen and services have been restored," said A S Negi, Public Relations Officer, Northern Railways.

Once the water level crosses 205.44 metres in the Yamuna, it is supposed to be a high flood situation. "But there is no possibility of a flood and the situation is under control," confirmed MCT Pareva, Chief Engineer, Irrigation and Flood Control Department.

"There is no fear of Delhi being affected by a temporary increase in the water level of the river," said a senior official of the Irrigation and Flood Control Department.

Officials maintain that the increasing water levels will be confined to the Yamuna riverbed, and the overall situation is under control, while the administration is well-equipped to deal with any emergency. S S Ghonkrokta, Divisional Commissioner (East) informed that the water is now receding as Delhi is in turn releasing water from the Wazirabad, ITO and Okhla barrages.

"Increase in the water level means that the riverbed will remain submerged in water. There has otherwise been no loss. Floodplain land is in any case, given out on a lease of eight months for cultivation. In these four months, the land is supposed to be submerged due to rising water levels, and hence, no cultivation is possible. People have also been living on the banks as the water levels have not risen in the past few years," Ghonkrokta said.

Meanwhile, the increase in water levels is likely to hit the supply of potable water in Delhi, as excessive quantities of floating material in the river at Wazirabad is choking the raw water bar screens at the Wazirabad and Chandrawal water treatment plants.

"Large quantities of floating material, including wild grass, shrubs and other aquatic plants is causing frequent choking of the system, which has affected potable water treatment at the Wazirabad and Chandrawal WTPs," Delhi Jal Board spokesperson Sanjam Chima said. "Water supply is likely to be affected in the command areas of these plants and the situation is likely to continue for the next two days," she added.

Heading: Proposal floated for second AIIMS campus in NCR - Indian Express
Content:
'Industry may flee district if situation unchanged'

Two days after L K Choudhary was killed by employees at Italian firm Graziano International, the mood among industrialists in the city is one of apprehension. "Accidents" like that on Monday are not new to the industrial hub, they say.

Vinod Kumar Vajpayee, president of the Noida Phase-II Industries Association, said: "There are many other companies that have seen violence over the last few years." Workers of Jaypee Greens in Greater Noida attacked the company's office in 2004 and killed one person. Similarly, employees at Daewoo attacked the office of the company after it went bankrupt. Some 125 workers and 10 policemen were injured in the clashes.

"Large-scale rioting like that on Monday (when Choudhary was killed and 34 others were injured) is a troubling phenomenon," Vajpayee said.

Hindon Rubber, another company that was based in Noida, wound up operations after similar protests by employees earlier this year.

Most clashes in the past, industrialists say, have been because of expelled or suspended employees. Graziano had expelled 192 of its regular employees on July 1 and opted for contracted workers, a practice opposed by the Mazdoor Sangh leaders.

Virender Singh Sirohi, secretary of the Uttar Pradesh unit of Hind Mazdoor Sabha, said: "We had taken the issue of workers to the president and all concerned authorities; the rioting is condemnable but there are issues that need to be addressed."

Sirohi alleges officials at Graziano had agreed to their demands in an earlier meeting and later refused to implement the steps promised. "The frustration had been building up," he said.

Industrialists, however, allege gangs that operate among the labourers are involved. Sahdev Sharma, chairman of the Greater Noida Industries Association, said: "We have reported about the involvement of bad elements and a few workers in the past; meetings between employees and owners have also been arranged."

Sharma alleges the police and administration have been neglecting the situation in the area. "Assurances have been given and some action taken but this incident goes to show that all is not well."

Sharma and members of other associations held a meeting with District Magistrate Shravan Kumar and SSP R K Chaturvedi on Wednesday to discuss security arrangements in the industrial area. After the meeting, Sharma said: "We do not want Gautam Budh Nagar to lose its image as an industrial hub; stern steps will need to be taken in this regard.

Till then, he says, some people might choose to keep away from Noida and Greater Noida and some might wind up their businesses as well.

Heading: Accused of attempted rape, cop held - Indian Express
Content:
The All India Institute of Medical Sciences may soon be replicated in the NCR. The institute has proposed to open a second AIIMS campus either in Noida or Haryana.

A proposal to this effect has been approved by the governing body of the institute headed by Health Minister Ambumani Ramadoss.

"We are facing infrastructure constraints for our expansion plans as our existing 166-acre campus cannot provide enough space for increasing the demands of the institution. As of now we have approached the NOIDA authority. We may approach Gurgaon as well," Shailesh Yadav, Deputy Director (Administration) said.

The institute has also demanded 300 acres of land in its proposal either in Noida or the NCR in Haryana, keeping in view easy accessibility from the main campus. "We have been offered 100 acres of land in Noida, but that will not cater to our needs," he added.

The new campus is expected to house research-related facilities, apart from regular OPDs. "The government has assured monetary assistance to set up the new campus," Yadav said.

Heading: Labour unions side with arrested workers - Indian Express
Content:
A 40-year-old Delhi Police Head Constable allegedly attempted to rape a 9-year-old minor in an inebriated condition in Nangloi area of West district. The police have, however, denied the allegations and claimed that the policeman has been booked for kidnapping.

Sources said the police received a call that Head Constable Sukhbir had allegedly attempted to rape a girl.

"We got the call that Sukhbir had tried to lure a minor in the area. He was, however, spotted by the local people and caught," a senior police officer said.

"The girl had not gone to school today and was playing outside her house when Sukhbir tried to lure her," a local said. The police added that locals saw him trying to lure the victim and confronted him. When they saw that he was drunk, they beat him up before handing him over to the police. "Sukhbir was in an inebriated state at the time of the incident, which has been confirmed from the medical examination that was conducted after the incident," the senior police officer added.

The Deputy Commissioner of Police (West district), Sharad Aggarwal said, "It was not a case of attempt to rape. We have registered a case of kidnapping under Section 363 of the Indian Penal Code at the Paschim Vihar police station."

Sukhbir was posted as head constable at the Nihal Vihar police post in Paschim Vihar area. "Sukhbir was not on duty when the incident took place," the senior police officer added.

The victim is a student of Class IV in a nearby MCD primary school.

Girl raped
GURGAON: A 22-year-old girl was allegedly raped at Gurgaon on Wednesday. The girl, a resident of Lakshmi Nagar, had met Vikram, the accused, who promised to employ her. He took her to a flat in Palam Vihar and raped her. A case has been lodged at the Palam Vihar police station.

Heading: New police district, separate police station at Barakhamba in the offing - Indian Express
Content:
Employees arrested for allegedly murdering the MD of Graziano Transmissioni have the support of the city labour unions. Virender Singh Sirohi, the regional head of Hind Mazdoor Sabha, on Wednesday said the employees have been treated badly.

"The charges against the employees cannot be accepted; not everyone was involved in rioting," he said.

Sirohi claims the employees had earlier held meetings with the company's top brass and also approached the Labour ministry. "Assurances had been given by the company authorities but no action was taken," he said.

Sirohi also alleged that many industries in Greater Noida have been violating labour laws.

"Companies have been taking in people on contractual basis and throwing out other employees in hordes," he alleged.

Graziano had sacked 192 employees on July 1 and hired workers on a contract basis. Sirohi said the Mazdoor Sabha would approach the Prime Minister and explain the situation to him.

Heading: This time, it’s tears of joy - Indian Express
Content:
With the Delhi Police sending in the final proposal for the much needed eleventh police district in Delhi, the workload of the existing police stations in the capital is all set to be distributed and eased.

While it is a known fact that there is just one police officer for approximately every 300 citizens in Delhi, police stations, mostly understaffed, are also faced with tackling the registration of a huge number of FIRs and case redressals.

The proposed new district, Southeast, will be split from the present South district, which has largest number of police stations (19). Around 12,000 FIRs are registered in this district alone every year, several times higher when compared to other districts.

Apart from demarcating a new district, modification have also been made in districts where certain police stations have longer jurisdiction.

"The step of defining areas for police stations will help in balancing police strength and complaints. Certain police stations receive a large number of complaints, while some do not receive too many, like the Dilshad Garden police station in the Northeast district, which receives only around 120 cases every year. We will thus make it a police post and Harsh Vihar will be made a police station," said Y S Dadwal, Delhi Police Commissioner.

Sources have also revealed that Barakhamba Road might get to see a new police station very soon. It is on the cards to ease the work of six police stations in New Delhi districts. Senior officers said the proposal for these modifications and the new district has been sent to the Delhi government this week and the new district is expected to become functional within the next few months.

The new district will have 15 police stations — Kalkaji, Greater Kailash, CR Park, New Friends Colony, Badarpur, Jamia Nagar, Okhla, Hazrat Nizamuddin, Sarita Vihar, Lajpat Nagar, Amar Colony, Govind Puri, Ambedkar Nagar, Sangam Vihar and Jaitpur. The DCP office for the Southeast district will be at the Sarita Vihar police station. Jaitpur and Govindpuri will be two new police stations. The police stations beyond the BRT corridor will remain in the South district, but four important police stations, Vasant Vihar, Vasant Kunj, RK Puram and Sarojini Nagar from Southwest district will be included in South district, with the DCP's office at the Vasant Vihar police station. The Southwest district is already quite a large area; hence plans are on for three police stations to be taken out of it and the Dwarka police station to be made its headquarters.

Apart from these changes, two police stations of West district, Patel Nagar and Anand Parbat, would be included in the Central district. Officials said the department is also working on increasing the strength of the police personnel at the stations, as almost all police stations are understaffed. The South district police have already registered 6,000 cases this year till now, while the figures at other police stations are around 1,200 to 3,000 cases. Outer district was formed in September last year which eased Northwest district operations.

Delhi Police, which is the largest metropolitan police force in the world— larger than London, Paris, New York and Tokyo — has at present three ranges, 10 districts and 136 police stations. The number of police stations will go up to 140 and one more district will be added by end of this year.

Heading: An Indian hand in a foreign cause - Indian Express
Content:
Nagaland, last year's losing finalists, walk away with the Subroto Cup title after a stroll in the park

Mughato Sumi, the Nagaland U-14 coach looked the busiest man on earth at the prize distribution ceremony after his team emerged champions of the Subroto Cup's sub-junior category.

At the final whistle of his team's 2-0 win over Bangladesh's Krira Sikkha Protisthan, the tears returned, but unlike last year, he wiped them off and ran to his players. And for a moment, controlling the mad celebrations of the Greenwood School boys had him look helpless. Seconds later, the celebrations erupted further as Sumi was adjudged the best coach of the tournament.

"I left Ambedkar Stadium in tears a year ago, having missed the trophy by a whisker. But this year, the boys have done it," said Sumi.

He went on to say that it was a "dream come true," but his players didn't quite have the pleasure of playing a dream final. "The semi-final, against Army Boys Bangalore, was probably our toughest match. This final I would count among the easiest," Lunminlal, the central midfielder of the Nagaland team, said.

It did look easy, when his left footer left Bangladesh goalkeeper Mohammad Saiful Islam rooted as the ball swirled into the net in just the second minute. Apart from giving Nagaland an early lead, the strike also seemed to have inspired Nyuhenho, who followed suit seventeen minutes later, from a couple of yards right. Islam and the wall again stood surprised.

While Bangladesh coach Ujjal Chakroborty blamed the wrong positioning of the goalkeeper for both goals, Sumi said it was his plans that worked to perfection. "Lunminlal, Nyuhenho and Lusinei are our free-kick specialists. They practice extra just lobbing balls over the wall," said Sumi.

Better than ever
Chakroborty couldn't stop praising his opponents. "They were better than us in every department of the game — physically, tactically. Our boys looked listless, they ran short of energy. Anyway when we came we hadn't dreamt of winning, but we still managed to reach the final. These boys had joined the institution just a couple of months ago. Considering that, our performance was praiseworthy. And if am right, this was our best performance in the Subroto Cup too," said Chakroborty.

No matter how difficult he found his opponents on Tuesday, the coach said there's been a rapid improvement in the performance of teams from India. "We played Assam and Haryana in 2006, but this year most of the teams were better prepared, especially on the technical front," said Chakroborty.

Lunminlal: Hope for the future
Lunminlal is full of hope. He hopes he plays like Deco, he hopes he plays the pivotal role for his team, he hopes he will, one day, don the Indian colours, and he hopes he will be able to see the I-League this year on television as his part of the world doesn't yet have a cable connection.

But the thing he never fathomed, let alone hoped for, was the significance of his second-minute strike against Bangladesh in the U-14 final of the Subroto Cup. The goal, his only one in the tournament, went on to fetch him the Player of the Tournament award.

"Bijay Sugha was his closest contender for the prize, but today's goal gave him the edge. Its importance on the game showed, as the Bangladesh team got demoralised by the early strike. The effect was more psychological," said Kallol Kumar Chowdhury, one of the panellists for the awards. Former India vice-captain Ranjit Thapa, another member of the panel, agreed: "The goal was also important in the way it was scored. I couldn't have imagined somebody that age swirling the ball that big, so effectively. It was unbelievable."

The goal gave Lunminlal a clear edge over Sugha, but there were other things to his favour. "We haven't given him the points considering just today's performance. He's played at all positions as per his team's requirements. He played as a sweeper back to guard his defence in a couple of matches and today he took charge of the forward line, feeding them with balls from both sides. He is the backbone of the side and if you leave him out, the team will look very different," added Chowdhury.

With so many wishes, one thing Lunminlal failed to hope for was that his rewards multiply this year, qualitatively as well as quantitatively, after his Subroto Cup stipend last year got misplace.

Heading: The Globetrotting Harp - Indian Express
Content:
Ahead of India tour, Lincolnshire invite Abhay Sharma to help team learn how to play spin

That Indian cricket has a penchant for foreign coaches is well documented. What doesn't get an equal amount of column-centimetres is that it is also returning the favour, albeit on a smaller scale, at an individual level.

If Lincolnshire do well on their tour of India and Sri Lanka this winter, they may like to share the credit with one man: Abhay Sharma. The Railways coach was recently invited by the Minor County side to tip their players on how to play spin, especially in the sub-continental conditions.

"I went to Lincolnshire last month and was with the team for about a fortnight," Sharma told Sportline. "It was a fruitful association. You know, cricketers in England, generally, aren't good players of spin, so I tried to help them out in this department," he added.

But how did the county touch base with him? "I used to play county cricket. I played against Mark Fell, who is now the Lincs coach, many times. He followed my first season as coach and got in touch with me, and I agreed," Sharma elaborated.

Up to the task
Going by what Sharma has achieved in his yearlong coaching career, Lincs couldn't have got a better man for the task.

A Level II certified coach from the NCA and England and Wales Cricket Board, the 39-year-old revived Railways' fortunes in his very first year at the helm. Relegated to the Plate Group in the previous season, Sharma helped the team finish second and get promoted to the Elite Group. He wasn't done yet and capped his rookie season as coach by guiding the Central Zone to the title win in the Deodhar Trophy.

Augurs well for Lincolnshire, doesn't it? "It remains to be seen," said the former wicketkeeper-batsman. "I did my job. But you know, you can't learn how to play spin unless you play on turning tracks and against good spinners. Still, I told them to use their feet a little more. Sound footwork has to be there. Besides, I told them not to play with the spin against the off-spinners. Let's see how they perform when they come here. I'll also be helping them once they are here."

Enough tips for the county side, some advice for the domestic teams who will be up against Lincs? "Watch out for Karan Bansal, he's gonna trouble you a lot," Sharma signed off.

Heading: Atif showed Gujarat riot visuals to provoke youngsters: cops - Indian Express
Content: After Indian cricket captain Mahendra Singh Dhoni, it is now the turn of Bipasha Basu to turn designer for sportswear brand Reebok. Basu, who is also a brand ambassador of the label, has worked closely with in-house designers to develop a line of women's gym wear that will hit stores soon. The look of the collection, in keeping with the actor's image, is funky and energetic with a lot of classic colours like blues, pearl whites and blacks. That apart, Basu is also excited about her forthcoming regional film, Pankh by Bengali director Sudipto Chattopadhyay's Pankh, where she plays an alter-ego to a boy going through gender confusion. "It's a delightful role, quite different from anything I have done before in my career. The script was so convincing that I just could not give up the offer," she says.

Heading: SIMI financed July 26 attacks with funds collected for earthquake victims, say cops - Indian Express
Content:
9/13: 5 arrested 'terrorists' tell police Atif wanted to avenge violence against Muslims

Interrogation of the five men arrested in connection with the Delhi serial blasts has revealed that Atif Amin alias Basheer, the alleged Indian Mujahideen operative killed in the September 19 encounter, repeatedly showed them visuals of the 2002 Gujarat riots to provoke them against the system.

DCP (South) H G S Dhaliwal, who arrested three of the suspected terrorists on Sunday, confirmed this.

During the questioning, Mohammad Saif, Zeeshan, Shakil, Zia-ur-Rehman and Saqib Nisar reportedly told the police that Atif was seeking revenge against the violence against Muslims by Hindus in Gujarat, as had been mentioned in the 13-page email sent after the blasts. The students were also shown other material related to Mujahids and terrorism, police sources said.

Atif reportedly deleted most of the content and videos related to Gujarat violence from his laptop that was recovered by the police.

The five suspected terrorists arrested by the Special Cell and the South District police are being interrogated by the Madhya Pradesh, Karnataka, Hyderabad and Gujarat police, besides the Rajasthan Anti-Terrorist Squad and the UP Special Task Force, in coordination with the Delhi Police. During raids at the hideouts of the accused, the police claimed to have found incriminating evidence.

The Delhi Police now claims to have gathered substantial evidence against Indian Mujahideen terrorists, including mobile phone records, travel details and reservation slips. The Indian Mujahideen logo used in emails was stored in Atif's laptop, besides photographs of the members of his module and clips of the Ahmedabad blasts. The laptop also has photos of two stolen cars used in Ahmedabad, the police said. His mobile phone records showed Atif was in touch with Tauqeer, who is said to be the mastermind of the planned attacks and the one who sent mails after every blast — Bangalore, Ahmedabad, Jaipur and Delhi.

Clips of Delhi blast sites on Atif's mobile
Forensic experts managed to recover from Atif's Samsung mobile phone video clips of the sites where blasts were triggered on September 13, police claimed on Wednesday. Officers said terrorists had taken shots of the sites before placing the bombs.

Delhi hawala link identified
The Special Cell has identified a hawala operator from Delhi, Hakim, who delivered money for the terror operations. Hakim has not been arrested yet. "The money came through hawala and was delivered in Delhi," said a source. The money reportedly came from the West Asia. The police are scrutinising a few numbers that have been used to make calls to Vietnam and Saudi Arabia.

Heading: War of words expected in Assembly today - Indian Express
Content:
The Students Islamic Movement of India (SIMI)-owned house in Bhuj, which was sold off in 2007 reportedly to fund the July 26 blasts in Ahmedabad, was bought with the money the organisation had collected for relief and rehabilitation of victims of the 2001 earthquake in the state.

SIMI treasurer Mohammad Ali alias Vikram Sen made this startling revelation during his interrogation by a team of Gujarat Police, which was camping at Bhopal until recently. Ali (30) was arrested from Kareli town of Narsinghpur district in Madhya Pradesh (MP) last week. A Gujarat Police team headed by the Anti Terrorist Squad (ATS) SP, G L Singhal, had visited Bhopal and interrogated Ali for nearly two days, sources said.

"Ali is at present in the custody of Madhya Pradesh Police and we are working on the process for getting him here soon. We want to interrogate Ali in connection with the serial blasts here," Deputy Commissioner of Police, Detection of Crime Branch (DCB), Abhay Chudasama said.

Chudasama refused to divulge details on the role Ali played in the Ahmedabad blasts saying, "We have some leads which need to be properly investigated." Sources, however, said that Ali is believed to have arranged for the money used by SIMI to purchase the 'terror house' in Bhuj.

"SIMI had bought this house in Bhuj in 2001 under a fake name. Ali, who is the national treasurer of the organisation, arranged the money from funds that SIMI had collected from various states in 2001, for relief and rehabilitation of Gujarat quake victims. The house was later sold off to finance the July 26 serial blasts," a DCB officer said.

DCB investigations have until now revealed that the serial blasts in Ahmedabad, which claimed more than 55 lives, were funded mainly by the money obtained from the sale of this house, which is located in the cantonment area of Bhuj. A resident of village Jadura in Kutch district and an active SIMI member, Abbas alias Umar Sameja is accused of having facilitated this deal in 2007. Sameja, who worked as an instructor in a private health club, was arrested by the DCB from Bhuj and is presently in their custody.

A lesser-known name in the outfit, Ali has been working as the treasurer of SIMI since 2001. "In his statement recorded by Bhopal police, he has also disclosed names of some of the regular sponsors of SIMI activities. Ali has also confessed to having financially helped family members of Safdar Nagori and other SIMI activists ever since they were arrested," the officer added.

The fact that Ali worked as the national treasurer for SIMI came up in March this year, when MP police arrested hardcore SIMI activists from Indore. The ATS of MP Police started hunting for Ali since then. The hunt ended on September 10, in an operation they called "Operation Jimma".

Court remands SIMI activist Raziuddin Nasir in police custody for a day
A Metropolitan Court on Wednesday sent Raziuddin Nasir, a SIMI member who had been in Belgaum jail in Karnataka, to 24 hours of police custody with the Ahmedabad City Detection of Crime Branch (DCB) in connection with his role in the serial blasts of July 26.
Nasir, who had been arrested in February in Hubli, Karnataka, was brought to the city by the DCB on Wednesday on a transit warrant from Karnataka. Nasir is the son of Maulana Naseerudin, an accused in the killing of former home minister Haren Pandya in Ahmedabad.
A DCB official said: "Nasir was arrested by Karnataka Police on suspicion of having been part of a conspiracy to carry out bomb blasts in Goa, Karnataka and Hyderabad. We believe he too attended the SIMI training camp in Wagamon forest of Kerala with the other blast accused in our custody." The DCB is looking to pinpoint the exact role Nasir played in the Ahmedabad blasts conspiracy. It is also expected to seek a 14-day remand of Nasir on Thursday afternoon after the 24-hour remand period ends.

Heading: Wake-up call for VMC: 800 dog bite cases recorded in a month - Indian Express
Content:
The three-day monsoon session of the Gujarat Assembly is commencing from Thursday. The House appears all set to witness a war of words between the ruling BJP and the Congress-led Opposition during a debate on the government-sponsored special resolution on the controversial GUJCOC Bill.

The official resolution urging the Centre to clear the amended GUJCOC Bill is slated to be moved in the House on Friday. The resolution will stress upon the need for a stringent legislation like GUJCOC to deal with terrorist activities in Gujarat, especially in view of the recent serial blasts in Ahmedabad and the recovery of "live bombs" from Surat.

In fact, the Congress has already made the GUJCOC issue a bone of contention, with Leader of the Opposition Shaktisinh Gohil having shot off a letter to Assembly Speaker Ashok Bhatt. In the letter, Gohil has contended that since the Gujarat High Court, on a petition filed by an NGO, has issued notices to both the Centre and the state government on the GUJCOC issue, it becomes a matter of Subjudice and hence cannot be discussed in the House.

Even at the Congress Legislature Party (CLP) meeting held here on Wednesday, the Opposition members resolved to take on the ruling BJP during a debate on the GUJCOC resolution being brought in the Assembly. "We lost our party's two leaders Indira Gandhi and Rajiv Gandhi, who had fallen victims to terrorism. Despite that we have never politicised the issue. And if the ruling BJP attempts to politicise terrorism during a discussion on the resolution, the Congress will counter it with all might," said GPCC spokesman and senior party MLA Arjun Modhwadia.

The CLP meeting chaired by Shaktisinh Gohil and other senior party leaders accused Chief Minister Narendra Modi and the BJP of "playing politics in the name of GUJCOC".
