It was during the NDA regime in 2001 that the ruling BJP had sent the GUJCOC Bill draft to the Centre, which had not sanctioned this "draconian" legislation, the Congress pointed out, asserting that it will oppose the GUJCOC resolution in the Assembly on Friday, for there are certain "unconstitutional and anti-human" clauses in the amended Bill pending with the Centre since 2004.

During the short monsoon session, the government will bring in as many as six official bills—the Gujarat Maritime Board (Amendment) Bill, the Gujarat Homoeopathic (Amendment) Bill, the Gujarat Metropolitan Planning Committees Bill, the Bombay Land Revenue (Gujarat Amendment) Bill, the Gujarat Cotton Seeds (Regulation of supply, distribution, sale and fixation of sale price) Bill and the Gujarat Forensic Sciences0 University Bill.

Heading: Village mourns death of ‘blessed’ peacock - Indian Express
Content:
The city records about 800 cases of dog bite every month. Sir Sayajirao General Hospital alone records about 400 cases. The situation is no different in other hospitals of the city.

But, the Vadodara Municipal Corporation is yet to take up the issue seriously. While the corporation is working on the birth control of dogs to reduce its population, it has taken no step to keep a check on the stray dogs loitering around.

"Stray dogs are even seen inside the hospital wards, which is extremely unhygienic. However, there is no check on this aspect," said an SSG hospital official on condition of anonymity.

But the VMC officials have their own take on this. "As per the norms laid down by the Animal Birth Control (ABC) Scheme, we must sterilise and vaccinate stray dogs. But we cannot dislocate them and have to set them free at the place from where they were picked up," said VMC Market Superintendent M Jaiswal, who is in-charge of checking the menace.

Working under the Central government's ABC Scheme, the VMC allotted Rs 20 lakh per year for the purpose. "Stray dogs are sterilised and given anti-rabies vaccine. We had kept a target of sterilising over 5,000 female dogs since August 2007, and have been able to sterilise 4,220. As far as the city is concerned, there are about 800 dog bite cases every month," said Jaiswal.

The VMC project has been undertaken along with Vadodara Society for Prevention of Cruelty to Animals (VSPCA).

"We only get financial assistance from the VMC. We have about 15 people in the field and veterinary doctors to do the operation. Each sterilising operation is done at a cost of Rs 550. We have our daily aim of operating 30 stray dogs," said Ashok Krishnadas, VSPCA president.

Heading: Battle for elected Gandhinagar municipality goes to HC - Indian Express
Content:
In a unique incident, villagers of Pir-Lakhasar in Jamnagar district performed burial rites on a pet peacock of the shrine of a Muslim saint. The people even mourned the death of the bird for a day. The locals were fond of the bird that took shelter in the shrine over ten years ago.

Locals even believe that the bird was blessed with spiritual powers.

Heading: Cable operators torch rival’s office, die in fire - Indian Express
Content:
Gandhinagar is the only state capital in the country that does not have an elected local body

The battle for an elected civic body for Gandhinagar — the only state capital in the country without an elected municipality — has now reached the Gujarat High Court.

After all efforts of the Gandhinagar Shaher Jagrut Nagrik Parishad to get a favourable decision from the court failed, it moved a Public Interest Litigation (PIL) on Tuesday before a two-judge bench comprising Chief Justice K S Radhakrishnan and Justice M S Shah.

Through a petition, the Parishad requested the state government for an elected municipal body for Gandhinagar like those in Ahmedabad, Vadodara, Surat and Rajkot.

Putting up a strong argument, petitioner's advocate Jayant Patel contended that with 74th Constitutional amendment in June 1993, the government came with the Gujarat Municipalities (Amendment) Act that made all notified area committees defunct, barring industrial townships. He pointed out that Gandhinagar notified area committee also became defunct with the Municipalities Act coming into force from May 31, 1993, and an elected body had to be constituted in its place. But despite all legal and other conditions in its favour, Gandhinagar is "illegally" continuing as a notified area, with the state government having taken no measure to set up a municipal body to manage the civic affairs of the town, which was declared the state's capital in 1965.

Substantiating his point, Patel said that if Junagadh — with a population of merely 1.68 lakh — could be made a municipal corporation in 2006, Gandhinagar had all the similar parametres for being given a municipal corporation. As per the 2001 census, its population is 1.95 lakh, with a population density of 3,453 per square kilometre.

Spread over 56.75 square kilometres with 30 sectors and a few villages within its geographical limits, it now has an info-city, an electronic estate and a thermal power station. A number of industries have also been attracted to the city, besides several new town planning schemes proposed by Gandhinagar Urban Development Authority in the recent past.

The issue has been taken up with the authorities earlier as well. In November, 1996, senior citizen's council took the matter to the then chief minister, Parishad president Premshankar Bhatt said. In March 1997, the Parishad took up the matter with the state legal department, which in turn advised the state government to set up a municipality in Gandhinagar under Article 243(Q) of the Constitution. In January 2002, the Parishad approached the Urban Development Ministry. In October 2006, the Parishad met Chief Minister Narendra Modi and officers concerned in this regard. In February 2007, it submitted a memorandum to Governor Naval Kishore Sharma. But all of it went in vain with a cryptic reply from the state government that "the matter is under consideration".

Bhatt and vice-president Amrutbhai Modh said there were three reasons for demanding a municipal corporation for Gandhinagar. The state capital can get the benefit of Jawaharlal Nehru National Urban Renewal Mission (JNNURM) like other municipal corporations.

Gandhinagar being a 'C' category city can get 80 per cent of the cost for development projects under JNNURM as against 35 per cent for Ahmedabad, and 50 per cent for Vadodara and other cities. Second, it can expand its geographical boundaries by incorporating the nearby villages. Third, civic amenities would also improve.

Heading: Financer shot at in Rander, critical - Indian Express
Content:
Two persons died and another two were seriously injured in a fire at the office of a cable operator in Shapar-Verval industrial area on the outskirts Rajkot city early Wednesday morning.

The fire was an outcome of a business rivalry between two cable operators — Sadguru World Vision owned by Parmanand Sindhi and Shiv World Vision owned by Mahendarsinh Jadeja — who got embroiled in a price war.

Shapar police said that two persons set ablaze the Sadguru World Vision control room, but got trapped in it and died, while the two employees in the control room managed to escape with injuries.

As per the statement given by Chetandas Thakarshi (35) and Tulsi Gyanchand (41), who suffered severe burn injuries, they were sleeping in their cable control room on the first floor of Syam Shopping Centre in Shapar area when Lakshmansinh Jadeja and Indrajitsinh Jadeja reached the place in a two-wheeler. Armed with a country-made gun and petrol, they told the Sadguru staff to sprinkle petrol in the entire office. Then one of the Jadejas lit a matchstick and the entire office was in flames. The Sadguru staff jumped out of the window and managed to escape, but the Jadejas got trapped in the office. Seeing the flames, neighbours called the fire brigade, but by the time it reached, the two were already dead.

The injured Sadguru staff were taken to Rajkot civil hospital and later shifted to a private hospital for treatment.

Thakarshi has filed a complaint against unknown persons. Forensic Science Laboratory (FSL) and police are together investigating the case.

On the other hand, the family of the deceased has accused the Sadguru staff of killing the two. They have refused to claim their body and threatened to sit on an indefinite fast in front of the office of Rajkot rural SP demanding a neutral probe.

Veshubha Jadeja, father of Indrasinh, said: "Sadguru owners had called Indrasinh and his friend Lakshmansinh to settle the rivalry. They must have attacked and burnt them alive. How else is it possible that both the Sadguru staff managed to escape and our children could not even move out of the room?"

Rajkot Rural Superintendent of Police N D Solanki however said: "Our investigation is always neutral. We do not know either of the group. After the assurance, the family accepted the bodies."

Heading: Monsoon Session for just 3 days: Cong finds it distressing - Indian Express
Content:
A city-based financer was shot at by two unidentified men in the parking of Western view complex at Rander area on Wednesday afternoon.

According to the police, Praveen Kali alias Bhagat, a resident of Machhiwad, Nanpura was on his way to his friend's office at Western view complex at Adjan in Rander. Kali parked his car at the complex parking. He had already spotted the two masked men chasing him on a bike. But before Kali could realise the danger, the pillion rider opened one round of fire at Kali and the duo escaped. The bullet hit Kali's shoulder.

Kali was rushed to BAPS hospital at Adajan where his condition is said to be still critical as the bullet is still in his body.

The police suspect that some dispute might have resulted in the incident. According to sources, Kali is accused of murdering Kamlesh Reliyawala, General Secretary of K P Commerce College at Athwalines. He was out on bail and has been running his property and finance business.

Sources in the police department said that Kali and his friends including Balwant Kahar, a bootlegger of Nanpura, assaulted one Sajju Kothari, a resident of the neighbouring area, over an old dispute. Later, the quarrel turned ugly and the police had to resort to tear gas cells to disperse the mob. The incident took place in the first week of September.

Rander police inspector R H Hadiya said: "Kali is still unconscious as the bullet is in his body. We checked his past records and found that he was also involved in land grabbing and several other anti-social activities. We suspect some old dispute might have resulted in this incident."

Heading: PSEs set aside funds for social welfare - Indian Express
Content:
The congress has expressed serious concern over the declining number of days of the State Assembly sessions during the current Bharatiya Janata Party regime in Gujarat. The Leader of the Opposition Shaktisinh Gohil described this trend as "an insult to the Parliamentary democracy."

In a statement issued after the Congress Legislature Party (CLP) meeting held in Gandhinagar on Wednesday, Gohil said it is distressing that the Modi Government has called the monsoon session only for three days, starting from Thursday.

Even in the previous years, the BJP government had convened the Assembly monsoon session for a meager two days in 2007 and 2006 each, and for three days in 2005.

This is in sharp contrast with the previous Congress regime having called the monsoon session for 24 days in 1994 and 10 days in 1993. Even in 1995, when BJP's Keshubhai Patel was the chief minister, the monsoon session was held for 29 days, Gohil said, adding that even the number of Assembly sittings in a year has been on the decline ever since Modi took over as the chief minister.

Quoting from a report prepared by the Presiding Officers' committee on "Procedural Uniformity and Better Management of the Time of the House" set up by the Lok Sabha Speaker in 2001, the Congress leader said this panel had recommended that a State Legislative Assembly having more than 100 members should have minimum100 days of business in a year. For a Legislative Assembly having less than 100 MLAs, the committee had recommended minimum 60 days of business in a year.

"Despite the recommendations of the committee of which Gujarat Assembly Speaker was also one of the members then, the Modi Government continues to call Assembly sessions for less number of days just to fulfill the obligation laid down by the Constitution that six months should not intervene between two successive sessions of the House," said the Congress leader.

While the BJP government in Gujarat continues to hold Assembly sessions for much less number of days (ranging between 25 and 30 days) in a year, the number is higher (between 35 and 55 days) in several other states such as Kerala, Karnataka and West Bengal for such sessions, he said.

Heading: ‘Benchmark’ of crisis: Municipal schools in soup - Indian Express
Content:
Following in the footsteps of GIPCL, another corporation has taken the initiative. An upper limit of Rs 122.52 crore has been fixed for the Gujarat Socio Economic Development Society

After the state-owned Gujarat Industries Power Co Ltd (GIPCL) agreed to set aside 30 per cent of their Profit Before Tax (PBT) to carry out welfare activities across the state, another listed Public Sector Enterprise (PSE) of the Gujarat government, Gujarat Mineral Development Corporation (GMDC) followed suit on Wednesday.

The resolution for reserving 30 per cent of PBT for social welfare got the approval of GMDC's majority shareholders in a stormy rescheduled 45th annual general meeting.

However, when contacted individually, most of the shareholders denied having agreed to the resolution that allowed reserving up to Rs 122.52 crore of the PBT.

Explaining the resolution, Vijayalakshmi Joshi, MD, GMDC said: "An upper limit of Rs 122.52 crore has been fixed for reserving the funds for Gujarat Socio-economic Development Society. In any case, excess provisions would not be given for the said cause."

She also informed that the approval of the amount would be subject to the approval from the Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT). The funding to the social project would then be exempted under the Income Tax act 35 AC.

Kulshreshtha, GM Finance, GMDC, said: "On the basis of last year's profits, we have calculated an upper limit of Rs 122.52 crore to give away for the social cause. But that is subject to the approvals from the CBDT."

As per the details, considering the outer limit of Rs 122.52 crore, GMDC is liable to 33.99 per cent of tax on its PBT on the basis of which the company is entitled to get Rs 41.48 crore worth of tax benefit.

There was a feeling of discontent among the shareholders as the resolution got the majority approval. Premal Jani, a GMDC shareholder, maintained that the meeting was deliberately scheduled at an inconvenient time of 4 pm so as to avoid detailed discussions.

Heading: Govt surveys Asaram ashram’s land - Indian Express
Content:
More than 70 per cent of the schools do not have adequate number of benches to seat students

There seems to be a bench crisis in several municipal schools in the city these days. The number of students far exceeds the number of benches in the schools. As a result, the students are made to sit on the floor. They find it difficult to study from the blackboard.

"This crisis comes at a time when the School Board passed a budget of Rs four crore in the current financial year just for the purchase of benches", said Board member Habib Mev. According to him, more than 70 per cent of the schools do not have adequate number of benches to seat students. Most of them come from poor families.

Ideally, two students should sit on one bench. Keeping this in mind, there should be at least 30,000 benches in these schools, which run in two shifts.

Even if cramped, and three students are made to share one bench, there has to be a minimum of 20,000 benches.

"Compared to this, there are hardly 1,000 benches in these schools at present," Mev said inquiring with the School Board officials.

According to him, no fresh purchase was made in the past 15 years. Moreover, this has not deterred the School Board authorities to make budgetary provisions year after year on this account. "In the current year, the Board has approved Rs 4 crore for purchase of benches and prior to that Rs 2 crore was earmarked in the budget. However, nothing was procured," he said.

When contacted, School Board's administrative officer Dr Lagdheerbhai Desai acknowledged the fact that there is an acute shortage of benches in schools run by the Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation (AMC).

He, however, added: "We will be taking several steps shortly. We will be placing an order for 10,000 benches with the Forest Department if their sample is approved. In addition, we are planning to recycle the waste wooden furniture that is lying at various AMC sites."

Heading: Count your ‘pigeons’ before they hatch: city zoo conserves endangered bird - Indian Express
Content:
Acting on several complaints of land-grabbing filed by the residents of Motera village, the state government has started a survey of the land in possession of Asaram Bapu's ashram.

The state government had initially shown reluctance after the ashram came into controversy following the mysterious death of two students of Asaram Gurukul in July. However, it seems to have buckled under public pressure.

Ahmedabad and Gandhinagar collectorate officials said that the ashram's survey began on Tuesday.

Ahmedabad district land record inspector J D Charal informed that surveyors from Ahmedabad were also deputed for the survey, as the village was earlier a part of Ahmedabad district and the surveyors had more knowledge about the land records of the village.

However, neither Charal nor Gandhinagar district land record inspector J N Joshi could give the exact area of the ashram saying that the land record files were with the surveyors. "I can get you the details only after I get back the record files from the surveyor," Joshi said.

Asharam spokesperson Udai Sanghani confirmed that the survey work was on, but said that they had not encroached upon any land, public or private.

However, he said that the ashram has constructed embankments on the western side of the ashram to protect it from rains. "Another embankment was constructed on the back side to prevent soil erosion and protect ashram land. Some people have reported these areas as encroachments," Sanghani said.

Villagers however, accuse the ashram of grabbing land belonging to a few farmers.

Heading: HC postpones hearing on Haj pilgrims’ ‘erroneous’ list - Indian Express
Content:
KamAla Nehru Zoological Park at Kankaria in Ahmedabad is home to many species of birds that are on the verge of extinction. Nicobar Pigeon is just one of them.

The Nicobar Pigeon falls under Schedule I of the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972. Only a thousand of these birds are found in the wild today. Kankaria Zoo has 17 of them. The pigeons bred here are sent to other zoos in the country. Already, four pigeons have been sent to the Centre for Cellular and Molecular Biology at Hyderabad, six to Nadankanan Zoo in Orissa, four to Shakarbaug Zoo in Junagadh and two to Indroda Park in Gandhinagar.

"We have two pairs of Nicobar Pigeons here. They belong to Andaman and Nicobar Islands, but have been breeding here for many years. Although we cannot provide them with the wild food and atmosphere of Nicobar forests, they are comfortably staying here," said Dr R K Sahu, superintendent of the zoo.

Sahu added that breeding of birds is not as easy as compared to animals. Therefore, the zoo makes it sure that the birds get a suitable nesting atmosphere. Some birds like high nests while some are comfortable on the ground. Even accommodating birds of the same sex can be counter-productive, as sometimes they break each other's eggs.

The birds feed on fruits, soaked grains and chopped greens. They breed once a year and lay only one egg. The incubation period is about 30-40 days. The Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation (AMC) has sanctioned a fund of Rs 2 crore for the overall development of the zoo. In the last 10 years, the zoo has received almost over Rs 2 crore from the government.

"The government has also showed its interest in encouraging the breeding of the Nicobar Pigeons in Kankaria Zoo with all facilities for them. In future, if the bird becomes extinct in their original habitat, then pigeons from our zoo will be sent to Chidiyatapu Zoo in Andaman and Nicobar Islands to keep the species alive over there," Sahu said.

The Central Zoo Authority has defined the process of the upkeep of animals in zoos. Any zoo that does not follow the norms faces the risk of closure. As a practice, the zoos keep a record of the complete information about the pedigree, food habits, schedule of medicines and other details of the animals.

"Local awareness regarding the threatened species thriving in their locality should be promoted by the Forest Department and other local NGOs involved in conservation. The community level participation should be encouraged in the management and conservation programmes of the pigeons," said Sonal Dehskar of the Gujarat Ecology Society.

Dr R K Sahu believes that education can be a constructive tool to preserve endangered species like the Nicobar Pigeon. "We receive a lot of entries for internships and a considerable number of young students are opting for PhDs in Zoology. This awareness will further help them to conserve many species. Zoos have always played an important role to sensitise and educate people about many species," he said.

Sahu added: "I believe in the friends-for-zoo scheme. If people adopt an animal or a bird from the zoo, each such contribution can conserve many species that are on the verge of extinction. The customers have to only pay for the food and health expenditure of their chosen species for a year or more and maintenance will be done by the zoo authorities. They can also keep a check on how their pet is fed and taken care of."

Heading: Stripping for bet lands youth in trouble - Indian Express
Content:
The Gujarat High Court's division bench of Chief Justice K S Radhakrishnan and Justice M S Shah on Tuesday deferred further hearing on the 'erroneous' list of Haj pilgrims from Gujarat to October 6.

As every state is allotted a limited quota as per their population ratio and there is huge rush of pilgrims, the names are sorted out through draw of lots by Haj committees of respective states.

In Gujarat, which has been allotted a quota of 4,211 pilgrims by the Central Haj Committee (CHC), about 7,200 pilgrims were selected by mistake through a computer generated draw on April 21 this year.

Although the CHC corrected the mistake on April 22 and held another draw for 4,211 from among the 7,200, it led to complications. Those who had their names on the list of 7,200 sorted out earlier had celebrated the event and made arrangements for the pilgrimage.

Mohammed Moosa Hajiba, whose name got dropped during the second draw, approached the Gujarat High Court, beseeching that it was the mistake of the Haj committee and hence, he should be allowed to go for Haj. Hajiba and others, through their counsel Javed Ghasura, demanded that more than 4,211 people be accommodated in the VIP quota or the vacant quota of other states.

However, the CHC and Ministry of External Affairs, through advocates Abhishek Mehta and Rituraj Meena respectively, submitted in the court that 24,000 applications were received against the VIP quota of 6,000 and hence there was no way to accommodate the people from the 'erroneous' list. They also submitted that there were no vacancies in the quota of other states. In fact, there was waiting list in every state.

When approached, H A Munshi, an official of the Gujarat Haj Committee (GHC) said that GHC had no role in the draw of lots. "It was the sole prerogative of the CHC but even CHC can't increase or decrease the quota strength allotted to each state on the basis of their population," he said.

According to him, Gujarat was allotted 3.22 per cent of the total 1.57 lakh Haj pilgrims from India allowed by the Saudi Government. "In fact, the Gujarat quota at a rate of 3.22 per cent comes to 3,457 only, but CHC accommodated 754 extra pilgrims by utilising the spare quota of other states," said Munshi.

Heading: Mystery surrounds death of BJP worker - Indian Express
Content:
A 24-year-old youth's stripping act to win a Rs 10,000 bet has landed him in trouble. The youth, Dilip Jain, a resident of Lakhni village near Deesa in Banaskantha district, ran naked in the Lakhni Market Yard complex on Tuesday afternoon, to win the bet. Following the incident, authorities of the Lakhni Market Yard have ordered an inquiry against Jain and the people who provoked him to do the act.

The inquiry will be headed by an inspector of Lakhni Market Yard, Ramjibhai Pankuta. The authorities will decide whether to take any punitive steps against them or not once the inquiry is over.

Dinesh Bharatiya, secretary of the Deesa APMC, said: "As soon as I came to know about the incident I sent an inspector there and asked him to give a detailed report about the same. The market yard is a public place and we cannot tolerate such an obscene act inside it. The matter will be discussed in the board meeting of the APMC once I get the

report."

Pankuta added: "The youth, son of one of the merchants of the market yard, Kirtilal, entered into the bet on the provocation of some of the merchants of the market yard. We are trying to find out who were the people who provoked the youth to indulge in such an act." Pankuta is likely to submit the report in a day or two.

Heading: Court extends remand of five SIMI activists by another 12 days - Indian Express
Content:
Bharatiya Janata Party worker Satish Brahmbhatt, whose body was found on the Ranoli-Vasad railway track under mysterious circumstances on Sunday, may have died due to an accident.

According to Inspector N L Zala of Jawaharnagar police, Brahmbhatt was drunk when the private security guard and a beat constable brought him to the police station, on suspicion for entering the Reliance- IPCL refinery premises. Brahmbhatt's family is, however, alleging foul play.

Even as Brahmbhatt's autopsy report is awaited, Inspector B D Chudasama of Chhani police said the doctor, upon examining the body, said that Brahmbhatt died of a brain hemorrhage. "The doctor examined the body at SSG Hospital. There were no injury marks on the body," said Chudasama. Sources within Brahmbhatt's family said that he was a high blood pressure patient.

Officials of Jawaharnagar and Chhani police stations said Brahmbhatt entered the Reliance refinery premises on a motorcycle and went past the security guards towards the parking lot for the trucks carrying oil. "A security guard said he was in such a hurry that they could not stop his motorcycle," said Chudasama. Brahmbhatt banged into a refinery wall before the guards could apprehend him. "The guards are under suspicion," added Chudasama.

Zala said: "A constable along with the security guards brought him to the police station. He was kept in custody. He used the toilet in the police station and even made a phone call to his son. Thereafter, he escaped."

Meanwhile, sources close to Brahmbhatt said he had stakes in a transport business ferrying refined oil from Reliance. Sources also revealed that Brahmbhatt's family members have refused to believe that he died due to accident and have suspected some of his business partners for his death. However, no formal complaint has been registered for murder.

Two die in road accidents
Two persons became victims of careless driving in different areas of the city on Wednesday. While both the victims died on the spot, both the accused managed to escape. The first accident took place at 8:30 am near the southern part of Pratap Nagar flyover near Lal Baugh, when a dumper truck ran over a scooterist. According to Makarpura police, a yellow coloured dumper truck (GJ 6 –VV- 4077), ran over a scooterist, Anil Dabekar, a resident of Vishalnagar, killing him on the spot. The truck driver fled from the spot. The dumper truck belonged to a private construction company, police said. The second accident occurred near the Dena Village National Highway 8 when a jeep hit a motorcycle from behind, killing the biker and injuring his wife. According to Karelibaugh police, a Tata Scorpio Jeep (GJ 24-A-1782) hit a motorcyclist, Manoj Mehta, near Dena Village crossing on National Highway 8. According to the complaint filed by the deceased's wife, Neelam, they were hit from behind and the jeep ran over Manoj, killing him on the spot.

Heading: Gujarat government had information about Ahmedabad blasts conspiracy: Modhwadia - Indian Express
Content:
A Metropolitan Court extended the remand of five SIMI men from Madhya Pradesh including its national general secretary by 12 more days on Wednesday.

Aamil Pervez, Asif Hussain, Sibli Abdul, Qamruddin Nagori and Safdar Nagori have now spent more than a month in police custody.

The Madhya Pradesh Police had arrested all the five

men in March this year. The latest remand will expire on October 6.

The latest extension in remand has come in the case registered under Khadia police station where two bomb blasts had killed five and injured 45 others. Earlier, the accused had been interrogated in connection with the Civil Hospital and Maninagar blast cases.

In their remand application, the Ahmedabad City Detection of Crime Branch (DCB) stated that they needed more time to find out the SIMI plan of conducting bomb blasts in important cities across the country.

The DCB has contended that the role of Safdar Nagori needs to be further probed in the blasts and his 'jihadi plans' need to be unravelled. The DCB is also looking for the details and links between the training camps that were held in Wagamon in Kerala and Halol in Gujarat.

The remand application states that information about the others who attended the training camps is necessary like the names of the other conspirators.

Special Public Prosecutor Mitesh Amin said, "The accused are so dangerous that they could hatch the conspiracy of the bomb blasts even when they were inside jails in Madhya Pradesh."

Appearing for the accused, advocate I M Munshi presented before the court an application that stated that he is allowed to meet his clients alone, without the presence of policemen around.

He further contended that the accused are being physically and mentally harassed by the police and an in-chamber inquiry must be conducted by the magistrate and the statements of the accused recorded.

The court rejected Munshi's application and stated in its order that if the accused wanted their advocate can be present during police interrogation provided they do not waste the time of the investigating agency.

Reacting to the order, Munshi said, "The order has not been of any help at all. How will the accused, who are anyhow terrified of the police, make such a request to them?"

Heading: Jail escape: 2 constables suspended - Indian Express
Content:
Replying to a statement made by Minister of State for Home Amit Shah, chief spokesperson of the Gujarat Pradesh Congress Committee, Arjun Modhwadia, said here on Tuesday that SIMI activists Safdar Nagori and Amil Pervez had confessed that there was a plan to bomb Ahmedabad and Jaipur during their interrogation by MP police in March 2008.

The two SIMI men were arrested by the Madhya Pradesh police on the information given by another SIMI activist in Karnataka. During interrogation, Nagori and Pervez had revealed the names of 11 SIMI activists, including Sajid Mansuri, who were likely to take part in the blasts that finally took place on July 26.

According to Modhwadia, the two had also confessed to have organised a training camp in Halol, near Vadodara. He said that this vital information was given to the Gujarat government by the Intelligence Bureau. However, the state government did not take any action. "Had the state government acted on the information, Ahmedabad blasts could have been avoided," Modhwadia said.

"Why were Nagori and Pervez not questioned in advance? Why didn't the state government take steps to prevent the bomb blasts by arresting the suspects named by Nagori and Pervez?", he asked.

Modhwadia challenged Chief Minister Narendra Modi to hold a debate on Ahmedabad bomb blasts in the state assembly. "We have the evidence to prove that the state government had advance information about the blast conspiracy," he said.

Heading: Water from Sardar Sarovar: Govt nod after assessment - Indian Express
Content:
Two constables of Dahod police were suspended following the escape of a hardened criminal from Garbada sessions court premises.

However, in a complaint filed at the Garbada police station on Monday, the suspended constables, Ratna Khengar and Narpatsinh Mokamsinh, said that they were given the responsibility of taking three criminals from Limkheda to Garbada on a private bus going to Madhya Pradesh via Garbada.

They stated in the complaint that while the other two criminals could not escape, the convict, Manu Meda, managed to flee as there was just one handcuff to keep three criminals together.

Vipul Aggarwal, Dahod Superintendent of Police, said that Meda was brought from the Devgadh Baria sub jail to Garbada for a case hearing at a sessions court, from where he escaped.

"Meda has made attempts to escape from Dahod jail in the past, but was apprehended after police firing. The constables were suspended under CrPC Sections 223 and 224 for negligence in their duty," Aggarwal said.

When asked if adequate arrangements were made to transfer the criminal to Gharbada, Aggarwal said if there were no adequate arrangements, the constables should have reported to their superiors. "We are conducting an inquiry into the matter. Apart from the constables, whoever is responsible for the escape will also be punished," he said. As per the law, such hardened criminals should be accompanied to the court by at least two constables and one beat constable.

Heading: Vadodara wetlands under constant threat - Indian Express
Content:
The state government will give the green signal to Vadodara Municipal Corporation's (VMC) proposal to get 300 million litres of water per day (MLD) from Sardar Sarovar by the year 2035, after conducting an overall assessment. VMC authorities along with the Sardar Sarovar Narmada Nigam Limited (SSNNL) officers discussed the logistics of the process in a meeting at Gandhinagar on Wednesday.

Anticipating the shortage of water that the city might face in the next two decades, VMC has turned to SSNNL for help. VMC estimates that the population of the city will touch 38 lakh by 2035 and scarcity of water will be the main problem to tackle. Taking long-term preventive measures into consideration, the Corporation has asked SSNNL for water supply.

"We have made the calculation keeping in mind the changes that will take place over the next 30 years. We are in talks with the authorities in Gandhinagar and the decision is likely to come

shortly," said M K Das, VMC commissioner.

The project, which is an undertaking of the Jawaharlal Nehru National Urban Renewal Mission (JNNURM), will supply water to the city in two phases. Nearly 160 MLD of water will be supplied to meet the requirements till 2025, another 300 MLD of water will be supplied to the city by 2035.

"Baroda has been growing demographically. In the meeting with VMC officials we tried to understand their requirements and have agreed to supply them water from SSNNL. But the state government will undertake the necessary assessment of water requirement as well," said N V Patel, chairman SSNNL.

Heading: Income-Tax dept searches businessmen’s establishments - Indian Express
Content:
Gujarat Ecology Society undertakes centrally-sponsored project on the conservation of wetlands in and around the city

Taking notice of the degraded state of wetlands in Vadodara, the Gujarat Ecology Society (GES) has undertaken a centrally sponsored project on the 'Conservation of wetlands in and around Vadodara city'.

The GES has submitted its report to the Union Ministry of Environment and Forests. The report comments on the current status of the wetlands and has suggested conservation strategies through ecological study, while involving local population within the limits of Vadodara Urban Development Agency.

Jayendra Lakhmapurkar of GES said: "We took a sample of 10 wetlands like Harni, Bhaili, Koili etc. in the Vadodara district and assessed the water quality. We also suggested measures to improve water availability and the environment around the area."

As per the GES report, the main reason behind the degradation of wetlands in Vadodara is the presence of oil refineries, fertiliser plants, alkali plants, cyanide plants and Nandesari Industrial Estate with more than 200 small-scale industries. The most common pollutants are oxides of nitrogen, sulphur, ethylene, ammonia, acid mist and fluorides. The illegal solid waste dumping by these huge industrial complexes is also responsible for the degradation of wetlands.

While talking about the conservation strategies, Lakhmapurkar said: "We need to adopt the Public-Private-Partnership approach and carry out intensive awareness drives. Conserving wetlands by preventing illegal disposal of industrial wastes and growing pockets of grass is also needed."

He further elaborated on the necessity and usefulness of wetlands. He said that wetlands are important for biodiversity conservation as some of the most endangered species survive on them, especially migratory birds. Wetlands are also vital for the maintenance of ground water at an optimum level. Also, if not properly conserved, the catchment area of the wetlands gets blocked upstream, causing water-logging in nearby residential and commercial societies. This has severe economic and health repercussions.

Wetlands include swamps, marshes, billabongs, lakes, salt marshes, mudflats, mangroves, coral reefs, fens, peat lands, or bodies of water — whether natural or artificial, permanent or temporary. Water within these areas can be static or flowing, fresh, brackish or saline.

Seven wetlands in Gujarat, including Nalsarovar in Ahmedabad, Little Rann, Greater Rann, Pariyej in Anand, Wadhwana in Vadodara, Thol in Mehsana and Khijadia in Jamnagar, have been declared as 'Wetlands of National Importance'.

Heading: Rahul leaves Congressmen high and dry - Indian Express
Content:
In a massive operation, the Income-Tax officials raided at least 50 premises of builders, industrial contractors and packaging industries of Surat, Navsari, Valsad, Vapi, and Daman.

The search and survey operations that started on Wednesday morning are likely to continue till Thursday evening, an I-T official said on condition of anonymity.

More than 230 I-T officials from Surat, Vadodara and Ahmedabad are involved in the drive.

A few days ago, the textile businessmen had alleged harassment by the I-T department and had taken out a rally from the Ring Road to Majura Gate of the I-T office. The representatives of textile merchants had met the Chief Commissioner of Income-Tax to make their representations.

The search and survey operations were carried out in offices, bank lockers, houses, shops, godowns, farm house, factories etc.

Heading: Dengue: more cases pour in, tally stands at 127 - Indian Express
Content:
More than 5,000 party workers had to wait for five hours before they could get a glimpse of their leader

He shook hands with a few workers, waved to the crowd as his convoy moved on.

This is how Rahul Gandhi greeted 5,000-odd Congress workers who had thronged the Hotel Amaltas to the young leader. He left most of the visitors high and dry. The workers, who had come from across the district, were waiting for Rahul since 1 pm. To their dismay, the AICC general secretary arrived two and half hours behind the schedule i.e. at 5.30 pm.

"Has Rahul Gandhi left? I did not even come to know that he has left the venue. I wanted to hand over a bouquet to him," said Harpreet Singh, a Congress worker. Kalia - a drummer, who had come from Tajpur Road could not beat his dhol to welcome the young leader.

Clad in white kurta pajyama, he stepped out of the car for a second and again he was back on his seat thereby leaving hundreds of bouquets in Congress workers' hands.

As more than 500 vehicles had been arranged by MLAs and Congress councillors to bring the workers to the venue, MLA Jassi Khangura had also arranged for a community kitchen for roughly 800-odd party workers at his Hotel Park Plaza.

Traffic snarls, however, were an order of the day.

The Congress workers had put up illegal hoardings on all the legal unipoles, flex sheets of Rahul Gandhi's pictures were pasted above the displayed advertisements without any permission of the advertiser.

Heading: He bowls over farmers with his demeanour - Indian Express
Content:
The number of dengue cases touched the 127 mark after the Health department confirmed 15 more cases today. With this, the number of overall cases registered with various hospitals in the city has crossed the 450 mark.

Since most of the hospitals in the city are now going in for Elisa test, the number of fresh cases is now being reported as confirmed.

As many as 16 new cases of the suspected dengue were reported from the Dayanand Medical College and Hospital, while the Christian Medical College and Hospital (CMCH) and the SPS Apollo Hospitals recorded five cases each. Two patients were admitted into the Civil Hospital.

On the other hand, the number of overall cases registered with DMCH so far has mounted to 270 while the number at CMCH has reached 100.

Meanwhile, SPS Apollo Hospitals, Mohan Dai OSwal Cancer Hospital and Sri Rama Charitable Hospital have recorded 45, 25 and 15 cases respectively.

Civil Surgeon Dr SP Sharma said that maximum cases of dengue are reported in September because there is an optimum temperature for mosquitoes in the month. "Once the temperature subsides, the number will also start decreasing," said Dr Sharma.

Heading: Villagers divided over govt doctors’ transfer - Indian Express
Content:
Though Rahul Gandhi's meeting with farmers was scheduled for only 20 minutes, farmers made it sure that the Congress general secretary was glued to his seat for an hour. The Gandhi scion met a group of about 60 farmers at the Punjab Agricultural University (PAU) today.

"Unlike the typical politicians, Rahul Gandhi is very well informed. He has assured us to take up our grievances at the top level," said Nishan Singh, a vegetable grower.

"We discussed everything with Rahul Gandhi. He threw open the discussion forum with a volley of questions. The discussion swung from the impact of agriculture on global warming to minimum support price, subsidies, drug addiction, depleting water table, stagnating farmer income to farmers' suicides," said one Mehrabhaan Singh Sahouli.

Rice grower Nirbhay Singh was the most pleased of the lot. "Rahul Gandhi has assured us to take up the case of 1121-paddy variety which the Centre has declared non basmati. We have apprised him that this variety is a long-grain basmati and is sold under this name the world over. Rahul patiently listened to the fact that how by declaring this variety as non-basmati now, when the farmers are ready to harvest, will hit our incomes."

Dr Kirpal Singh Aulakh, former V-C, PAU, said, "This was not a usual meeting where politicians come and make hollow promises. Rahul knew his subject well. The farmers got a platform to voice their concerns honestly."

Cong leaders overwhelmed
Outside the venue, PCC President Mohinder Singh Kaypee who was flanked by senior leaders like Rajinder Kaur Bhattal and Manish Tewari said, "Rahul Gandhi has received overwhelming response from the public. He has connected well with the masses." Bhattal added, "Rahul's visit has not only rejuvenated the youth of Punjab but also pressed a panic button in the Akali camp."

Heading: A day of protests and rallies at PAU - Indian Express
Content:
The tussle over the transfer of Dr Gurmeet Singh and Dr Mandeep Kaur of Mansura village has resulted in the formation of two factions in Mansura and the nearby villages.

While one of the groups comprising some Panchayat members of a few villages is favouring the doctors saying that their transfer is not justified as it was politically motivated, the other group alleges that the doctor has not only caused blindness to some patients but has been practising privately and has taken with her all the donated goods. Meanwhile, the group that is favouring these doctors staged a protest rally today in Chandigarh against their transfer saying that they have been made victims of a conspiracy hatched by a local private doctor - whose business was hit due to their popularity.

"We have been very happy with the services of these two doctors. There used to be an OPD of about 100 patients at the dispensary every day. But one private practitioner whose business was taking a hit, tried to get them transferred in connivance with some health officials. So we are only voicing the opinion of the locals," said Hardeep Singh of Mansura Block Samiti.

The other group that also consists of some Panchayat members, on the other hand, has levelled allegations against Dr Mandeep Kaur. The group has also sent a complaint to the health minister saying that Dr Mandeep Kaur was not only caught practising privately but has taken along with her the goods donated to the dispensary at Mansura.

Asked about the whole issue, Dr Mandeep Kaur said, "I cannot fight the system anymore and therefore I am resigning from the job. In fact, I have already tendered my resignation on September 17. I am thankful to those who have stood by me and are supporting me."

However, Civil Surgeon Dr SP Sharma said that the department had not received any resignation from her. "We have still not received any resignation from her."

Heading: One from city confirms seat, results to be out today - Indian Express
Content:
It was a noisy Wednesday at the Punjab Agricultural University with the university's non-teaching employees and students' associations holding massive rallies outside the Thapar Hall. Apart from this, the PAU Teachers' Association also observed a protest day by wearing black badges on the campus. While the non teaching employees and the teachers registered a protest, the students of the university have gone on an indefinite strike till their demands are met.

Thapar Hall is the main administrative building of the university which houses the offices of the university's vice-chancellor, registrar, dean post graduate studies and other senior officials.

Meanwhile, the day began with the PAU non-teaching staff holding a rally. Harbans Singh Mundi, president, PAU Non-Teaching Employees said, "We had submitted a charter of demands in February this year. It was in July that we were invited for talks and were assured by the V-C that all our demands will be looked into but till date nothing has been done till date. Whenever we remind the V-C or comptroller or the registrar of the university about our demands, we are given false assurances."

Meanwhile, on the call of the Federation of North Zone Agricultural University Teachers' Association (FNZAUTA), the Punjab Agricultural University Teachers' Association (PAUTA) observed a protest day by wearing black badges. The federation includes agricultural universities from Himachal Pradesh, Punjab, Jammu&Kashmir, Haryana and Uttar Pradesh. The protest was against the undue delay in submission of the UGC pay review committee report for the implementation of new pay scales for teachers. The protest was also against the non setting up of the pay committee by the Indian Council of Agricultural Research, New Delhi, which is responsible for notifying the scales for agricultural scientists all over the country. Dr MS Mahal, Chairman, FNZAUTA, has demanded immediate set up of pay committee by ICAR to provide distinct pay package for agriculture scientists over and above the UGC recommendations.

Gurprit Singh Brar, president, PAU Students' Association, adds, "We students will not call off our strike till our demands are fulfilled. We had submitted our demands on the kissan mela. The worse is that no university official has come out to talk to us even once." The demands put up by the students include reopening of students' home canteen, hot water in hostels, good infrastructure, provision of coaches and lights in playgrounds, internet facility and recruitment of agriculture officers and other such cadres.

Heading: Dalbir Kaur left high and dry - Indian Express
Content:
As the 42 candidates in Graduates' constituency, which is the largest constituency of the PU Senate elections, kept waiting eagerly for the results during the day, the only candidate from city who confirmed his seat in the Senate today was Prof Jagpal Singh.

Prof Jagpal Singh was polled 3,222 votes while the results of the other candidates are still awaited. It is expected to be out by tomorrow.

The other four candidates who are in the fray in the graduates constituency are Dr Madanjit Kaur Sahota, principal of Master Tara Singh Memorial College for Women, Rajeev Bhasin and Praveen Sharma from Arya College and Lakhvinder Singh Bedi from GGN Khalsa College.

A total of 42 candidates are in the fray for 15 seats for Graduates' constituency in the Senate. The constituency which has an electorate of over four lakh voters has recorded only 20 per cent voting in the elections conducted on Sunday.

In the results of Lecturers and Principals constituency in the fourth phase of the PU Senate elections declared yesterday, all three lecturer constituency candidates had registered wins while in the principals' constituency, three of the six contestants from the district got place in the Senate.

PU SENATE ELECTIONS

Tense moments
AS counting of votes was on throughout the day at Panjab University, candidates for the Graduate constituency were keeping their fingers crossed. With the first preferences being counted, the names of only 5 candidates with a considerable lead could be known till the filing of the report. Only two candidates have crossed the 3,462 votes mark fixed as the limit for declaring a candidate as a winner, while the other three have secured winning position on the reserved seats of which two are for Punjab and one is for Chandigarh. The counting of votes in the constituency is expected to take another day at least as votes are counted manually.

Heading: ‘Robust’ Congress takes Rahul by surprise - Indian Express
Content:
Dalbir Kaur, sister of Sarabjit Singh, who is imprisoned in a high-security Lahore jail, kept waiting here today for meeting Rahul Gandhi, General Secretary of All India Congress Committee, but could not do so. Dalbir Kaur reached Green Land Senior Secondary School, Jalandhar bye-pass, around 10 a.m and wanted to have a word with Gandhi hoping that that he may help in getting his brother freed.

Dalbir Kaur said, "I tried to jostle through the crowd near Green Land School, the security personnel did not allow Rahul to stay there for more than a second. So I could not meet him. Now I will go to Delhi on September 30 to meet Rahul Gandhi." She further said that Rahul had helped her a lot in a communicating with with Home Minister of India along with other officers. She said,"He also promised to help me in getting my brother released from Lahore jail."

Sarabjit Singh was convicted for his involvement in 1990 serial bomb blasts in Lahore and Multan that killed 14 people. He claims that he is just a poor farmer and victim of mistaken identity, who strayed into Pakistan from his village located on the border. Earlier he was to be given a death sentence, but on April 29, 2008, his hanging was deferred.

She said,"I have only one brother and no one else. He has two daughters: one of them is 18-year-old while the other is 21-year-old."

Meanwhile, students of Green Land Senior Secondary School, Jalandhar Bye-pass, handed over a memorandum of demands to Rahul Gandhi when his cavalcade reached near the school on way to Jalandhar Bye-pass. Rajesh Rudhra, Director of the school, said, "Students thanked him for coming to the city and also demanded that Ashok Ganguli, the former chairman of Central Board of Secondary Education, Delhi, should be re-appointed in the same post. Ganguli had brought many positive changes in the board and also improved the level of education in CBSE schools. The students also requested Rahul Gandhi to hold a meeting with them in Delhi, following which the Congress leader assured them that he would soon call them for a meeting and listen to their problems."

Heading: Bank employees’ stir gets underway - Indian Express
Content:
"I was under the impression that Congress in Punjab was not very active and was dominated by the Akalis. But looking at the spirit of Congress workers I think I was wrong."

These were the opening lines of Rahul Gandhi's speech who addressed the members of Punjab Pradesh Congress Committee (PPCC) at Guru Nanak Bhawan on Wednesday evening.

"Congress has become aggressive in Punjab and it certainly has a bright future," he added. However, motivation of the youth is what is needed the most at present and the the leaders must focus on this aspect. Rahul addressed the members for about five minutes and told them that it was an organisational tour to boost the membership of Youth Congress workers. He added that in future all the visits would be planned and would be political in nature.

"I enjoyed my tour of Punjab and it can be called more of a study tour in which I have met a cross-section of people to know more about the state," he added.

Rahul Gandhi also hailed the nuclear deal which, he said, would benefit the nation. S.S Dullo, former PPCC president, also threw his lot behind him on the issue even as he extended a warm welcome to the young leader. Former Congress president Rajinder Kaur Bhattal too praised Rahul for this.

He conducted separate meetings with the PPCC workers and Youth Congress workers and told them that he would be organising separate tours in Malwa, Majha and Doaba belts in future.

Only a few leaders were invited to the meetings leaving a number of other workers high and dry who could not get a chance to meet their leader.

Heading: Seminar on career opportunities held - Indian Express
Content:
All branches of nationalized banks were closed on Thursday following a two-day strike by the employees in response to a calls given by All India Bank Employees' Association. The strike will continue tomorrow as well and hence no banking activity will take place thus causing loss worth crores to the banks.

Today, the bank employees staged a dharna outside the Canara Bank. They were protesting against the proposed privatization of various banks, which according to them, is not in the interest of the employees.

Heading: Passing out parade organised - Indian Express
Content:

Prof. K. S. Saini, Prof. and Head (Trg. & Placement) coordinated the placement process and thanked the Army team for visiting the college for recruitment.

Heading: Chasing the commonwealth dream - Indian Express
Content:
Achanta Sharath Kamal heard the crowd roar as he played a shot during his match on Wednesday at Sector 23 Table Tennis Hall and he knew he had to come out with a winning performance for his fans. And he did not leave his fans disappointed as he headed straight to the fans. "I never disappoint my fan. I want to meet each of them personally," says Kamal as he gets ready for his next match in the All India Public Sector table Tennis Tournament at Sector 23 Table Tennis Hall on Wednesday. The 76th ranked paddler in the world is enjoying his time after Beijing Olympics and with his current training schedule on hold, will sit back and like, most of the Indian paddlers tune his mind onto the forthcoming Indian Open.

"I guess Beijing Olympics was special for a player like me. When I took part in Athens Olympics, I was very young and my game did not suit international standards. But things have improved a lot in the last four years and I guess Beijing experience will do me good in the forthcoming years," feels India's top ranked paddler who lost to China-born Austrian Weixing Chen in second round in Beijing Olympics.. For most of the paddlers in the world, playing in China is just like a dream and the same goes for Sharath. "For most of players, playing in China is like a dream come true. They have the best facilities, best players apart from the best training schedule. It is very tough for a normal player to know how they train and Beijing Olympics gave us a glimpse of that," shares Kamal who won the gold medal in 2006 Commonwealth Games. The medal winner in the Commonwealth Games is now setting his eyes on 2010 Commonwealth Games. "2010 Commonwealth Games will be very important for us. I hope to repeat the same performance which I gave in Melbourne Olympics and I will be participating in a lot of tournaments before 2010 Commonwealth Games," shares Kamal. The 26-year-old paddler is looking to enjoy the coming month before taking part in the forthcoming Indian Open. "I will be taking part in the Indian Open in October and after that I will be concentrating more on the German and French circuit. Hopefully I will be able to good in those tournaments," feels Kamal. The player from Chennai, who also plays for Spanish club San Sebastian, will also be playing in the Spanish circuit in the coming months. "I will be playing for my club San Sebastian in the coming months and next year I will be shifting my base from Spain to either Germany or France. Let's see what happens next but as far as my coaching is concerned, I am satisfied with my coaches Sriniwas Rao and Muralidharan Rao," says Sharath. Kamal is one of the few Indian players who have been able to crack the International code and feels that if players like him perform well, it will be good for the youngsters. "A lot depends on players like me. If we keep performing well, it will set a good example for the youngsters in the game and I hope to see many faces in the international circuit in the coming years," says Sharath who is the only Indian player in top 100 in the world.

Heading: SC Railways drub BSF 3-0 - Indian Express
Content:
Her Olympic dream may have lasted only 34 minutes, but young Neha Aggarwal is hopeful of putiing up a confident display in the international circuit and is eyeing a medal in the 2010 Commonwealth Games. Sounding that she gained a lot from the Beijing experience, she says her next target will be to play well in the international circuit. "The experience in the Beijing was something that I will not be able to forget for a long time. Though I lost to Chinese born Australian Lay Jiang Fang in the first round, I guess it will do me good. Being still a junior, I considered Beijing Olympics as to gain more experience. Qualifying for the Olympics was a very big achievement in itself and it gave a chance to interact with some of the top paddlers of the world," feels the 18-year-old player who is currently studying in BA second year at St Stephen's College. "Chinese players are very competitive and the facilities there are very good. They also lay emphasis on the mental aspect of the game and each player consults a psychologist at least once in week. It is very important for a player to maintain a sound mental level," feels Neha who currently ranked 248th in the world.

Neha did not let herself intimidated by the presence of some bigger names in Beijing Olympics and is now eyeing playing more and more in the international circuit. "The best part about the Beijing Olympics was that we got to meet some of the big names in table tennis. Apart from world top ten players, we also interacted with some of the coaches and it helped us a lot," shares Neha. And the teenager from Delhi feels that players like her and Saina hope to do well in the coming years.

"Saina has been a huge inspiration for me. She was my room mate during the Beijing Olympics and we chatted for long hours about each other's game during the Olympics. She is a very competitive player and I guess I will be able to play like her in the international circuit," shares Neha who also won the bronze medal for India in the Indian Open held from September 11 to September 14. "Tournaments like the Indian Open are very important for a player like me as it give us a chance to rub shoulders with some of Asia's best players. I am eyeing more and more international tournaments this year as it will be a good preparation for the 2010 Commonwealth games. Before that, I will also like to train abroad and I am hopeful of getting a sponsor during that time,"shares Neha who is currently ranked 20 in the world junior rankings.

Heading: CYDA launches Hamara Beej campaign - Indian Express
Content:
SC Railways, Hyderabad drubbed BSF, Mohali by 3-0 in a league match of 38th SN Vohra's All India Gurmeet memorial Hockey Tournament on Wednesday. Prabhakar scored the opening goal for SC Railways in the third minute of the match scoring a field goal. Amit Sirwas extended the leeway for his team when he scored the second goal in the 29th minute of the match while Magun sealed the win for his team by netting the third goal in the 55th minute.

Vikram Saini opened the account for Chandigarh XI when he scored a field goal in the ninth minute before Simrandeep scored the equaliser for Rail Coach Factory in the 14th minute. Simrandeep put his team into lead when he scored another goal in the 27th minute before Vikram Saini scored the equaliser for Chandigarh XI in the 33rd minute. Gagandeep again put Rail Coach Factory, Kapurthala ahead in the 37th minute when he scored a field goal before Deepak scored the fourth goal for RCF, Kapurthala in the 50th minute. Down by 4-2, Chandigarh XI displayed some fine hockey when they scored four goals in the last 17 minutes. Rupinder scored the third goal for Chandigarh XI in the 53rd minute before scoring another goal in the 60th minute. Rupinder scored his third goal in the 65th minute before Kamal sealed the win for Chandigarh XI with a field goal in the 69th minute.

Heading: Bangalore Development Authority team visits BRTS - Indian Express
Content:
At a time when the country is anticipating the first Genetically Modified (GM) food crop to be approved on a commercial basis, Centre for Youth Development and Activities (CYDA) has launched Hamara Beej in the city to spread awareness and mobilisation on GM foods, called I am no lab rat.

With Bt Brinjal in the last year of trials and the biotech industry claiming that this is the first of its kind vegetable for commercial use, CYDA's Mathew Mattan points out that there is no independent research to prove that it is safe for the environment and health. Scientifically it is also proven that genetic engineering is inherently imprecise, unpredictable and irreversible and the adverse effects of such GM are well documented.

"There is absolutely no need for this hazardous and irreversible technology in our farming and food since there are proven alternative technologies being practiced by farmers in many acres across the country. Such alternatives are able to provide healthy, chemical free, nutritious food to consumers and demand that the government promotes such ecological alternatives and stop GM foods from coming in,''said Col Vikram Bokey, president of Maharashtra Organic Farmers' Federation (MOFF). The adverse affects of the use of such food was pointed out by Kavita Kuruganti, member secretary coalition of GM free India while Mattam shared the plans for the campaign.

The campaign is to be taken up in two phases and will cover Pune city in the first phase with youth spreading awareness about GM food. The campaign has started on September 19 and will be on till October 15.

Heading: Mehar Singh bags super heavyweight gold - Indian Express
Content:
A team from the Bangalore Development Authority (BDA) on Monday visited the Bus Rapid Transport System (BRTS) in Pune along Swargate and Hadapsar. BRTS route is being planned in Bangalore as part of the Ring Road proposal.

"We thought a visit to Pune's BRTS would be a good exposure," said BDA commissioner A Siddaiyah. The team was scheduled to visit Mumbai to finalise a statue of Lal Bahadur Shashtri, but extended the tour to Pune.

A Y Karche, joint managing director, PMPML said that the BRTS proposal for Bangalore had made use of the space at the terminals better than Pune.

"There, the bus station building will have four level parking area, where the ground floor is the station and the upper storeys will reserved for travellers who can park their vehicles. The upper floors will used for commercial purposes," he said.

Karche added that these inputs will be taken into consideration in the next stage of planning for BRTS, Pune. Meanwhile, Siddaiyah said that the city needed to build skywalks for the convenience of pedestrians.

Heading: Maharashtra bowlers have a tough day - Indian Express
Content:
Havaldar Mehar Singh from the Army Sports Institute (Green team) won the gold medal in his Super Heavyweight bout against Indian Navy's CPOPTI Hardeep Singh in the 58th Senior Services Boxing Championship held at the boxing hall of the Army Sports Institute on Wednesday.

It was a truly intense contest with the first 2 rounds belonging to Havaldar Mehar Singh, in the red corner and the last 2 rounds belonging to CPOPTI Hardeep Singh, in the blue corner. In the first round Mehar Singh threw some good left hooks and put his opponent on the ropes. His punches were flying in thick and fast and he won the first round with ease.

The second round was also dominated by the boxer in red. He showed some good footwork and was pulling away at the right time, avoiding most of his opponents' punches.

At the same time he connected with most of his jabs and punched his way to a second round victory. Hardeep Singh then staged a good comeback in rounds 3 and 4. Mehar Singh found it hard to deal with his opponents left upper cut and the man in blue was landing some forceful punches. He brought the score to within one point but the eventual winner, Mehar Singh, managed to slip away and stall time. In the end he won the bout 6-4.

In the Light Flyweight category Havaldar Paramjit Singh from the Army Green team beat POAH Jonathan of the Indian Navy by 7 points to 6 in a tough encounter. In the Bantam Weight category R/Nb/Sub S Santosh from the Army Green team beat Nb/Sub P Narjit Singh from the Army Reds by 8 points to 7.

In the Feather Weight category Havaldar Chotte Lal Yadav from the Army Red team beat Nk Manoj Rana from the Army Green Team 9-4 with ease.

In the Light Welter Weight category Sub S B Pun, SM from the Army Red team strolled past Indian Navy's MER Rana Moharia 11-4.

In the Light Heavy Weight category Nb/Sub Mahendra Thapa from the Army Red team proved to be too quick for his opponent Sep Gurudev Singh from the Army Green team and beat him 6-1.

Heading: Extreme Warriors edge past Gunners FC - Indian Express
Content:
The Maharashtra bowlers had quite an unpleasant day as the Karnataka batsmen put up a mammoth total 444 for the loss of 3 wickets in reply to Maharashtra's total of 253 of the friendly match between the two teams played at the PYC gymkhana.

Content:
